questions.rationale: QCDNUM, HOPPET, QCD-PEGASUS, and brute-force solvers use different representations, heavy-flavor treatments, and accuracy controls that have not been fully standardized against one another [1][2][3][4].

questions.question: Can polarized PDF evolution be pushed to the same practical accuracy and flexibility as unpolarized NNLO evolution while preserving robustness at small x and under Q^2 devolution?
questions.rationale: The supplied tools generally provide unpolarized NNLO evolution but polarized evolution only to NLO, while brute-force polarized studies emphasize percent-level control and Q^2-dependent spin asymmetries [1][2][3][5].

questions.question: How should future DGLAP codes expose alternative evolution kernels and convolution engines so that nuclear, fragmentation, and nonstandard evolution equations can be tested without sacrificing speed or reproducibility?
questions.rationale: QCDNUM explicitly allows alternative kernels and versatile convolutions, while HOPPET emphasizes accessible splitting-function and PDF objects [1][2].

node_443099e02e56.summary: These papers develop analytic DGLAP, Regge, Pomeron, and saturation-based treatments for extracting and evolving gluon distributions and structure functions at low Bjorken x.

questions.question: Can the Wilson renormalization group at finite parton density be matched quantitatively to analytic DGLAP or Regge descriptions in the transition region between dilute BFKL-like evolution and saturated nuclear gluon fields?
questions.rationale: The representative papers derive finite-density low-x RG evolution while also connecting multiple-pomeron evolution to the GLR equation in the double-leading-log limit [2], [5].

questions.question: What transverse-momentum-dependent observables can directly test the predicted modification of the small-k_T gluon distribution caused by high parton density in large nuclei or very small-x hadrons?
questions.rationale: The McLerran-Venugopalan extensions predict nontrivial transverse-momentum dependence and density-modified gluon distributions at small transverse momentum [3], [4].

node_658c6ef167fa.summary: This cluster studies transverse-momentum-dependent parton densities using BFKL, DGLAP, CCFM, dipole, and saturation frameworks for small-x processes.

questions.question: Which measured associated distributions at small x can cleanly distinguish angular-ordered CCFM-like coherence from the multi-Regge BFKL limit when inclusive cancellations no longer mask hard-scale dependence?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] argues that angular ordering is hidden in inclusive fixed-transverse-momentum structure functions but can survive in associated distributions.

questions.question: How universal are the Weizsacker-Williams and dipole unintegrated gluon distributions beyond the large-Nc dilute-probe dense-target limit used for dijet and photon-jet correlations?
questions.rationale: Papers [2] and [5] show that different small-x dijet channels reduce to combinations of Weizsacker-Williams and dipole distributions in specific limits.

questions.question: Can unified BFKL-DGLAP evolution with angular ordering fit both inclusive F2 data and process-dependent small-x transverse-momentum observables using the same nonperturbative input?
questions.rationale: Papers [1] and [4] describe unified evolution frameworks that reproduce HERA F2, while [2] and [5] stress process-dependent access to different gluon distributions.

node_9d914ba1f1d1.summary: These works test next-to-leading BFKL resummation through Mueller-Navelet jet cross sections and azimuthal decorrelations at the LHC.

questions.question: Which Mueller-Navelet jet observables can break the apparent similarity between complete NLL BFKL predictions and NLO DGLAP-like behavior at LHC kinematics?
questions.rationale: This derives from the complete NLL BFKL calculation finding that standard cross sections and azimuthal decorrelations can look surprisingly similar to NLO DGLAP treatments [4].

questions.question: How can Mueller-Navelet and forward-dijet analyses be consistently matched to small-x saturation or CGC effects when azimuthal broadening approaches the saturation scale?
questions.rationale: This follows from CGC calculations of forward dijet and gluon production including nonlinear small-x evolution and saturation-induced angular broadening [1], [2], [5].

node_ac2edf6d37df.summary: This cluster analyzes forward jets, dijets, and four-jet observables in high-energy and multi-Regge kinematics as experimental probes of BFKL dynamics.

questions.question: Which forward multijet observable most robustly isolates BFKL evolution from DGLAP logarithms, multiparton interactions, and parton-distribution effects at fixed collider energy?
questions.rationale: Forward-physics surveys emphasize BFKL dynamics, multiparton interactions, and saturation, while classic Mueller-Navelet proposals warn that rapidity-gap cross-section growth is entangled with PDFs [1,5].

questions.question: Can collinearly improved NLO BFKL kernels for all conformal spins quantitatively reproduce azimuthal decorrelations of widely separated jets at LHC rapidity intervals?
questions.rationale: NLO and collinearly improved BFKL treatments improved convergence and Tevatron agreement but still fell short of a good fit, motivating larger-rapidity LHC tests [3].

questions.question: How can high-energy factorization predictions for exclusive forward-jet production be matched to measured multigluon large-angle emission patterns in LHC forward kinematics?
questions.rationale: Forward-jet studies use QCD high-energy factorization to resum hard-transverse-momentum and large-rapidity logarithms and compute exclusive matrix elements for multigluon emission [2].

node_e3fb31230c98.summary: These papers propose hadron, heavy-flavor, Higgs, and jet final states with large rapidity gaps as channels for studying high-energy QCD resummation.

questions.question: Which semi-hard final state gives the cleanest separation of BFKL rapidity logarithms from DGLAP transverse-momentum logarithms and parton-distribution effects at the LHC?
questions.rationale: Forward-jet production at the LHC involves both hard-scale and large-rapidity logarithms, while large-rapidity jet pairs were proposed to avoid PDF-driven ambiguities by using azimuthal decorrelations [2], [4].

questions.question: Can azimuthal correlations in Higgs-plus-jet production at large rapidity separation provide a competitive BFKL probe compared with Mueller-Navelet jets and dihadron spectra?
questions.rationale: Inclusive Higgs-plus-jet production with large transverse momenta and rapidity separation was proposed as a BFKL channel with predictions for azimuthal correlations [5].

questions.question: How can BFKL and saturation contributions be disentangled in rapidity-separated dihadron spectra when moving from high-multiplicity pp to p-nucleus collisions?
questions.rationale: The dihadron-spectra study described LHC high-multiplicity pp data using combined BFKL and saturation dynamics and predicted the corresponding p-nucleus systematics [3].

node_5b97ede8b693.summary: This cluster focuses on azimuthal angle correlations and decorrelations of widely separated jets at HERA, Tevatron, and LHC as signatures of BFKL evolution.

questions.question: Can collinearly improved NLO BFKL kernels with conformal-spin dependence and realistic jet vertices achieve a simultaneous fit to Tevatron and LHC Mueller-Navelet azimuthal decorrelations?
questions.rationale: This question follows from NLO and collinearly improved BFKL studies that improve convergence and agreement but still remain far from a good Tevatron fit, and from conformal-spin corrections that reduce decorrelation [1][2].

questions.question: Which ratios of azimuthal-angle correlation functions in three- and four-jet multi-Regge kinematics best isolate BFKL gluon Green functions from phase-space and running-coupling effects?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in order-by-order BFKL treatments of emitted gluons with phase-space constraints and in proposed four-jet azimuthal correlation ratios using BFKL Green functions [3][5].

questions.question: How can parton Reggeization with unintegrated PDFs be experimentally distinguished from standard BFKL evolution in inclusive dijet azimuthal decorrelations?
questions.rationale: This derives from LHC dijet decorrelation studies using parton Reggeization, Kimber-Martin-Ryskin unintegrated PDFs, and Fadin-Lipatov vertices that describe ATLAS and CMS data [4].

node_816c6d4ab0b9.summary: These works study small-x gluon saturation and Sudakov effects in forward dijet and hadron production in proton-nucleus and DIS collisions.

questions.question: How can forward dijet azimuthal decorrelations in pA collisions quantitatively disentangle saturation-scale broadening, multiple scattering, and nonlinear small-x evolution?
questions.rationale: This follows from the CGC derivation of forward inclusive dijets with multiple scattering and nonlinear evolution [2] and the predicted p-Pb suppression of central-forward jet decorrelations from saturation [5].

questions.question: Can hard diffractive dijet angular correlations at an electron-ion collider reconstruct the small-x gluon Wigner distribution and its QCD evolution unambiguously from color-dipole amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the proposed connection between the small-x gluon Wigner distribution, the color-dipole amplitude, and diffractive dijet angular correlations [4].

questions.question: Does the apparent AGK cutting-rule violation in two-gluon production survive beyond the quasi-classical CGC approximation once nonlinear small-x evolution is included?
questions.rationale: This is based on the calculation of two-gluon production in DIS and pA and the reported direct violation of AGK cutting rules in QCD [3].

node_92b24804a24f.summary: This cluster develops complete next-to-leading BFKL predictions for Mueller-Navelet jet rates, vertices, and angular distributions compared with LHC data.

questions.question: Which Mueller-Navelet observables can unambiguously discriminate NLL BFKL dynamics from NLO DGLAP-like predictions once full NLL jet vertices are included?
questions.rationale: Complete NLL BFKL calculations find large corrections from both Green's function and jet vertices but surprisingly similar behavior to NLL DGLAP-type treatments [1].

questions.question: How stable is the apparent CMS agreement of NLL BFKL azimuthal correlations under realistic cuts, binning, PDFs, and BLM renormalization-scale choices?
questions.rationale: NLL BFKL predictions with realistic LHC cuts and BLM scale setting give a very good description of CMS azimuthal-correlation data [3][4].

node_98eb2d2ab4f8.summary: These papers use gauge-string duality and AdS/QCD models to describe deep inelastic scattering, small-x Pomeron exchange, and saturation at strong coupling.

questions.question: What observable in small-x DIS would cleanly distinguish weak-coupling twist-two parton dominance from the strong-coupling double-trace or whole-hadron scattering regime predicted by gauge-string duality?
questions.rationale: The issue is grounded in the coupling-dependent transition between ordinary twist-two operators and double-trace dominance described for DIS in dual string theories [2].

questions.question: Can the BPST Pomeron kernel plus realistic proton and current wavefunctions reproduce HERA F2 data and geometric scaling without relying on the simple local approximations used in early AdS/QCD fits?
questions.rationale: This extends the successful but simplified BPST-kernel fit to small-x DIS and the eikonal saturation picture with geometric scaling [4].

node_af7d686bbc38.summary: This large cluster covers NRQCD, color-octet mechanisms, photoproduction, hadroproduction, polarization, double quarkonium, and ultraperipheral heavy-ion quarkonium processes.

questions.question: What combination of quarkonium production rates, polarization observables, and decay data would decisively test whether the NRQCD hierarchy of short-distance coefficients and velocity-scaled matrix elements gives a universal description across hadroproduction, photoproduction, and exclusive electroproduction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the NRQCD factorization program for inclusive quarkonium production and annihilation in [1], together with the broad production and decay landscape summarized in [4].

questions.question: Can multiparton interactions in high-energy photoproduction be separated well enough from single hard-scattering quarkonium mechanisms to make photon gluon-density extractions and quarkonium production tests mutually consistent?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the finding in [2] that multiple interactions can strongly distort photoproduction final states and complicate gluon-density extractions.

questions.question: Which experimentally accessible production or transition observables most cleanly distinguish conventional charmonium and bottomonium from the unexpectedly narrow or charged exotic quarkonium-like states above open-flavor thresholds?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Snowmass emphasis that newly observed charged and narrow quarkonium states challenge the QCD spectrum [S1].

node_05d82945aadb.summary: These works apply NRQCD factorization at leading and next-to-leading order to quarkonium production and polarization across HERA, Tevatron, RHIC, and LHC data.

questions.question: Can one global NRQCD analysis of charmonium and bottomonium production simultaneously fit high-pT fragmentation-dominated data, low-pT mass-scale data, and polarization without violating velocity-scaling expectations for color-octet matrix elements?
questions.rationale: This follows from NRQCD factorization and velocity scaling in [1], the color-octet fits in [3]-[5], and the broad production challenges summarized in [2].

questions.question: At what transverse momentum does the fragmentation approximation become quantitatively reliable for prompt J/psi, psi-prime, and Upsilon production, and how should the transition region pT ~ M be factorized?
questions.rationale: The question is directly motivated by the breakdown of fragmentation when pT becomes comparable to the quarkonium mass in [3].

questions.question: Which measurements can separate the 1S0(8), 3S1(8), and 3PJ(8) channels that currently enter only through fitted linear combinations of long-distance matrix elements?
questions.rationale: This derives from the extraction of color-octet matrix elements and linear combinations in [3]-[5].

node_ec020494acc0.summary: This cluster emphasizes J/psi photoproduction and inclusive production calculations using NRQCD color-octet matrix elements and comparisons with global collider data.

questions.question: Can a single set of J/psi color-octet long-distance matrix elements describe hadroproduction, photoproduction, p_T spectra, inelasticity distributions, and polarization at NLO?
questions.rationale: The combined HERA, RHIC, Tevatron, and LHC fit in [5] supports NRQCD factorization for p_T spectra but reports worse agreement for H1 inelasticity distributions.

questions.question: What experimental observable most cleanly separates the 1S0[8], 3S1[8], and 3PJ[8] channels in prompt J/psi and psi-prime production?
questions.rationale: The need arises because Tevatron data constrain only linear combinations of 1S0[8] and 3PJ[8] matrix elements in [3] and new combinations at NLO in [4].

questions.question: Do higher-order short-distance coefficients and relativistic corrections resolve or sharpen the J/psi polarization puzzle implied by color-octet dominance at high p_T?
questions.rationale: The original fragmentation picture predicts strong transverse alignment [2], while [3] and [4] show that additional color-octet channels and NLO effects modify this expectation.

node_82ceb0795b99.summary: These papers use NLO NRQCD, color-octet matrix-element fits, fragmentation, and CGC+NRQCD methods to describe J/psi and psi' production across HERA, Tevatron, RHIC, LHC, photon, and e+e- data.

questions.question: Are the NLO NRQCD color-octet LDMEs extracted from Tevatron and HERA pT spectra universal across RHIC, LHC, photoproduction, two-photon scattering, and e+e- data once inelasticity distributions are included?
questions.rationale: The global NLO fits test color-octet LDME universality across many production environments but note worse agreement for some H1 inelasticity distributions [1].

questions.question: What matching prescription between low-pT CGC+NRQCD and high-pT collinear NLO NRQCD avoids double counting while preserving the observed smooth overlap region in proton-proton collisions?
questions.rationale: The CGC+NRQCD calculation describes low-pT production and observes an overlap region matching smoothly to collinear NLO NRQCD [4].

questions.question: Can the fragmentation-dominated large-pT description of prompt J/psi, chi_c feeddown, and psi-prime production be reconciled with the historical psi-prime disagreement and modern global LDME fits?
questions.rationale: The fragmentation studies found chi_c feeddown dominance for J/psi and serious disagreement for psi-prime data, while later NLO global fits include broad quarkonium data [3].

node_89d5c2760f6c.summary: This cluster tests NRQCD color-octet mechanisms for prompt J/psi production in photoproduction, e+e- annihilation, RHIC pp collisions, and fragmentation-dominated high-pT regimes.

questions.question: What measurement would decisively test whether high-pT prompt J/psi and psi-prime production is dominated by color-octet gluon fragmentation or by competing production models?
questions.rationale: This follows from the original color-octet fragmentation explanation of Tevatron prompt quarkonium excesses and the review of competing models [1][2][5].

questions.question: Can a universal set of color-octet long-distance matrix elements describe Tevatron, LHC, RHIC, photoproduction, and e+e- data while also resolving the J/psi polarization puzzle?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in extracted NRQCD matrix-element combinations, NLO predictions, and the persistent polarization issue [3][4].

questions.question: At what transverse momentum does the fragmentation approximation become reliable enough that finite-mass color-octet diagrams no longer change the extracted matrix elements?
questions.rationale: This derives from the statement that fragmentation dominates at high energy but breaks down when transverse momentum is comparable to the quarkonium mass [1].

node_89d5c2760f6c_1.summary: These works examine color-octet contributions and NLO corrections to J/psi production in photon-proton, e+e-, B-factory, and RHIC processes, often comparing Tevatron-fitted matrix elements with other data.

questions.question: Can a single universal set of NRQCD color-octet matrix elements reconcile Tevatron and LHC high-pT prompt J/psi production with HERA inelastic photoproduction z and pT^2 spectra?
questions.rationale: NLO NRQCD fits to CDF data can describe CMS production, but Tevatron-fitted color-octet matrix elements overpredict or conflict with HERA photoproduction data [1][3][4].

questions.question: What role do the 1S0(8), 3S1(8), and 3PJ(8) channels play at NLO in the J/psi polarization puzzle, given the large negative high-pT 3PJ coefficient?
questions.rationale: The complete NLO calculation finds a large negative 3PJ short-distance coefficient, while NLO singlet-plus-octet calculations still fail to explain the polarization data [1][5].

questions.question: Which inelastic photoproduction observables provide the cleanest test of whether color-octet contributions are genuinely smaller than NRQCD scaling and Tevatron fits suggest?
questions.rationale: Photoproduction was proposed as a clean perturbative test, and the observed HERA tension directly challenges the expected size of color-octet contributions [2][3].

node_7678f045860d.summary: This cluster covers NRQCD and color-evaporation treatments of double quarkonium production, color-octet effects in Upsilon decays, radiative spectra, and low-pT J/psi hadroproduction.

questions.question: Can NRQCD color-octet fragmentation and lower-pT color-octet production be described by one set of long-distance matrix elements across J/psi, psi-prime, and Upsilon without process-specific refitting?
questions.rationale: Color-octet fragmentation explains the high-pT psi-prime surplus, while additional 1S0(8) and 3PJ(8) channels are needed to fit prompt Psi and Upsilon spectra [1][2][3].

questions.question: What combination of pT spectra, spin alignment, and prompt/direct production separation would decisively distinguish color-octet NRQCD from color-evaporation descriptions at hadron colliders?
questions.rationale: The review contrasts CSM, CEM, and contemporary quarkonium models, while quantitative CEM tests and color-octet studies both target collider production systematics [3][4][5].

questions.question: Does the breakdown of the fragmentation approximation at pT comparable to the quarkonium mass explain residual low-pT discrepancies, or is an additional production mechanism required?
questions.rationale: The color-octet production work explicitly notes that fragmentation approximations fail when transverse momentum is comparable to the quarkonium mass [1].

node_a545b16f5cd6.summary: These papers analyze charmonium production and decay data to extract or challenge NRQCD color-octet matrix elements in hadron collisions, fixed-target experiments, B decays, P-wave decays, and eta_c production.

questions.question: Can a single NRQCD long-distance-matrix-element fit simultaneously describe J/psi yields and polarization, chi_cJ cross-section ratios, B decays to P-wave charmonia, and eta_c production under heavy-quark spin symmetry?
questions.rationale: This unifies the LDME extractions and tests in [1], [2], and [3] with the eta_c challenge to spin-symmetry-based NRQCD predictions in [4].

questions.question: Which measurement would decisively distinguish color-octet collinear NRQCD from color-singlet-dominated k_t-factorization with off-shell gluons in chi_cJ hadroproduction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrasting interpretations of the chi_cJ puzzle in [2] and [5].

questions.question: Do NLO 3P_J color-singlet corrections and chi_c feed-down reduce the required color-octet matrix elements enough to reconcile Tevatron charmonium data with LHCb eta_c constraints?
questions.rationale: The NLO chi_c mechanism and feed-down estimates are from [2], while the eta_c overshoot problem is from [4].

node_66a0ccd44d32.summary: This broad review-oriented cluster surveys theoretical frameworks, NRQCD factorization, soft-gluon resummation, photoproduction, and collider data for heavy quark and quarkonium production.

questions.question: What experimental result would most directly test whether NRQCD factorization with velocity-ordered color-singlet and color-octet matrix elements is the right paradigm for inclusive quarkonium production?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question is grounded in the NRQCD factorization formalism for inclusive annihilation and production in [1] and the shortcomings discussed in collider comparisons in [4].

questions.question: Can NLO soft-gluon structure and covariant-projector calculations produce quarkonium production and decay predictions that are stable across hadroproduction and photoproduction data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the NLO production and decay calculations including soft-gluon emission in [3] and the confrontation with Tevatron and HERA data in [4].

questions.question: How should quarkonium production frameworks be modified, if at all, to accommodate the spectroscopy of narrow and charged states above open-heavy-flavor thresholds?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the Snowmass emphasis on unexpected exotic quarkonium states challenging the QCD spectrum [S1] and the broader quarkonium overview in [2].

node_f7d83af2a545.summary: These works review the status of charmonium and bottomonium production theory, comparing color-singlet, color-evaporation, and NRQCD approaches with measurements from fixed-target experiments, Tevatron, HERA, RHIC, and the LHC.

questions.question: What single set of quarkonium production and polarization measurements across charmonium and bottomonium would most decisively discriminate color-singlet, color-octet NRQCD, color-evaporation, and s-channel-cut mechanisms?
questions.rationale: The reviews stress unresolved shortcomings in comparing NRQCD and other mechanisms with Tevatron, HERA, RHIC, and LHC data, and identify new observables as discriminants [2], [5].

questions.question: Can heavy-quarkonium production theory use one universal set of long-distance matrix elements to describe fixed-target, ep, pp, and heavy-ion environments without process-dependent retuning?
questions.rationale: The status reviews compare hadroproduction, photoproduction, and collider data while emphasizing the need to confront theoretical frameworks with data from many facilities [2], [3], [4].

questions.question: How should production observables be integrated with spectroscopy of above-threshold and charged exotic quarkonium states to test whether the same QCD dynamics controls conventional and manifestly exotic heavy hadrons?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass framing identifies unexpected narrow and charged quarkonium states as a challenge to the QCD spectrum, while the reviews place production among the central probes of quarkonium physics [1], [S1].

node_ec28d6e8028c.summary: This cluster focuses on the theoretical structure of NRQCD factorization for quarkonium production and decay, including gauge-completed matrix elements, NNLO infrared behavior, and low-pT resummation.

questions.question: Are Wilson-line gauge-completed NRQCD production operators sufficient to cancel infrared poles at all orders, or do higher-order soft exchanges require additional nonlocal operators outside the usual velocity expansion?
questions.rationale: This is the direct open issue raised by the NNLO infrared poles, Wilson-line repair, and possible higher-order nonlocal operators discussed in [5].

questions.question: How should the NLO finiteness of color-singlet and color-octet quarkonium production and decay be reconciled with the NNLO factorization problem at large transverse momentum?
questions.rationale: The NLO soft-gluon finiteness and projector treatment in [2] contrast with the large-pT NNLO infrared mismatch identified in [5].

questions.question: Can automated quarkonium generators incorporate gauge-completed NRQCD matrix elements, P-wave off-shell currents, parton showers, and spin-entangled decays while preserving NRQCD power counting?
questions.rationale: HELAC-Onia's P-wave recursion, shower interfaces, and spin-entangled decay machinery in [3] and [4] motivate extending automation to the factorization structures of [5].

node_15a1fd834737.summary: These papers study quarkonium and heavy-quark pair production in proton-nucleus, heavy-ion, diffractive, and ultraperipheral collisions using CGC, NRQCD, color evaporation, and photoproduction formalisms.

questions.question: How can quarkonium pT spectra, nuclear modification factors, and momentum broadening in pA collisions isolate the non-kT-factorizable multi-parton correlations predicted by CGC quark-pair production?
questions.rationale: CGC calculations show that quark-pair production is generally not kT-factorizable, while quarkonium applications compute J/psi and Upsilon nuclear modification and broadening using small-x evolution [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: Can ultraperipheral quark-antiquark photoproduction provide an independent measurement of the saturation scale that is consistent with saturation effects inferred from quarkonium production in proton-nucleus collisions?
questions.rationale: Photoproduction spectra are predicted to be sensitive to Qs, while pA quarkonium calculations use saturation-evolved nuclear gluon distributions [2], [4].

node_6b7082d9c4ef.summary: This cluster computes NLO and NNLO QCD, relativistic, and electromagnetic corrections to inclusive and exclusive charmonium production in e+e- collisions at B-factory energies.

questions.question: Is the historical B-factory double-charmonium discrepancy best resolved by higher-order NRQCD corrections, relativistic matrix elements, or a breakdown of the nonrelativistic expansion for exclusive channels at sqrt(s)=10.6 GeV?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the order-of-magnitude gap between early NRQCD predictions and Belle data [1,3], the large NLO enhancement [2], and the claim of poor NRQCD applicability [4].

questions.question: Can improved S-wave color-singlet matrix elements with resummed relativistic corrections bring a consistent description of charmonium production and electromagnetic decay observables?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the finding that resummed relativistic corrections significantly increase the extracted J/psi and eta_c matrix elements [5].

node_1157bdf1d86a.summary: These works address double charmonium and associated charmonium production in e+e- annihilation, especially J/psi plus eta_c, chi_cJ, c cbar, or gluons, using NRQCD factorization and higher-order corrections.

questions.question: What NNLO QCD contributions are needed to determine whether the large NLO K factor in e+e- -> J/psi + eta_c fully resolves the B-factory double-charmonium cross-section puzzle?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1] and [5], which find large NLO enhancements and explicitly suggest that NNLO corrections may also be sizable.

questions.question: How should relativistic v^2 corrections be resummed and combined with alpha_s corrections and improved color-singlet matrix elements without double counting in exclusive double-charmonium production?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [2], [3], and [4], which improve S-wave matrix elements, compute relativistic corrections, and resum a class of relativistic effects for J/psi + eta_c.

questions.question: Why are relativistic corrections large in exclusive J/psi + eta_c production but tiny in inclusive J/psi + c cbar production, and can this difference be turned into a general NRQCD power-counting diagnostic?
questions.rationale: This directly follows from [3], which finds significant v^2 corrections for the exclusive process but negligible corrections for inclusive J/psi + c cbar.

node_a30544dce7be.summary: This cluster examines discrepancies between Belle measurements and theory for exclusive double charmonium production in e+e- annihilation, including virtual-photon, QED, NRQCD, and light-cone explanations.

questions.question: What single set of exclusive e+e- measurements at B-factory energies would decisively separate large relativistic or QED corrections within NRQCD from light-cone wave-function explanations of the J/psi+eta_c cross-section excess?
questions.rationale: The tension comes from NRQCD predictions undershooting Belle in [1] and [2], while [3] argues that hard exclusive QCD with realistic charmonium wave functions can naturally explain the result.

questions.question: Can angular distributions in e+e- to J/psi plus charmonium verify the J^PC assignment of the recoil system strongly enough to rule out contamination from J/psi+J/psi or other electromagnetic channels?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] proposes testing the 0-+ nature of the eta_c assignment through triple angular distributions, and [5] argues that J/psi+J/psi could account for part of the discrepancy.

questions.question: How large must the combined electromagnetic, NLO, and relativistic corrections be across S-wave, P-wave, and D-wave double-charmonium channels before the apparent failure of perturbative QCD can be considered resolved or confirmed?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the sizable electromagnetic effects in [1], the order-of-magnitude shortfall in [2], and the large K-factor requirement emphasized in [4].

node_e52b8f207276.summary: These papers use NRQCD, color-octet channels, and feeddown effects to predict prompt J/psi and psi(2S) production rates and polarizations at hadron colliders.

questions.question: What measurement of prompt J/psi and psi(2S) polarization would decisively test whether cancellation between the 3S1[8] and 3PJ[8] transverse components resolves the polarization puzzle?
questions.rationale: The NLO NRQCD calculation in [1] attributes near-unpolarized J/psi production to cancellations between color-octet channels.

questions.question: How can feeddown from chi_c and psi(2S) be constrained well enough to resolve the tension between CDF Run-I, CDF Run-II, and LHC prompt J/psi polarization data?
questions.rationale: The complete NLO prompt-polarization study in [5] found feeddown to be important and reported agreement with some data but conflict with CDF Run-II.

questions.question: Is there a common heavy-quarkonium production picture in which NLO and higher-order color-singlet enhancements reduce the need for color-octet contributions without spoiling charmonium polarization predictions?
questions.rationale: Large high-pT color-singlet corrections in [3] and the Upsilon study in [4] challenge how much color-octet strength is required.

node_e3e8e5f965c8.summary: This cluster studies exclusive vector meson photoproduction and electroproduction using QCD factorization, dipole, Pomeron, and GPD-based descriptions across HERA and heavy-ion collider settings.

questions.question: At experimentally accessible moderate Q^2, how large are intrinsic-transverse-momentum and soft-overlap power corrections to leading-twist handbag factorization for exclusive vector-meson electroproduction?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the power-correction estimates for photon and meson electroproduction in [4] and the handbag-factorization analysis in [5].

questions.question: Can measurements of meson polarization separate gluon, helicity, and transversity generalized parton distributions in hard exclusive electroproduction?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the factorization theorem showing access to ordinary, helicity, and transversity off-diagonal parton densities through meson production and polarization in [1].

questions.question: How accurately can photonuclear vector-meson production in heavy-ion collisions be predicted by scaling gamma-p data once coherent photon spectra, Pomeron exchange, and nuclear dependence are included?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the heavy-ion photon-Pomeron production framework and gamma-p scaling in [3], together with the nuclear-dependence tests in [2].

node_c76d1fbaa735.summary: These works model coherent J/psi and other vector meson photoproduction in ultraperipheral nuclear collisions to predict LHC cross sections and probe nuclear gluon dynamics.

questions.question: How precisely can coherent J/psi photoproduction in ultraperipheral ion collisions constrain the small-x nuclear gluon distribution once photon fluxes, rescattering, and nuclear shadowing are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: UPC vector-meson rates are proposed as probes of proton and nuclear gluons in [1] and [5], while [2] shows the sensitivity of diffractive J/psi production to small-x gluon densities.

questions.question: Can measurements of the J/psi transverse-momentum spectrum isolate destructive source-target interference and thereby test the entangled decay-product picture in heavy-ion UPCs?
questions.rationale: The interference mechanism from indistinguishable photon emitters and targets predicts destructive effects at small transverse momentum in [3].

questions.question: What combination of exclusive J/psi and Upsilon production in pp and AA collisions best separates skewness, real-amplitude, absorptive, and relativistic wave-function corrections?
questions.rationale: The corrections to exclusive quarkonium production are explicitly treated in [2] and [4], which use them to constrain low-x gluons at HERA and the LHC.

node_5e9048578211.summary: This cluster focuses on exclusive J/psi and related quarkonium photoproduction in UPCs and proton collisions as a perturbative QCD probe of low-x gluon distributions.

questions.question: How can exclusive J/psi and Upsilon photoproduction data be combined to constrain the low-x gluon distribution while controlling skewedness, real-amplitude parts, and absorptive corrections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of HERA and LHC exclusive quarkonium data to constrain low-x gluons with skewed, real-part, and absorptive corrections included [2].

questions.question: Which uncertainty dominates coherent J/psi production in ultraperipheral PbPb and pPb collisions: dipole model normalization, vector-meson wave function choice, or nuclear gluon shadowing?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the strong model and wave-function dependence of normalization but constrained rapidity dependence [4], and the ALICE evidence for nuclear gluon shadowing [5].

questions.question: Can relativistic ccbar motion and rescattering corrections be constrained well enough that diffractive J/psi photoproduction becomes a precision discriminator among modern gluon distributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the pQCD analysis showing HERA diffractive J/psi data can discriminate gluon distributions once relativistic and rescattering effects are estimated [1].

node_ab3970d66f96.summary: These papers analyze coherent and incoherent J/psi photoproduction in ultraperipheral, peripheral, and proton-nucleus collisions, including nuclear shadowing, dissociation, and neutron-tagging effects.

questions.question: Can the rapidity dependence of coherent J/psi photoproduction be used to separate nuclear gluon shadowing from dipole-model and vector-meson-wave-function normalization uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This follows from the strong normalization dependence but constrained rapidity dependence found in [2] and the shadowing extraction from ALICE data in [3].

questions.question: Which measurements of the incoherent-to-coherent J/psi ratio and transverse-momentum spectrum can isolate subnucleonic hot-spot fluctuations in heavy nuclei?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the energy-dependent hot-spot model of [4] and the predicted factor-of-two enhancement and high-p_T spectral modifications in [5].

questions.question: How should neutron tagging and proton-nucleus comparisons be incorporated into a unified extraction of nuclear gluon distributions from coherent and incoherent J/psi production?
questions.rationale: This derives from the use of quarkonium photoproduction as a gluon probe in [1] and the coherent and incoherent Pb+Pb and p+Pb predictions in [2].

node_bc9491cab166.summary: This cluster develops NLO and phenomenological methods for extracting or constraining the small-x gluon distribution from exclusive J/psi and Upsilon photoproduction data.

questions.question: What combination of exclusive J/psi, Upsilon, and open-charm diffractive data would resolve whether low-x photoproduction extractions are measuring the ordinary collinear gluon PDF or saturation-driven proton fluctuations?
questions.rationale: This reflects the tension between collinear gluon constraints from exclusive quarkonium production and hot-spot saturation interpretations of dissociative J/psi energy dependence [2],[5].

questions.question: Can a simultaneous proton and nuclear UPC analysis determine the small-x gluon with controlled skewness, real-part, and absorptive corrections across gamma p and gamma A channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that joint pp and Pb ultraperipheral J/psi data reduce ambiguities in pQCD descriptions of gamma p and gamma A cross sections [3].

questions.question: How large are relativistic c-cbar motion and rescattering uncertainties compared with NLO gluon-PDF sensitivity in diffractive J/psi photoproduction?
questions.rationale: This is based on the original use of diffractive J/psi data to discriminate gluon PDFs while estimating relativistic and rescattering corrections [1].

node_5341002ee7c0.summary: These studies predict coherent and incoherent vector meson production in ultraperipheral and semi-central hadron or ion collisions using photon fluxes, dipole models, and saturation physics.

questions.question: Can the t-distribution dips in coherent vector-meson photoproduction be measured with enough control over photon fluxes and nuclear geometry to decisively separate saturation from non-saturation dipole models?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] argues that pronounced dips in the t-distribution offer a unique discriminator of saturation dynamics.

questions.question: How do interference effects between the two indistinguishable photon-emitter and target assignments modify low-pT vector-meson yields in modern RHIC and LHC ultraperipheral datasets?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] shows destructive interference when the vector-meson transverse wavelength exceeds the impact parameter.

questions.question: Can rapidity-dependent ratios such as J/psi to rho production in pp and AA collisions isolate the transition between soft vector dominance and CGC-like small-x dynamics?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] updates color-dipole and CGC predictions for rapidity-dependent J/psi and rho production ratios at RHIC and LHC.

node_8f016af385ae.summary: This cluster uses near-threshold charmonium photoproduction and vector meson dominance or QCD-based approaches to infer J/psi-proton scattering lengths and related nonperturbative dynamics.

questions.question: What near-threshold J/psi photoproduction observable would decisively distinguish vector-meson dominance from Lambda_c anti-D(*) intermediate-state production mechanisms?
questions.rationale: This framing question follows from the challenge to the usual vector-meson-dominance picture and the proposed Lambda_c anti-D(*) cusp mechanism in [5].

questions.question: Can high-precision threshold data consistently extract both the J/psi-proton scattering length and the gluonic gravitational form factors of the proton?
questions.rationale: This combines the gluonic van der Waals scattering-length estimate in [3] with the QCD factorization proposal for extracting gluonic gravitational form factors at large skewness in [4].

questions.question: How universal is the dipole two-gluon form factor inferred from J/psi photoproduction when compared with other near-threshold vector-meson channels such as phi electroproduction?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the dipole two-gluon form factor fit to J/psi photoproduction and its stated match to phi electroproduction near threshold in [2].

node_275c98dfee63.summary: These papers formulate and apply collinear factorization for hard exclusive meson, photon-meson, and quarkonium-pair production as probes of generalized parton distributions.

questions.question: For which meson-production channels do transversity GPD contributions accompanied by twist-3 meson wave functions remain compatible with leading-power collinear factorization, and where must they be treated as controlled power corrections?
questions.rationale: This question connects the all-log leading-power factorization theorem for hard exclusive meson electroproduction with the phenomenological need for twist-3 transversity effects in pseudoscalar channels [1][4][5].

questions.question: Can dispersion-constrained two-pion distribution amplitudes, fixed by pi-pi phases and chiral subtraction constants, provide a quantitatively universal description of both resonance and nonresonant backgrounds in hard exclusive two-pion production?
questions.rationale: This follows from the construction of two-pion light-cone distribution amplitudes using dispersion relations, pi-pi scattering phases, and chiral low-energy constants [3].

questions.question: What polarization observables in hard exclusive meson electroproduction most cleanly separate helicity, unpolarized, and transversity off-forward parton densities without being dominated by pion-pole or twist-3 contamination?
questions.rationale: This is based on the factorization theorem's statement that meson polarization can probe ordinary, helicity, and transversity generalized parton densities, together with the observed prominence of pion-pole and twist-3 effects in pi-plus production [1][4].

node_ef9f7018d348.summary: This cluster examines exclusive photon-meson, meson-pair, and pseudoscalar production channels designed to access chiral-even and chiral-odd generalized parton distributions.

questions.question: Can exclusive pi0 electroproduction extract the nucleon tensor charge with controlled separation of chiral-odd GPDs from C-odd Regge exchange and final-state interactions?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] proposes pi0 electroproduction as a way to isolate chiral-odd t-channel quantum numbers and access the tensor charge.

questions.question: How can twist-3 meson wave-function effects be tested experimentally as the source of large transverse cross sections in pseudoscalar meson electroproduction?
questions.rationale: Papers [2] and [3] find that H_T, H-tilde_T, and E-bar_T with twist-3 meson wave functions are required for key cross sections and asymmetries.

questions.question: Can two-pion distribution amplitudes constrained by pi pi phases and soft-pion theorems provide an independent bridge between resonance production and pion parton distributions?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] derives dispersion relations, soft-pion theorems, and crossing relations for two-pion light-cone distribution amplitudes.

node_9f1a6b39ce3b.summary: These works study QCD factorization, twist corrections, and two-photon mechanisms in exclusive rho meson and meson-pair production processes.

questions.question: What power-suppressed or higher-twist mechanism explains why QCD descriptions using rho-meson wave-function convolutions make sigma_T fall too rapidly with Q2 in diffractive rho electroproduction?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the review finding that both perturbative and non-perturbative wave-function convolution approaches underpredict the Q2 behavior of sigma_T, while an open qqbar plus parton-hadron duality model fits the data [4].

questions.question: Can generalized distribution amplitudes in gamma* gamma to meson pairs and generalized parton distributions in meson electroproduction be constrained together through common analyticity and dispersion-relation structure?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in factorization for hard exclusive meson electroproduction, two-meson GDA factorization in gamma* gamma processes, and subtracted dispersion relations with the D-term in hard exclusive amplitudes [1][2][3][5].

node_1e95abd6fabe.summary: This cluster analyzes light and heavy vector meson electroproduction and photoproduction at HERA using GPD, dipole, perturbative QCD, and Pomeron-based models.

questions.question: At what Q^2 and x does handbag or perturbative-QCD factorization become quantitatively reliable for vector meson electroproduction once intrinsic transverse momentum, Sudakov suppression, and soft-overlap power corrections are included?
questions.rationale: Leading-order skewed-distribution calculations explicitly introduced intrinsic transverse momentum and soft-overlap corrections because accessible experiments operate at only moderate Q^2 [2].

questions.question: Can one simultaneous description of longitudinal and transverse cross sections, spin-density matrix elements, and flavor dependence distinguish gluon GPD effects from vector-meson wave-function uncertainties?
questions.rationale: Small-x GPD analyses and handbag calculations model polarized amplitudes with double distributions, Gaussian wave functions, transverse momenta, and Sudakov factors, then compare to cross sections and spin observables [3],[5].

questions.question: How can nuclear dependence in diffractive vector meson leptoproduction be used to test color transparency while respecting the unitarity limits on hard cross sections and pQCD evolution?
questions.rationale: Perturbative QCD predicts Q^2 and nuclear dependence as tests of color transparency, while hard diffractive analyses identify unitarity limits and Fermi-motion effects near the onset of the asymptotic regime [1],[4].

node_2420099c95be.summary: This cluster studies exclusive light vector meson electroproduction at small Bjorken-x using QCD factorization, generalized parton distributions, hard-scattering amplitudes, and comparisons with HERA and HERMES data.

questions.question: At the moderate Q^2 accessible in vector-meson electroproduction, can intrinsic transverse-momentum and soft-overlap power corrections be separated experimentally from leading skewed-parton or GPD amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The leading-order electroproduction study estimates intrinsic-kT and soft-overlap power corrections because experiments operate at moderate Q^2 [1].

questions.question: How well do double-distribution GPD models constrained by ordinary PDFs predict longitudinal and transverse rho, phi, and omega cross sections and spin-density matrix elements at HERA and HERMES?
questions.rationale: The handbag analyses build GPDs from double distributions and compare longitudinal, transverse, and spin-density observables with HERA and HERMES data [2].

questions.question: Where is the onset of the asymptotic hard-diffractive regime, and how do quark Fermi motion, Sudakov suppression, and unitarity limits bound the applicability of perturbative evolution?
questions.rationale: The hard-diffraction and small-x GPD studies emphasize quark Fermi motion, Sudakov suppression, and a unitarity limit on hard-process cross sections [3].

node_48e0faa2cd64.summary: This cluster covers diffractive vector meson photo- and electroproduction, especially at large momentum transfer or with proton dissociation, using BFKL, color-dipole, and kT-factorization methods.

questions.question: How precisely can the Q^2 and nuclear dependence of longitudinal vector-meson electroproduction test perturbative-QCD factorization and color transparency?
questions.rationale: The diffractive leptoproduction study predicts dominant longitudinal production with Q^-6 behavior and nuclear dependence fixed by a perturbative-QCD factorization theorem [1].

questions.question: Can measurements of 2S light-vector-meson production isolate the node effect in radial wave functions and thereby constrain the energy dependence of the color-dipole cross section?
questions.rationale: The color-dipole phenomenology predicts strikingly different Q^2 and energy dependence for 1S and 2S vector mesons due to the node of the radial wave function [2].

questions.question: Which vector-meson light-cone wave-function features are required to reconcile heavy-quarkonium photo/electroproduction, transverse polarization, and the expected small-distance QCD behavior?
questions.rationale: The heavy-quarkonium study emphasizes the role of the q qbar light-cone wave function, including high-momentum tails and deviations from the expected z(1-z) behavior [3].

node_b042ffbc92d4.summary: This cluster links prompt photons, jets, and heavy-quark photoproduction in high-energy ep, pp, and ultraperipheral collisions through NLO QCD, kT-factorization, collinear factorization, and saturation models.

questions.question: How large are multiparton interactions in high-energy photoproduction, and can multi-jet rates isolate them well enough to extract the gluon density in the photon?
questions.rationale: The HERA photoproduction study finds that multiple interactions can strongly affect final states and complicate photon-gluon-density extraction [1].

questions.question: Can heavy-flavor photoproduction predictions be made reliable from small to large pT by matching exact mass effects through order alpha_em alpha_s^2 to next-to-leading logarithmic pT resummation?
questions.rationale: The heavy-flavor photoproduction formalism was built to retain exact mass effects at fixed order while resumming large-pT logarithms [2].

questions.question: How should coherent gamma-gamma and gamma-A fluxes, nuclear-size effects, and strong-interaction backgrounds be modeled to isolate photon-hadron heavy-flavor signals in very peripheral ion collisions?
questions.rationale: The peripheral-collision review stresses equivalent photon luminosities, nuclear-size effects, and diffractive backgrounds in gamma-gamma and photon-hadron physics [5].

node_d1bb370777c7.summary: This cluster examines electromagnetic photon-photon and photon-nucleus interactions in very peripheral heavy-ion collisions, including light-by-light scattering, coherent dileptons, and equivalent-photon fluxes.

questions.question: What single class of measurements would most decisively settle the normalization and geometry of equivalent-photon fluxes in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: The UPC reviews stress that coherence gives large photon fluxes but that nuclear size, collision geometry, and strong-interaction exclusion require special care [2,5].

questions.question: Is elastic light-by-light scattering in Pb-Pb collisions best viewed as a precision QED standard candle for UPC modeling or as a discovery channel limited by photon-flux and exclusivity systematics?
questions.rationale: The light-by-light study predicts sizable Pb-Pb rates with little background, while STARlight emphasizes geometry-dependent Monte Carlo modeling for UPC final states and detector efficiency [4,3].

questions.question: Can photon-photon and photon-nucleus event generators consistently describe hadronic production, vector mesons, dileptons, and meson-pair final states across RHIC and LHC invariant-mass ranges?
questions.rationale: STARlight simulates many UPC final states, while earlier photon-photon studies compare hadronic production across photon-photon, photon-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions [3,1].

node_3bf3301ca38e.summary: This cluster focuses on exclusive photon-fusion simulations and predictions for light-by-light scattering and related diphoton final states in ultraperipheral proton and nuclear collisions.

questions.question: What measurement or distribution in ultraperipheral Pb-Pb collisions would most decisively separate pure Standard Model loop-induced gamma gamma -> gamma gamma scattering from VDM-Regge and QCD-initiated exclusive backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by calculations including lepton and quark box diagrams, VDM-Regge contributions, and SuperChic studies of QCD-initiated backgrounds [3,5].

questions.question: Can STARlight-style impact-parameter photon flux simulations and SuperChic gap-survival treatments be reconciled into a single uncertainty framework for light-by-light cross sections in p-p, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from STARlight's geometry-based UPC event simulation and SuperChic's unified heavy-ion treatment with a theory of gap survival and A scaling [1,3].

questions.question: Are the large quasi-real photon fluxes in heavy ions sufficient to make light-by-light scattering a precision probe, or will detector acceptance, exclusivity requirements, and residual backgrounds keep it statistics-limited?
questions.rationale: This broad question derives from the prediction of about 70 Pb-Pb signal events per run after typical selections and the claim of negligible backgrounds in early estimates [2].

node_6030bb81cd02.summary: This cluster centers on coherent two-photon production of lepton pairs in peripheral hadronic and ion collisions, emphasizing low-transverse-momentum enhancements and equivalent-photon descriptions.

questions.question: How accurately can equivalent-photon descriptions of coherent lepton-pair production incorporate nuclear size, strong-interaction vetoes, and impact-parameter dependence in very peripheral heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: Reviews of coherent gamma gamma and gamma-A interactions emphasize high photon fluxes but require special treatment of nuclear size and strong-interaction effects [2], [3].

questions.question: What measurements of elastic, single-dissociative, and double-dissociative lepton-pair channels best constrain survival probabilities and dissociation modeling in photon-initiated pp production?
questions.rationale: SuperChic 4 treats elastic, single-dissociative, and double-dissociative channels, including dissociation decays and no-additional-interaction survival probabilities [4].

questions.question: Where is the boundary between photon-photon and Drell-Yan dominance for charged-lepton or heavy charged-particle production once elastic, semi-elastic, and inelastic photon components are consistently included?
questions.rationale: High-energy pp studies found gamma gamma production far below Drell-Yan for heavy charged particles and noted that elastic, semi-elastic, and inelastic photon components are comparable [5].

node_d399c04b5669.summary: This cluster studies isolated photon, photon-plus-jet, and photon-plus-dijet production with realistic isolation criteria and higher-order perturbative QCD corrections at HERA and hadron colliders.

questions.question: How can experimental cone isolation be translated into perturbative predictions that remain both infrared safe and quantitatively faithful to fragmentation-sensitive measurements?
questions.rationale: Smooth-cone isolation in [2] removes fragmentation dependence, while the fixed-cone NLO treatment in [3] keeps direct and fragmentation components with full cone-radius dependence.

questions.question: Which observables in photon-plus-jets or multiphoton production can separate higher-order perturbative corrections from multiparton-interaction effects in photoproduction and hadron collisions?
questions.rationale: Multiparton interactions were found in [1] to strongly affect photoproduction final states and gluon-density extractions, while [3] and [4] focus on NLO isolated photon and photon-pair predictions.

questions.question: What residual scale and isolation-parameter uncertainties must be reduced before isolated prompt photons can serve as precision constraints on QCD and parton densities across RHIC, Tevatron, and LHC data?
questions.rationale: The world-data comparison with JETPHOX in [5] and the scale and isolation studies in [3] identify these uncertainties as central limitations.

node_60989d711595.summary: This cluster addresses jet and dijet photoproduction in ep and photon-photon collisions, comparing direct and resolved photon contributions with next-to-leading-order QCD predictions and HERA data.

questions.question: Which jet and underlying-event observables can isolate multiparton interactions in HERA photoproduction strongly enough to avoid biasing extractions of the photon gluon density?
questions.rationale: The multiparton-interaction model predicted significant effects on photoproduction final states and warned that photon gluon-density extractions could become difficult [1].

questions.question: Where do NLO direct-plus-resolved photoproduction predictions lose perturbative reliability because of scale dependence, phase-space cuts, or experimental separation of pointlike and hadronic photon components?
questions.rationale: The NLO HERA jet study explicitly examined scale dependence, possible perturbative breakdown, and the experimental definition of pointlike versus hadronic photon components [2].

questions.question: Can one define a unified NLO framework for gamma p and gamma gamma one- and two-jet production in which slicing or subtraction choices do not affect extracted proton and photon structure functions?
questions.rationale: Inclusive jet calculations in gamma p and gamma gamma processes use exact NLO direct and resolved cross sections with singularities canceled or absorbed into parton densities [5].

node_eeb1917a7d02.summary: This cluster focuses on prompt and diphoton production in hadronic collisions, including isolation prescriptions, fragmentation contributions, NLO and NNLO calculations, and comparisons to collider data.

questions.question: Can smooth-cone isolation be made experimentally equivalent to fixed-cone isolation with controlled power corrections, so that fragmentation-independent prompt-photon predictions can be compared directly to collider measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the smooth isolation prescription that removes the parton-to-photon fragmentation contribution while fixed-cone experimental criteria retain direct and fragmentation components [1], [2].

questions.question: Which isolation parameters and cone-radius regimes expose the largest difference between exact R-dependent NLO predictions and small-cone approximations for isolated prompt photons?
questions.rationale: The NLO Monte Carlo calculation explicitly studied scale dependence, isolation-parameter sensitivity, and full versus approximate cone-radius dependence [2].

questions.question: For diphoton backgrounds to Higgs measurements, which infrared-sensitive configurations identified at full NLO require NNLO or resummed treatment before isolation systematics can be considered under control?
questions.rationale: The full NLO diphoton study included single and double fragmentation contributions, Higgs-background predictions, scale uncertainties, and infrared-sensitive situations requiring further work [3].

node_4284f4dae5d1.summary: This cluster studies charm and bottom production in photon-nucleon, photon-photon, proton-proton, and ultraperipheral heavy-ion environments using perturbative QCD, kT-factorization, and saturation approaches.

questions.question: What measurement program in heavy-flavor photoproduction would most cleanly separate small-x gluon-density uncertainties from photon-parton-density and hadronic-photon-component uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The HERA total and differential studies identify small-x proton gluons, photon parton densities, and the hadronic photon component as leading theoretical ambiguities [4,5].

questions.question: Are NLO exclusive heavy-quark correlation observables sufficient to discriminate perturbative QCD descriptions once fragmentation and intrinsic transverse momentum are included?
questions.rationale: The NLO correlation and differential-distribution papers compute heavy-quark, antiquark, and jet correlations while emphasizing fragmentation and intrinsic-kT effects [2,5].

questions.question: Which transverse-momentum range in charm photoproduction provides the most decisive test of a framework that simultaneously resums large-pT logarithms and retains exact heavy-quark mass effects?
questions.rationale: The pT-spectrum paper constructs a formalism combining next-to-leading logarithmic resummation with exact mass effects through order alpha_em alpha_s^2 [1].

node_b678240c83cf.summary: This cluster investigates prompt photon production, often with heavy quarks or jets, using kT-factorization, off-shell partonic amplitudes, and unintegrated parton distributions at HERA and the LHC.

questions.question: Can a single set of doubly-unintegrated parton distributions in z and k_t describe both HERA inclusive jet data and hadron-collider prompt photon spectra once NLO matching is included?
questions.rationale: This combines the z,k_t-factorization and NLO extension proposed for HERA jets [1] with the unintegrated-density treatment of prompt photon transverse-momentum spectra [3].

questions.question: How can direct photon, diphoton, and pion data separate nonperturbative Gaussian k_t broadening from perturbatively generated large-q_t enhancements in extractions of the gluon distribution?
questions.rationale: The issue is motivated by the phenomenological broadening uncertainties in direct photons [2], the separate small- and large-q_t treatments of prompt photons [3], and loop-induced diphoton contributions with resummation [5].

node_a9e76c675792.summary: This cluster examines double parton scattering in proton and nuclear collisions, including double charm, double J/psi, double Drell-Yan, and correlations in double parton distributions.

questions.question: What measurable correlations in double charm, double J/psi, or double Drell-Yan production would falsify the common factorized ansatz for double parton distributions?
questions.rationale: The multiparton-interactions theory paper highlights spin, color, space-time correlations and the need for all-order factorization elements beyond simple independent scatterings [3].

questions.question: Can dPDF evolution with momentum and quark-number sum rules be constrained by heavy-flavor production data strongly enough to distinguish double scattering from higher-order single-scattering backgrounds?
questions.rationale: The dPDF paper constructs leading-order distributions satisfying momentum and number sum rules, while heavy-flavor benchmark calculations provide the single-production baselines needed for comparison [4].

node_165046e96039.summary: These papers model open charm and double-charm production at the LHC, comparing k_t-factorization predictions, gluon distributions, fragmentation, and single- versus double-parton scattering contributions.

questions.question: Can open-charm pair correlations at the LHC cleanly isolate double-parton scattering once FONLL, MC@NLO, POWHEG, GM-VFNS, fragmentation, and kt-factorization single-parton baselines are brought under common uncertainty control?
questions.rationale: This follows from precision charm and bottom predictions in FONLL and NLO-matched frameworks, GM-VFNS charmed-hadron predictions, and kt-factorization studies of D-Dbar correlations [1,3,5].

questions.question: Which unintegrated gluon distribution features make the KMR model reproduce LHC open-charm data while other UGDF choices underpredict transverse-momentum and rapidity spectra?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the kt-factorization analysis where only the Kimber-Martin-Ryskin UGDF gives results comparable to ATLAS, ALICE, and LHCb data [5].

questions.question: Can large-rapidity charm measurements simultaneously constrain intrinsic charm and separate nuclear or multiple-scattering effects from ordinary heavy-flavor production uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This follows from the observation that large-rapidity charmed-hadron measurements can pin down intrinsic charm and from heavy-flavor benchmarks used to identify nuclear effects [2,3,4].

node_5e42e39c1ffa.summary: This cluster develops the theory of double parton scattering through double parton distributions, emphasizing QCD evolution, sum rules, perturbative splitting, and spin, color, flavor, and spatial correlations.

questions.question: How can double parton distributions be parametrized so that momentum and quark-number sum rules, perturbative splitting correlations, and transverse spatial information are all preserved under QCD evolution?
questions.rationale: This combines the sum-rule-preserving leading-order dPDF construction [1], perturbative splitting correlations [2], and transverse parton-structure information from hard exclusive processes [5].

questions.question: At what hard scales and rapidity separations are spin, color, flavor, and parton-exchange interference correlations still phenomenologically relevant before Sudakov suppression renders them negligible?
questions.rationale: This follows from the factorization analysis of color, spin, flavor, and interference contributions and their Sudakov suppression in double Drell-Yan [3].

questions.question: Can perturbatively generated two-parton correlations quantitatively resolve multi-jet excesses in back-to-back kinematics without double counting single hard scattering contributions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the proposed role of perturbative splitting correlations in the Tevatron multi-jet excess [2] and the revised inclusive DPS cross-section formulation [4].

node_f97c92531011.summary: These works study double parton scattering phenomenology at the LHC in final states such as J/psi pairs, quarkonium plus vector bosons, four jets, and proton-nucleus or nucleus-nucleus collisions.

questions.question: Can LHC measurements isolate the nonperturbative two-parton correlations in dPDFs from perturbative splitting correlations in double parton scattering?
questions.rationale: This follows from the distinction between large-distance and small-distance correlations in generalized two-parton distributions in [2].

questions.question: Which final state gives the cleanest extraction of sigma_eff and dPDF correlations: four back-to-back jets, same-sign W pairs, or prompt J/psi pairs?
questions.rationale: The candidate channels are developed respectively in [4], [3], and [5].

questions.question: Can all-order factorization for double hard scattering be made predictive once spin, color, transverse-distance dependence, and Sudakov logarithms are included?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the factorization elements, spin-color structure, and Sudakov-logarithm analysis of multiparton interactions in [1].

node_3daa3733f622.summary: This cluster analyzes charm, charmonium, and light-meson production in antiproton-proton or antiproton-nucleon annihilation, often motivated by PANDA and described with factorization, exchange models, and threshold dynamics.

questions.question: Can PANDA measurements of antiproton-proton charm production discriminate between Regge-based hadronic exchange models and factorized short-distance descriptions near threshold?
questions.rationale: Charm yields at PANDA are estimated with Regge-pole hadronic models in [5], while factorized annihilation frameworks are developed in [2].

questions.question: What observables in antiproton-deuteron annihilation best isolate D N and anti-D N rescattering from the primary open-charm production amplitude?
questions.rationale: The use of pbar d to D anti-D N reactions to extract D N and anti-D N interactions, including methods to isolate rescattering terms, is the focus of [3].

questions.question: Do handbag factorization relations observed in two-photon meson and baryon-pair production extend quantitatively to timelike transition distribution amplitudes in antiproton annihilation?
questions.rationale: Handbag factorization and timelike distribution amplitudes are developed in [1] and [4], while antiproton-to-meson transition distribution amplitudes are introduced in [2].

node_b87cb4d712f8.summary: These papers address perturbative QCD factorization, infrared singularities, event-shape power corrections, jet observables, threshold logarithms, and soft-gluon resummation in high-energy scattering.

questions.question: How can subtraction algorithms generalizing dipole factorization be extended to higher perturbative orders while retaining exact phase-space factorization for arbitrary jet observables in lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the NLO dipole-subtraction construction and exact dipole phase-space factorization of [1], extended toward the precision needs described in [S2].

questions.question: Can operator-level soft-collinear factorization in effective field theory be unified with high-energy Wilson-line evolution so that threshold, small-x, and multi-TeV electroweak collinear logarithms are resummed in one consistent framework?
questions.rationale: The question combines the Wilson-line evolution origin of high-energy logarithms in [2], SCET operator factorization in [3], and electroweak fragmentation-log resummation in [S3].

questions.question: For soft-drop observables such as energy correlation functions, groomed radius, and energy loss, what is the smallest set of perturbative, nonperturbative, and Sudakov-safe ingredients needed for percent-level collider predictions across the full beta and z_cut parameter space?
questions.rationale: This follows from the resummed soft-drop calculations and Sudakov-safe beta=0 energy-loss behavior introduced in [5], in the Snowmass precision-QCD context [S1].

node_6403eb4dfa54.summary: This cluster focuses on Drell-Yan lepton-pair production at small transverse momentum, developing TMD factorization and high-order q_T resummation for precision cross-section predictions.

questions.question: How can qT-space effective-theory factorization with the collinear anomaly be matched to CSS resummation and global nonperturbative Gaussian fits across Drell-Yan and Z-boson data?
questions.rationale: The Tevatron CSS analysis favors a Gaussian nonperturbative function, while the SCET derivation relates qT-space resummation to CSS and identifies the collinear anomaly [4], [5].

questions.question: To what extent can process-independent TMD parton distributions survive the combined constraints of gauge links, soft subtraction, and transverse links at light-cone infinity across SIDIS and Drell-Yan?
questions.rationale: One-loop SIDIS factorization uses off-light-cone gauge links and soft subtraction, while final-state interactions require transverse gauge links for TMD gauge invariance [2], [3].

questions.question: Can first-subleading-twist and polarization-dependent low-transverse-momentum structure functions be incorporated consistently into precision qT resummation for Drell-Yan-like processes?
questions.rationale: The SIDIS structure-function analysis is complete through first subleading twist with polarization, motivating analogous precision extensions of low-qT factorization [1].

node_86e1b1775604.summary: These works review and develop transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions and fragmentation functions, including QCD evolution, factorization, Wilson-line structure, and nonperturbative Collins-Soper dynamics.

questions.question: Can a single TMD factorization framework with gauge-invariant light-cone Wilson lines and explicit soft subtraction describe both SIDIS and low-qT Drell-Yan while preserving the expected process dependence of gauge links?
questions.rationale: This combines the SIDIS factorization with off-light-cone gauge links and soft subtraction in [2], the transverse gauge link at light-cone infinity in [3], and the light-cone Wilson-line Drell-Yan theorem in [4].

questions.question: What nonperturbative Collins-Soper kernel and impact-parameter-space parametrization are required for QCD-evolved TMD PDFs and FFs to pass direct universality tests in spin-independent processes?
questions.rationale: This follows from the CSS-based program to build QCD-evolved TMD PDFs and FFs and test factorization in [5].

questions.question: How do first-subleading-twist TMD structure functions in polarized SIDIS evolve beyond tree level, and which observables isolate them from leading-twist contributions at low transverse momentum?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the complete tree-level SIDIS structure-function decomposition through first subleading twist with beam and target polarization in [1].

node_86e1b1775604_1.summary: This cluster emphasizes phenomenological extraction and evolution of TMD distributions across SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and small-x processes, testing universality and nonperturbative evolution kernels.

questions.question: Can a global TMD fit simultaneously describe low-transverse-momentum SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and Z-boson data while maintaining universality of the nonperturbative evolution kernel at scales near 1 GeV^2?
questions.rationale: This derives from the first simultaneous low-qT extraction using NLL TMD evolution and special low-scale prescriptions [5].

questions.question: Which spin-independent observables provide the cleanest evidence for either TMD factorization or its expected breakdown across SIDIS and hadronic multi-scale processes?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the program of QCD-evolved TMD parametrizations intended to test factorization and search for factorization breaking [3].

questions.question: How should leading- and subleading-twist SIDIS structure functions be incorporated into phenomenology without double counting soft-gluon subtraction and gauge-link effects?
questions.rationale: This connects the complete tree-level leading and first-subleading twist SIDIS decomposition [1] with the one-loop factorization formula using off-light-cone gauge links and soft subtraction [2].

node_04e01d3afdf5.summary: These papers study QCD-evolved TMD parton and fragmentation functions, including unpolarized distributions, small-x behavior, gluon TMDs, JIMWLK evolution, and their use in modern factorization analyses.

questions.question: Can global QCD-evolved TMD fits simultaneously describe spin-independent SIDIS, Drell-Yan, vector-boson qT spectra, and fragmentation data using NNLO matching coefficients with controlled nonperturbative evolution?
questions.rationale: Early CSS-based phenomenology called for reliable QCD-evolved TMD PDFs and FFs [1], while NNLO calculations provide matching coefficients for unpolarized TMD distributions and fragmentation functions [4].

questions.question: Which processes give the cleanest quantitative test of universal process-independent TMDs versus the expected breakdown of TMD factorization?
questions.rationale: QCD-evolved parametrizations were proposed both to test TMD factorization and to search for its breakdown [1], and TMD reviews highlight multi-scale collider applications [2].

node_24ddd10b31f3.summary: This cluster centers on extracting unpolarized TMD parton distributions, fragmentation functions, and Collins-Soper kernels from global fits to SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and vector-boson transverse-momentum data.

questions.question: Can one global SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and Z-boson fit extract a universal nonperturbative Collins-Soper kernel while remaining stable under low-scale TMD evolution choices near 1 GeV^2?
questions.rationale: This follows from the first global unpolarized TMD fits using NLL evolution and later fits claiming universality of nonperturbative TMD distributions and evolution kernels [3],[5].

questions.question: Which SIDIS azimuthal or spin observables fail to match between low-qT TMD factorization and high-qT collinear factorization, and what interpolation is theoretically justified in the intermediate region?
questions.rationale: This is based on the systematic study of matches and mismatches between low- and high-transverse-momentum descriptions of semi-inclusive processes [4].

questions.question: How do gauge-link definitions and soft-factor subtractions affect the universality tests of TMD PDFs and fragmentation functions across SIDIS and Drell-Yan data?
questions.rationale: This derives from the all-order SIDIS factorization framework using off-light-cone gauge links and subtracted soft-gluon radiation [2].

node_0ae86a9a3a29.summary: These works analyze gauge-invariant operator definitions of TMD parton distributions, focusing on Wilson lines, light-cone divergences, soft-factor subtraction, renormalization, and process dependence.

questions.question: Can one construct a gauge-invariant TMD operator definition with light-cone Wilson lines, transverse links at infinity, and soft-factor subtraction that is free of light-cone divergences and reduces to the integrated PDF after kT integration?
questions.rationale: This follows from the need for transverse gauge links at light-cone infinity and from the light-cone TMDPDF definition with explicit soft subtraction in Drell-Yan factorization [1,2].
