questions.rationale: This follows from the EIC energy-dependence simulations showing that transformational measurements depend strongly on energy reach [4] and from the planned polarized electron and light-ion programs [1,2].

node_998c92bfc539.summary: These papers study tensor-polarized quark and antiquark distributions in spin-one hadrons, especially deuteron structure functions such as b1 and b2 in DIS and Drell-Yan processes.

questions.question: Can forthcoming b1 data disentangle pion-exchange contributions at small x from hidden-color six-quark configurations at x > 0.2 while testing the Close-Kumano sum rule?
questions.rationale: Pionic contributions were estimated to be measurable at small x, while a 0.15 percent hidden-color six-quark component gives substantial b1 contributions at x > 0.2 and fits HERMES data [1].

questions.question: Which polarized proton-deuteron Drell-Yan structure functions provide the cleanest access to tensor-polarized antiquark distributions that cannot appear in proton-proton reactions?
questions.rationale: The spin-1 Drell-Yan formalism predicts additional tensor-polarized structure functions, including one related to b1, which are absent in spin-1/2 proton-proton reactions [4].

node_ecc186bad1d2.summary: This cluster surveys the physics goals, detector concepts, machine parameters, and theory challenges for future electron-ion colliders in the United States and China.

questions.question: What minimum energy reach and detector performance are required for EIC measurements to deliver transformational constraints on gluon-dominated nucleon and nuclear structure?
questions.rationale: The EIC detector requirements are tied to accessing gluon-dominated regions [1], and simulations show that a larger energy range enhances the chance of key scientific insights [4].

questions.question: How should polarized proton, deuteron, and helium-3 programs be coordinated across EIC, EicC, and a possible 22 GeV CEBAF upgrade to separate spin and spatial structure information?
questions.rationale: The U.S. EIC and EicC emphasize polarized beams and light ions [1],[2], while the 22 GeV CEBAF case targets nonperturbative hadron-structure dynamics [3].

questions.question: Which theory uncertainties in lepton-ion scattering most directly limit the particle-physics reach of EIC measurements beyond the traditional nuclear-physics program?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass EIC white paper frames the collider as a high-energy-physics facility with broad opportunities from its versatility, resolving power, and intensity [S1].

node_90a3da34f655.summary: This cluster studies real and virtual photon structure functions and photon parton distributions, including perturbative QCD corrections, hadronic components, heavy flavors, and resolved photon processes.

questions.question: What observable would most cleanly separate the perturbative anomalous component of the photon structure function from the nonperturbative low-mass VMD component?
questions.rationale: This follows from the decomposition of photon distributions into calculable high-mass anomalous terms and low-mass nonperturbative contributions [1].

questions.question: Can a single parametrization describe real and virtual photon PDFs smoothly in P^2 while preserving the logarithmic suppression of virtual-photon parton content in electron-initiated processes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed ansaetze for virtual photon PDFs and the observation that effective photon factorization must be modified for virtual photons [5].

questions.question: How should factorization-scheme dependence and heavy-charm thresholds be absorbed into the hadronic input so that photon structure fits remain stable beyond leading logarithms?
questions.rationale: This derives from the analysis of large MSbar terms, modified hadronic components, and charm-threshold effects in photon structure functions [3].

node_b433b5571d08.summary: This cluster examines how resonance-region electron and neutrino scattering averages reproduce partonic scaling behavior, using phenomenological models, transition form factors, and structure-function integrals.

questions.question: What kinematic averaging over W, Q2, flavor, spin, and nuclear targets would most decisively test whether local and global quark-hadron duality survive in the resonance region?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the review of global and local duality, including flavor, spin, and nuclear dependence, in [1] and the spin-structure-function tests in [5].

questions.question: What minimal dynamical conditions make coherent resonance excitation average into the incoherent partonic sum of charge squares, especially when SU(6) symmetry is broken?
questions.rationale: This derives from the square-of-sums versus sum-of-squares problem in [2] and the SU(6)-breaking duality scenarios in [4].

questions.question: Can the local-duality effective pion light-cone wave function be quantitatively connected to the suppression of higher Fock components and radiative corrections in exclusive processes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], which interprets local duality as an effective two-body pion light-cone wave function modeling soft higher-Fock dynamics.

node_485373144167.summary: This cluster centers on generalized parton distributions as probes of multidimensional hadron structure, especially through deeply virtual Compton scattering, QCD factorization, lattice calculations, and higher-order corrections.

questions.question: What experimental and theoretical inputs are sufficient to turn DVCS measurements into a quantitatively controlled three-dimensional image of quark and gluon structure rather than a model-dependent GPD extraction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the GPD reviews' emphasis on three-dimensional hadron structure, spin decomposition, modeling, QCD evolution, and phenomenological strategies [1].

questions.question: How can leading-power GPD factorization be systematically extended to the kinematics where higher-power corrections, Bethe-Heitler interference, and exclusive electroproduction effects compete with the DVCS signal?
questions.rationale: The DVCS paper compares DVCS with the Bethe-Heitler process, while the GPD overview explicitly discusses reactions at leading power accuracy and beyond [2].

questions.question: Can double distributions, nonforward distribution functions, and light-ray-operator evolution kernels be unified into phenomenological parametrizations that preserve polynomiality, form-factor sum rules, and NLO evolution constraints?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the formulations of nonforward matrix elements through double distributions and light-ray operators, including their evolution equations, kernels, and sum rules [3].

node_ca21af74f4c5.summary: This cluster develops generalized parton distribution descriptions of nucleon structure using light-front wave functions, quark-diquark and soliton models, GTMD connections, and hard exclusive reaction phenomenology.

questions.question: How can DVCS and hard exclusive meson observables be combined to extract GPDs while enforcing double-distribution spectral properties, QCD evolution, and factorization beyond leading power?
questions.rationale: The GPD and nonforward-distribution reviews connect DVCS and hard exclusive reactions to double distributions, evolution, and leading-power and beyond-leading-power factorization [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: What model-independent constraints are needed for three-dimensional nucleon tomography from impact-parameter dependent GPDs at zeta equals zero and finite skewness?
questions.rationale: GPDs are described as tools for three-dimensional hadron structure, and the zeta-to-zero limit has a direct impact-parameter interpretation [1], [3], [5].

questions.question: Can large-Nc and chiral-quark-soliton parametrizations of GPDs be tested through observables sensitive to nucleon spin structure in hard exclusive reactions?
questions.rationale: The hard-exclusive-reaction review develops large-Nc and chiral-soliton GPD parametrizations and lists observables sensitive to different GPD components [4].

node_18379dd60675.summary: This cluster focuses on representing generalized parton distributions in transverse impact-parameter space, including nonzero skewness, light-front overlap formulations, positivity constraints, and double-distribution symmetries.

questions.question: Can impact-parameter GPD probability interpretations be extended beyond xi = 0 while preserving polynomiality, positivity, and consistency with double-distribution support?
questions.rationale: Impact-parameter distributions have a probability interpretation and positivity constraints at xi = 0, while nonforward distributions and double distributions encode the more general off-forward kinematics [1,2,3].

questions.question: How can the transverse distortion encoded by the GPD E in a transversely polarized nucleon be constrained by hard exclusive measurements without violating impact-parameter positivity bounds?
questions.rationale: The impact-parameter interpretation relates E to distortions of unpolarized quark distributions in the transverse plane for transversely polarized nucleons [3].

questions.question: Can asymmetric gluon distributions used in hard diffractive electroproduction be mapped into a unified double-distribution and impact-parameter framework for nonzero momentum transfer?
questions.rationale: Hard diffractive electroproduction requires asymmetric gluon matrix elements described by double distributions rather than ordinary gluon PDFs [5].

node_18379dd60675_1.summary: This cluster studies proton generalized parton distributions at nonzero skewness using light-front and constituent quark models, with emphasis on helicity, chiral-odd structure, and transverse position dependence.

questions.question: How can the probabilistic impact-parameter interpretation at xi = 0 be generalized or constrained for nonzero skewness without losing positivity and Lorentz-invariance consistency?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which establishes probability-density and positivity properties at xi = 0, and [2], which studies the nonzero-skewness impact-parameter representation.

questions.question: Which combinations of chiral-odd GPD moments and twist-three matrix elements can be used to isolate transverse spin-orbit correlations in the proton?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4] and [5], which relate polarized transverse-plane densities, chiral-odd GPDs, equations of motion, and quark angular-momentum decomposition by transversity.

questions.question: Can the transverse deformation encoded in E and chiral-odd GPDs quantitatively predict the sign and flavor pattern of T-odd transverse-momentum distributions?
questions.rationale: The question comes from [5], which proposes a qualitative connection between transverse impact-parameter distortions and the Sivers effect.

node_78cddd1ffd62.summary: This cluster develops the formalism of nonforward, off-diagonal, skewed, and double parton distributions, including their symmetries, evolution equations, small-x behavior, and role in hard exclusive reactions.

questions.question: What experimental combination of DVCS, hard vector-meson production, and two-pion production data can most sharply test the double-distribution representation of skewed nucleon and pion GPDs?
questions.rationale: The double-distribution formalism was introduced for hard exclusive reactions, while crossing relations to two-pion production were proposed as additional constraints [1], [5].

questions.question: Can the two-component structure of skewed distributions in the regions |X| greater than xi/2 and |X| less than xi/2 be made into a quantitatively controlled model of nucleon tomography at nonzero skewness?
questions.rationale: The need to include all twist-2 structures naturally led to a two-component skewed-distribution representation [5].

node_21f51f8a43a6.summary: This cluster studies transverse-momentum-dependent and generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions in light-front, spectator, and quark models, emphasizing spin structure, Wigner functions, and unified correlator frameworks.

questions.question: Which apparent GPD-TMD relations survive when the full Wilson-line-dependent generalized parton correlation function is used, and which are irreducibly model artifacts of spectator or light-cone quark models?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the lack of model-independent GPD-TMD relations in [1,2] and the Wilson-line-induced correlator structures in [5].

questions.question: Can spectator and light-cone quark models be constrained by known unpolarized and helicity distributions strongly enough to make falsifiable predictions for T-odd TMDs, pretzelosity, and Wigner-function spin structure?
questions.rationale: This combines the spectator-model calculation with gluon rescattering in [3] and the light-cone quark-model analysis of T-even TMDs and pretzelosity in [4].

node_64d984eb9e11.summary: This cluster investigates model relations among TMDs, GPDs, GTMDs, and generalized parton correlation functions, including gluon distributions, spin-1 hadrons, and covariant or light-cone nucleon models.

questions.question: Which relations among GPDs, TMDs, and GTMDs survive once the full Wilson-line structure of the quark-quark correlator is kept, and can any be promoted beyond spectator-model artifacts?
questions.rationale: Generalized parton correlation analyses find that proposed GPD-TMD relations arise in models but do not become model-independent once the full correlator structure is classified [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: How can generalized parton correlation functions be parameterized at subleading twist so that their GPD and TMD limits preserve gauge invariance, time-reversal properties, and process dependence simultaneously?
questions.rationale: The spin-1/2 and spin-0 GPCF papers classify mother distributions and beyond-leading-twist GPDs, while the Wilson-line analysis introduces additional twist-3 time-reversal-odd structures [2], [4], [5].

questions.question: Can light-cone wave-function models that reproduce T-even TMDs and pretzelosity also reproduce the corresponding GPD and GTMD structures without violating the model-independent correlator classification?
questions.rationale: The light-cone quark model expresses leading-twist TMDs through three-quark amplitudes, while the GPCF classifications constrain which cross-relations can be universal [2], [3].

node_498defef9815.summary: This cluster focuses on subleading and higher-twist TMDs and GPDs of protons and pions, using light-front quark-diquark, spectator, and basis light-front quantization frameworks.

questions.question: Can higher-twist TMDs computed in spectator or light-front quark models be matched to a common set of light-cone amplitudes constrained by parity, time reversal, and quark orbital angular momentum?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] gives analytic spectator-model TMDs with rescattering, while [2] classifies three-quark light-cone amplitudes and connects them to twist-three distributions and orbital-motion observables.

questions.question: How large are finite-hadron-momentum mismatches between quasi-GPDs and light-cone GPDs for twist-2 and higher-twist observables, and can spectator-model estimates guide lattice-QCD extrapolations?
questions.rationale: Papers [3] and [5] calculate quasi-GPDs in a scalar diquark model and quantify their approach to standard GPDs at finite hadron momentum.

questions.question: Which measured azimuthal asymmetries in semi-inclusive lepton-nucleon scattering are most sensitive to genuine quark-gluon higher-twist dynamics rather than model-dependent transverse-momentum structure?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] identifies higher-twist TMDs as central to explaining sizable azimuthal asymmetries but emphasizes that their interpretation remains theoretically challenging.

node_9228554ed45c.summary: This cluster reviews generalized parton distributions as a framework for nucleon and nuclear structure, connecting form factors, parton densities, hard exclusive processes, spatial imaging, spin, and internal strong forces.

questions.question: What minimal global set of DVCS and hard meson electroproduction observables can separate quark and gluon GPD contributions to nucleon spin, transverse spatial imaging, and the D-term force distributions?
questions.rationale: This draws on the broad GPD program linking exclusive reactions, spin structure, three-dimensional imaging, and internal strong forces in [1,3,4].

questions.question: How can phenomenological GPD models enforce polynomiality, evolution, form-factor limits, and parton-density limits while still allowing data to determine the poorly constrained off-forward dynamics?
questions.rationale: The modeling challenge follows from the reviews of GPD properties, QCD evolution, and phenomenological status in [1,2,5].

node_6534977c24d7.summary: This cluster provides introductory and phenomenological treatments of generalized parton distributions and their experimental access through DVCS, meson production, and complementary exclusive hadron-beam reactions.

questions.question: Which minimal set of DVCS, hard meson electroproduction, and complementary exclusive observables can disentangle the quark and gluon GPD combinations controlling nucleon spin, transverse spatial structure, and mechanical moments?
questions.rationale: The reviews identify DVCS and meson production as key probes of GPDs and emphasize their roles in three-dimensional structure, spin, and mechanical properties [1], [3], [4].

questions.question: Can dual t-channel parametrizations satisfy polynomiality, Lorentz-invariance constraints, evolution, and dispersion-relation consistency while remaining flexible enough for global phenomenological fits?
questions.rationale: Dual parametrizations express GPDs through t-channel exchanges, while dispersion representations provide all-order consistency checks for models with imperfect Lorentz invariance [4], [5].

questions.question: How much GPD information is irreducibly lost when extracting real and imaginary parts of hard exclusive amplitudes beyond the Born approximation?
questions.rationale: The dispersion-representation analysis directly addresses what can be inferred about GPDs from the real and imaginary parts of exclusive amplitudes at all perturbative orders [5].

node_62f636b41e81.summary: These papers develop generalized parton distributions as a unified description of nucleon form factors, spatial parton structure, internal forces, and quark angular momentum.

questions.question: How can GPD parametrizations be simultaneously constrained by elastic form-factor sum rules, DVCS observables, and polynomiality while retaining reliable x-t correlations for nucleon tomography?
questions.rationale: The form-factor sum-rule program and empirical zero-skewness fits demonstrate strong constraints on GPD x and t dependence but also expose model dependence in tomography [2], [3], [4].

questions.question: What measurements or global fits are needed to turn the GPD D-term and related gravitational form factors into quantitative maps of pressure, shear forces, and internal stress distributions in nucleons and nuclei?
questions.rationale: The connection between hard exclusive processes and spatial distributions of strong forces motivates a direct but still incomplete extraction of internal force profiles [1].

questions.question: How robust are Ji-sum-rule extractions of u- and d-quark angular momentum against assumptions about valence-region GPD functional forms and the treatment of neutron form-factor data?
questions.rationale: Form-factor-based GPD extractions estimate valence-quark angular momentum but depend on fitted functional forms and critically assessed electromagnetic form-factor inputs [3], [5].

node_1fa55354aea8.summary: This cluster studies twist-3 and twist-2 nucleon parton distributions, especially sum rules, x=0 delta-function terms, and large-Nc chiral quark-soliton calculations.

questions.question: How robust are the fast crossovers of the isosinglet off-forward distribution H(x,xi,Delta^2) at |x|=xi/2 once 1/Nc corrections, Dirac-continuum contributions, and QCD evolution from the low soliton scale are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the strong xi-dependence and crossover behavior predicted for H in the chiral quark-soliton model, together with the level-sum treatment of quark and antiquark distributions in the pion soliton background [2,3].

questions.question: Can the pion-pole dominance of the helicity GPD E-tilde in the ERBL region be embedded in a global soliton calculation that simultaneously satisfies soft-pion theorems, axial Ward identities, and the Bjorken and momentum sum rules?
questions.rationale: The helicity skewed-distribution analysis attributes the small-Delta^2 behavior of E-tilde to chiral Ward identities and a pion pole, while the leading-twist soliton PDFs are validated through multiple sum rules [1,4].

questions.question: What observables in DVCS or related exclusive processes would most directly discriminate the large-Nc soliton antiquark flavor asymmetry from conventional parametrizations at the same low normalization point?
questions.rationale: The soliton calculations predict sizeable antiquark distributions and a Gottfried-sum-rule-violating flavor asymmetry that agree with existing low-scale phenomenology but need sharper exclusive tests [1,5].

node_510ff5a6f75b.summary: These works establish deeply virtual Compton scattering as a probe of GPDs, covering QCD factorization, evolution, higher-order corrections, small-x behavior, and fitting strategies.

questions.question: How can DVCS extractions of GPDs simultaneously enforce all-order factorization, evolution-kernel constraints, twist-three azimuthal moments, and form-factor sum rules?
questions.rationale: This derives from the original DVCS GPD framework, evolution equations, twist-three asymmetry analysis, and all-order QCD factorization proof [1], [2], [3], [4].

questions.question: What experimental and inversion precision is required for DVCS femtophotography to produce reliable real-space proton or nuclear images while retaining control of Bethe-Heitler interference?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of DVCS amplitudes for spatial imaging and from the comparison of DVCS with the accompanying Bethe-Heitler process [1], [5].

node_e0cc05d74b81.summary: This cluster focuses on extracting GPD information from DVCS and related measurements, including HERMES, CLAS, small-x, nuclear, and double-DVCS observables.

questions.question: How can global DVCS fits enforce polynomiality, analyticity, dispersion relations, skewness dependence, and realistic t-dependence while remaining flexible enough for HERMES, JLab, H1, and ZEUS data through NNLO corrections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the small-x GPD analysis and radiative-correction discussion in [2], the fitting recommendations in [4], and the flexible parametrization in [5].

questions.question: Which combination of proton, nuclear, small-x, and double-DVCS observables can break degeneracies between GPD H, the chromomagnetic-pomeron interpretation, and access to the nucleon's anomalous gravitomagnetic moment?
questions.rationale: This derives from the spatial-imaging program in [1], the small-x access to GPD H and anomalous gravitomagnetic moment in [2], and valence-region constraints reviewed in [3].

questions.question: How should femtophotographic real-space images propagate experimental amplitude uncertainties and momentum-transfer resolution into spatial images of protons and nuclei?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the DVCS femtophotography proposal, where spatial resolution is determined by momentum transfer and amplitudes are used to image targets, in [1].

node_5b2be266301a.summary: These papers develop the perturbative QCD foundations of DVCS, including scaling limits, all-order factorization, twist-three corrections, light-cone representations, and NNLO amplitudes.

questions.question: How can twist-three Fourier moments and beam-target polarization asymmetries be used to separate genuine generalized parton distributions from power corrections in precision DVCS data?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3], which develops twist-three DVCS observables and azimuthal asymmetries for accessing generalized parton distributions.

questions.question: Can all-order DVCS factorization be matched consistently to light-cone wavefunction representations so that form-factor sum rules, spin decomposition, and small-t scaling constraints are enforced in one phenomenological framework?
questions.rationale: This combines the GPD evolution and spin sum rules in [1], the all-order factorization proof in [4], and the light-cone wavefunction representation in [5].

node_bf380c451c4b.summary: This cluster examines timelike Compton scattering and exclusive lepton-pair photoproduction as complementary channels to DVCS for accessing generalized parton distributions.

questions.question: Which timelike Compton scattering angular observables most cleanly isolate the real part of the Compton amplitude in the presence of Bethe-Heitler backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal that the lepton angular distribution in gamma p to l+l- p accesses the real Compton amplitude and from the known role of Bethe-Heitler backgrounds in virtual Compton scattering [4], [5].

questions.question: Can a single generalized-parton-distribution parametrization describe both DVCS and timelike Compton scattering while respecting the soft-overlap behavior seen in form factors and wide-angle Compton scattering?
questions.rationale: This connects the claimed complementarity of TCS and DVCS with the use of nonforward parton densities or light-cone wave functions for form factors and Compton scattering [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: At what momentum transfers does exclusive Compton scattering transition from soft handbag dominance to hard-scattering sensitivity to endpoint regions of the nucleon wave function?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by studies identifying wide-angle Compton scattering as a test of soft versus hard contributions and by proposed handbag-approximation scaling tests [1], [3].

node_3e751d00ee84.summary: These works use lattice QCD to compute PDFs, GPDs, TMDs, and gluon distributions, often through LaMET and quasi-distribution methods for nucleon structure.

questions.question: Can LaMET extractions of light-front PDFs, GPDs, and wave functions be made quantitatively controlled at the moderate boosts gamma about 2-5 actually achievable on current lattices?
questions.rationale: This follows from LaMET's proposed 1/P expansion for extracting parton observables from finite-momentum Euclidean matrix elements [2] and its claim that moderate boosts may be sufficient [5].

questions.question: What lattice observables or matching strategies best separate genuine light-front parton structure from the primordial rest-frame momentum-distribution contamination present in quasi-PDFs?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the finding that quasi-PDFs have a convolutional hybrid nature and may require p3 around 3 GeV, while pseudo-PDFs and Ioffe-time distributions offer an alternative separation of z3 dependence [3].

questions.question: How large are disconnected diagrams, nonperturbative renormalization effects, and physical-pion extrapolation corrections in lattice determinations of nucleon GPD moments?
questions.rationale: This extends the limitations of a full-QCD GPD moment study that used pion masses down to 350 MeV, one-loop improved renormalization, and only connected diagrams in the isosinglet channel [4].

node_053aaa8cd880.summary: This cluster centers on extracting quark and gluon parton distribution functions from lattice QCD using LaMET, quasi-PDFs, physical-pion ensembles, and perturbative matching.

questions.question: What hadron boost, nonlocal-operator separation, and matching accuracy are required for quasi-PDFs to reach controlled light-front PDF limits on present lattice ensembles?
questions.rationale: This follows from LaMET's large-momentum expansion and the observation that quasi-PDFs may need p3 around 3 GeV to approach the PDF limit [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: Can pseudo-PDF and Ioffe-time methods remove rest-frame and Wilson-line artifacts more reliably than quasi-PDFs for extracting small-x and large-x behavior?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the proposal to use pseudo-PDFs and Ioffe-time distributions to divide out problematic z3 dependence in quasi-PDFs [3].

questions.question: How should lattice-QCD PDF calculations be benchmarked against global-analysis moments and distributions so that systematic errors from finite momentum, matching, and lattice spacing are comparable across methods?
questions.rationale: This derives from the community white paper's call for benchmark numbers linking lattice-QCD calculations and global PDF analyses [5].

node_082892f5a89c.summary: These papers compute nucleon generalized parton distributions and polarized parton distributions on the lattice, including unpolarized, helicity, and transversity channels.

questions.question: How can lattice calculations of nucleon GPD moments incorporate disconnected isosinglet diagrams, nonperturbative renormalization, and physical pion masses without losing control of generalized form-factor signals at large t?
questions.rationale: This follows from the full-QCD GPD-moment study that included only connected isosinglet diagrams and used one-loop renormalization, and from the overdetermined-observable method for large-t generalized form factors [1],[2].

questions.question: Can LaMET calculations of helicity and transversity PDFs at larger nucleon momentum settle the antiquark and sea-flavor asymmetries predicted from current finite-momentum lattice data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the first LaMET calculation of polarized isovector PDFs and its discussion of antiquark structure and transversely polarized sea-flavor asymmetry [3].

questions.question: How consistently do lattice moments of GPDs and light-cone quark distributions account for the total quark spin and orbital angular momentum contribution to the proton spin?
questions.rationale: This derives from the quenched GPD moment study assessing total quark angular momentum and the full-QCD moments of density, helicity, and transversity distributions [4],[5].

node_9af0b03b29e7.summary: This cluster studies pion parton structure using continuum models, chiral quark models, lattice QCD, quasi-distributions, and GPD frameworks.

questions.question: How can Drell-Yan, leading-neutron electroproduction, lattice current correlators, and future EIC data be combined to determine pion sea and gluon PDFs at small x without model-dominated chiral-splitting uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the parameter-free small-x pion predictions [1], the Monte Carlo global analysis including HERA leading neutrons [5], and the EIC motivation in [4].

questions.question: Does threshold resummation remain sufficient to reconcile high-x pion valence PDFs with perturbative-QCD counting rules once modern global fits include lower-x constraints and lattice position-space distribution-amplitude information?
questions.rationale: The high-x softening from NLL threshold resummation [2] motivates combining it with global pion PDFs [5] and position-space lattice correlators for pion distribution amplitudes [3].

node_d99c8127bb09.summary: These works model and extract pion and kaon parton distribution functions, emphasizing valence structure, gluon and sea generation, light-front dynamics, and QCD evolution.

questions.question: Can a combined global analysis of pion-nucleus Drell-Yan and leading-neutron electroproduction determine whether the high-x pion valence PDF is genuinely softer once threshold resummation is included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the NLL threshold-resummed Drell-Yan extraction in [2] and the Monte Carlo global fit combining Drell-Yan with HERA leading-neutron data in [4].

questions.question: How can future pion and kaon measurements separate dynamical sea and gluon generation from model dependence in chiral splitting functions and low-scale light-front wave functions?
questions.rationale: The question combines the parameter-free dynamical pion sea/gluon construction in [1], the chiral-splitting uncertainty in [4], and the light-front Hamiltonian input-scale approach in [5].

questions.question: What observable set at an Electron-Ion Collider would most directly test whether the kaon marks the transition between strong-interaction and Higgs-generated mass mechanisms in meson structure?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the EIC perspective on pion and kaon mass budgets and the special role of the kaon in [3].

node_8e594fcaab2a.summary: This cluster develops pion generalized parton distribution models using chiral quark, Dyson-Schwinger, double-distribution, and impact-parameter approaches with QCD constraints.

questions.question: Can pion GPD models enforce polynomiality, positivity, soft-pion theorems, and nonfactorized t dependence while retaining the gluon binding contributions missing from impulse approximations?
questions.rationale: Chiral quark models achieve polynomiality and other constraints through covariant double distributions [1], whereas the Dyson-Schwinger analysis argues that impulse-approximation GPDs omit essential binding-gluon contributions [5].

questions.question: Which experimentally or lattice-accessible observables can discriminate whether the large-t pion form factor and x -> 1 valence distribution are controlled by the same one-gluon-exchange short-distance mechanism across covariant and light-front GPD models?
questions.rationale: The question follows from comparisons of covariant and light-front constituent models that infer a common short-distance mechanism for the electromagnetic form factor at large momentum transfer and the PDF near x = 1 [3].

node_0ccbfcaae902.summary: These papers compute pion and kaon distribution amplitudes and valence PDFs from lattice QCD using LaMET, current-current correlators, continuum extrapolations, and nonperturbative renormalization.

questions.question: Can position-space current-current correlators and LaMET extractions be made quantitatively consistent for the pion distribution amplitude once NNLO kernels, twist-4 corrections, Wilson-line renormalization, and finite-momentum mass corrections are controlled together?
questions.rationale: This combines the position-space NNLO plus twist-4 strategy of [1] with the LaMET pion-DA calculation including all-order m_pi^2/P_z^2 corrections and Wilson-line renormalization [2].

questions.question: Which lattice systematics dominate the current large-x discrepancy in direct LaMET calculations of the pion valence PDF, and can coordinate-space current-current methods isolate the same artifacts?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reported agreement at small x but sizeable large-x discrepancy in the first direct LaMET pion-PDF calculation and the complementary current-current approach proposed for valence PDFs [4],[5].

questions.question: How do continuum extrapolation, nonperturbative renormalization, and physical light- and strange-quark masses shift the Gegenbauer moments of pion and kaon distribution amplitudes relative to early O(a)-improved Wilson-fermion determinations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the lattice extraction of a_2^pi, a_1^K, and a_2^K using nonperturbative renormalization and mass extrapolations [3].

node_813900a345f1.summary: This cluster develops QCD renormalization and evolution kernels for light-ray, twist-three, twist-four, singlet, nonsinglet, and skewed parton operators using conformal symmetry and perturbative methods.

questions.question: Can conformal Ward identity methods determine the full off-diagonal anomalous-dimension matrices and ERBL kernels for singlet and nonsinglet light-ray operators beyond the two-loop order where broken conformal invariance is already constrained?
questions.rationale: This extends the conformal-consistency construction of two-loop off-diagonal anomalous dimensions and NLO exclusive evolution kernels from conformal anomalies [3].

questions.question: Which three-particle twist-three QCD evolution Hamiltonians remain integrable away from the large-Nc or multicolour limits, and can the non-integrable gluonic addenda be organized into controlled corrections to the spin-chain spectrum?
questions.rationale: This follows from the integrable XXX spin-chain structure found for baryon and quark-gluon evolution equations [2] and the partially non-integrable pure-gluon twist-three sector [4].

questions.question: Can quasiclassical expansions in total conformal spin be made accurate enough to predict the fine structure of anomalous dimensions for phenomenologically relevant multiparton correlators entering polarized structure functions and asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the use of quasiclassical methods and integrals of motion to resolve the spectrum of quark-gluon twist-three operators, including the chiral-odd sector [5].

node_59cbf27c99d1.summary: These works address global determinations of proton and nuclear parton distribution functions, including uncertainties, nuclear shadowing, and constraints from DIS, Drell-Yan, RHIC, Tevatron, and LHC data.

questions.question: What common validation standard should determine whether Hessian eigenvector fits, dynamic tolerance procedures, and neural-network closure-tested PDFs give reliable uncertainties for precision LHC and EIC predictions?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the CTEQ Hessian eigenvector uncertainty program, MSTW dynamic eigenvector procedure, and NNPDF closure-test methodology [1].

questions.question: Which data tensions should be treated as evidence for underestimated systematics, missing QCD theory ingredients, or genuine PDF shape freedom in global fits?
questions.rationale: The CT10 analysis explicitly found difficulty fitting both D0 Run-II W lepton asymmetry data and fixed-target DIS data, leading to alternate PDF families [4].

questions.question: What theoretical and computational advances are needed to make N2LO and N3LO global PDF analyses routine while incorporating heavy-quark, strange, photon, small-x, and LHC constraints consistently?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Snowmass precision-frontier goals for N2LO and N3LO PDFs and the xFitter survey of strange PDFs, photon PDFs, small-x resummation, and heavy-quark production [S1].

node_5701b418ccae.summary: This cluster focuses on major proton PDF fits such as MSTW, MMHT, MSHT, CTEQ, and NNPDF, emphasizing global datasets and precision LHC phenomenology.

questions.question: What dataset and theory ingredients are required before global proton PDFs can be delivered consistently at N3LO accuracy for HL-LHC and EIC precision observables?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Snowmass precision-frontier target of N2LO and N3LO PDF infrastructure in [S1].

questions.question: How should correlated systematic uncertainties, Hessian eigenvector tolerances, and closure-tested neural-network methods be compared on common pseudo-data to quantify methodological PDF uncertainty?
questions.rationale: The question combines correlated-systematic Hessian methods in [1], dynamic eigenvector uncertainties in [2], and closure-test validation in [3].

questions.question: Which tensions between W lepton asymmetry, fixed-target DIS, strange-quark constraints, jet data, and top production should define the next generation of global-fit stress tests?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the CT10/CT10W tension in [4] and the LHC-era datasets constraining strange, jets, vector bosons, and top production in [2], [3], and [5].

node_24e520384dc6.summary: These papers update, compare, and benchmark modern PDF sets for collider predictions, assessing their parametrizations, uncertainties, and impact on precision Standard Model calculations.

questions.question: Which discrepancies among modern global PDF sets are driven by data selection, parametrization flexibility, heavy-quark treatment, or uncertainty propagation rather than by genuine experimental tension?
questions.rationale: The comparison problem is motivated by MSTW dynamic eigenvectors [1], NNPDF closure-tested methodology [2], and the CT10/CT10W split caused by W asymmetry data [3].

questions.question: What validation standard should replace or extend PDF4LHC combinations when HL-LHC predictions require N2LO or N3LO PDF accuracy?
questions.rationale: PDF4LHC Run II provides a combined prescription [5], while the Snowmass precision-frontier report identifies N2LO and N3LO PDFs as a future requirement [S1].

questions.question: How can open QCD fitting frameworks consistently propagate correlated systematics from LHC vector-boson, jet, W+c, top, and forward data into strange, gluon, and flavor-separated PDFs?
questions.rationale: NNPDF2.3 and NNPDF3.0 use these LHC datasets to constrain PDFs [2,4], and xFitter highlights open-source analyses of strange, photon, heavy-quark, and small-x effects [S2].

node_1cf9cd2138a1.summary: This cluster reviews PDF determinations and PDF4LHC recommendations, highlighting how proton structure uncertainties affect Run I, Run II, HL-LHC, and future collider measurements.

questions.question: What common validation standard should determine whether closure-tested Monte Carlo PDFs, Hessian combinations, and PDF4LHC prescriptions are adequate for HL-LHC precision measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from NNPDF closure testing, PDF4LHC combined-set recommendations, and the Snowmass need for precision-frontier PDF methodology [1][3][S1].

questions.question: Which new collider datasets most reduce disagreement in charm, gluon, and forward-region PDFs without introducing hidden tensions among global fits?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the inclusion of LHC W/Z, jet, W+c, top, forward LHCb data, and fitted charm PDFs in modern NNPDF determinations [2][4].

questions.question: How should PDF access tools prevent silent misuse of concurrent PDF sets, metadata, and uncertainty prescriptions as precision-collider workflows scale?
questions.rationale: The question derives from LHAPDF6's redesign to remove multi-set and metadata failure modes that could silently produce incorrect results [5].

node_80b77afcddca.summary: These works combine H1 and ZEUS inclusive deep-inelastic scattering cross sections and use them, often with ABM or HERAPDF analyses, to extract PDFs, alpha_s, and heavy-quark parameters.

questions.question: Where does the combined HERA inclusive DIS dataset most strongly discriminate between dynamical valence-like low-scale PDF inputs and conventional global-fit parametrizations?
questions.rationale: The dynamical PDF program in [1] is tested against small-x DIS data, while [2] provides the combined H1 and ZEUS inclusive cross sections used in modern QCD fits.

questions.question: How much do heavy-quark mass schemes and fitted MSbar masses shift alpha_s and benchmark LHC cross sections when the same HERA inclusive data are analyzed in ABM-style fixed-flavor fits versus other PDF frameworks?
questions.rationale: ABMP16 and ABM11 extract PDFs, alpha_s, and heavy-quark masses at NNLO using fixed-flavor schemes and HERA data in [4] and [5].

questions.question: Can open-source xFitter workflows make the treatment of correlated HERA systematics, heavy-quark production, and small-x resummation transparent enough to identify the source of PDF-set disagreements?
questions.rationale: The HERA combination in [2] depends on correlated systematic uncertainties, and [S1] highlights xFitter applications to heavy quarks, strange PDFs, and small-x resummation.

node_ccb80ff5163f.summary: This cluster traces CTEQ and related global QCD PDF fits, incorporating DIS, jet, vector-boson, Tevatron, and LHC data to refine parton distributions for collider physics.

questions.question: What single global-fit criterion should decide whether internally tense data sets, such as W lepton asymmetry and fixed-target DIS, are included, reweighted, or split into alternative PDF families?
questions.rationale: CT10 and CT10W were both released because the D0 Run-II W lepton asymmetry data were difficult to fit simultaneously with some fixed-target DIS data [2].

questions.question: How much of the current uncertainty in LHC standard-candle predictions is driven by heavy-flavor treatment, especially the shift between zero-mass and general-mass schemes?
questions.rationale: CTEQ6.6 found increased W and Z cross sections in the general-mass scheme compared with the zero-mass scheme and studied the resulting collider uncertainties [4].

questions.question: Can more flexible PDF parametrizations and correlated LHC data reduce flavor-separation ambiguities without hiding real tensions among strange, d/u, jet, and vector-boson constraints?
questions.rationale: CT14 introduced LHC data, D0 lepton asymmetry data, and more flexible parametrizations to better fit different quark-flavor combinations [5].

node_05a571e82bdf.summary: These papers develop quantum-statistical parametrizations of unpolarized, polarized, and transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions and test them against DIS, Drell-Yan, jet, and spin-asymmetry data.

questions.question: Which high-x flavor and helicity measurements would most decisively test the statistical parton model predictions for dbar/ubar and a large positive gluon helicity distribution?
questions.rationale: The statistical approach predicts the dbar/ubar behavior probed by W production and highlights confirmation of a large positive gluon helicity as a key challenge [1], [3].

questions.question: Can transverse-momentum-dependent statistical PDFs with Melosh-Wigner rotation describe semi-inclusive DIS cross sections and double longitudinal-spin asymmetries without introducing many additional parameters?
questions.rationale: The TMD extension of statistical PDFs includes Melosh-Wigner effects and was compared with semi-inclusive DIS data and spin asymmetries [4].

node_f94dffcac618.summary: This cluster develops methods for estimating and propagating PDF uncertainties, including Hessian approaches, experimental covariance treatments, and missing higher-order theory uncertainties.

questions.question: What common benchmark would reveal when Hessian eigenvector propagation ceases to approximate the full PDF uncertainty for collider observables?
questions.rationale: The CTEQ and MRST uncertainty studies rely on Hessian eigenvector methods while checking limitations against Lagrange-multiplier approaches [1,3,4].

questions.question: How should correlated experimental systematics and tolerance choices be defined so that global PDF uncertainty bands have a statistically interpretable meaning across incompatible data sets?
questions.rationale: The new-generation CTEQ analysis emphasizes full correlated systematic-error treatment and pragmatic uncertainty definitions in global QCD fits [1].

questions.question: Can Bayesian constrained-fitting ideas provide a controlled alternative to Hessian PDF uncertainty estimates in highly constrained or poorly linearized PDF directions?
questions.rationale: The constrained curve-fitting paper motivates Bayesian methods that may address limitations of conventional linear error propagation [5].

node_df14eafc62b4.summary: These works study heavy-quark mass effects and fixed- versus variable-flavor-number schemes in DIS and global PDF fits, including their consequences for LHC cross-section predictions.

questions.question: What observable combination of DIS charm data and LHC cross sections most sharply distinguishes fixed-flavor, zero-mass variable-flavor, and general-mass variable-flavor treatments of charm and bottom mass effects?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark mass choices alter PDFs and LHC predictions in global NNPDF fits [2], while NNLO analyses compare fixed-flavor PDFs with matched 4- and 5-flavor GMVFN results [3].

questions.question: Can NNLO flavor-threshold matching be formulated so that discontinuities in PDFs and alpha_s are minimized or made diagnostically useful while all physical structure functions remain continuous across Q^2 = m_Q^2?
questions.rationale: This derives from the NNLO VFNS construction in which PDFs can be discontinuous at flavor transitions even though physical quantities remain continuous [5].

node_aba4177960d2.summary: This cluster determines photon and lepton parton distributions in the proton and incorporates QED corrections into DGLAP evolution for precision LHC phenomenology.

questions.question: What residual uncertainty in the photon PDF remains when one replaces direct global fitting by structure-function determinations based on F2 and FL, and how does it propagate to high-mass dilepton and W-pair production?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between NNPDF-style photon-PDF fitting and the model-independent LUX-type determination from electron-proton structure functions [1], [4], [5].

questions.question: At what precision do QED-induced isospin violation and photon-initiated subprocesses become limiting systematics in global proton PDF fits?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the finding that QED DGLAP evolution generates up-down isospin violation and a photon distribution with phenomenological consequences [2].

questions.question: How should NNLO QCD plus QED evolution libraries treat heavy-quark thresholds and photon contributions so that different photon-PDF determinations remain mutually comparable?
questions.rationale: This derives from APFEL's coupled QCD+QED evolution with variable flavor number schemes and heavy-quark mass choices [3].

node_70e6c7294ed3.summary: These papers develop NNPDF-style Monte Carlo neural-network determinations of nucleon parton distribution functions with unbiased parametrizations and faithful uncertainty estimates for DIS and collider data.

questions.question: How can neural-network PDF fits quantify whether observed deviations in complex LHC final states reflect PDF uncertainty, alpha_s and scale variation, or genuine Standard Model tension?
questions.rationale: This follows from NNPDF2.0's dataset-impact and normalization-uncertainty treatment in [1] and the APPLGRID and fastNLO tools for a posteriori PDF, alpha_s, and scale variation in [2] and [4].

questions.question: What validation tests ensure that neural-network PDF parametrizations remain unbiased while faithfully propagating experimental correlations from DIS to global collider observables?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Monte Carlo neural-network uncertainty method in [3] and the structure-function error-correlation parametrization introduced in [5].

node_c39b33feb68c.summary: These works perform global QCD analyses of nuclear parton distribution functions, incorporating DIS, Drell-Yan, RHIC, and LHC proton-nucleus data to quantify nuclear modifications and uncertainties.

questions.question: What minimal combination of DIS, Drell-Yan, inclusive pion, and proton-lead observables would decisively test whether conventional collinear factorization is the right organizing framework for nuclear PDF extractions?
questions.rationale: This follows from EPS09 finding that DIS, Drell-Yan, and RHIC pion data can be described in collinear factorization, while EPPS16 extended the same framework to LHC proton-lead data [1].

questions.question: Can global fits separate genuine flavor-dependent nuclear modifications from parametrization choices once LHC, neutrino DIS, and pion-nucleus Drell-Yan data are included?
questions.rationale: EPPS16 emphasizes that adding new data allows much more freedom in flavor dependence and makes uncertainty estimates more objective [3].

node_c39b33feb68c_1.summary: This cluster centers on modern NLO and NNLO nPDF extractions such as EPS, EPPS, and nCTEQ, emphasizing heavy-flavor schemes, nuclear corrections, and uncertainty propagation across nuclear targets.

questions.question: What new data would most reduce the still-large nuclear gluon and high-x antiquark uncertainties in global nPDF fits?
questions.rationale: Early NLO analyses found valence quarks relatively well determined but gluon modifications and high-x antiquarks poorly constrained [4].

questions.question: Can LHC proton-lead data and neutrino-nucleus DIS establish flavor-dependent nuclear modifications without overfitting tensions among experimental inputs?
questions.rationale: EPPS16 added LHC pPb, neutrino-nucleus DIS, and pion-nucleus Drell-Yan data while allowing more freedom in flavor dependence and more objective uncertainties [2].

questions.question: How should Hessian uncertainty tolerances and eigenvector rescalings be standardized so that EPS, EPPS, and nCTEQ nuclear-PDF uncertainties can be compared process by process?
questions.rationale: nCTEQ15 emphasizes Hessian uncertainties with optimized eigenvector rescaling and correlations of data sets with individual nPDF flavor components [3].

node_6a8d731e0c8b.summary: These papers examine how the EMC effect signals modifications of bound nucleon structure and how its size correlates with short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations and high-momentum nuclear components.

questions.question: What single experimental pattern would decide whether the EMC-SRC correlation is caused by high-virtuality nucleons in short-range pairs rather than by another nuclear modification mechanism?
questions.rationale: This broad test follows from the reviewed claim that highly virtual nucleons in SRC pairs drive the EMC effect and from the lack of a generally accepted explanation [1,5].

questions.question: How universal is the modification of proton and neutron structure in SRC pairs across nuclei once simultaneous high-precision EMC and SRC measurements are extended beyond the currently measured systems?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the reported simultaneous EMC/SRC measurements and their interpretation in terms of universal modification of nucleons in correlated pairs [4].

questions.question: Can the linear EMC-SRC relation be used to extract F2n/F2p with controlled deuteron corrections over the intermediate-x region 0.35 <= xB <= 0.7?
questions.rationale: This follows from the quantitative linear relation used to infer the deuteron-to-free-pn ratio, free neutron DIS cross section, and F2n/F2p [3].

node_78c69a39362c.summary: This cluster covers phenomenological and DGLAP-based models of nuclear modifications to quark and gluon distributions, including shadowing, recombination, Fermi motion, and correlated-nucleon effects.

questions.question: What new data or observable combination would most sharply separate leading-twist DGLAP nuclear shadowing from parametrization artifacts in small-x antiquark and gluon nuclear distributions?
questions.rationale: Small-x distributions, medium-x antiquarks, and gluons remained weakly determined or functional-form dependent in the global nuclear fits of [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can correlated heavy-flavor lepton-pair production in pA collisions be made precise enough experimentally and theoretically to serve as a direct constraint on R_g^A across SPS, RHIC, and LHC kinematics?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark decay lepton-pair ratios in pA versus pp were proposed as a direct proxy for the nuclear gluon modification R_g^A because production is dominated by gg fusion [5].

node_5f8aadf05eef.summary: These works study nonperturbative flavor asymmetries in the nucleon sea, especially the observed excess of anti-down over anti-up quarks and its interpretation through meson-cloud, chiral, and phenomenological models.

questions.question: What measurements over small, intermediate, and large x can determine whether the suggested sign change in dbar-ubar is real and whether meson-cloud dynamics is its dominant origin?
questions.rationale: The sign-changing sea-quark distributions found in the CTEQ analysis [1] and the E866 comparison to virtual-meson models [5] motivate this question.

questions.question: Can physical-pion-mass lattice QCD quantitatively reproduce both Gottfried-sum violation and the helicity ordering Delta ubar > Delta dbar seen in phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This extends the qualitative lattice observation of dbar > ubar and Delta ubar > Delta dbar at heavy pion mass in [4] toward the experimental and review context of [2].

node_5f8aadf05eef_1.summary: This cluster focuses on quark-antiquark and flavor symmetry breaking in the light and strange nucleon sea, connecting DIS and Drell-Yan measurements to meson-cloud and chiral model explanations.

questions.question: What measurement would most decisively distinguish meson-cloud and chiral explanations of the observed dbar-ubar asymmetry from alternative mechanisms such as Pauli blocking, isospin violation, or nuclear corrections?
questions.rationale: The flavor-asymmetry review lists these competing mechanisms, while E866 Drell-Yan data support virtual-meson contributions to dbar-ubar [1,4].

questions.question: Can lattice QCD reproduce the x dependence and helicity pattern of the light antiquark sea at physical pion mass well enough to connect the Gottfried sum violation with STAR spin data?
questions.rationale: The lattice calculation already observes dbar greater than ubar and Delta ubar greater than Delta dbar at pion mass 310 MeV, qualitatively consistent with experimental indications [3].

questions.question: How much of the nucleon sea flavor asymmetry is carried by connected backward-time quark propagation, and can this mechanism be isolated in phenomenological PDF fits?
questions.rationale: The Euclidean path-integral analysis attributes the Gottfried-sum violation to connected insertions involving backward-time propagation rather than disconnected quark loops [5].

node_edf7471e486c.summary: These papers analyze the anti-down to anti-up asymmetry in the proton sea using Drell-Yan and DIS data, comparing measurements with chiral, Pauli-blocking, and other nonperturbative nucleon-structure models.

questions.question: What Drell-Yan or DIS measurement at small and large x would most directly reconcile the E866 dbar/ubar and dbar-minus-ubar results with the Gottfried-sum-rule violation, including deuteron shadowing uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The review highlights small-x and deuteron nuclear corrections, while E866 provides the key Drell-Yan extraction of dbar/ubar and its integral [1].

questions.question: Can physical-pion-mass lattice QCD reproduce both dbar greater than ubar and Delta ubar greater than Delta dbar in a way that quantitatively matches E866 and STAR observables?
questions.rationale: The lattice study found qualitative Gottfried-sum-rule violation and polarized sea ordering at pion mass 310 MeV [2].

questions.question: How can meson-cloud, chiral, and Pauli-blocking pictures be experimentally separated from the connected backward-time quark-line mechanism for the light-antiquark flavor asymmetry?
questions.rationale: The review catalogs nonperturbative model explanations, while the path-integral analysis attributes the Gottfried-sum-rule violation to connected insertions with backward time propagation [4].

node_6adbc9fe0e9d.summary: This cluster investigates possible differences between strange and antistrange parton distributions in the nucleon and their implications for the NuTeV anomaly and electroweak parameter extraction.

questions.question: How can the x-dependent strange-antistrange momentum and helicity distributions be decomposed into an intrinsic meson-baryon component and the universal three-loop QCD evolution contribution seeded by nonzero up- and down-valence densities?
questions.rationale: This follows from the tension between the light-cone meson-baryon prediction of intrinsic strange momentum and helicity asymmetries in [1] and the purely perturbative three-loop generation of s(x)-sbar(x) in [2].

questions.question: Can a single low-scale matching framework consistently connect dynamical chiral symmetry breaking, intrinsic parton transverse momentum correlations, and the collinear strange sea asymmetry after QCD evolution?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [3], which matches chiral quark-soliton parton distributions at the scale rho^{-2}, together with [2], where evolution generates a sizable strange-antistrange asymmetry.

questions.question: What constraints on K-meson cloud form factors and meson-nucleon cutoffs are required for virtual meson cloud models to reproduce both strange sea asymmetry and the observed low-x antiquark behavior?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4], which studies pi and K cloud contributions, singlet versus non-singlet evolution, and cutoff scales, and [5], which notes failures of strange-distribution meson-cloud calculations in the low-x region.

node_de4fea192b7e.summary: These works constrain the strange quark and antiquark PDFs through global QCD fits using neutrino dimuon production, charm-tagged DIS, HERA data, and LHC vector-boson measurements.

questions.question: What combination of neutrino dimuon, charm-tagged DIS, HERA, LHC vector-boson, and semi-inclusive DIS data can resolve whether the strange sea is suppressed for x greater than about 0.01 or enhanced in collider W and Z production?
questions.rationale: This targets the tension between strange suppression found in simultaneous PDF-fragmentation-function fits and the ATLAS-enhanced-strangeness interpretation mentioned in [5].

questions.question: How much of the inferred strange-antistrange shape and normalization is driven by heavy-quark factorization choices in neutrino DIS versus experimental constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of massive factorization schemes for charm structure functions and general-mass CTEQ analyses of strange PDFs [3],[4].

questions.question: Can global fits determine s(x) and sbar(x) with enough uncertainty control to make electroweak quantities such as |V_cd|, |V_cs|, and NuTeV-like parameters insensitive to strange-PDF modeling assumptions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the NNPDF dimuon analysis that used strange and antistrange uncertainties to reassess electroweak parameter determinations [2].

node_1e44d540c173.summary: This cluster studies nuclear shadowing of structure functions at small Bjorken x using multiple scattering, Glauber-Gribov theory, dipole formalisms, and high-density QCD approaches.

questions.question: Can leading-twist nuclear shadowing be formulated in a single global analysis that consistently combines Gribov-Glauber diffraction, DGLAP evolution, off-shell nucleon effects, and high-density QCD limits?
questions.rationale: The supplied papers compare multiple shadowing mechanisms, global nuclear-structure fits, and leading-twist diffraction-based shadowing in hard nuclear processes [1,2,3].

questions.question: Which future diffractive DIS or proton-nucleus observable would best separate gluon shadowing from final-state rescattering effects in the interpretation of small-x nuclear structure functions?
questions.rationale: Structure functions are argued not to be simple parton probabilities because rescattering of outgoing quarks produces leading-twist shadowing and diffraction [5].

questions.question: At what energies do coherent mini-jet diffraction and hard diffraction in nuclei become leading-twist probes rather than higher-twist corrections to color transparency?
questions.rationale: Coherent diffractive dijet production predicts A^2 scaling with A^(7/3) multiple-scattering corrections and a reappearance of hard diffractive shadowing at TeV energies [4].

node_bea9d8438023.summary: These papers develop and apply leading-twist, Glauber-Gribov, and color-dipole descriptions of nuclear shadowing, linking HERA diffraction constraints to hard scattering processes with nuclei.

questions.question: Can leading-twist nuclear shadowing, constrained by HERA diffraction and QCD factorization, produce a quantitatively unique gluon shadowing prediction for future hard processes with nuclei?
questions.rationale: The leading-twist framework combines Gribov-Glauber theory, QCD factorization, and HERA diffractive DIS to predict sea-quark and gluon nuclear shadowing [2].

questions.question: Which measurements best discriminate Glauber rescattering, Gribov inelastic shadowing, and high-density QCD pictures in the small-x nuclear structure-function regime?
questions.rationale: The nuclear-shadowing review presents these three related approaches and compares their phenomenological consequences [1].

questions.question: Does the delayed onset of gluon shadowing implied by nonperturbative quark-gluon interactions survive when confronted with coherent hard diffraction and mini-jet production over a wide nuclear-mass range?
questions.rationale: Nonperturbative gluon-radiation modeling predicts weaker and delayed gluon shadowing, while coherent nuclear diffractive mini-jet production probes color transparency and leading-twist shadowing [3,5].

node_eac2df74be32.summary: These papers study nuclear modifications of deep inelastic structure functions, especially shadowing and antishadowing at small Bjorken x in charged-lepton and neutrino scattering.

questions.question: What combination of charged-lepton and neutrino nuclear DIS data can isolate whether nuclear antishadowing is process dependent rather than a universal modification of nuclear PDFs?
questions.rationale: The Gribov-Glauber treatment predicts different antishadowing for charged and neutral current reactions, with consequences for extracting the weak mixing angle [3].

questions.question: Can a single phenomenological framework reconcile off-shell corrections, pion excess, Fermi motion, and coherent shadowing while preserving Adler and Gross-Llewellyn-Smith sum-rule constraints in neutrino scattering?
questions.rationale: The nuclear-structure-function analyses combine these nuclear effects for charged-lepton and neutrino DIS and explicitly test neutrino sum rules and PCAC effects [1,4].

questions.question: At what x, Q^2, and A does nuclear-enhanced power-correction resummation become experimentally distinguishable from purely diffractive or eikonal explanations of shadowing?
questions.rationale: Power-correction resummation describes the x-, Q^2-, and A-dependence of F2A and FL A, while the eikonal picture ties shadowing to final-state diffractive rescattering rather than intrinsic nuclear wave functions [2,5].

node_5e5a65a4e84f.summary: This cluster concerns theoretical, phenomenological, and global-PDF evidence for nonperturbative charm and other intrinsic heavy-quark components in the proton.

questions.question: What combination of DIS charm data, collider charm production, and global PDF constraints would decisively distinguish a light-cone-like intrinsic charm distribution from a sea-like charm distribution in the proton?
questions.rationale: Global analyses allow both model-shaped and sea-like intrinsic charm components with bounds ranging from zero to above older model estimates [1].

questions.question: Can the EMC charm-production excess be reanalyzed with modern NLO extrinsic charm calculations and correlated systematics well enough to decide whether it is genuine evidence for intrinsic charm?
questions.rationale: The NLO comparison of extrinsic and intrinsic contributions to F2 found evidence for intrinsic charm in the EMC DIS data [2].

questions.question: Are leading versus nonleading D-meson asymmetries at high x_F and low p_T best explained by coalescence from intrinsic heavy-quark Fock states, or can factorized fragmentation be restored with improved hadronization modeling?
questions.rationale: The observed leading charm asymmetries violate the usual fragmentation-factorization assumption and were modeled using intrinsic heavy-quark Fock-state coalescence [5].

node_80a5af9f09fc.summary: These works develop and compare Sivers, Collins, TMD, and twist-three descriptions of transverse single-spin asymmetries across SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and hadronic collisions.

questions.question: What decisive measurement would establish the predicted sign reversal of the Sivers asymmetry between SIDIS and Drell-Yan as a breakdown of naive TMD universality rather than a process-dependent modeling artifact?
questions.rationale: This follows from Collins' argument that the gauge-link structure permits a Sivers asymmetry and requires its sign reversal between SIDIS and hadron-induced hard processes [4].

questions.question: How can Collins fragmentation, Sivers distributions, and final-state-interaction phases be disentangled experimentally in azimuthal single-spin asymmetries with polarized targets and identified hadrons?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Collins fragmentation mechanism, the tree-level azimuthal-asymmetry formalism, and the final-state-interaction explanation of large HERMES and SMC asymmetries [1].

questions.question: Can twist-2 TMD descriptions and order-1/Q polarized leptoproduction calculations be matched consistently in the kinematic regions used to extract transverse single-spin asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the twist-2 spin-dependent fragmentation function and the complete tree-level calculation of polarized leptoproduction through order 1/Q with transverse-momentum dependence [2].

node_c30ee9cb542c.summary: This cluster focuses on phenomenological descriptions of azimuthal and transverse single-spin asymmetries in inclusive and semi-inclusive hard scattering processes.

questions.question: What combined SIDIS and Drell-Yan measurement would be decisive for the predicted sign reversal of the Sivers asymmetry from the gauge-link structure of T-odd parton distributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the path-ordered-exponential origin and predicted sign reversal in [4], together with the T-odd leptoproduction asymmetries of [3].

questions.question: Can Collins fragmentation and Sivers distribution effects be separated model-independently in azimuthal single-spin asymmetries with polarized targets and unpolarized lepton beams?
questions.rationale: The question connects the spin-dependent fragmentation function of [1] with the full tree-level polarized leptoproduction structure in [2].

questions.question: How can final-state interaction phases be related quantitatively to proton spin-flip amplitudes and the anomalous magnetic moment while remaining leading twist at fixed x_Bj?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the final-state interaction mechanism and its relation to spin-flip amplitudes and the anomalous magnetic moment in [5].

node_22e67ead7795.summary: These papers analyze single transverse-spin asymmetries in Drell-Yan, SIDIS, photon, and hadron production using collinear twist-three quark-gluon and gluon correlation functions.

questions.question: How precisely can the predicted SIDIS-to-Drell-Yan sign reversal of the Sivers function be tested once twist-three quark-gluon correlations and TMD factorization are matched in the intermediate-q_perp region?
questions.rationale: This combines the non-universality and sign-reversal argument of [1] with the twist-three/TMD overlap relation established in [4].

questions.question: Can a gauge-link treatment in light-cone gauge yield a process-independent mapping between final-state and initial-state interaction phases across SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and photon production asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The role of light-cone gauge links and spatial-infinity gauge potentials in reproducing final-state interactions is central to [2], while [3] identifies initial-state interactions as the Drell-Yan source of the asymmetry.

questions.question: What experimental observables can separate Sivers-type chiral-even effects from Boer-Mulders chiral-odd effects in Drell-Yan when both arise from initial-state gluon exchange?
questions.rationale: This derives from [5], which connects the cos 2 phi Drell-Yan distribution to the chiral-odd h_1^perp function and compares it with the Sivers mechanism.

node_e65d9bc26f4e.summary: This cluster studies transverse spin effects in Drell-Yan production, including single and double asymmetries, transversity, Sivers mechanisms, and gauge-invariant twist-three formulations.

questions.question: How precisely can the predicted sign reversal of the Sivers function between SIDIS and Drell-Yan be tested while preserving the gauge-link definition of T-odd transverse-momentum-dependent distributions?
questions.rationale: This directly follows from [1], where the path-ordered exponential invalidates the naive time-reversal argument and predicts a sign reversal in hadron-induced hard processes.

questions.question: In the overlap region Lambda_QCD << q_perp << Q, what matching terms are required so that twist-three quark-gluon correlations and TMD Sivers mechanisms give identical Drell-Yan single-spin asymmetries beyond leading order?
questions.rationale: The matching question derives from [4], which shows that twist-three and TMD mechanisms describe the same physics in their common kinematic domain.

questions.question: Can the same initial-state interaction phase that generates Drell-Yan single-spin asymmetries also account quantitatively for the unpolarized cos(2 phi) asymmetry through the Boer-Mulders distribution?
questions.rationale: This is based on [3] and [5], which tie leading-twist Drell-Yan spin asymmetries and the unpolarized cos(2 phi) distribution to initial-state gluon interactions.

node_386cd1813e0d.summary: These works connect Drell-Yan single-spin asymmetries to Sivers functions, initial-state interactions, gluonic poles, and the matching between TMD and twist-three approaches.

questions.question: How precisely can Drell-Yan measurements test the predicted sign reversal of the Sivers function caused by past-pointing versus future-pointing gauge links in the TMD operator definition?
questions.rationale: The sign reversal follows from the gauge-link structure of T-odd parton densities and is tied to initial-state interactions in Drell-Yan [1][2][3].

questions.question: In the overlap region Lambda_QCD much less than q_perp much less than Q, can twist-three quark-gluon correlations and TMD Sivers functions be matched beyond leading order without spoiling the unified description of single-spin asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The unified-picture papers show that twist-three and TMD mechanisms describe the same physics in their common kinematic domain [4][5].

questions.question: Which light-front wavefunction orbital-angular-momentum components and initial-state interaction phases control the size of the Drell-Yan transverse single-spin asymmetry across pion-proton and proton-proton kinematics?
questions.rationale: The Drell-Yan mechanism attributes the asymmetry to initial-state interaction phases and overlaps of proton light-front wavefunctions differing by one unit of orbital angular momentum [3].

node_463d42ad53f7.summary: This cluster examines double transverse-spin asymmetries, transversity distributions, and Boer-Mulders-type azimuthal effects in polarized and unpolarized Drell-Yan processes.

questions.question: Can Drell-Yan measurements of cos 2phi and transverse double-spin asymmetries jointly isolate Boer-Mulders-type chiral-odd TMD effects from collinear transversity evolution?
questions.rationale: This connects the unsuppressed initial-state-interaction contribution to cos 2phi with NLO transversity predictions for polarized Drell-Yan asymmetries [1],[4].

questions.question: Does NLO evolution preserve phenomenologically useful saturation bounds from Soffer's inequality strongly enough to set robust upper limits on Drell-Yan transverse spin asymmetries?
questions.rationale: This follows from the two-loop transversity splitting functions and numerical studies of Soffer inequality under NLO evolution [2],[3].

questions.question: How can acceptance effects in polarized Drell-Yan experiments be incorporated into global transversity extractions without biasing rapidity-dependent asymmetry predictions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the detailed study of limited muon acceptance effects on transverse double-spin asymmetry measurements [4].

node_5b04e52d4b80.summary: These papers derive twist-three quark-gluon, three-gluon, and fragmentation contributions to single transverse-spin asymmetries in SIDIS, Drell-Yan, photon, charm, and hadron production.

questions.question: Can the full hard-pole, soft-fermion-pole, and soft-gluon-pole twist-three SIDIS cross section be organized into a manifestly gauge-invariant phenomenology that remains stable under Ward-identity constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reexamination showing that Ward identities are crucial to derive the complete gauge-invariant twist-three SIDIS factorization formula [1].

questions.question: What is the correct evolution of flavor-singlet and flavor-nonsinglet twist-three correlation functions at arbitrary parton momenta, and how can discrepancies with vanishing-gluon-momentum calculations be resolved phenomenologically?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the derivation of scale dependence for twist-three functions and the reported disagreement with previous zero-gluon-momentum evolution results [2].

questions.question: Can a global fit using collinear twist-three fragmentation, quark-gluon, and multi-parton correlation functions simultaneously describe RHIC pion asymmetries, SIDIS azimuthal asymmetries, and e+e- fragmentation data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that fragmentation in collinear twist-three factorization can describe high-pT pion data and connect proton-proton, SIDIS, and e+e- spin observables [4].

node_e510e33c181f.summary: This cluster addresses large transverse single-spin asymmetries in inclusive pion and hadron production in polarized proton collisions through twist-three, Collins, and transverse-momentum mechanisms.

questions.question: Can twist-three quark-gluon correlation functions quantitatively describe inclusive pion single-spin asymmetries from fixed-target energies through RHIC over the full measured xF and pT range?
questions.rationale: The twist-three QCD factorization studies find natural leading contributions at large xF and include later non-derivative hard-scattering terms tested against fixed-target and RHIC data [1,4].

questions.question: Which inclusive or semi-inclusive measurements can separate twist-three mechanisms from intrinsic-transverse-momentum descriptions involving imaginary interference between helicity amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The perturbative parton-model study links asymmetries to intrinsic motion and imaginary amplitude products, while the review compares competing perturbative-QCD approaches to azimuthal and single-spin asymmetries [3,5].

questions.question: How much ambiguity in phenomenological extractions of transverse single-spin asymmetries remains from conventions, signs, and definitions across processes?
questions.rationale: The Trento conventions paper was created to standardize definitions and notations for intrinsic-transverse-momentum spin effects [2].
