node_69933eaf0e9e.summary: These works extract quark transversity distributions from SIDIS, electron-positron annihilation, and proton-proton data using dihadron fragmentation functions and pion-pair asymmetries.

questions.question: Can SIDIS, e+e- two-hadron production, and polarized hadron-hadron back-to-back hadron data be fit simultaneously to disentangle transversity from spin-dependent fragmentation functions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the twist-2 spin-dependent fragmentation probe proposed in [1] and the first global extraction of transversity and Collins functions from SIDIS and e+e- data in [5].

questions.question: How universal are T-odd distribution and fragmentation effects once gauge-link structure and subleading inverse-hard-scale observables are included across spacelike and timelike processes?
questions.rationale: This derives from the analysis of T-odd functions and their universality in leptoproduction, Drell-Yan, and e+e- two-hadron production in [2] and [3].

questions.question: What measurements can determine flavor-separated and sea-quark transversity beyond the extracted u and d components while testing how close transversity can approach positivity bounds?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the review of transversity phenomenology and future measurements [4] and by the extracted u and d transversity distributions being smaller than positivity bounds [5].

node_e069e628f00e.summary: This cluster reviews and develops transversity, time-reversal-odd distribution and fragmentation functions, and their role in generating spin and azimuthal asymmetries.

questions.question: Can the process dependence of T-odd transverse-momentum-dependent distributions be quantified beyond leading power in SIDIS, Drell-Yan, and e+e- observables without losing the gauge-invariant operator interpretation of Sivers and Collins effects?
questions.rationale: This derives from the extension of gauge-invariant TMD matrix elements to the next order in inverse hard scale and the leading-power universality discussion of T-odd effects [2].

questions.question: Can a single chiral-odd T-odd distribution with intrinsic transverse momentum consistently explain both transverse single-spin asymmetries in polarized proton collisions and the large cos(2 phi) asymmetry in unpolarized Drell-Yan?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the proposal that the same T-odd distribution may account for pion single-spin asymmetries and the unresolved Drell-Yan cos(2 phi) asymmetry [4].

questions.question: How precisely can transversity be extracted by combining dihadron azimuthal correlations in jets with Drell-Yan and semi-inclusive leptoproduction data under consistent QCD evolution at leading and next-to-leading order?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review of transversity evolution and phenomenology and from the proposal to measure quark transverse polarization through two-hadron azimuthal distributions in jets [3,5].

node_518badf18b2f.summary: These papers extract quark transversity by combining SIDIS, electron-positron annihilation, and proton-proton data with Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions.

questions.question: Can a single global fit of SIDIS and e+e- azimuthal asymmetries determine u- and d-quark transversity and Collins fragmentation functions without strong parametrization bias?
questions.rationale: The first and updated global analyses extracted transversity and Collins functions simultaneously and tested revised parametrizations with HERMES, COMPASS, and Belle data [2], [4], [5].

questions.question: Which measurements of back-to-back hadrons or hadron pairs most directly test the twist-2 spin-dependent fragmentation mechanism proposed for transversely polarized quark jets?
questions.rationale: The original fragmentation-function paper identifies azimuthal hadron distributions in SIDIS and singly polarized hadron-hadron scattering as probes of transverse quark spin [1].

questions.question: How should gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions and their positivity bounds enter future transversity-oriented analyses of azimuthal asymmetries involving multiple hadrons?
questions.rationale: The gluon TMD study emphasizes twist-two gluon distributions, intrinsic transverse momentum, azimuthal asymmetries, and bounds relevant for future estimates [3].

node_b39bbcafdb75.summary: This cluster studies single- and double-spin azimuthal asymmetries in semi-inclusive scattering and hadron-in-jet production using transverse-momentum-dependent and higher-twist distributions.

questions.question: Which subleading 1/Q azimuthal asymmetries in semi-inclusive DIS are robust enough to separate genuine twist effects from intrinsic transverse-momentum and fragmentation contributions?
questions.rationale: The complete tree-level SIDIS calculation in [1] identifies polarization-dependent transverse-momentum effects and azimuthal asymmetries through order 1/Q.

questions.question: Can final-state interactions that generate leading-twist single-spin asymmetries be quantitatively tied to the same spin-flip amplitudes responsible for the proton anomalous magnetic moment?
questions.rationale: The rescattering mechanism in [2] links leading-twist SIDIS single-spin asymmetries to phase differences in spin-flip amplitudes also needed for the anomalous magnetic moment.

questions.question: How consistently can azimuthal asymmetries measured in SIDIS, back-to-back hadron production in e+e-, and hard exclusive pseudoscalar electroproduction constrain the same transverse-spin structure of the nucleon?
questions.rationale: Azimuthal asymmetries appear in SIDIS in [1], in e+e- two-hadron production in [4], and in spin-sensitive exclusive meson electroproduction through the spin-flip distribution in [5].

node_063f1aabe4c1.summary: These works use quarkonium, heavy-quark, jet, hadron, and diffractive production to probe polarized and linearly polarized gluon distributions through spin and azimuthal asymmetries.

questions.question: Which polarized-collider observables among A_LL for high-pT pions, A_LL for jets, and dilepton angular structure most cleanly determine gluon polarization once NLO QCD corrections and polarization-axis conventions are handled consistently?
questions.rationale: This derives from NLO calculations for pion and jet double-spin asymmetries and from the formal treatment of polarization definitions in lepton-proton and dilepton processes [1], [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: Can proposed processes for linearly polarized gluons discriminate Weizsacker-Williams from dipole gluon distributions by testing their different positivity-bound behavior at small and large transverse momentum?
questions.rationale: This follows from the color-glass-condensate result that the two linearly polarized gluon distributions have distinct saturation and suppression patterns [4].

node_adb0359ddd02.summary: This cluster focuses on extracting the longitudinally polarized gluon distribution from jet, hadron, hadron-plus-jet, and photoproduction observables at RHIC and polarized ep colliders.

questions.question: Which jet or high-pT hadron double-spin asymmetry measurement would most directly resolve the remaining uncertainty in the polarized gluon distribution Delta g at RHIC kinematics?
questions.rationale: NLO pion and jet calculations in [1], [3], and [5] were developed specifically to extract Delta g from RHIC double-spin asymmetries.

questions.question: How much do jet algorithm choices bias polarized cross sections versus spin asymmetries in Delta g extractions?
questions.rationale: The algorithm study in [4] finds sizable jet-cross-section dependence on cone versus kt-type algorithms but relatively robust spin asymmetries.

questions.question: Can target-polarization definitions relative to the lepton beam or virtual photon direction be standardized across polarized lepton-proton and proton-proton analyses of gluon polarization?
questions.rationale: The analysis framework in [2] shows that the polarization-axis convention affects azimuthal final-state distributions in polarized lepton-proton scattering.

node_b7c1152c0698.summary: These papers compute next-to-leading-order QCD corrections for polarized hadron, jet, heavy-flavor, and photoproduction processes used to constrain the polarized gluon density.

questions.question: How robust is the extraction of polarized gluon density Delta g from A_LL in pion, hadron, and jet production once NLO hard parts, fragmentation, and jet-algorithm dependence are treated in one fit?
questions.rationale: NLO corrections for pion and hadron production in [1] and [5] and jet-algorithm effects in [4] all feed directly into Delta g constraints.

questions.question: Where does the small-cone approximation cease to be reliable for polarized inclusive jet A_LL at RHIC-like and higher energies, especially for cone versus kT jet algorithms?
questions.rationale: The small-cone NLO jet calculation in [3] and the algorithm comparison in [4] explicitly assess the approximation and its impact on cross sections and spin asymmetries.

questions.question: Can azimuthal effects from defining target polarization relative to the lepton beam rather than the virtual photon be consistently incorporated into polarized hard-production analyses used for spin-PDF constraints?
questions.rationale: The lepton-proton analysis in [2] shows that polarization-frame choices affect final-state azimuthal distributions across SIDIS, exclusive meson production, and DVCS.

node_26516019ef46.summary: This cluster examines proposed and measured spin asymmetries in jets, hadron pairs, prompt photons, quarkonium, and pion production as experimental handles on gluon polarization.

questions.question: Which polarized final state gives the cleanest Delta G constraint below eta about 0.2: correlated high-pT hadron pairs, inclusive jets, J/psi production, or associated J/psi plus gamma?
questions.rationale: The candidate handles are proposed respectively in [1], [2], [3], and [5], with [4] warning that some J/psi channels are ineffective probes of Delta g.

questions.question: Can the perturbative-QCD helicity, twist, and chirality selection-rule prediction A_TT/A_LL << 1 in two-jet production be verified with enough precision to validate the spin-dependent hard-scattering framework used in Delta G extractions?
questions.rationale: This is the central test proposed for polarized hadron collisions in [2].

questions.question: Can quarkonium-based probes of Delta g be made robust against color-octet dominance and collinear-scattering suppressions of polarization asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The color-octet sensitivity of J/psi asymmetries in [3] and the vanishing asymmetry in exclusive collinear J/psi leptoproduction in [4] create this methodological issue.

node_673917a773df.summary: These works develop quarkonium, heavy-quark, jet, and scalar-particle production channels for measuring linearly polarized gluon transverse-momentum distributions in unpolarized hadrons.

questions.question: Which future EIC or LHeC measurement of cos(2 phi) asymmetries can most directly separate Weizsäcker-Williams from dipole linearly polarized gluon distributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the distinct saturation behavior of Weizsäcker-Williams and dipole distributions in a large nucleus and from DIS and Drell-Yan dijet cross sections where they enter different azimuthal terms [1,2].

questions.question: Can heavy-quark pair and jet production in electron-hadron collisions determine the proton's linearly polarized gluon distribution without contamination from the factorization-breaking effects expected in hadron-hadron channels?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by proposals for direct probes in jet or heavy-quark production at EIC or LHeC and the warning that analogous hadron-hadron asymmetries suffer factorization breaking [3].

questions.question: How well can linearly polarized gluon effects in Higgs transverse-momentum spectra be distinguished from ordinary unpolarized-gluon contributions when testing scalar versus pseudoscalar Higgs hypotheses?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the prediction that linearly polarized gluons modify the Higgs transverse-momentum distribution in a characteristic way sensitive to the Higgs parity assignment [5].

node_02fef57b165b.summary: This cluster uses W, Z, Drell-Yan, and diffractive production spin asymmetries to constrain helicity parton distributions and spin-dependent exchange dynamics.

questions.question: Which minimal set of W, Z, and Drell-Yan spin asymmetries in polarized pp, pn, and pd collisions can disentangle sea-quark helicity, transversity, and flavor asymmetry with the least dependence on unpolarized PDF inputs?
questions.rationale: The RHIC electroweak-boson study stresses unpolarized cross sections, double helicity asymmetries, double transverse asymmetries, and parity-violating asymmetries as complementary PDF probes [2].

questions.question: Can lepton-level single-spin asymmetries from W decay be predicted with sufficient accuracy across non-hermetic detector acceptances using soft-gluon resummation rather than fixed-order NLO alone?
questions.rationale: The RHIC weak-boson asymmetry work compares resummed spin-dependent cross sections with NLO results and argues that lepton-level asymmetries can be directly compared to data [4].

questions.question: How can the full angular structure-function formalism for polarized dilepton production be used to test leading-twist TMD factorization in the low-pair-transverse-momentum regime at NICA-SPD?
questions.rationale: The polarized dilepton formalism identifies a complete set of structure functions in the TMD region, and NICA-SPD proposes DY asymmetry measurements accessing twist-two collinear and TMD PDFs [1,5].

node_21ff5b30b30a.summary: These papers extract and evolve quark and gluon Sivers functions from SIDIS, Drell-Yan, weak-boson, heavy-flavor, and hadronic single-spin asymmetry data.

questions.question: What Drell-Yan or W-production measurement would most decisively test the predicted SIDIS-to-Drell-Yan sign change of the Sivers function after QCD evolution?
questions.rationale: The QCD-evolution study fits SIDIS Sivers data and predicts DY and W asymmetries specifically to test the Sivers sign change [4].

questions.question: Can a universal nonperturbative Sudakov factor describe SIDIS, DY, and W/Z transverse-momentum spectra while preserving flavor-separated Sivers extractions?
questions.rationale: The evolution paper identifies a universal spin-independent Sudakov factor that reasonably describes transverse-momentum distributions across SIDIS, DY, and W/Z production [4].

questions.question: How much do exact intrinsic-kperp kinematics and the Cahn effect bias the extracted u, d, and sea-quark Sivers functions from pion and kaon SIDIS?
questions.rationale: The Cahn/Sivers analysis uses exact kinematics to estimate intrinsic transverse momentum and then extract simple quark Sivers models, while later SIDIS fits determine flavor-separated functions [1],[2],[3].

node_7d55a06ddb1e.summary: This cluster centers on fitting quark Sivers distributions from SIDIS and related Drell-Yan or weak-boson data, including TMD evolution and flavor dependence.

questions.question: What precision in Drell-Yan and W-boson transverse single-spin asymmetries is needed to establish the predicted SIDIS-to-DY sign change of the quark Sivers function under TMD evolution?
questions.rationale: This derives from global SIDIS fits with QCD evolution that make Drell-Yan and W-production predictions to test the Sivers sign change [4].

questions.question: How well can current SIDIS pion and kaon data separately constrain sea-quark and strange-quark Sivers functions once fragmentation and intrinsic transverse momentum uncertainties are propagated?
questions.rationale: This follows from the flavor extraction of u, d, s quark and antiquark Sivers functions using HERMES and COMPASS pion and kaon data [1].

questions.question: Can a universal nonperturbative Sudakov factor simultaneously describe unpolarized transverse-momentum spectra and spin-dependent Sivers asymmetries across SIDIS, DY, and W/Z production?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the use of a universal spin-independent Sudakov factor to fit transverse-momentum distributions and evolve Sivers asymmetries [4,5].

node_7e6dc73be531.summary: These works investigate the poorly known gluon Sivers function through transverse single-spin asymmetries in J/psi, D-meson, pion, photon, and electroproduction channels.

questions.question: Which process among back-to-back jets, diphotons, and D-meson production can most cleanly isolate the gluon Sivers function once Sudakov suppression and TMD evolution are included?
questions.rationale: The representative studies propose jets, diphotons, and D mesons as gluon-Sivers probes, while TMD evolution suppresses transverse single-spin asymmetries [1].

questions.question: Can future transverse-spin measurements test the QCD momentum-sum constraint that the gluon and all quark Sivers transverse momenta cancel in a polarized nucleon?
questions.rationale: The Sivers-mechanism analysis finds that the average transverse momenta from gluons and all quark flavors sum to zero [5].

node_83f58e0a9294.summary: This cluster studies longitudinal and transverse Lambda and anti-Lambda polarization in unpolarized and polarized hadronic, SIDIS, and electron-positron processes through spin-dependent fragmentation.

questions.question: What measurement would decisively distinguish competing spin-dependent Lambda fragmentation-function sets that all fit existing e+e- polarization data?
questions.rationale: This question comes from the insufficiency of current data to fix polarized Lambda fragmentation functions in [1].

questions.question: Does Lambda polarization in the current-fragmentation region provide a clean enough probe of nucleon helicity and transversity to justify treating polarized Lambda production as a spin-structure observable?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal that polarized Lambda electroproduction can test u-quark helicity and transversity correlations in [2].

questions.question: Can polarizing fragmentation functions extracted from unpolarized hadron collisions be reconciled with flavor-separated spin-dependent fragmentation functions from e+e- and SIDIS data in one QCD evolution framework?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the phenomenological polarizing fragmentation functions fitted to p-N Lambda and anti-Lambda data in [4] and the evolved fragmentation framework of [1].

node_d571ffb061e5.summary: These papers study charge and spin asymmetries from Pomeron-Odderon interference and two-photon exchange as experimental probes of C-odd QCD dynamics.

questions.question: Which charge-asymmetry measurement would most cleanly settle whether hard diffractive two-pion electroproduction contains a QCD Odderon contribution: the forward-backward asymmetry shape, its dipion invariant-mass dependence, or polarization dependence?
questions.rationale: This follows from predictions that Pomeron-Odderon interference produces a sizable forward-backward charge asymmetry with distinctive pi+ pi- invariant-mass dependence [1,3].

questions.question: Can charm-anticharm jet energy asymmetries in diffractive photoproduction provide a less ambiguous Odderon signal than light-meson charge asymmetries, given existing constraints from proton-proton and proton-antiproton scattering?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the prediction of an order-15% charm versus anticharm fractional-energy asymmetry from Pomeron-Odderon interference under saturated elastic-scattering constraints [4].

questions.question: How accurately can the absorptive two-photon exchange amplitude in elastic electron-proton scattering be constrained from resonance electroproduction and total photoproduction data used to predict beam and target normal spin asymmetries?
questions.rationale: This combines the resonance-region unitarity model of doubly virtual Compton scattering [2] with the optical-theorem, collinear-photon enhancement calculation of beam normal asymmetry [5].

node_5d9c529ec3bd.summary: This cluster focuses on global QCD extractions of pion, kaon, proton, and charged-hadron fragmentation functions from electron-positron, proton-proton, deep-inelastic, and LHC data.

questions.question: What minimal combination of charge-identified SIDIS, charge-sign asymmetric pp data, and flavor-tagged e+e- data would decisively remove the need for flavor-symmetry assumptions in global pion, kaon, and proton fragmentation fits?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of charge-separated hadron data to distinguish quark from antiquark fragmentation in [1] and pp charge-sign asymmetries to constrain valence fragmentation in [5].

questions.question: How robust are present global fragmentation functions when the input scale, heavy-quark factorization scheme, and fitted hadron-mass treatment are varied within the same NLO framework?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the factorization-scheme issues for heavy flavors in [3] and the fitted hadron-mass corrections introduced in [5].

questions.question: Can scaling violations in low-energy e+e- data and longitudinal cross sections determine the gluon fragmentation function and alpha_s consistently with pp-inclusive hadron data?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the use of PEP and LEP longitudinal data to constrain scaling violation and alpha_s in [2], together with the added pp data emphasized in [5].

node_5d9c529ec3bd_1.summary: These works determine and review fragmentation functions for identified light hadrons, emphasizing NLO analyses, charge and flavor separation, and uncertainty estimates.

questions.question: Which identified-hadron data set would most reduce flavor separation uncertainties in pion, kaon, and proton fragmentation functions without imposing strong SU(2) or valence-hierarchy assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by charge-identified global fits that avoid nontrivial flavor assumptions [1] and flavor-tagged e+e- fits that still impose symmetry and hierarchy inputs [2], [3].

questions.question: Can a single NLO fragmentation framework consistently describe e+e-, SIDIS, and pp identified light-hadron production once hadron-mass effects, heavy-quark schemes, and gluon fragmentation uncertainties are fitted together?
questions.rationale: The combined-process global analysis [1], heavy-flavor scheme issues [3], and AKK improvements including pp data and hadron-mass effects [4] motivate this question.

node_5d9c529ec3bd_2.summary: This cluster centers on modern pion, kaon, and proton fragmentation-function determinations with faithful uncertainty quantification across perturbative QCD orders and datasets.

questions.question: Which identified-hadron data most reduce flavor separation uncertainties in pion and kaon fragmentation functions without imposing strong quark-antiquark or SU(2) flavor assumptions?
questions.rationale: The global pion and kaon analysis showed that charge-identified e+e-, pp, and DIS data discriminate quark from antiquark fragmentation functions and reduce reliance on flavor-symmetry assumptions [1].

questions.question: How should global fits consistently propagate hadron-mass effects, charge-sign asymmetries, and low-x e+e- data into proton, kaon, and pion fragmentation uncertainties at NLO and beyond?
questions.rationale: The AKK update added pp data, charge-sign asymmetries, low-x and lower-energy e+e- measurements, and fitted hadron-mass effects for several identified hadrons [4].

questions.question: Can photon fragmentation functions be constrained in a factorization-scheme-invariant way that matches the uncertainty standards now used for light-hadron fragmentation fits?
questions.rationale: The photon-fragmentation study emphasized beyond-leading-log evolution, initial conditions, and factorization-scheme invariance, while modern hadron fits stress uncertainty quantification [1],[5].

node_7de2c76983b7.summary: These papers develop theory, evolution equations, jet observables, and phenomenological models for single- and dihadron fragmentation functions.

questions.question: Can universal dihadron fragmentation functions be validated across e+e-, SIDIS, pp, and identified-hadron-inside-jet measurements once transverse momentum, polarization, and higher-twist effects are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review's emphasis on testing fragmentation functions across electron-positron annihilation, lepton-nucleon scattering, proton-proton collisions, TMD dependence, polarization, higher twist, and dihadron functions [2].

questions.question: Can spectator-model constraints such as crossing, support, Lorentz-invariance relations, and C/P/T symmetry be turned into reliable priors for fitting polarized and subleading dihadron fragmentation functions?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the spectator-model construction that enforces crossing and support while studying polarized, higher-twist, and symmetry-implied relations [1].

questions.question: How should fragmenting jet functions be extended and tested for two identified hadrons inside narrow jets so that matching to standard fragmentation functions remains infrared safe beyond one loop?
questions.rationale: This extends the NLO hadron-in-jet calculation and the one-loop fragmenting-jet-function matching program to the dihadron case [3],[4].

node_1fef023dfe8e.summary: This cluster studies perturbative and nonperturbative fragmentation of heavy quarks and partons into heavy mesons and quarkonia at large transverse momentum.

questions.question: What observable in high-pT quarkonium production most cleanly tests the NRQCD factorization of fragmentation functions with gauge-invariant color-octet matrix elements?
questions.rationale: Gauge-invariant NRQCD octet matrix elements with nonabelian phases are required to absorb NNLO infrared divergences in [5].

questions.question: How large are finite-heavy-mass corrections in global charm fragmentation fits once Belle, CLEO, ALEPH, and OPAL data are combined with modern electroweak and QCD corrections?
questions.rationale: Finite-mass effects are assessed in a general-mass variable-flavor-number extraction of D-meson fragmentation functions in [4].

questions.question: Can in-medium heavy-meson formation and dissociation near the QGP critical temperature be constrained by the same fragmentation-function framework used for vacuum open-heavy-flavor production?
questions.rationale: Vacuum charm and beauty fragmentation functions are combined with in-medium bound-state formation and dissociation in [3].

node_33ba491e0166.summary: These works compute gluon fragmentation functions into heavy quarkonium states, including NRQCD factorization, color-octet contributions, spin dependence, and higher-order corrections.

questions.question: Can NNLO fragmentation calculations demonstrate full NRQCD factorization for gluon-to-quarkonium fragmentation once gauge-invariant color-octet matrix elements with nonabelian phases are used?
questions.rationale: The NNLO factorization analysis identifies uncanceled infrared divergences and argues that gauge-invariant octet matrix elements absorb them [3].

questions.question: How large are higher-order and evolution effects on the relative gluon-fragmentation probabilities into S-wave and P-wave quarkonium states at collider scales?
questions.rationale: The leading-order fragmentation functions for S-wave and P-wave quarkonia rely on Altarelli-Parisi evolution and nonperturbative long-distance parameters [1].

node_89d4d3186e0b.summary: This cluster addresses heavy-quark fragmentation into heavy-light mesons such as D and D* states using perturbative QCD, mass effects, resummation, and collider phenomenology.

questions.question: What single comparison between massive, general-mass, and perturbative-fragmentation descriptions would settle the useful domain of finite heavy-quark mass effects in D and D* production?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finite-mass corrected e+e- fits and the massive versus massless charm treatment of inclusive D* hadroproduction [2,4].

questions.question: Can one fragmentation framework consistently describe vacuum D and B meson formation and the in-medium formation-dissociation dynamics needed for heavy-meson suppression in QCD matter?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the light-cone wave-function calculation of vacuum fragmentation plus in-medium bound-state formation, dissociation, and quenching [1].

questions.question: Do NLO perturbative fragmentation functions in the heavy-quark limit provide a controlled model for the vector-to-pseudoscalar production fraction as a function of z and transverse momentum?
questions.rationale: This derives from the heavy-quark effective theory calculation of heavy-light fragmentation and its prediction for the vector meson fraction P_V [3].

node_9816487c638d.summary: These papers analyze perturbative-QCD production of Bc and Bc* mesons in hadronic and electron-positron collisions, comparing exact calculations with fragmentation approximations.

questions.question: What measurement would decisively test whether high-energy Bc and Bc* production is dominated by perturbative bbar or c fragmentation with the predicted hierarchy of fragmentation probabilities?
questions.rationale: The fragmentation mechanism and the much larger bbar-to-Bc probabilities are central results of [2].

questions.question: How far can updated PDFs, heavy-quark masses, alpha_s choices, and realistic fragmentation functions remove the historical bottom-production excess that feeds into Bc production uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The reduction of apparent bottom-production discrepancies using updated NLO inputs and fragmentation information is the core issue in [1], [3], and [5].

node_290fb8a54f64.summary: This cluster predicts production rates and kinematic distributions for doubly heavy baryons at colliders using NRQCD, diquark production, photoproduction, and hadronic mechanisms.

questions.question: Which measurement, such as J/psi plus D plus Dbar production or B-factory double-charm production, would most reduce alpha_s, charm-mass, and duality uncertainties in Xi_cc cross-section predictions?
questions.rationale: The use of J/psi plus D plus Dbar to reduce Xi_cc uncertainties is proposed in [1], while B-factory production is estimated using perturbative QCD and duality in [2].

questions.question: How can NRQCD matrix elements for the (cc) color-antitriplet 3S1 and color-sextet 1S0 diquark configurations be constrained so GM-VFN predictions become testable?
questions.rationale: The NRQCD factorization setup of [4] and the sizable GM-VFN diquark-channel contributions in [5] motivate this question.

questions.question: At what energies and transverse momenta does heavy-quark fragmentation into a compact QQ diquark followed by QQq baryon formation become quantitatively valid across e+e-, fixed-target, Tevatron, and LHC production?
questions.rationale: The fragmentation picture of [3] needs to be reconciled with the collider and fixed-target production estimates in [1] and [4].

node_47d9d45d711f.summary: These papers investigate color transparency and nuclear filtering in hard nuclear reactions, connecting QCD small-size configurations with measured nuclear transparency and attenuation.

questions.question: What measurement would most decisively resolve the tension between null quasielastic A(e,e'p) transparency trends and positive vector-meson electroproduction evidence for color transparency onset?
questions.rationale: No significant rise in quasielastic nuclear transparency was observed in [1], whereas [3] interprets rho electroproduction data as evidence for color-transparency onset.

questions.question: Can model-independent transparency observables be constructed that separate small-size-configuration formation, wave-packet expansion, and nuclear filtering effects?
questions.rationale: The need for minimally model-dependent analyses and the interplay between wave-packet evolution and nuclear filtering are emphasized in [2].

questions.question: Under what kinematic conditions does the QCD dipole description with color triviality remain valid for hard projectiles propagating through extended nuclear color fields?
questions.rationale: The non-abelian Furry approximation and the color-triviality condition for parametrizing nuclear dependence by a dipole cross section are derived in [5].

node_f207dfdfd6c1.summary: This broad cluster covers LHC searches for supersymmetry and beyond-Standard-Model Higgs or scalar resonances, including MSSM, NMSSM, littlest Higgs, and diphoton-excess interpretations.

questions.question: Which future Higgs measurements would most cleanly distinguish an extended two-Higgs-doublet or supersymmetric Higgs sector from a Standard Model Higgs sector described only by dimension-six effective operators?
questions.rationale: This combines the 2HDM review's focus on extended scalar sectors and flavor constraints with the Higgs Handbook and Warsaw-basis EFT programs for interpreting Higgs properties [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: What is the smallest benchmark set that still spans the phenomenologically relevant MSSM Higgs possibilities for LHC and future linear-collider searches?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass Points and Slopes established consensus MSSM benchmarks, while the Higgs cross-section handbooks and ILC report emphasize updated precision Higgs measurements and search contexts [S1], [3], [S2].

questions.question: How should theoretical uncertainties in charged and neutral Higgs decay widths and branching ratios be standardized when comparing HDECAY-style predictions with modern LHC fiducial and simplified-template measurements?
questions.rationale: HDECAY provides decay widths and branching ratios for SM and MSSM Higgs bosons, while the Higgs Handbook promotes pseudo-observables, fiducial cross sections, and simplified template cross sections as measurement baselines [4], [3].

node_0ebb9f010b98.summary: These papers study beyond-Standard-Model Higgs sectors, especially NMSSM and 2HDM scenarios, using collider constraints, decay patterns, and future measurements to assess light, charged, heavy, and self-coupled Higgs states.

questions.question: Which combination of precision Higgs coupling, width, and self-coupling measurements would most decisively reveal a decoupled two-Higgs-doublet sector whose light scalar remains Standard-Model-like?
questions.rationale: The decoupling-limit study shows that heavy 2HDM states can leave only small coupling deviations, while Snowmass emphasizes future precision on couplings, width, and self-coupling [4], [S1].

questions.question: How should pseudo-observables, simplified template cross sections, and fiducial cross sections be optimized to constrain extra Higgs states with off-shell production and interference effects?
questions.rationale: The LHC Higgs Cross Section Handbook identifies these measurement frameworks and includes off-shell Higgs production and interference as central ingredients for deciphering the Higgs sector [1].

questions.question: Can boosted jet-substructure searches in associated production be generalized into a robust discovery strategy for extended-Higgs decays such as A -> HZ and H -> AZ with bbll final states?
questions.rationale: Boosted VH with H -> bb was recovered using jet reconstruction and decomposition, while Snowmass studies exotic A/H -> HZ/AZ -> bbll searches at the LHC [3], [S2].

node_fb7da39f90e0.summary: This cluster examines light neutral and charged Higgs bosons in two-Higgs-doublet models, connecting LHC, LEP, flavor constraints, and possible 95 GeV excesses to viable parameter space.

questions.question: Which combination of precision Higgs coupling deviations, electroweak-fit observables, and flavor constraints would most sharply distinguish an exactly decoupled 2HDM from a light non-SM Higgs sector?
questions.rationale: This follows from the decoupling-limit corrections in [2] and the combined electroweak, Higgs-coupling, and flavor constraints in [3].

questions.question: Can boosted b-jet and top/Higgs tagging strategies recover light neutral Higgs signals in associated production across the viable Type-II and Type-X 2HDM parameter regions?
questions.rationale: The question combines the boosted-substructure recovery of VH and ttH channels in [1] and [5] with the Yukawa-type collider distinctions in [4].

questions.question: How much of the light-A or light-H 2HDM parameter space remains discoverable through A -> HZ, H -> AZ, or h -> AZ after LHC and ILC projections include realistic branching-ratio hierarchies?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the exotic AZ/HZ search reach of [S1] and the 2HDM LHC/ILC projection program in [S3].

node_b666ea407e6b.summary: These works focus on sub-top-mass charged Higgs bosons in 2HDMs, mapping LHC production and decay channels such as associated production, bosonic decays, and multi-bottom final states.

questions.question: What search strategy would close the remaining window for charged Higgs bosons near 75 GeV with strongly suppressed fermionic couplings?
questions.rationale: A light charged Higgs as low as 75 GeV remains allowed only when its fermionic couplings are severely suppressed in the 2HDM analysis of [2].

questions.question: Can off-shell three-body decays below top, W/Z, or heavy-Higgs thresholds become the leading discovery handle for light or compressed charged Higgs spectra at the LHC?
questions.rationale: The partial-width analysis in [1] shows that three-body decays of charged and heavy Higgs bosons can be large below important two-body thresholds.

questions.question: How should charged-Higgs searches be combined with A0 -> Z H0 and H/A -> AZ channels to test the 2HDM spectra associated with a first-order electroweak phase transition?
questions.rationale: The electroweak-phase-transition scenario in [4] identifies A0 -> Z H0 as a smoking-gun signature, while [5] frames charged scalars as part of the broader multi-Higgs search program.

node_b666ea407e6b_1.summary: This cluster emphasizes alternative LHC discovery modes for light charged Higgs bosons in Type-I 2HDMs, including pair production and bosonic decay channels beyond standard top-decay searches.

questions.question: Which light-charged-Higgs search channel would most decisively test the remaining 2HDM parameter space where fermionic charged-Higgs couplings are severely suppressed?
questions.rationale: Ref. [2] finds that charged Higgs bosons as light as 75 GeV can survive combined data when their couplings to fermions are strongly suppressed.

questions.question: Can bosonic cascade channels such as A0 to Z H0 or related AZ/HZ modes provide stronger coverage of light 2HDM spectra than standard top-decay charged-Higgs searches?
questions.rationale: Refs. [4] and [S1] identify A0 to ZH0 and AZ/HZ exotic Higgs decays as promising signatures of extended Higgs sectors.

questions.question: How important are below-threshold three-body decays involving off-shell top quarks, W/Z bosons, or heavy scalars for reinterpretations of light charged-Higgs limits?
questions.rationale: Ref. [1] shows that three-body decay branching ratios of charged and heavy Higgs bosons can be large below thresholds involving top quarks, W/Z bosons, or heavy scalars.

node_72c0461bf738.summary: These papers calculate neutral and charged Higgs pair production in two-Higgs-doublet models at photon, lepton, gluon, and hadron colliders, highlighting loop effects and enhanced cross sections.

questions.question: Can ratios such as sigma(W phi)/sigma(Z phi) provide a cleaner 2HDM discriminator than absolute Higgs-pair or associated-production rates once Yukawa signs and loop-induced gluon fusion are included?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposal that W phi/Z phi ratios are sensitive to 2HDM parameters and in loop-induced ZH production studies [1],[2].

questions.question: Which 2HDM parameter regions allow measurable enhancements in hh, gamma gamma -> hh, gg -> hh, or H+- W-+ production while satisfying perturbativity and current Higgs-rate projections?
questions.rationale: This follows from loop-enhanced Higgs-pair and charged-Higgs-associated production studies together with Snowmass projections constraining 2HDM parameter space [3],[4],[S1].

questions.question: How should public 2HDM cross-section tools combine higher-order corrections for neutral Higgs production with matched 0- and 1-jet loop samples for differential LHC predictions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by interim recommendations on 2HDM cross sections and the need for merged loop samples to describe high-pT ZH distributions [2],[5].

node_f00b78635710.summary: This cluster centers on reported ATLAS, CMS, and LEP excesses near 95 to 96 GeV and their interpretation in extended scalar sectors such as 2HDM, N2HDM, singlet, and Higgs-portal models.

questions.question: What combined LEP, LHC diphoton, and extended-scalar decay analysis would settle whether a 95-96 GeV excess is a real light scalar rather than channel-dependent background fluctuation?
questions.rationale: This broad question is anchored in the cluster's reported 95-96 GeV hints and in [5], which studies experimentally constrained N2HDM scalar spectra and Higgs-to-Higgs decays.

questions.question: Can singlet-extended Higgs models accommodate a light 95 GeV state while maintaining vacuum stability, perturbativity, and a global electroweak minimum across resonant di-Higgs channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the global-minimum constraints in singlet resonant di-Higgs production in [2] and the theoretical scrutiny of the N2HDM in [5].

questions.question: Could cascade production, rather than direct production, be the dominant discovery mode for a 95 GeV scalar in multi-scalar singlet or N2HDM spectra?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [S1], where new scalar resonances can be primarily produced through s-channel decay of another scalar, and by the multi-Higgs decay structure of [5].

node_53eb424819ae.summary: These papers investigate possible new scalar or pseudoscalar resonances at electroweak-scale masses, exploring their LHC signatures through associated Higgs production, multileptons, gauge bosons, and resonant Higgs pairs.

questions.question: What single cross-channel pattern would turn electroweak-scale scalar hints in multileptons, Higgs transverse-momentum distortions, and exotic Higgs decays into a coherent extended-Higgs-sector signal rather than mismodeled Standard Model backgrounds?
questions.rationale: The multilepton-anomaly study, the H -> h S mediated scenario, and Higgs decays to light CP-odd scalars each identify different electroweak-scale scalar signatures [1][2][5].

questions.question: Are the most decisive tests of light scalar portals likely to come from meson-decay beam experiments, LHC Higgs production, or direct proton-induced production channels?
questions.rationale: The GeV-scale scalar portal review compares meson decays, Higgs decays, proton bremsstrahlung, DIS, and coherent scattering across DUNE, SHiP, and LHC-based experiments [3].

questions.question: What experimental signature would most cleanly distinguish a GeV-scale Higgs-portal scalar decaying to e+e- from a heavier electroweak scalar cascade producing missing energy or multileptons?
questions.rationale: MicroBooNE constrains kaon-produced scalars decaying to e+e-, while LHC studies focus on heavier scalar cascades such as H -> h chi chi and H -> h S [2][4][5].

node_021ce1f724a4.summary: This cluster specifically analyzes the recurring 95 GeV diphoton, ditau, and bottom-quark excesses and their explanations within 2HDM, NMSSM, and singlet-extended Higgs models.

questions.question: What combined pattern in diphoton, ditau, and b-bar final states would most decisively distinguish a real 95-96 GeV Higgs boson from mutually compatible statistical excesses?
questions.rationale: The 95-96 GeV interpretation rests on the coexistence of CMS diphoton and ditau excesses with the LEP b-bar excess [2][5].

questions.question: Within the N2HDM, how tightly do vacuum stability, perturbativity, and global-minimum requirements restrict the parameter space that fits a 95 GeV scalar and a Standard-Model-like 125 GeV Higgs?
questions.rationale: The N2HDM scrutiny implements perturbativity, vacuum stability, and global-minimum tests, while the 96 GeV studies require simultaneous consistency with the 125 GeV Higgs and exclusion bounds [1][2].

questions.question: Can correlations among inclusive diphoton, exclusive VBF or associated-production diphoton, and ditau rates identify the 2HDM-plus-singlet Yukawa type responsible for a 95 GeV signal?
questions.rationale: Exclusive and inclusive Higgs search channels show discriminating correlations across CP- and flavor-conserving 2HDM coupling patterns [3].

node_69bcadf60cad.summary: These works study Higgs-pair production as a probe of extended scalar sectors, covering resonant singlet or supersymmetric contributions, nonresonant enhancements, and HL-LHC discovery prospects.

questions.question: Which resonant di-Higgs final states would most cleanly determine whether an observed enhancement comes from a singlet-like scalar decay h2 to h1 h1 rather than from nonresonant new electroweak physics?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] frames di-Higgs and di-Higgs+jet production as complementary probes of resonant Higgs-portal or MSSM scenarios and nonresonant pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Higgs scenarios.

questions.question: How should benchmark planes for singlet-extended scalar sectors be chosen so that they preserve the electroweak global minimum while covering the largest experimentally distinct resonant multi-scalar decay chains?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] bounds the maximum di-Higgs enhancement by requiring a global electroweak minimum, while [S1] and [S2] emphasize benchmark choices for multi-scalar resonant cascades.

questions.question: Can kinematic clustering of Higgs-pair events be extended to three-scalar singlet models so that searches remain sensitive when the dominant discovery channel is production and decay of one new scalar through another?
questions.rationale: This combines the clustering strategy for Higgs-pair benchmark selection in [5] with the multi-scalar production chains highlighted in [4] and [S1].

node_90844e977cef.summary: This cluster examines how Higgs signal measurements, heavy-Higgs searches, flavor data, and alignment-limit assumptions constrain Type-I, Type-II, aligned, and general two-Higgs-doublet models.

questions.question: What precision in SM-like Higgs coupling measurements would make the 2HDM decoupling interpretation distinguishable from exact natural alignment without directly observing the heavier scalars?
questions.rationale: The decoupling analysis computes leading deviations in Higgs couplings, while the maximally symmetric 2HDM realizes alignment independently of charged-Higgs mass and tan beta before symmetry-breaking effects [1,5].

questions.question: Can a single search strategy use the observed Higgs signal strengths to predict which direct heavy-scalar channels are most constraining across Type-I, Type-II, Type-X, and aligned 2HDM Yukawa structures?
questions.rationale: The collider-strategy paper emphasizes complementarity between SM-like Higgs couplings and additional scalar searches, while the Yukawa-model study shows distinct collider phenomenology among the four discrete-symmetry types [4,3].

questions.question: Where do electroweak precision, flavor, and Higgs-coupling constraints leave genuine non-decoupled 2HDM parameter space after including current top, W, and effective weak-mixing-angle inputs?
questions.rationale: The global electroweak fit combines updated precision data with Higgs coupling strengths and flavor observables to constrain two-Higgs-doublet models [2].

node_2c7e425e2b39.summary: These papers develop LHC strategies for detecting heavy charged or nonstandard Higgs bosons using jet substructure, multi-bottom tags, tau-neutrino modes, and boosted hadronic final states.

questions.question: Can boosted fat-jet Higgs and top taggers recover bottom-rich Higgs search channels that are otherwise overwhelmed by QCD backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This follows from the recovery of high-pT WH/ZH with H -> b bbar using jet substructure in [1] and boosted top/Higgs taggers for ttH in [2].

questions.question: What background-control strategy would make H -> b bbar modes competitive with cleaner leptonic or rapidity-gap Higgs searches in the 114-130 GeV mass range?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the detailed bbbar-background studies in rapidity-gap channels in [5] and the high-pT associated-production strategy in [1].

questions.question: Can jet-based reconstruction of top-rich final states expose MSSM-like Higgs bosons through peak-dip structures in the t tbar invariant-mass spectrum?
questions.rationale: This derives from the predicted peak-dip signal for Higgs bosons decaying mainly to top quarks in [4] and the boosted top reconstruction methods in [2].

node_de18b12956fb.summary: This cluster focuses on jet-based Higgs discovery methods at the LHC, including boosted associated production, exotic gluon-rich decays, forward proton tagging, and heavy-Higgs semileptonic modes.

questions.question: How far can boosted Higgs and top tagging extend the viability of H -> b bbar searches in WH, ZH, and ttH channels once realistic QCD backgrounds and pileup are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1] and [2], which recover difficult H -> b bbar associated-production channels using high-pT fat-jet substructure and boosted taggers.

questions.question: What jet-based analysis strategy most cleanly separates a heavy Higgs peak-dip interference pattern in gg -> t tbar from continuum top-pair production?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [4], which predicts a potentially observable peak-dip structure in the t tbar invariant-mass spectrum for Higgs bosons decaying mainly to top quarks.

questions.question: Can rapidity-gap Higgs production with tagged protons or weak-boson fusion provide an independent H -> b bbar confirmation channel competitive with boosted associated production?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which studies exclusive tagged-proton production and weak-boson fusion with H -> b bbar, including backgrounds and experimental issues.

node_0870b4b12a15.summary: This cluster studies charged Higgs production and discovery channels at hadron colliders, especially heavy MSSM states decaying through tau-neutrino, top-bottom, and Wh final states.

questions.question: Which charged-Higgs search channel can provide the most model-robust coverage across low and high tan beta once tb, tau nu, and WH final states are evaluated with realistic b-tagging, mistagging, and top-pair backgrounds?
questions.rationale: The representative LHC studies find complementary reach in ttb, hadronic tau, tb, and WH channels but show that backgrounds and parameter coverage differ sharply by channel [1], [3], [4], [5].

questions.question: Can tau polarization and transverse-mass observables in hadronic tau decays still yield an unambiguous heavy charged-Higgs mass estimate when detector effects and non-MSSM Higgs-sector possibilities are included?
questions.rationale: The hadronic tau channel was identified as nearly background-free at large tan beta and as providing mass information, while ATLAS studies discuss broader SUSY and extended-Higgs interpretations [3], [5].

node_3c73052e9b03.summary: This cluster surveys collider searches and phenomenology for non-Standard-Model Higgs bosons, especially light or extended supersymmetric states constrained by LEP and LHC data.

questions.question: What fiducial and simplified-template measurements are most useful for recasting LHC Higgs data into exclusions of arbitrary supersymmetric or extended Higgs sectors?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the standardized Higgs prediction and measurement frameworks in [1] and [2] and the arbitrary-Higgs-sector exclusion strategy of HiggsBounds in [5].

questions.question: Can the MSSM heavy-Higgs wedge be closed by combining tau+tau- searches with A -> Zh and precision Higgs-property measurements at 300 and 3000 fb^-1?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the MSSM wedge strategy of [S3] and the precision Higgs program described in [1]-[3].

questions.question: How should invisible or resonance-spread Higgs decays through singlet hidden sectors be incorporated into standard supersymmetric Higgs search combinations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the hidden-sector Higgs portal mechanisms in [4] and invisible ZH projections in [S2].

node_2b3aa05c54f3.summary: This cluster focuses on light scalar and pseudoscalar Higgs states in the NMSSM, including exotic Higgs-to-Higgs decays and possible 98 and 125 GeV collider signals.

questions.question: Can strong singlet-doublet mixing in the NMSSM enhance the 125 GeV diphoton rate while remaining compatible with bb, VV*, dark-matter, muon g-2, and stop-sector constraints?
questions.rationale: The NMSSM enhancement mechanism through reduced h -> bb width is proposed in [5], and comparative MSSM/NMSSM scans with these constraints are performed in [2].

questions.question: What LHC search combination is most sensitive to the second lighter CP-even Higgs predicted in NMSSM regions with a SM-like 125 GeV state?
questions.rationale: The NMSSM scenario in [5] predicts a potentially observable lighter CP-even Higgs accompanying the 125 GeV state.

questions.question: How can MSSM benchmark scenarios after the Higgs discovery be generalized to NMSSM light-Higgs spectra without obscuring the distinct singlet-driven phenomenology?
questions.rationale: Post-discovery MSSM benchmark scenarios are constructed in [3], while [2] contrasts MSSM and NMSSM parameter requirements for a 123-127 GeV SM-like Higgs.

node_d234c12ffdd2.summary: This cluster examines MSSM and NMSSM scenarios with very light neutral, charged, or CP-odd Higgs bosons that evade standard LEP limits through altered couplings or nonstandard decays.

questions.question: Can light NMSSM scenarios with h -> aa and ma < 2mb still explain LEP excesses while remaining compatible with the 125 GeV Higgs rates and current LHC searches for heavier supersymmetric Higgs bosons?
questions.rationale: This combines the LEP h -> aa interpretation in [3] with the post-discovery MSSM Higgs benchmark and rate constraints in [1] and [2].

questions.question: Which low-fine-tuning observable best tests a light CP-odd Higgs below the bb threshold: altered LEP Zh final states, Upsilon -> gamma a, or LHC exotic Higgs decays?
questions.rationale: The h -> aa low-fine-tuning scenario is described in [3], and [5] identifies Upsilon radiative decays as a dedicated probe of the light CP-odd Higgs.

questions.question: How do B-physics, dark-matter relic-density, direct-detection, and muon-g-2 constraints reshape the allowed lightest-Higgs mass window in constrained and phenomenological MSSM scenarios?
questions.rationale: The combined collider, flavor, dark matter, and muon anomalous magnetic moment constraints are central to [4], with complementary post-Higgs-discovery pMSSM analysis in [2].

node_0ee0e9a9e3b6.summary: This cluster emphasizes post-discovery MSSM and phenomenological supersymmetry benchmarks where light Higgs states remain viable and can be tested through specialized collider channels.

questions.question: Which post-Higgs-discovery MSSM benchmark scenarios still allow the 125 GeV state to be interpreted as either the light or heavy CP-even Higgs after current heavy-Higgs, SUSY, B-physics, and dark-matter constraints?
questions.rationale: Benchmark studies allow the observed state as the light CP-even Higgs [1], while MSSM interpretations also considered light- or heavy-Higgs assignments under early rate deviations [4].

questions.question: Can Higgs decays to neutralinos and charginos reopen light-Higgs parameter regions that would otherwise be excluded by standard visible-channel searches?
questions.rationale: Neutralino and chargino Higgs decays can be important for heavy Higgs states and create a small light-Higgs window, including invisible decays that affect exclusion limits [5].

node_d3c5c76ca030.summary: This cluster centers on very light CP-odd NMSSM Higgs bosons probed through neutralino decays, Upsilon and B physics, HyperCP-inspired signatures, and multi-Higgs collider cascades.

questions.question: Is the ideal-Higgs NMSSM scenario with h1 to a1 a1 and m_a below 2m_b still viable after radiative Upsilon bounds and rare B and K constraints are imposed in a single fit?
questions.rationale: The LEP-excess interpretation and natural NMSSM scenario require dominant h to aa decays, while Upsilon and flavor studies strongly constrain the light CP-odd Higgs coupling and mass windows [1][2][3][4].

questions.question: Can the symmetry-protected light pseudoscalar mechanism at large tan beta survive the combined b to s a1, B mixing, muon g-2, and Higgs-signal constraints without collapsing into a narrow tuned coupling region?
questions.rationale: The NMSSM large-tan-beta analysis allows very light A1 states with distinctive b-physics effects, while the light-pseudoscalar 2HDM study shows strong correlated constraints from g-2, Higgs data, and B_s to mu+mu- [3][5].

questions.question: What branching-ratio pattern among h to aa, a to tau tau, a to mu mu, light hadrons, and gamma a Upsilon decays would decisively confirm or exclude the sub-2m_b pseudoscalar explanation of low-fine-tuning Higgs scenarios?
questions.rationale: The ideal-Higgs papers rely on h to aa dominance with m_a below 2m_b and on radiative Upsilon searches as direct probes of the a b b coupling [1][2][4].

node_56084e62610e.summary: This cluster studies natural NMSSM parameter regions with 125 GeV Higgs compatibility, enhanced diphoton rates, singlet-doublet mixing, light companion Higgs bosons, and distinctive LHC decay signatures.

questions.question: Can current and HL-LHC Higgs-rate data still accommodate the natural NMSSM mechanism in which strong singlet-doublet mixing suppresses the 125 GeV Higgs bb partial width while enhancing the diphoton branching ratio?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed NMSSM region where singlet-doublet mixing reduces the bb width and enhances the diphoton signal [4].

questions.question: What search strategy would most decisively test the light companion CP-even Higgs predicted in natural NMSSM benchmark regions with light stops and gluinos below 1 TeV?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the benchmark studies that combine a 125 GeV SM-like Higgs, natural superpartner spectra, and potentially observable lighter Higgs states [4],[5].

node_789942946c31.summary: This cluster reviews Higgs searches and measurements from LEP through Tevatron and LHC, including Standard Model discovery history and beyond-Standard-Model interpretations.

questions.question: What unified statistical framework should combine fiducial cross sections, simplified template cross sections, pseudo-observables, EFT fits, and direct exotic-Higgs exclusions without double counting information?
questions.rationale: The LHC Higgs Cross Section Working Group identifies these measurement frameworks as the baseline for Higgs property interpretations in [1].

questions.question: Which remaining MSSM or extended-Higgs parameter regions are least covered after combining tau+tau-, A -> hZ, invisible, off-shell, and Higgs-coupling constraints?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass wedge study focuses on tau+tau- and pseudoscalar-to-hZ searches as essential coverage for MSSM heavy Higgs sectors [S1].

questions.question: How can tools like HiggsBounds be extended so arbitrary Higgs sectors with hidden-sector decays, split resonances, or invisible widths are tested against modern LHC topological limits?
questions.rationale: HiggsBounds maps arbitrary Higgs predictions to LEP and Tevatron topological exclusions [5], while Higgs-portal hidden sectors can spread or invisibly deplete Higgs signals [4].

node_fd3d35da4896.summary: This cluster provides broad theoretical and phenomenological reviews of Higgs physics, electroweak symmetry breaking, supersymmetric Higgs sectors, and discovery prospects at current and future colliders.

questions.question: What measurement framework should be treated as the field standard for comparing Higgs EFT coefficients, pseudo-observables, simplified template cross sections, and fiducial cross sections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the LHC Higgs Cross Section Working Group's presentation of these frameworks as the baseline for Higgs property measurements [1].

questions.question: Which precision Higgs property measurement would most clearly distinguish a weakly coupled SM-like Higgs sector from MSSM or hidden-sector Higgs-portal extensions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in reviews of SM/MSSM Higgs phenomenology and the possibility that Higgs-portal singlets create invisible channels or multiple weaker resonances [4][5].

questions.question: How should theory uncertainties in production cross sections, branching ratios, PDFs, off-shell production, and interference be propagated into future collider claims about the nature of the Higgs sector?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Higgs handbook focus on state-of-the-art cross sections, branching ratios, PDFs, off-shell effects, and interference in Higgs-sector interpretation [1][2][3].

node_d54005613e03.summary: This cluster concerns the interpretation of LEP, Tevatron, and LHC Higgs search limits for MSSM and extended Higgs sectors, including tools such as HiggsBounds and likelihood recasts.

questions.question: How can HiggsBounds-style exclusion tests be upgraded from most-sensitive-channel logic to statistically consistent combinations of correlated LEP, Tevatron, and LHC searches for arbitrary extended Higgs sectors?
questions.rationale: HiggsBounds selects the topology with highest expected exclusion power in [1] and [2], while HiggsSignals in [3] emphasizes correlations and chi-squared compatibility tests.

questions.question: What public likelihood information is required for exclusion tools to recast heavy MSSM Higgs searches in the tau tau and A -> hZ channels at 300 and 3000 fb^-1 without benchmark-specific assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the HL-LHC wedge-closing projections in [S1] and the model-independent input philosophy of HiggsBounds in [2].

questions.question: Can one define a common input standard for masses, widths, branching ratios, effective couplings, and production cross sections that remains valid for overlapping neutral and charged Higgs signals?
questions.rationale: The need is suggested by the HiggsBounds 2.0 and 4 input schemes for neutral and charged Higgs sectors in [2] and [4], and by the mass-rate testing framework in [3].

node_bacd716b92f2.summary: This cluster studies Standard Model extensions with additional scalar singlets, their mixing with the Higgs, hidden or broadened scalar signatures, and constraints from present and future colliders.

questions.question: What combination of Higgs coupling precision, direct scalar searches, and double-Higgs measurements would most decisively distinguish a real singlet Higgs extension from a purely Standard Model-like Higgs sector?
questions.rationale: This broad discriminator is motivated by singlet mixing effects on LHC Higgs phenomenology [1], coupling bounds [2], and global Higgs-property fits after discovery [5].

questions.question: In which singlet-extended parameter regions do collider-accessible scalar signatures remain compatible with perturbative unitarity, electroweak precision data, perturbativity, and vacuum stability up to high scales?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the full-mass-range post-Run-1 constraint analysis including unitarity, electroweak precision, perturbativity, and vacuum stability in [3].

questions.question: Can future hadron collider searches for heavy scalar decays to electroweak final states be recast into a singlet-specific discovery strategy that covers hidden, weakly mixed, and broadened scalar scenarios?
questions.rationale: This connects the singlet LHC scenarios in [1] and [4] with the future heavy-Higgs search channels emphasized in the Snowmass study [S1].

node_8ac78c09369d.summary: This cluster analyzes Higgs bosons with invisible or exotic decay modes, their theoretical motivations such as dark matter or majorons, and search strategies at the Tevatron and LHC.

questions.question: What combination of ZH, weak-boson-fusion, and targeted exotic-decay searches would most robustly close the gap between invisible Higgs branching-ratio limits and weakly coupled Higgs-portal scenarios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the WBF sensitivity strategy in [2], the global-fit degeneracies in [4], and the ZH HL-LHC projections and Higgs-portal interpretation in [S1].

questions.question: Which hidden-sector Higgs decay topologies are still most likely to evade standard LHC Higgs measurements despite being compatible with the 125 GeV signal?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the broad exotic-decay survey in [1] and the concrete lepton-jet and four-lepton hidden-sector examples in [3] and [5].

questions.question: Can future Higgs factories distinguish NMSSM-like h -> a1 a1 -> 4 tau decays from broader classes of undetected or partially invisible Higgs decays in a model-independent way?
questions.rationale: This derives from the ILC sensitivity study for h -> a1 a1 -> tau tau tau tau in [S2] and the wider invisible-or-undetected Higgs fit framework in [4].

node_380270d4f934.summary: This cluster links Higgs self-coupling measurements in single and double Higgs production with collider searches for exotic doubly charged Higgs states.

questions.question: Which double-Higgs production channel or combination of channels can most cleanly separate a modified trilinear Higgs self-coupling from new colored states, strong-sector effects, or resonant Higgs-pair production?
questions.rationale: The LHC self-coupling studies compare gluon fusion, vector-boson fusion, Higgs-strahlung, ttHH, boosted topologies, and rare bb gamma gamma modes, while MSSM and strong-sector scenarios can enhance pair production [1][2][4][5].

questions.question: Can precision single-Higgs coupling measurements and double-Higgs rates reveal nondecoupling charged or additional Higgs-sector loop effects even when hZZ remains Standard-Model-like?
questions.rationale: The two-Higgs-doublet analysis shows that the renormalized hhh coupling can receive enhanced nondecoupling loop corrections even when the hZZ coupling is close to the Standard Model value [3].

node_ff7ad9a935a3.summary: These papers study production, decay modes, and LHC bounds for doubly charged Higgs bosons, especially same-sign dilepton and diboson signatures tied to neutrino-mass models.

questions.question: What single LHC or future lepton-collider search strategy would most cleanly distinguish a type-II-seesaw doubly charged scalar from a left-right-symmetric triplet scalar when both same-sign dilepton and W+W+ decays are allowed?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the left-right W-fusion same-sign dilepton signal in [2], the type-II-seesaw spectrum dependence in [4], and future low-mass scalar channels in [S1].

questions.question: How should mass limits on H^{++} be reinterpreted when associated production H^{++}H^- and two-photon pair production are comparable to or more important than the assumed Drell-Yan pair-production channel?
questions.rationale: This follows from the enhanced search potential of associated production in [3] and the two-photon contribution to pair production emphasized in [5].

questions.question: Can collider branching-ratio measurements of H^{++}->l^+l^+ and H^{++}->W^+W^+ determine whether the underlying neutrino spectrum is normal, inverted, or degenerate?
questions.rationale: This derives from the comparison of dilepton and cascade or diboson branching ratios under different neutrino-mass spectra in [3] and [5].

node_587e3542e610.summary: This cluster focuses on Higgs Triplet Model searches for doubly charged scalars through multi-lepton, same-sign lepton, diboson, and associated-production channels at hadron and electron-proton colliders.

questions.question: How can LHC doubly charged Higgs searches be made robust against the triplet spectrum, given that H^{++} mass limits change when H^{++} -> l+l+, H^{++} -> H+ W*, and diboson modes compete?
questions.rationale: The dependence of H^{++} bounds on the particle spectrum is emphasized in [4], and the competing leptonic and cascade branching ratios are studied in [3].

questions.question: What same-sign dilepton and W-fusion observables most directly separate right-triplet Delta_R^{++} production in left-right models from Higgs Triplet Model single and associated production?
questions.rationale: This derives from the W-fusion Delta_R^{++} study and same-sign lepton signal in [2], together with the associated-production mechanism in [3].

questions.question: Can long-lived charged scalar tracks plus missing transverse energy in real-triplet models be combined with two-photon Higgs-rate deviations to test the vanishing-triplet-vev dark-matter scenario?
questions.rationale: This question follows from [5], which predicts light charged scalars, a dark matter candidate for zero triplet vev, charged tracks, missing energy, and enhanced diphoton events.

node_6e0e26dd6288.summary: These works examine neutral, singly charged, and doubly charged scalar particles as sources of lepton number or flavor violation at the LHC and future lepton colliders.

questions.question: What observation pattern of H++ -> l+l+ and H++ -> W+W+ decays, including pair and associated production, would be sufficient to establish lepton-number violation rather than only a charged-scalar signal?
questions.rationale: The need to observe both dilepton and diboson modes and the dependence on production channel and electroweak multiplet are emphasized in [1] and [4].

questions.question: Can weak-scale flavor-specific scalar couplings suppress FCNCs while producing testable rare leptonic B decays or lepton-flavor-universality-violating tau and muon observables?
questions.rationale: Approximate flavor symmetries for weak-scale scalars in [2], flavor-specific scalar mediators in [3], and singly charged scalar LFU signals in [5] motivate this question.

questions.question: Which future e+e- collider channels are most decisive for low-mass neutral, singly charged, or doubly charged scalars whose LHC limits depend strongly on branching-fraction assumptions?
questions.rationale: The branching-fraction dependence of present LHC doubly charged scalar limits in [4] connects to the future lepton-collider low-mass scalar overview in [S1].

node_bcfe196ce25d.summary: This cluster studies how trilinear and quartic Higgs self-couplings can be extracted from single-Higgs, double-Higgs, and multi-Higgs production at current and future colliders.

questions.question: Which combination of double-Higgs production modes and boosted HH+jet kinematics can most robustly disentangle a modified trilinear Higgs self-coupling from other effective-field-theory deformations of the di-Higgs final state?
questions.rationale: This follows from the multi-channel LHC strategy in [1], the boosted and hard-recoil sensitivity in [2], and the EFT framing of di-Higgs searches in [5].

questions.question: What pattern of deviations between hZZ and hhh couplings would provide the cleanest collider evidence for non-decoupling heavy scalar loops in extended Higgs sectors?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [3], which emphasizes that hhh can deviate substantially even when hZZ remains close to the Standard Model value.

questions.question: At future proton-proton colliders, can the trilinear and quartic Higgs self-couplings be jointly constrained without relying on strong assumptions about new scalar resonances in multi-Higgs final states?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the future-collider self-coupling program in [S2] and the broader Higgs-potential perspective in [5].

node_bcfe196ce25d_1.summary: These papers analyze direct and indirect collider strategies for reconstructing the Higgs potential through precision measurements of Higgs self-interactions.

questions.question: Which collider observable would most decisively show that double-Higgs production is measuring the Standard Model trilinear self-coupling rather than compensating EFT or BSM effects in other Higgs interactions?
questions.rationale: The status review frames di-Higgs searches together with EFT interpretations and specific new-physics scenarios that can alter the same final states [5].

questions.question: Can boosted and unboosted HH analyses with a hard recoiling jet make gg to HH sensitivity to the trilinear coupling robust against backgrounds and kinematic degeneracies at the HL-LHC?
questions.rationale: The LHC study found enhanced sensitivity by combining boosted, unboosted, and hard-jet-recoil di-Higgs configurations [2].

questions.question: How can direct HH channels at HL-LHC and FCC-hh be combined with precision Higgs-factory constraints to distinguish nondecoupling two-Higgs-doublet loop effects in hhh from near-SM hZZ coupling?
questions.rationale: The two-Higgs-doublet analysis shows large loop deviations in hhh even when hZZ is SM-like, while Snowmass reports emphasize future precision Higgs and self-coupling measurements [3].

node_e0e360131919.summary: This cluster concerns triple and double Higgs production as probes of Higgs trilinear and quartic couplings in the Standard Model, EFT, and two-Higgs-doublet scenarios.

questions.question: In gg -> hh, which invariant-mass and final-state distributions can separate the Higgs trilinear coupling from ttbarhh and other dimension-six EFT coefficients at 14 TeV and 100 TeV colliders?
questions.rationale: This follows from the EFT double-Higgs analyses emphasizing m_hh information, bb gamma gamma simulations, and anomalous ttbarhh sensitivity in [1] and [2].

questions.question: Can hhjj production provide a clean extraction of HHH, WWhh, and ZZhh couplings once the finite-top-mass one-loop gluon-fusion contribution is included reliably?
questions.rationale: The need for a complete hhjj analysis beyond the m_t -> infinity approximation and its relevance for trilinear extraction are stressed in [4].

questions.question: How tightly can an improved finite-temperature sphaleron decoupling condition in singlet-extended Higgs sectors predict observable deviations of the triple Higgs coupling?
questions.rationale: The link between v_C/T_C, the one-loop daisy-resummed sphaleron energy, and enhanced triple-Higgs deviations is established in [5].

node_11d5f933727e.summary: These papers investigate Standard Model and MSSM Higgs production through photon, electron-positron, and hadron collider processes, including neutral Higgs pairs and associated squark production.

questions.question: How accurately can neutral MSSM Higgs-pair production in gluon-gluon collisions determine trilinear Higgs couplings once higher-order QCD, electroweak, and supersymmetric corrections are propagated through the LHC signal and background systematics?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the use of gg -> neutral Higgs pairs to reconstruct trilinear couplings in [1] and [2], together with the higher-order uncertainty program summarized in [4] and [5].

questions.question: Which combination of e+e-, hadron, and photon-collider Higgs-production channels would best resolve MSSM extended-Higgs-sector couplings rather than only confirm a Standard-Model-like light Higgs?
questions.rationale: This combines the spin/parity and background analysis for e+e- -> ZH in [3], the coupling reach discussed in [5], and the Snowmass assessment of photon-collider Higgs factories in [S1].

node_291ecf9214fb.summary: This cluster focuses on measuring Higgs production and decay at photon-photon colliders, especially gamma-gamma to Higgs to bottom quarks with realistic luminosity and background modeling.

questions.question: Can a photon-collider Higgs factory measure Gamma(H -> gamma gamma) precisely enough to detect the 5-7% loop-induced deviations predicted in TeV-scale Little Higgs scenarios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the predicted H -> gamma gamma width reduction in the Littlest Higgs model and the statement that a photon collider could probe it in [5].

questions.question: What luminosity spectrum and background modeling are required for gamma gamma -> H -> b bbar to outperform complementary e+e- Higgsstrahlung and WW-fusion measurements in the intermediate-mass Higgs range?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by intermediate-mass Higgs production and backgrounds in e+e- channels [1] and [4], H -> b bbar search complementarity in [3], and the photon-collider Higgs-factory framing in [S1].

questions.question: Can linearly polarized gamma gamma collisions provide a cleaner parity measurement of scalar versus pseudoscalar Higgs states than angular distributions in e+e- associated production?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of angular distributions for spin and parity in [1] and the photon-fusion parity prospects discussed in [2] and [S1].

node_e0bbc8c09b6a.summary: These works assess photon-collider sensitivity to Standard Model-like Higgs bosons through bottom-quark, photon, W-boson, and Z-boson decay channels.

questions.question: What single Higgs-collider measurement would most decisively establish the physics case for a photon collider rather than an e+e- Higgs factory alone?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the critical Snowmass discussion of photon-collider Higgs factories with and without an e+e- option [S1].

questions.question: Can percent-level measurements of Higgs to gamma gamma and Higgs to Z gamma separate multi-doublet, MSSM, and Little Higgs loop effects once QCD radiative corrections are included?
questions.rationale: This derives from QCD-corrected two-photon Higgs widths in extended Higgs sectors [1], Little Higgs loop-induced deviations [2], and extended-model contributions to the Higgs-gamma-Z coupling [4].

questions.question: How should realistic gamma gamma luminosity spectra and detector simulations be optimized to distinguish a SM-like Higgs, heavy MSSM Higgs bosons, and Higgs states without WW or ZZ couplings?
questions.rationale: This follows from the photon-photon collider study incorporating realistic luminosity spectra and detector simulations for these Higgs scenarios [5].

node_783bba11a955.summary: This cluster studies Higgs production with photons, vector bosons, or heavy-flavor final states at electron-positron, hadron, and photon-induced collider environments.

questions.question: Which associated-production channel gives the most model-independent spin-parity and coupling information for an intermediate-mass Higgs: e+e- to ZH angular distributions, hadronic VH with H to b bbar, or gamma plus Higgs production?
