questions.rationale: The e+e- ZH study emphasized angular distributions sensitive to Higgs spin and parity, while other representative papers develop VH and gamma-Higgs associated channels [1].

questions.question: How should Higgsstrahlung and WW-fusion interference be exploited near their cross-over region when Z to neutrino decays make the mechanisms experimentally inseparable?
questions.rationale: The e+e- calculation found positive interference between ZH and WW-fusion amplitudes that can be comparable to the individual cross sections in the cross-over region [3].

questions.question: If an intermediate-mass Higgs has dominant exotic h to eta eta decays, what combination of VH production, four-b tagging, and standard gamma gamma or b bbar modes gives the least ambiguous discovery strategy?
questions.rationale: The h to eta eta study showed that standard gamma gamma and VH to b bbar searches are substantially affected, while VH with eta eta to 4b can be complementary [4].

node_2727b489f226.summary: These papers analyze supersymmetric neutral Higgs production through gluon fusion, pair production, scalar-quark association, and related channels at hadron and lepton colliders.

questions.question: What neutral MSSM Higgs-pair channel would provide the cleanest practical access to trilinear Higgs couplings at future hadron colliders?
questions.rationale: The Higgs-pair studies identify neutral Higgs pair production in gluon-gluon collisions as a route to measuring trilinear Higgs couplings [1,2].

questions.question: Which higher-order corrections to MSSM Higgs masses, couplings, and decays remain phenomenologically limiting once real and complex parameters are included?
questions.rationale: The higher-order MSSM Higgs review emphasizes corrections to masses, couplings, production, and fermionic decays for real and complex parameters [3].

questions.question: Can bottom-parton and gluon-initiated descriptions of heavy-Higgs associated production be matched in a way that remains reliable across the charged-Higgs mass threshold?
questions.rationale: The associated top charged-Higgs study compared bottom-parton and gluon-initiated NLO differential cross sections and included top-decay contributions at low Higgs mass [5].

node_865ac4c8330b.summary: This cluster studies how Higgs production and decay measurements at the LHC and future colliders constrain Higgs couplings and possible new physics.

questions.question: How can off-shell Higgs production and Higgs-continuum interference be incorporated into precision coupling fits so that total-width constraints are not biased by the zero-width approximation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the demonstrated 1% and O(10%) off-shell effects in gg -> H -> VV in [1] and the ZZ off-shell width bound in [5].

questions.question: What is the most model-independent way to translate future Higgs coupling sensitivities into a new-physics scale when fits allow modified branching ratios, loop particles, anomalous top couplings, or invisible decays?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the universal Higgs-fit framework in [3], HXSWG benchmark parametrizations in [4], and Snowmass unitarity bounds on new-physics scales from coupling sensitivities in [S1].

node_82116d2326ce.summary: This cluster develops collider strategies to measure quark Yukawa couplings through rare Higgs decays, kinematic distributions, and associated production.

questions.question: Which collider observable can most cleanly lift degeneracies in Higgs Yukawa couplings by exploiting interference rather than rate information alone?
questions.rationale: This broad question is motivated by Yukawa profile-likelihood degeneracies and interference in single-top plus Higgs production [5] and by interference-sensitive quarkonium radiative Higgs decays [1].

questions.question: Can rare Higgs decays to quarkonium plus a photon become a quantitatively robust direct probe of the charm Yukawa once quarkonium and indirect-amplitude uncertainties are controlled?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposed H to J/psi gamma sensitivity to the Hcc coupling through interference of production mechanisms in [1].

questions.question: How precisely must boosted-Higgs plus jet and ttH measurements determine the top Yukawa to distinguish TeV-scale naturalness models from scenarios where the Standard Model remains stable to much higher scales?
questions.rationale: This combines boosted Higgs production as an alternative top-Yukawa probe [2] with the extreme vacuum-stability sensitivity to yt discussed in [4].

node_81f6ddace6f7.summary: This cluster focuses on measuring the top-quark Yukawa coupling using associated Higgs production with top quarks at hadron and electron-positron colliders.

questions.question: Can boosted Higgs plus jet production disentangle the top Yukawa coupling from short-distance new physics in gluon fusion with a precision competitive with direct ttbarH measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal to use a very boosted Higgs recoiling against a high-pT jet to resolve long- and short-distance contributions to gluon fusion [1].

questions.question: Which combination of ttbarH, t-channel single-top plus Higgs, and h -> gamma gamma data can fully lift the remaining sign and magnitude degeneracies in the top Yukawa coupling?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the use of interference in single-top plus Higgs production to break coupling-profile degeneracies and probe the sign of the Htt coupling [3,5].

questions.question: How precise must direct e+e- -> ttbarH measurements and QCD-corrected theory predictions become for the inferred top Yukawa coupling to meaningfully constrain electroweak vacuum stability up to inflationary or Planckian scales?
questions.rationale: This links the cosmological sensitivity of the critical top Yukawa value to direct e+e- ttbarH measurements including important QCD corrections [2,4].

node_82116d2326ce_1.summary: This cluster examines indirect and direct methods for constraining first- and second-generation quark couplings to the Higgs boson.

questions.question: What single experimental strategy can most directly distinguish a modified charm Yukawa from indirect Higgs-production effects: H to J/psi gamma, broader h to M gamma channels, or Higgs pT distributions?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] proposes H to J/psi gamma as a direct charm-Yukawa probe, [5] generalizes exclusive radiative decays, and [4] uses Higgs transverse-momentum spectra.

questions.question: Can the destructive interference in h to vector-meson plus photon decays be controlled theoretically well enough for first- and second-generation Yukawa measurements at the HL-LHC or future hadron colliders?
questions.rationale: Papers [3] and [5] show that h to M V and h to V gamma rates probe light-quark Yukawas through interference, with [5] including NLO QCD factorization, logarithmic resummation, and flavor mixing.

questions.question: How can Higgs-dependent Yukawa scenarios be constrained jointly by altered Higgs branching ratios, flavor-violating processes, and top decay t to h c?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] links Higgs-field-dependent Yukawas to modified Higgs branching fractions, new flavor violation, and observable t to h c decays.

node_bdaeb88940af.summary: This cluster uses LHC and Tevatron Higgs data to fit gauge and fermion couplings in model-independent or effective-field-theory frameworks.

questions.question: What global Higgs-fit framework can extract absolute couplings and the total width while consistently including off-shell VV production, Higgs-continuum interference, and the assumptions behind zero-width or universal-scaling approximations?
questions.rationale: This combines the coupling-extraction program of [2] and [4] with the off-shell and width limitations identified in [1] and [5].

questions.question: Which future Higgs coupling precisions would translate, through unitarity bounds, into model-independent lower bounds on the scale of new physics for composite Higgs, extra-doublet, supersymmetric, or loop-induced scenarios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the universal-fit methodology in [3] and the Snowmass proposal to convert coupling sensitivities into new-physics scale bounds in [S1].

node_36d9fc1b683d.summary: This cluster analyzes interference between Higgs-mediated resonances and continuum backgrounds in diphoton, diboson, and related collider final states.

questions.question: For which Higgs and new-physics searches does the narrow-width approximation fail at a level comparable to QCD corrections once off-shell decay matrix elements and spin correlations are retained?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1] and [4], which show that off-shell and decorrelation effects can significantly alter rates and reconstructed couplings beyond the narrow-width approximation.

questions.question: Can Higgs-continuum interference in gg to gamma gamma and gg to WW be incorporated into precision Higgs coupling fits without biasing the inferred resonance mass, width, or Lagrangian parameters?
questions.rationale: The question is based on the diphoton interference effects in [3] and [5] and the WW interference calculation with massive quark loops in [2].

questions.question: What level of higher-order QCD control over the diphoton apparent mass shift is needed for interferometric bounds on the Higgs width to become competitive with direct or off-shell constraints?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [5], which finds that next-to-leading QCD corrections reduce the interference-induced mass shift by about 40 percent.

node_2024f62cb611.summary: This cluster studies Higgs searches and coupling measurements in weak or vector boson fusion channels using forward-jet signatures for background suppression.

questions.question: How should VBF Higgs analyses jointly optimize forward-jet tagging and central-jet vetoes to retain sensitivity to H to tau tau while controlling Z to tau tau, Drell-Yan, W+jet, and bb backgrounds in realistic detector conditions?
questions.rationale: The original H to tau tau VBF studies rely on energetic forward jets for background suppression and identify these specific irreducible and reducible backgrounds [1,3].

questions.question: Can the H to WW and H to tau tau VBF channels be combined into a precision coupling measurement that preserves the low-background advantages seen in parton-level studies after realistic ATLAS-like simulation effects?
questions.rationale: The VBF WW studies find very high signal-to-background performance, while the ATLAS simulation emphasizes discovery potential from forward jets and suppressed central activity in both WW and tau tau modes [2,5].

questions.question: Which VBF observables most cleanly test the historical claim that H to WW could be the discovery mode for a light Higgs despite its small branching fraction near mH=115 GeV?
questions.rationale: The light-Higgs VBF analysis argued that the distinctive two-forward-jet topology could overcome the small H to WW branching fraction and yield a 5 sigma signal with sufficient luminosity [4].

node_52bea05b8e8b.summary: This cluster explores extended Higgs sectors with custodial triplets, including low-mass excesses, fiveplet scalars, and LHC constraints in Georgi-Machacek models.

questions.question: How can LHC Higgs coupling data and direct searches jointly test the Georgi-Machacek decoupling limit when hVV couplings may remain enhanced by O(v^2/M_new^2) effects?
questions.rationale: The decoupling behavior and possible enhanced hWW and hZZ couplings are described in [1] and generalized to exotic Higgs representations in [5].

questions.question: Which combination of fiveplet, triplet, and singlet mass measurements would provide a decisive collider test of custodial SU(2)_V in the Georgi-Machacek scalar spectrum?
questions.rationale: Mass degeneracy within custodial multiplets and characteristic H5, H3, and H1 couplings are proposed as tests of custodial symmetry in [2].

questions.question: Can nonstandard Higgs decays hide the simultaneous production-rate enhancements still allowed by B-physics, electroweak precision, perturbativity, and vacuum-stability constraints?
questions.rationale: The possibility that LHC Higgs-pole rate measurements are blind to allowed production enhancements if nonstandard decays exist is noted in [4].

node_3be92204960c.summary: This cluster covers precision theoretical calculations of Higgs masses, decays, electroweak observables, and vacuum stability including higher-order radiative corrections.

questions.question: What higher-order corrections are still needed to make MSSM neutral-Higgs mass predictions from spectrum codes mutually consistent at the level required by present Higgs-mass measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the two-loop and leading higher-order Higgs-mass calculations in FeynHiggs [4], the two-loop spectrum treatment in SPheno [5], and benchmark-code comparisons in [S1].

questions.question: How should uncertainties in the top Yukawa coupling, Higgs quartic matching, and three-loop running be combined to determine whether Standard Model vacuum metastability is a physical near-criticality signal or an artifact of perturbative inputs?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the NNLO Higgs-potential stability analysis in [2] and the extraction and high-scale running of SM parameters in [3].

questions.question: Can Higgs decay and SUSY-spectrum tools consistently incorporate light-higgsino naturalness scenarios so that branching ratios, electroweak observables, and collider signatures are computed with common radiative-correction conventions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in HDECAY's Higgs branching-ratio framework [1], SPheno's SUSY spectrum and decay calculations [5], and the Snowmass naturalness emphasis on small mu and light higgsinos [S2].

node_b91463a3f9e7.summary: This cluster investigates Higgs mass bounds and naturalness in supersymmetric models, especially how a 125 GeV Higgs constrains MSSM and non-minimal SUSY scenarios.

questions.question: Does electroweak naturalness in the MSSM reduce robustly to small mu and light higgsinos once a 125 GeV Higgs forces large A-terms or multi-TeV stops?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the 126 GeV Higgs naturalness analysis and the Snowmass argument that small mu and light higgsinos are the basic consequence of natural SUSY [4] and [S1].

questions.question: Can NMSSM lambda S H_u H_d models maintain percent-to-ten-percent tuning while satisfying perturbativity, collider, B-physics, dark-matter, and cosmological constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the NMSSM reviews and the claim that singlet-Higgs couplings can improve naturalness for a 125 GeV Higgs [1], [4], and [5].

node_40647f8cfa52.summary: This cluster studies upper bounds on the lightest supersymmetric Higgs boson mass across MSSM extensions, singlet models, and gauge-extended frameworks.

questions.question: After the measured Higgs mass, what residual parameter space in the NMSSM genuinely improves the lightest-Higgs mass naturalness problem without reintroducing tadpole, domain-wall, flavor, or dark-matter tensions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the NMSSM reviews' emphasis on Higgs-sector radiative corrections together with tadpole, domain-wall, collider, B-physics, and dark-matter constraints [1][3].

questions.question: How robust are supersymmetric scalar-mass upper bounds inferred from the Higgs mass when split or mini-split spectra include suppressed gaugino masses and RG trajectories that risk tachyonic squarks or up-type Higgs fields?
questions.rationale: This follows from split and mini-split scenarios where the measured Higgs mass constrains scalar masses while unification, dark matter, suppressed gaugino masses, and RG evolution restrict model building [2][5].

questions.question: Can future precision in the top mass, stop mixing parameter, and supersymmetric threshold scale reduce the model-independent MSSM lightest-Higgs upper-bound uncertainty enough to discriminate MSSM from singlet-extended Higgs sectors?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the two-loop MSSM upper-bound calculation in terms of the pole top mass, supersymmetry scale, tan beta, and stop mixing [4].

node_40647f8cfa52_1.summary: This cluster analyzes how perturbativity, gauge unification, singlet extensions, and extra gauge interactions modify the allowed mass of the lightest SUSY Higgs.

questions.question: How tightly does the measured Higgs mass bound the scalar superpartner scale in split and high-scale supersymmetry once complete threshold corrections and two-loop running are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from Higgs-mass matching studies in Split and High-Scale Supersymmetry, where NLO corrections reduce the predicted Higgs mass by a few GeV [4].

questions.question: Can gauge unification and dark matter remain sufficient organizing principles for supersymmetry if naturalness is abandoned, or do Higgs-mass limits force additional structure?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in Split Supersymmetry, which abandons the hierarchy criterion while retaining unification and dark matter as guiding principles [1].

questions.question: Which combinations of stop mixing, tan beta, and supersymmetry-breaking scale maximize the MSSM lightest Higgs mass without relying on parameter choices destabilized by higher-order corrections?
questions.rationale: This derives from the model-independent MSSM upper-bound calculation including one- and two-loop corrections as functions of MS, tan beta, and stop mixing Xt [2].

node_a47033401b3e.summary: These papers study NMSSM, nMSSM, twin SUSY, and related singlet or pseudo-Goldstone extensions that address the mu problem and reduce supersymmetric Higgs fine-tuning.

questions.question: In the NMSSM, what remaining parameter regions simultaneously minimize Higgs-sector fine tuning, evade direct Higgs searches through h -> aa decays, and satisfy dark-matter, B-physics, and cosmological constraints?
questions.rationale: This combines the low-fine-tuning h -> aa mechanism in [3] with the broader NMSSM constraints reviewed in [1] and [2].

questions.question: When do singlet fields genuinely reduce supersymmetric Higgs naturalness pressure rather than decoupling into an effective MSSM with altered neutralino signatures?
questions.rationale: [4] finds that singlets often decouple but can make the singlino the lightest neutralino, while [1] and [2] stress singlet-specific Higgs and neutralino phenomenology.

questions.question: Can strongly coupled or composite singlet-Higgs variants preserve gauge coupling unification and precision-electroweak consistency while allowing Higgs and superpartner masses in the 200-450 GeV range?
questions.rationale: The fat-Higgs construction in [5] claims this spectrum, precision-electroweak consistency, and maintained unification despite strong electroweak dynamics.

node_e56c1d23c6d1.summary: This cluster examines how the 125 GeV Higgs and null LHC new-physics searches strain traditional naturalness arguments and motivate nonminimal SUSY or revised fine-tuning principles.

questions.question: Which fine-tuning measure remains stable under changes of fundamental parameters, mediation scale, and soft-term universality assumptions after imposing a 125 GeV Higgs and LHC null searches?
questions.rationale: Focus-point supergravity stresses the dependence of naturalness on the choice of fundamental parameters, while Higgs-mass studies find very different tunings in MSSM, low-scale, high-scale, and singlet-extended models [2],[3].

questions.question: Are light higgsinos the irreducible experimental consequence of natural supersymmetry, or can radiative running and nonuniversal scalar sectors keep electroweak fine-tuning low with heavier colored superpartners?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass whitepaper identifies small mu and light higgsinos as the most basic naturalness implication, whereas nonuniversal and radiative-natural spectra allow heavier first/second-generation and even heavier third-generation scalars [1],[5],[S1].

questions.question: What collider or precision observable would most cleanly distinguish singlet-assisted natural Higgs sectors from MSSM large-A-term, focus-point, and radiative-natural explanations of the 125 GeV Higgs?
questions.rationale: A 126 GeV Higgs was argued to favor nonminimal SUSY such as lambda S H_u H_d, while alternative naturalness mechanisms rely on focus-point behavior or large negative trilinear terms [2],[3],[5].

node_876425774a2e.summary: These works compare electroweak fine-tuning measures across MSSM, CMSSM, NUHM, NUGM, and NMSSM scenarios under Higgs-mass, collider, and dark-matter constraints.

questions.question: Which fine-tuning measure most faithfully compares MSSM, low-mediation SUSY, and singlet-extended models once the Higgs mass near 125 GeV, gluino limits, light stops, and the mu parameter are imposed together?
questions.rationale: This question combines the critique of standard naturalness measures with post-Higgs comparisons showing that the MSSM is stressed while singlet extensions and small mu can improve tuning [1,3,S1].

questions.question: Can large stop A-terms, light stops, moderately large tan beta, and light higgsinos define a genuinely natural MSSM region that survives current collider constraints without shifting the tuning into mediation-scale assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that large top-squark A-terms and small mu can avoid severe MSSM fine-tuning, contrasted with the Higgs-mass dependence on mediation scale [1,2,S1].

questions.question: In NMSSM-like models with lambda S H_u H_d, how can one distinguish a true reduction of electroweak fine-tuning from new tuning introduced by large lambda, singlet-doublet mixing, or strong dynamics below unification?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that singlet couplings can improve Higgs naturalness while large lambda or mixing effects may introduce new sources of tuning [1,5].

node_e1a6fbdf57e8.summary: This cluster reassesses the conceptual, statistical, and phenomenological status of naturalness after the Higgs discovery and the absence of confirmed beyond-Standard-Model signals.

questions.question: What empirical result would most clearly falsify naturalness as a useful organizing principle for weak-scale new physics rather than merely forcing a revised fine-tuning measure?
questions.rationale: This broad reappraisal follows from the post-LHC naturalness discussions in [1] and [4] and the subjectivity of naturalness quantification emphasized in [5].

questions.question: Can finite naturalness define a predictive experimental program, or does ignoring uncomputable power divergences make its TeV-scale implications too model-dependent?
questions.rationale: The modified finite-naturalness criterion and its special parameter ranges for dark matter, neutrino masses, strong CP, vacuum instability, and inflation are proposed in [3].

questions.question: How should Higgs-rate constraints in diphoton, four-lepton, and vector-boson-fusion channels be combined with naturalness priors in Bayesian fits of supersymmetric or Little-Higgs-like simplified models?
questions.rationale: This joins the effective Higgs constraints on natural new physics in [2] with the Bayesian naturalness-prior treatment of the CMSSM in [5].

node_740ff28af63e.summary: These papers review natural weak-scale supersymmetry, sparticle mass bounds, nonuniversal soft terms, and collider or dark-matter prospects in light of LHC exclusions.

questions.question: Which definition of electroweak fine tuning gives a stable target spectrum for natural supersymmetry once nonuniversal soft terms, focus-point behavior, and radiative natural SUSY are all allowed?
questions.rationale: [1], [2], and [4] reach different natural spectra through nonuniversality, focus-point running, and radiative effects, while [5] stresses the subjectivity of naturalness measures.

questions.question: Can weak-scale supersymmetry remain natural if first- and second-generation scalars are multi-TeV while Higgsinos, stops, and gluinos evade current collider bounds?
questions.rationale: Heavy light-generation scalars in [1], multi-TeV scalar focus-point regions in [2], and light-Higgsino radiative natural spectra in [4] motivate this question.

questions.question: What collider and dark-matter search combination most directly tests the remaining natural-SUSY spectra compatible with a 125 GeV Higgs boson and flavor/CP constraints?
questions.rationale: [4] builds spectra with a 125 GeV Higgs and low electroweak fine tuning, and [5] reviews collider, Higgs-mass, dark-matter, flavor, and CP constraints on weak-scale supersymmetry.

node_baf27cbeae95.summary: This cluster studies fine-tuning, Veltman conditions, unitarity, scalar mass limits, and naturalness in two-Higgs-doublet, twin Higgs, and related extended Higgs models.

questions.question: Do tree-level unitarity, all-direction boundedness, and renormalization-group stability still allow a genuinely natural two-Higgs or extended Higgs spectrum once present scalar mass constraints are imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Lee-Quigg-Thacker mass bounds in two-doublet models and the combined unitarity and boundedness constraints in the type-II seesaw Higgs potential [1].

questions.question: Can pseudo-Goldstone twin-Higgs constructions retain sizable quartic couplings and multi-TeV cutoffs without reintroducing fine-tuning through the scalar potential constraints familiar from two-Higgs models?
questions.rationale: The partially Goldstone twin-Higgs model reduces fine-tuning by enforcing symmetry in quadratic terms while allowing asymmetric quartics [5].

node_015e8ebdbb52.summary: These works analyze Standard Model and extended-sector vacuum stability or metastability with a 125 GeV Higgs, emphasizing singlet dark matter, neutrinos, perturbativity, and top-mass dependence.

questions.question: What precision in the top mass, Higgs mass, and alpha_s is required to turn the Standard Model vacuum from a metastability indication into a decisive stability classification?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the NNLO and 3-loop RGE studies showing strong top-mass and theoretical-uncertainty dependence of the stability boundary in [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Does the near-vanishing of the Higgs quartic coupling at the Planck scale point to a calculable boundary condition, or is it only an accidental feature of current measured parameters?
questions.rationale: This follows from the near-criticality and high-scale phase-diagram interpretations discussed in [1] and [2].

questions.question: How robust are reheating-temperature bounds from electroweak vacuum stability once finite-temperature tunneling and current Higgs-top uncertainties are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: This is based on [4], which links finite-temperature stability after inflation to an upper bound on the reheating temperature that depends critically on Higgs and top masses.

node_65f09cc15052.summary: This cluster focuses on high-order renormalization-group and effective-potential calculations of Standard Model Higgs vacuum stability, metastability, and new-physics scale bounds.

questions.question: What single improvement in the top-quark mass, alpha_s, or Higgs-mass matching prescription would most decisively resolve whether the Standard Model vacuum is absolutely stable, metastable, or near the stability boundary up to the Planck scale?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question reflects the NNLO and three-loop analyses showing that the stability conclusion is controlled by precision matching and running, with theoretical uncertainties at the 1 GeV scale [1][2][3].

questions.question: Is the near-vanishing of the Higgs quartic coupling and beta function at high scales a statistically meaningful clue about ultraviolet physics, or an accidental consequence of current central values of Standard Model parameters?
questions.rationale: This follows from the phase-diagram analysis identifying the measured Higgs mass with near-critical values of the quartic, top Yukawa, and gauge couplings [2].

questions.question: How should finite-temperature vacuum decay constraints be consistently combined with inflationary reheating bounds when present uncertainties still allow both Planck-scale stability and high-scale metastability?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that a 124-126 GeV Higgs gives an instability around 10^11 GeV for central inputs while finite-temperature stability imposes reheating-temperature bounds sensitive to Higgs and top masses [4].

node_2424dd73604e.summary: These papers investigate Higgs mass bounds from triviality, vacuum stability, cutoff effects, effective operators, and possible new physics beyond the minimal Standard Model.

questions.question: What precision in the top mass, alpha_s, and Higgs matching conditions is needed to decide whether the observed Higgs mass implies absolute stability, metastability, or Planck-scale criticality of the Standard Model vacuum?
questions.rationale: Papers [1], [2], and [3] show that multi-loop running, effective-potential improvement, and one-loop matching conditions shift Higgs stability and upper bounds.

questions.question: Can Planck-scale boundary conditions for the Higgs quartic coupling be made predictive without assuming the Standard Model remains valid unchanged up to the Planck scale?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] derives Higgs mass ranges from generic quantum-gravity boundary conditions assuming the Standard Model plus right-handed neutrinos up to the Planck scale.

questions.question: Is multiple-point criticality a falsifiable explanation of Higgs and top masses, or can threshold and cutoff effects always be adjusted to preserve degenerate vacua?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] predicts top and Higgs masses by imposing two degenerate minima of the Standard Model effective potential near the Planck scale.

node_b4baeb440c16.summary: This cluster emphasizes precise and gauge-consistent treatments of the Standard Model effective potential, metastability bounds, and Higgs-mass stability limits.

questions.question: How can Standard Model vacuum decay rates and effective-potential stability bounds be formulated so that the NNLO critical Higgs mass and metastability lifetime are gauge-consistent physical statements?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the NNLO Higgs-potential stability analysis in [1] and the tunnelling-probability calculation in [4].

questions.question: What top-quark mass definition and conversion precision is required to decide whether the measured Higgs mass places the Standard Model in the stable, metastable, or unstable region?
questions.rationale: The critical dependence on the top mass is emphasized in [3] and [5], while the high-scale phase diagram is developed in [2].

questions.question: How do finite-temperature stability and reheating-temperature bounds shift when full two-loop matching, three-loop running, and correlated Higgs, top, and alpha_s uncertainties are propagated together?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finite-temperature stability bound in [3] and the precision two-loop and three-loop treatment in [2].

node_9438512e411e.summary: These works study how scalar or fermion singlet dark matter, Higgs portals, and seesaw neutrino sectors affect electroweak vacuum stability and perturbativity.

questions.question: Can a scalar-threshold correction from a heavy singlet stabilize the electroweak vacuum while preserving the relic-density and collider phenomenology of a viable singlet dark-matter candidate?
questions.rationale: Heavy singlet threshold effects stabilize the Higgs quartic, while singlet dark-matter studies impose relic-density, perturbativity, and collider constraints [2,3].

questions.question: In complex singlet models, what parameter region simultaneously supports one or two cold-dark-matter candidates, a strong first-order electroweak phase transition, and perturbative stability up to high scales?
questions.rationale: The complex singlet extension can contain viable dark matter and ingredients for a strong first-order electroweak phase transition, while later work studies vacuum stability and perturbativity [1,4].

questions.question: How much do gauge-invariant vacuum-stability analyses shift the allowed light singlet-like scalar parameter space relative to conventional gauge-dependent treatments?
questions.rationale: The complex scalar singlet study explicitly compares gauge-invariant vacuum-stability analysis with the conventional gauge-dependent procedure under dark-matter and electroweak constraints [4].

node_e4b9ba0e8be9.summary: This cluster derives tree-level boundedness, metastability, copositivity, and global-minimum conditions for two-Higgs-doublet and singlet-extended scalar potentials.

questions.question: Can analytic copositivity and tensor-eigenvalue criteria be extended into a practical necessary-and-sufficient stability test for general CP-conserving two-Higgs-doublet plus singlet scalar potentials?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the copositivity methods in [1] and the broader few-field scalar-potential criteria and tensor-eigenvalue approach in [5].

questions.question: How do tree-level metastability and global-minimum conditions in softly broken Z2 two-Higgs-doublet models change once LHC Higgs constraints are imposed together with perturbativity up to high scales?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the metastability bounds and LHC implications of [2] and the high-scale perturbativity and vacuum-stability constraints in [4].

questions.question: Can the simple quartic-coefficient condition for spontaneous CP breaking be embedded in automated scans that also guarantee absence of deeper charge-breaking vacua?
questions.rationale: This derives from [3], which shows that a charge- and CP-preserving minimum is global when it exists and gives a simple quartic condition for spontaneous CP breaking.

node_0344b634334e.summary: These papers analyze charge- and color-breaking minima, unbounded directions, and tunneling constraints on viable MSSM parameter space.

questions.question: How do full one-loop and two-loop MSSM effective potentials change the analytic charge- and color-breaking constraints derived from tree-level dangerous directions?
questions.rationale: Tree-level CCB and unbounded-direction constraints are strong [2], but successful electroweak breaking and Higgs minimization depend sensitively on complete one-loop and two-loop effective potentials [1],[5].

questions.question: Can metastability bounds based on vacuum tunneling be converted into reliable collider-scale constraints for MSSM spectra with many scalar fields and loop-corrected minima?
questions.rationale: False-vacuum tunneling can rule out MSSM parameter regions [3], and Vevacious was developed to find one-loop minima and compute tunneling times in models with many scalars [4].

node_2596fb108480.summary: This cluster studies one-loop QCD and electroweak corrections to MSSM particle decays, masses, and collider production involving squarks, Higgs bosons, charginos, and neutralinos.

questions.question: Can the large-tanβ resummation of bottom-Yukawa and tbH corrections be made precise enough to predict charged-Higgs branching ratios across the MSSM parameter space rather than only in dominant-limit formulae?
questions.rationale: The effective tbH Lagrangian paper resums dominant soft-SUSY and QCD corrections at large tanβ and derives simplified decay-rate formulae [2].

questions.question: Which flavor observables most cleanly test Higgs-mediated MSSM flavor violation after SU(2)xU(1)-breaking and electroweak-coupling effects are included in the effective Lagrangian?
questions.rationale: The large-tanβ flavor study shows that simplified SU(2)xU(1)-limit formulae can overestimate resummed effects and gives improved formulae for B observables [4].

questions.question: How should one consistently combine one-loop corrections to MSSM masses, couplings, electroweak observables, and superpartner decay rates in scans testing gauge and Yukawa unification?
questions.rationale: The precision-corrections paper computes complete one-loop mass and coupling corrections and discusses their impact on electroweak observables and coupling unification [1].

node_aed71278cd1a.summary: These works compute supersymmetric QCD and electroweak radiative corrections to top and single-top production at hadron colliders.

questions.question: Could any realistic pattern of left-right and intergenerational squark mixing raise supersymmetric t -> cV branching fractions into observable reach without conflicting with electroweak precision constraints?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in one-loop supersymmetric enhancements of t -> c gamma, cZ, and cg that remain below expected top-factory sensitivity, together with sizable scalar-quark effects in the rho parameter [1,2].

questions.question: How should gluon-exchange, gluino-exchange, and mixing-angle renormalization effects be combined consistently when using scalar-quark radiative corrections to constrain MSSM stop and sbottom sectors?
questions.rationale: This follows from two-loop QCD corrections to scalar-quark electroweak observables and order-alpha_s corrections to squark-pair production with left-right squark mixing [4,5].

questions.question: Do soft-gluon resummation effects in heavy-quark fusion substantially alter discovery or exclusion contours for charged Higgs and neutral scalar production in supersymmetric two-Higgs-doublet scenarios?
questions.rationale: The question derives from complete O(alpha_s) QCD corrections and multiple-soft-gluon resummation for charged scalar and pseudoscalar production via heavy-quark fusion [3].

node_61625a9f1a22.summary: This cluster focuses on supersymmetric QCD corrections to Higgs, squark, and top decays, especially channels involving stops, sbottoms, and large tan beta effects.

questions.question: Can the large-tan beta resummation of bottom-Yukawa SUSY-QCD effects in tbH+ and H+ -> tb be made quantitatively reliable once SU(2)xU(1)-breaking and electroweak g1,g2 effects are included beyond the semi-quantitative limit?
questions.rationale: This follows from the all-order large-tan beta resummation in [2] and the warning in [4] that simpler SU(2)xU(1)-limit formulae overestimate some effects.

questions.question: Which combination of B^0_{d,s} -> mu+mu-, Delta M_{d,s}, B -> X_s gamma, B -> tau nu, and charged-Higgs decay rates best disentangles Delta_b threshold corrections from Higgs-mediated flavor-changing neutral currents at large tan beta?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Higgs-mediated B-decay effects in [3], the combined weak-decay formalism in [4], and the large-tan beta flavor pattern discussed in [5].

questions.question: How far can compact one-loop approximations to MSSM masses and couplings be trusted across radiative-electroweak-symmetry-breaking parameter space when squarks, A terms, and Higgs states are heavy?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the complete one-loop MSSM correction program and compact approximations tested over unified parameter space in [1].

node_b0bc299d1d21.summary: These papers develop full one-loop renormalization treatments for chargino and neutralino masses, mixings, and decay widths in the MSSM and cMSSM.

questions.question: Which on-shell input choices for M1, M2, and mu minimize scheme dependence in one-loop chargino-neutralino pole masses when counterterms are fixed by only three measured masses?
questions.rationale: This follows from the complete one-loop chargino-neutralino calculation using two chargino and one neutralino pole masses to determine the on-shell counterterms [4].

questions.question: How should full one-loop chargino and neutralino mass shifts be propagated into collider exclusion maps for mu, M2, and tan(beta) when corrections can move LEP-style bounds by tens of GeV?
questions.rationale: This derives from findings that neutralino and chargino corrections can be several percent, exceed 20 percent for light neutralinos, and shift excluded parameter regions [3],[4].

questions.question: Can automated MSSM one-loop tools define a unified renormalization of chargino-neutralino mixing, sfermion mixing angles, and tan(beta) that remains stable for collider and astrophysical processes?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the SloopS program's automated on-shell treatment of chargino-neutralino and sfermion sectors and its comparison of different schemes [5].

node_38a1370079cf.summary: This cluster covers multi-loop QCD and electroweak corrections to Standard Model Higgs decay rates and related Higgs self-coupling calculations.

questions.question: How can the light-fermion two-loop electroweak corrections to gg→H, H→gg, and H→γγ be consistently combined with higher-order QCD decoupling and low-energy-theorem calculations to reduce the missing-higher-order uncertainty in Standard Model Higgs branching ratios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the sizable two-loop light-fermion effects reported for gluon fusion and H→gg/H→γγ in [1], the all-order low-energy-theorem relation to decoupling constants in [2], and the uncertainty budget emphasized in [5].

questions.question: What differential observables in H→WW/ZZ→4f remain most sensitive to missing mixed QCD-electroweak or higher-order final-state-radiation effects once the complex-mass scheme is used without on-shell or resonance expansions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the complete O(alpha) four-lepton and four-fermion calculations with complex gauge-boson masses and enhanced distribution-level corrections in [3] and [4].

questions.question: Can the remaining parametric uncertainties from charm, bottom, top masses and alpha_s be disentangled experimentally from genuine missing higher-order corrections in global fits to Higgs partial widths?
questions.rationale: This extends the uncertainty decomposition of Standard Model Higgs branching ratios in [5] into a forward-looking fit question.

node_38a1370079cf_1.summary: These works refine Standard Model Higgs decay predictions into photons, bottom quarks, and gluons using two-loop and higher-order perturbative calculations.

questions.question: Which missing higher-order QCD and electroweak terms now dominate the uncertainty budget for Standard Model Higgs branching ratios into gamma gamma, gg, bb, and four-fermion final states?
questions.rationale: The branching-ratio update explicitly separates parametric uncertainties from missing higher-order corrections across relevant Higgs decay channels [4].

questions.question: Can the complex-mass scheme be extended to deliver uniformly precise differential predictions for H -> WW/ZZ -> 4f across leptonic, semileptonic, and hadronic final states?
questions.rationale: The four-fermion decay calculations treat W and Z resonances without on-shell expansion using the complex-mass scheme and find sizable corrections in distributions [2,3].

questions.question: How can two-loop treatments of internal unstable particles and collinear-log cancellations be standardized for Higgs pseudo-observables such as H -> gamma gamma and H -> gg?
questions.rationale: The NNLO techniques paper develops recipes for unstable internal particles, collinear logarithms, and two-loop QCD/electroweak contributions to Higgs decay pseudo-observables [5].

node_c30988a11f63.summary: This cluster studies radiative corrections, renormalization schemes, decoupling behavior, and Higgs self-couplings in singlet, triplet, two-Higgs-doublet, and MSSM scalar sectors.

questions.question: What renormalization prescription gives the most stable extended-Higgs decay predictions when higher-order QCD decoupling, threshold matching, and low-energy Higgs-gluon theorems are combined?
questions.rationale: Three- and four-loop QCD decoupling relations reduce threshold uncertainties and connect heavy-quark decoupling constants to effective Higgs couplings through low-energy theorems [1,2,3].

questions.question: How should Higgs decay programs propagate scheme and model uncertainties for general two-Higgs-doublet and MSSM scalar sectors when radiative corrections and multi-body channels compete?
questions.rationale: HDECAY incorporates higher-order effects, multi-body channels, rescaled couplings, two-Higgs-doublet models, and MSSM Higgs sectors [4].

questions.question: Can any custodially constrained extended Higgs sector avoid worsening Rb and Ab at one loop while remaining compatible with precision Zbb data?
questions.rationale: General one-loop analyses found that charged-Higgs corrections in doublet, singlet, or custodially constrained larger-multiplet models tend to worsen agreement with experiment [5].

node_39bd9f5bf598.summary: These papers compute high-order electroweak and QCD corrections to precision observables such as the W mass, rho parameter, muon lifetime, and effective weak mixing angles.

questions.question: Which missing higher-order electroweak, QCD, and hadronic corrections most limit the combined precision reach of M_W, (g-2)_mu, and Z-pole observables?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the residual three-loop and hadronic uncertainties in [1], the remaining M_W theory error in [2], and the practical QCD correction systematics reviewed in [5].

questions.question: Can a uniform treatment of heavy-mass expansions, decoupling, matching, and master-integral reductions remove scheme and truncation ambiguities across rho-parameter, Z -> b bbar, and hadronic Z-decay predictions?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the complete alpha alpha_s Z -> b bbar calculation in [3], the three-loop rho-parameter computation in [4], and the matching and heavy-mass methods summarized in [5].

node_2fc99844e24d.summary: This cluster develops precise one-loop and two-loop predictions for MSSM neutral Higgs boson masses, including QCD corrections, complex parameters, and spectrum-code implementations.

questions.question: What set of missing higher-order corrections now dominates the theoretical uncertainty of MSSM neutral-Higgs mass predictions across real and complex parameter space?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the estimated uncalculated higher-order shifts of up to about 3 GeV in [3] and the complex-parameter one-loop treatment in [4].

questions.question: Can diagrammatic on-shell calculations, DRbar hybrid schemes, and RG-improved leading-log formulae be reconciled into a common uncertainty prescription for m_h and Higgs mixing angles?
questions.rationale: This follows from the FeynHiggs diagrammatic implementation in [1], the hybrid renormalization scheme in [4], and analytical RG-improved formulae in [5].

questions.question: How do stop mixing, tan beta, and M_A jointly control the upper bound on the lightest MSSM Higgs mass once leading two-loop QCD, electroweak, and higher-order QCD effects are included?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the two-loop QCD analysis and parameter scans for the lightest Higgs upper bound in [2].

node_b8fe46c2e8cf.summary: These works improve predictions for the light CP-even MSSM Higgs mass by combining fixed-order, effective-field-theory, renormalization-group, and three-loop methods.

questions.question: How can fixed-order, effective-potential, and EFT/RG-resummed calculations be combined so that the MSSM light-Higgs mass prediction reaches sub-GeV theoretical uncertainty across split and nondegenerate stop-sbottom spectra?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the need for Higgs-mass accuracy comparable to experiment [5] and the general-threshold two-loop leading-log effective-potential treatment with arbitrary stop and sbottom parameters [2].

questions.question: Which higher-order logarithmic and nonlogarithmic corrections dominate the residual two-GeV-level uncertainty in analytic approximations to MSSM Higgs masses at large stop mixing and variable mA?
questions.rationale: This derives from the simple approximation scheme targeting two-GeV accuracy [3] and the analytic two-loop leading-log formulae for arbitrary mA, tan beta, and stop mixing [1].

questions.question: Can analytical formulae for MSSM Higgs masses and couplings remain reliable in regions with light stops while preserving the correlations among masses, CP-even mixing angles, and trilinear Higgs couplings?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the light-stop generalization of the two-loop leading-log Higgs spectrum [2] and the RG-improved calculation of masses, mixing angles, and trilinear couplings [4].

node_599e5a8bcd0b.summary: This cluster emphasizes Feynman-diagrammatic calculations of MSSM neutral Higgs masses and mixings, including momentum-dependent two-loop QCD effects and FeynHiggs implementations.

questions.question: Which missing higher-order diagrammatic corrections to the MSSM neutral-Higgs mass matrix now dominate the residual mh uncertainty after complete one-loop, leading two-loop QCD, electroweak two-loop, and higher-order QCD improvements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the FeynHiggs correction content [1] and the estimate that uncalculated higher orders can shift the lightest Higgs mass by up to 3 GeV [3].

questions.question: How should momentum-dependent two-loop QCD effects and scalar-top mixing be incorporated into public Higgs-mass tools without degrading the on-shell parameter interpretation used in phenomenological scans?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the leading two-loop QCD diagrammatic calculations for arbitrary Higgs and scalar-top parameters [2,5] and their implementation philosophy in FeynHiggs [1].

questions.question: Can the complex-MSSM Higgs-sector calculation be extended with fully phase-dependent two-loop corrections and consistent external-Higgs wave-function normalization for precision collider observables?
questions.rationale: This derives from the complete one-loop complex-parameter treatment, hybrid on-shell/DRbar renormalization, and external-Higgs normalization factors in the complex MSSM [4].

node_a1ed35dd3ef3.summary: These papers develop and standardize software for computing supersymmetric spectra, Higgs and sparticle decays, model files, and interfaces among collider and dark matter tools.

questions.question: What benchmark suite would expose the residual theory and convention differences among modern SUSY spectrum, Higgs-decay, and model-generation tools as sharply as the Snowmass 2001 comparison did for earlier programs?
questions.rationale: Snowmass compared spectra from ISAJET, SUSYGEN, and PYTHIA, while HDECAY, SPheno, SOFTSUSY, SuSpect, and SARAH define overlapping modern calculations and interfaces [S1], [1], [2], [3], [4], [5].

questions.question: Can automated model builders generate SPheno-class spectrum and decay codes with transparent uncertainty estimates for two-loop RGEs, one-loop masses, and Higgs-sector higher-order corrections?
questions.rationale: SPheno, SOFTSUSY, and SuSpect document specific loop orders and approximations, while SARAH can generate SPheno source code for user-defined models [2], [3], [4], [5].

questions.question: How should Higgs and sparticle decay tools standardize inputs, schemes, and interfaces so branching-ratio predictions remain reproducible across MSSM and nonminimal SUSY extensions?
questions.rationale: HDECAY computes SM and MSSM Higgs branching ratios, while SPheno and SARAH extend decay-width and branching-ratio calculations across SUSY and non-SUSY model files [1], [2], [5].

node_85c617d50d8f.summary: This cluster revisits loop calculations for Higgs decays to photons or Z gamma, focusing on gauge choices, regularization, dispersion methods, and the W-boson contribution.

questions.question: What regulator-independent criterion uniquely fixes the finite W-loop contribution to H -> gamma gamma, resolving the decoupling versus nondecoupling tension between dimensional-regularization and direct unitary-gauge calculations?
questions.rationale: The question comes from the contrast between the standard finite, gauge-independent dimensional-regularization result and the revisited unitary-gauge calculation claiming decoupling [1].

questions.question: Can equivalence-theorem schemes with C_mod equal to unity in all R_xi gauges provide a practical cross-check of radiative Higgs amplitudes involving longitudinal gauge bosons or Goldstone modes?
questions.rationale: This is based on the use of the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem as a check on H -> gamma gamma and on schemes that remove radiative modification factors in R_xi gauges [3].

node_6b5b41b0c59c.summary: These works study supersymmetric particle production, search strategies, mass reconstruction, and implications of LHC constraints for MSSM scenarios including stops, gluinos, and neutralinos.

questions.question: What benchmark language can best connect full MSSM scenarios, simplified-model masses and cross sections, and future e+e- collider measurements so that LHC exclusions remain interpretable if a superpartner signal appears elsewhere?
questions.rationale: This follows from the tension between consensus MSSM benchmark points, simplified-model reporting, and the ILC/CLIC role in characterizing new particles [4], [5], [S2].

questions.question: How small must the theoretical uncertainty on squark and gluino production cross sections become before hadron-collider rates can provide competitive superpartner mass information rather than only exclusion limits?
questions.rationale: The NLO SUSY-QCD calculation showed that reducing renormalization and factorization scale dependence directly improves mass extraction from production cross sections [2].

questions.question: Which semi-invisible mass-reconstruction variables remain robust for SUSY pair production once realistic backgrounds, detector resolution, and missing-transverse-momentum systematics are included?
questions.rationale: The proposed transverse-mass-like variable was explicitly tested without backgrounds or measurement errors, leaving its realistic LHC reach open [3].

node_d26263f1ac8e.summary: This cluster uses LHC searches, Higgs data, precision observables, flavor measurements, and dark matter constraints to fit and reinterpret constrained supersymmetric models.

questions.question: How should constrained-SUSY global fits combine legacy benchmark lines, simplified-model limits, Higgs-mass constraints, relic-density constraints, and null LHC searches without hiding viable pMSSM-like corners?
questions.rationale: The question arises from the evolution from SPS benchmark points [1][S1] to simplified-model interpretations [2][4] and Snowmass pMSSM benchmarks that evade current searches while fitting the Higgs mass and relic density [S2].

questions.question: Which experimentally observable mass-edge, branching-ratio, and heavy-flavor measurements would be sufficient to invert a future jets-plus-missing-energy excess into a few-percent constrained-SUSY parameter determination?
questions.rationale: Precision LHC SUSY studies emphasize using observable distributions to determine mass combinations and branching ratios, while simplified models organize jet structure, electroweak decays, and heavy-flavor content [4][5].

node_3862b421e18b.summary: These papers perform frequentist and Bayesian analyses of CMSSM, NUHM, and pMSSM parameter spaces under LHC exclusions, XENON100 limits, and cosmological data.

questions.question: Are fixed SUSY benchmark points still an adequate language for comparing future searches, or should constrained-model and pMSSM sensitivity be expressed through scan-derived spokes?
questions.rationale: The SPS benchmarks provided consensus search targets, while later Snowmass pMSSM work uses benchmark models and spokes to compare future collider reach [1,S2,S3].

questions.question: Which assumptions in CMSSM and NUHM global fits dominate the inferred probability regions: priors, dark-matter relic density treatment, Higgs-mass constraints, or collider exclusions?
questions.rationale: The MCMC CMSSM study used Bayesian priors with collider, cosmological, and theoretical uncertainties, while pMSSM scans showed broader predictions [3,5].

questions.question: What future combination of collider searches, Higgs-coupling precision, anomalous muon magnetic moment, and dark-matter measurements can most efficiently resolve constrained MSSM, NMSSM, and pMSSM scenarios?
questions.rationale: The constrained NMSSM comparison focused on experimentally resolving models, and Snowmass pMSSM scans emphasize complementarity across collider, precision, cosmological, and rare frontiers [4,S3].

node_1a5f0fb08af0.summary: This cluster assesses the discovery potential and post-Run-I status of LHC supersymmetry searches across missing-energy, multijet, multilepton, and model-independent mass-hierarchy channels.

questions.question: After the failure of simple early mSUGRA expectations, what model-independent mass-hierarchy variables best preserve the discovery logic of simultaneous jets, missing-energy, and multilepton excesses?
questions.rationale: This follows from early mSUGRA studies predicting correlated missing-energy, multijet, and multilepton signals, and from post-Run-I reassessments of viable SUSY models [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: Which SUSY scenarios still make the HL-LHC gluino and electroweakino reaches quoted for gaugino-unified models a reliable guide, and which compressed or nonminimal spectra evade that framing?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Snowmass LHC14 reach estimates for gluino and W h plus missing-energy channels and the post-Run-I survey of surviving SUSY model classes [S1], [5].

questions.question: Can relic density, b to s gamma, muon g-2, Higgs data, and direct LHC searches still define a coherent constrained-SUSY target space, or do they mainly motivate abandoning CMSSM-style parameter scans?
questions.rationale: The question derives from mSUGRA reach studies incorporating relic density, b to s gamma, and a(mu), and from later discussions of naturalness and parsimony after LHC Run I [3], [5].

node_485eb65aea2d.summary: These works estimate LHC reach for minimal supergravity supersymmetry using jets, missing energy, multileptons, photons, and related channels at different collision energies and luminosities.

questions.question: After current LHC limits, is the mSUGRA/CMSSM discovery paradigm still best tested by simultaneous jets plus missing energy and multilepton signals, or by narrower electroweak channels such as W h plus missing energy?
questions.rationale: Early mSUGRA studies argued that gluino or squark production below about 1 TeV should yield several simultaneous lepton and missing-energy signals, while Snowmass projections emphasize both gluino pairs and electroweakino W h channels [1].

questions.question: Which observable pattern in jets, missing energy, photons, leptonically decaying Z bosons, and b or tau enriched final states would most cleanly distinguish large-tan beta mSUGRA from other SUSY spectra?
questions.rationale: Updated reach studies added photon and Z channels, while large-tan beta analyses emphasized enhanced tau and b final states from altered slepton and squark spectra [3].

questions.question: Can dijet searches without explicit missing energy provide a robust discovery or exclusion handle on squark production in compressed or background-dominated mSUGRA regions?
questions.rationale: Dijet strategies were proposed to search for supersymmetry without invoking missing energy and suggested discovery reach for squarks as heavy as about 1.7 TeV [5].

node_555abe7b0991.summary: This cluster summarizes ATLAS and CMS supersymmetry search programs, emphasizing Run 1 and Run 2 exclusions, compressed spectra, long-lived particles, and electroweak-scale scenarios.

questions.question: What minimal combined ATLAS/CMS search suite would close the remaining natural-SUSY gaps for spectra lacking large missing energy, top quarks, or high object multiplicity?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by the claim in [3] that a small set of searches excludes most accessible natural spectra while leaving identifiable gaps.

questions.question: How can compressed spectra, long-lived particles, and R-parity-violating scenarios be folded into coverage metrics that go beyond simplified-model mass exclusions?
questions.rationale: The broadened Run 2 ATLAS program including scenarios with or without R parity and long-lived sparticles is summarized in [4].

questions.question: Which hard-jet resonance plus soft-lepton and missing-energy strategies can make baryon-number-violating natural stop scenarios visible without relying on standard large-MET searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from the overlooked hard-jet resonance and soft-lepton signatures proposed for RPV natural supersymmetry in [5].

node_742e327497c8.summary: These papers examine how LHC and future linear colliders can measure sparticle masses, branching ratios, couplings, and underlying supersymmetry-breaking parameters.

questions.question: Can LHC endpoint and minimum-mass methods, combined with linear-collider threshold scans, reconstruct SUSY-breaking parameters with enough precision to discriminate mSUGRA from enlarged MSSM parameter spaces?
questions.rationale: This combines LHC mass-combination measurements in [1] and [4] with LHC/LC complementarity in [S1] and the SPA program in [2].

questions.question: How should higher-order corrections and scheme conversions be standardized so that masses, mixings, widths, production cross sections, relic density, and direct-detection observables can be fit consistently?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by the SPA convention and shared program framework described in [2].

questions.question: Can chargino and neutralino mass and cross-section measurements determine CP-violating phases at the level needed to test EDM-cancellation regions rather than only exclude them?
questions.rationale: This follows from the linear-collider phase sensitivity and EDM-constraint cancellation scans in [5].

node_6b6d186b39e2.summary: This cluster presents simplified-model frameworks and automated recasting tools such as CheckMATE, SModelS, and MadAnalysis for confronting new-physics models with LHC data.

questions.question: What minimal likelihood-information standard from ATLAS and CMS would make automated recasts in CheckMATE, MadAnalysis 5, and related tools statistically faithful enough for global fits rather than only exclusion estimates?
questions.rationale: This follows from the automated reinterpretation goals of [3], [4], and [5], where detector simulation and analysis details are central limiting issues.

questions.question: How can simplified-model result grids be systematically extended to cover non-simplified cascade topologies where optimized searches lose sensitivity, such as the SO(10) case with fewer b-jets than the nominal gluino simplified model?
questions.rationale: This derives from the simplified-model program in [1] and [2] and the Snowmass comparison showing weakened bounds for a specific SO(10) topology in [S2].

questions.question: At future 14, 33, and 100 TeV proton colliders, which systematic-error and pileup treatments dominate the uncertainty when recasting gluino-neutralino, squark-neutralino, and gluino-squark simplified planes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [S1], which compares future collider reach in SUSY simplified models and emphasizes systematic errors and pileup.

node_38c3a435bbfb.summary: These works study neutralino and chargino production, compressed electroweakino spectra, Higgsino scenarios, and collider constraints in MSSM settings with light electroweak superpartners.

questions.question: In compressed Wino or Higgsino spectra, which LHC and ILC trigger, missing-energy, soft-particle, and polarization observables can close the gaps left by conventional electroweakino searches?
questions.rationale: This derives from nearly degenerate Wino scenarios with soft decay products and from collider studies using polarized beams and comparative LHC/ILC searches [3], [4], [5], [S1].

questions.question: How far can bottom-up natural SUSY with light higgsinos around 100-300 GeV be tested by combining Wh, same-sign diboson, VBF, and chargino-neutralino pair-production channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from naturalness arguments for light higgsinos and Snowmass studies of Wh, diboson, VBF, and electroweakino search reach [1], [S1], [S2], [S3].

questions.question: If only the lightest chargino or neutralino states are kinematically accessible, what measurements are sufficient to reconstruct M1, M2, mu, tan beta, and possible CP phases?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in analyses showing how chargino and neutralino systems can be reconstructed using cross sections, asymmetries, polarization, and neutralino mixing information [4], [5].

node_69d9e885d1a6.summary: This cluster focuses on chargino production and decay at lepton and hadron colliders as a way to determine mixing angles, masses, and fundamental supersymmetric parameters.

questions.question: What minimal set of polarized cross sections, asymmetries, and chargino polarization observables is sufficient to reconstruct M2, |mu|, tan beta, and the CP phase when only the lightest chargino is accessible?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the need for transverse beam polarization or final-state chargino polarization to determine mixing angles in first-phase e+e- running [3].

questions.question: How do NLO SUSY-QCD corrections and radiative electroweakino mass shifts propagate into collider parameter extraction and dark-matter interpretations of the chargino-neutralino sector?
questions.rationale: This combines stable NLO hadron-collider production predictions [1] with radiative corrections altering the mapping into mu and gaugino-mass parameter space [5].

node_b9ee3b6dc631.summary: These papers study collider limits and search strategies for charginos and neutralinos, especially compressed higgsino, wino, and bino spectra with missing energy signatures.

questions.question: What combination of ISR-assisted soft-lepton, disappearing-track, VBF, and same-sign diboson searches closes the remaining coverage gaps for compressed higgsino and wino spectra required by natural SUSY?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the compressed higgsino strategy of [4], the disappearing-track wino phenomenology of [2,3], and the Snowmass comparison of LHC electroweakino channels in [S1,S3].

questions.question: How precisely must the charged-neutral wino mass splitting and lifetime be predicted and propagated through detector simulations to make disappearing-track limits robust across nearly pure wino models?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from [3], which shows that the LHC reach for wino LSPs is sensitive to the two-loop charged-neutral mass splitting.

questions.question: Can LHC and ILC electroweakino measurements distinguish bino-, wino-, and higgsino-like dark matter in the natural-SUSY parameter region with mu around 100-300 GeV?
questions.rationale: This derives from the natural-SUSY spectra in [1,5] and the comparative LHC/ILC reach study over bino, wino, and higgsino LSP cases in [S1].

node_a76f46aa1444.summary: This cluster focuses on chargino, neutralino, and selectron production at polarized lepton and electron-photon colliders as precision probes of supersymmetric parameters.

questions.question: If only the lightest chargino pair is kinematically accessible, what combination of longitudinal and transverse beam polarizations removes the residual ambiguity in the chargino mixing angles and CP phase of mu?
questions.rationale: Chargino reconstruction studies found that transverse polarization is needed to determine mixing angles unambiguously when only the lightest charginos are accessible [3].

questions.question: Can threshold scans of selectron and smuon production deliver SUSY mass measurements robust against nonzero-width, Coulomb rescattering, and irreducible supersymmetric-background effects?
questions.rationale: Slepton threshold studies included nonzero-width and Sommerfeld or Coulomb rescattering corrections and designed cuts to control irreducible SUSY backgrounds [1][5].

questions.question: Which neutralino and chargino decay angular asymmetries are most sensitive to complex SUSY couplings once full production-decay spin correlations and polarized beams are included?
questions.rationale: Neutralino and chargino studies showed that spin correlations strongly affect angular distributions and forward-backward asymmetries and depend on SUSY parameters and beam polarization [2][4].

node_00aab05e412e.summary: These works analyze light top-squark searches at the LHC and Tevatron in scenarios motivated by naturalness, electroweak baryogenesis, dark matter, and compressed spectra.

questions.question: What kinematic observables beyond missing transverse energy can close the stealth-stop region where stop events mimic Standard Model top-pair production?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the top-background problem in direct stop searches [3] and the Snowmass finding that near-degenerate stop-top-neutralino kinematics make standard searches challenging [S1].

questions.question: How should collider limits combine NLO stop production cross sections with naturalness-motivated spectra containing light stops and sbottoms but heavy first- and second-generation sfermions?
questions.rationale: This follows from NLO SUSY-QCD stop production calculations that raise and stabilize cross sections [1] and the bottom-up light-third-generation SUSY framework [2].

questions.question: Can the stop-neutralino coannihilation window with 15-30 GeV mass splitting be tested without losing the dark-matter and electroweak-baryogenesis motivation of the parameter region?
questions.rationale: This derives from the relic-density analysis in which light stops support electroweak baryogenesis and neutralino dark matter, but coannihilation creates a difficult compressed region [4].

node_00aab05e412e_1.summary: This cluster examines phenomenologically viable light stop spectra in MSSM, NMSSM, and gauge-mediated models under Higgs, dark matter, and direct-search constraints.

questions.question: Which compressed or stealth stop regions remain viable after combining NLO stop-production rates, top-background endpoint variables, and spin-correlation strategies at 14 TeV?
questions.rationale: This combines the stabilized NLO stop cross sections in [1], the M_T2^W endpoint strategy against ttbar in [3], and the stealth-stop spin-correlation challenge described in [S1].

questions.question: Can natural light-stop spectra simultaneously satisfy radiative electroweak stability, flavor and CP constraints, Higgs-sector constraints, and neutralino relic density without relying on special co-annihilation mass splittings?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the bottom-up natural third-generation SUSY scenario and indirect constraints in [2] and the Higgs-, Z-, and stop-co-annihilation relic-density regions in [4].

questions.question: How should hadronic stop searches be optimized when the stop-neutralino spectrum transitions between large missing-energy top decays and the 15-30 GeV co-annihilation mass gap?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the stop-neutralino co-annihilation mass gap in [4] and the all-hadronic stop reach studies for top plus light neutralino final states in [S2].

node_00aab05e412e_2.summary: These papers use LHC searches, Higgs measurements, and dark matter bounds to constrain light stops and their decay modes in supersymmetric models.

questions.question: Which stop decay topologies remain least constrained after combining NLO stop-pair cross sections, all-hadronic top plus neutralino searches, and RPV cascade searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from stabilized NLO stop production predictions [1], Snowmass all-hadronic stop reach [S1], and weak sensitivity to some UDD and tau-rich LQD RPV cases [4].

questions.question: Can sub-TeV stops simultaneously satisfy Higgs signal strengths, mW, b to s gamma, direct collider bounds, and the observed Higgs mass without abandoning natural SUSY assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in global Natural SUSY fits where Higgs, precision, flavor, and collider constraints leave allowed regions but make the Higgs mass difficult with sub-TeV stops [5].

questions.question: How compressed can the stop-neutralino spectrum be while still permitting electroweak baryogenesis, the observed relic density, and collider discovery through coannihilation-region signatures?
questions.rationale: This derives from light-stop electroweak baryogenesis scenarios in which the relic density can be set by stop coannihilation with a 15-30 GeV stop-neutralino splitting [3].

node_c8802e0e78c4.summary: This cluster develops methods to find top squarks through difficult decay channels, compressed regions, same-sign dileptons, and top-background rejection.

questions.question: Which endpoint-based kinematic variables can still separate stop pair production from dileptonic and semileptonic ttbar backgrounds in compressed or near-top-mass spectra?
questions.rationale: The M_T2^W strategy improves single-lepton stop sensitivity by exploiting background endpoints tied to on-shell W constraints [1].

questions.question: Can spin-correlation observables provide a systematics-limited discovery or exclusion strategy for stealth stops at 14 TeV when PDF and top-production uncertainties are included?
questions.rationale: The stealth-stop studies identify Delta phi between leptons as a robust spin-correlation handle but stress that PDF and top-production systematics can limit the search [4], [S1].

questions.question: How should experimental stop searches cover regions where four-body decays to b chi_1^0 f f' dominate over the loop-induced c chi_1^0 mode?
questions.rationale: The light-stop decay analysis shows that four-body decays can dominate across wide MSSM parameter regions, affecting searches that assumed charm plus neutralino final states [3].

node_f5c8c95b24e6.summary: These works investigate how second- and third-generation squark mixing modifies squark, gluino, and Higgs decays while remaining compatible with flavor constraints.

questions.question: How far can right-handed stop-scharm mixing be increased before D-Dbar mixing, electroweak precision data, and collider limits jointly eliminate the flavoured-naturalness window?
questions.rationale: Large top-charm squark mixing is argued to survive low-energy flavor constraints and reduce stop bounds, while D-Dbar mixing directly constrains the up-squark mass matrix [1,3].

questions.question: Which LHC search topology best covers non-minimal second- and third-generation squark flavor violation: charm plus missing energy, same-sign tops, flavor-changing Higgs decays, or mixed squark-gaugino cascades?
questions.rationale: The representative studies identify unsearched LHC signatures from stop-scharm mixing, radiative bcH+ and tch0 couplings, and altered squark/gaugino production and decay chains [2,3,5].

questions.question: Can reinterpretations of multijet plus missing-energy searches be made robust against departures from U(2) universality and MFV assumptions in first- and second-generation squark spectra?
questions.rationale: The light nondegenerate squark analysis shows that standard LHC squark limits weaken strongly when the usual eightfold degeneracy assumption is relaxed [4].

node_d8b5428c2502.summary: This cluster studies gluino phenomenology in scenarios with light, heavy-LSP, or long-lived gluinos, including collider signatures, decay patterns, and QCD constraints.

questions.question: What search observable would best close the gap between model-independent jets plus missing-energy limits and detector-dependent signatures of stable or long-lived gluino-containing hadrons?
questions.rationale: This follows from the model-independent visible-energy and missing-energy proposal and from the observation that gluino-LSP limits depend strongly on detector path length and charge exchange behavior [2],[3].

questions.question: In split or Dirac-gaugino scenarios, how can searches distinguish suppressed squark production from genuinely heavy or long-lived gluino phenomenology when the LSP mass weakens standard simplified-model bounds?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in split-SUSY long-lived gluino signals and the Snowmass finding that Dirac gluinos suppress jets plus MET sensitivity, especially for heavier LSPs [1],[S1].

questions.question: Can m_T2-based gluino mass reconstruction remain robust when gluino decays involve compressed spectra, metastable R-hadrons, or sgluon-like color-octet states with substantial QCD jet activity?
questions.rationale: This extends the gluino stransverse-mass proposal to the jet-rich and color-octet contexts emphasized in gluino decay and sgluon phenomenology [4],[5].

node_f21dce66eb22.summary: These papers explore collider signatures of gauge-mediated supersymmetry, including gravitino LSPs, long-lived sleptons, photons, trileptons, and Tevatron or LHC discovery reach.

questions.question: For gauge-mediated SUSY, which NLSP identity and lifetime range still yields a uniquely discoverable collider signature once displaced vertices, photons plus missing energy, kinks, and long-lived sleptons are analyzed together?
questions.rationale: The original gauge-mediation study emphasizes gravitino LSP phenomenology with gaugino, Higgsino, or slepton NLSP decays inside detectors, producing displaced or photon-rich signatures [1].

questions.question: Can the classic diphoton plus missing-energy strategy be generalized beyond nearly prompt neutralino-to-gravitino photon decays without losing the inclusive reach that made the Tevatron and LEP searches powerful?
questions.rationale: The Tevatron/LEP analysis focused on a light gravitino and nearly 100 percent neutralino branching to gravitino plus photon inside the detector, making inclusive diphoton plus missing-energy searches central [2].

questions.question: How do light, strongly mixed staus that modify the Higgs gamma gamma rate reshape gauge-mediated spectra and long-lived-slepton search priorities?
questions.rationale: The light-stau study connects large stau mixing, tan beta, and the Higgsino mass parameter to enhanced Higgs diphoton production and distinctive stau phenomenology [5].

node_7a62e23376eb.summary: This cluster centers on Tevatron and LEP searches for supersymmetry through trilepton, photon, slepton, chargino-neutralino, and light-gravitino signatures.

questions.question: What Tevatron or LEP result would have most decisively distinguished low-energy gauge mediation with a gravitino LSP from supergravity-inspired scenarios with a stable neutral LSP?
questions.rationale: This broad retrospective question follows from the contrast between gauge-mediated gravitino signatures and the SUGRA working group’s neutral stable LSP framework [1,4].

questions.question: Can the inclusive gamma gamma plus missing transverse energy strategy be reinterpreted model-independently across neutralino, slepton, chargino, and selectron production topologies with detector-scale NLSP decays?
