questions.rationale: This is grounded in the inclusive diphoton plus missing-energy searches and the detector-decay phenomenology of neutralino or slepton NLSPs [1,2,5].

questions.question: How much of the CDF ee gamma gamma plus missing transverse energy event parameter space survives once the required selectron decay-chain branching ratios, low-energy constraints, and companion l gamma gamma or gamma gamma rates are imposed?
questions.rationale: This directly follows from the selectron interpretation of the CDF event and the predicted associated Tevatron and LEP processes [3,5].

node_ab7906b13540.summary: These works study stau NLSP scenarios with distinctive collider signatures such as heavy charged tracks, time-of-flight measurements, tau-rich decays, and neutralino reconstruction.

questions.question: If long-lived staus are observed, how well can time-of-flight, stopping-detector decays, and tau-polarization observables reconstruct the stau, gravitino, and neutralino mixing parameters?
questions.rationale: This combines stopped-stau lifetime and gravitino-mass studies in [3] and [5] with tau-polarization sensitivity to stau and neutralino mixing in [4].

questions.question: Can future e+e- collider measurements of stau masses, mixing angles, decay distributions, and tau polarization overconstrain the MSSM parameters that also control light-stau effects in the Higgs gamma gamma rate?
questions.rationale: The collider determination strategy in [2] and the light-stau Higgs diphoton mechanism in [1] motivate this overconstraint test.

questions.question: What detector geometry and material budget would maximize the number of stopped long-lived staus at the LHC while preserving precision measurements of late decay products?
questions.rationale: This practical open problem follows from the external stopper concepts and event-yield estimates in [3] and [5].

node_d05a2677e259.summary: This cluster summarizes the ILC physics program, emphasizing precision Higgs, electroweak, top-quark, Standard Model, and beyond-Standard-Model measurements.

questions.question: What single precision measurement or combination of Higgs, electroweak, and top observables at a 250-500 GeV ILC would most decisively test the Standard Model and motivate the 1 TeV upgrade?
questions.rationale: The ILC design reports emphasize staged running at 250 GeV, 500 GeV, and possible 1 TeV upgrades for Higgs, electroweak, top, and BSM physics [1], [4], [S1].

questions.question: How should LHC discoveries or null results be combined with polarized-beam ILC measurements to distinguish supersymmetry from alternative BSM explanations?
questions.rationale: The LHC-ILC interplay report stresses combined interpretation and analysis of hadron-collider and linear-collider data for identifying the origin of new physics [3].

questions.question: Which detector and software capabilities are still most limiting for Snowmass-style e+e- studies of missing-energy, Higgs, and top observables at future linear colliders?
questions.rationale: The ILC Snowmass study questions were framed around useful e+e- projects and a new software framework, while the TDR specifies two high-performance detector concepts [1], [S3].

node_af19e1ea66b1.summary: These papers compute precision SUSY QCD predictions for squark, gluino, and related superpartner production at hadron colliders using NLO corrections and soft-gluon threshold resummation.

questions.question: For gluino-pair and squark-gluino production near threshold, how much of the residual mass-extraction uncertainty would be removed by extending soft-gluon resummation beyond NLL while preserving full NLO SUSY-QCD matching?
questions.rationale: This follows from the large NLL soft-gluon corrections and reduced scale dependence found especially for gluino production [3,5].

questions.question: Can the PROSPINO-style total and differential cross-section framework be consistently updated to include modern PDFs, higher-order threshold effects, and correlations among pT, rapidity, and mass extraction uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in PROSPINO's NLO predictions for total and differential squark and gluino production [2] and in later work emphasizing PDF and scale uncertainties [3].

node_4846144aaba8.summary: This cluster develops transverse kinematic variables such as MT2 and MCT to determine masses in events with pair-produced particles decaying to visible states plus invisible missing-energy particles.

questions.question: How stable are MT2 endpoint and kink mass determinations once realistic backgrounds, detector resolution, combinatorics, and upstream transverse momentum are included for semi-invisible pair decays?
questions.rationale: [1] introduced MT2 in an idealized no-background and no-measurement-error setting, while [5] showed that practical construction of the MT2 maximum is central to extracting mother and invisible-particle masses.

questions.question: Can the interpretation of MT2 as the boundary of the mass region allowed by minimal kinematic constraints be extended into a systematic hierarchy of stronger mass estimators when extra on-shell or event-pair constraints are available?
questions.rationale: [4] identifies MT2 with the boundary from missing-particle and mother-particle mass-shell constraints and suggests building more sophisticated methods when additional constraints exist.

questions.question: For decay chains with massive visible systems, when can contra-linear-boost-invariant observables independently determine both parent and invisible masses in experimentally realistic samples?
questions.rationale: [3] shows in principle that nonzero visible invariant masses allow independent mass determination using contra-linear Lorentz-boost invariance but warns that contamination may obstruct the method in practice.

node_b31a77d4cd9f.summary: These works study Higgs bosons emerging as composite pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone states, focusing on model classes, top partners, naturalness, tuning, and electroweak precision constraints.

questions.question: What single pattern of Higgs-coupling deviations, longitudinal vector-boson scattering, and double-Higgs production would convincingly separate a light composite pseudo-Goldstone Higgs from other electroweak-symmetry-breaking scenarios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the effective low-energy description in terms of m_rho and g_rho and its proposed probes through anomalous Higgs couplings, vector-boson scattering, and double-Higgs production [4].

questions.question: If light resonances near the originally expected few-TeV scale remain unobserved, what quantitative tuning or flavor assumptions keep minimal AdS composite-Higgs models viable?
questions.rationale: The minimal composite Higgs model predicts a mostly composite top sector, controlled electroweak precision corrections, and resonances around 2 TeV [2].

questions.question: Can simplified resonance descriptions of new physics in vector-boson scattering be matched to UV-complete composite-Higgs dynamics in a way that preserves perturbative unitarity across the experimentally relevant energy range?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass discussion stresses that resonance-only simplified models can violate perturbative unitarity without a UV-complete theory behind them [S1].

node_53488ee5d763.summary: This cluster centers on minimal composite Higgs constructions in which electroweak symmetry breaking arises from strong dynamics while collider and precision data constrain the resonance spectrum.

questions.question: If no roughly 2 TeV resonances, top-compositeness deviations, or light custodians are found, what evidence would still keep the minimal composite pNGB Higgs paradigm viable?
questions.rationale: This comes from the minimal AdS composite-Higgs prediction of TeV resonances and top-sector deviations, and from the warped custodial models predicting 500-1500 GeV custodians [1] and [3].

questions.question: Which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering, double-Higgs production, and anomalous Higgs couplings best separate genuinely strong-sector operators from effects of the resonance spectrum alone?
questions.rationale: This follows from the effective Lagrangian description distinguishing operators sensitive to the strong force from those sensitive only to resonance spectra [2].

node_9efe7e1efa1f.summary: These papers analyze how light composite Higgs scenarios balance Higgs mass predictions, top-partner spectra, electroweak tests, and fine-tuning requirements.

questions.question: After the non-observation of generic 2 TeV resonances, what minimal deformation of the five-dimensional pseudo-Goldstone composite Higgs framework can preserve dynamical electroweak breaking by top loops without reintroducing large electroweak-precision corrections?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], where the minimal AdS composite Higgs predicts top-loop electroweak breaking, controlled precision observables, and resonances around 2 TeV.

questions.question: Which combination of anomalous Higgs couplings, longitudinal vector-boson scattering, and double-Higgs production can most cleanly separate operators genuinely sensitive to strong dynamics from those only sensitive to resonance spectra?
questions.rationale: The distinction between strong-force-sensitive operators and spectrum-sensitive operators, together with the listed collider probes, is stated explicitly in [2].

questions.question: Can light custodians remain the characteristic naturalness signal of composite Higgs models once flavor and electroweak constraints are imposed simultaneously, or do viable spectra require a different top-partner organization?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], which identifies light exotic custodial fermions as a trademark consequence of top compositeness and custodial protection in warped composite Higgs models.

node_9efe7e1efa1f_1.summary: This cluster examines light Higgs bosons in composite models, emphasizing pseudo-Goldstone dynamics, partial compositeness, top partners, and phenomenological constraints.

questions.question: After current LHC limits on top partners and vector resonances, what region of minimal pseudo-Goldstone composite Higgs parameter space still gives a loop-generated light Higgs with tolerable tuning and protected electroweak observables?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the minimal AdS composite Higgs construction in [1], the custodial protection mechanism in [2], and the tuning assessment in [5].

questions.question: Are light custodians with charges 5/3, 2/3, and -1/3 still the decisive collider signature of natural composite Higgs models, or can deviations in Higgs and top couplings provide a more robust test?
questions.rationale: The role of light custodians as trademark states is emphasized in [2], while [1] predicts top compositeness and Standard Model coupling deviations.

questions.question: Which symmetry-breaking cosets and holographic embeddings minimize flavor violation while preserving the calculability of the Higgs potential in light composite Higgs models?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the symmetry-based and holographic construction reviews in [3] and [4], together with the flavor-protection discussion in [5].

node_9efe7e1efa1f_2.summary: These works investigate tuning in composite Higgs theories and its relation to Higgs mass generation, electroweak precision limits, and the expected mass scale of partner resonances.

questions.question: What is the least tuned composite Higgs parameter region still compatible with Higgs coupling measurements, electroweak precision limits, and the non-observation of the expected light top partners?
questions.rationale: Minimal composite Higgs models predict TeV-scale resonances and top compositeness [1], while later reviews emphasize that tuning is not negligible in any model [5].

questions.question: Can custodial symmetry and light custodians still protect electroweak observables if the exotic colored fermions are pushed above the original 500–1500 GeV natural range?
questions.rationale: The warped custodial models rely on light top resonances and custodial partners to satisfy precision tests while triggering electroweak symmetry breaking [2].

node_426fb1f3081e.summary: This cluster develops four-dimensional, deconstructed, holographic, and extra-dimensional composite Higgs models designed for calculable spectra and collider phenomenology.

questions.question: What single collider or precision-Higgs result would most sharply distinguish a calculable four-dimensional composite Higgs description from its holographic or little-Higgs counterparts based on the same SO(5) structure?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the comparison of minimal SO(5) composite Higgs phenomenology with little-Higgs and holographic extensions [1].

questions.question: Can a deconstructed four-dimensional model with one accessible resonance multiplet remain natural while satisfying electroweak precision, flavor, and direct-search constraints after future collider bounds?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finite, calculable Higgs potential and collider-ready resonance spectrum emphasized in discrete and 4D composite Higgs constructions [2],[3].

questions.question: Where is the complementarity between direct spin-one resonance searches and indirect Higgs-coupling deviations strongest in excluding or discovering minimal composite Higgs parameter space?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in future-collider projections comparing direct resonance searches with indirect Higgs-compositeness probes [5].

node_0e2c498c24e6.summary: These papers study heavy spin-1 vector and axial resonances predicted by composite Higgs models, including simplified descriptions and LHC diboson, dilepton, and top-partner searches.

questions.question: Can the heavy-vector-triplet simplified Lagrangian be extended to include top-partner decay channels while preserving analytic reinterpretability of LHC diboson, dilepton, and fermionic searches across weakly coupled and composite limits?
questions.rationale: This follows from the model-independent heavy vector triplet strategy in [2] and the explicit emphasis on vector-resonance interactions with lighter top partners in minimal composite Higgs models in [5].

questions.question: Which deviations from the leading SO(5)/SO(4) chiral Lagrangian in high-energy longitudinal vector-boson scattering would distinguish a genuine spin-1 composite resonance from scalar singlet or tensor resonance effects?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the partial-UV-completion treatment of scalar and vector resonances and their depletion/enhancement patterns in vector-boson scattering in [3].

questions.question: How tightly do perturbative-unitarity sum rules constrain the allowed mass-coupling window for custodial rho triplets once Higgs coupling deviations and direct LHC resonance limits are combined?
questions.rationale: This combines the unitarity-sum-rule constraints on Higgs and rho couplings in [4] with the two-parameter composite Higgs description in terms of m_rho and g_rho in [1].

node_e66c3a1aed56.summary: This cluster explores UV completions, partial compositeness, and flavor or CP constraints in composite Higgs theories, including fermionic strong sectors and Higgs-mediated flavor violation.

questions.question: Which purely fermionic hypercolor theories satisfying custodial symmetry and top-partner requirements survive once partial compositeness and flavor or CP constraints are imposed together?
questions.rationale: The group-theoretic classification identifies viable hypercolor candidates with top partners and custodial symmetry [1], while the node centers on UV flavor constraints in composite Higgs models.

questions.question: Can large anomalous dimensions for fermion bilinears and top-partner operators be realized in UV descriptions without elementary scalars strongly enough to generate realistic Yukawa hierarchies?
questions.rationale: Four-fermion UV descriptions rely on large anomalous dimensions to drive symmetry breaking and realize partial compositeness [4].

questions.question: How can models where the Higgs mixes between pseudo-Goldstone and massive-condensate excitations be distinguished experimentally through electroweak and flavor observables?
questions.rationale: Fundamental composite Higgs dynamics predicts mixing between pseudo-Goldstone and massive Higgs-like states with phenomenological repercussions [3].

node_2d04e26cef0a.summary: These works classify and construct fundamental gauge-theory UV completions of composite Higgs models, emphasizing fermionic matter, hypercolor dynamics, custodial symmetry, and top partners.

questions.question: Which fundamental hypercolor gauge theories from the SU(5)/SO(5) and SU(4)/Sp(4) classifications survive simultaneous requirements of custodial symmetry, top partners, and viable flavor?
questions.rationale: The group-theoretic classification in [1] identifies necessary but not sufficient viability conditions for fermionic UV completions.

questions.question: Can lattice or other nonperturbative calculations determine whether the SU(4)/Sp(4) realization produces the required Higgs-Goldstone and condensate-scalar mixing without violating electroweak precision constraints?
questions.rationale: The unified effective and fundamental SU(4)/Sp(4) analysis in [3] predicts mixing between pseudo-Goldstone and massive condensate excitations with electroweak phenomenological consequences.

questions.question: Is large anomalous-dimension dynamics in gauged-NJL-like UV descriptions sufficient to realize partial compositeness with composite top partners while avoiding elementary scalars?
questions.rationale: The UV descriptions in [4] rely on four-fermion interactions, large fermion-bilinear anomalous dimensions, and composite top-partner operators.

node_94516a4b8601.summary: This cluster focuses on flavor, CP, lepton-flavor violation, and flavor-anomaly constraints on composite Higgs and partial-compositeness models.

questions.question: What minimal flavor or CP symmetry in a partially composite Higgs sector can simultaneously suppress epsilon_K, Higgs-mediated FCNCs, lepton-flavor violation, and Z-pole deviations without erasing LHC signatures of light-quark compositeness?
questions.rationale: Flavor- and CP-invariant composite Higgs models seek MFV-like protection while higher-dimensional Higgs operators can generate epsilon_K-sensitive flavor-changing Higgs couplings [1], [2].

questions.question: Are composite-Higgs explanations of lepton-flavor nonuniversality in B to K l+l- compatible with the strongest lepton-sector constraints, especially mu to e gamma and protected Z mu mu couplings, in a predictive minimal setup?
questions.rationale: Composite Higgs models can address R_K with sizable left-handed muon compositeness and custodial protection, but minimal partial compositeness faces strong mu to e gamma tension [3], [4], [5].

node_e5d4d6b95cac.summary: These papers develop preon and supersymmetric compositeness models in which quarks, leptons, Higgs fields, or weak bosons emerge as bound states of new confining dynamics.

questions.question: What single experimental signature would most decisively distinguish TeV-scale preonic compositeness from more conventional composite-Higgs or supersymmetry-breaking scenarios?
questions.rationale: This framing question follows from models predicting composite quarks, leptons, or Higgs fields with observable effects in scalar masses, b physics, and the rho parameter [1], [2].

questions.question: Can preon-level flavor symmetries simultaneously explain Yukawa hierarchies, suppress flavor-changing neutral currents, and avoid dangerous baryon-number violation without fine tuning?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed links between operator dimensionality, compositeness scales, flavor symmetries, and accidental baryon-number protection [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: Are stable charged hyperbaryons an unavoidable failure mode of confining hypercolor models, or can the restricted renormalizable decay mechanisms identified for TeV-scale scalars be made generic?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the classification of hypercolor models needed to avoid unwanted stable charged relics [4].

node_bd70773407f5.summary: This cluster surveys Higgs-sector electroweak symmetry breaking, strong alternatives, and the role of unitarity constraints in gauge-boson and scalar scattering.

questions.question: What minimal pattern of Higgs, vector-boson-scattering, and fermion-coupling deviations would settle whether electroweak symmetry breaking is weakly coupled, supersymmetric, or driven by strong dynamics?
questions.rationale: The representative reviews compare Standard Model Higgs properties [1], MSSM Higgs sectors [2], strong electroweak dynamics [3], and effective-Lagrangian strategies for diagnosing weak versus strong dynamics [5].

questions.question: How can simplified vector-boson-scattering resonance models enforce perturbative unitarity while remaining flexible enough to map onto little-Higgs, composite-Higgs, and decoupled-resonance effective operators?
questions.rationale: Snowmass simplified VBS models emphasize that explicit resonances without a UV completion can violate perturbative unitarity, while little-Higgs and light-Higgs effective Lagrangians provide concrete model and EFT targets [S1][4][5].

node_5a5d5256571d.summary: These works study longitudinal vector-boson scattering at the LHC as a probe of strong electroweak dynamics, resonances, and unitarization beyond the minimal Higgs picture.

questions.question: What vector-boson-scattering observable would most cleanly separate genuine strong electroweak dynamics from Standard Model backgrounds and unitarized effective-Lagrangian artifacts?
questions.rationale: Early LHC studies relied on forward-jet tags, central-jet vetoes, and leptonic cuts to isolate strong WW scattering signals from large backgrounds [2,3].

questions.question: Can simplified resonance models for vector-boson scattering be matched to low-energy effective operators in a way that preserves perturbative unitarity across all relevant spin and isospin channels?
questions.rationale: Generic VBS parameterizations include resonances of all spin-isospin combinations matched to chiral Lagrangians, while Snowmass framing highlights unitarity violation in non-UV-complete resonance models [4,S1].

questions.question: Where does the heavy-Higgs or scalar-resonance narrow-width approximation fail in realistic WW scattering simulations once gauge invariance and off-shell lineshape effects are imposed?
questions.rationale: Heavy-Higgs lineshape studies question the validity of Breit-Wigner sampling and narrow-width assumptions, emphasizing gauge invariance and residual theoretical uncertainties [5].

node_6ab2bf1eb901.summary: This cluster focuses on effective and dispersive unitarization methods for WW, ZZ, and Higgs scattering when electroweak interactions become strong or partially strong.

questions.question: What experimentally accessible combination of vector-boson-scattering cross sections, resonance line shapes, and angular distributions can distinguish different unitarization prescriptions of the electroweak chiral Lagrangian?
questions.rationale: LHC WW-scattering studies compared unitarization protocols and found that scalar or vector resonances could appear in realistic jj+l+nu final states [1].

questions.question: Can simplified resonance models for all spin and isospin channels be matched to higher-dimensional operator descriptions without introducing artifacts from the minimal unitarization scheme used in Monte Carlo generation?
questions.rationale: The WHIZARD parameterization implements resonances of all spin and isospin combinations matched to the low-energy chiral Lagrangian with a minimal unitarization scheme [2], [S1].

questions.question: How precisely can LHC vector-boson-scattering data test the sum rules required for partial unitarity restoration in Higgsless or strongly coupled electroweak scenarios?
questions.rationale: Higgsless phenomenology identifies charged vector resonances and mass-coupling sum rules as central to partial unitarity restoration and experimental verification [4].

node_14a9d786b751.summary: These papers analyze vector-boson scattering signatures, backgrounds, and gold-plated channels at the LHC for testing the Standard Model and strongly interacting electroweak sectors.

questions.question: Which combination of purely leptonic ZZ, W+W-, WZ, and same-sign WW channels gives the most robust LHC test of strong electroweak symmetry breaking after forward-jet tagging, central-jet vetoing, and back-to-back lepton cuts?
questions.rationale: The gold-plated VBS search strategy and channel comparison are the core sensitivity tools developed in [1] and [2].

questions.question: How should LHC VBS EFT interpretations impose positivity bounds on the 18 dimension-eight quartic-gauge operators while retaining the UV-completable directions most relevant to data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finding in [3] that only a small fraction of the usual dimension-eight parameter space is compatible with UV completion.

questions.question: Under what collider-frame and event-selection conditions can longitudinal W/Z scattering be reliably replaced by Goldstone-boson scattering when extracting chiral expansion coefficients?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the safe-frame conditions for the Equivalence Theorem in [5] and the chiral-coefficient program in [4].

node_9035b10564c6.summary: This cluster contains broad reviews of electroweak theory, Higgs production and decay, collider searches, precision limits, and beyond-Standard-Model symmetry-breaking scenarios.

questions.question: What single pattern of Higgs production and decay measurements would most decisively distinguish weakly coupled electroweak symmetry breaking from strong or composite dynamics?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the reviews of Standard Model Higgs properties [1], strong electroweak symmetry breaking [3], and effective light-Higgs Lagrangians designed to diagnose weak versus strong dynamics [5].

questions.question: Where is the experimental consensus weakest among MSSM Higgs sectors, little-Higgs partners, and strong-dynamics scenarios once collider precision and rare-process constraints are considered together?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the MSSM Higgs review [2], minimal little-Higgs construction [4], and Snowmass emphasis on distinguishing electroweak-symmetry-breaking mechanisms through collider and precision probes [S1].

node_47a69b573906.summary: These works review the Standard Model Higgs sector, electroweak symmetry breaking mechanisms, LHC implications, and alternatives such as supersymmetry, strong dynamics, or extra dimensions.

questions.question: What decisive pattern of Higgs couplings, electroweak scattering, or rare-process deviations would distinguish a weakly interacting Standard Model-like Higgs sector from strong electroweak symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: The broad distinguishing strategy is framed by the SM Higgs review [1], the strong-dynamics review [3], and the effective light-Higgs Lagrangian analysis in [4].

questions.question: Which measurements at a high-luminosity lepton collider or 100 TeV pp collider most directly test whether additional MSSM Higgs bosons or strong-dynamics resonances complete the electroweak sector?
questions.rationale: MSSM Higgs production and decay modes are reviewed in [2], future collider roles are emphasized in [S1], and 100 TeV opportunities are summarized in [5].

questions.question: Is the current effective-Lagrangian description of a light Higgs-like scalar sufficient to classify all plausible electroweak-breaking alternatives, or does it miss discriminants tied to top-quark privileged dynamics?
questions.rationale: The effective-Lagrangian strategy in [4] and the top/third-generation emphasis in strong-dynamics models reviewed in [3] motivate this field-level question.

node_e7d82d9f1b34.summary: This cluster explores electroweak models that avoid a conventional physical Higgs boson, including theory-space, little-Higgs, constrained-Higgs, and gauge-invariant mass-generation approaches.

questions.question: What observable would most cleanly decide whether Higgsless deconstructed electroweak breaking can delay W+W- unitarity violation without conflicting with precision electroweak constraints?
questions.rationale: The Higgsless theory-space model suppresses the E^2/m_W^2 growth of W+W- scattering amplitudes by a factor of (N+1)^-2 [3].

questions.question: Can spurion-suppressed nonstandard fermion couplings and generalized Weinberg sum rules make Higgsless electroweak effective theories phenomenologically viable beyond leading order?
questions.rationale: The spurion analysis found that some couplings arise only at higher spurion order, leading to generalized Weinberg sum rules and suppressed nonstandard fermion couplings [5].

questions.question: Is the topology of theory space a practical organizing principle for constructing electroweak models with controlled low-energy scalar content and potentials?
questions.rationale: The theory-space topology study argued that the fundamental group determines the relevant classical low-energy physics and can guide construction of desired particle content and potentials [4].

node_703c0c1ca323.summary: These papers study BESS-like and other strong electroweak models with heavy vector or axial resonances, emphasizing precision constraints and collider probes at lepton and hadron machines.

questions.question: What measurement would most decisively reveal a low-energy strong electroweak sector that is nearly invisible to precision tests because of vector-axial degeneracy or cancellations among extra vectors?
questions.rationale: This follows from the degenerate BESS decoupling mechanism in [3] and the parameter-space interplay among multiple vectors in precision constraints in [1].

questions.question: At future lepton or muon colliders, can ratios of WW to ZZ vector-boson-scattering channels distinguish scalar, vector, and nonresonant strong electroweak dynamics better than direct annihilation searches?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the WW/ZZ ratio proposal in [4] and the dominance of vector-boson fusion at multi-TeV lepton colliders in [2].

node_c276e70a42fd.summary: This cluster derives perturbative unitarity constraints on scalar couplings and masses in two-Higgs-doublet, three-doublet, triplet, and related extended Higgs-sector models.

questions.question: Which measured pair of scalar masses and tan beta would decisively distinguish an exact discrete-symmetry 2HDM from a softly broken or fully general CP-violating 2HDM under tree-level unitarity?
questions.rationale: This follows from the strong Mh-tan beta correlation with exact discrete symmetry and its relaxation by symmetry breaking in [1] and [5], plus the general CP-violating constraints in [2].

questions.question: Can the block-diagonal high-energy scalar scattering matrix used for the most general 2HDM be extended analytically to larger multi-Higgs sectors without losing a transparent map to physical scalar masses?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the analytic block-diagonalization of neutral, singly charged, and doubly charged two-body scattering states in [4] and the mass-bound analyses in [3].

node_fbf92ab66adb.summary: These works examine walking technicolor, topcolor-assisted technicolor, technidilatons, technipions, and vector resonances under precision constraints and collider searches.

questions.question: What collider signature would most decisively distinguish an almost-conformal two-techniflavor higher-representation technicolor model from a weakly coupled extended Higgs sector: light composite Higgs couplings, vector resonances, technipions, or the anomaly-canceling lepton spectrum?
questions.rationale: This follows from the tension between the minimal near-conformal orientifold constructions and their electroweak-precision/LHC predictions in [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can topcolor-assisted technicolor or top-quark seesaw models still produce a natural top mass and electroweak scale while evading direct searches for top-pions, composite scalars, and other TeV-scale resonances?
questions.rationale: This derives from the generic top-pion prediction of topcolor-assisted technicolor in [1] and the composite scalar spectrum computed for top seesaw electroweak breaking in [4].

node_a77c8ad1bd48.summary: This cluster reviews technicolor and extended-technicolor mechanisms for dynamical electroweak and flavor symmetry breaking, including topcolor assistance and precision-electroweak challenges.

questions.question: What collider signature would most clearly distinguish topcolor-assisted technicolor, with top-pions near the top mass scale, from other composite Higgs or extended-scalar explanations of electroweak symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from [1], where top-pions are a generic testable consequence of topcolor-assisted technicolor.

questions.question: Can nearly conformal technicolor theories with only two techniflavors evade precision-electroweak constraints while still producing realistic electroweak symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [2], which constructs almost-conformal orientifold theories with few techniflavors for electroweak breaking.

questions.question: How can top-seesaw or topcolor-assisted models generate the observed top mass without producing unacceptable pseudo-Goldstone spectra, anomaly problems, or flavor mixing tensions?
questions.rationale: This combines the top-quark seesaw dynamics in [3] with the anomaly-free and generation-mixing structure of natural topcolor-assisted technicolor in [5].

node_4f3dfb0db1f2.summary: These papers study how technicolor and extended technicolor affect precision electroweak observables, especially the Z b bbar vertex, oblique parameters, walking dynamics, and top-mass generation.

questions.question: Can walking technicolor produce a reliably small S parameter once the cancellation between positive QCD-like contributions and anomalous-dimension-driven negative contributions is computed with controlled nonperturbative input?
questions.rationale: Walking dynamics are argued to reduce S through a large cancellation tied to the technifermion condensate anomalous dimension, but with considerable uncertainties [5].

questions.question: Which pattern of Z -> b bbar deviations would distinguish weak-singlet ETC from noncommuting ETC gauge bosons responsible for top-mass generation?
questions.rationale: Noncommuting ETC can increase the Z -> b bbar branching ratio, in contrast with conventional ETC corrections to the same vertex [2][3].

questions.question: Can effective theories for minimal walking technicolor simultaneously satisfy modified Weinberg sum rules, spin-one spectrum predictions, and precision electroweak constraints?
questions.rationale: The collider-ready minimal walking technicolor setup derives spin-one relations from modified Weinberg sum rules and computes electroweak parameters in the same effective theory [1].

node_e6c18650888d.summary: This cluster develops and reviews technicolor, conformal, gauge-assisted, and extended-gauge mechanisms for dynamically breaking electroweak symmetry while addressing flavor and precision constraints.

questions.question: What nonperturbative evidence would most decisively identify a small-techniflavored gauge theory as near-conformal enough for viable dynamical electroweak symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: Orientifold and related gauge theories were proposed to enter an almost conformal phase with very few techniflavors [1], and phase diagrams are central to model viability [2][5].

questions.question: Can conformal technicolor realize an electroweak order parameter with scaling dimension d = 1 + epsilon without reintroducing fine tuning or conflicting with walking-technicolor gap-equation constraints?
questions.rationale: The conformal-technicolor proposal requires d = 1 + epsilon with epsilon of order one over a few and notes restrictions from fine tuning, large-N CFTs, and walking analyses [3].

questions.question: In minimal conformal technicolor, how predictive is the vacuum alignment between top-loop effects and technifermion mass terms once precision electroweak constraints are imposed?
questions.rationale: The SU(2) minimal conformal technicolor model uses top loops and technifermion mass terms to align the vacuum and determine a composite Higgs mass without top partners [4].

node_4dc5cd4a0e09.summary: These works construct and constrain topcolor-assisted technicolor models for generating the top mass, generation mixing, and flavor physics while satisfying electroweak and FCNC bounds.

questions.question: Is there still a viable topcolor-assisted technicolor paradigm in which top-pions, generation mixing, and the large top mass coexist with modern electroweak and flavor-changing neutral-current limits?
questions.rationale: Topcolor-assisted technicolor predicts top-pions and was motivated by the large top mass, while technicolor reviews identify FCNC and precision electroweak constraints as central obstacles [1], [4].

questions.question: Can top-quark seesaw models produce a restrictive and testable composite-Higgs spectrum while maintaining a realistic bottom mass and acceptable precision electroweak parameters?
questions.rationale: The top-seesaw analyses study composite scalar spectra, vacuum structure, bottom mass generation, and precision constraints, often predicting a heavy composite Higgs near 1 TeV [2], [5].

node_7d950254e802.summary: This cluster studies collider signatures of walking and low-scale technicolor, including vector resonances and the possibility that the 125 GeV Higgs-like state is a technidilaton.

questions.question: What collider signature would decisively distinguish walking technicolor from other Higgs-sector extensions: Drell-Yan heavy vector production, vector-boson fusion, or deviations in composite-Higgs phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the LHC study comparing Drell-Yan and vector-boson-fusion production of composite heavy vectors and composite Higgs signatures [5].

questions.question: Can technibaryon or TIMP dark matter in minimal technicolor models satisfy relic density, sphaleron, electric-neutrality, direct-detection, and electroweak-precision constraints at the same time?
questions.rationale: The question combines technibaryon relic-density and sphaleron analyses [2], ultraminimal TIMP dark matter [3], and low-energy effective technicolor theories constrained by precision data [1,4].

node_7bf988b143c0.summary: These papers analyze top-pion and top-Higgs production, decay, and flavor-changing signatures in topcolor-assisted technicolor at lepton colliders and the LHC.

questions.question: What single flavor-changing top-charm signature would most decisively separate topcolor-assisted technicolor scalars from generic heavy scalar or vectorlike-quark explanations?
questions.rationale: This broad discriminator is motivated by the claim that tc decays of neutral scalars below the ttbar threshold are a model-independent consequence of non-universal top-condensation interactions [1].

questions.question: Can rare top decays t -> cg, t -> cZ, and t -> c gamma probe the same top-pion and top-Higgs parameter space as LHC top-charm associated production, or do the two channels test complementary regions?
questions.rationale: This follows from TC2 predictions of 6-9 order-of-magnitude enhancements in rare top decays and observable top-charm associated production through scalar exchange [2,5].

questions.question: Is there any viable TC2 parameter region in which charged top-pion effects evade the negative R_b shift while preserving observable top-charm or top-prime collider signals?
questions.rationale: The tension comes from LEP/SLD vertex-correction constraints driven by charged top-pion exchange versus proposed Tevatron and LHC discovery channels [3,4,5].

node_e9f35c4c2120.summary: This cluster uses effective theories and deconstructed or extra-dimensional Higgsless models to calculate oblique parameters and assess precision electroweak viability.

questions.question: What minimum set of oblique parameters beyond S, T, and U is needed to make Higgsless or low-scale electroweak models falsifiable when new vector states lie near the 100 GeV to TeV range?
questions.rationale: The extended oblique-parameter framework shows that V, W, and X are required for lower-energy new physics coupled primarily to W and Z bosons [3].

questions.question: Can light-fermion localization or brane kinetic terms lower the Higgsless S parameter while preserving perturbative unitarity and avoiding direct bounds on W-prime and Z-prime modes?
questions.rationale: Warped Higgsless studies show that fermion localization and brane kinetic terms can suppress S, but too low an S can lead to loss of tree-level unitarity [4][5].

questions.question: How should precision constraints from Delta rho and the full S,T,U,V,W,X set be combined when scalar sectors and Higgsless vector sectors coexist in deconstructed or extra-dimensional models?
questions.rationale: General multi-Higgs expressions constrain Delta rho and oblique parameters, while Higgsless models generate tree-level oblique corrections from warped gauge sectors [1][2][5].

node_3e4ea6f6ef8f.summary: These works explore dynamical electroweak symmetry breaking through top-quark or fermion condensates, including topcolor, seesaw extensions, composite Higgs scenarios, and anomalous-dimension effects.

questions.question: What single phenomenological signature would still make top-condensation electroweak symmetry breaking competitive with elementary-Higgs and other composite-Higgs interpretations?
questions.rationale: The review emphasizes extensions of minimal top condensation, underlying topcolor-assisted dynamics, and unresolved theoretical and phenomenological issues [2].

questions.question: Can top-seesaw models produce the observed top mass and acceptable S and T parameters without tuning once the isosinglet-quark spectrum and topcolor scale are confronted with current bounds?
questions.rationale: The top-condensation seesaw was introduced to reconcile a natural top condensate with the observed top mass and acceptable electroweak precision parameters [1].

questions.question: Are large anomalous dimensions in gauged NJL dynamics sufficient to generate realistic fermion mass hierarchies without inducing unwanted light pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons or exotic fermions?
questions.rationale: Large anomalous dimensions motivate top-condensate dynamics, while tumbling models illustrate anomaly-cancellation requirements, color-sextet fermions, and many pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons [4], [3].

node_5a344e110a6d.summary: This cluster reports lattice studies of Sp(4) and SU(4) gauge theories with multiple fermion representations as ultraviolet completions of composite Higgs models.

questions.question: Which lattice-measured resonance spectrum would most decisively distinguish an SU(4)/Sp(4) pseudo-Goldstone composite Higgs realization from a scenario where the Higgs is a massive excitation of the condensate?
questions.rationale: This follows from the unified composite-Higgs framework in SU(2) with two fundamentals [4] and the Sp(4) lattice program aimed at the SU(4)/Sp(4) coset [5].

questions.question: Can lattice determinations of scalar, vector, axial-vector, glueball, and Goldstone spectra identify parameter regions where composite dark matter and composite-Higgs phenomenology are simultaneously viable?
questions.rationale: This connects composite dark matter operator and spectroscopy needs [1], SU(2) Goldstone dark matter confirmation [2], and light-scalar/vector-resonance lattice results relevant to LHC searches [3].

node_cff0bc07b48d.summary: These papers examine CP violation and flavor-changing neutral currents involving top quarks and Higgs sectors, especially in two-Higgs-doublet and related beyond-Standard-Model frameworks.

questions.question: Which basis-independent combinations of 2HDM parameters provide the most robust experimental language for top-Higgs flavor-changing and CP-violating effects, given that tan(beta) is not meaningful in the most general model?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the basis-independent formulation of the general 2HDM and its warning that physical observables cannot depend on the Higgs-basis choice [4].

questions.question: Can tree-level scalar FCNCs in Type III 2HDMs be simultaneously large enough to affect top-Higgs observables and small enough to satisfy existing flavor constraints without imposing overly tuned Yukawa ansatze or family symmetries?
questions.rationale: The 2HDM review identifies scalar-mediated FCNCs as a generic problem and discusses Type III suppression through Yukawa ansatze or family symmetries [1].

questions.question: How should future measurements of Ztt, Wtb, top Yukawa, and Higgs CP observables be combined to test custodial-protection scenarios that shield Zbb but predict deviations in top couplings?
questions.rationale: This follows from the custodial-symmetry result that protection of Zbb cannot simultaneously protect Ztt and Wtb, together with Snowmass emphasis on precision top and Higgs CP measurements [2].

node_653acd4d4dc6.summary: This cluster focuses on anomalous top-quark flavor-changing neutral-current couplings in rare decays and single-top production at hadron and future lepton colliders.

questions.question: What combination of rare top decays and single-top production can distinguish anomalous tqZ, tqgamma, tqg, and tqH effective vertices from SUSY-QCD or electroweak enhancements of t->c h?
questions.rationale: This is based on the effective-vertex review, the minimal anomalous-coupling parameterization, and the MSSM study of enhanced FCNC top-Higgs decays [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Given the SM t->cH branching ratio of order 10^-13 to 10^-14, what collider sensitivity would make a top-Higgs FCNC signal an unambiguous discovery of physics beyond the SM?
questions.rationale: This derives from the recalculated SM t->cH width and the Snowmass emphasis on future top-coupling measurements at high statistics [3] and [S3].

node_a0e6a32d9a7c.summary: These works probe nonstandard top-quark interactions, including Wtb, top-gluon, and CP-violating couplings, using single-top production, top-pair observables, and collider asymmetries.

questions.question: What minimal, nonredundant SMEFT parameterization of off-shell Wtb, Ztt, gamma tt, and gtt interactions is sufficient for a global top-coupling fit across single-top, ttbar decay, and ttV production data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the equation-of-motion reduction to gamma^mu and sigma^{mu nu} q_nu structures in [1] and the Snowmass emphasis on global top-coupling determinations in [S2] and [S3].

questions.question: Which single-top observables can isolate off-shell Wtb operators that vanish in top decay but dominate or significantly affect Wg-fusion and tW production channels?
questions.rationale: The question is directly motivated by [2], which shows that off-shell Wtb operators can be relevant in Wg fusion and dominant in tW production while affecting top decays differently.

questions.question: Can angular asymmetries and W-helicity fractions in top-pair decays remove flat directions in anomalous Wtb couplings when combined with B -> Xs gamma constraints on gauge-invariant dimension-six operators?
questions.rationale: This combines the W-helicity and angular-asymmetry sensitivity analysis in [3] with the B -> Xs gamma bounds on anomalous Wtb Wilson coefficients in [5].

node_ffaee7721d18.summary: This cluster studies anomalous Wtb and related top-quark couplings through single-top production, associated Wt processes, polarization observables, and LHC sensitivity analyses.

questions.question: Which minimal set of gauge-invariant dimension-six Wtb operators can be constrained without flat directions when combining single-top production, top decay angular asymmetries, and B to Xs gamma?
questions.rationale: Papers [1], [2], [3], and [5] respectively define reduced anomalous vertices, production dependence, decay asymmetries, and flavor constraints.

questions.question: Are off-shell Wtb operators in Wg fusion and tW production experimentally separable from the usual gamma^mu and sigma^{mu nu} q_nu structures at the LHC or future lepton colliders?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] finds off-shell operators can be relevant in Wg fusion and dominant in tW production, despite vanishing in on-shell top decay.

questions.question: What single measurement program would most reduce the systematics-limited uncertainty on electroweak top couplings: W helicity fractions, associated ttV production, or threshold/top-decay measurements at an ILC?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass reports [S1], [S2], and [S3] frame Wtb, ttgamma, ttZ, and future-collider coupling measurements as complementary precision targets.

node_a1b245a9b5be.summary: These papers study anomalous chromomagnetic and chromoelectric top-gluon dipole moments, using top-pair production and related collider observables to constrain possible new physics.

questions.question: Which fully differential ttbar observables at NLO plus parton shower maximize sensitivity to the top chromomagnetic dipole after accounting for total-rate flat directions in the dipole-parameter plane?
questions.rationale: This combines the zero-net-contribution regions in total top production discussed in [3] with the NLO differential and shower-matched predictions of [5].

questions.question: Can direct CP-odd observables in ttbar production test any chromoelectric top-dipole parameter space that is not already excluded by neutron electric-dipole-moment bounds?
questions.rationale: The tension comes from the proposed CP-odd collider observable in [3] and the strong indirect neutron-EDM constraint on the top chromoelectric dipole in [2].

questions.question: How can cross-section ratios and angular correlations be combined to disentangle top-gluon, ttgamma, ttZ, and tbW dipole operators while reducing scale and PDF uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The ratio and angular-correlation strategy for electroweak top dipoles in [4] complements the NLO top-gluon dipole treatment of [5].

node_c38605568a66.summary: This cluster develops lepton and bottom-quark angular or energy distributions as probes of anomalous top production, tbW decay vertices, and CP-violating dipole interactions.

questions.question: Does the secondary-lepton angular distribution remain a decay-vertex-independent probe of anomalous top production after energy integration and longitudinal beam polarization are included?
questions.rationale: The claimed insensitivity of lepton angular distributions to anomalous tbW couplings, including beam polarization, is derived in [2] and [5].

questions.question: Which optimal-observable combinations at polarized gamma-gamma colliders best disentangle CP-violating ttgamma, gamma gamma H, and anomalous tbW couplings?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the polarized gamma-gamma optimal-observable analysis of dimension-six anomalous couplings in [1].

questions.question: How can precision-electroweak constraints on the nine dimension-six third-generation operators be combined with lepton and bottom-quark energy-angle distributions to separate production and decay new physics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the electroweak-operator constraints in [3] and the production-versus-decay distribution strategy in [4].

node_9488fdc69745.summary: These works investigate flavor-changing neutral-current top interactions with photons, Z bosons, gluons, and Higgs bosons through rare decays and single-top production at present and future colliders.

questions.question: Which rare top process, among t -> qH, t -> qZ, t -> qgamma, t -> qg, and FCNC-induced single-top production, provides the cleanest discriminator between MSSM, two-Higgs-doublet, and topcolor-like sources of top flavor violation?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the survey of effective top FCNC vertices in [1], MSSM t -> ch enhancements in [3], and flavor-mixed charged-scalar production in [4].

questions.question: How low must experimental limits on B(t -> cH) go before any observed signal unambiguously excludes the Standard Model expectation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the recalculated Standard Model branching fraction B(t -> cH) around 10^-13 to 10^-14 in [2].

questions.question: Can collider measurements of charged-scalar Yukawa couplings to charm and bottom quarks constrain the same flavor-mixing dynamics that generates neutral top FCNC couplings?
questions.rationale: This derives from the charged-scalar detection method based on top-charm mixing in [4] and the Higgs-sector FCNC rare top decays in [5].

node_2b8db510a29a.summary: This cluster focuses on rare top decays into a light quark and neutral Higgs boson, especially in two-Higgs-doublet or other beyond-Standard-Model scenarios where rates can become observable.

questions.question: Given the Standard Model branching ratio near 10^-13 to 10^-14 for t to cH, what model-independent experimental limit would begin to probe plausible MSSM or two-Higgs-doublet enhancements rather than just exclude older overestimates?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] recalculates the Standard Model rate far below observability, while [2] and [3] discuss potentially visible BSM enhancements.

questions.question: Can SMEFT operator mixing and indirect constraints from EDMs, flavor, and electroweak precision data close the parameter space for observable top-charm-Higgs couplings at colliders?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] finds indirect probes competitive or dominant once renormalization-group evolution and operator mixing are included.

questions.question: Is e+e- to t anti-c plus conjugate a cleaner probe of flavor-changing top-charm-scalar interactions than rare top decays once Higgs-sector flavor assumptions are relaxed?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] proposes e+e- production of t anti-c as a distinctive signature in a two-Higgs-doublet model without natural flavor conservation.

node_2b8db510a29a_1.summary: These papers analyze collider strategies for detecting top-Higgs flavor-changing neutral currents, including t to qh decays and Higgs decay channels at the LHC and future hadron colliders.

questions.question: Is t to ch still the benchmark discovery channel for top-Higgs FCNC once indirect SMEFT constraints and direct collider searches are combined, or do production modes such as cg to t provide stronger falsification in SUSY and 2HDM scenarios?
questions.rationale: The LHC SUSY scan finds only cg to t and t to ch potentially observable, while SMEFT operator mixing makes indirect probes competitive or dominant [3][5].

questions.question: What collider measurement would most cleanly distinguish SUSY-QCD-induced top-charm-Higgs couplings from tree-level flavor-changing scalar interactions in two-Higgs-doublet models?
questions.rationale: MSSM studies emphasize large SUSY-QCD effects in t to c h, whereas 2HDM analyses use tree-level flavor-changing neutral Higgs couplings and e+e- to t c signatures [1][2][4].

questions.question: How should LHC, future lepton-collider, flavor, electroweak, and electric-dipole-moment constraints be combined into a model-independent limit on chirality-flipping top-Higgs FCNC operators?
questions.rationale: The SMEFT analysis shows that collider and indirect CP-even and CP-odd observables jointly constrain anomalous top-Higgs and top-gauge couplings [3].

node_208310ee21d9.summary: This cluster surveys rare top-quark decay modes such as t to cH, c gamma, cg, bWZ, and cWW as sensitive probes of Standard Model suppression and new physics.

questions.question: What experimental sensitivity to t→cH, t→cγ, and t→cg would decisively separate Standard Model GIM suppression from flavor-dependent supersymmetry or vector-like-quark effects?
questions.rationale: This frames the huge Standard Model suppression of t→cH and rare FCNC top modes against BSM scenarios that can enhance them [1],[2],[3].

questions.question: Can rare top-decay limits be converted into model-independent constraints on nonuniversal SUSY breaking and squark flavor mixing once B-physics and electroweak baryogenesis constraints are imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dependence of observable SUSY rates on nonuniversal flavor-dependent breaking and large up-squark mixings subject to external constraints [2],[5].

questions.question: Which rare top channel is the cleanest broad probe of new flavor physics: t→cZ, t→cγ, t→cg, or t→cH?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the representative studies comparing different FCNC top decay modes and their distinct suppression or enhancement mechanisms [2],[4].

node_ca87ebda2b92.summary: These studies use anomalous tqgamma, tqZ, and tqg flavor-changing neutral-current couplings to predict and constrain single-top or same-sign top production at hadron and lepton colliders.

questions.question: Can a fully gauge-invariant EFT fit to tqgamma, tqZ, tqg, and tqH interactions combine single-top production, rare top decays, and same-sign top channels without basis-dependent interpretations of FCNC limits?
questions.rationale: The global EFT approach calls for gauge-invariant operator coefficients and combined experimental information, while reviews list the Ztq, gamma tq, gtq, and Htq vertices as the relevant FCNC targets [1], [3].

questions.question: Which NLO QCD corrections and operator interferences most affect the translation between collider limits on anomalous single-top production and bounds on top-quark FCNC decay branching ratios?
questions.rationale: The global analysis emphasizes next-to-leading-order QCD treatment, while rare-decay studies connect anomalous Ztc couplings to t to Zc observability [3], [4].

questions.question: How can low-energy flavor constraints and precision diagonal Z-coupling measurements be consistently folded into collider searches for FCNC single-top signals from exotic-quark or extended-Higgs scenarios?
questions.rationale: Exotic-quark models translate precise diagonal Z-coupling data into off-diagonal FCNC bounds, while charged-scalar studies connect single-top production to flavor-changing dynamics [2], [5].

node_cae1c61cfd7a.summary: This broad cluster examines CP violation in Higgs interactions and decays, including Higgs-top, Higgs-gauge, neutral Higgs mixing, tau decays, and charged-Higgs production.

questions.question: Which CP-sensitive Higgs observable gives the cleanest separation between CP-even and CP-odd tensor structures when collider limits are combined with electric-dipole-moment constraints?
questions.rationale: This combines the weak-boson-fusion azimuthal-angle method in [1] with EDM constraints on third-generation CP-violating Higgs couplings in [3] and Snowmass benchmark goals in [S1].

questions.question: Can resonant scalar mixing in extended Higgs sectors produce observable CP violation while satisfying CPT and gauge-invariant resummation requirements in transition amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The question follows directly from the pinch-technique analysis of resonantly enhanced CP violation from CP-even and CP-odd Higgs mixing in [2].

questions.question: What collider environment best probes top-Higgs CP violation beyond the negligible Standard Model expectation: pp, e+e-, gamma-gamma, or mu+mu- collisions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the top-physics CP review of production and decay searches across collider types in [4] and the photon-collider parity prospects in [5].

node_502c9907dc1f.summary: These papers propose collider observables and asymmetries for determining the CP nature of Higgs bosons through gauge-boson couplings, top production, and Higgs decay angular correlations.

questions.question: Which benchmark set of Higgs CP-violating couplings can be compared consistently across weak-boson fusion, H -> ZZ -> 4l, top production, photon colliders, and EDM constraints?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the Snowmass benchmark-measurement program in [S1] and the CP-sensitive collider observables in [1], [3], [4], and [5].

questions.question: How robust is the azimuthal-angle distribution of weak-boson-fusion tagging jets as a CP analyzer when the Higgs decay channel and detector environment vary?
questions.rationale: This derives from the claim that the forward-tagging-jet azimuthal distribution determines the dominant Higgs CP nature independently of Higgs mass and decay channel in [1].

questions.question: Can resonant scalar-pseudoscalar Higgs mixing generate measurably enhanced CP violation while respecting CPT invariance and gauge-invariant resummation requirements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the pinch-technique analysis of resonantly enhanced CP violation from CP-even and CP-odd Higgs mixing in [2].

node_506463a71a2f.summary: This cluster studies CP-even and CP-odd structures in Higgs couplings using LHC, photon-collider, and weak-boson-fusion observables such as angular correlations and forward-jet distributions.

questions.question: Which single class of Higgs CP observables best resolves the current tension between rate-based CP fits and shape-based angular or jet-correlation measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from signal-strength-ratio CP fits and independent CP-sensitive observables in weak-boson-fusion jet azimuths and H to ZZ angular distributions [4][1][5].

questions.question: How can forward-tagging-jet azimuthal distributions in weak-boson fusion be combined with H to ZZ to 4l asymmetries to separately constrain CP-even, CP-odd, and CP-violating HZZ tensor structures?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the WBF jet-angle method and analytic HZZ angular asymmetries for CPC and CPV couplings [1][5].

questions.question: What future proton, e+e-, photon, or muon collider measurement would most directly benchmark Higgs-sector CP violation against electric-dipole-moment constraints?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Snowmass framing of benchmark Higgs CP measurements across collider types and comparison with virtual effects in EDM measurements [S1].

node_1ee16e5adfae.summary: These works compare collider methods for extracting Higgs CP quantum numbers, including photon-collider top pairs, Higgs plus two jets, weak-boson fusion, and decay-correlation measurements.

questions.question: Which combination of weak-boson-fusion tagging-jet azimuthal angles, H -> ZZ -> 4l decay correlations, and global signal-strength ratios gives the least model-dependent separation of CP-even, CP-odd, and mixed Higgs couplings?
questions.rationale: This follows from the WBF azimuthal method in [1], the four-lepton angular analysis in [3], and the coupling-ratio fit strategy in [4].

questions.question: Can polarized photon-photon collisions provide CP-mixing sensitivity to neutral Higgs sectors that is orthogonal to proton-collider and electric-dipole-moment constraints?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the photon-collider parity and CP-asymmetry proposals of [2] and [5] and the future-experiment comparison in [S1].

questions.question: What benchmark CP-violating Higgs parameters should be used so that proton, electron-positron, photon, and muon collider projections can be compared on a common footing?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Snowmass call for limited, well-defined benchmark CP measurements across future facilities in [S1].

node_5c231ffd2b37.summary: This cluster focuses on anomalous and CP-violating Higgs-Z interactions, using angular asymmetries in H to ZZ, H to Z lepton pairs, and e+e- to HZ processes.

questions.question: Which angular asymmetry, or combination of asymmetries, gives the most direct separation of CP-even HZgamma, CP-odd HZgamma, and HZll contact terms in H→Zℓℓ and e+e−→HZ?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dimension-six analysis showing that some angular asymmetries reveal BSM effects hidden in other observables [4].

questions.question: Can full-event four-lepton kinematics distinguish a renormalizable HZZ tensor structure from higher-dimensional ZZ or Zγ couplings with realistic event counts and backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This is based on the claim that full kinematic information in H→4ℓ can discriminate Standard Model-like and higher-dimensional gauge-boson couplings with O(50) signal events [3].

questions.question: How much do polarized e+e− beams improve sensitivity to the real and imaginary parts of CP-violating ZZh form factors beyond unpolarized angular asymmetries?
questions.rationale: This derives from the construction of CP asymmetries in e+e−→f fbar h and their complementarity between Zh production and ZZ fusion [5].

node_c1c7f3991902.summary: These papers study CP-violating effects in neutral and charged MSSM Higgs production, mixing, and decay across LHC, linear, muon, and photon collider settings.

questions.question: Can a gauge-invariant resummation framework for CP-even and CP-odd Higgs mixing identify MSSM parameter regions where resonant CP asymmetries remain observable after current collider bounds?
questions.rationale: The pinch-technique analysis in [1] derives conditions for resonantly enhanced CP violation from scalar mixing, while [4] studies explicit CP violation in MSSM Higgs benchmarks.

questions.question: Which CP-odd observables built from top decay-product momenta can separate extended-Higgs-sector CP violation from Standard Model backgrounds at the 10^-3 level?
questions.rationale: The top-pair analysis in [3] constructs observables from t and tbar decay products and estimates CP-violating effects around 10^-3 with small SM contamination.

questions.question: Are the CPX blind regions in standard MSSM Higgs search channels closed by combining gamma-gamma, tau-tau, b-bbar, and future lepton or photon collider CP-asymmetry measurements?
questions.rationale: The CPX study in [4] finds small regions where no neutral MSSM Higgs is detected in standard hadron-collider channels, while [2] surveys CP searches across collider types.

node_738122abf9e0.summary: This cluster focuses on CP-odd triple-product and spin-correlation asymmetries in supersymmetric neutralino, chargino, and sfermion production and decay at colliders.

questions.question: Can CP-odd triple-product asymmetries in neutralino production and decay remain observable once electron-EDM constraints, realistic beam polarization, and branching-fraction suppressions are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the EDM-constrained neutralino spin-correlation study in [1] and the polarized-beam triple-product analysis in [2].

questions.question: Which collider measurements best disentangle phases in mu, M1, and A_tau when neutralino, chargino, stau, and sneutrino decay rates all show phase dependence?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the neutralino phase sensitivity in [1] and [2] and the stau and sneutrino phase-dependence analysis in [3].

questions.question: How should CP-violating spin observables in supersymmetric production be combined with squark and tbW CP asymmetries to test whether a common nonstandard phase is responsible?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by phase-dependent squark decays in [4] and CP asymmetries in p pbar -> t bbar X tied to radiative tbW form factors in [5].

node_39bc680f37ee.summary: These works develop collider observables for determining Higgs CP structure through tau-pair decays, top-quark couplings, and associated Higgs production.

questions.question: Can direct LHC observables in ttH, single-top plus Higgs, and boosted dileptonic top decays close the parameter space for a pseudoscalar top-Higgs coupling that remains allowed after EDM constraints and possible cancellation assumptions?
questions.rationale: EDM bounds strongly constrain third-generation CP-violating Higgs couplings [1], while associated ttH and single-top Higgs production provide direct sensitivity to scalar and pseudoscalar top couplings [4].

questions.question: How robust are CP-sensitive azimuthal and top-decay-product correlations once NLO QCD, parton showers, boosted-Higgs substructure, hadronization, and backgrounds are treated in a common inference framework?
questions.rationale: NLO plus parton-shower studies show reduced theory uncertainties for H+2 jet and ttH CP observables [2], while boosted dileptonic ttH analyses exploit the lepton azimuthal-angle difference after realistic showering and underlying-event effects [5].

node_f149c30f512e.summary: This broad cluster examines flavor-changing Higgs couplings in two-Higgs-doublet models, including quark and lepton flavor violation, rare decays, and phenomenological constraints.

questions.question: What combination of B -> X_s gamma, meson mixing, and direct Higgs decay searches most tightly tests flavor-changing neutral currents in general two-Higgs-doublet models?
questions.rationale: This follows from strong charged-Higgs constraints from B -> X_s gamma in [1] and [4], the Model III flavor survey in [2], and flavor-violating Higgs decay constraints in [5].

questions.question: How far can NNLO Standard Model predictions for inclusive weak radiative B decays reduce the theory error that weakens charged-Higgs bounds?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the leading-order uncertainty discussion in [1] and the updated NNLO branching-ratio predictions in [3].

questions.question: Can percent-level h -> tau mu or h -> tau e branching ratios remain viable once rare decays, dipole moments, and meson oscillations are analyzed in a common flavor-violating Higgs framework?
questions.rationale: This derives from [5], which finds order-10% lepton-flavor-violating Higgs branching ratios can be allowed by existing low-energy constraints.

node_e4e186bbb7f2.summary: These papers analyze how alignment, discrete symmetries, minimal flavor violation, and CKM-controlled textures suppress or organize flavor-changing neutral currents in 2HDMs.

questions.question: What flavor data would most sharply distinguish true Yukawa alignment from a generic type-III 2HDM whose tree-level FCNC couplings are merely small by naturalness or decoupling?
questions.rationale: This follows from the alignment condition eliminating tree-level neutral-scalar FCNCs and from generic Yukawa-structure studies constraining non-holomorphic flavor-changing couplings [2], [3].

questions.question: Can the three complex alignment parameters produce observable CP violation while remaining consistent with Delta F equals 2 processes, rare B decays, Z to bb, and the rho parameter?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in model-III FCNC constraints and the aligned 2HDM result that three complex couplings introduce new CP-violating phases despite neutral flavor conservation [1], [2].

questions.question: How do charged-Higgs constraints on lambda_tt, lambda_bb, lambda_tautau, and second-generation Yukawa combinations change in multi-Higgs models with natural flavor conservation compared with the minimal 2HDM?
questions.rationale: This derives from charged-scalar coupling relations in general multi-Higgs-doublet models and flavor constraints on general 2HDM Yukawa couplings and charged-Higgs masses [4], [5].

node_d83adef03235.summary: This cluster studies rare leptonic, radiative, and penguin B-meson decays in two-Higgs-doublet models, emphasizing charged-Higgs effects, CP asymmetries, and QCD corrections.

questions.question: Which residual theoretical uncertainties in inclusive B -> X_s gamma most limit charged-Higgs mass bounds once NNLO QCD and updated nonperturbative effects are included?
questions.rationale: The evolution from leading-order scale uncertainty [1] through NLO 2HDM matching [3,4] to updated NNLO SM predictions [2] makes the limiting uncertainty a central open issue.

questions.question: Can rare radiative and leptonic B decays be combined into a stable constraint on large-tan(beta) scalar and pseudoscalar Higgs interactions in type-II 2HDMs?
questions.rationale: The large-tan(beta) Higgs contributions to B_s -> l+l- and B -> K l+l- were constrained jointly with b -> s gamma and related observables in [5].

questions.question: In which regions of two-Higgs-doublet parameter space does the perturbative series for B -> X_s gamma cease to converge fast enough for reliable phenomenological bounds?
questions.rationale: The NLO 2HDM study explicitly notes that bounds and CP asymmetries are reliable only where the perturbative series converges sufficiently fast [4].

node_40fdfb4508b4.summary: These works use radiative and gluonic B decays, especially b to s gamma, to compute QCD-corrected rates and constrain charged-Higgs masses in 2HDMs.

questions.question: What residual theoretical uncertainty in inclusive B to X_s gamma now limits charged-Higgs bounds: perturbative matching, scale dependence, nonperturbative effects, or photon-energy-cut extrapolation?
questions.rationale: The NNLO update incorporated O(alpha_s^2) corrections and new nonperturbative estimates, while the earlier uncertainty analysis identified scale dependence as dominant at leading order [1], [2].

questions.question: Can a consistent NLO-to-NNLO treatment of magnetic and chromomagnetic Wilson coefficients stabilize charged-Higgs mass limits across the viable 2HDM parameter space?
questions.rationale: NLO matching for Delta B = 1 magnetic and chromomagnetic operators strengthened the charged-Higgs bound but was sensitive to error definitions and perturbative convergence [3], [4].

questions.question: How tightly do combined b to s gamma, B_s to mu+mu-, and B to K(*) mu+mu- data constrain scalar and pseudoscalar Higgs-mediated interactions at large tan beta?
questions.rationale: The rare-B Higgs analysis derived model-independent constraints on Higgs-mediated interactions using radiative and semileptonic rare B decay data in 2HDM and minimal-flavor-violation SUSY settings [5].

node_48b7460d00ae.summary: This cluster focuses on CP-violating asymmetries in rare exclusive and inclusive B decays within general or CP-broken two-Higgs-doublet models.

questions.question: Can direct CP asymmetry in b -> s gamma reach the 10^-2 to 10^-1 level in a general CP-violating 2HDM once inclusive radiative constraints and charged-Higgs cancellation mechanisms are included?
questions.rationale: This combines the large possible asymmetry in [1] with the cancellation mechanism for charged-Higgs contributions discussed in [3].

questions.question: In the aligned 2HDM, are isospin asymmetries in B -> K* gamma and B -> rho gamma the decisive observables compared with branching ratios and direct CP asymmetries?
questions.rationale: The complementary constraining power of Delta(K* gamma) and Delta(rho gamma) is identified in [4].

questions.question: Can neutral-Higgs effects in B -> X_s tau+ tau- and penguin-dominated time-dependent CP asymmetries isolate CP-odd phases in top-specific two-Higgs-doublet flavor structures?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the neutral-Higgs contribution to B -> X_s tau+ tau- in [2] and the top-2HDM interpretation of penguin-mode deviations in [5].

node_257ff954437b.summary: These papers investigate Higgs decays such as h to mu tau as probes of lepton flavor violation in 2HDMs, effective theories, supersymmetry, and future collider searches.

questions.question: What experimental result in h -> tau mu or h -> tau e would decisively separate viable lepton-flavor-violating Higgs couplings from low-energy flavor constraints?
questions.rationale: The flavor-violating Higgs studies find that h -> tau mu and h -> tau e can have large branching ratios while remaining weakly constrained compared with quark or e-mu channels [1,3,4].

questions.question: Can a type-III two-Higgs-doublet flavor structure that explains B decays to taus also predict correlated Higgs lepton-flavor-violating signals?
questions.rationale: The type-III 2HDM paper explains B -> D tau nu, B -> D* tau nu, and B -> tau nu using flavor parameters, while other papers identify 2HDM-III as a source of LFV Higgs decays [2,4].

questions.question: In supersymmetric Higgs sectors, how tightly do tau -> mu gamma and tau -> 3mu bound observable (h,H,A) -> mu tau rates at large tan beta?
questions.rationale: The supersymmetric LFV Higgs paper links non-negligible mu-tau Higgs decays to large tan beta, smuon-stau mixing, and correlated charged-lepton flavor violation [5].

node_6e59b938c99a.summary: This cluster connects nonstandard 2HDM flavor structures to muon g-2, tau and muon flavor violation, tauonic B anomalies, and modified Higgs couplings.

questions.question: Is a type-III two-Higgs-doublet model with a single dominant epsilon^u_32 parameter still a viable minimal explanation of B -> D tau nu, B -> D* tau nu, and B -> tau nu once correlated lepton-flavor constraints are imposed?
questions.rationale: The simultaneous explanation of the tauonic B anomalies by epsilon^u_32 in a type-III 2HDM is the central result of [1].

questions.question: Can an observable h -> tau mu rate be reconciled with tau -> mu gamma without tuned Barr-Zee cancellations, and would that force a non-Higgs source of muon and electron mass?
questions.rationale: This follows from the mass-generation argument in [2] and the tau -> mu gamma versus collider-production tension in [3].

questions.question: Are flavor-enhanced Higgs couplings and t -> c h robust discovery signals of higher-dimensional fermion-mass generation, or are the required Yukawa structures already excluded by one-loop leptonic tau-decay constraints?
questions.rationale: This connects the flavor-dependent Higgs-coupling and t -> c h predictions of [4] with the large-tanbeta tau-decay loop constraints in [5].

node_969bbc9b814e.summary: These works assess direct collider sensitivity to lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decays, especially h or H to mu tau, across hadron, linear, and future facilities.

questions.question: What single collider-level pattern across h -> tau mu, h -> tau e, and h -> e mu would most decisively distinguish generic effective LFV Higgs couplings from structured flavor-symmetry explanations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between large allowed tau-mu/tau-e branching ratios in effective analyses and the correlated predictions of A4 and L_mu-L_tau models [3][5].

questions.question: Can present and future collider searches close the remaining gap between weak indirect bounds on lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decays and branching ratios at the percent-to-ten-percent level?
questions.rationale: Low-energy constraints were found to allow sizable h -> tau mu and h -> tau e rates while motivating direct LHC and collider sensitivity estimates [1][2].

questions.question: Which combination of tau -> mu gamma, tau -> 3 mu, and direct (h,H,A) -> mu tau searches is needed to decide whether supersymmetric Higgs LFV at large tan beta is viable?
