questions.rationale: The MSSM study ties detectable LFV Higgs decays to large tan beta, smuon-stau mixing, and correlated charged-lepton flavor violation [4].

node_f07d71c7a5ea.summary: This cluster develops invariant, symmetry-based, and phenomenological treatments of explicit and spontaneous CP violation in two-Higgs-doublet and supersymmetric Higgs sectors.

questions.question: Which basis-independent CP-odd invariants most directly map onto measurable Higgs masses, couplings, and decay patterns in general two-Higgs-doublet models?
questions.rationale: This follows from the basis-independent description of 2HDM masses and couplings in [4] and the phenomenological survey of 2HDM variants in [1].

questions.question: Can public 2HDM tools be extended from CP-conserving calculations to explicit or spontaneous CP violation while preserving positivity, unitarity, flexible Yukawa sectors, and decay predictions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the CP-conserving capabilities of 2HDMC described in [3] and the CP-violating Higgs mixing effects studied in [5].

questions.question: How do flavor-control strategies in type I, type II, lepton-specific, inert, and type III 2HDMs correlate with CP-violating Higgs-sector observables and charged-scalar phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This extends the 2HDM flavor-changing-neutral-current control strategies and charged-Higgs phenomenology reviewed in [1].

node_68e992b750cd.summary: Papers develop basis-independent, geometric, and phenomenological treatments of CP violation in general and complex two-Higgs-doublet models, including flavor constraints and strong-CP implications.

questions.question: Which basis-independent CP-violating invariants provide the most direct bridge between general 2HDM scalar potentials, flavor-changing scalar interactions, and experimental CP constraints?
questions.rationale: Basis-independent quantities determine physical Higgs masses and couplings [3], while flavor-changing scalar interactions generically overproduce CP violation in kaon mixing [4].

questions.question: Can public 2HDM parameter-space tools be extended from CP-conserving calculations to fully basis-independent CP-violating scans including positivity, unitarity, decays, and oblique parameters?
questions.rationale: 2HDMC provides CP-conserving calculations and constraints [2], while basis-independent work gives CP-violating oblique-parameter expressions [5].

questions.question: How tightly does custodial symmetry constrain CP violation and scalar mass degeneracies in phenomenologically viable type I, type II, lepton-specific, inert, and type III 2HDMs?
questions.rationale: The 2HDM review surveys these model classes and their flavor-control strategies [1], while custodial basis-independent constraints impose CP conservation plus mass-degeneracy conditions [5].

node_14d3bcf549d1.summary: This cluster studies explicit and spontaneous CP violation in extended scalar sectors, especially S3-symmetric three-Higgs-doublet models, along with their Higgs spectra, self-couplings, and flavor-changing interactions.

questions.question: What basis-invariant criterion should replace the simple 'all scalar-potential coefficients can be made real' test for deciding whether a multi-Higgs scalar sector explicitly conserves CP?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] shows that CP-conserving multi-Higgs models can contain irremovable complex coefficients, challenging the common real-basis criterion.

questions.question: Can geometrical CP-violating vacua in three-Higgs-doublet models remain stable once all symmetry-allowed nonrenormalizable scalar-potential terms are included?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] demonstrates preservation of a geometrical CP-violating vacuum to arbitrarily high order for Delta(27) or Delta(54) triplet scalar potentials.

questions.question: Is there a viable multi-Higgs flavor structure in which approximate CP symmetry suppresses neutral-kaon CP violation while still allowing observable scalar-mediated flavor-changing neutral currents?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] argues that multi-scalar theories can suppress flavor-changing rates but generically overproduce CP violation in the neutral-kaon mass matrix unless CP is approximately conserved.

node_d440ab059070.summary: These works characterize CP violation in two-Higgs-doublet potentials through weak-basis invariants and measurable parameters, connecting theoretical conditions to LHC constraints and predictions.

questions.question: What basis-independent observable set is sufficient to reconstruct CP violation in the general 2HDM without relying on tan beta as a fundamental parameter?
questions.rationale: Basis-independent 2HDM methods show that physical quantities cannot depend on Higgs-basis choices and that tan beta is not meaningful in the general model [2][4].

questions.question: How can public 2HDM tools be extended from CP-conserving calculations to fully CP-violating scalar potentials while preserving positivity, unitarity, decay, and precision-observable constraints?
questions.rationale: 2HDMC provides a flexible CP-conserving calculator, while the invariant literature gives necessary and sufficient conditions for explicit CP conservation or violation [1][5].

questions.question: Which mass degeneracies and oblique-parameter patterns would distinguish custodial-symmetric CP-conserving limits from genuinely CP-violating 2HDM spectra at colliders?
questions.rationale: The basis-independent custodial-symmetry analysis links custodial constraints to CP conservation, mass degeneracies, and S, T, U parameters in the general CP-violating 2HDM [3].

node_e25bbd830822.summary: The papers analyze explicit and spontaneous CP violation in MSSM and NMSSM Higgs sectors, emphasizing loop-induced scalar-pseudoscalar mixing, Higgs mass spectra, and electric dipole constraints.

questions.question: How can loop-induced scalar-pseudoscalar mixing in the MSSM Higgs sector be constrained jointly by neutral-Higgs production rates, charged-Higgs relations, third-generation squark thresholds, and electric dipole moments?
questions.rationale: Neutral-Higgs mixing and modified production are analyzed in [1], unified charged-neutral corrections in [2], and EDM consequences of CP-odd tadpole renormalization in [5].

questions.question: In the nearly degenerate H-A regime, what renormalization prescription for CP-odd tadpoles gives stable, gauge-consistent predictions for mass splitting, mixing angles, and fermionic decay rates?
questions.rationale: Large HA mixing in the degenerate heavy-Higgs regime is found in [3], while CP-odd tadpole consistency conditions are developed in [5] and decay-rate changes are emphasized in [4].

node_448c9c188259.summary: This cluster classifies accidental, custodial, discrete, and continuous symmetries of two- and multi-Higgs potentials using invariant and geometric formalisms, with implications for stability and symmetry breaking.

questions.question: Can the Minkowski-space orbit formalism provide a complete, basis-independent classification of all explicit and spontaneously broken symmetries in general two-Higgs-doublet potentials?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3] and [5], which use the GL(2,C)-induced Minkowski structure to analyze stationary points, minima, symmetries, and topology.

questions.question: How do stability and electroweak-symmetry-breaking criteria in the general 2HDM change when custodial protection of Zbb is imposed together with realistic top and Wtb couplings?
questions.rationale: This combines the concise stability criteria of [4] with the custodial-subgroup protection and unavoidable Ztt or Wtb deviations identified in [1].

questions.question: Which symmetry-breaking patterns in pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone two-Higgs-doublet models minimize the scalar-potential parameter space while avoiding unwanted charge-breaking or CP-violating vacua?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the symmetry assumptions and top-sector-controlled potential of [2] together with the no-coexistence and CP-minimum criteria of [3].

node_1083b692f162.summary: These papers use effective-field-theory operators to test anomalous gauge, top, Higgs, diboson, and electroweak interactions at colliders as model-independent probes of physics beyond the Standard Model.

questions.question: Is dimension-six SMEFT, with the 59 baryon-number-conserving operator classes, the right common language for future gauge, Higgs, top, diboson, and electroweak precision measurements, or will dimension-eight effects become unavoidable in the key channels?
questions.rationale: The operator-basis paper establishes the independent dimension-six set, while vector-boson-scattering and triboson studies explicitly compare dimension-six and dimension-eight sensitivity to anomalous gauge interactions [1,S2].

questions.question: Which future collider measurements most reduce flat directions in global SMEFT fits once one-loop anomalous-dimension mixing, Yukawa flavor mixing, and dimension-six corrections to Standard Model parameter running are included?
questions.rationale: The SMEFT renormalization papers compute the complete one-loop anomalous-dimension matrix, including gauge, Yukawa, lambda, and Standard Model parameter-running effects [2,4,5].

questions.question: Can automated one-loop matching from ultraviolet models to SMEFT Wilson coefficients be made precise enough that top-coupling and multiboson deviations can be interpreted without basis or running ambiguities?
questions.rationale: Functional matching is described as largely solved and partially automated, while Snowmass top-coupling projections rely on global SMEFT bounds on Wilson coefficients [S1,S3].

node_dbacc42a5062.summary: The cluster focuses on SMEFT operator bases, simulation tools, and global fits combining collider and low-energy data to constrain Wilson coefficients and infer possible new physics.

questions.question: What global-fit strategy prevents operator-basis redundancies and equation-of-motion replacements from biasing Wilson-coefficient constraints across collider and low-energy SMEFT data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reduced independent dimension-six operator basis and the role of EOM-induced operator mixing in SMEFT renormalization [1] and [5].

questions.question: How much do full one-loop anomalous-dimension effects, including gauge, Yukawa, and Higgs-self-coupling mixing among the three-generation dimension-six parameters, change projected SMEFT bounds from top, Higgs, and electroweak measurements?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the complete one-loop anomalous-dimension program and the Snowmass global-fit prospects for top-sector SMEFT coefficients [2], [4], [5], and [S1].

node_f846ed7c922f.summary: These works develop public tools and combined SMEFT likelihoods for interpreting Higgs, electroweak, diboson, top, flavor, and Drell-Yan measurements in global dimension-six analyses.

questions.question: Which experimental result format best preserves enough information for future SMEFT reinterpretation without committing to a fragile operator basis or UV prior?
questions.rationale: The EFT review and Snowmass framing both stress that projecting raw measurements into consistent EFT results is useful but can be degraded by interpretation pitfalls [1,S1].

questions.question: When do quadratic dimension-six terms and NLO QCD corrections materially change the posterior directions in global SMEFT fits, rather than only rescaling existing bounds?
questions.rationale: The combined LHC SMEFT fit found that NLO QCD and O(Lambda^-4) effects are instrumental for mapping Wilson-coefficient posteriors [5].

questions.question: How can one consistently connect one-loop covariant matching of UV models to global Higgs, electroweak, diboson, top, and flavor likelihoods with RG running included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the practical matching procedure using covariant derivative expansion and the global multi-dataset SMEFT analyses [2,3].

node_eee41100b165.summary: This cluster emphasizes SMEFT fits with detailed flavor structure, combining Higgs, electroweak, diboson, top, Drell-Yan, and flavor data to constrain broad classes of new-physics models.

questions.question: How much flavor structure can current Higgs, diboson, top, Drell-Yan, and precision electroweak data actually resolve before SMEFT fits become dominated by flat directions and theory assumptions?
questions.rationale: Global SMEFT fits compare flavor-universal, top-specific, and fully general flavor implementations while emphasizing dataset interplay and marginalization [1][2][4].

questions.question: For which Wilson-coefficient directions do NLO QCD corrections and dimension-six-squared terms qualitatively change the posterior relative to a linear dimension-six SMEFT fit?
questions.rationale: The combined LHC interpretation finds that NLO QCD and O(Lambda^-4) effects are instrumental for accurately mapping fitted SMEFT posteriors [2].

questions.question: What reporting standard for SMEFT likelihoods would make future collider results accurately reusable for broad new-physics model interpretation without losing correlations among BSM primary effects?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass paper warns that SMEFT utility can be degraded by poor reinterpretability, while BSM primary effects identify correlated leading deviations across Higgs and electroweak processes [S1][5].

node_adea6edb0e77.summary: The papers explain how to formulate, use, and validate the Standard Model as an effective field theory, including SMEFT versus HEFT, matching to UV models, and next-to-leading-order effects.

questions.question: What experimental reporting standards for differential measurements allow SMEFT global fits to test EFT validity and truncation errors without assuming a specific UV power counting?
questions.rationale: This derives from the consistency issues in projecting measurements into EFTs in [1] and the practical prescription for validity and truncation errors in [5].

questions.question: How can complete tree-level UV/IR dictionaries be merged with covariant one-loop matching and RG running to identify ultraviolet models compatible with measured dimension-six Wilson coefficients?
questions.rationale: The tree-level dictionary of [3] naturally complements the one-loop covariant derivative expansion and RG procedure of [2].

questions.question: Which top, electroweak, and Higgs observables require SMEFT@NLO treatment of bosonic, two-fermion, and four-fermion operators to avoid basis- or scale-dependent interpretations?
questions.rationale: The automated dimension-six one-loop implementation and its applications to top, electroweak, and Higgs phenomenology are presented in [4].

node_6f9e35abb37c.summary: This cluster studies dimension-six SMEFT operators involving top quarks, using top production, decay, four-top processes, future colliders, and low-energy observables to constrain top-philic new physics.

questions.question: Which common EFT prescriptions for top measurements are still limiting global SMEFT interpretations: truncation at dimension six, treatment of quadratic terms, theory covariance, or flavor assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the LHC top-EFT standards paper and the Monte Carlo SMEFiT program for faithful uncertainty propagation in top-sector Wilson-coefficient space [1], [2].

questions.question: Which differential top-production and decay observables most efficiently lift flat directions that remain after inclusive ttbar, single-top, associated-production, width, asymmetry, and polarization data are combined?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in Run-II-era global fits showing the interplay between inclusive and differential measurements across top production and decay observables [5].

questions.question: How much can future Higgs, electroweak, and top factories improve constraints on top-philic SMEFT operators once LHC high-pT dilepton tails and low-energy semileptonic bounds are included consistently?
questions.rationale: This derives from Snowmass projections for future top-coupling fits and from complementary constraints from CKM universality and high-pT quark-lepton contact interactions [S1], [3], [4].

node_4466e730d854.summary: These works classify and evolve SMEFT and low-energy operators beyond leading dimension-six analyses, especially dimension-eight effects, renormalization-group running, matching, and baryon- or lepton-number violation.

questions.question: How can global SMEFT analyses decide when dimension-eight effects are required, rather than treating deviations with dimension-six running and matching alone?
questions.rationale: This broad question is grounded in the complete dimension-six anomalous-dimension matrix [1]-[3] and the complete dimension-eight operator basis in [5].

questions.question: Can the 44,807 dimension-eight SMEFT operators be reduced into phenomenologically usable sectors that retain the flavor structures relevant for electroweak precision and light-by-light scattering?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the complete dimension-eight classification and its noted phenomenological examples in [5].

questions.question: How do SMEFT constraints on low-energy effective coefficients survive one-loop running and tree-level electroweak matching in tests of baryon and lepton number violation below the weak scale?
questions.rationale: This derives from the low-energy operator classification and SMEFT matching in [4] and the one-loop SMEFT running program in [1]-[3].

node_47428de922df.summary: These papers develop Hilbert-series, group-theoretic, conformal, and amplitude-based methods to enumerate complete nonredundant SMEFT operator bases at high mass dimensions.

questions.question: What is the simplest community-standard way to verify that high-dimensional SMEFT bases are complete and nonredundant when equations of motion, integration by parts, Fierz identities, and flavor permutation symmetries all matter?
questions.rationale: This reflects the repeated correction of redundant or missing operators in dimension-six, dimension-seven, dimension-eight, and sterile-neutrino SMEFT bases [1],[3],[4],[5].

questions.question: Can conformal-algebra and Hilbert-series methods be made constructive enough to output explicit operators, flavor symmetries, and redundancy relations through dimension 12 for arbitrary fermion generations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the conformal-algebra counting of SMEFT operators up to dimension 12 and Hilbert-series checks of sterile-neutrino operator counts [2],[5].

questions.question: How do lepton- and baryon-number-violating high-dimensional operators reorganize SMEFT phenomenology once dimension-seven and sterile-neutrino operators are included consistently?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that all dimension-seven SMEFT operators contain fermions and violate lepton number, with some also violating baryon number, and in the corrected sterile-neutrino dim-7 basis [3],[5].

node_4bd39cecd340.summary: This cluster studies collider sensitivity to anomalous electroweak gauge-boson self-interactions, especially quartic photon-involving couplings, across LHC, electron, photon, and muon collider channels.

questions.question: What combination of polarized e+e- beams, weak-boson-fusion WW production, and two-photon W/Z pair production best separates anomalous quartic couplings from trilinear gauge-coupling effects?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the polarized-linear-collider physics case, LHC weak-boson-fusion quartic-vertex study, two-photon anomalous-coupling analysis, and Tevatron trilinear-coupling review [1], [3], [4], and [5].

questions.question: How should anomalous quartic gauge-coupling searches be formulated in gauge-invariant EFTs so that high-energy sensitivity is not confused with spurious unitarity violation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the EFT argument that anomalous couplings should respect SM gauge symmetries and clarify unitarity issues [2].

node_c67f5c638396.summary: These works use photon-induced production and forward-detector signatures at hadron colliders to constrain anomalous quartic gauge couplings and WWgamma triple gauge interactions.

questions.question: How should photon-induced WW and ZZ production constraints on anomalous triple and quartic gauge couplings be embedded in a gauge-invariant EFT without double-counting high-energy unitarity effects?
questions.rationale: This follows from the EFT argument for anomalous couplings and the two-photon LHC studies of WWgamma, WWgammagamma, and ZZgammagamma couplings [1], [3], [4].

questions.question: Which forward-detector observables in photon-induced WW production maximize sensitivity to anomalous WWgamma couplings while controlling leptonic-decay backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposed use of forward proton detectors in photon-induced WW production and the leptonic two-photon sensitivity studies [3], [4].

questions.question: Can complete matrix-element calculations for weak-boson fusion and photon-induced channels be combined to separate genuine quartic electroweak effects from QCD and top backgrounds at the LHC?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the weak-boson-fusion calculation requiring exact electroweak and mixed QCD matrix elements plus simulated top backgrounds [2].

node_da3143e0b4cc.summary: This cluster focuses on measuring anomalous quartic vector-boson interactions at the LHC through photon-pair, weak-boson-fusion, and multi-lepton final states.

questions.question: How can LHC analyses of vector-boson scattering separate genuine quartic electroweak operators from correlated triple-gauge effects while preserving the SU(2)xU(1)-invariant EFT interpretation?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the EFT argument for gauge-invariant anomalous couplings and the classification of quartic operators without associated triple vertices [1],[4].

questions.question: Which combination of weak-boson-fusion multi-lepton channels and photon-induced tagged processes gives the most robust constraints on anomalous quartic couplings once exact electroweak amplitudes and top backgrounds are included?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the exact pp -> jj e mu nu nu calculations with ttbar backgrounds and the photon-interaction tagging program at the LHC [2],[5].

node_a58f06c51bd9.summary: These papers probe anomalous WWgamma trilinear couplings using single-W, W-pair, photon-induced, ep, and electron-positron collider processes.

questions.question: Which future measurement gives the cleanest decisive test of anomalous WWgamma couplings: photon-induced WW with forward proton tagging, leptonic two-photon diboson production, or e+e- to W+W- angular fits?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in proposed LHC two-photon and forward-detector methods and in linear-collider scaling laws for trilinear gauge-coupling sensitivity [1][2][4].

questions.question: How can WWgamma coupling fits remain valid at high transverse momentum when dimension-6 SMEFT truncation may fail around 500-1000 GeV and NLO QCD corrections alter helicity-sensitive constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the NLO QCD EFT analysis showing important fit effects, especially for longitudinal-transverse W polarization, and breakdown of the dimension-6 approximation at high pT [5].

node_8e3d56b97467.summary: This cluster examines charged and neutral anomalous triple gauge couplings, including CP-violating and dimension-eight SMEFT effects, at current and future hadron, lepton, and muon colliders.

questions.question: What observable strategy can isolate neutral triple gauge couplings when SMEFT interference with the Standard Model is suppressed by helicity and Z-polarization selection effects?
questions.rationale: Interference suppression in LHC aTGC extractions is explained in [3], while [4] finds tiny neutral-boson interference due to Z polarization mismatch.

questions.question: Can dimension-eight neutral triple-gauge operators be constrained consistently without relying on dimension-six-squared effects that obscure the EFT power counting?
questions.rationale: The EFT analysis in [3] warns that strong LHC aTGC limits often arise from partial Lambda^-4 terms, while [4] identifies the independent dimension-eight operators for neutral vertices.

questions.question: Which combination of ZZ and Z gamma measurements at hadron, lepton, and future muon colliders can test correlated neutral-coupling patterns predicted by heavy virtual fermion effects?
questions.rationale: The phenomenological study in [2] uses heavy-fermion virtual effects to motivate relations among ZZZ, ZZ gamma, and Z gamma gamma couplings.

node_b5786af2e33f.summary: These studies forecast SMEFT and anomalous triple-gauge-coupling constraints from CEPC, LHC, FCC-hh, muon-collider, diboson, VBF, and ZZ or Zgamma channels.

questions.question: At future colliders, which diboson observables can improve anomalous charged triple-gauge-coupling constraints at order Lambda^-2 rather than relying mainly on dimension-six-squared effects?
questions.rationale: The LHC SMEFT analysis finds that strong experimental aTGC bounds often come from partial Lambda^-4 terms, while consistent Lambda^-2 fits are not improved over Higgs and LEP-2 data [2][5].

questions.question: Can polarization-sensitive measurements overcome the tiny Standard Model interference of dimension-eight neutral triple-gauge operators in on-shell ZZ or Z gamma production?
questions.rationale: Only one CP-even dimension-eight neutral-TGC operator interferes with the Standard Model for on-shell neutral boson pairs, and the effect is tiny because of Z-polarization mismatch [3].

questions.question: What combined LEP, LHC, and future-collider fit strategy best removes flat directions among anomalous WWgamma and WWZ couplings in different EFT bases?
questions.rationale: LEP2 and Tevatron studies established the TGC program, while combined Higgs and LEP-2 EFT fits show that separate datasets have flat directions that are reduced in combination [1][4][5].

node_ccfc36ffc928.summary: This cluster covers theoretical structures, loop effects, LEP bounds, collider signatures, and radiation-amplitude zeros associated with anomalous neutral gauge-boson self-couplings.

questions.question: Can future ZZ and Z gamma measurements distinguish loop-induced fermionic neutral gauge self-couplings from more general anomalous ZZZ, ZZ gamma, and Z gamma gamma form factors while respecting unitarity bounds at high energy?
questions.rationale: This follows from collider studies of anomalous neutral vertices and from the severe high-energy unitarity restrictions on general ZZZ and ZZ gamma form factors [1,5].

questions.question: Are the one-loop relations h3Z = -f5gamma and h4Z = h4gamma = 0 robust signatures of fermionic new physics, or can two-loop or nonminimal sectors generate observable h4-type neutral gauge couplings?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that one-loop fermion diagrams generate only CP-conserving neutral couplings with specific relations, while two-loop new physics can produce nonzero h4 couplings [2].

questions.question: How should low-energy precision constraints be consistently matched to collider limits on anomalous neutral gauge couplings in linear light-Higgs EFTs versus electroweak chiral Lagrangians?
questions.rationale: This derives from the comparison of low-energy and Z-pole constraints in linear electroweak effective Lagrangians and heavy-Higgs or strongly interacting chiral scenarios [4].

node_b175c3c4c167.summary: These papers use initial-beam polarization and final-state W or Z polarization observables to improve collider constraints on anomalous triple and quartic gauge couplings.

questions.question: What collider observable would most clearly show whether positron polarization is essential, rather than merely beneficial, for identifying the dynamics of new interactions at a linear collider?
questions.rationale: The ILC polarization reports argue that adding positron polarization strongly improves searches and dynamics identification, especially at the staged 250 GeV machine [1,3].

questions.question: Can optimal-observable analyses of e+e- -> H f fbar determine HZgamma couplings with competitive precision without both beam polarization and multiple collider energies?
questions.rationale: The HZV-coupling study finds HZZ couplings relatively well constrained but HZgamma couplings significantly improved by beam polarization and energy choices [2].

questions.question: How should final-state helicity information and beam polarization be combined to disentangle anomalous gauge or Higgs couplings from polarization-dependent radiative effects?
questions.rationale: The general-Higgs-coupling and SME radiative-effect papers both show strong dependence on tau, photon, and charged-particle polarization states [2,4].

node_96911e336d46.summary: This cluster analyzes how dimension-six SMEFT operators modify Higgs production, decay, gauge couplings, and self-interactions, and how collider data constrain them.

questions.question: Which subset of dimension-six Higgs operators remains genuinely open after combining precision electroweak data, Higgs signal strengths, and differential Higgs distributions in one consistent global fit?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Higgs operator reduction and anomalous dimensions in [2], the precision electroweak operator bounds in [4], and the global-fit program in [5].

questions.question: How large can NLO QCD and parton-shower effects be in apparent CP or anomalous HVV measurements before they mimic or obscure dimension-six Higgs interactions?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the Higgs-characterisation framework with NLO QCD and showers in [1] and the matrix-element analyses of anomalous HVV interactions in [3].

questions.question: Can vector-boson scattering and triboson measurements at 14, 33, and 100 TeV disentangle dimension-six Higgs-sector deviations from dimension-eight effects in the same EFT analysis?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the Snowmass sensitivity studies of dimension-six and dimension-eight operators in vector-boson scattering and triboson production in [S1].

node_d34fdeb46a09.summary: These works combine Higgs measurements, electroweak precision observables, associated production, and diboson data to constrain dimension-six operators affecting Higgs and gauge sectors.

questions.question: Which dimension-six Higgs and electroweak operators remain weakly constrained after combining Higgs rates, associated-production kinematics, triple-gauge couplings, and precision electroweak data?
questions.rationale: Global EFT fits identify which windows for BSM effects remain open after electroweak precision, Higgs, Tevatron/LHC associated-production, and triple-gauge constraints are combined [3],[4],[5].

questions.question: How important are one-loop anomalous dimensions and leading-log operator mixing when translating high-scale MSSM or composite-Higgs Wilson coefficients into low-energy Higgs-coupling constraints?
questions.rationale: The Higgs d=6 analysis computed anomalous dimensions for the most relevant Wilson coefficients and applied leading-log corrections to MSSM and composite-Higgs examples [1].

questions.question: Can vector-boson scattering and triboson measurements at 14, 33, or 100 TeV break degeneracies among dimension-six and dimension-eight Higgs-gauge operators left by current global fits?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass study frames multiboson production as a probe of electroweak symmetry breaking and EFT deviations through dimension-six and dimension-eight operators at future proton colliders [S1].

node_d34fdeb46a09_1.summary: This cluster emphasizes global dimension-six SMEFT fits using Higgs, diboson, electroweak precision, and LHC Run II data to bound Higgs and electroweak interactions.

questions.question: Which linear combinations of dimension-six Higgs and electroweak Wilson coefficients remain genuinely weakly bounded after combining Higgs rates and kinematics, triple-gauge couplings, EW precision data, neutrino scattering, atomic parity violation, and LEP/SLD measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the global-fit program that separates tightly and weakly constrained operators across precision electroweak and Higgs data [2].

questions.question: How large are leading-log operator-mixing effects between the heavy scale and the electroweak scale in current global SMEFT interpretations of MSSM-like or composite-Higgs ultraviolet scenarios?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the anomalous-dimension analysis of Higgs-relevant dimension-six coefficients and its application to MSSM and composite-Higgs models [1].

questions.question: At which VBS and triboson observables, and at which collider energies, do dimension-eight operators add information that cannot be captured by the dimension-six electroweak SMEFT fit alone?
questions.rationale: Snowmass sensitivity studies explicitly compare dimension-six and dimension-eight EFT effects in vector-boson scattering and triboson production at 14, 33, and 100 TeV [S1].

node_96911e336d46_1.summary: These papers use Higgs rates and kinematic distributions at current and future colliders to constrain dimension-six SMEFT operators affecting Higgs couplings and self-interactions.

questions.question: How should Higgs signal strengths, differential VH distributions, and electroweak precision data be combined to lift flat directions among CP-conserving dimension-six Higgs operators?
questions.rationale: This follows from the global dimension-six SM fit in [2] and the use of associated H+V kinematic distributions to remove weakly constrained directions in [4].

questions.question: When extracting Higgs Wilson coefficients, how large are the leading-log operator-mixing effects between the heavy new-physics scale and the electroweak scale for models such as the MSSM or composite Higgs?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the anomalous-dimension and operator-mixing analysis of Higgs dimension-six coefficients in [1].

questions.question: Can Higgs-pair production in bbtautau distinguish a modified trilinear coupling from correlated dimension-six changes in single-Higgs observables and gluon-fusion production?
questions.rationale: This derives from the dimension-six Higgs-pair analysis including c6, full EFT parameter space, and single-Higgs bounds in [5].

node_be6a9d48e74d.summary: These works derive model-independent limits on dimension-six operators from electroweak precision observables, vector-boson production and scattering, and partial-wave unitarity.

questions.question: What electroweak observable or diboson measurement would most reduce the remaining flat directions among dimension-six SMEFT operators beyond the traditional S,T,U description?
questions.rationale: This question follows from model-independent electroweak EFT fits that identify which operator combinations are constrained by pole observables and W-pair production [1],[4].

questions.question: Can a basis-independent effective-coupling formalism consistently combine LEP, SLD, low-energy parity violation, LHC Higgs, and triple-gauge-coupling data without hiding correlations among operators?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in global fits using broad electroweak datasets and in formalisms designed to map constraints independently of the chosen operator basis [1],[2],[4].

questions.question: Which weakly bounded dimension-six interactions remain plausible targets for large new-physics effects after present electroweak and Higgs precision data are combined?
questions.rationale: This follows from the systematic EFT surveys that identify both strongly bounded and poorly bounded effective interactions [3].

node_2a33028f6003.summary: These papers compute one-loop electroweak and NLO QCD SMEFT corrections to Higgs decays and production processes while assessing anomalous-coupling effects and EFT truncation uncertainties.

questions.question: Can the one-loop running and operator mixing of Higgs-gauge dimension-six operators be incorporated consistently in joint fits to h -> gamma gamma, h -> Z gamma, and the S parameter across commonly used SMEFT bases?
questions.rationale: This derives from the RG mixing and revised relation among S, h -> gamma gamma, and h -> Z gamma emphasized in [1].

questions.question: Which differential ttH observables best disentangle O_tphi, O_phiG, and O_tG at NLO QCD while controlling EFT truncation uncertainties shared with inclusive H, Hj, and HH production?
questions.rationale: The relevant three operators, NLO QCD treatment, differential study, and cross-process implications are presented in [4].

questions.question: Can NLO non-linear EFT parametrizations of Higgs-pair production with full top-mass dependence be matched to linear SMEFT interpretations without losing the non-uniform K-factor information in m_hh and Higgs pT distributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the significant non-homogeneous NLO K-factors and analytic HH parametrization reported in [5].

node_96007d21c29f.summary: These studies constrain nonstandard Higgs interactions with electroweak gauge bosons using collider channels such as HWW, HZγ, Hγ, and associated Higgs production.

questions.question: Can a unified matrix-element framework consistently extract CP-even and CP-odd anomalous HVV couplings across VBF, VH, gluon fusion, and H -> ZZ, WW, gamma gamma, and Z gamma channels once NLO QCD and parton showers are included?
questions.rationale: The Higgs-characterisation framework combines EFT interactions with tree-level and NLO QCD simulations matched to showers [1], while anomalous HVV studies use matrix-element methods across multiple production and decay topologies [2].

questions.question: Which VBF azimuthal-angle observables remain linearly sensitive to interference between SM, CP-even anomalous, and CP-odd anomalous Higgs-gauge couplings after realistic collider selections?
questions.rationale: Anomalous VBF Higgs production at NLO introduced an azimuthal variable designed to directly measure interference among CP-even, CP-odd, and SM couplings [3].

node_c2b08e89f642.summary: These papers develop, renormalize, and match electroweak chiral and low-energy effective Lagrangians with light or heavy Higgs sectors using one-loop and functional methods.

questions.question: How can one systematically match a nonlinear electroweak chiral EFT with a light Higgs onto SMEFT in the regime where dimension-eight operators compete with or dominate dimension-six effects?
questions.rationale: [1] compares linear and nonlinear Higgs representations and notes cases where dimension-eight operators can be more important than dimension-six operators.

questions.question: Can functional one-loop matching be fully automated for the complete NLO electroweak chiral Lagrangian with arbitrary Higgs functions and gauge-Higgs operators?
questions.rationale: [2] constructs the complete light-Higgs electroweak chiral Lagrangian at NLO, while [S1] describes functional matching as solved at one loop and partially automated for EFT applications.

questions.question: Which combinations of S, T, U and anomalous WWgamma or WWZ couplings can still discriminate heavy weakly coupled physics from genuinely nonlinear electroweak symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: [5] connects chiral-Lagrangian operators to oblique parameters and triple-gauge vertices and estimates their coefficients in a heavy-fermion model.

node_5bb04e690556.summary: This broad cluster explores beyond-Standard-Model collider signatures including the 750 GeV diphoton excess, vector-like fermions, extended Higgs sectors, and colored scalar resonances.

questions.question: What analysis framework would most reliably turn a single new-resonance excess into measurements of spin, parity, and tensor couplings while retaining spin correlations and finite-width effects in NLO Monte Carlo event samples?
questions.rationale: This follows from the spin-entangled decay method in MadGraph [1] and the angular/mass-distribution programs for determining resonance spin and parity in diboson final states [3,4].

questions.question: Which combination of single production, pair production, and indirect top, bottom, and Higgs coupling measurements can close the viable parameter space for vector-like quarks that remains after electroweak precision and Z -> b bbar constraints?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the vector-like-quark mixing constraints and LHC decay/single-production implications in [2], extended by the chromomagnetic single-production reach emphasized in [S2].

questions.question: At future hadron colliders, what minimal set of resonance observables beyond a bump in the invariant-mass spectrum would distinguish Z-prime, coloron, and other heavy-resonance interpretations across the coupling-versus-mass plane?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Snowmass study of projected dijet-resonance discovery and exclusion reach for Z-prime and coloron models in coupling-mass space [S1].

node_e810e43cd793.summary: These papers study LHC and future-collider strategies for discovering or constraining vector-like quarks through pair and single production in many final states.

questions.question: Which combination of single production, pair production, charged-current decays, and neutral-current decays is sufficient to identify the SU(2)_L representation and electric charge of a discovered vector-like quark?
questions.rationale: The top-partner study compares T, B, X, and Y signals across twelve final states and uses channel combinations to establish charged and neutral decays [2].

questions.question: Can electroweak precision constraints, Z→bb data, Higgs production, and top/bottom coupling measurements be folded into LHC searches without assuming that vector-like quarks couple only to the third generation?
questions.rationale: The handbook derives mixing constraints from oblique corrections and Z→bb and studies implications for decays, single production, Higgs production, and top/bottom couplings [1].

questions.question: How much new parameter space do chromomagnetic single-production modes open at the HL-LHC and 100 TeV colliders compared with electroweak single production and QCD pair production?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass white paper argues that chromomagnetic production can extend reach where traditional pair-production and electroweak single-production searches are insensitive [S1].

node_a0765e34909a.summary: These works focus on vector-like quark phenomenology, especially bottom-like states and nonstandard decay modes that affect LHC search strategies and mass bounds.

questions.question: What minimal set of LHC final states can distinguish bottom-like vector-like quark isosinglets from doublets once nonstandard branching fractions and single-production channels are allowed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the multiplet-dependent decay and single-production constraints in [1] and the channel-combination strategy in [2].

questions.question: How much do current vector-like bottom mass bounds weaken in models where decays feed confining-sector resonances, stable charged states, or multi-boson final states rather than the standard electroweak modes?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the diverse vectorlike-confinement signatures in [3] and the model-dependent mass exclusions summarized in [5].

node_49a47294a236.summary: These papers examine theoretical vector-like quark and lepton extensions of the Standard Model, emphasizing flavor structure, mixing constraints, precision tests, and collider implications.

questions.question: What single pattern of deviations in charged currents, neutral currents, and flavor-changing neutral processes would establish vector-like quark mixing as the right explanation rather than a generic flavor EFT?
questions.rationale: This broad discriminant is motivated by the classification of vector-like quark models and their neutral-current and charged-current relations in [2] and [4].

questions.question: Where is the weakest point in the consensus that TeV-scale vector-like leptons can evade electroweak precision, lepton-flavor, EDM, and LHC multilepton constraints while still affecting Higgs decays?
questions.rationale: This derives from the electroweak-precision limits in [1] and the correlated Higgs, lepton-flavor, g-2, EDM, and collider effects in [5].

questions.question: Can vector-like matter that raises the lightest supersymmetric Higgs mass while preserving perturbative unification be distinguished experimentally from non-SUSY vector-like fermion extensions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the SUSY vector-like matter mechanism for increasing the Higgs mass and maintaining perturbative gauge unification in [3].

node_abd15135f27d.summary: These studies propose searches for vector-like top partners at the LHC and LHeC using single production, exotic decays, Higgs-associated channels, and same-sign dileptons.

questions.question: What minimal simplified-model parameterization lets pair production, electroweak single production, and chromomagnetic single production of vector-like top partners be compared without experiment-specific recasting?
questions.rationale: This combines the model-independent effective-Lagrangian framework, the simplified-model interpretation strategy, and the Snowmass chromomagnetic-production program [1],[4],[S1].

questions.question: Which final states best close the remaining blind spots between same-sign dilepton searches for Q=5/3 or Q=-1/3 partners and exotic Higgs-decay searches for uncolored top partners?
questions.rationale: This follows from the same-sign dilepton t tbar W W strategy for colored partners and exotic Higgs decays to mirror-sector states in uncolored-naturalness models [2],[3].

questions.question: Can LHC kinematics determine the mass and spin of a discovered top partner well enough to distinguish weakly coupled naturalness scenarios with a parity-stabilized WIMP from composite-Higgs vector-like quarks?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the model-independent study of discovery, mass determination, and spin measurement for a parity-odd top partner with a WIMP candidate [5].

node_8170ed1934fd.summary: These papers interpret the reported 750 GeV diphoton anomaly with singlet scalars, extended Higgs sectors, vector-like fermions, and related resonance models.

questions.question: What minimal follow-up measurement would have been required to decide whether the 750 GeV diphoton excess was a narrow elementary resonance, a broad strongly interacting state, or a cascade/edge topology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the narrow-versus-wide interpretations in [1] and the loop, messenger, edge, and hidden-valley possibilities in [5].

questions.question: Can a heavy Higgs-like scalar or pseudoscalar produce an observable diphoton rate through vector-like fermion loops while remaining compatible with Run 1 constraints and minimal two-Higgs-doublet expectations?
questions.rationale: The need for extra charged or vector-like matter is argued in modified diphoton-width studies [2], fermion-loop interpretations [3], and two-Higgs-doublet analyses [4].

node_f51fb2aced10.summary: These works analyze sequential fourth-generation fermions and their consequences for Higgs physics, electroweak precision constraints, flavor observables, CP violation, and viable mass spectra.

questions.question: What single experimental result, combining Higgs rates with electroweak precision fits, would have definitively separated a viable sequential fourth generation from tuned mass-and-mixing spectra?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the allowed mass and mixing ensembles and dramatic Higgs effects in [1], the oblique-parameter correlations in [2], and the post-126 GeV global fits in [5].

questions.question: Can any fourth-generation spectrum satisfy vacuum stability, triviality, perturbative unification, and empirical mixing-angle constraints while retaining distinctive LHC decay signatures?
questions.rationale: This derives from the cutoff-scale, vacuum-stability, and triviality discussion in [1] and the mass, mixing, lifetime, and decay-mode constraints surveyed in [3].

questions.question: Was the most robust fourth-generation search strategy direct discovery, full LHC exclusion, or indirect exclusion through Higgs and electroweak observables?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [4], which framed LHC discovery or exclusion as decisive, and [5], which quantified the impact of the 126 GeV Higgs on three- and four-generation fits.

node_2a1fc6c57902.summary: These papers study how a sequential fourth fermion generation would alter Higgs production, decay, and electroweak precision fits, with LHC Higgs data strongly constraining or excluding much of the scenario.

questions.question: Given the observed 126 GeV Higgs signal, is there any remaining sequential fourth-generation parameter region in which electroweak oblique-parameter correlations, Higgs production enhancement, and Higgs decay data can all be reconciled without adding non-sequential new physics?
questions.rationale: Earlier allowed spectra and Higgs-rate modifications in [1] and oblique-parameter correlations in [2] are directly challenged by the post-Higgs statistical analysis in [5].

questions.question: What decisive collider signature would have been needed to distinguish a constrained fourth chiral family from other sources of modified Higgs rates, such as same-sign dilepton Higgs decays, long-lived heavy fermions, or altered angular distributions?
questions.rationale: The distinctive Higgs and exotic signatures proposed in [1] connect to the broader fourth-generation decay and lifetime taxonomy in [3].

node_bec254015649.summary: This cluster examines possible fourth-generation neutrinos, especially Majorana or long-lived states, and their implications for collider searches, Higgs decays, dark matter, and low-energy constraints.

questions.question: What single collider signature would most decisively revive or close the fourth-family neutrino interpretation of Higgs-sector anomalies with invisible decays?
questions.rationale: The two-Higgs-doublet fourth-family study used invisible decays of a light Higgs state to fourth-family neutrinos to explain gamma-gamma and VV signals [3].

questions.question: Can a bottom-up effective-operator description of fourth-family mass generation remain compatible with electroweak precision constraints once the leptonic sector is included explicitly?
questions.rationale: The fourth-family discovery study emphasized electroweak precision constraints on fourth-family lepton masses and modeled new strong dynamics with effective four-fermion operators [1].

questions.question: Are searches optimized for heavy quark decays with missing energy sufficient to cover fourth-generation scenarios where invisible particles accompany top-rich final states?
questions.rationale: Dark-matter-motivated T' searches showed that t-tbar plus missing energy had not been central in fourth-generation searches despite applying broadly to invisible-particle production with tops [4].

node_1dc4b3b77b79.summary: These works explore how fourth-generation quarks and new CKM phases could affect rare B and K decays, CP violation, mixing, and flavor-changing neutral-current observables.

questions.question: Which rare K and B observables would now provide the cleanest remaining test of fourth-generation flavor violation once Delta F=2 mixing, epsilon_K, b to s gamma, and oblique constraints are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This is derived from the global SM4 analyses of neutral-meson mixing, rare K and B decays, and electroweak constraints in [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Can the correlations among S_psi phi, S_psi K_S, B to K pi direct CP asymmetries, and b to s l+l- still distinguish a fourth-generation electroweak-penguin effect from other non-minimal flavor-violating explanations?
questions.rationale: The correlation is motivated by the fourth-generation explanations of B CP anomalies and electroweak-penguin effects in [3] and [5], constrained by rare-decay inputs in [2].

questions.question: How large can mixing with a fourth family remain under exact 4 by 4 CKM unitarity when QCD-correction uncertainties in FCNC constraints are treated systematically rather than simplistically?
questions.rationale: This follows from the exploratory CKM4 study that allowed unexpectedly large fourth-family mixing under simplifying assumptions for QCD corrections [4].

node_17cf7a278bb2.summary: This broad cluster studies collider production, decay signatures, and discovery prospects for new colored particles such as color-octet scalars, colorons, and related resonances.

questions.question: What dijet or top-distribution measurement at future hadron colliders would most cleanly distinguish a coloron, color-octet vector, color-singlet vector, or colored scalar resonance if no narrow bump is observed?
questions.rationale: This follows from top kinematic sensitivity to vector color singlet or octet resonances in [1], the general colored-resonance classification in [2], and future coupling-versus-mass reach in [S1].

questions.question: Can searches for pair-produced color-octet particles with jets plus missing energy be made topology-complete enough that CMSSM-motivated HT and MET cuts no longer leave discoverable spectra uncovered?
questions.rationale: The question is directly based on [3], which shows that current Tevatron searches can miss spectra unless HT and MET cuts are optimized.

questions.question: How can flavor-universal coloron explanations of high-ET jet excesses be stress-tested against modern dijet limits while preserving their role as baseline models for new strong interactions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the coloron model proposed for the CDF jet excess in [5] and the LHC dijet-resonance bounds and formulation in [2].

node_e8f6572d595c.summary: These papers focus on color-octet scalar models, including MFV and supersymmetric sgluon scenarios, and their LHC signatures in multijet, heavy-quark, and same-sign dilepton channels.

questions.question: Which collider signature would most decisively separate minimally flavor-violating color-octet scalars, N=2 sgluons, composite octets, and octetonium-like metastable colored scalars?
questions.rationale: This broad discriminating question follows from the distinct MFV, sgluon, composite, and octetonium scenarios and their multijet, heavy-quark, and diphoton signatures [2,3,4,5].

questions.question: Can the semitauonic B to D(*) tau nu anomaly be explained by a sub-TeV weak-doublet colored scalar without conflicting with Z to bb, muon magnetic moment, and scalar mass-matrix constraints?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by the minimally coupled colored-scalar explanation of the semitauonic puzzle and its listed precision constraints [1].

questions.question: How much viable parameter space remains for color-octet scalar cascade decays into lighter colored scalars plus gauge bosons once renormalization-group running, mass splittings, and Tevatron/LHC limits are imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Manohar-Wise color-octet scalar analysis of Higgs-coupling-induced splittings, RG constraints, and limited room for two-body cascade decays [3].

node_653ef1b18678.summary: This cluster centers on massive colored resonances, especially colorons and diquarks, using dijet, top-pair, and multijet searches to map collider constraints and distinguish resonance properties.

questions.question: What single collider observable would most cleanly distinguish a coloron from other colored dijet resonances with comparable mass and production rate?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from [2], which classifies colored resonances with large dijet rates, and [5], which maps dijet limits in coupling-mass space for colorons and leptophobic Z bosons.

questions.question: Can top-quark high-pT and W-boson distributions provide a robust cross-check of dijet-based color-octet vector searches near the TeV scale?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], which shows that vector color-singlet or octet s-channel new physics can distort high-pT top and W distributions.

questions.question: How should future-hadron-collider dijet searches present coupling-versus-mass reach so that coloron limits are directly comparable across energies and luminosities?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the coupling-mass mapping of [5] and the future-collider Snowmass projections in [S1].

node_05261f6edf25.summary: These works analyze scalar and vector bileptons in models such as 3-3-1 theories, deriving current bounds and proposing collider discovery channels with same-sign leptons and four-lepton final states.

questions.question: Which same-sign lepton or four-lepton channel would provide the most model-independent discovery test of scalar versus vector bileptons once present low-energy mass-coupling bounds are imposed?
questions.rationale: The general bilepton Lagrangian and hadron-collider studies combine low-energy constraints with collider reach for scalar and vector bilepton production [1], [3].

questions.question: Can e-e- collider measurements of beam polarization, initial-state radiation, and hard photon emission determine whether a doubly charged bilepton is a gauge vector rather than a scalar resonance?
questions.rationale: The e-e- study stresses polarization, beam spread, ISR, and hard photon emission as tools for discovering and identifying the gauge nature of vector bileptons [4].

questions.question: How do exotic fermion or squark cascade decays in extended gauge models obscure or complement the classic bilepton signatures used in 3-3-1-inspired collider searches?
questions.rationale: The exotic isosinglet-quark study shows that extended models can contain new fermions with varied decay modes, while bilepton production studies often rely on clean leptonic channels [2], [3].

node_ec33c899f7c8.summary: This cluster develops methods for determining the spin and parity of newly discovered resonances, especially Higgs-like particles, through angular correlations and decay distributions at colliders.

questions.question: What minimal angular and invariant-mass observables would settle whether a single-produced resonance has spin 0, 1, or 2 when full reconstruction in X -> ZZ, WW, and gamma gamma is only partially available?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from full angular-analysis methods for single-produced resonances decaying to vector bosons [2] and their extension to ZZ, WW, and gamma gamma channels [3].

questions.question: How accurately must Monte Carlo resonance decays preserve spin correlations and finite-width effects before spin-parity discrimination becomes limited by data rather than event-generation systematics?
questions.rationale: This comes from the MadGraph spin-entangled decay method for narrow resonances [1] and the reliance of spin-parity analyses on complete spin correlations [2,3].

node_85f63d004787.summary: These papers review and update precision electroweak tests of the Standard Model, using global fits and collider measurements to constrain Higgs, top, and possible new-physics effects.

questions.question: Which electroweak precision observable at future e+e- Higgs, Z, and WW factories would most sharply reveal a failure of the Standard Model global fit?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [2] and [4], which emphasize CEPC-scale Z, W, and Higgs samples and NNLO global electroweak fits as precision tests of the Standard Model.

questions.question: How should future lepton-collider running scenarios balance Higgs-factory, Z-pole, and WW-threshold data to maximize sensitivity to indirect new-physics effects?
questions.rationale: This follows from the CEPC operating modes in [2] and the Snowmass discussion of linear-collider running scenarios and precision electroweak measurements in [S3].

questions.question: Can theory uncertainties in multi-loop electroweak predictions be reduced fast enough to match the experimental precision expected from future e+e- collider programs?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [4], which identifies accurate multi-loop predictions as central to using global electroweak fits to test the Standard Model and constrain new physics.

node_e951dcbac2ea.summary: This cluster surveys the physics potential of future electron-positron colliders such as ILC, CLIC, FCC-ee, and CEPC for precision Higgs, electroweak, top, and new-physics studies.

questions.question: What single precision measurement program would most decisively establish whether a future e+e- collider should be optimized as a Higgs factory, Z factory, WW-threshold machine, top-threshold machine, or high-energy linear collider?
questions.rationale: This framing question follows from the CEPC and TLEP cases for very high luminosity Higgs, Z, W, and top studies [2,4] and the linear-collider emphasis on 500 GeV to multi-TeV energy reach [5,S2].

questions.question: How should running scenarios, positron polarization, photon-photon operation, e-e- operation, and the number of interaction regions be prioritized against precision Standard Model and BSM reach?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Snowmass resource discussion of accelerator and experimental options for the linear collider program [S3].

questions.question: Which beyond-LHC null result or anomaly would most strengthen the physics case for complementary non-collider experiments versus a next e+e- collider stage?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Physics Beyond Colliders report's emphasis on complementary CERN infrastructure [3] alongside future e+e- collider programs for Higgs, electroweak, and new-particle studies [2,5].

node_5694d329e183.summary: These reports synthesize community studies on future collider programs, comparing HL-LHC, lepton colliders, muon colliders, and complementary CERN initiatives for Higgs and beyond-Standard-Model physics.

questions.question: What community-agreed metric should decide between future collider options after the HL-LHC: Higgs-coupling precision, BSM mass reach, rare-signature coverage, technical readiness, or complementarity with non-collider facilities?
questions.rationale: This follows from the uniform Higgs-collider comparisons in [3], the European strategy synthesis in [4], and the Energy Frontier prioritization context in [S1].

questions.question: Which HL-LHC or HE-LHC outcome would most strongly change the strategic case for a future e+e- Higgs factory, muon collider, or CERN Physics Beyond Colliders program?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the HL-LHC experimental challenges and physics reach in [2], the HE-LHC BSM study in [5], and the complementary CERN program in [1].

questions.question: Where is the consensus weakest in comparing broad BSM sensitivity across proposed facilities for SUSY, compositeness, leptoquarks, new bosons, dark matter, long-lived particles, and anomaly searches?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Snowmass BSM Energy Frontier comparison of proposed experiments across many model classes and signatures in [S2].

node_09cd9526cc96.summary: This cluster collects strategic planning documents and community input reports for U.S. and European particle physics, including Snowmass, P5, European Strategy, and early-career perspectives.

questions.question: What single set of physics-deliverable criteria should determine whether the next major collider priority is chosen for Higgs precision, energy-frontier BSM reach, flavor or dark-sector coverage, or long-term accelerator readiness?
questions.rationale: This broad strategy question follows from EPPSU, Snowmass Energy Frontier, and P5 documents that compare proposed projects through community priorities, physics reach, and implementation needs [1,2,3].

questions.question: Where is the community consensus weakest in comparing model-specific BSM searches with more general anomaly-detection and long-lived-particle programs as drivers for future collider design?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Snowmass BSM report's explicit combination of model-specific explorations, general explorations, dark matter at colliders, long-lived particles, and anomaly detection [5,S2].

questions.question: How should U.S. and European planning processes quantitatively balance near-term experimental continuity against mid- and long-term facilities when different frontiers target dark matter, dark energy, inflation, and collider new physics?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the bottom-up EPPSU process, the P5 prioritization report, and Snowmass frontier reports that span Energy and Cosmic Frontier goals [1,3,S3].

node_d6527317c44c.summary: These reports survey the physics reach of LHC upgrades, future hadron and lepton colliders, and complementary CERN facilities for Higgs studies, Standard Model tests, and searches beyond the Standard Model.

questions.question: What uniform benchmark set would allow the HL-LHC, HE-LHC, future lepton colliders, and CERN Beyond-Collider proposals to be compared on common Higgs, Standard Model, and BSM physics metrics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the uniform future-collider Higgs methodology in [3] and the complementary CERN program scope in [1].

questions.question: Which detector and accelerator R&D bottlenecks most strongly determine whether a 10^35 cm^-2 s^-1 luminosity upgrade translates into real gains in Higgs precision and BSM reach?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the explicit coupling of high-radiation detector performance, luminosity, and physics reach in [2].

questions.question: How should the field prioritize high-energy colliders, high-intensity beams, and complementary non-collider facilities over the next 10-20 years when present LHC measurements remain Standard-Model-like?
questions.rationale: This broad strategy tension is grounded in the Beyond Colliders 10-20 year program in [1], the HL/HE-LHC BSM survey in [4], and accelerator-capability framing in [S1].

node_f6e5a4760136.summary: This cluster focuses on FCC and CEPC physics cases, emphasizing high-luminosity circular colliders as precision Z, W, Higgs, and top factories and as pathways toward 100 TeV proton collisions.

questions.question: What precision measurement at a circular e+e- collider, among Z-pole observables, WW threshold quantities, Higgs couplings, and top-threshold parameters, would most decisively justify the staged FCC-ee or CEPC program if no direct new particle appears?
questions.rationale: The CEPC and FCC-ee programs emphasize enormous Z, W, Higgs, and top samples in [1], [3], [5], and [S1].

questions.question: How should detector concepts and run plans be optimized across the Z pole, WW threshold, ZH peak, and ttbar threshold to maximize sensitivity to indirect new physics while preserving the option of a later 100 TeV proton collider?
questions.rationale: The staged FCC-ee to FCC-hh program and detector requirements are described in [3] and [5], while CEPC detector and operation scenarios are summarized in [1] and [S1].

node_a9fded088c7f.summary: These papers collect personal recollections and historical studies of theoretical particle physics and early collider development, especially the roles of Bruno Touschek, Raoul Gatto, and AdA.

questions.question: Which archival or oral-history evidence would most decisively clarify how informal exchanges, letters, visits, and institutional choices shaped the first AdA electron-positron collisions between Frascati and Orsay?
questions.rationale: This follows from the account of AdA's move and the collaboration's reconstruction from unpublished documents, interviews, visits, and correspondence [5].

questions.question: How can historical studies of particle theory best separate personal reminiscence and retrospective conference perspective from contemporaneous technical decision-making and error correction?
questions.rationale: The node juxtaposes personal lecture reminiscences, reflections on mistakes, conference summaries, and Pauli's unpublished letters as distinct historical sources [1].

node_863ec789e289.summary: This cluster reviews TeV-scale electron-positron linear collider programs, covering Higgs, top, electroweak precision, supersymmetry, exotic physics, beam polarization, and accelerator options.

questions.question: What running scenario for a staged e+e- linear collider best balances 500 GeV precision Higgs and top measurements against later TeV-scale searches for supersymmetry, new vector bosons, and exotic sectors?
questions.rationale: Linear-collider studies emphasize an initial 500 GeV phase followed by upgrades to about 1 TeV or beyond for precision Standard Model and new-particle studies [2].

questions.question: How decisive are positron polarization, photon-photon running, e-e- running, and one-versus-two interaction-region choices for separating Standard Model precision tests from beyond-Standard-Model discovery modes?
questions.rationale: Snowmass accelerator and experimental options explicitly discuss running scenarios, positron polarization, photon-photon collisions, e-e- collisions, and detector design choices [S3].

questions.question: Which measurements at a linear collider would remain uniquely valuable if a future 100 TeV proton-proton collider also probes the energy frontier?
questions.rationale: Linear-collider reports stress clean precision access to Higgs, top, electroweak, exotic, and supersymmetric physics [1],[4], while 100 TeV pp studies motivate a complementary energy-frontier program [3].

node_b69c720dcf01.summary: These works analyze precision electroweak observables and global Standard Model fits, using LEP, SLC, Tevatron, and LHC data to determine parameters and constrain new physics.

questions.question: Which future measurement of the W mass, effective weak mixing angle, Higgs couplings, or top mass would most sharply decide whether the electroweak global-fit tensions are statistical fluctuations, theory-limitations, or evidence for BSM vacuum polarization effects?
questions.rationale: The NNLO global-fit study frames precision fits as overconstrained SM tests and as tools for constraining new physics with LHC and ILC inputs [2].

questions.question: How can electroweak fits consistently combine fermion-scattering precision observables with multi-boson and vector-boson-scattering measurements without double counting SMEFT or oblique new-physics information?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass report identifies both W/Z-mediated fermion scattering and multi-boson processes as complementary precision probes of BSM physics [S1].

node_dda1980fdf25.summary: This cluster centers on global electroweak fitting frameworks such as Gfitter and their use in combining precision measurements, theoretical predictions, and Higgs-era constraints.

questions.question: What single unresolved inconsistency among W mass, effective weak mixing angle, top mass, Higgs data, and LEP/SLC observables most limits the credibility of the current global electroweak fit?
questions.rationale: Post-Higgs global fits overconstrain the Standard Model at the electroweak scale and report nontrivial goodness-of-fit values after including radiative corrections and uncertainties [2,3].

questions.question: How should global electroweak fitting frameworks combine theoretical uncertainties, direct-search information, and toy-Monte-Carlo statistical interpretations so that BSM constraints are reproducible?
questions.rationale: Gfitter was introduced as a modular framework with theory plugins, direct Higgs-search constraints, and toy Monte Carlo statistical analysis [5].

questions.question: Can future LHC and ILC electroweak measurements distinguish oblique new physics from deviations in multi-boson and vector-boson-scattering processes within one coherent precision-fit methodology?
questions.rationale: Snowmass framing identifies both fermion scattering mediated by W/Z bosons and multi-boson or VBS processes as precision targets for indirect BSM searches [S1].

node_b7266d9e6c9d.summary: These papers review experimental electroweak measurements from LEP, SLC, Tevatron, and the LHC, highlighting precision observables, W-pair data, and tests of Standard Model consistency.

questions.question: What single global electroweak-fit framework can consistently combine LEP W-pair-era cross sections, LHC high-energy Drell-Yan tails, and multi-boson measurements without double counting SMEFT sensitivity?
questions.rationale: This reflects the need to connect LEP precision measurements, high-energy Drell-Yan electroweak tests, and Snowmass multi-boson precision goals [1],[3],[S1].

questions.question: Where is the present electroweak precision program most vulnerable to systematics: classic observables such as M_W and sin^2 theta_eff, or high-energy observables whose SMEFT sensitivity grows with energy?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Snowmass framing of massive gauge boson observables and the claim that LHC Drell-Yan spectra can rival or surpass LEP sensitivity [3],[5],[S1].

node_eaa99c55057d.summary: This cluster focuses on electroweak precision fits after the Higgs discovery, using the measured Higgs mass to overconstrain the Standard Model and bound model-independent new physics effects.

questions.question: What single precision measurement would most sharply decide whether the post-Higgs electroweak fit tension is a statistical fluctuation, a theory-uncertainty issue, or evidence for oblique new physics?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the p-value and overconstrained Standard Model fit after the Higgs discovery in [2] and the oblique-parameter interpretation of precision data in [3].

questions.question: Are current global-fit methodologies robust enough that different treatments of theoretical uncertainties, direct-search constraints, and toy-Monte-Carlo statistics lead to the same new-physics conclusions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the NNLO global-fit program in [1] and the Gfitter emphasis on modular models and statistical interpretation in [4].

questions.question: Can models that stabilize the weak scale while suppressing electroweak precision corrections, such as folded supersymmetry, be cleanly distinguished from generic model-independent fit deviations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the folded-supersymmetry solution to the LEP paradox in [5] and the use of global fits to constrain new physics after all SM parameters became measured in [1].

node_23f955322967.summary: These papers study how precision electroweak data, top and W mass measurements, and theoretical consistency bounds were used to infer or constrain the Higgs boson mass.

questions.question: After direct Higgs discovery, what residual role do indirect Higgs-mass constraints from M_W, sin^2 theta_eff, m_t, and g-2_mu play as consistency tests of the Standard Model versus MSSM loop effects?
questions.rationale: The MSSM precision-observable review in [1] and the broader electroweak precision framework in [5] motivate using Higgs-mass consistency as a loop-level new-physics probe.

questions.question: Which improved precision measurement would most sharply distinguish a genuinely heavy-Higgs-compatible extension from compensating shifts in oblique corrections or hadronic inputs to g-2_mu?
questions.rationale: Heavy-Higgs-compatible models are argued to have distinctive precision or collider signatures in [2], while [4] shows that changing hadronic input to g-2_mu also shifts the electroweak Higgs bound.

node_f4d818bf3934.summary: This cluster examines the theoretical development and phenomenological impact of electroweak radiative corrections, higher-order calculations, and Z-pole line-shape analyses in precision tests.

questions.question: What field-level criterion should decide when electroweak precision fits should use universal propagator form factors, S-matrix line-shape parameters, or full pseudo-observable and realistic-observable calculations?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the differing model-independent strategies in the form-factor approach [1], the S-matrix Z-line-shape analysis [4], and the TOPAZ0/ZFITTER precision-calculation conventions [5].

questions.question: Which electroweak radiative corrections are indispensable before TeV-scale explanations of B anomalies can be considered viable against Z-pole and tau-decay constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finding that electroweak corrections modify W and Z leptonic couplings and generate purely leptonic effective interactions that challenge B-anomaly models [3].

node_4b6b2b9bb1ee.summary: These review articles introduce the electroweak Standard Model, summarize its experimental status, and survey motivations and phenomenology for physics beyond it.

questions.question: Which future precision Standard Model calculation or collider measurement would most sharply expose the Standard Model as an approximation rather than merely tightening agreement with existing data?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the excellent empirical status but acknowledged incompleteness of the Standard Model in [1].

questions.question: How should theory uncertainties from PDFs, multi-leg QCD/EW corrections, Monte Carlo generators, underlying events, and infrared subtraction be combined so that Higgs and standard-candle measurements can be used consistently as backgrounds to new physics?
questions.rationale: The ingredients are those emphasized in the Les Houches reports on PDFs, generators, Higgs production, standard candles, and precision calculations [2], [3], [4], and [5].

node_f918d255d4f3.summary: This cluster gathers broad pedagogical and phenomenological reviews of beyond-Standard-Model ideas, including LHC-motivated signatures, supersymmetry, and other extensions of electroweak theory.

questions.question: Which incompleteness of the Standard Model is most likely to become experimentally sharp at the precision frontier rather than through direct discovery of new resonances?
questions.rationale: The Standard Model review emphasizes excellent agreement with data but persistent reasons for incompleteness, while the precision-frontier review frames high-precision calculations as central to future tests [1,5].

questions.question: What level of control over PDFs, underlying event modeling, multi-leg QCD, NNLO corrections, and NLO electroweak effects is needed before LHC deviations can be credibly interpreted as BSM signals?
questions.rationale: The Les Houches reports identify PDFs, underlying events, Monte Carlo generators, and multi-leg NLO and NNLO calculations as essential for comparing LHC data with theory [2,3,4].

questions.question: Can broad BSM searches be organized around precision Standard Model standard candles in a way that reduces dependence on model-specific signatures?
questions.rationale: The 2005 Les Houches report treats W, Z, and ttbar production both as known-physics signals and as backgrounds to unknown physics [4].

node_5f9075631aac.summary: These papers review the Standard Model, electroweak constraints, and broad phenomenological motivations for new physics at colliders.
