questions.question: After the Higgs discovery and the precision success of renormalizable gauge theory, what empirical signature would most clearly show that the Standard Model is an approximation rather than a complete high-energy theory?
questions.rationale: The Standard Model review stresses its excellent agreement with data but also the reasons it is likely incomplete, while LHC lectures emphasize the post-Higgs status of the theory [1].

questions.question: Given that acceptable MSSM phenomenology occupies exceptional regions of MSSM-124 parameter space, what minimal collider or precision pattern would make supersymmetry more compelling than other electroweak-symmetry-breaking mechanisms?
questions.rationale: The MSSM review highlights the exceptional nature of viable MSSM-124 parameter regions and discusses Higgs, precision, and collider probes [3].

questions.question: Should future pp and e+e- programs be optimized primarily for discovering new particles or for stress-testing weak-interaction symmetry breaking through Higgs, QCD, and electroweak precision observables?
questions.rationale: The BSM lectures frame new physics around the mechanism of spontaneous weak-interaction symmetry breaking and future collider probes [5].

node_19c6b2a12909.summary: This cluster centers on Les Houches and LHC studies of Standard Model measurements, Higgs physics, and signatures of possible new physics.

questions.question: What benchmark set of Standard Model processes would most cleanly expose whether TeV-collider theory uncertainties are dominated by PDFs, missing higher orders, underlying events, or Monte Carlo modeling?
questions.rationale: The Les Houches reports repeatedly organize precision collider work around standard candles, PDFs, underlying events, Higgs production, and event-generator developments [1][3].

questions.question: Which Run-II-and-beyond measurements most directly test the consistency of multi-leg NLO, NNLO QCD, and NLO electroweak calculations across Higgs and electroweak final states?
questions.rationale: The 2013 report centered on multi-leg NLO/NNLO QCD and NLO electroweak cross sections compared with LHC Run 1 data and projected to Run 2 [2].

questions.question: Can the precision-frontier program converge on common subtraction, amplitude, and semi-numerical standards that make future BSM interpretations limited by data rather than by theory bookkeeping?
questions.rationale: The precision review emphasizes multi-loop amplitudes, numerical methods, and infrared subtraction schemes beyond NLO as enabling technologies for precision collider physics [4].

node_e5078aafdbe1.summary: These lecture-style works introduce quantum field theory, gauge invariance, QCD, electroweak symmetry breaking, and precision tests of the Standard Model.

questions.question: What low-energy neutral-current measurement would most decisively complement Z-pole determinations of the weak mixing angle in discriminating among broad classes of beyond-Standard-Model physics?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] emphasizes low-energy neutral-current precision measurements as competitive and complementary weak-mixing-angle determinations that reduce BSM parameter space.

questions.question: Where is the Standard Model foundation program most limited by theory rather than experiment: neutrino observables, electric dipole moments, weak decays, or muon physics?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] highlights these low-energy weak-interaction areas as complementary probes with important theoretical open issues.

questions.question: Which precision test most directly probes the gauge-invariant structure of the SU(3)c x SU(2)L x U(1)Y Lagrangian beyond confirming its established particle content and symmetries?
questions.rationale: Papers [2]-[4] frame gauge invariance, particle content, and phenomenological precision tests as the core foundations of the Standard Model.

node_681294b721c8.summary: These papers develop the physics case, precision opportunities, and technical challenges for future high-energy muon colliders.

questions.question: What machine-design milestone would make high-luminosity 10 TeV muon collisions credible enough to anchor the next energy-frontier program?
questions.rationale: This follows from the emphasis on 10 TeV design, high luminosity, short muon lifetime, emittance, and demanding technologies in [1] and [2].

questions.question: Can the same muon collider program truly merge energy reach and precision through point-like muon collisions and electroweak radiation, rather than forcing a tradeoff between discovery and measurement?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the claim that muon beams and their electroweak radiation cloud blur the energy-versus-precision divide for EWSB, dark matter, and naturalness studies in [3] and [5].

questions.question: What energy resolution, luminosity, and detector performance are required for s-channel Higgs production to directly determine Higgs masses, total widths, and partial widths?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposed s-channel muon-collider Higgs program and its machine requirements in [4] and [S1].

node_228e3ba664ab.summary: This cluster studies Little Higgs solutions to the hierarchy problem, their new TeV-scale states, electroweak constraints, and collider signals.

questions.question: What single pattern of electroweak precision, Higgs-coupling, and direct-search measurements would most cleanly distinguish collective symmetry breaking from a generic TeV-scale extension of the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: The broad issue comes from Little Higgs models protecting the Higgs mass through collective symmetry breaking while facing precision and Higgs-data constraints [2,S1].

questions.question: Is T-parity still the most viable organizing principle for Little Higgs phenomenology once one simultaneously requires low fine tuning, consistency with precision data, a stable weakly interacting particle, and observable collider signals?
questions.rationale: This derives from the use of T-parity to remove dangerous tree-level corrections, solve the little hierarchy problem, and provide a dark matter candidate [4,5].

questions.question: Which regions of Littlest Higgs and Simplest Little Higgs parameter space remain genuinely natural after combining heavy gauge boson, vector-like T quark, scalar triplet, Higgs-data, and electroweak precision limits?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the low-energy constraint analysis and collider signatures in the Littlest Higgs model [3] and the Snowmass comparison of exclusions across implementations [S1].

node_ab2be513c33b.summary: These works analyze Littlest Higgs models with T-parity, focusing on Higgs production, top partners, T-odd fermions, dark matter candidates, and collider phenomenology.

questions.question: Is T-parity still the minimal viable way for Little Higgs models to evade precision electroweak and Higgs constraints while keeping a natural electroweak scale?
questions.rationale: T-parity was introduced to remove the precision-data constraints that otherwise reintroduce fine tuning, and Snowmass fits compare these indirect limits with LHC direct searches [1,S1].

questions.question: Which region of f, Higgs mass, and T-odd spectrum simultaneously gives the correct heavy-photon relic abundance and avoids direct LHC exclusions of T-odd fermions or top partners?
questions.rationale: The dark matter analyses map relic-density and coannihilation regions, while phenomenology studies and Snowmass limits compare collider reach across the LHT parameter space [2,5,S1].

questions.question: Can linear UV extensions of the SU(5)/SO(5) littlest Higgs reproduce the same low-energy T-parity phenomenology without introducing new precision or flavor problems?
questions.rationale: Linear T-parity invariant constructions are proposed as possible UV extensions sharing similar low-energy phenomenology with CCWZ-based models [3].

node_1a96cd64c70b.summary: This cluster emphasizes LHC and linear-collider searches for Littlest Higgs with T-parity signatures, especially top partners and modified Higgs processes.

questions.question: After electroweak precision and Higgs coupling fits, is T-parity still sufficient to preserve Little Higgs naturalness without pushing the symmetry-breaking scale f beyond the reach of direct LHT searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from the original T-parity motivation in [1] and the Snowmass comparison of electroweak, Higgs, and direct-search exclusions in [S1].

questions.question: Which collider channel most directly tests the Little Higgs electroweak-symmetry-breaking mechanism: heavy singlet top production, T-odd gauge-boson signatures, or modified Higgs processes?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the LHT phenomenology in [2], the top-partner tests proposed in [4], and the direct-search outlook in [S1].

questions.question: Can heavy-photon lightest T-odd particle dark matter regions selected by relic abundance and coannihilation calculations be covered by future direct, indirect, and collider searches?
questions.rationale: This derives from the LHT dark-matter analyses in [2] and [5].

node_8daac723edb4.summary: These papers investigate production, decay, and detection prospects for the extra heavy gauge bosons predicted by Littlest Higgs models.

questions.question: Which production and decay measurements of heavy gauge bosons would most cleanly identify a Littlest Higgs origin rather than a generic TeV-scale W' or Z' signal?
questions.rationale: This follows from LHC studies proposing searches for Little Higgs heavy gauge bosons and testing the model through their production and decay properties [1],[2].

questions.question: How do uneaten pseudo-axions reshape Littlest Higgs search strategies for heavy quarks, heavy gauge bosons, and diphoton resonances?
questions.rationale: This derives from the observation that spontaneously broken U(1) subgroups can leave physical pseudoscalars that strongly affect heavy-quark phenomenology and collider signatures [3],[4].

questions.question: Can electroweak precision constraints and direct production consistently support a light heavy photon A_H, and what measurement would settle the viable parameter region?
questions.rationale: The heavy-photon study found that lighter A_H can suppress electroweak precision corrections and may be producible at a 500 GeV linear collider for f around 3 TeV [5].

node_527633715177.summary: This cluster covers the construction of Little Higgs theories, collective symmetry breaking, pseudo-Goldstone Higgs mechanisms, and precision electroweak constraints.

questions.question: Is collective symmetry breaking still a viable minimal paradigm for natural electroweak symmetry breaking when precision data prefer new physics above the TeV scale?
questions.rationale: This is the central tension between the natural pseudo-Goldstone Higgs construction in [1] and the precision-electroweak constraints reviewed in [2] and [5].

questions.question: Which ingredient, such as T-parity or modified gauge structure, most cleanly reconciles a light Little Higgs with precision constraints while preserving testable collider signatures?
questions.rationale: The model-dependent corrections and extensions in [3] and the T-parity solution to the little hierarchy problem in [4] motivate this question.

questions.question: What pattern of heavy gauge bosons, vector-like T quarks, scalar states, or stable T-parity particles would most decisively identify a Little Higgs theory rather than another 10 TeV completion?
questions.rationale: These characteristic states and their LHC relevance are described in [3], [4], and [5].

node_10ceae8f927a.summary: These papers study quark and lepton flavor-changing processes, CP violation, rare decays, and anomalous flavor signatures in Littlest Higgs models with T-parity.

questions.question: After the removal of logarithmic UV cutoff dependence in LHT Z-penguin amplitudes, which rare K and B observables remain the most robust probes of non-MFV mirror-fermion flavor structure?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1] and [4], which first exposed UV sensitivity and then updated FCNC predictions after the new Z-penguin contribution removed the cutoff dependence.

questions.question: Can LHT parameter space simultaneously accommodate epsilon_K, S_psiK, S_psiphi, Delta M_s, and rare K to pi nu nubar enhancements without requiring mirror-fermion degeneracy that erases observable effects?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], [4], and [5], which study meson mixing, CP asymmetries, epsilon_K tuning, and the degeneracy constraints on T-odd fermions.

questions.question: Do charged-lepton flavor-violating ratios in LHT provide a clean enough pattern to distinguish mirror-lepton effects from supersymmetric explanations if mu to e gamma, mu to eee, and mu-e conversion limits improve?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2], which finds lepton-flavor effects much larger than mirror-quark effects and emphasizes a clear distinction from supersymmetry.

node_55fddc3c2e91.summary: This cluster explores explanations of the muon anomalous magnetic moment in supersymmetry, two-Higgs-doublet models, and related beyond-Standard-Model scenarios.

questions.question: What correlated pattern across muon g-2, collider searches, flavor observables, and cosmology would make a supersymmetric loop explanation compelling rather than merely parameter-compatible?
questions.rationale: This follows from the MSSM tan beta enhanced contribution to a_mu [1] and the review of correlations with collider and cosmological observables [5].

questions.question: How robust are the preferred supersymmetric parameter ranges for a_mu once two-loop effects, CP phases, light smuon scenarios, and the absence of model-independent chargino bounds are combined in a global analysis?
questions.rationale: The question is based on the leading one- and two-loop supersymmetric contributions [5] and the finding that light smuons can satisfy E821 bounds without a model-independent chargino mass bound [4].

questions.question: Can a gauged L_mu-L_tau two-Higgs-doublet framework simultaneously accommodate muon g-2 and the same h to mu tau, B to K* mu+ mu-, and R(K) correlations without violating tau to 3 mu and B_s mixing constraints?
questions.rationale: This extends the simultaneous flavor-anomaly explanation in a two-Higgs-doublet model with gauged L_mu-L_tau under the stated flavor constraints [3].

node_d2027cb4edce.summary: These works examine two-Higgs-doublet model explanations of muon and electron g-2 anomalies, lepton flavor violation, and related electroweak tensions.

questions.question: What correlated pattern in h -> mu tau, B -> K(*) mu mu, R(K), tau -> 3mu, and B_s mixing would uniquely identify a gauged L_mu-L_tau two-Higgs-doublet explanation?
questions.rationale: A single 2HDM with gauged L_mu-L_tau is shown to correlate these anomalies while facing tau -> 3mu and B_s-mixing constraints in [1].

questions.question: Can a lepton-specific or perturbed type-X 2HDM still explain muon g-2 once vacuum stability, perturbativity, electroweak precision bounds, B physics, and direct scalar searches are imposed together?
questions.rationale: The relevant type-X parameter space and combined theoretical, collider, electroweak, and B-physics constraints are analyzed in [2] and [3].

questions.question: How light can a pseudoscalar Higgs remain while producing the needed Barr-Zee two-loop contribution to muon g-2 without conflicting with Higgs decay and lepton-flavor measurements?
questions.rationale: Large pseudoscalar Barr-Zee contributions to g-2 are computed in [5], and Higgs-decay implications of lepton-sector new physics are emphasized in [4].

node_f6edea755f9c.summary: These papers examine whether supersymmetric particles can explain the muon anomalous magnetic moment discrepancy across supergravity, MSSM, and dark matter compatible parameter spaces.

questions.question: After current muon g-2, dark-matter, and LHC constraints, what MSSM spectra still realize the tan beta times sign(mu) over M_SUSY squared enhancement without requiring tuned electroweak or slepton sectors?
questions.rationale: Supersymmetric g-2 contributions scale dominantly with tan beta sign(mu)/M_SUSY squared, and recent surveys combine g-2, dark matter, and LHC searches across MSSM parameter space [4], [5].

questions.question: Can model-independent supersymmetric explanations of a_mu be distinguished experimentally when light smuons are required but no universal lower bound exists on the lightest chargino mass?
questions.rationale: The E821-era supersymmetric analysis found that low tan beta can satisfy the one-sigma range with a light smuon but no model-independent chargino mass bound for tan beta at least 3 [3].

questions.question: Which correlated collider or cosmological observable is the most robust discriminator between MSSM loop explanations and other few-field new-physics explanations of the muon anomaly?
questions.rationale: The recent FNAL-motivated survey compares MSSM and simple models with up to three new fields using state-of-the-art predictions for a_mu, dark matter, and LHC searches [5].

node_8c7ba6bb331e.summary: This cluster focuses on detailed supersymmetric calculations of the muon magnetic dipole anomaly and the resulting constraints on MSSM masses, tan beta, and model parameters.

questions.question: After the FNAL muon g-2 result, what MSSM parameter regions can still deliver the required Delta a_mu through one- and two-loop dipole contributions while satisfying collider, dark-matter, and flavor constraints?
questions.rationale: This extends the MSSM tan beta and superparticle-loop dependence in [1] and [4] to the post-FNAL global-survey setting of [5].

questions.question: Can a model-independent lower or upper bound on smuon, chargino, or neutralino masses be derived once the dominant tan beta sign(mu)/M_SUSY^2 behavior is supplemented by realistic mixing and CP-phase dependence?
questions.rationale: The absence of a model-independent chargino bound in [3] and the qualitative tan beta sign(mu)/M_SUSY^2 behavior in [4] motivate this question.

questions.question: What level of hadronic Standard Model uncertainty reduction is needed before MSSM dipole calculations, rather than SM theory error, dominate the interpretation of the muon g-2 discrepancy?
questions.rationale: The scrutiny of QED, hadronic, and electroweak uncertainties in [2] motivates asking when supersymmetric prediction uncertainties become the limiting factor.

node_9cd868617b39.summary: These works connect the Fermilab and Brookhaven muon g-2 anomaly to electroweak supersymmetry, neutralino dark matter, and LHC searches for sleptons and electroweakinos.

questions.question: Which electroweakino-slepton spectra still explain muon g-2 after LHC slepton searches, especially in the chargino-dominated region with m_smuon_L greater than or comparable to m_chargino?
questions.rationale: The recent MSSM interpretation finds broad exclusions but leaves chargino-dominated parameter space open when the left smuon is not lighter than the chargino [3].

questions.question: Can the MSSM simultaneously explain electron and muon g-2 with opposite-sign deviations without producing excluded flavor violation or visible non-colored SUSY signals?
questions.rationale: The simultaneous explanation requires different bino-slepton and chargino-sneutrino contributions across lepton sectors and relies on light selectrons and degenerate spectra [4].

node_5dfb821b4a74.summary: This broad cluster covers lattice and continuum studies of non-Abelian gauge theories, including supersymmetric Yang-Mills, QCD topology, confinement, propagators, and conformal behavior.

questions.question: What single nonperturbative benchmark would best test whether lattice chiral fermion formulations preserve continuum chiral and anomaly physics without fine tuning?
questions.rationale: Overlap-like massless lattice quarks and domain-wall/topological-defect chiral fermions were proposed specifically to avoid doublers, fine tuning, and to expose anomalies on finite lattices [1], [3].

questions.question: Can lattice QCD, instanton phenomenology, and Dyson-Schwinger truncations be made mutually consistent on the role of topological configurations in chiral symmetry breaking and confinement?
questions.rationale: The instanton review connects instantons to the light-hadron spectrum and chiral transition, while the Green's-function review discusses confinement, positivity violation, and instanton effects in DSE approaches [2], [5].

questions.question: How can generalized symmetry and anomaly constraints be incorporated into lattice and functional-renormalization approaches to non-Abelian gauge dynamics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the exact renormalization-group program for nonperturbative effective actions and by the Snowmass framing of generalized symmetries and anomalies as constraints on QFT dynamics [4], [S1].

node_dcfe862bbb71.summary: These papers study functional and exact renormalization group methods, high-loop beta functions, gradient flow, and lattice evidence for conformal windows in gauge theories.

questions.question: How can functional renormalization-group truncations be systematically optimized so that symmetry identities, composite operators, and Dyson-Schwinger constraints remain consistent along the flow?
questions.rationale: The FRG structural review derives flows for correlation functions, lifted symmetry relations, composite operators, optimization criteria, and links to Dyson-Schwinger equations [4].

questions.question: What is the minimal nonperturbative approximation to the exact RG effective action that reproduces universal critical equations of state while controlling irrelevant-operator corrections?
questions.rationale: Exact-RG work emphasizes effective-average-action approximations for universal critical behavior and Polchinski-flow approximations based on irrelevancy expansions [1], [5].

questions.question: Can high-loop beta functions, anomalous-dimension matrices, and scheme-cancellation methods be made interoperable with continuum nonperturbative tools for strongly coupled conformal gauge theories?
questions.rationale: The four-loop QCD beta function and weak-Hamiltonian RG lectures highlight scheme dependence, operator mixing, anomalous dimensions, and cancellations in physical amplitudes [2], [3].

node_66563aa2d8e5.summary: This cluster centers on perturbative and nonperturbative renormalization of scalar field theories and sigma models, especially critical exponents, effective potentials, and resummation methods.

questions.question: Can nonperturbative renormalization-group, optimized perturbation theory, and Hamiltonian truncation be benchmarked against the same O(N) scalar critical equation of state to determine where each method gives controlled real-time or finite-temperature predictions?
questions.rationale: This connects the effective-average-action treatment of O(N) critical behavior in [1] and [3], the finite-temperature OPT construction in [5], and the nonperturbative real-time motivation of [S1].

questions.question: What single set of universal quantities should define the precision target for scalar critical phenomena: critical exponents from epsilon expansions, the full critical equation of state, or finite-temperature spectral functions near a chiral transition?
questions.rationale: The alternatives are represented by five-loop epsilon-expansion exponents in [4], universal equations of state in [1], and thermal spectral functions in [5].

questions.question: Can worldline or Bern-Kosower one-loop effective-action methods be integrated with nonperturbative scalar RG flows to preserve explicit gauge invariance while improving resummations of scalar theories coupled to background gauge fields?
questions.rationale: This follows from the explicitly gauge-invariant one-dimensional path-integral effective action in [2] and the nonperturbative RG framework of [1].

node_d6e5e0c8be0a.summary: These works address thermal quantum field theory using 2PI methods, Dyson resummation, renormalization group improvement, and symmetry behavior at high temperature.

questions.question: Which resummation framework gives the most reliable finite-temperature spectral functions near chiral restoration: optimized perturbation theory, screened perturbation theory, or self-consistent nPI effective actions?
questions.rationale: The comparison is motivated by OPT predictions for scalar and pseudoscalar threshold enhancement in [2], screened-loop convergence improvements in [4], and self-consistently dressed nPI expansions in [5].

questions.question: Can finite-temperature resummation schemes be constructed that simultaneously preserve renormalizability, Nambu-Goldstone constraints, and gauge-invariant organization of off-shell effective actions?
questions.rationale: This combines the renormalization and Nambu-Goldstone theorem proof for finite-temperature OPT in [2] with the explicitly gauge-invariant one-loop worldline effective-action organization in [1].

questions.question: What is the minimal nPI truncation needed to reproduce Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal-enhanced transport or kinetic-theory limits without losing self-consistent completeness at finite temperature or out of equilibrium?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [5], which gives the nPI equivalence hierarchy and notes that the three-loop effective action already captures leading on-shell LPM-enhanced results.

node_acfebebdc9f6.summary: This cluster studies whether symmetries can remain broken or become inversely broken at high temperature, using scalar models, resummation, and nonperturbative approximations.

questions.question: Which resummation prescription for finite-temperature scalar theories gives regulator- and scheme-stable predictions for symmetry nonrestoration or inverse symmetry breaking at strong coupling?
questions.rationale: Papers [1], [2], [3], and [5] all address reorganized finite-temperature perturbation theory because naive weak-coupling expansions fail.

questions.question: Can optimized perturbation theory maintain both renormalizability and the Nambu-Goldstone theorem in multi-scalar models where competing order parameters drive high-temperature nonrestoration?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] proves systematic renormalization and the Nambu-Goldstone theorem in finite-temperature OPT for O(N) phi^4 theory.

questions.question: What observable thermal spectral-function signature would distinguish genuine symmetry nonrestoration from slow convergence of screened perturbative approximations?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] identifies threshold enhancement in scalar and pseudoscalar spectral functions as a signal of the chiral transition, while [2] and [5] emphasize improved convergence of screened perturbation theory.

node_52c0a7280e9f.summary: These papers develop renormalization frameworks for self-consistent 2PI, nPI, and Phi-derivable approximations in scalar and gauge quantum field theories.

questions.question: Can the local vacuum counterterm construction for Phi-derivable 2PI approximations be extended systematically to self-consistently complete nPI gauge-theory truncations at O(g^6)?
questions.rationale: Local vacuum renormalization of finite-temperature Phi-derivable schemes is proven in [2], while [1] constructs self-consistently complete nPI gauge-theory approximations through four loops or O(g^6).

questions.question: How can Ward-Takahashi identities be restored or consistently imposed on renormalized self-consistent approximations without losing exact conservation laws and thermodynamic consistency?
questions.rationale: The global-symmetry analysis in [5] shows that Phi-derivable solutions conserve Noether currents but generally do not satisfy Ward-Takahashi identities.

questions.question: Do 2PI-resummed proper vertices renormalized by derivatives of Gamma[phi] give numerically stable finite-temperature results beyond the sunset approximation?
questions.rationale: The complete renormalization of n-point functions from the 2PI-resummed effective action is developed in [3], and the sunset application is studied numerically in [4].

node_6fce09da4d0b.summary: This cluster concerns derivative and heat-kernel expansions of one-loop effective actions, especially finite-temperature gauge theories, Polyakov loops, and string-inspired worldline methods.

questions.question: What observable calculation would settle whether worldline, Bern-Kosower, and covariant heat-kernel methods give the most efficient gauge-invariant organization of one-loop effective actions?
questions.rationale: Worldline rules produce compact off-shell gauge-invariant one-loop effective actions [1], and their form factors were explicitly compared with heat-kernel results in [2].

questions.question: Can derivative expansions exact in the field strength be extended beyond QED to non-Abelian backgrounds while preserving a minimal invariant basis at high derivative order?
questions.rationale: QED derivative expansions exact in F_mu nu were derived in [4], while computerized non-Abelian worldline calculations produced a sixth-order inverse-mass expansion in a minimal invariant basis [5].

questions.question: How far can higher-dimensional functional determinant methods based on Gel'fand-Yaglom ideas be pushed for nontrivial quantum-field-theory backgrounds where spectral methods are impractical?
questions.rationale: Progress in extending Gel'fand-Yaglom determinant techniques from one-dimensional problems to higher-dimensional differential operators is reviewed in [3].

node_26faa6676a5e.summary: These papers use Monte Carlo simulations, finite-size scaling, and renormalization group methods to test asymptotic freedom, mass gaps, and universality in two-dimensional O(N) sigma models.

questions.question: What finite-size-scaling observable would most cleanly settle whether the two-dimensional O(3) sigma model reaches perturbative asymptotic scaling only at enormous correlation length or exhibits a genuine nonperturbative deviation?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the Monte Carlo result that deviations from asymptotic scaling shrink from about 25 percent at xi around 100 to about 4 percent at xi around 100000 [2].

questions.question: Can functional RG derivative expansions capture both the Kosterlitz-Thouless behavior of the O(2) linear sigma model and the mass-gap physics of O(N greater than 2) models within one controlled universality framework?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the nonperturbative flow-equation treatment that avoids infrared divergences and gives a good picture of the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition for N=2 [1].

questions.question: How do renormalon growth, inverse-log singularities at the mass gap, and double-scaling behavior in large-N principal chiral and unitary matrix models constrain the universality claims drawn from finite-N simulations?
questions.rationale: This follows from exact large-N principal chiral field results showing factorial perturbative growth and mass-gap singularities, together with large-N unitary-matrix double-scaling analyses [3][5].

node_26faa6676a5e_1.summary: This cluster focuses on high-precision lattice tests of the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model, including continuum scaling, form-factor predictions, and relations to discrete spin models.

questions.question: What precision observable would finally distinguish true O(a^2 log^3 a) Symanzik lattice artifacts from apparent linear cutoff effects in the two-dimensional O(3) nonlinear sigma model?
questions.rationale: This follows from [4], which explains the apparent O(a) artifacts as large logarithmic corrections to O(a^2) Symanzik terms and compares with Monte Carlo data.

questions.question: At what correlation length and statistical precision should asymptotic scaling of the two-dimensional O(3) sigma model become quantitatively indistinguishable from renormalization-group predictions?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by [2], which finds deviations falling from about 25 percent at xi around 10^2 to about 4 percent at xi around 10^5.

questions.question: Can nonperturbative flow-equation methods that capture the O(2) Kosterlitz-Thouless transition be extended to clarify the scaling and infrared behavior of O(3) models?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], which uses an exact nonperturbative evolution equation and derivative expansion to treat infrared divergences and the O(2) Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.

node_1f5152e225d0.summary: These papers use large-N and bootstrap methods to solve sigma, Gross-Neveu, CP(N), and principal chiral models, emphasizing phases, correlators, and asymptotic freedom.

questions.question: What physical criterion distinguishes extended-object spectra from point-particle spectra in the N=infinity principal chiral field near the mass-gap singularity?
questions.rationale: The exact large-N principal chiral field solution finds an inverse logarithmic singularity in the ground-state energy suggesting extended objects rather than pointlike particles [1].

questions.question: Can renormalon factorial growth in the large-N principal chiral field be connected quantitatively to double-scaling behavior in unitary matrix or chiral-chain models?
questions.rationale: The principal chiral solution exhibits factorially growing perturbative coefficients, while large-N unitary matrix models emphasize double-scaling properties [1], [2].

questions.question: In large-N effective field theories with infinitely many coupling types, what low-momentum observables remain predictive rather than adjustable by counterterms?
questions.rationale: The large-N EFT analysis finds exact nontrivial solutions but notes that infinitely many free parameters limit quantitative predictions except at small momenta [4].

node_a3593ee604e6.summary: This cluster studies scalar phi-four and O(N) theories with lattice, series, Monte Carlo, and Hamiltonian truncation methods to determine critical behavior, spectra, and triviality.

questions.question: What single benchmark in low-dimensional phi4 theory would convince the community that Hamiltonian truncation can deliver continuum, real-time, strongly coupled QFT results with controlled errors?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Snowmass framing of Hamiltonian truncation as a continuum nonperturbative method and from phi4 studies using analytic renormalization to control cutoff dependence [S1], [3].

questions.question: Can TCSA or Fock-space Hamiltonian truncation reproduce both sides of the two-dimensional phi4 phase transition, including the Z2-broken phase and Chang duality, with lattice-level precision?
questions.rationale: This derives from TCSA in general dimensions and the two-part Hamiltonian-truncation study of 2D phi4 theory including the broken phase and Chang duality [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: How can nonperturbative methods determine whether the Higgs amplitude mode remains a sharp resonance or becomes overdamped near the two-dimensional superfluid-Mott transition?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the experimental and theoretical debate over the Higgs amplitude mode in low-dimensional systems near the superfluid-Mott transition [1].

node_b02971216194.summary: These works compute critical couplings, scaling corrections, and spectra of low-dimensional phi-four and related O(N) models using Monte Carlo and Hamiltonian truncation.

questions.question: Is Hamiltonian truncation now accurate enough to replace lattice methods for selected strongly coupled scalar QFT observables, or is its role limited to spectra and real-time quantities inaccessible to Euclidean simulations?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the Snowmass claim that Hamiltonian truncation enables nonperturbative continuum real-time computations in strongly coupled QFTs [S1].

questions.question: How should zero modes and cutoff-dependent counterterms be treated so that Fock-space Hamiltonian truncation gives controlled critical couplings and spectra on both sides of the two-dimensional phi-four transition?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Hamiltonian truncation studies of the symmetric phase, critical point, broken phase, and zero-mode treatment in two-dimensional phi-four theory [3,5].

questions.question: Can amplitude-mode resonance properties near the two-dimensional superfluid-Mott transition be predicted quantitatively from continuum phi-four or O(N) computations rather than inferred phenomenologically?
questions.rationale: This follows from the experimental and theoretical debate over whether the low-dimensional Higgs amplitude mode is a resonance or overdamped excitation [1].

node_0dc36da5087a.summary: This cluster debates four-dimensional phi-four triviality in the broken phase, focusing on lattice evidence for condensate rescaling, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and Higgs mass implications.

questions.question: What lattice observable would decisively settle whether four-dimensional broken-phase lambda phi-four theory has only conventional triviality or also a nonperturbative condensate rescaling that changes Higgs-mass implications?
questions.rationale: The nontrivial-effective-potential lattice test argues that trivial shifted fields can coexist with spontaneous symmetry breaking and predicts a heavy Higgs from nonperturbative renormalization [2].

questions.question: Can high-precision broken-phase scaling analyses with standard and Symanzik-improved actions distinguish perturbative finite-volume effects from genuine nonperturbative states near the critical point?
questions.rationale: O(4) phi-four simulations find one-loop finite-volume behavior near kappa_c, while lower-dimensional studies identify nonperturbative spectral states affecting universal ratios [3], [4].

node_08085185bdcf.summary: These papers determine critical exponents and beta functions in phi-four, phi-three, Gross-Neveu, and O(N) universality classes using high-loop, large-N, and nonperturbative renormalization group methods.

questions.question: What cross-check between nonperturbative effective-average-action flows and six-loop epsilon-expansion resummations would most cleanly identify the residual systematic error in three-dimensional O(N) critical exponents?
questions.rationale: This follows from the agreement of exact-flow estimates with precision results in [2] and the high-loop minimal-subtraction/resummation program in [3,4].

questions.question: Can the proposed cubic scalar theory in 6-epsilon dimensions be connected quantitatively to the Wilson-Fisher O(N) fixed point across dimensions without losing unitarity outside the very-large-N regime?
questions.rationale: The issue is grounded in [5], where the cubic sigma phi phi plus sigma^3 theory has a real IR-stable fixed point only for N greater than 1038 at one loop.

node_4e47f039b49e.summary: This cluster focuses on precision estimates of O(N) critical exponents and fixed points using perturbative, nonperturbative, Wilsonian, and large-N renormalization group approaches.

questions.question: Can nonperturbative effective-average-action truncations be systematically benchmarked against six-loop resummation and large-N results for O(N) critical exponents across N and dimension?
questions.rationale: This follows from the exact RG effective-average-action program and perturbative six-loop estimates for O(n) models [1],[2],[4].

questions.question: What is the true critical value of N for real-coupling fixed points in the cubic O(N) model as d is continued from 6-epsilon toward five dimensions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the one-loop and three-loop studies of cubic sigma phi phi plus sigma^3 theories and their reduced critical N estimates [3],[5].

questions.question: Which universal parts of the O(N) critical equation of state are stable under improvements of nonperturbative RG truncations in two, three, and four dimensions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nonperturbative RG review claiming a unified description of O(N) models and universal critical equations of state across dimensions [1].

node_c34fe116d860.summary: These works compute and resum multi-loop renormalization group functions for phi-four, phi-three, and Gross-Neveu-type theories to extract critical exponents and beta-function behavior.

questions.question: Which independent recalculations or consistency checks are needed before high-loop phi^4 beta functions and anomalous dimensions can be treated as precision inputs for critical exponents?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] was motivated by discovered errors in published five-loop O(n) phi^4 diagrams and performs a full analytic reevaluation.

questions.question: How should resummation methods combine exact six-loop O(n) phi^4 data, estimates of higher-loop primitive diagrams, and known large-order asymptotics to minimize uncertainty in two and three dimensions?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] computes six-loop minimal-subtraction RG functions, estimates diagrams up to 11 loops, compares with asymptotic behavior, and resums critical exponents.

questions.question: Can nonperturbative RG calculations of full momentum-dependent n-point functions be quantitatively matched to high-loop perturbative RG results across both scaling and perturbative regimes?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] develops an approximation scheme for momentum-dependent n-point functions and tests it in both perturbative and scaling regimes of the O(N) model.

node_a44582dc17bc.summary: This cluster develops renormalization group improvement techniques for effective potentials, especially in scalar and Yukawa theories with multiple fields or mass scales.

questions.question: What is the most reliable RG-improvement prescription for an effective potential with several field-dependent masses when no single renormalization scale suppresses all logarithms?
questions.rationale: The multimass-scale studies generalize RGE improvement, use decoupling at mu_i=Mi(phi_c), and propose mu*=min_i Mi(phi_c) as the scale with the best loop behavior [3,4].

questions.question: Can gauge-invariant vacuum energies and physical quantities be extracted from perturbative effective potentials without summing uncontrolled infinite loop classes in gauge theories?
questions.rationale: The scalar-QED analysis shows that effective potentials are gauge dependent and that an infinite class of loops must be summed to obtain a gauge-invariant value at the minimum [2].

questions.question: Do multiscale subtraction schemes with partial RG equations produce stable vacuum conclusions beyond the O(N) phi4 two-scale example?
questions.rationale: The multiscale subtraction work introduces one scale per generic mass scale and finds, in its two-scale O(N) phi4 application, indications of no stable vacuum [5].

node_ef9c55c31497.summary: These papers review and apply exact and functional renormalization group flows to strongly coupled field theories, critical phenomena, gradient flow, and optimized regulator choices.

questions.question: What regulator-optimization criterion best predicts convergence of truncated FRG flows across derivative expansions, finite temperature, and bosonic or fermionic systems?
questions.rationale: Functional optimization criteria and optimized finite-temperature flows are explicit themes of the FRG structural and optimized-flow papers [1], [3].

questions.question: How can symmetry identities, gauge symmetry, and composite-operator or NPI relations be preserved and quantitatively monitored inside practical truncated FRG calculations?
questions.rationale: The FRG structural analysis derives flows for symmetry relations and composite operators, while the gauge-theory lectures focus on flow equations and gauge symmetries [1], [5].

questions.question: Can combined FRG and Dyson-Schwinger equations define renormalization schemes with controlled truncation errors for strongly coupled gauge theories and critical phenomena?
questions.rationale: The combined use of functional flows and Dyson-Schwinger equations is proposed as a practical route to nonperturbative schemes and applications [1], [4].

node_da3d0195e926.summary: This cluster compares alternative treatments of ultraviolet divergences, including dimensional, loop, lattice, gradient-flow, and infinity-free regularization and renormalization methods.

questions.question: Is there a regulator-independent benchmark set of composite operators and running couplings for which Schrödinger-functional, dimensional, and gradient-flow schemes can be compared beyond formal equivalence at the level of numerical precision?
questions.rationale: This broad comparison is grounded in the Schrödinger functional as a renormalizable coupling probe in [1], the scheme comparisons in [4], and the regularization-independent positive-flow-time products in [3].

questions.question: Can the small-flow-time expansion of Yang-Mills gradient-flow observables provide a systematically improvable lattice definition of the conserved energy-momentum tensor with controlled fermionic and continuum-limit uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the construction of the Yang-Mills energy-momentum tensor in [3] and its generalization to vector-like gauge theories with fermions in [5].

questions.question: Which conceptual criteria should decide when different ultraviolet and infrared regularization schemes are physically interchangeable rather than merely calculationally convenient?
questions.rationale: This framing question reflects the foundational perspective on quantum field theory in [2], the explicit scheme comparisons in [4], and the broader formal-QFT overview in [S1].

node_7ee61281f4de.summary: These works develop exact and functional renormalization group equations, derivative expansions, optimized flows, and structural formulations for nonperturbative quantum and statistical field theory.

questions.question: What benchmark result would establish that optimized exact RG flows converge systematically enough to replace less controlled truncations in nonperturbative field theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the optimized-flow program, which argues that suitable regulator choices improve convergence of approximate ERG solutions [3].

questions.question: Can symmetry identities, composite-operator flows, and Dyson-Schwinger equations be combined into a practical renormalization scheme whose truncation errors are quantitatively controlled?
questions.rationale: This derives from the structural FRG work on lifting symmetry relations to regularized theories and combining functional flows with quantum equations of motion [1].

questions.question: Which approximation strategy, derivative expansion, sharp-cutoff irrelevancy expansion, or optimized flow, gives the most reliable nonperturbative observables in simple scalar test theories?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in Polchinski-flow approximate solutions and the later comparison of optimized flows with generic flows through derivative expansion [2], [3].

node_801f036d2cd7.summary: This cluster studies gradient flow in gauge theories as a perturbative and nonperturbative tool for renormalized observables, step scaling, lattice improvement, and composite operators.

questions.question: Can the all-order finiteness of positive-flow-time gauge-field correlators be extended into practical renormalized composite-operator schemes that include flowed quark fields and controlled chiral-limit observables?
questions.rationale: This follows from the all-loop finiteness of gradient-flow gauge correlators and the extension to quark fields for nonperturbative renormalization and chiral observables [1,2].

questions.question: What is the minimal Symanzik counterterm structure needed to remove O(a^2) boundary and flow-discretization artifacts for realistic lattice gauge observables beyond tree level?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the 4+1-dimensional Symanzik improvement program and tree-level improvement of the flow, gauge action, and E(t) observable [4,5].

questions.question: Can gradient-flow step-scaling and scale-setting observables be designed so that arbitrary lattice discretizations are tree-level improved without biasing continuum extrapolations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed future lattice-QCD applications and the perturbative correction factors for improving arbitrary flow discretizations [3,5].

node_b4e1c500ab4a.summary: These papers use lattice and perturbative methods to map conformal windows and infrared fixed points in non-Abelian gauge theories with varied fermion flavors and representations.

questions.question: What lattice observable and continuum-extrapolation standard would settle whether SU(3) with N_f=8 is confining and chirally broken while N_f>=12 is infrared conformal?
questions.rationale: This follows from the lattice evidence placing SU(3) fundamental fermions with 12<=N_f<=16 inside the conformal window and N_f<=8 outside it [5].

questions.question: Can gradient-flow step scaling with separated flow-time and volume changes become a controlled benchmark for locating IR fixed points across colors, flavors, and fermion representations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed gradient-flow step-scaling strategy and the phase-diagram study of SU(N) theories with higher-representation fermions [1] and [3].

node_1736c42ff102.summary: This cluster focuses on SU(3) gauge theories with many fundamental fermions, testing whether specific flavor numbers lie inside, below, or near the conformal window.

questions.question: What lattice observable would most decisively locate the lower edge N_f^c of the SU(3) fundamental conformal window between N_f=8 and N_f=12?
questions.rationale: This reflects the open boundary identified in [5], where N_f=12 appears infrared conformal while N_f=8 shows confinement and chiral symmetry breaking.

questions.question: Can walking behavior below the conformal window be quantitatively described as RG flow near complex fixed points rather than as slow running near a real infrared fixed point?
questions.rationale: This follows from [4], which interprets walking gauge theories through complex CFTs and approximate scale invariance.

questions.question: How do higher-dimensional fermion representations shift the conformal window relative to many-flavor fundamental SU(3) theories relevant for dynamical electroweak breaking?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which shows that higher-representation matter can require fewer flavors to reach near-conformal dynamics.

node_05e791e51b5f.summary: These works compare analytic and lattice determinations of conformal windows across QCD-like, supersymmetric, SO, Sp, and beyond-asymptotic-freedom gauge theories.

questions.question: What single lattice observable or scaling test would most decisively locate the lower edge N_f^c of the SU(3) fundamental conformal window between N_f = 8 and N_f = 12?
questions.rationale: [3] and [4] find confinement for N_f <= 8 and infrared conformality at N_f = 12, while [5] suggests the onset may be below 12.

questions.question: How do higher-dimensional fermion representations shift the conformal window relative to fundamental fermions, and can lattice spectra confirm the analytic screening arguments?
questions.rationale: [1] predicts that higher-representation matter reaches near-conformality with fewer flavors because it screens more strongly.

questions.question: Can conformal-symmetry methods used in short-distance QCD calculations be connected quantitatively to nonperturbative lattice signals of infrared conformality?
questions.rationale: [2] reviews practical uses of conformal symmetry in QCD, while [3]-[5] identify lattice signatures of infrared fixed points and Coulomb-like phases.

node_4f28594f9c32.summary: This cluster studies near-conformal SU(3) theories relevant to composite Higgs models, emphasizing walking behavior, chiral symmetry breaking, and light dilaton-like scalar states.

questions.question: Can lattice hyperscaling of masses, decay constants, the chiral condensate, and Dirac eigenvalue density distinguish an IRFP-deformed conformal SU(3) theory from a confining walking theory with heavy fermions?
questions.rationale: The hyperscaling analysis gives RG scaling laws intended to separate mass-deformed conformal theories from confining heavy-fermion theories [3].

questions.question: In eight-flavor QCD, what continuum-controlled measurements can establish whether the light flavor-singlet scalar is a technidilaton tied to approximate scale symmetry rather than an ordinary scalar meson?
questions.rationale: The lattice observation of a scalar as light as the pion is interpreted as a possible technidilaton in a walking theory [4].

questions.question: Do complex-CFT fixed-point pairs provide quantitatively testable predictions for walking observables in SU(3) composite dynamics, or mainly a unifying RG interpretation of near-conformal behavior?
questions.rationale: The complex-CFT framework explains walking as RG flow between complex fixed points and proposes computing walking observables by perturbing those complex CFTs [1].

node_04c926265c0b.summary: These papers investigate SU(2) lattice gauge theories with adjoint or fundamental fermions, measuring running couplings, spectra, and mass anomalous dimensions near infrared conformality.

questions.question: What lattice observable would most decisively establish whether SU(2) gauge theory with two adjoint fermions is infrared conformal rather than merely near-conformal over accessible volumes?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the observed infrared fixed point in the Schrodinger-functional coupling study [5] and the near-conformal spectrum considerations in [2].

questions.question: How do first-order bulk transitions and the locus of minimum meson mass in the bare coupling-quark mass plane affect continuum extrapolations of the SU(2) adjoint beta function?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the detailed phase diagram with a first-order transition line and crossover locus in [4] and the continuum beta-function measurement in [5].

questions.question: Can spectral-function sum rules and lattice spectroscopy jointly determine whether reduced vector-axial mass splitting leads to a small or negative electroweak S parameter in near-conformal SU(2) theories?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the continuum contribution to spectral sum rules and possible small or negative S parameter in [2], together with lattice spectroscopy baselines in [1].

node_890409ebe6a9.summary: This cluster uses gradient-flow and step-scaling schemes to determine nonperturbative beta functions and fixed points in SU(3), SU(2), and sextet-fermion lattice gauge theories.

questions.question: Can the two-step gradient-flow step-scaling strategy separate continuum-extrapolation systematics from genuine near-fixed-point behavior in SU(3) sextet and other conformal-window candidates?
questions.rationale: This follows from the systematic finite-size strategy of [1] and the ambiguous zero of the discrete beta function in sextet SU(3) reported in [4].

questions.question: How should flow scales such as t0 and w0 be cross-calibrated with traditional scales like r0 so that beta-function studies and continuum scale setting share a common systematic-error budget?
questions.rationale: This combines the Wilson-flow scale-setting results of [2] and [3] with the high-statistics Sommer-scale determination in [5].

node_9233d47bbff8.summary: These works analyze ultraviolet fixed points and asymptotic safety in four-dimensional gauge-Yukawa and supersymmetric theories, emphasizing the role of gauge, scalar, and Yukawa interactions.

questions.question: Is the perturbatively controlled Veneziano-limit ultraviolet fixed point in four-dimensional gauge-Yukawa theories stable enough beyond large N to define a realistic asymptotically safe paradigm?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from [1], which establishes fully interacting perturbative UV fixed points in the Veneziano limit and discusses extensions beyond it.

questions.question: What field-content and low-energy spectrum constraints analogous to c-theorem inequalities can rule in or rule out strongly coupled asymptotically safe completions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [2], which proposes an inequality limiting infrared degrees of freedom relative to ultraviolet ones in strongly coupled field theories.

questions.question: Can vacuum stability, separatrix structure, and Coleman-Weinberg effective potentials provide a decisive phenomenological discriminator between asymptotically safe gauge-Yukawa theories and ordinary asymptotically free theories?
questions.rationale: This derives from [4], which analyzes running couplings, crossover scales, separatrices, and vacuum stability in asymptotically safe gauge-Yukawa theories.

node_9541e0f9e3ea.summary: This mixed cluster spans conformal bootstrap constraints on CFT data and high-order perturbative calculations of anomalous dimensions in QCD, effective theories, and supersymmetric gauge theories.

questions.question: Can extremal numerical bootstrap solutions for mixed correlators be systematically translated into precision CFT data, including operator decoupling patterns, beyond the 3D Ising universality class?
questions.rationale: The c-minimization and mixed-correlator bootstrap papers reconstruct Ising operator dimensions and OPE coefficients and observe sharp spectral transitions and decoupling near the Ising point [3][4].

questions.question: Is there a unified way to track scheme dependence, evanescent operators, and gamma5 prescriptions in high-order anomalous-dimension matrices so that physical amplitudes remain manifestly scheme independent?
questions.rationale: The weak-Hamiltonian lectures and two-loop Delta S=1 calculation emphasize anomalous-dimension matrices, evanescent operators, gamma5 schemes, and cancellation of scheme dependence in physical amplitudes [1][5].

node_652df9c30e89.summary: These papers compute anomalous dimension matrices for twist-two, weak-decay, effective-field-theory, and supersymmetric operators using multi-loop perturbative and conformal methods.

questions.question: What convention-independent benchmark calculation would settle discrepancies among NDR, HV, and RI anomalous-dimension matrices for Delta F=1 and Delta F=2 four-quark operators?
questions.rationale: This follows from the explicit NDR/HV two-loop Delta S=1 calculations in [2] and the NDR-MSbar versus RI Delta F=2 discrepancy discussed in [3].

questions.question: How can gamma5 and evanescent-operator choices be specified so Wilson coefficients, finite terms, and physical amplitudes exhibit scheme cancellation transparently?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the discussion of gamma5, evanescent operators, and scheme-scale cancellation in [1] and the finite NDR-to-HV terms in [4].

questions.question: Can the large low-energy effective theory anomalous-dimension system below the electroweak scale be organized into a practical phenomenology basis without equation-of-motion ambiguities?
questions.rationale: This derives from the LEFT calculation with thousands of dimension-five and dimension-six operators and noted equation-of-motion ambiguities in [5].

node_b07851fe4684.summary: This cluster centers on anomalous dimensions and renormalization of higher-dimensional operators in weak Hamiltonians and effective field theories, including evanescent-operator and on-shell amplitude methods.

questions.question: Can one construct a scheme-independent workflow in which gamma5 prescriptions and evanescent-operator choices cancel transparently between Wilson coefficients and two-loop anomalous-dimension matrices?
questions.rationale: This directly targets the scheme, scale, gamma5, and evanescent-operator issues reviewed in [1] and computed in [2] and [4].

questions.question: How can the discrepancies among NDR-MSbar, RI, and extracted Delta F=2 anomalous dimensions for four-quark operators be resolved in a basis-independent way?
questions.rationale: The need for such a resolution is highlighted by the Delta F=2 comparison and re-extraction from Delta F=1 operators in [3].

questions.question: In the low-energy EFT below the electroweak scale, can equation-of-motion ambiguities and double insertions of dimension-five operators be organized into invariant anomalous-dimension maps for the full dimension-six basis?
questions.rationale: This follows from the large LEFT anomalous-dimension calculation and its stated EOM ambiguity in [5].

node_91694d2d4c2a.summary: These works calculate high-loop anomalous dimensions of twist-two Wilson operators in QCD and planar or supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, often reconstructing spin-dependent results.

questions.question: Can universal shifted-argument structures found in N = 4 SYM twist-two anomalous dimensions be used to constrain or reconstruct higher-loop QCD spin-dependent anomalous dimensions?
questions.rationale: The N = 4 SYM two-loop anomalous-dimension matrix has eigenvalues expressed through a universal shifted function, while QCD twist-two calculations reconstruct spin-dependent moments at high loop order [1][2][4].

questions.question: How do non-zeta knot-valued counterterms at large N enter all-spin anomalous dimensions, and can their appearance be predicted before explicit high-loop calculation?
questions.rationale: Large-N analyses find irreducible double sums associated with positive knots in anomalous dimensions beyond triangle and uniqueness relations [3].

questions.question: Can off-shell operator-matrix-element methods for three-loop nonsinglet and transversity splitting functions be generalized without gauge artifacts obscuring higher-loop physical anomalous dimensions?
questions.rationale: Three-loop nonsinglet and transversity anomalous dimensions were computed in a gauge-dependent off-shell operator-matrix-element framework [4].

node_6ab995828886.summary: This cluster develops and applies conformal bootstrap techniques to constrain operator dimensions, OPE coefficients, and critical exponents in fermionic, Ising, O(N), and related CFTs.

questions.question: What is the weakest set of bootstrap assumptions that still isolates small islands for 3d Ising and O(N) CFT data?
questions.rationale: Mixed-correlator bootstrap islands in [3] and [5] rely on assumptions about the lowest relevant operators, while [S1] frames the numerical bootstrap as an active open-problem program.

questions.question: Can the c-minimization principle and operator decoupling observed near the 3d Ising point be derived from general bootstrap geometry rather than treated as numerical evidence?
questions.rationale: The precision Ising study in [2] conjectures c-minimization and observes operator decoupling as the Ising spectrum is approached.

questions.question: How can numerical bootstrap methods be extended to deliver rigorous current two-point functions and transport-relevant data across the O(N) archipelago?
questions.rationale: The O(N) mixed-correlator study in [5] determines current two-point functions in O(2) and O(3) models with applications to transport.

node_83e829448860.summary: These papers develop momentum-space conformal Ward identity methods for CFT correlation functions involving stress tensors, currents, scalars, graviton vertices, and conformal or chiral anomalies.

questions.question: Can momentum-space conformal Ward identities and triple-K renormalization be used to derive positivity or sum-rule constraints equivalent to the averaged null energy condition for general spinning CFT three-point functions?
questions.rationale: ANEC positivity and spinning-operator inequalities are derived from causality in [1], while momentum-space renormalized scalar, current, and stress-tensor correlators are developed in [2], [4], and [5].

questions.question: What is the complete classification of ultralocal, semilocal, nonlocal, type A, and type B anomalies in mixed momentum-space correlators involving stress tensors, currents, and scalars in arbitrary dimension?
questions.rationale: Scalar triple-K divergences are classified in [2], and mixed tensor-scalar correlators plus type A and B anomalies are analyzed in [4] and [5].

node_c5307ab7113f.summary: This cluster focuses on high-loop calculations of cusp anomalous dimensions in QCD and N=4 super Yang-Mills theory using form factors, Wilson lines, and analytic integration techniques.

questions.question: Can the Wilson-loop and form-factor definitions of the QCD cusp anomalous dimension be matched at five loops with full color dependence, including a controlled treatment of light-cone singularities?
questions.rationale: The question extends the Wilson-loop origin of large-x splitting functions and the four-loop form-factor calculation of quark and gluon cusp anomalous dimensions [1].

questions.question: What analytic constraints from Wilson-loop OPE discontinuities, finite integrals, and syzygy reductions are sufficient to reconstruct higher-loop cusp and collinear anomalous dimensions without full integral evaluation?
questions.rationale: This combines the polygon Wilson-loop discontinuity program with the finite-field and syzygy strategy used in four-loop QCD form factors [4].

node_514c3d3e148d.summary: These works compute multi-loop beta functions and anomalous dimensions for QCD, Yang-Mills theory, the Standard Model, and supersymmetric gauge theories.

questions.question: Which physical observable most directly shows that five-loop running of alpha_s has reduced perturbative uncertainty beyond a formal improvement of the beta function?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [5], which connects the five-loop QCD beta function to reduced alpha_s uncertainty from tau decays and improved Higgs effective-coupling predictions.

questions.question: How should scheme dependence be quantified when four- and five-loop MS-bar beta functions and anomalous dimensions are used for precision quark-mass evolution?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the four-loop quark mass anomalous dimension and invariant-mass reference advocated in [3] together with the MS-scheme beta-function computations in [1] and [4].

questions.question: Can high-loop running in supersymmetric models with extra SU(5) matter multiplets produce spectrum shifts large enough to change benchmark-point phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This derives from [S1], which studies full three-loop MSSM beta functions with additional matter and their effects on Snowmass benchmark spectra.

node_fd97b328f6be.summary: This cluster covers high-order renormalization group equations for Standard Model gauge, Yukawa, Higgs, and QCD couplings across two to five loops.

questions.question: Which phenomenological Standard Model predictions actually require five-loop QCD running rather than four-loop running once experimental and scheme uncertainties are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the five-loop beta-function result reducing alpha_s uncertainty from tau decays and improving Higgs effective-coupling and decay-rate predictions [5].

questions.question: How should invariant quark masses be used as reference quantities in precision evolution when four-loop mass anomalous dimensions are combined with higher-loop beta functions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the four-loop quark mass anomalous-dimension calculation and its conclusion that invariant quark masses are useful for accurate MS-bar mass evolution [3].

questions.question: What is the clearest benchmark for validating high-loop RG calculations across QCD, the Standard Model, and MSSM extensions with additional matter multiplets?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the sequence of three-, four-, and five-loop QCD calculations and the Snowmass use of three-loop MSSM running for benchmark spectra with extra matter [1], [2], [4], [5], [S1].

node_f91692a82424.summary: These papers determine QCD beta functions, anomalous dimensions, and renormalization constants in various gauges and schemes through four and five loops.

questions.question: Which physical QCD observable most stringently tests whether five-loop MS-bar running has reduced perturbative uncertainty beyond residual scheme and threshold-matching ambiguities?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from [5], which computes the five-loop beta function and applies it to alpha_s evolution, Higgs effective couplings, and hadronic Higgs decay rates.

questions.question: How should invariant quark masses be defined and matched across flavor thresholds so that four-loop mass anomalous dimensions give stable phenomenological evolution?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], which computes the four-loop quark mass anomalous dimension and emphasizes the invariant quark mass as a precise reference quantity.

questions.question: Can high-loop anomalous dimensions of quark, gluon, ghost, and vertex fields expose scheme-independent information about infrared fixed points or are such features purely scheme artifacts?
questions.rationale: The question draws on [2] and [4], which compute beta functions and anomalous dimensions in covariant gauges and for general compact simple Lie groups.

node_ccece5711568.summary: This cluster centers on precision multi-loop beta functions for Standard Model gauge couplings, Yukawa matrices, Higgs self-coupling, and mass parameters.

questions.question: What cross-checks between the two-loop Standard Model effective potential and direct multi-loop beta-function calculations are needed to make the running Higgs quartic and mass parameter unambiguous across schemes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the effective-potential derivation of scalar beta functions in [1] and the corrected two-loop Standard Model RGEs in [5].

questions.question: Can the dominant three-loop QCD, top-Yukawa, and Higgs-self-coupling contributions be embedded into a complete uncertainty budget for high-scale Standard Model running?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the three-loop top-Yukawa and Higgs beta-function computation in [2] and the general two-loop framework in [3].

questions.question: How much do full three-loop running and extra SU(5) matter multiplets shift benchmark supersymmetric spectra relative to two-loop evolution?
questions.rationale: This is the Snowmass-level extension posed by the benchmark-point and three-loop-running study in [S1].

node_8b5328b432c4.summary: These works analyze the NSVZ beta-function relation, anomalous dimensions, and renormalization schemes in N=1 supersymmetric gauge theories using higher-derivative regularization.

questions.question: What decisive calculation or scheme construction would settle whether the NSVZ beta function is a physical exact relation or primarily a special renormalization-scheme statement?
questions.rationale: The holomorphy and scheme-dependence papers present different interpretations of NSVZ and construct coupling redefinitions relating NSVZ and DRED results [2,5].

questions.question: Can higher-derivative or dimensional-reduction regularizations preserve the supersymmetric Ward identities needed for NSVZ-type relations beyond currently checked loop orders?
questions.rationale: The DRED consistency paper proves the quantum action principle and studies when dimensional reduction preserves supersymmetry [3].

questions.question: Do coupling-constant redefinitions inferred from abelian calculations uniquely determine non-abelian three- and four-loop gauge beta functions in N=1 supersymmetric theories?
questions.rationale: The three-loop and scheme-dependence studies use abelian calculations and redefinitions to infer non-abelian DRED beta-function terms, leaving one four-loop parameter undetermined [4,5].

node_86ac0aa9b392.summary: This cluster studies ultraviolet and infrared zeros of gauge-theory beta functions, scheme dependence, conformal windows, and fixed-point anomalous dimensions.

questions.question: Which features of ultraviolet and infrared beta-function zeros are invariant under scheme changes once four-loop and large-Nf information are combined?
questions.rationale: This follows from four-loop classifications of gauge-theory phase diagrams and large-Nf analyses of beta-function singularity structure [1], [4].

questions.question: Can the all-orders beta-function description of infrared fixed points be quantitatively reconciled with three- and four-loop anomalous dimensions in theories with fundamental and higher-representation fermions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the comparison of infrared fixed points and mass anomalous dimensions from higher-loop calculations with all-orders beta-function expectations [1], [2].

questions.question: Do Padé-based five-loop beta-function predictions reliably identify fixed points, or do their failures for anomalous dimensions and Abelian theories limit their use in conformal-window studies?
questions.rationale: The question derives from APAP and WAPAP predictions for high-loop beta functions and their noted limitations for anomalous mass dimensions and Abelian theories [5].

node_01be26d24015.summary: These papers examine Eguchi-Kawai volume reduction and center-symmetry conditions in large-N lattice gauge theories with adjoint fermions and QCD-like dynamics.

questions.question: What is the minimal, nonperturbatively testable set of center-symmetry realization conditions that guarantees large-N volume independence for Yang-Mills, QCD(AS), and QCD(Adj) across reduced volumes?
questions.rationale: This follows from the orbifold-equivalence interpretation of volume independence and its center-symmetry conditions [3] together with lattice large-N extrapolation studies [1].

questions.question: Can double-trace deformations or modified twisted Eguchi-Kawai actions preserve the correct large-N string tension and mass gap down to arbitrarily small volumes without introducing finite-N artifacts that survive continuum extrapolation?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in center-stabilized Yang-Mills volume independence through double-trace deformations [2], continuum large-N reduction evidence with a critical size [4], and modified TEK actions avoiding Z_N breaking [5].

node_e20cd79741f3.summary: This cluster investigates quark confinement in lattice Yang-Mills theory through Abelian monopoles, center vortices, dual superconductivity, and gauge-independent reformulations.

questions.question: What gauge-invariant lattice observable can decisively connect Z(N) center symmetry, vortex or monopole pictures, and the measured heavy-quark potential from short to intermediate distances?
questions.rationale: The confinement review emphasizes Z(N) center symmetry, while precision lattice studies extract the static quark-antiquark potential and force with controlled continuum extrapolations [1], [2].

questions.question: Can string breaking in n_f=2 lattice QCD be quantitatively related to the static-light meson interactions that determine quarkonium phenomenology?
questions.rationale: The string-breaking study resolves the transition from a static quark-antiquark string to static-light meson pairs and also studies short-distance interactions between two static-light mesons [3].

questions.question: Do electroweak strings and monopoles have experimentally testable stability or production signatures that can be connected to non-topological defect dynamics in the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: The electroweak-string review discusses stability with external influences and possible accelerator relevance, while the Snowmass monopole paper frames LHC searches for electroweak monopoles [5], [S1].

node_9a38e5ad7165.summary: These works focus on color confinement as a dual Meissner effect driven by Abelian monopole condensation and monopole dominance in SU(2) and SU(3) gauge theories.

questions.question: What lattice observable would decisively test whether monopole condensation accounts for the full non-Abelian string tension rather than only an approximate Abelian-projected contribution affected by Gribov copies?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Gribov-copy uncertainty and abelian/non-abelian string-tension ratio in [1] and the monopole string-tension agreement reported in [5].

questions.question: Can the dual Ginzburg-Landau description of monopole condensation incorporate light-quark screening and chiral-symmetry breaking while retaining a predictive expression for the confining string tension?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the dual Ginzburg-Landau treatment of confinement, quark-pair creation, and dynamical chiral-symmetry breaking in [4].

questions.question: How continuously are semiclassical magnetic-bion confinement on small S^1 x R^3 and monopole-based dual-superconductor confinement in four-dimensional Yang-Mills related?
questions.rationale: This connects the controlled magnetic-bion mechanism of [2] and the R^3 x S^1 monopole analysis of [3] to the monopole-condensation confinement scenario in [1], [4], and [5].

node_caf9d1fe0d91.summary: This cluster emphasizes gauge-independent descriptions of confinement based on Abelian or non-Abelian monopoles, dual superconductivity, and Abelian-projected effective theories.

questions.question: Can a gauge-independent monopole disorder parameter be constructed that quantitatively reproduces the full non-Abelian string tension without relying on maximal Abelian gauge fixing?
questions.rationale: The need for a projection-independent confinement diagnostic is motivated by the Gribov-copy sensitivity of Abelian string tensions in [1] and the Abelian-projection-independent disorder parameter in [4].

questions.question: What is the precise relation between magnetic bion condensation on small S^1 x R^3 and monopole condensation or dual Meissner descriptions in four-dimensional Yang-Mills confinement?
questions.rationale: Magnetic charge-two bions rather than unit monopoles cause confinement in controllable QCD(adj) regimes in [2], while [4] frames confinement as monopole condensation.

questions.question: Can lattice measurements distinguish confinement driven by monopoles, field-strength correlators, and classical configurations within one gauge-invariant set of order parameters?
questions.rationale: The survey in [5] explicitly compares gauge-invariant order parameters, field correlators, dual Meissner effective Lagrangians, and candidate classical configurations.

node_ae62f7320b25.summary: These papers develop gauge-independent Yang-Mills reformulations in which Abelian or non-Abelian monopoles produce quark confinement through dual superconductivity and the dual Meissner effect.

questions.question: Is confinement in gauge-independent Yang-Mills reformulations driven by charge-one monopoles, charge-two magnetic bions, or a dual-Meissner condensate whose identity depends on compactification and matter content?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the magnetic-bion confinement mechanism in [1], monopole contributions on R3 x S1 in [2], and the dual-superconductivity picture reviewed in [3].
