questions.rationale: This combines the systematic bond-algebra characterization of dualities with the dual-variable program for solving complex-action problems at nonzero density [3,5].

questions.question: What criteria determine when partial dualization preserves enough locality and positivity to make spectroscopy feasible in dual finite-density lattice field theories?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the stated conceptual challenge of spectroscopy and the proposed strategy of partial dualization in limits where full dualization is difficult [5].

questions.question: Can modified Villain formulations of fracton and exotic gauge theories provide continuum-near dual variables that retain emergent symmetries while avoiding complex weights?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the modified Villain construction, which was designed to clarify continuum limits, singularities, emergent symmetries, and dualities of exotic lattice theories [4].

node_5051ccbc56f0.summary: These papers analyze chirally symmetric minimally doubled fermion actions, focusing on species control, hypercubic-symmetry breaking, radiative counterterms, conserved currents, and chiral effective theory.

questions.question: Is minimizing fermion doubling primarily a problem of discrete-symmetry bookkeeping, or of preserving the physically correct Lorentz-representation and global-symmetry content of the low-energy spectrum?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question is motivated by the correlation-function definition of symmetry breaking in [1], the Lorentz-based taxonomy of Dirac, Majorana, and Weyl fields in [2], and the enhanced-symmetry discussion in [3].

questions.question: What calculable spectrum-level signature would distinguish genuine parity doubling near a chiral transition from accidental degeneracies in finite periodic volumes or background magnetic fields?
questions.rationale: This follows from the parity-doubled enhanced-symmetry scenario in [3] and [5] and the finite-volume accidental-symmetry analysis on a magnetic torus in [4].

questions.question: How should discrete symmetry assignments for Dirac, Majorana, and Weyl fields constrain epsilon terms in effective Lagrangians near a chiral or conformal transition?
questions.rationale: This derives from the clarification of fermion definitions versus discrete symmetries in [2] and the enhanced-global-symmetry constraints on epsilon terms in [5].

node_b8494089f5f7.summary: This cluster studies topological charge, susceptibility, instanton structure, and finite-temperature topology in lattice QCD and SU(N) Yang-Mills theory.

questions.question: What observable lattice criteria can distinguish an instanton-liquid description of light-hadron physics from other nonperturbative mechanisms for chiral symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which reviews the role of instantons and the instanton liquid in generating the light-hadron spectrum and the chiral phase transition.

questions.question: Can Wilson flow define continuum topological sectors precisely enough to remove ambiguities in topological susceptibility measurements at small lattice spacing and finite temperature?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [2], where Wilson flow makes smooth renormalized gauge fields and reveals how topological sectors emerge dynamically in the continuum limit.

questions.question: How far above the QCD crossover can lattice determinations of the finite-temperature axion potential and topological susceptibility be trusted before semiclassical or other methods must take over?
questions.rationale: This derives from [3] and [4], which use lattice QCD to determine the axion potential and topological susceptibility while emphasizing reliability limits at high temperature.

node_310235e51402.summary: These works compute topological susceptibility in pure gauge theory and dynamical QCD, examining quark-mass dependence, continuum limits, and behavior across deconfinement.

questions.question: What Wilson-flow observable and flow-time prescription would settle whether lattice topological susceptibility is continuum-universal enough for precision QCD axion applications?
questions.rationale: This derives from Wilson-flow arguments that flowed gauge fields define renormalized observables and make continuum topological sectors transparent [1].

questions.question: What temperature range and lattice-spacing control are needed to bridge the chiral-crossover regime and the high-temperature dilute-instanton-gas regime for axion cosmology?
questions.rationale: This follows from lattice studies finding different temperature dependences of topological susceptibility below and above about 250 MeV and using them for axion constraints [3], [4].

node_1d54dfafed8d.summary: The papers characterize SU(2), SU(3), and large-N Yang-Mills vacuum topology through susceptibility measurements, instanton distributions, cooling methods, and temperature dependence.

questions.question: Can Wilson flow provide a regulator-independent definition of Yang-Mills topological sectors that reconciles cooling-based instanton pictures with overlap-fermion topological charge measurements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Wilson-flow argument that smooth renormalized fields reveal topological sectors in the continuum limit [1], together with improved-cooling SU(2) instanton studies [4] and Neuberger-operator SU(3) susceptibility measurements [5].

questions.question: What microscopic change in the pure SU(3) vacuum accounts for the order-of-magnitude drop in topological susceptibility across the deconfinement temperature?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in finite-temperature SU(3) Yang-Mills calculations showing that topological susceptibility sharply decreases at T_c [3].

questions.question: Is the minimum of the volume integral of A squared a physically useful probe of topological structure in non-Abelian gauge theory, or only a gauge-fixing-dependent diagnostic?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposal that the minimum of the Euclidean integral of A squared may carry physical meaning related to topological structures and shows a phase-transition jump in lattice photodynamics [2].

node_1e54dd6aed91.summary: This cluster develops and applies improved cooling, smoothing, and fixed-point methods to isolate instantons, dislocations, and topological structures in lattice gauge fields.

questions.question: Which cooling or smoothing prescription gives instanton size and density distributions that are stable under continuum, volume, and dislocation-cutoff tests across both SU(2) and SU(3) pure gauge theory?
questions.rationale: Improved cooling found scale-invariant instantons peaked near 0.43 fm in SU(2), while other smoothing studies reported substantially different average sizes and densities [2].

questions.question: Can the apparent dense topological vacuum and charge-polarization pattern in SU(3) be shown to survive changes in filters and smoothing depth, rather than being an artifact of under-relaxed cooling?
questions.rationale: The SU(3) cooling study found a densely packed vacuum and sign polarization of large and small topological charges using several filters after smoothing [3].

questions.question: What gauge-invariant or gauge-fixed observable can decide whether instanton-dominated smoothed configurations are actually responsible for confinement when they retain the Wilson-loop area law?
questions.rationale: Renormalization-group smoothing produced instanton-dominated configurations with the original string tension, yet the authors concluded that instantons did not appear directly responsible for confinement [5].

node_3e77f3059e77.summary: These studies refine continuum and large-N determinations of Yang-Mills topological susceptibility using improved charge operators, Wilson or gradient flow, and finite-temperature comparisons.

questions.question: Can Wilson or gradient flow define topological charge cumulants whose continuum limits agree with chiral Ward-identity definitions at precision high enough to remove operator-systematic ambiguities in chi_top?
questions.rationale: Gradient-flow cumulants were found to coincide in the continuum with the universal chiral Ward-identity definition while being much less demanding than Neuberger-fermion operators [5].

questions.question: What flow-time window gives a smooth renormalized gauge field while preserving the physical topological-sector separation needed for reliable susceptibility measurements?
questions.rationale: Wilson flow makes local gauge-invariant observables finite at positive flow time and clarifies how topological sectors dynamically separate as the lattice spacing is reduced [1].

questions.question: How precisely can the sharp drop of SU(3) Yang-Mills topological susceptibility across Tc be related to changes in the full non-Gaussian topological-charge distribution?
questions.rationale: Finite-temperature SU(3) studies found chi dropping by about an order of magnitude at Tc, while high-statistics work measured deviations from Gaussianity through higher cumulants [2].

node_166855e697d1.summary: The papers measure topological susceptibility in two- and 2+1-flavor lattice QCD, linking quark masses, chiral fermions, finite temperature, theta dependence, and axion cosmology.

questions.question: What continuum-extrapolated finite-temperature topological susceptibility in 2+1(+1)-flavor QCD is needed for post-inflationary axion mass predictions to be limited by cosmology rather than lattice QCD?
questions.rationale: This follows from the precision QCD extraction of axion properties in [1] and the high-temperature lattice-QCD axion-mass calculation in [2].

questions.question: Why does chi(T) fall more mildly below about 250 MeV but approach dilute-instanton-gas behavior above that scale, and which lattice observables best identify the crossover between regimes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the distinct temperature dependences observed in [3] and the finite-temperature susceptibility and fourth-moment comparison to dilute instanton gas predictions in [4].

questions.question: How can fixed-topological-charge simulations use 1/V corrections in correlation functions to recover theta-dependent observables with controlled finite-volume errors?
questions.rationale: This derives from the saddle-point 1/V expansion for fixed-topology observables and methods to determine topological susceptibility in [5].

node_a849e82eb7fe.summary: This cluster connects instanton theory and instanton-liquid models to hadron structure, chiral symmetry breaking, deep inelastic scattering, and possible HERA signatures.

questions.question: What lattice observable could falsify the claim that instantons dominate light-hadron structure after cooling has removed non-instanton gluon fluctuations?
questions.rationale: The cooled-lattice study finds close agreement between cooled and uncooled hadronic current and density-density correlators as evidence for instanton dominance [3].

questions.question: Can the instanton-liquid derivation of an NJL-type effective fermion theory reproduce chiral symmetry breaking and hadronic matrix elements of gluon operators with controlled 1/N_c and theta-dependence uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The gluon-operator study maps instanton-vacuum gluon operators to effective fermion operators and treats theta dependence, topological susceptibility, and 1/N_c correlation functions [5].

node_55fd3165bccd.summary: These works emphasize instantons as nonperturbative QCD vacuum objects that shape chiral dynamics, hadron correlators, glueballs, finite-density effects, and phase-transition behavior.

questions.question: What lattice observable would decisively establish whether instantons dominate light-hadron structure rather than merely surviving as artifacts of cooling or filtering procedures?
questions.rationale: This broad question is grounded in cooled-lattice studies where hadronic current and density-density correlators closely match uncooled quenched configurations after non-instanton fluctuations are removed [3].

questions.question: Can instanton-induced chiral symmetry breaking and an NJL-type effective fermion action be reconciled with a quantitatively predictive confinement mechanism in the same vacuum framework?
questions.rationale: This follows from reviews deriving chiral symmetry breaking and effective chiral actions from instantons while leaving possible confinement mechanisms as an open issue [1][4].

questions.question: How robust are instanton-vacuum predictions for gluon-operator matrix elements once theta-dependence, instanton-number fluctuations, and fermion-determinant effects on topological susceptibility are treated beyond leading 1/Nc?
questions.rationale: This derives from the instanton-vacuum method for gluon-operator matrix elements that incorporates theta dependence, number fluctuations, the fermion determinant, and a 1/Nc expansion [5].

node_7c53d73b87d0.summary: The papers develop predictions and searches for QCD instanton-induced deep inelastic scattering at HERA, including fiducial kinematics, cross sections, event topology, and experimental limits.

questions.question: What fiducial DIS kinematic region would make instanton perturbation theory, lattice constraints on instanton sizes, and HERA-like experimental limits mutually consistent?
questions.rationale: This follows from the hard-scale infrared cutoff in DIS and the lattice-motivated fiducial Bjorken region used to estimate large instanton-induced cross sections [1], [5].

questions.question: Which event-shape or multiplicity observable would provide the cleanest field-level test of the proposed isotropic instanton fireball signature against ordinary QCD backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed high-multiplicity final-state structure and isolation criteria for QCD instanton searches at HERA [4].

questions.question: Can instanton-induced structure-function corrections and Wilson-line high-energy scattering amplitudes be placed in a common phenomenological framework for near-forward hadronic processes?
questions.rationale: The question connects instanton corrections to DIS coefficient functions with instanton contributions to Wilson-line and Wilson-loop high-energy scattering [2], [3].

node_9314d209b091.summary: This cluster studies finite-temperature instantons with nontrivial holonomy, showing how SU(N) calorons decompose into monopole or dyon constituents visible in cooled lattice fields.

questions.question: What lattice observable would most decisively establish that finite-temperature topological charge in Yang-Mills theory is carried by dyon constituents of nontrivial-holonomy calorons rather than by conventional instantons?
questions.rationale: The representative works show charge-one calorons decompose into monopole constituents and discuss recovering topological charge through abelian projection and cooled lattice fields [1,2,3].

questions.question: How does the exact dyon quantum weight modify the Yang-Mills partition function near the temperature where trivial holonomy becomes unstable?
questions.rationale: The functional determinant calculation predicts holonomy-, temperature-, and separation-dependent caloron weights and argues for instability of trivial holonomy below a critical temperature [5].

questions.question: Can the Taub-NUT moduli-space metric of SU(2) calorons be connected quantitatively to finite-temperature confinement observables or string-duality interpretations?
questions.rationale: The caloron moduli space is identified with R^3 x S^1 times Taub-NUT, with implications noted for finite-temperature field theory and Kaluza-Klein/H-monopole duality [1,4].

node_51ee20ab9794.summary: These papers construct and analyze self-dual Yang-Mills instanton configurations, including calorons, monopole constituents, and fractional instantons on compact spaces with twisted boundary conditions.

questions.question: How universal is the decomposition of finite-temperature instantons into fractional topological constituents across SU(N) calorons, CP(N-1) models with twisted boundary conditions, and O(3) sigma models?
questions.rationale: Constituent monopoles in SU(2) calorons [1], fractionalized instantons and neutral bions in CP(N-1) [3], and O(3) instanton constituents [5] point to a common but not yet fully unified structure.

questions.question: Can the moduli-space metrics of caloron constituents be matched quantitatively to the short- and long-distance interaction potentials of fractional instanton-anti-instanton bions?
questions.rationale: The SU(2) caloron moduli-space metric is normalized in [1], while [3] computes the separation- and N-dependent neutral-bion interaction potential.

node_d70b89cc2a15.summary: This cluster studies calorons, monopole or dyon constituents, and nontrivial holonomy in finite-temperature SU(2) and SU(3) lattice gauge theory near confinement.

questions.question: Can lattice observables identify separated SU(N) caloron dyon constituents through their Polyakov-loop eigenvalue-dependent masses in a way that is insensitive to the choice of Abelian projection?
questions.rationale: Papers [1] and [2] describe calorons as monopole constituents whose masses are tied to nontrivial holonomy and discuss recovery of topological charge under Abelian projection.

questions.question: Does the exact quantum weight for nontrivial-holonomy calorons quantitatively explain the onset of trivial-holonomy instability and dyon ionization near the confinement transition in SU(2) and SU(3)?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] derives the caloron weight and argues that below a critical temperature trivial holonomy becomes unstable and calorons ionize into dyons.

questions.question: How robust is the dyon-ensemble prediction of zero average Polyakov line and linear static-quark potential once moduli-space interactions beyond charge-one caloron constituents are included?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] constructs a many-dyon measure yielding confinement observables, while [1]-[3] establish the charge-one moduli-space structure.

node_6e8a7a3f0c24.summary: These works use lattice and analytic methods to study how SU(N) gauge theories depend on the topological theta term, including vacuum energy, CP behavior, and deconfinement.

questions.question: What lattice measurement across N and temperature would decisively confirm whether the theta-dependence variable changes from theta/N below deconfinement to theta above deconfinement?
questions.rationale: This follows from lattice evidence that theta dependence changes sharply across deconfinement from large-N theta/N scaling to instanton-gas theta scaling [3].

questions.question: Can topological interference at theta=pi be connected quantitatively to the large-N vacuum-energy expansion measured near theta=0 in four-dimensional SU(N) Yang-Mills?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by Witten-like large-N theta scaling near theta=0 and semiclassical destructive monopole-instanton interference at theta=pi [2].

questions.question: How does imaginary-theta analytic continuation control systematic errors in determining the theta dependence of the deconfinement temperature?
questions.rationale: This derives from lattice simulations at imaginary theta used to infer that the SU(3) deconfinement temperature decreases with theta [5].

node_f39aa886405b.summary: This cluster probes QCD vacuum topology through low-lying overlap Dirac eigenmodes, local chirality, localization, and tests of instanton dominance.

questions.question: Can overlap-Dirac topological charge density distinguish, in the continuum limit, a genuinely low-dimensional or fractal sign-coherent vacuum structure from smoothing- or filtering-dependent lattice artifacts?
questions.rationale: This follows from the sign-coherent sheet and skeleton structures found with the overlap Dirac operator in pure-glue SU(3) [1] and the multifractal vacuum interpretation from quenched overlap studies [2].

questions.question: What observable pattern in low-lying overlap eigenmode localization and local chirality would decisively separate confinement-driven topological charge fluctuations from an instanton-fluid description across zero and finite temperature?
questions.rationale: The question targets the tension between evidence against instanton dominance in low-mode chirality [3] and finite-temperature results supporting instanton-like dominant excitations [5].

node_054c568a61a2.summary: These papers address renormalization-scale and scheme ambiguities in perturbative QCD, including the principle of maximum conformality, running coupling determinations, and renormalon effects.

questions.question: What empirical or theoretical test would decide whether renormalon-inspired power-correction models are a reliable organizing principle for hard-process QCD, rather than a useful but process-dependent parametrization?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the review's emphasis on both the successes and failures of renormalon-inspired models of nonperturbative power corrections [1].

questions.question: Can a ghost-free analytic running coupling with a universal infrared value be reconciled quantitatively with alpha_s extractions from tau decay, jet data, and high-energy Z decay within one scale-setting framework?
questions.rationale: The analytic-coupling model proposes a universal finite alpha_s(0) and claims coherence with tau and jet information, while five-loop Z and tau analyses test alpha_s running across widely separated energies [2][3].

questions.question: Does all-order resummation of beta_0 alpha_s corrections genuinely reduce residual radiative corrections for tau widths and heavy-quark pole masses, or does it mainly reorganize the same renormalon sensitivity?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposed all-order resummation of one-loop vacuum polarization insertions and its applications to tau hadronic width and heavy-quark pole mass [5].

node_4c01c462f146.summary: This cluster examines factorial divergence, Borel singularities, renormalons, and resurgent transseries as tools for connecting perturbative and nonperturbative quantum field theory.

questions.question: Is the renormalon picture the right organizing principle for nonperturbative power corrections in QCD, or only a useful but limited phenomenological model?
questions.rationale: This low-generality framing question follows from the review's discussion of both successes and failures of renormalon-inspired models of power corrections to hard QCD processes [1].

questions.question: What observable would most directly test whether low-order perturbative behavior is already dominated by infrared renormalons and whether eliminating the pole mass genuinely improves convergence?
questions.rationale: This derives from the bubble-chain resummation study showing renormalon dominance in low orders for the pole mass and top decay width, and improved convergence after avoiding the pole mass [2].

questions.question: Can the cancellation between perturbative IR-renormalon ambiguities and semiclassical bion or kink-instanton sectors in CP(N-1) be extended into a practical continuum definition of asymptotically free QFTs?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the resurgent transseries construction on R1 x S1L, where kink-instantons, bions, and IR-renormalon ambiguities are classified in the CP(N-1) model [4].

node_c61997bd1672.summary: These works develop and compare Padé, Borel-Padé, conformal mapping, Weniger, and Meijer-G methods for estimating and resumming divergent perturbative series.

questions.question: For which QCD observables can Borel-Pade approximants reliably locate infrared-renormalon residues before the known perturbative coefficients visibly enter their asymptotic regime?
questions.rationale: This sharpens the Bjorken-sum-rule case study in [3], where Padé and Borel-Padé methods are argued to converge when renormalon behavior dominates.

questions.question: Can renormalization-scheme dependence be converted into a quantitative diagnostic for choosing among Padé, Borel-Padé, PMS, and effective-charge resummations in extractions of alpha_s?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which compares Padé summation with PMS and ECH and finds reduced scheme dependence in the Bjorken effective charge.

node_8d4ecac7b65c.summary: This cluster analyzes ultraviolet and infrared renormalons in QCD and QED, their Borel-plane singularities, large-order behavior, and associated power corrections.

questions.question: In which QCD observables do renormalon-inspired power-correction models genuinely predict nonperturbative effects, and where do they fail as phenomenological descriptions?
questions.rationale: This directly reflects the review's assessment of the successes and failures of renormalon-based power-correction models in hard QCD processes [1].

questions.question: Can formulations with an infrared-finite coupling or a confining background remove infrared renormalons without spoiling data-tested perturbative predictions such as R(e+e-) and the Adler function?
questions.rationale: This combines the freezing of the optimized couplant in R(e+e-), the claim that renormalons are absent in a confining-background expansion, and Adler-function comparisons to e+e- data [2],[4],[5].

questions.question: How should all-order resummation of Sudakov shoulders be distinguished from renormalon-driven factorial divergence in infrared-safe observables that are nevertheless finite-order divergent inside phase space?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the identification of Sudakov shoulders as finite-order divergences cured by resummation and in the broader renormalon analysis of perturbative divergence patterns [3],[1].

node_a3f66ea402d8.summary: These papers apply resurgence and transseries methods to integrable and asymptotically free field theories, linking renormalons, instantons, bions, and semiclassical expansions.

questions.question: What would be the cleanest field-theoretic evidence that infrared renormalon ambiguities in four-dimensional asymptotically free gauge theories are continuously connected to calculable neutral-bion sectors on R^3 x S^1?
questions.rationale: The CP(N-1) transseries program relates IR-renormalon ambiguities to kink-instanton and bion sectors under continuity on R x S^1 [3], while adjoint gauge theories on a circle contain neutral bions requiring generalized treatment [4].

questions.question: Can perturbative large-order data alone reliably identify non-topological saddle points in QFT path integrals when conventional homotopy classifications predict no instantons?
questions.rationale: Resurgence in the SU(N) principal chiral model is presented as a way to decode nonperturbative saddles from perturbation theory even when standard homotopy groups miss them [5].

node_06cf99609465.summary: This cluster focuses on determining the strong coupling from hadronic tau decay data using finite-energy sum rules, perturbative prescriptions, and nonperturbative corrections.

questions.question: What common analysis framework would settle the perturbative-prescription ambiguity in alpha_s from tau decays by applying fixed-order terms, analytic-continuation resummation, and beta0 resummation to the same spectral moments?
questions.rationale: This follows from the alpha_s^4 stabilization in [1], the beta0-resummation program in [3], and the analytic-continuation resummation technique in [5].

questions.question: How can finite-energy sum rules disentangle OPE condensates through dimension ten from quark-hadron duality violations strongly enough to reduce the theoretical error on alpha_s(m_tau)?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the V-A spectral-function and OPE sum-rule analysis up to dimension ten in [2] and the duality-testing role of tau spectral functions in [4].

questions.question: Does the alpha_s comparison between tau and Z decays remain the cleanest asymptotic-freedom test once low-energy nonperturbative uncertainties and high-order perturbative corrections are treated in one fit?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], which compares alpha_s from Z and tau decays using alpha_s^4 corrections, and [4], which emphasizes tau decays as a precision QCD laboratory.

node_08debfa48b39.summary: These works update and refine extractions of alpha_s from inclusive hadronic tau decays, emphasizing ALEPH and OPAL data, higher-order QCD corrections, and theoretical systematics.

questions.question: What treatment of perturbative truncation, fixed-order versus contour-improved summation, and spectral-moment choice would make alpha_s(m_tau) extractions from ALEPH and OPAL data reproducible at the level set by the alpha_s^4 Adler-function correction?
questions.rationale: The alpha_s^4 correction stabilizes tau perturbation theory in [1], while [4] revisits alpha_s(m_tau) using the fourth-order coefficient and inclusive spectral moments.

questions.question: Can updated unfolded non-strange tau spectral functions reduce the dominant theoretical uncertainty in alpha_s(m_tau), or is the limiting issue now quark-hadron duality rather than experimental covariance?
questions.rationale: The ALEPH unfolding update and corrected bin correlations are presented in [3], while [2] identifies spectral sum rules and duality tests as central to hadronic tau physics.

node_9267cef15fbc.summary: This cluster uses tau decay and related spectral functions to extract QCD vacuum condensates, low-energy constants, and chiral sum-rule constraints.

questions.question: Can tau V-A spectral functions and finite-energy chiral sum rules separate OPE condensates from duality violations without relying on model-dependent stability criteria?
questions.rationale: Tau and e+e- sum-rule extractions fit condensates, while duality-violation studies show that OPE moments and spectral moments need not match at finite momentum [2][4].

questions.question: Which condensates can be reliably extracted from tau decay, given the suppression of the gluon-condensate contribution and possible cancellations among nonstandard power corrections?
questions.rationale: Power-correction analyses argue that tau decay is poor for the gluon condensate and that instantons, duality violation, and tachyonic-gluon-mass effects partially cancel in V+A tau decay [3].

node_49a6fe7ec699.summary: These papers compare fixed-order, contour-improved, renormalon-based, and modified perturbative treatments for extracting the strong coupling from hadronic tau decays.

questions.question: What renormalon-based criterion can decide whether FOPT or CIPT is the better approximation for extracting alpha_s from hadronic tau decays?
questions.rationale: This follows from the persistent FOPT-CIPT systematic difference and the Adler-function model constrained by known coefficients and OPE large-order behavior [3].

questions.question: Can UV and IR renormalon ambiguities be absorbed into OPE power corrections in a way that yields stable uncertainties for tau spectral moments?
questions.rationale: This question derives from studies of UV renormalon ambiguities and the absorption of IR renormalon ambiguities into redefined nonperturbative OPE parameters [4],[5].

questions.question: Does exact resummation of (beta0 alpha_s)^n terms or analytic-continuation corrections reduce higher-order uncertainty enough to shift the alpha_s value inferred from the tau hadronic width?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed all-order one-loop vacuum-polarization resummation and the separate summation of analytic-continuation corrections in tau decay [1],[2].

node_7134b8c47ca0.summary: This cluster studies finite-energy sum rule extractions of V_us and the strange quark mass from flavor-breaking strange hadronic tau decay data.

questions.question: Can a finite-energy sum-rule analysis of strange hadronic tau spectra be made stable against the choice of invariant-mass moment while simultaneously extracting |V_us| and m_s?
questions.rationale: The moment dependence of m_s and its sensitivity to |V_us| are identified as leading limitations in the phenomenological scalar/pseudoscalar treatment of Ref. [2].

questions.question: Which new measurements of strange tau invariant-mass distributions would most directly reduce the experimental uncertainty in |V_us| from tau decays below that of K_e3 determinations?
questions.rationale: Ref. [1] finds the |V_us| uncertainty dominated by experiment while already competitive with K_e3 extractions.

questions.question: Can quadratic strange-quark mass corrections and dimension-four condensate contributions be organized so that renormalization-scale choices no longer dominate the theoretical uncertainty in Cabibbo-suppressed R_tau?
questions.rationale: Refs. [4] and [5] emphasize sizable O(alpha_s^2 m_s^2) and O(alpha_s^3 m_s^2) effects and the need for suitable condensate scale choices.

node_d52e1688e46b.summary: These works develop and apply the Principle of Maximum Conformality and related renormalization-group methods to remove scale and scheme ambiguities in perturbative QCD predictions.

questions.question: What observable pair would most decisively test whether commensurate scale relations remove renormalization scheme and scale ambiguity rather than merely reshuffle perturbative uncertainty?
questions.rationale: This derives from the scheme-independent transitivity of commensurate scale relations and the example relating R_e+e- to the Bjorken sum rule in [1].

questions.question: Can an automated PMC prescription uniquely identify all beta_i-dependent nonconformal terms in genuinely multi-scale QCD observables at finite order, or are there cases where the claimed beta-term degeneracy is insufficient?
questions.rationale: This follows from the all-orders PMC construction, which relies on exposing nonconformal beta_i terms and a special degeneracy in perturbative coefficients in [2] and [3].

questions.question: After four-loop PMC/BLM scale fixing, how should residual theoretical uncertainty be quantified when different schemes yield different effective PMC scales but scheme-independent observables?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the four-loop extended renormalization-group treatment and the claim that proper scale setting absorbs all beta-dependent terms into the coupling in [4] and [5].

node_7d75cc3e4d2d.summary: This cluster develops analytic perturbation theory and ghost-free running couplings to extend QCD perturbative predictions into low-energy Euclidean and Minkowskian regimes.

questions.question: What observable would most decisively test whether ghost-free analytic QCD couplings with a universal finite alpha_s(0) are a physical infrared description rather than a useful resummation prescription?
questions.rationale: The analytic-coupling model predicts a universal finite infrared limit and claims consistency with tau and jet information, but the node centers on whether that analyticity prescription has observable content [1], [5].

questions.question: Can causal analyticity, perturbative freezing, and Schwinger's beta-function spectral-density relation be made mutually consistent beyond special two- and three-loop Lambert-W constructions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the studies of Landau singularities, APT analytic continuation, and the relation between the beta function and spectral density [2], [3].

node_cc386ce4c708.summary: These papers use variational, semiclassical, renormalization-group, multiple-scale, and resurgent techniques to extract nonperturbative quantum behavior from anharmonic oscillator perturbation series.

questions.question: What criterion should determine when delta expansion, order-dependent mappings, Borel-resurgence, or semiclassical quantization is the right resummation language for a given anharmonic potential?
questions.rationale: Convergence proofs for delta expansion coexist with resurgent instanton expansions and generalized perturbation tools, leaving the organizing principle across potentials open [1], [2], [4], [5].

questions.question: Can convergence domains for order-dependent mappings be extended from single-well and strong-coupling double-well oscillators to metastable and complex-coupling problems with rigorous error estimates?
questions.rationale: The improved proof covers uniform convergence for g in [0,infinity], complex domains of E(g), double wells via Symanzik scaling, and some metastable potentials [2].

questions.question: Can high-order Bender-Wu data be used to test quantitatively how instanton actions, logarithmic factors, and nonanalytic exp(-a/g) terms reconstruct energies with vanishing perturbation series?
questions.rationale: The BenderWu package enables very high perturbative orders, while resurgent instanton analyses describe cases where perturbation theory vanishes but nonperturbative ground-state energies remain positive [4], [5].

node_64a80cd7fba7.summary: This cluster analyzes polarized deep-inelastic sum rules, especially the Bjorken sum rule, using high-order perturbative QCD, analytic couplings, Crewther relations, and low-Q2 data.

questions.question: Can the commensurate-scale relation between the Bjorken-sum effective charge and the Adler-function effective charge be extended and experimentally tested beyond O(alpha_s^4) without reintroducing renormalization-scheme ambiguity?
questions.rationale: This follows from the O(alpha_s^4) Bjorken-sum and Adler-function calculation and commensurate-scale equation [2] together with the BLM scheme-invariant Crewther relation program [4].

questions.question: Which higher-order analytic-continuation, singlet, and beta-function terms dominate the uncertainty in using polarized deep-inelastic sum rules as precision low-Q2 determinations of QCD effective couplings?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in scheme-invariant estimates requiring explicit analytical-continuation effects [1] and the singlet/non-singlet O(alpha_s^4) Crewther tests [5].

node_359b5ab81750.summary: These papers use chiral random matrix theory to model universal QCD Dirac spectra, chiral symmetry breaking, spectral sum rules, and finite-density effects.

questions.question: What lattice or instanton-ensemble tests would most sharply delimit the universality of Leutwyler-Smilga spectral sum rules beyond the symmetry assumptions built into chiral random matrix theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the conjectured symmetry-based universality of inverse-eigenvalue sum rules and their instanton-liquid check in [1].

questions.question: How do the chGOE, chGUE, and chGSE classifications fail or need refinement when QCD-like theories include additional deformations beyond gauge group and fermion representation?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the threefold classification of near-zero Dirac spectra by gauge group and representation in [2].

questions.question: Can finite-density chiral random matrix models give controlled diagnostics of when quenched QCD must be replaced by a quark-plus-conjugate-quark theory rather than an n to 0 replica limit?
questions.rationale: This derives from the finite-chemical-potential result that the naive replica trick fails and that quenched QCD is instead a 2n-quark limit in [3].

node_359b5ab81750_1.summary: This cluster focuses on random matrix descriptions of near-zero QCD Dirac eigenvalues, including Dyson-class universality, microscopic spectral densities, and chiral symmetry constraints.

questions.question: What finite-volume and topology-dependent tests would most stringently establish the universality of Leutwyler-Smilga spectral sum rules beyond the original chiral random matrix ensembles?
questions.rationale: This derives from the conjectured universal inverse-eigenvalue sum rules [1], the three Dyson chiral classes [2], and exact microscopic spectral densities [5].

questions.question: Can random matrix models at nonzero chemical potential provide controlled predictions for the complex Dirac spectrum that distinguish quenched QCD from the n to 0 replica limit with conjugate quarks?
questions.rationale: The issue is precisely the failure of the naive replica trick and the conjugate-quark interpretation of quenched finite-density QCD in [3].

node_3451ee44c1e0.summary: These works emphasize universal microscopic correlations and spectral densities of QCD Dirac eigenvalues near zero virtuality and their connection to chiral symmetry breaking.

questions.question: Where is the quantitative boundary between chiral-random-matrix universality and partially quenched chiral perturbation theory as the valence mass crosses E_c ~ F^2/(Sigma_0 L^2)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the separation of ergodic and diffusive domains by E_c in the pqChPT analysis of Dirac spectra [4].

questions.question: How universal are Leutwyler-Smilga inverse-eigenvalue sum rules across gauge groups, fermion representations, flavor numbers, and topological sectors?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the conjectured universality of spectral sum rules in [1] and the chGOE/chGUE/chGSE classification in [2].

questions.question: Can exact supersymmetric-manifold expressions for microscopic spectral densities be generalized to nonzero topology and arbitrary N_f in a form directly testable in lattice QCD?
questions.rationale: This derives from the exact spectral density and correlations in [3] and the Gl(N_f+1|1) representation of the microscopic density in [5].

node_fefc2d29f5f9.summary: This cluster applies chiral random matrix models to QCD phase structure, chemical potential, non-Hermitian Dirac spectra, quenched limits, and chiral transitions.

questions.question: Can finite-density chiral random matrix theory identify exactly when the quenched limit must be represented by quarks plus conjugate quarks rather than by a naive replica n to 0 limit?
questions.rationale: This comes directly from the random matrix solution showing that the naive replica trick fails at nonzero chemical potential [1].

questions.question: Which non-Hermitian Dirac eigenvalue correlations remain universal at baryon chemical potential once model parameters are scaled so that thermodynamic quantities are independent of mu below the finite-density transition?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the review’s universality claims for chiral random matrices and in the alternate finite-density model with exact eigenvalue correlations [2,3].

questions.question: Can the factorization method be extended beyond random matrix tests to isolate how the imaginary part of the finite-density action drives a first-order chiral transition without reintroducing an overlap problem?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the factorization-method test that reproduces exact quark number density and clarifies how the imaginary action induces the transition [5].

node_812ad173b6aa.summary: These papers determine chiral condensates and symmetry-breaking behavior from lattice QCD Dirac eigenvalue spectra, including overlap, Wilson, and finite-density formulations.

questions.question: How can the Silver Blaze behavior at small chemical potential be reconstructed directly from the motion and weighting of Dirac eigenvalues in lattice formulations with Wilson or overlap fermions?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the tension between chemical-potential-dependent Dirac spectra and the unchanged zero-temperature free energy emphasized in [1].

questions.question: Can low-mode counting methods for Wilson fermions be extended into a controlled finite-density estimator of chiral order parameters without losing the renormalizability advantages of spectral observables?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the Banks-Casher mode-counting calculation of the condensate with Wilson quarks in [3] and the finite-density spectral issue in [1].

questions.question: What scaling laws for the Wilson-Dirac spectral gap survive when approaching simultaneously the chiral, continuum, and large-volume limits in simulations designed to measure condensate spectra?
questions.rationale: This follows from the observed gap median scaling with quark mass and width scaling as a/sqrt(V) in [5].

node_bdf44bc2c876.summary: This cluster studies Anderson-like localization transitions of low Dirac eigenmodes in finite-temperature QCD and related lattice gauge theories across deconfinement and chiral transitions.

questions.question: Is the finite-temperature chiral crossover in physical 2+1 flavor QCD causally driven by Anderson localization of the lowest Dirac modes, or are localization and chiral restoration correlated consequences of another gauge-field disorder mechanism?
questions.rationale: This follows from evidence that low Dirac modes undergo a metal-insulator transition near the chiral transition [1] and from physical-mass simulations showing localized low modes across the finite-temperature crossover [5].

questions.question: What is the universality class of the QCD Dirac mobility edge across fermion discretizations, gauge actions, and quark masses, and does the critical exponent always match the unitary Anderson model?
questions.rationale: This extends finite-size scaling evidence for a genuine mobility edge with a correlation-length exponent compatible with the unitary Anderson model [4].

questions.question: Can the transition from Poisson to random-matrix spectral statistics be derived from a microscopic description of chiral disorder that connects ergodic, diffusive, ballistic, and localized regimes of the quark spectrum?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the chiral-disorder framework using GOR and semiclassical arguments [2] and high-temperature observations of Poisson-localized low modes crossing over to random-matrix bulk statistics [3].

node_b860df438a32.summary: These papers develop and review lattice formulations of super Yang-Mills theories that preserve exact supercharges and reduce continuum fine tuning.

questions.question: For four-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills, which exact-lattice formulation gives the smallest residual fine tuning needed to recover the full continuum supersymmetry?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that exact lattice supersymmetry reduces or eliminates continuum fine tuning and from the open-problem emphasis in [3] and [4].

questions.question: Can exact-supersymmetric lattice simulations of N=4 Yang-Mills produce nonperturbative strong-coupling results away from the planar limit that sharply test holographic quantum-gravity predictions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Snowmass framing that such formulations open a window on nonperturbative physics away from the planar limit with applications to holography [S1].

questions.question: Which observables in supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics most robustly discriminate the dual black-hole prediction from lattice artifacts, finite-N effects, and thermal boundary-condition effects?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the finite-temperature Monte Carlo interpolation between weak-coupling behavior and the strong-coupling dual black-hole prediction in [1].

node_a550956ed457.summary: This cluster studies Wess-Zumino models on the lattice, focusing on exact or approximate supersymmetry, Ward identities, Leibniz-rule issues, and supersymmetry breaking.

questions.question: What lattice prescription gives the clearest continuum restoration test of Wess-Zumino supersymmetry: exact preservation of one supercharge, approximate preservation of all supercharges, or improvement-term restoration?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the exact single-supercharge lattice construction in [2] and improvement-term approach in [5].

questions.question: Can supersymmetric Ward identities distinguish genuine supersymmetry restoration from accidental boson-fermion mass degeneracy at finite lattice spacing?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Ward-identity and mass-gap checks in [2] and the O(a) Ward-identity restoration issue in [4].

questions.question: Which lattice derivative and surface-integral discretization minimize finite-spacing violations in two-dimensional N=2 Wess-Zumino simulations while remaining practical for dynamical fermions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison of Wilson, Stratonovitch, SLAC, and improvement-term prescriptions in [5].

node_d27636a5c1c0.summary: These works construct exact-supersymmetry lattice Yang-Mills actions using twisted, topological, orbifold, and Kahler-Dirac formulations, including two-dimensional and four-dimensional extended theories.

questions.question: For lattice N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills, which exact twisted or orbifold supersymmetries are sufficient to eliminate all fine tuning needed for the full continuum supersymmetry to emerge?
questions.rationale: The reviews and constructions state that exact lattice supersymmetry reduces or can eliminate fine tuning, especially for N=4 SYM, but frame restoration of the target continuum theory as a central issue [1], [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: Can numerical simulations of exact-supersymmetry lattices access strong-coupling, non-planar observables in N=4 Yang-Mills accurately enough to test holographic quantum-gravity expectations?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass paper emphasizes exact-supersymmetry lattice formulations of N=4 Yang-Mills as a route to strong-coupling and non-planar physics relevant to holography [S1].

questions.question: How far can the equivalence between twisted supersymmetry and orbifold-deconstruction constructions be pushed across dimensions and supercharge counts?
questions.rationale: The exact-lattice-supersymmetry review states that twisted and orbifold-deconstruction approaches are equivalent for gauge theories, while the Euclidean Ad* construction spans d=1,2,3,4 theories with sixteen supercharges [1], [5].

node_1c188e8ceac5.summary: This cluster centers on numerical lattice simulations of four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, especially gluino tuning and low-lying bound-state spectra.

questions.question: Which finite-N lattice observables in the bosonic spectrum of N=1 SYM most sharply test the predicted orientifold parity doubling and condensate relations before taking the large-N limit?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claimed large-N orientifold equivalence and its predicted parity doublets and bifermion condensate in the bosonic sector [1].

questions.question: Can lattice simulations identify the symmetry-breaking conditions under which orbifold or orientifold equivalences fail, and thereby separate genuine N=1 SYM spectral predictions from daughter-theory artifacts?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the failure of orientifold equivalence on small R^3 x S^1 due to charge-conjugation breaking and by the stated necessary symmetry conditions for large-N equivalence [3].

node_01f0c9885b5f.summary: These papers use lattice and non-lattice simulations of maximally supersymmetric matrix quantum mechanics to test gauge-gravity duality and D0-brane black-hole thermodynamics.

questions.question: Can large-N continuum simulations of 16-supercharge matrix quantum mechanics determine the first stringy corrections to E/N^2 beyond the supergravity coefficient 7.41 T^(14/5)?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the precision lattice confirmation of the supergravity internal-energy coefficient and its stated use in constraining stringy corrections [4].

questions.question: How robust is the apparent absence of a sharp Polyakov-line phase transition in the full fermionic theory when comparing non-lattice simulations, naive lattice actions, and manifestly supersymmetric discretizations?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the observed low-temperature Polyakov-line behavior in the 16-supercharge simulation and the comparison of naive and supersymmetric lattice actions [1].

questions.question: Can simulations of maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on rectangular and skewed two-tori map the full shape-parameter phase diagram predicted by dual black-hole and hot-string geometries?
questions.rationale: This comes from the proposal to test holography on flat two-tori where skewed torus parameters modify the dual black-hole predictions [5].

node_69846405e87c.summary: This cluster examines spontaneous symmetry breaking, Goldstone modes, conservation laws, gauge invariance, and particle mixing in non-Hermitian and PT-symmetric quantum field theories.

questions.question: What is the correct Goldstone-counting principle when the symmetry-breaking theory is non-Hermitian or PT-symmetric rather than a conventional Lorentz-invariant Hermitian system?
questions.rationale: This broad question is grounded in the failure of naive Goldstone counting for spacetime symmetries in [1] and the non-Lorentz-invariant counting frameworks in [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can expectation values of commutators of broken charges still determine the number and dispersion type of Nambu-Goldstone modes when the effective theory has non-Hermitian time evolution?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the counting rule using the rank of the broken-charge commutator matrix in [3] and the conjugate-pair interpretation in [2].

questions.question: How should effective Lagrangians on coset spaces be modified when the partially symplectic geometry of nonrelativistic symmetry breaking is combined with non-Hermitian conservation laws?
questions.rationale: The coset-space and partially symplectic structure emphasized in [2] motivates asking how those tools extend beyond the Hermitian cases reviewed in [5].

node_d5336b1d4434.summary: These works analyze non-Hermitian PT-symmetric quantum field theories, including real spectra, inner products, discrete symmetries, renormalization, and extensions of gauge and Goldstone mechanisms.

questions.question: What experimental or theoretical criterion would decide whether PT-symmetric field theories are merely dual reformulations of Hermitian theories or genuinely new quantum field theories?
questions.rationale: The exact equivalence of PT-symmetric Thirring and Sine-Gordon models to Hermitian versions contrasts with claims of new renormalizable scalar dynamics [1], [2].

questions.question: Can a general variational and Noether framework be formulated in which conserved currents, not Lagrangian invariances, are the primary consistency data of non-Hermitian quantum field theories?
questions.rationale: This derives from the result that non-Hermitian PT-symmetric Lagrangian invariance does not generally imply the corresponding conserved current, while Goldstone modes still rely on conserved currents [3], [5].

questions.question: Are non-Hermitian gauge and Yukawa extensions capable of producing small neutrino masses and CP violation without losing unitarity, gauge consistency, or a real spectrum beyond the special equal-mass limits?
questions.rationale: The gauge-extension paper restores gauge invariance in a special anti-Hermitian/Hermitian mass limit and proposes implications for neutrino masses and leptonic CP violation [4].

node_6b0b917a054b.summary: This cluster develops counting rules and effective theories for Nambu-Goldstone modes in systems without Lorentz invariance, including type-A/type-B dispersions and redundant modes.

questions.question: What broad criterion unifies Goldstone counting for internal and spacetime symmetry breaking when some broken generators are redundant rather than paired into canonically conjugate type-B modes?
questions.rationale: This follows from the failure of naive counting for broken spacetime symmetries [1] and the effective-Lagrangian pairing rule based on nonzero commutator expectation values [2].

questions.question: Can the rank formula based on expectation values of commutators be derived with the same predictive power at zero and finite temperature for systems with non-semisimple algebras and central extensions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by Mori-projection derivations of the rank counting rule at zero and finite temperature [3] and the role of central extensions and partially symplectic coset geometry [2].

node_5c258aaa1b64.summary: This broad cluster covers theoretical and experimental studies of exotic hadrons, including pentaquarks, tetraquarks, hybrid mesons, glueballs, and heavy quarkonium spectra.

questions.question: What experimental pattern of masses, decay modes, and production rates would decisively distinguish hadronic molecules from compact tetraquarks or diquark-based multiquark states?
questions.rationale: Hadronic-molecule reviews emphasize controlled EFT predictions and identification methods, while Snowmass frames the central unresolved issue as molecular versus compact organization of multiquark hadrons [1], [S1].

questions.question: Can any single theoretical framework accommodate the charged Z states, hidden-charm pentaquarks, and broader XYZ spectrum without conflicting with current experimental puzzles?
questions.rationale: The hidden-charm pentaquark and tetraquark review explicitly lists puzzles and theoretical challenges, and the XYZ review notes that no simple quark-model classification captures the observed states [2], [5].

questions.question: What reaction-amplitude and lattice-QCD inputs are needed to separate glueballs, hybrids, two-hadron states, and conventional quark-model states in the experimentally accessible spectrum?
questions.rationale: The anisotropic lattice glueball study stresses continuum spin identification and separation from two-glueball and torelon states, while the Snowmass spectroscopy summary highlights remaining work to extract hybrids and glueballs from amplitude data [4], [S3].

node_3980113a3695.summary: These papers focus on exotic charmoniumlike and hidden-charm states, especially molecular interpretations of LHCb pentaquarks and related multiquark candidates.

questions.question: Which finite-volume lattice and nonrelativistic EFT observables can distinguish a shallow hidden-charm hadronic molecule from a compact tetraquark or threshold effect with controlled uncertainty?
questions.rationale: The hadronic-molecule review identifies nonrelativistic EFTs, finite-volume methods, lattice QCD, and structure diagnostics as central tools, while Snowmass notes that no single interpretation accommodates all exotics [1], [S1].

questions.question: What future measurements of hidden-charm pentaquark line shapes, decay modes, and production mechanisms would discriminate molecular and multiquark interpretations?
questions.rationale: The hidden-charm pentaquark and tetraquark review explicitly lists puzzles, theoretical challenges, and future measurements needed to distinguish underlying structures [2].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel chiral-unitary resummation methods be adapted to hidden-charm thresholds to extract resonance poles for XYZ states without relying on ad hoc Breit-Wigner parameterizations?
questions.rationale: The kaon-nucleon work uses dispersion relations and coupled-channel resummation to identify resonance content, while Belle's pi+ pi- J/psi analysis describes Y and charged charmoniumlike structures with Breit-Wigner forms [4], [5].

node_ce706703d1cf.summary: This cluster studies heavy-quark pentaquark candidates using molecular, chiral quark, chromomagnetic, QCD sum-rule, and scattering approaches.

questions.question: Which coupled-channel line-shape and decay measurements can unambiguously distinguish hidden-charm pentaquark molecules from compact diquark-based multiquark configurations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the competing molecular and multiquark interpretations and the proposed discriminating measurements reviewed in [1] and [5].

questions.question: Can heavy-quark spin and flavor analogues across charm and bottom pentaquarks provide selection rules that reduce the overpopulation problem in multiquark spectroscopy models?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the predicted charm and bottom analogues in [2] and the absence of selection rules emphasized in [4].

questions.question: What minimal set of pole positions, quantum numbers, and open-channel branching fractions would force a first-principles or lattice-QCD description beyond current phenomenological models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the lack of rigorous first-principles control for complex short-lived exotics in [3] and the model challenges summarized in [1] and [4].

node_76d51c5c8060.summary: These works model pentaquark masses, parities, and flavor structures using diquark, diquark-triquark, chiral quark, and QCD sum-rule frameworks.

questions.question: Which spin, parity, and decay measurements of hidden-charm pentaquarks would decisively separate compact diquark-triquark or diquark-diquark-antiquark pictures from molecular interpretations?
questions.rationale: The reviews in [1] and [4] identify hidden-charm pentaquarks as multiquark candidates and note that LHCb evidence strongly informs the molecular versus compact-structure debate.

questions.question: Can diquark pentaquark spectroscopy develop selection rules that prevent the overproduction of unobserved multiquark states?
questions.rationale: The absence of selection rules limiting the number of predicted states is highlighted as a major problem for multiquark models in [3].

questions.question: How should QCD-inspired pentaquark mass models incorporate thresholds, short lifetimes, and coupled-channel effects when lattice QCD cannot yet fully resolve complex exotic states?
questions.rationale: The limitations of first-principles lattice treatment for complex short-lived states and reliance on phenomenological models are emphasized in [2].

node_9d32d4aff930.summary: These papers model exotic five-quark baryons, especially hidden-charm and fully heavy pentaquarks, using chiral, chromomagnetic, diquark, and constituent quark approaches to predict masses and stability.

questions.question: What minimal selection rule or dynamical organizing principle can prevent heavy pentaquark quark models from predicting far more multiquark states than are observed?
questions.rationale: The overpopulation problem and absence of selection rules are highlighted as central model-building challenges in [3].

questions.question: Which measured properties of hidden-charm pentaquarks would most decisively distinguish compact diquark pentaquarks from hadronic molecules in the quark-model descriptions?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in [1], which reviews competing interpretations and future measurements needed to distinguish underlying structures, and [4], which notes LHCb evidence favoring molecular pictures.

questions.question: Can constituent, chromomagnetic, and diquark models give stable mass and width predictions for pentaquarks with two, three, or four heavy quarks once thresholds and short-lived-state effects are included?
questions.rationale: The motivation comes from the broad exotic spectrum reviewed in [4] and the limitation of phenomenological QCD-inspired models for complex short-lived states described in [2].

node_1a5862a07b8c.summary: This cluster examines pentaquark structures across light, strange, charmed, bottomed, and fully heavy sectors using SU(3), diquark-triquark, chromomagnetic, and heavy-quark symmetry frameworks.

questions.question: Which correlated spin, parity, flavor-multiplet, and decay signatures would distinguish diquark-triquark pentaquarks from other QCD-inspired descriptions of heavy exotic baryons?
questions.rationale: The diquark-triquark model predicts a P-wave J^P=1/2^+ SU(3) antidecuplet structure [3], while reviews stress the multiplicity of competing phenomenological models [1],[2].

questions.question: Does the positive-parity p-shell ordering produced by flavor-spin hyperfine interactions persist when extended from strange uudd sbar pentaquarks to heavy-flavor pentaquark multiplets?
questions.rationale: The constituent-quark calculation finds the lowest strange pentaquark is a positive-parity p-shell state stabilized by flavor-spin hyperfine forces [5].

node_c898a78e7348.summary: These works interpret LHCb P_c resonances and related heavy-flavor partners as compact hidden-charm pentaquarks, assigning masses, spins, parities, and decay patterns through chromomagnetic and diquark models.

questions.question: Which spin-parity and decay-pattern measurements of Pc(4312), Pc(4440), and Pc(4457) can decisively discriminate compact diquark pentaquarks from Sigma_c Dbar and Sigma_c Dbar* molecular compositeness?
questions.rationale: This question reflects the competing compact-diquark and compositeness/effective-range interpretations of the narrow LHCb Pc peaks [4],[5].

questions.question: Are broad J/psi p contributions hidden in Lambda_b→J/psi p K− data required by compact pentaquark multiplets, and how can amplitude analyses recover them without bias from the narrow peaks?
questions.rationale: This follows from the note that the LHCb analysis is not sensitive to broad J/psi p contributions such as the former Pc(4380) [5].

questions.question: Can heavy-flavor partner searches impose selection rules that prevent compact multiquark models from overpredicting hidden-charm pentaquark states?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the broader review challenge that multiquark models lack selection rules limiting the number of predicted states [2].

node_d5427ce5bd9d.summary: This cluster uses QCD sum rules and diquark-diquark-antiquark interpolating currents to estimate masses, residues, parities, and assignments of hidden-charm, strange, and doubly charmed pentaquarks.

questions.question: Which interpolating currents, molecular anti-D Sigma_c-type or diquark-diquark-antiquark type, give stable and distinguishable QCD sum-rule predictions for Pc masses, pole residues, and parities?
questions.rationale: This compares the molecular QCD sum-rule assignment in [2] with the diquark-diquark-antiquark current construction in [4].

questions.question: What measurements of spin-parity assignments and partner states, including isospin doublets, hidden-bottom analogues, and extra Dbar Sigma_c-star configurations, would decisively test compact-diquark versus molecular interpretations?
questions.rationale: The proposed tests follow from the diquark-model pattern in [1] and [3] and the partner predictions in [2].

questions.question: How sensitive are pentaquark QCD sum-rule parity assignments to the energy-scale prescription, condensate truncation through dimension 10, and continuum-threshold choice?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the scale formula and dimension-10 OPE used in [4] and the long-standing parity issue emphasized in [5].

node_91ac33fdb56c.summary: These papers treat the LHCb P_c and P_cs states as loosely bound meson-baryon molecules near Sigma_c anti-D thresholds, studying their interactions, quantum numbers, and partner states.

questions.question: What measurements in Lambda_b -> K chi_c1 p and related channels can decisively distinguish a genuine Pc resonance from the chi_c1 p triangle-singularity explanation of the narrow 4.45 GeV structure?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from [1], which argues that the Pc(4450) signal may arise from chi_c1 p rescattering and calls for measuring Lambda_b^0 -> K^- chi_c1 p.

questions.question: Can a contact-range EFT with heavy-quark spin symmetry predict all seven S-wave antimeson-baryon molecular pentaquarks once the Pc(4312), Pc(4440), and Pc(4457) pole parameters are fixed?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [3], which accommodates the three narrow LHCb states and predicts four additional S-wave heavy antimeson-baryon molecules using heavy-quark spin symmetry.

questions.question: Which coupled-channel effects among J/psi N, Dbar* Lambda_c, Dbar Sigma_c*, and Dbar* Sigma_c channels are essential to reproduce both the J/psi p and K p mass distributions in Lambda_b decays?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4], which describes Lambda_b -> J/psi K^- p using coupled hidden-charm baryon channels while also fitting the K^- p distribution near threshold.

node_975427ab947b.summary: This cluster focuses on molecular interpretations of hidden-charm and open-strange pentaquarks built from charmed baryons and anti-charmed mesons, using coupled-channel, one-boson-exchange, and chiral effective approaches.

questions.question: Do the P_c(4312), P_c(4440), and P_c(4457) complete a seven-state S-wave heavy-quark spin symmetry multiplet, and where should the four missing antimeson-baryon molecular partners appear?
questions.rationale: The complete seven-state HQSS molecular multiplet prediction is the central result of [2].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel dynamics among J/psi N, Dbar* Lambda_c, Dbar* Sigma_c, Dbar Sigma_c*, and Dbar* Sigma_c* reproduce both the J/psi p and Kp spectra in Lambda_b decays without imposing a preselected molecular assignment?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the coupled-channel description of Lambda_b -> J/psi K p and the simultaneous Kp and J/psi p spectrum analysis in [3].

questions.question: Which spin-parity assignments for P_c states are stable under one-boson-exchange model variations between Dbar Sigma_c, Dbar Sigma_c*, and Dbar* Sigma_c thresholds?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the OBE assignments in [4] and [5], which relate specific P_c states to loosely bound charmed-baryon and anticharmed-meson channels.

node_7d7912d43120.summary: These studies propose and analyze experimental production channels for hidden-charm pentaquarks, including Lambda_b, Xi_b, and Omega_b decays as well as photoproduction and pion-induced scattering.

questions.question: Can combined measurements of Lambda_b -> K chi_c1 p and J/psi photoproduction decisively separate a genuine Pc(4450) resonance from the chi_c1 p triangle-singularity explanation?
questions.rationale: The triangle-singularity interpretation predicts a key test in Lambda_b -> K chi_c1 p, while photoproduction is argued not to satisfy the anomalous triangle condition [1][3].

questions.question: Which decay-channel pattern in gamma p production of Pc(4380) and Pc(4450) would discriminate baryocharmonium, antiquark-diquark-diquark, and molecular interpretations?
questions.rationale: Photon-nucleon formation rates and additional decay channels are described as sensitive to internal pentaquark dynamics, while competing structural assignments are proposed for the same peaks [2][4].

questions.question: Do Xi_b^- -> J/psi K^- Lambda data reveal the predicted strangeness S = -1 counterpart of Pc(4450), and are its line shape and rate consistent with a unitary molecular final-state-interaction mechanism?
questions.rationale: The Xi_b decay study gives a concrete prediction for a J/psi Lambda hidden-charm pentaquark counterpart with a comparable decay rate [5].

node_ae79c6b81cd1.summary: This cluster centers on the proposed Theta+ pentaquark, its parity, lattice-QCD evidence, photoproduction and pion-production mechanisms, experimental status, and possible heavy analogs.

questions.question: What experimental or lattice observable would have definitively distinguished a genuine narrow Theta(1540)+ resonance from KN scattering effects in the reported S=+1 channel?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in phenomenological discussions of Theta signals and KN scattering, together with experimental width limits in the 1-4 MeV range [4], [5].

questions.question: Can lattice QCD with modern unquenched ensembles and a variational basis of diquark-diquark-antiquark and scattering operators resolve the parity conflict between positive-parity diquark models and negative-parity lattice signals?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the positive-parity diquark model prediction and quenched lattice studies favoring a lowest negative-parity Theta state [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: Do searches for exotic Xi states near 1750 MeV and heavy charm or bottom Theta analogues still provide a sharp test of the correlated-diquark classification?
questions.rationale: This derives from the diquark model's predictions of exotic Xi multiplets and strong-decay-stable charm and bottom analogues, contrasted with lattice results placing Theta_c above DN threshold [1], [2].

node_7d86dc5d616f.summary: These papers review and analyze charmoniumlike XYZ states observed in electron-positron and hadron experiments, including Y, Z_c, and coupled-channel structures beyond conventional quarkonium.

questions.question: Which amplitude-analysis observables can decide whether the Y(4260), Zc(3900), and related structures are genuine poles, threshold effects, hadronic molecules, compact tetraquarks, or hybrids?
questions.rationale: This follows from the observed Y and charged Zc structures in [2] and the lack of a single successful interpretation emphasized in [1] and [S1].

questions.question: Can one spectroscopy framework consistently describe charged Zc states, Y states, open-heavy tetraquarks, pentaquarks, hybrids, and glueball candidates without proliferating unconstrained states?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the broad catalog of new hidden and open heavy flavor states in [1], [3], [5], and the Snowmass summary [S1].

questions.question: What BESIII data-taking priorities would most efficiently discriminate among molecule, diquark, and hybrid interpretations of charmoniumlike XYZ states?
questions.rationale: This derives from the future BESIII program for tau-charm and hadron physics in [4] and the interpretation challenges reviewed in [1] and [3].

node_5860e3d83b99.summary: This cluster investigates vector charmoniumlike resonances such as Y(4260), Y(4360), and Y(4500) in electron-positron annihilation channels and explores charmonium, molecular, and threshold interpretations.

questions.question: Are the Y(4260), Y(4008), and newer vector structures best described by distinct resonances, threshold distortions, or coupled-channel effects across e+e- to pi+ pi- J/psi and open-charm channels?
questions.rationale: Belle measured Y(4260), reported an excess compatible with Y(4008), and observed charged charmoniumlike structure in the pi J/psi spectrum, motivating a unified line-shape interpretation [1].

questions.question: Do near-threshold charged structures such as Zc(4025) and the Ds D* threshold enhancement arise from the same dynamics that produce vector Y states in e+e- annihilation?
questions.rationale: BESIII observed a Zc(4025) near the D* anti-D* threshold at sqrt(s)=4.26 GeV and a separate near-threshold structure in K+ recoil spectra near Ds D* thresholds [3],[5].

questions.question: What decisive decay pattern would distinguish a diquark-antidiquark interpretation of Y(4260) from conventional charmonium or molecular alternatives?
questions.rationale: The four-quark interpretation predicts Y(4260) as an orbital [cs][cbar sbar] excitation with predominant Ds Dbar_s decay and production in B nonleptonic decays with a kaon [4].

node_e9582945dd01.summary: These works study charged and neutral charmoniumlike enhancements arising in hidden-charm dipion and di-kaon decays of higher charmonia, including resonance assignments and interference explanations.

questions.question: Can coupled-channel amplitude analyses distinguish genuine charged Zc resonances from ISPE-driven interference structures in Y(4260) to pi+ pi- J/psi?
questions.rationale: This follows from Belle's observation of a charged structure in pi J/psi and the ISPE mechanism that reproduces the Zc(3900) line shape through interference [1][5].

questions.question: Are the Zc(4025) and strange near-threshold structures governed by a common threshold dynamics across D*D* and DsD* channels, or do their production ratios require distinct resonance assignments?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in BESIII observations of near-threshold structures in D*D* pi and K recoil spectra with measured masses, widths, and production ratios [3][4].

questions.question: What precision measurements of pi+pi- J/psi cross sections between 3.8 and 5.5 GeV would settle whether the Y(4008)-like excess is a separate vector state or part of the Y(4260) decay dynamics?
questions.rationale: This derives from Belle's measurement of e+e- to pi+pi- J/psi, where both Y(4260) and an excess near 4 GeV are described phenomenologically [1].

node_ae32bf501dcd.summary: This cluster analyzes electron-positron cross-section line shapes for J/psi-family and open-charm channels to extract vector charmonium resonance parameters and classify Y states within charmonium spectra.

questions.question: Can a coupled line-shape analysis of hidden-charm and open-charm e^+e^- channels determine whether Y(4220) is a conventional 4S-3D charmonium state or an exotic vector state?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Y(4220) charmonium assignment and partner-state predictions in [2] together with the precision pi^+pi^-J/psi line-shape measurements in [1].

questions.question: How should OZI-evading meson-loop rescattering be incorporated into vector charmonium fits so that non-D\bar D branching ratios and dipion transition structures are described consistently?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the meson-loop explanation of psi(3770) non-D\bar D decays in [3] and the Y-state dipion structures observed in [1].

questions.question: Can Pomeron-exchange and coupled-channel final-state-interaction mechanisms be distinguished experimentally in the di-J/psi spectrum near X(6900), X(6200), X(6680), and X(7200)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dynamical X(6900) production mechanism in [4] and the partial-wave coupled-channel pole analysis in [5].

node_5ec7117cce2d.summary: This cluster centers on BESIII observations and theoretical predictions of charged charmoniumlike structures near open-charm thresholds in hidden-charm and open-strange decay channels.

questions.question: Can energy-dependent line-shape measurements near D*D* and DsD* thresholds distinguish genuine charged charmoniumlike poles from cusp or initial-single-pion-emission effects?
questions.rationale: This question connects the BESIII Zc(4025) threshold enhancement with the ISPE reproduction of the Zc(3900) structure without requiring a conventional resonance interpretation [2],[4].

questions.question: Do hidden-charm open-strange threshold enhancements predicted in J/psi K spectra appear with correlated partners near D Ds* and D*Ds thresholds at BESIII or Belle II?
questions.rationale: This follows from predictions of charged charmoniumlike structures in hidden-charm di-kaon decays near open-strange charm thresholds [5].

questions.question: What minimal set of decay channels and recoil-mass spectra is needed to map whether Zc(3982), Zc(4025), and related structures share a common open-charm molecular or kinematic origin?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in BESIII observations of near-threshold structures in D*D* and DsD* recoil spectra with measured masses, widths, and production fractions [2],[3].

node_9ff79019f0ac.summary: These papers explore whether Y states such as Y(4260), Y(3940), Y(4140), and Y(4274) are conventional charmonia or hadronic molecules with distinctive decay patterns.

questions.question: Which decay pattern among D_s D_sbar, J/psi pi pi, J/psi omega, J/psi phi, radiative modes, and open-charm channels can decisively separate tetraquark and molecular interpretations of the Y states?
