questions.rationale: Tetraquark models predict distinctive D_s D_sbar and isovector-partner channels for Y(4260) [1][2], while molecule models emphasize J/psi V, radiative, and rescattering-driven decay modes [3][4].

questions.question: Can precision quantum-number measurements of Y(3940), Y(4140), and Y(4143) confirm the proposed D*D*bar and D_s*D_s*bar molecular assignments with J^PC = 0++ or 2++?
questions.rationale: The molecular assignments of Y(3940), Y(4140), and Y(4143) hinge on predicted heavy-vector-meson bound states and their quantum numbers [3][4].

questions.question: Does the charged structure in Y(4260) -> pi+ pi- J/psi favor tetraquark partners near 3880 MeV or a molecular D*D*bar peak near 4020 MeV?
questions.rationale: The charged-resonance analysis contrasts a tetraquark peak near 3880 MeV with a molecular D*D*bar expectation near 4020 MeV [5].

node_2cb9d1d2a40f.summary: This cluster consists of broad reviews on the experimental discoveries, theoretical interpretations, and open questions surrounding heavy-quark XYZ exotic hadrons.

questions.question: What single pattern of masses, widths, quantum numbers, and production or decay modes would most decisively rule in or rule out molecules, threshold effects, diquark compounds, hybrids, or glueballs as a unified explanation of the XYZ spectrum?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the review consensus that no single interpretation accommodates all new multiquark particles [1,2,S1].

questions.question: How should BESIII and related amplitude analyses prioritize charm, charmoniumlike, glueball, and hybrid channels to distinguish genuine exotic poles from reaction-dependent enhancements?
questions.rationale: This derives from the BESIII future-program survey in [3] and the Snowmass emphasis on extracting hybrid and glueball signals from reaction-amplitude data [S1].

node_d71bb6d8e535.summary: These works survey developments in heavy hadron spectroscopy, including charmonium, open-charm mesons, pentaquark candidates, and broader exotic-hadron classifications.

questions.question: What minimal set of reaction-amplitude observables can discriminate molecules, threshold effects, diquark compounds, hybrids, and glueballs across the XYZ, pentaquark, and open-heavy spectra?
questions.rationale: This is the central unresolved classification problem summarized in [S1] and reviewed across heavy-quark exotica in [1] and [3].

questions.question: Which BESIII tau-charm measurements of XYZ states, proton-antiproton threshold enhancements, X(1835), and charm meson or baryon thresholds should be prioritized to resolve the current theory-experiment ambiguities?
questions.rationale: The specific BESIII opportunities are surveyed in [2], while the confused status of exotic spectroscopy is emphasized in [4].

questions.question: Why do confirmed multiquark candidates appear preferentially with heavy quarks, and what QCD principle explains the historical absence or suppression of comparable light exotics?
questions.rationale: This broad question is posed by the exotics puzzle in [4] and sharpened by the heavy-quark emphasis in [5].

node_df41470ceba0.summary: This cluster reviews charmoniumlike XYZ mesons, emphasizing B-factory discoveries, charged four-quark candidates, and competing molecule, tetraquark, and quarkonium assignments.

questions.question: What experimentally accessible pattern of masses, widths, quantum numbers, decay modes, and production environments can decisively distinguish hadronic molecules from compact tetraquarks among the XYZ charmoniumlike states?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from reviews emphasizing that many XYZ states do not fit the conventional c cbar spectrum and that molecule and tetraquark interpretations remain in conflict [1,3,5].

questions.question: Can heavy-quark symmetry and chiral dynamics predict undiscovered partners of X(3872), Y(4260), Zc, and Zb states with enough precision to make the molecular interpretation falsifiable?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review emphasizing molecular dynamics governed by chiral symmetry and heavy-quark symmetry and its predictions for yet-undiscovered exotic hadrons [2].

questions.question: How can QCD sum-rule calculations be made discriminating enough to separate conventional charmonium, molecular, tetraquark, and hybrid assignments for rapidly accumulating XYZ data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the QCD sum-rule review that presents concrete calculations for newly observed charmoniumlike states and compares them with other approaches and data [4].

node_101256b01f60.summary: These papers analyze Zc(3900), Zc(4020), and strange partners as near-threshold molecular resonances using coupled-channel dynamics, pole extractions, and flavor-symmetry arguments.

questions.question: For Zc(3900) and Zc(4020), can coupled-channel amplitude analyses locate S-matrix poles in the elastic channels with enough precision to distinguish genuine molecular states from threshold cusps?
questions.rationale: The pole-versus-cusp diagnostic proposed in [5] directly addresses the cusp interpretations of Zc structures in [2], [3], and [4].

questions.question: Which decay-channel correlations of Y(4260) into low-momentum D anti-D* pairs and J/psi pi spectra would falsify the interpretation of Y(4260) as a D anti-D1 molecule feeding a Zc threshold cusp?
questions.rationale: The molecular Y(4260) mechanism in [2] predicts unavoidable population of low-momentum D anti-D* pairs and a cusp at the D anti-D* threshold.

questions.question: Can the predicted visibility pattern of Zc structures in neutral and charged B decay modes be reconciled with a common coupled-channel description of the Zb and Zc candidates?
questions.rationale: The coupled-channel cusp model in [4] predicts that Zc signals should appear in some B decay charge channels but not others.

node_351cd05b66c8.summary: This cluster focuses on the internal structure and experimental line shapes of Zc(3900) and Zcs(3985), comparing molecular, tetraquark, hadrocharmonium, and threshold interpretations.

questions.question: Which combined measurements of Zc quantum numbers and decay rates into pi psi-prime, pi h_c, rho eta_c, and D D-star channels would decisively separate molecular, tetraquark, hadrocharmonium, and threshold explanations?
questions.rationale: This is the model-discrimination program proposed explicitly in [1].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel amplitudes constrained by lattice QCD determine whether the Zc(3900) enhancement is a genuine pole or a threshold cusp?
questions.rationale: The pole-versus-cusp issue is raised by the lattice coupled-channel result in [3] and the unitary line-shape analysis in [4].

questions.question: Do related charged or strange four-quark candidates follow the partner-state pattern expected from a D D-star molecular interaction, or the spectrum expected from compact tetraquark dynamics?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the predicted related four-quark states in [1] and the I=1 D D-star molecular analysis in [2].

node_bbe3e9ce6954.summary: These papers reinterpret several X and T structures near charm thresholds through coupled-channel molecular dynamics, triangle singularities, and threshold-cusp effects in B decays.

questions.question: Which elastic-channel line-shape measurement can unambiguously separate a kinematic threshold cusp from a nearby S-matrix pole for X(3872), Z_c(3900), and related near-threshold structures?
questions.rationale: [5] argues that a pure kinematic cusp cannot create a narrow elastic-channel peak, while [1], [2], [3], and [4] debate molecular, cusp, and pole interpretations.

questions.question: Can coupled-channel dynamics of D D*, D* D*, and D D1 thresholds simultaneously explain the masses, widths, isospin assignments, and production-channel dependence of Z_c and Z_b candidates?
questions.rationale: [2] links Y(4260) to a D D1 molecule and an unavoidable D D* cusp, while [4] models Z_b and Z_c candidates as coupled-channel cusp effects with channel-specific predictions.

questions.question: What decay-channel pattern in B decays or e+e- production would decisively distinguish an isovector molecular partner of X(3872) from a cusp generated by low-momentum open-charm pairs?
questions.rationale: [2] proposes molecular and cusp signatures for Z_c(3900), while [4] predicts where Z_c states should and should not appear in specific B decay modes.

node_4a2e3be61e24.summary: This cluster studies Zb(10610) and Zb(10650) as bottom-meson molecular states influencing Upsilon dipion transitions and bottomonium-plus-pion decay channels.

questions.question: What line-shape and phase information near the B B* and B* B* thresholds can distinguish true weakly bound Z_b molecules from kinematic cusp explanations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the competing molecular bound-state analyses and threshold-cusp explanation of the Z_b(10610) and Z_b(10650) peaks [3,5].

questions.question: Can the equal-amplitude spin-triplet and spin-singlet b bbar structure predicted for the twin Z_b states be tested through amplitude relations in Upsilon pi and h_b pi decay channels?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the heavy-quark spin-structure analysis predicting orthogonal spin mixtures and observable amplitude relations consistent with Belle data [1].

questions.question: Are the heavy-quark-spin-symmetry partner states with I^G = 1- observable in radiative Upsilon(5S) transitions, and what production rates would make this test decisive?
questions.rationale: This derives from the prediction of additional G-odd molecular bottomoniumlike states and the proposal to search for them in radiative transitions from Upsilon(5S) [2].

node_7b4978cc57ec.summary: These works use lattice QCD and Lüscher methods to extract charmed-meson scattering amplitudes, near-threshold bound states, and charmoniumlike resonances in coupled channels.

questions.question: Can lattice QCD determine whether the Ds0*(2317) is dominantly a DK bound state by extracting coupled-channel amplitudes with both DK and c-sbar interpolating fields at physical pion mass and controlled continuum limit?
questions.rationale: This follows from lattice support for a DK molecular interpretation through scattering lengths [4] and the below-threshold level found using both DK and c-sbar interpolators [5].

questions.question: How do heavy-quark symmetry and chiral unitary dynamics constrain the pole structure of charm and bottom scalar mesons, including the predicted BK bound state and broad-narrow partner pattern?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the heavy chiral unitary prediction of DK and BK bound states and broad/narrow charm-bottom scalar partners [1].

questions.question: Which finite-volume observables can distinguish near-threshold charmed-meson molecules such as X(3870)-like states from compact hadro-charmonium configurations?
questions.rationale: This question contrasts the low-energy universality interpretation of X(3870) as a finely tuned D0 D*0 molecule [2] with the hadro-charmonium binding picture for charmoniumlike resonances [3].

node_b06238663eea.summary: This large cluster systematically investigates heavy-flavor hadronic molecules, including X(3872), pentaquark candidates, doubly heavy systems, and open-charm exotic states.

questions.question: Which threshold-adjacent heavy-flavor exotics can be identified as hadronic molecules with controlled uncertainty by combining nonrelativistic EFT scattering parameters, finite-volume lattice spectra, and production and decay observables?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review's emphasis on controlled molecular predictions, finite-volume EFT/lattice tests, and production and decay diagnostics [1].

questions.question: Does one-pion exchange, including its tensor component, quantitatively bind the predicted B B*, B* B*, D D*, and D* D* deuson channels, or are channel-dependent short-distance counterterms essential?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the deuteron-like meson-meson analysis in which pion exchange alone binds bottom systems and places charm systems near threshold [2].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel chiral dynamics distinguish dynamically generated DK and hidden-charm scalar molecules from compact c sbar or multiquark assignments through DK couplings, isospin mixing, and pole trajectories?
questions.rationale: The question combines the DK-molecule interpretation of the 2.32 GeV state with the unitarized coupled-channel generation of open and hidden charm resonances [3], [4].

node_eaeaa4106caa.summary: These papers model heavy-meson molecular states with one-boson exchange, coupled channels, and heavy-quark symmetries across hidden-charm, bottom, pentaquark, and open-charm sectors.

questions.question: Can nonrelativistic EFT, finite-volume lattice spectra, and production/decay systematics be combined into a single uncertainty-controlled criterion for deciding when a near-threshold heavy-quarkonium excitation is a hadronic molecule?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which reviews molecular identification methods, nonrelativistic EFT in continuum and finite volume, lattice QCD, and production and decay diagnostics.

questions.question: How predictive is heavy-quark flavor symmetry across the charm and bottom sectors once short-range counterterms and pion-exchange tensor forces are fixed from X(3872), Z_b, and related thresholds?
questions.rationale: The question combines the one-pion-exchange deuson predictions in [2] with the heavy-quark-flavor-symmetry molecular multiplet predictions in [3].

questions.question: Which coupled-channel measurements involving heavy meson-meson, meson-baryon, and baryon-baryon thresholds would falsify the isospin-exchange molecular binding mechanism proposed for doubly-heavy exotic resonances?
questions.rationale: This follows from [4], which generalizes molecular-like isospin-exchange attraction to many doubly-heavy meson and baryon channels, and from the chiral EFT framework reviewed in [5].

node_acdb0942859d.summary: These papers use one-boson exchange, Bethe-Salpeter, and coupled-channel methods to test whether exotic X, Z, P, and heavy-meson systems can be bound hadronic molecules.

questions.question: Which heavy-meson molecular candidates remain bound when pion, scalar, and vector exchanges are varied within allowed couplings and cutoff ranges, rather than tuned channel by channel?
questions.rationale: The sensitivity to exchanged mesons, effective couplings, and cutoffs is explicit in the meson-exchange studies of [4] and [5].

questions.question: Can tensor forces from one-pion exchange alone explain near-threshold D D*, D* D*, B B*, and B* B* molecular patterns, or is short-range attraction unavoidable outside the bottom sector?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which finds pion exchange sufficient for bottom deusons but marginal or insufficient for many charm and light meson systems.

questions.question: What experimental test can settle whether the reported X(5568) B_s pi structure is a genuine four-flavor hadronic molecule, a different decay-chain effect, or not a bound state at all?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the narrow B_s pi evidence and possible B_s* pi interpretation reported in [3].

node_e627f5fb95af.summary: This cluster focuses on deuteron-like D, D*, B, and B* meson-antimeson or doubly heavy bound states, especially molecular interpretations of X(3872) and related exotics.

questions.question: Can a single one-boson-exchange framework with controlled short-distance cutoffs simultaneously describe X(3872), the Z_b(10610), Z_b(10650), and predicted heavy-flavor partner molecules without overbinding unobserved D^{(*)}\bar D^{(*)} and B^{(*)}\bar B^{(*)} channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the tension between robust pion-driven binding in bottom systems and cutoff-dependent meson-exchange predictions across charm and bottom sectors in [1], [2], and [5].

questions.question: Which experimentally accessible spin-isospin channels can most cleanly distinguish deuteronlike pion-exchange binding from additional short-range attraction in near-threshold D\bar D^*, D^*\bar D^*, B\bar B^*, and B^*\bar B^* systems?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the contrast in [1] between pion-exchange binding in heavy sectors and the need for extra short-range attraction in lighter systems, together with the channel-specific predictions of [2].

questions.question: How can coupled-channel analyses incorporate possible four-flavor structures such as X(5568) while remaining consistent with molecular binding expectations near heavy-meson thresholds?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the reported narrow B_s^0\pi^\pm structure in [3] and the molecular threshold systematics developed in [1], [2], and [5].

node_89155d9ab82a.summary: These works study possible molecular states formed from charmed or charmed-strange baryons, including hidden-charm pentaquarks, Xi_c states, and doubly charmed baryon systems.

questions.question: Which coupled-channel potentials and light-meson-exchange couplings are required to make Sigma_c anti-D*, Xi_c anti-D*, and Lambda_c N binding predictions simultaneously consistent with heavy-quark, chiral, and hidden local symmetries?
questions.rationale: The OBE and Bethe-Salpeter studies use heavy-quark, chiral, and hidden local symmetry inputs to predict hidden-charm and charmed-baryon molecular binding [1][2][5].

questions.question: Can S-D mixing and flavor coupled-channel effects produce a unified pattern of deuteron-like double-charm, strange hidden-charm, and charmed-baryon molecules with stable binding energies and RMS radii?
questions.rationale: The molecular calculations identify S-D mixing and coupled-channel effects as essential in heavy meson, Lambda_c N, and heavy-baryon deuteron-like systems [2][3][4].

questions.question: Is P_cs(4459) better described as one Xi_c anti-D* molecular pole or as a two-peak J^P=1/2- and 3/2- structure, and which Xi_c(*) anti-D(*) partner states must then appear?
questions.rationale: The P_cs analysis finds two Xi_c anti-D* molecular states with J^P=1/2- and 3/2- and states that a two-peak structure cannot be excluded [5].

node_dc8c18dda118.summary: This cluster develops broad effective-field-theory and symmetry-based descriptions of heavy-quark hadronic molecules and surveys how observed exotic states fit molecular spectra.

questions.question: Which near-threshold heavy-quark exotic states admit controlled molecular predictions with uncertainties small enough to distinguish them from compact multiquark interpretations?
questions.rationale: The hadronic-molecule review emphasizes that nonrelativistic EFT can make controlled predictions and identify molecular structures among heavy-quarkonium-sector discoveries [1].

questions.question: How accurately do heavy-quark flavor symmetry relations between X(3872), Z_b states, and predicted bottom or charm partners survive chiral corrections and finite-volume lattice effects?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark symmetry predicts partner molecules from X(3872) and Z_b inputs, while chiral EFT and lattice methods are central tools for heavy-hadron molecules [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: Can isospin-exchange binding produce a coherent spectrum of doubly-heavy meson-meson, meson-baryon, baryon-baryon, and baryon-antibaryon molecular resonances consistent with observed X, Z_c, and Z_b states?
questions.rationale: The doubly-heavy molecule survey generalizes molecular isospin-exchange attraction from observed X, Z_b, and Z_c states to many predicted heavy-hadron channels [3].

node_65cf81ba49b0.summary: These papers interpret recently observed Xi_c, Omega_c, Omega(2012), P_c, and Tcc structures as hadronic molecules and analyze their strong, radiative, or three-body decay signatures.

questions.question: For Tcc+, can the pole position be extracted model-independently only when pion exchange and the finite D* width are included simultaneously so that three-body unitarity is preserved?
questions.rationale: This question is directly motivated by [2], which argues that both manifestations of three-body dynamics are required for a self-consistent Tcc+ analysis.

questions.question: What additional DDpi spectra or charged partners can resolve the I=0 versus I=1 ambiguity of Tcc+ that cannot be inferred from the D0D0pi+ line shape alone?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which finds that the D0D0pi+ spectrum alone does not determine the isospin and predicts other DDpi spectra and triplet partners.

questions.question: For Ds0*(2317) and Ds1(2460), which ratios of isospin-violating strong widths to radiative widths would decisively test DK and D*K molecular assignments?
questions.rationale: This derives from the molecular decay calculations for Ds0*(2317) in [1] and Ds1(2460) in [4].

node_f6a6200c0202.summary: This cluster studies three-hadron molecular systems such as DDK, DKbarK, DDBbar, and related states using Faddeev, fixed-center, Schrödinger, and quark-model approaches.

questions.question: How robust are predicted DDK and DDDK bound states against uncertainties in the DK interaction that underlies the molecular interpretation of the Ds0*(2317)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the DK molecule assignment for the Ds0*(2317) and the later Gaussian Expansion Method prediction that DDK and DDDK systems bind robustly [1,5].

questions.question: Where does the fixed-center approximation to the Faddeev equations fail for three-hadron molecules whose dominant two-body amplitudes are strongly energy dependent or coupled-channel in origin?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in fixed-center treatments of multi-rho states and the KbarNN system, where two-body rho-rho or chiral KbarN amplitudes govern the multi-body result [3,4].

questions.question: Can quark-Born-derived low-energy hadron potentials and hadronic-molecule Faddeev calculations be reconciled into common criteria for when threshold enhancements become genuine bound states?
questions.rationale: This derives from quark Born diagram predictions of attractive KN-related channels and molecular calculations that identify bound or enhanced few-hadron systems [2,4,5].

node_4b3c33bedb94.summary: These works generate charmed, bottom, and hidden-charm baryon resonances dynamically from meson-baryon coupled channels constrained by chiral and heavy-quark spin symmetries.

questions.question: How can coupled-channel unitarization with heavy-quark spin symmetry be constrained well enough to distinguish genuine hidden-charm baryon molecules from model-dependent SU(4)-breaking artifacts?
questions.rationale: Hidden-charm baryon calculations include Dbar B, Dbar* B, eta_c N, and J/psi N channels required by heavy-quark spin symmetry, while earlier SU(4)-based models rely on explicit symmetry breaking [4][5].

questions.question: Which predicted exotic or crypto-exotic charm baryon channels have the most robust pole positions across vector-meson-exchange and chiral-symmetry-based interaction kernels?
questions.rationale: The crypto-exotic baryon study predicted strongly bound states from vector-meson exchange constrained by chiral symmetry and large-Nc considerations [3].

questions.question: Can open-bottom partners predicted by heavy-light chiral dynamics provide a sharper test of the same anti-triplet and sextet resonance pattern inferred from narrow open-charm states?
questions.rationale: The heavy-light chiral SU(3) analysis reproduced narrow open-charm states and predicted corresponding anti-triplet, sextet, and open-bottom resonances [2].

node_546c0fedc084.summary: This cluster applies QCD sum rules and interpolating molecular currents to estimate masses and properties of exotic charmonium-like, bottom-like, and B_c-like molecular candidates.

questions.question: What QCD-sum-rule criterion can distinguish a true molecular pole from a virtual state when pole dominance and OPE convergence lead to incompatible assignments for the same candidate, such as Y(4140)?
questions.rationale: This question is driven by the conflicting D_s^* D_sbar^* QCD-sum-rule interpretations of Y(4140), one matching the observed mass and another finding an inconsistent mass and possible virtual state [4],[5].

questions.question: How robust is the scale-setting prescription mu=sqrt(M_XYZ^2-(2 M_Q)^2) for hidden-charm, hidden-bottom, and doubly charmed molecular currents once color singlet-singlet and octet-octet currents are compared?
questions.rationale: This follows from the explicit use of that scale formula and current choices in QCD-sum-rule assignments of X(3872), Z_c, Z_b, and related molecular states [1],[2].

questions.question: Would observation of the predicted heavier isovector DD^* state provide a decisive test of the molecular QCD-sum-rule assignment of T_cc^+?
questions.rationale: This derives from the prediction that T_cc^+ is the lighter isoscalar DD^* molecule while a heavier isovector DD^* state remains undetected and would illuminate its nature [3].

node_104b10bd3f31.summary: These papers use chiral unitary coupled-channel dynamics to describe dynamically generated hadron resonances, compositeness, meson-baryon scattering, and related femtoscopic observables.

questions.question: Can higher-order chiral unitary coupled-channel analyses of Kbar N, pi Sigma, pi Lambda, eta Lambda, and K Xi data determine the Lambda(1405) pole structure uniquely, including Coulomb and isospin-breaking effects?
questions.rationale: This follows from the relativistic chiral unitary Kbar N treatment in [1], the DEAR-data reassessment with Coulomb and isospin breaking in [4], and the pole extractions in [5].

questions.question: What observables can distinguish dynamically generated axial-vector and meson-baryon resonances from preexisting quark-model states when both can appear as poles in unitarized scattering amplitudes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the pole and coupling analysis of dynamically generated axial-vector resonances in [3] and the resonance-content discussions of meson-baryon amplitudes in [1] and [2].

node_2d88d3ffe3dc.summary: This cluster centers on the Lambda(1405), especially its two-pole molecular structure, antikaon-nucleon dynamics, production reactions, and chiral-unitary interpretations.

questions.question: What combined chiral-unitary fit to kaonic hydrogen, hadronic Kbar N data, K- p -> pi0 pi0 Sigma0, CLAS photoproduction, and lattice-QCD levels can pin down the broad Lambda(1405) pole as well as the narrow one?
questions.rationale: This follows from the pole-structure analysis in [1], the reaction selectivity in [3], and the CLAS constraint on the broad-pole uncertainty in [4].

questions.question: How large are Coulomb and isospin-breaking effects in extracting the Kbar N threshold amplitude and the two-pole Lambda(1405) structure from precision kaonic-hydrogen and scattering data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the explicit treatment of Coulomb and isospin-breaking effects in the near-threshold Kbar N analysis of [1].

questions.question: Which lattice observables beyond the strange magnetic form factor, analyzed with Hamiltonian EFT, can distinguish an antikaon-nucleon molecular state from a compact quark-model Lambda(1405) or a threshold cusp?
questions.rationale: This derives from the lattice-QCD molecular evidence and Hamiltonian EFT analysis in [2], together with the near-threshold cusp criteria discussed in [5].

node_4ac9e2dfb381.summary: These works study meson-baryon, vector-baryon, and vector-vector interactions in chiral or hidden-gauge unitary frameworks to generate baryon and meson resonances dynamically.

questions.question: Which pole residues and channel couplings would decisively separate dynamically generated vector-meson resonances from states requiring explicit bare fields in chiral or hidden-gauge unitary amplitudes?
questions.rationale: Papers [1], [3], and [5] identify resonances through poles and residues in unitarized coupled-channel amplitudes.

questions.question: How stable are the predicted vector-vector bound and resonant states under variations of subtraction constants once the tensor states used for fine tuning are excluded from the fit?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] uses known tensor-state masses to tune subtraction constants for vector-vector loop functions, leaving the predictive stability of the remaining states open.

questions.question: Can inclusion of three-body channels such as pi-pi-N or additional vector-pseudoscalar channels shift the pole content enough to change the identification of low-lying axial-vector and baryon resonances?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] finds that the pi-pi-N channel has important effects in S=0 meson-baryon scattering, while [3] assigns axial-vector resonances from vector-pseudoscalar coupled channels.

node_6355020cd8dd.summary: This cluster uses femtoscopy correlation functions from high-energy collisions to probe meson-baryon, baryon-baryon, DK, Kp, Tcc, and strange-sector hadron interactions.

questions.question: How accurately must source functions, pair purities, and feed-down corrections be controlled before femtoscopy can determine the sign and magnitude of the Lambda-Lambda scattering length unambiguously?
questions.rationale: Lambda-Lambda analyses found strong sensitivity to scattering parameters, collective flow, pair purity, and feed-down from long-lived particles, with opposite scattering-length interpretations possible [1][5].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel femtoscopic correlation functions resolve near-threshold structures such as the Xi N opening or a possible H-dibaryon in Lambda-Lambda data?
questions.rationale: Coupled-channel calculations predicted detectable traces of the Xi N threshold and pronounced effects if an H-dibaryon lies close to or below it [3].

questions.question: Which collision systems and source sizes best suppress uncertain pi-Sigma source contributions in K-p femtoscopy while preserving sensitivity to chiral SU(3) Kbar-N dynamics?
questions.rationale: The K-p chiral SU(3) calculation found that larger systems are less affected by the pi-Sigma source function and better expose the underlying Kbar-N interaction [4].

node_70b7184eb4e1.summary: These papers develop wave-function, effective-field-theory, and Weinberg-relation methods to quantify the molecular two-body content of near-threshold bound states and resonances.

questions.question: Can compositeness relations based on pole residues be made probabilistic for broad resonances without losing invariance under the choice of channel basis or separable interaction parametrization?
questions.rationale: The resonance compositeness papers define complex compositeness from pole positions, residues, and Green-function derivatives, then propose positive-coefficient interpretations only under specific Laurent-convergence conditions [2,3].

questions.question: What minimal experimental input is sufficient to apply generalized Weinberg compositeness tests to higher partial waves and coupled channels in near-threshold exotic hadrons?
questions.rationale: The generalized wave-function framework extends Weinberg's condition beyond one-channel s-wave bound states to coupled channels, arbitrary partial waves, and resonances [1].

questions.question: How sharply can bound, virtual, and resonance pole locations distinguish molecular from compact hidden-charm states when the decay width is nonzero?
questions.rationale: The near-threshold pole analysis extends Weinberg's criterion to shallow virtual states and argues that the nature of physical states is encoded in pole positions and residues [4,5].

node_74b53950cc70.summary: This cluster compares molecular, charmonium, and mixed interpretations of X(3872), using radiative decays, hadronic decays, isospin breaking, and coupled-channel effects as diagnostics.

questions.question: Which combination of radiative transitions, J/psi pi pi modes, and D0 D0bar pi0 or gamma decays can decisively determine the molecular, charmonium, or mixed structure of X(3872)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the molecular decay tests in [3], the charmonium radiative and strong-decay diagnostics in [5], and the broader status of X(3872) interpretations in [1].

questions.question: How should coupled-channel pole residues be translated into statements about the long-range molecular component versus short-range structure of X(3872)?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the relation between scattering-matrix residues, channel couplings, and coordinate-space wave functions developed in [4].

questions.question: Can the observed isospin breaking in X(3872) decays be explained solely by the neutral and charged D D* threshold splitting, or does it require additional short-range charmonium admixture?
questions.rationale: This derives from the large isospin breaking expected for a deuson near the neutral D D* threshold in [2] and the short-range admixture model in [3].

node_7ce35da7089b.summary: These papers examine whether X(3872) is best described as a D D* molecule, a chi_c1(2P) charmonium state, or a charmonium-molecule mixture constrained by decay observables.

questions.question: Which combination of radiative transitions, open-charm decay modes, and J/psi pi pi or J/psi pi pi pi branching ratios can unambiguously distinguish a D0 D*0 molecule from a chi_c1(2P)-like charmonium assignment for X(3872)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed molecular decay tests and the charmonium-assignment program using C-parity and radiative transitions [3], [5].

questions.question: How should the near-threshold neutral and charged D D* coupled channels be used to infer the wave-function composition of X(3872), given that pole residues probe short-distance wave functions rather than channel probabilities?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the coupled-channel analysis relating scattering-matrix residues to wave functions and finding nearly equal couplings despite loose neutral binding [4].

questions.question: Can the observed isospin-breaking decays of X(3872) be reconciled with an dominantly I=0 state once the neutral-charged D meson mass splitting is treated dynamically?
questions.rationale: This derives from the deuson interpretation predicting large isospin breaking near the neutral D D* threshold while retaining predominantly isoscalar character [2].

node_7b6460eb1df2.summary: This cluster focuses on radiative and light-hadron decay channels of X(3872) as probes of its molecular, charmonium, or high-spin assignments.

questions.question: Can precision spectra in X(3872) to D0 anti-D0 pi0 and D0 anti-D0 gamma resolve the predicted interference pattern of neutral D* and anti-D* decays and thereby measure the molecular component's C parity and binding structure?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] identifies these spectra and interference effects as detailed probes of a dominant D anti-D* molecular component.

questions.question: Which ratio of radiative decays X(3872) to gamma J/psi and gamma psi' remains robust against short-range charmonium admixtures while still distinguishing a molecule from viable 2P or 1D charmonium assignments?
questions.rationale: Papers [3] and [5] both emphasize radiative transitions as diagnostic tests of charmonium versus molecular interpretations.

questions.question: Can the observed isospin-violating J/psi rho channel be quantitatively tied to the charged-neutral D meson mass splitting without overproducing other light-hadron decay modes?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] predicts large isospin breaking in a deuson picture because X(3872) lies at the neutral D anti-D* threshold.

node_749948e1ff9b.summary: These works model X(3872) and related states through coupled charmonium and meson-meson continuum components, emphasizing hybrid structure and threshold dynamics.

questions.question: What pole-residue and wave-function criteria can quantitatively determine the charmonium, neutral D D* molecular, and charged D D* components of X(3872) in a coupled-channel description?
questions.rationale: The coupled-channel residue analysis relates channel couplings to wave functions near the origin and found nearly equal neutral and charged D D* couplings for an isoscalar X(3872) [2].

questions.question: Which radiative, D0 D*0, and D Dbar decay measurements can decisively distinguish 1^3D2 or 1^3D3 charmonium assignments from a threshold-generated 1++ structure?
questions.rationale: Charmonium-threshold studies identified 1^3D2 and 1^3D3 candidates with prominent radiative and open-charm decays, while meson-loop models generate a D D* threshold structure in the 1++ wave [3].

questions.question: Can the observed X(3872) production rates and binding energy be reproduced only after explicit c cbar and D D* mixing, or do they still challenge a predominantly molecular interpretation?
questions.rationale: The molecule-versus-charmonium analysis argued that binding and production rates strain a pure molecule picture but may fit after c cbar and D D* mixing is included [4].

node_08f81886df5b.summary: This cluster studies X(3872) production in hadron colliders and heavy-ion collisions to distinguish compact charmonium or tetraquark scenarios from extended hadronic molecules.

questions.question: What production observable can decisively tell whether prompt X(3872) rates at hadron colliders are compatible with a loosely bound D0 Dbar0^* molecule rather than a compact component?
questions.rationale: This follows from the debate over whether the Tevatron prompt cross section is too large for a molecule and the NRQCD-based Tevatron and LHC production analysis [1],[2].

questions.question: Can high-multiplicity pp collisions calibrate the spatial size of X(3872) by comparing its suppression relative to psi(2S) with the established suppression pattern of excited Upsilon states?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the comover-interaction analysis of LHCb high-multiplicity pp data and its validation against excited-over-ground Upsilon suppression [4].

questions.question: In heavy-ion collisions, which transport input carries the clearest structural information about X(3872): its inelastic reaction rate or its thermal-equilibrium limit in the evolving QCD medium?
questions.rationale: This follows from the kinetic-rate transport treatment where the equilibrium limit is controlled by charm production and medium spectra, while structure information is encoded in the reaction rate [5].

node_05619c69e94b.summary: These papers analyze how triangle-loop singularities and threshold cusps can generate resonance-like structures in heavy-hadron decay invariant-mass spectra.

questions.question: What amplitude-analysis criteria can reliably distinguish an S-matrix pole from a threshold cusp or triangle singularity in heavy-hadron invariant-mass spectra?
questions.rationale: This follows from the warning that kinematical singularities such as two-body thresholds and triangle singularities can produce resonance-like peaks that may be misidentified as exotic hadrons [1].

questions.question: In Lambda_b to J/psi K- p, which observed or predicted pentaquark-like enhancements survive once all relevant anomalous triangle singularities, normal thresholds, and possible pole contributions are treated in a coupled analysis?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by ATS explanations for the Pc(4380), Pc(4450), and possible 4.5 GeV peaks [2], together with the special Lambda(1890) chi_c1 p loop whose normal threshold and triangle singularity merge near 4.45 GeV [4].

questions.question: Can triangle-singularity mechanisms quantitatively explain anomalously large isospin violation and narrow f0(980) structures in eta(1405/1475) decays without requiring two distinct nearby eta states?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the proposal that a triangle singularity between charged and neutral K Kbar thresholds explains the narrow f0(980) enhancement and the eta(1405/1475) puzzle [3].

node_9ac869590931.summary: This broad cluster covers quark-model, Regge-trajectory, Bethe-Salpeter, and related calculations of meson and baryon spectra across light and heavy flavors.

questions.question: How can quark-model predictions for higher charmonia, including E1/M1 transition widths and open-charm decay amplitudes, be systematically matched onto pNRQCD descriptions that include retardation effects and renormalon cancellation?
questions.rationale: This derives from the detailed higher-charmonium model predictions in [1] and the pNRQCD formulation of potentials, non-potential effects, and renormalon cancellation in [2].

questions.question: Which spectroscopy observables most cleanly separate conventional quark-antiquark levels, gluonic excitations between static quarks, and threshold-induced distortions in heavy quarkonium spectra?
questions.rationale: The question follows from pNRQCD results on gluonic excitations and heavy-quarkonium energies in [2] and the EFT spectroscopy program reviewed in [3].

questions.question: Can a unified hadron-spectrum framework connect chiral Goldstone-boson exchange in light and strange baryons with EFT-controlled heavy-quarkonium potentials without losing the successful multiplet structure of either sector?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the chiral constituent-quark description of nucleon and hyperon multiplets in [4] and the EFT treatment of heavy quark-antiquark bound states in [3].

node_f51d3ec76524.summary: These papers calculate charmonium and bottomonium masses, transitions, and strong decays using potential models, coupled-channel methods, and quark-pair-creation frameworks.

questions.question: Which combined pattern of higher-charmonium masses, E1/M1 radiative widths, and open-charm strong decay amplitudes would decisively validate or falsify current potential-model assignments?
questions.rationale: The higher-charmonia study tabulates these observables for all c cbar states up to the 4S multiplet specifically to guide experimental identification [1].

questions.question: How should pNRQCD matching incorporate short-distance potentials, ultrasoft retardation effects, and renormalon cancellation when describing quarkonium levels near open-flavor thresholds?
questions.rationale: Potential NRQCD defines the potential, treats non-potential effects systematically, and shows how static-potential renormalons cancel in the effective theory [2], [4].

questions.question: Can EFT-derived QCD Schrodinger equations in weak and strong coupling regimes reduce model dependence enough to connect charmonium spectroscopy, inclusive decays, and threshold production in one framework?
questions.rationale: The EFT review emphasizes pNRQCD equations governing quarkonium in both coupling regimes and applications to spectroscopy, decays, and electromagnetic threshold production [3].

node_c1a569bbb1b9.summary: This cluster focuses on higher charmonium spectra, open-charm strong decays, radiative transitions, and assignments of observed X and psi states.

questions.question: Which measured combination of E1 radiative widths and open-charm strong decay amplitudes would most sharply discriminate conventional higher charmonia from X,Y,Z assignments?
questions.rationale: The higher-charmonia study tabulated spectra, E1 and M1 widths, and open-charm decay amplitudes for c-cbar states up to the 4S multiplet [1].

questions.question: Can screened-potential mass shifts and coupled-channel pole definitions be reconciled into a unified assignment scheme for the Y(4008), Y(4260), Y(4360), Y(4660), and psi(4415)?
questions.rationale: Screened potentials lower higher charmonium masses and suggest assignments for Y states, while coupled-channel models define above-threshold resonances by complex poles [3,5].

questions.question: How do unquenched lattice-QCD transition form factors modify potential-model predictions for radiative charmonium decays above charm threshold?
questions.rationale: The lattice calculation computed charmonium radiative transition form factors in the quenched approximation, providing a QCD-based comparison point for model predictions [4].

node_4707ac175981.summary: These works compute two-photon, two-gluon, leptonic, and radiative decay rates of heavy quarkonia with relativistic, QCD, lattice, and factorization methods.

questions.question: What experimental pattern across leptonic, radiative, two-photon, and light-hadron annihilation widths would most clearly validate the NRQCD color-octet factorization picture for P-wave quarkonia?
questions.rationale: P-wave decay factorization expresses all four P-state decay rates in terms of perturbative coefficients and two phenomenological parameters including a color-octet S-wave component [2].

questions.question: Can full lattice QCD reach comparable precision for bottomonium and excited charmonium annihilation or radiative matrix elements as achieved for J/psi leptonic and J/psi -> gamma eta_c decays?
questions.rationale: The lattice J/psi calculation obtains percent-level tests for the mass splitting, leptonic width, and radiative decay rate using HISQ sea quarks [3].

questions.question: How large are relativistic negative-energy components in heavy-quarkonium two-photon widths, and can they be separated from perturbative QCD corrections in data?
questions.rationale: The relativistic Salpeter calculation finds negative-energy wave-function components important even for heavy quarkonia in two-photon decays [4].

node_d48a4a40588f.summary: This cluster studies heavy-quarkonium spectra and decay properties using Cornell, Yukawa, Hulthen-Hellmann, logarithmic, and other phenomenological interquark potentials.

questions.question: Which precision observable would most decisively test whether phenomenological quarkonium potentials or first-principles perturbative QCD better describe states near flavor threshold?
questions.rationale: This broad question is grounded in [1] on wave functions at the origin for near-threshold levels and [2,3,4] on perturbative and potential-model calculations of spectra and decays.

questions.question: Can wave functions at the origin used for production and leptonic widths be made consistent with O(alpha_s^4) or O(alpha_s^5 m_q) mass determinations in one uncertainty framework?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1] on wave-function inputs and [3,5] on high-order quarkonium spectrum calculations and heavy-quark mass extraction.

questions.question: How do the Lorentz structure of confinement, state mixing, and one-loop short-distance potentials jointly affect radiative and leptonic width predictions?
questions.rationale: This derives from [4], which studies spectra, radiative widths, leptonic widths, mixing, and the scalar versus vector nature of confinement.

node_655012d117c2.summary: These papers model charmonium, bottomonium, and related heavy quark-antiquark spectra and decay widths using Cornell-like, QCD-inspired, relativistic, and Bethe-Salpeter potential approaches.

questions.question: Which quarkonium observables still require phenomenological potential-model input once perturbative calculations reach O(alpha_s^5 m_q) for ground-state energies?
questions.rationale: The NNNLO ground-state calculation relates bottom and top quark masses to quarkonium resonance energies, while potential models continue to address spectra, wave functions, and decay widths [4], [5].

questions.question: Can wave functions at the origin for near-threshold c cbar, b bbar, and b cbar states be predicted with uncertainties small enough for precision production and leptonic-width calculations?
questions.rationale: Tabulated radial wave functions and derivatives at zero separation are essential inputs for quarkonium production cross sections and decay observables [1].

questions.question: How should relativistic corrections, one-loop short-distance potentials, and gluon-condensate contributions be combined without double counting in charmonium versus bottomonium spectroscopy?
questions.rationale: First-principles QCD evaluations and O(alpha_s^4) calculations include relativistic, loop, and leading nonperturbative gluon-condensate effects with different precision across bottomonium and charmonium [2], [3].

node_7068e85ab00e.summary: These works derive approximate or analytic bound-state solutions for phenomenological quark-antiquark potentials and apply them to heavy-meson mass spectra.

questions.question: Can analytic Bohr-Sommerfeld or shifted-large-N approximations reproduce not only Cornell-potential quarkonium masses but also wave functions at the origin and spin-dependent splittings with accuracy competitive with numerical Schrödinger solutions?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] derives analytic spectra and wave-function observables for the Cornell potential, while [1] and [2] rely on numerical or shifted-large-N treatments of spectra and spin splittings.

questions.question: How tightly can Cornell model parameters be matched to NRQCD quantities such as heavy-quark masses and S-wave matrix elements without losing the phenomenological fit to charmonium, bottomonium, and B_c spectra?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] calibrates Cornell parameters against N3LO NRQCD bottomonium predictions, and [5] connects Cornell S-wave quantities to NRQCD matrix elements.

questions.question: Which decay observables, such as digamma, digluon, and dilepton widths, provide the most stringent test of analytic quarkonium potential solutions beyond mass spectroscopy alone?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] computes both mass spectra and decay properties using Cornell wave functions, making decays a direct test of the potential solution.

node_564316c5ac9d.summary: This cluster develops and reviews NRQCD and potential NRQCD frameworks that connect QCD to systematic heavy-quarkonium potentials, scale separation, and high-order spectrum corrections.

questions.question: What observable in heavy-quarkonium spectroscopy would most decisively test whether pNRQCD's scale-separated potential plus retardation framework is the right organizing principle beyond short distances?
questions.rationale: This broad question is grounded in pNRQCD's definition of a QCD potential, systematic treatment of non-potential retardation effects, and applications in weak and strong coupling regimes [1,2].

questions.question: Can infrared-renormalon cancellation in pNRQCD be implemented with sufficient precision to reduce dominant uncertainties in quarkonium energy levels and decay matrix elements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the explicit statement that infrared renormalons affecting the static potential cancel within the effective theory [1].

questions.question: How consistently can short-distance coefficients, wave functions at the origin, and order-v corrections be matched between full QCD and NRQCD for S-wave leptonic and inclusive quarkonium decays?
questions.rationale: This derives from the two-loop leptonic-decay matching calculation and the correction of order-v^4 S-wave decay contributions [4,5].

node_7f73bd8bdbce.summary: These papers predict spectra, radiative transitions, and strong decays of bottomonium, bottom, and bottom-strange mesons to guide experimental assignments and searches.

questions.question: Which measured pattern of E1, M1, hadronic, and open-bottom decay widths would most cleanly distinguish conventional bottomonium assignments from unconventional components in newly observed states?
questions.rationale: This derives from model studies using spectra and electromagnetic, hadronic, annihilation, and open-bottom decay properties to discuss quark content and search strategies [3,4].

questions.question: How sensitive are B_c excited-state discovery channels at hadron colliders to disagreements among relativized quark-model predictions for radiative and hadronic branching ratios?
questions.rationale: This follows from the B_c spectroscopy work comparing models, estimating transition rates, and identifying promising Tevatron and LHC signals [2].

questions.question: Can NRQCD long-distance coefficients extracted from potential-model wave functions be made precise enough to give model-independent bottomonium and charmonium decay-width predictions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the NRQCD-formalism study that obtains long-distance coefficients from phenomenological potential models and uses them for Q Qbar decay widths [5].

node_63bffb0a1e97.summary: This broad cluster studies singly, doubly, and triply heavy baryon spectra using relativistic quark models, quark-diquark approximations, QCD sum rules, and chiral or hyperfine dynamics.

questions.question: Which missing spin-parity measurements of heavy-quark baryons would most sharply distinguish constituent-quark spectra with pseudoscalar Goldstone exchange from relativistic three-quark bound-state calculations?
questions.rationale: The chiral quark model explains light and strange baryon multiplets, while heavy-quark baryons are limited by missing spin-parity assignments [1], [4].

questions.question: Can functional Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter approaches, calibrated against lattice QCD, resolve the excitation spectrum and electromagnetic structure of heavy baryons?
questions.rationale: The relativistic three-quark review frames baryon spectra and electromagnetic properties as unsolved problems and emphasizes functional methods connected to lattice QCD [3].

questions.question: What mechanism explains parity patterns and possible positive-negative parity degeneracies across light, strange, and heavy baryon spectra within a single QCD-based framework?
questions.rationale: The baryon spectroscopy review highlights unresolved positive- and negative-parity degeneracies and the broader lack of understanding of excitation mechanisms [4].

node_e00ea8713c96.summary: These works seek quark-model descriptions spanning light, strange, charmed, and bottom baryons, emphasizing confinement, hyperfine forces, chiral dynamics, and relativistic treatments.

questions.question: Is a single constituent-quark Hamiltonian with confinement, Goldstone-boson exchange, and controlled SU(3)F breaking sufficient to describe light, strange, charmed, and bottom baryon spectra once spin-parity assignments of heavy baryons improve?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the chiral constituent-quark descriptions of light and strange baryons and the review's emphasis that heavy-quark baryons lack many known spin-parities [1][3][5].

questions.question: What observable pattern would distinguish chiral Goldstone-boson hyperfine dynamics from alternative relativistic three-quark or functional-QCD descriptions of the positive- and negative-parity baryon degeneracies?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the unresolved parity-degeneracy problem in baryon spectroscopy and in the competing quark-model and Dyson-Schwinger/Bethe-Salpeter perspectives [2][3].

questions.question: Can a unified quark-model treatment of meson and baryon spectra reliably flag which poorly established states are conventional quark configurations rather than glueball, hybrid, or multiquark candidates?
questions.rationale: This derives from the generalized constituent-quark model's use as a complementary tool for distinguishing conventional mesons from glueballs, hybrids, and multiquark states [4].

node_89e93bc26ef4.summary: This cluster focuses on relativistic Bethe-Salpeter, Salpeter, and quasipotential quark models for baryon spectra and electromagnetic properties across light, strange, and heavy sectors.

questions.question: Can a fully Poincare-covariant three-quark Faddeev or Bethe-Salpeter framework reproduce both baryon spectra and electromagnetic form factors across light, strange, and heavy sectors with kernels tied to dynamical chiral symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review of baryons as relativistic three-quark bound states and the covariant Faddeev calculation of the nucleon mass using meson-consistent interaction kernels [1,5].

questions.question: Which residual interaction, instanton-induced forces or one-gluon exchange, gives a more unified explanation of nonstrange and strange light-baryon hyperfine spectra once full Dirac structures are retained?
questions.rationale: This derives from covariant Salpeter studies claiming that 't Hooft instanton-induced interactions are phenomenologically favored over one-gluon exchange for nonstrange and strange spectra [2,4].

questions.question: How can relativistic three-quark bound-state models incorporate quark antisymmetry effects known from few-baryon systems while maintaining consistency with lattice-QCD current-mass evolution?
questions.rationale: This question connects quark-antisymmetry effects in one-, two-, and three-baryon systems with covariant three-quark results that compare well with lattice nucleon-mass evolution [3,5].

node_eadf947d7a39.summary: These papers review and apply constituent-quark models to hadron spectra, form factors, decays, and baryon classifications, comparing model systematics with experimental data.

questions.question: Can one construct a constituent-quark classification of poorly established meson and baryon resonances that simultaneously separates conventional quark-model states from glueball, hybrid, and multiquark candidates?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the meson-spectrum program of using constituent-quark fits to identify non-well-established states in [1] and the SU(3) baryon multiplet classification including two-star resonances in [3].

questions.question: Which observables in heavy-baryon spectra most cleanly discriminate color-hyperfine mass systematics from uncertainties in effective heavy-quark mass differences such as m_b minus m_c?
questions.rationale: The uncertainty budget in b-baryon mass predictions in [2] identifies the extraction of m_b minus m_c as the main limitation while finding potential and mixing corrections small.

questions.question: Can spectral-quark-model constraints on quark spectral functions be matched to effective hadronic Hamiltonians in a way that preserves chiral anomalies, Ward-Takahashi identities, and finite low-energy observables?
questions.rationale: This connects the spectral-function conditions and gauge-technique construction in [4] with the mapping from composite quark states to effective elementary hadron Hamiltonians in [5].

node_dfac22c4f118.summary: This cluster examines baryon resonances and heavy-baryon masses using quark-model, Faddeev, semiempirical, and experimental perspectives on the excitation spectrum.

questions.question: Which missing spin-parity assignments in heavy-quark baryons would most discriminate between constituent-quark Hamiltonians with antisymmetric LS forces and Faddeev solutions using flavor-dependent one-gluon exchange?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] emphasizes the lack of heavy-baryon spin-parities, while [3] and [5] make detailed quark-model and Faddeev predictions for low-lying heavy-baryon excitations.

questions.question: Can the positive-parity and negative-parity mass degeneracies in light baryon excitations be explained within unified quark-model dynamics, or do they point to missing degrees of freedom in the baryon spectrum?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] identifies parity degeneracy in light-quark baryons as an unresolved feature of the excitation spectrum despite quark-model successes.

questions.question: How should electromagnetic, photoproduction, and pion-beam data be combined to decide whether the high predicted density of quark-model resonances above 1.8 GeV corresponds to real but unresolved states?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] highlights the high-mass missing-resonance problem, and [2] stresses systematic studies with electromagnetic and strong probes as the route to identifying baryon resonances.

node_dbacbb934f6c.summary: These works describe light and strange baryon spectra through constituent quarks interacting via confinement and chiral Goldstone-boson exchange from spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking.

questions.question: Which features of the N, Delta, and strange-hyperon spectra most decisively test whether Goldstone-boson exchange, rather than another fine-structure interaction, is the effective remnant of spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking in baryons?
questions.rationale: Papers [1] and [2] attribute the successful unified light and strange baryon spectra to pseudoscalar Goldstone-boson exchange plus confinement.

questions.question: Can Faddeev and semirelativistic variational solutions of the same chiral constituent-quark Hamiltonian agree on all low-lying N and Delta states without retuning the confinement and pseudoscalar-exchange parameters?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] uses a semirelativistic variational solution, while [4] reports rigorous three-body Faddeev calculations for the 14 lowest N and Delta states.

questions.question: How far can the light-quark Goldstone-exchange picture be extended into charm and bottom hyperons before phenomenological flavor-exchange terms become unavoidable?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] describes C=1 hyperons by Goldstone exchange among light and strange quarks but adds a phenomenological flavor-exchange interaction involving charm to reproduce splittings.

node_ae44fcd6a20f.summary: This cluster studies baryons as quark-diquark systems, including heavy-baryon spectra, nucleon form factors, diquark correlations, and scalar or axial-vector diquark classifications.

questions.question: Which observed excitation pattern in doubly heavy baryons would most cleanly distinguish a heavy-diquark light-quark description from a full three-body treatment?
questions.rationale: The relativistic quark-model calculation assumes a light-quark heavy-diquark structure and predicts level inversion of p-wave light-quark excitations [1].

questions.question: How accurately can diquark-gluon form factors inferred from light-diquark wave functions be tested through excited heavy-baryon mass splittings?
questions.rationale: The heavy-baryon mass calculations include the internal diquark structure through diquark-gluon interaction form factors [2,3].

questions.question: Can Regge-trajectory and heavy-diquark heavy-antiquark symmetry relations predict a pattern of Xi_cc, Xi_bc, and Xi_bb excitations precise enough to guide experimental assignments?
questions.rationale: This is based on the use of Regge relations, heavy-pair binding, and mass scaling from heavy mesons to doubly heavy baryons [5].

node_69f5916eeac9.summary: These papers compute masses and properties of doubly and triply heavy baryons, especially with QCD sum rules and heavy-diquark interpolating currents.

questions.question: Can QCD sum rules, heavy-diquark EFT, and potential methods be reconciled into a common prediction for Xi_cc, Xi_bb, Xi_bc, and their hyperfine partners?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review of doubly heavy baryon spectroscopy using potential and QCD sum-rule methods and the EFT resolution of a hyperfine-splitting discrepancy [3],[5].

questions.question: Which production and decay channels at LHCb most sharply test the predicted doubly heavy baryon mass spectrum and lifetimes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the LHCb-motivated estimates of masses, production, decays, and detection prospects for baryons with two heavy quarks [2].

questions.question: Do chiral-doubling mass-gap relations established for heavy-light mesons have a controlled analogue in baryons containing two heavy quarks and one light quark?
questions.rationale: This extends the chiral-multiplet and chiral-doubling relations for heavy-light hadrons to the doubly heavy systems discussed with generalized heavy-quark methods [1],[4],[3].

node_fdc1cbffcb5f.summary: These papers examine whether parity doublets and chiral multiplet patterns in highly excited baryons and hadrons signal effective restoration of chiral and U(1)A symmetries.

questions.question: What experimental measurement would most clearly distinguish naive from mirror chiral assignments for positive- and negative-parity nucleons?
questions.rationale: This follows from the construction of naive and mirror linear sigma models for baryons and the proposal of experiments to distinguish the assignments [1].

questions.question: Do near parity doublets in highly excited baryons signal effective chiral restoration, or can they be explained by Regge dynamics with weak spin interactions and no restored Weyl-Wigner mode?
questions.rationale: This captures the tension between interpreting high-lying parity doublets as chiral restoration and the argument that linear equidistant Regge trajectories do not realize restored chiral symmetry [2,3,4].

questions.question: How does the nucleon mass in the chirally restored phase control meson-nucleon couplings, axial charges, and the N-N* mass splitting in competing sigma-model realizations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the finding that the chirally restored nucleon mass is the key quantity determining couplings, axial charges, and parity-partner mass splitting [5].

node_38b1aa426e20.summary: This cluster studies light and heavy mesons as quark-antiquark bound states using Bethe-Salpeter, Dyson-Schwinger, and relativistic quark-model frameworks to compute spectra and decay constants.

questions.question: Can relativistic quark models of heavy-light spectra determine whether P-level inversion is a robust consequence of the relativistic light-quark treatment or a model-dependent artifact?
questions.rationale: This follows from the relativistic heavy-light meson spectrum calculation, where the light quark is treated without expansion and different patterns of P-level inversion are discussed [5].

questions.question: What experimental set of open-flavor decay amplitudes and D/S ratios would cleanly separate scalar-confinement pair production from the phenomenological 3P0 decay model?
questions.rationale: This derives from the finding that scalar-confinement and one-gluon-exchange mechanisms can reproduce some amplitudes but differ significantly from 3P0 predictions in selected channels [4].

questions.question: How tightly can model-independent lower bounds on heavy-quark kinetic energy constrain wave functions used in covariant meson bound-state calculations and inclusive decay phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This is based on the derivation of a model-independent lower bound on heavy-quark kinetic energy and the analysis of Fermi motion inside hadrons [1].

node_f8909443a9ab.summary: These works use relativistic quark and potential models to calculate decay constants, spectra, and excited-state assignments for light, heavy, and especially B and D mesons.

questions.question: Can relativistic heavy-light quark models determine which measured excited D, D_s, B, and B_s states are radial versus orbital excitations using masses, P-level inversion patterns, and light-hadron transition widths simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows from the excited-state spectroscopy and transition-rate program in [2] and the relativistic quark-model treatment of orbital and radial spectra in [5].

questions.question: What model-independent constraints on heavy-quark kinetic energy and sum rules can be used to benchmark Fermi-motion inputs in inclusive heavy-hadron decay models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the QCD analog of Fermi motion and lower bound on heavy-quark kinetic energy in [1] and the heavy-quark-theory sum-rule and virial-theorem discussion in [3].

node_9fd383d4f7c7.summary: This cluster focuses on calculating pseudoscalar and vector meson decay constants, electroweak properties, semileptonic decays, and related strong-decay mechanisms in relativistic and light-cone quark models.

questions.question: Can a single relativistic or light-front quark-model framework reproduce pseudoscalar and vector decay constants together with V -> P gamma form factors across light, heavy-light, and heavy quarkonia?
questions.rationale: This combines the light-front calculation of heavy-meson decay constants and radiative form factors in [3] with the relativistic negative-energy-state corrections in [5].

questions.question: Which microscopic pair-production mechanism best explains open-flavor strong decays once S/D and P/F amplitude ratios and final-state interactions are controlled: scalar confinement, one-gluon exchange, 3P0, or 3S1?
questions.rationale: The scalar-confinement and OGE comparison in [1] and the amplitude-ratio tests favoring 3P0 over 3S1 in [4] frame this question.

questions.question: How do choices of confining potential and hyperfine interaction in light-cone wave functions propagate into eta-eta-prime and omega-phi mixing angles, charge radii, decay constants, and radiative widths?
questions.rationale: The sensitivity of these observables to harmonic versus linear confinement in a QCD-motivated light-cone Hamiltonian is studied in [2].

node_95e6c193f069.summary: These papers model orbitally and radially excited heavy-light mesons, especially B and D systems, using relativistic potentials to predict masses, wave functions, and hadronic transitions.

questions.question: What mass and width pattern of P-wave and radially excited D, Ds, B, and Bs mesons would discriminate between competing P-level inversion scenarios in relativistic heavy-light quark models?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the P-level inversion discussion in [4] and the use of excited heavy-light states for spectroscopy in [5].

questions.question: Can measured hadronic transition rates among excited and ground heavy-light mesons determine the chiral quark model coupling consistently with lattice estimates and known resonance widths?
questions.rationale: The need for this consistency test comes from the two alternative determinations of the effective coupling in [2].

questions.question: How strongly do heavy-quark kinetic-energy bounds, sum rules, and virial-theorem constraints restrict the wave functions used in heavy-light spectroscopy models?
questions.rationale: This connects the model-independent kinetic-energy bound in [1] with the heavy-quark sum-rule and virial-theorem discussion in [3].

node_01bc5481c40a.summary: This cluster applies coupled Schwinger-Dyson and Bethe-Salpeter equations to quark-antiquark mesons, including rainbow-ladder and beyond-ladder treatments of spectra and decay constants.

questions.question: Can a single symmetry-preserving 3PI-derived truncation quantitatively describe light pseudoscalar, vector, scalar, and axialvector mesons while resolving whether scalar and axialvector states require non-q anti-q components?
questions.rationale: This follows from the 3PI unquenching program in [1] and the finding in [3] that scalar and axialvector spectra are not well described as simple quark-antiquark bound states.

questions.question: What observable meson masses or decay constants can cleanly separate gluon-polarization unquenching, three-gluon-vertex dressing, and pion-cloud effects in beyond-rainbow-ladder Bethe-Salpeter kernels?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the cancellations and small-but-non-negligible unquenching effects reported in [4] and [5].

node_9948bba38ce7.summary: These works use Bethe-Salpeter approaches to compute ground and excited meson masses and decay constants across light, strange, heavy, and heavy-light quark sectors.

questions.question: What kernel improvements beyond the standard rainbow-ladder Bethe-Salpeter approach are required to describe scalar and axialvector mesons as accurately as pseudoscalar and vector mesons?
questions.rationale: Poincare-covariant Bethe-Salpeter studies describe pions, kaons, and vector mesons well but find scalar and axialvector spectra suggest more complex structure than simple q qbar bound states [2].

questions.question: How can analytic continuation of dressed quark propagators with complex conjugate mass poles be made numerically stable for mesons heavier than 1 GeV without losing confinement information?
questions.rationale: Confinement phenomenology studies show that quark propagator poles enter the integration domain during mass-shell continuation for heavier vector mesons and require special Feynman-integral techniques [4].

questions.question: Which low- and intermediate-momentum features of the effective interaction control exotic J^PC channels and heavy-light spectral splittings across quark masses from the chiral limit to bottom?
questions.rationale: The J=0,1 survey emphasizes each state's sensitivity to the long-range part of the interaction across quark masses, including exotic quantum numbers [3].

node_d79b590af883.summary: This cluster studies improvements to rainbow-ladder Bethe-Salpeter truncations through dressed quark-gluon vertices, pion-cloud effects, unquenching, and gluon self-interactions in light and heavy-light mesons.

questions.question: Can a symmetry-preserving Bethe-Salpeter kernel built from a dressed quark-gluon vertex quantitatively predict light-meson spectra once gluon self-interactions, pion back-coupling, and quark-loop unquenching are included together?
questions.rationale: Separate beyond-rainbow-ladder studies include non-Abelian vertex effects [2], pion back-coupling [4], and quark-loop unquenching in a 3PI-inspired truncation [1].

questions.question: Is the apparent cancellation between gluon self-interaction contributions and pion-cloud effects in the rho-meson mass a generic mechanism across vector and axial-vector channels?
questions.rationale: A nonperturbative cancellation between gluon self-interaction and pion-cloud effects was indicated for the rho-meson mass in [2].

questions.question: How can H-diagram and other two-particle-irreducible contributions be incorporated without breaking the axial-vector Ward-Takahashi identity or making the complex-plane BSE numerics intractable?
questions.rationale: The symmetry-preserving truncation framework exposes H-diagrams in the kernel [5], while beyond-ladder calculations require fully momentum-dependent complex-plane solutions [2][4].

node_b5ebfcea45ff.summary: These papers analyze excited charm and charm-strange mesons, using quark models and strong or radiative decay calculations to assign observed DsJ and related resonances.

questions.question: Which measured ratios of radiative to isospin-violating decays of D_sJ(2317) and D_sJ(2463) would decisively distinguish compact c sbar P-wave assignments from molecular or mixed interpretations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the D_sJ(2317) hadronic-versus-radiative decay analysis in [3], the radiative-transition test proposed in [4], and the molecular-state probes discussed in [1].

questions.question: Can strong-decay amplitudes, radiative widths, and spin-orbit/tensor mass relations jointly fix the P- and D-wave mixing angles of excited charm and charm-strange mesons?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the decay-amplitude and mixing-angle program of [1], the quark-model width calculations in [2], and the spin-orbit/tensor-force constraints in [5].

questions.question: Are tentative assignments such as D_J(3000) as a radial S-wave or orbital F-wave state stable once 3P0 decay-model uncertainties and radial-orbital mixing are propagated through all observed decay channels?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2], which assigns several observed charm states while explicitly leaving alternative assignments for D_J(3000) possible.

node_e6d4953ed974.summary: This cluster studies masses, strong decays, and radiative decays of charmed, bottom, and charm-strange singly heavy baryons in quark models, chiral approaches, and QCD sum rules.

questions.question: How can HHChPT couplings such as h2 and h10 extracted from Lambda_c(2593) and Sigma_c(2800) be reconciled with 3P0 decay-pattern assignments for P-wave and D-wave charmed baryons?
questions.rationale: This follows from the coupling extraction and nonresonant Lambda_c(2593) issue in [3] and the broad 3P0 analysis of S-, P-, D-, and radial charmed baryons in [4].

questions.question: Which radiative decay widths of singly heavy baryons are most sensitive to charm-quark magnetic-moment corrections rather than the two light-quark anomalous magnetic couplings of the chiral Lagrangian?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in [1], which separates gauged chiral interactions from anomalous magnetic terms and notes that charm-quark magnetic moments may be important.

questions.question: Which bottom-baryon masses and decay channels would most sharply discriminate among competing light-quark-pair dynamics once Sigma_b, Sigma_b*, and Xi_b inputs fix the model parameters?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2], which uses Faddeev solutions to predict bottom-baryon spectra and identifies states that can distinguish phenomenological dynamics.

node_babf970adc56.summary: These works focus on strong and radiative decay patterns of S-, P-, D-wave, and radially excited singly heavy baryons to determine their internal structure and quantum numbers.

questions.question: Which combined pattern of strong and radiative widths can unambiguously assign the internal quantum numbers of missing lambda-mode P-wave singly heavy baryons?
questions.rationale: This follows from constituent-quark-model predictions that many missing P-wave states are narrow and have diagnostic strong and radiative decay channels [5].

questions.question: Can HHChPT couplings extracted from Lambda_c(2593), Sigma_c(2800), and related channels remain consistent when nonresonant Lambda_c pi pi contributions and configuration mixing are included?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the extraction of h2 and h10 in HHChPT with nonresonant corrections [2] and by configuration mixing in singly heavy baryons [5].

node_d8da395b719a.summary: This cluster uses QCD sum rules and heavy-quark effective theory to assign masses, parities, and multiplet structures of excited charmed and bottom baryons, including Omega, Xi, Sigma, and Lambda states.

questions.question: Can QCD sum rules with derivative baryon currents unambiguously separate rho-mode and lambda-mode P-wave excitations in Lambda_c, Xi_c, Sigma_c, and bottom-baryon multiplets using both masses and decay widths?
questions.rationale: This derives from the systematic HQET sum-rule treatment of derivative currents in [4] and the light-cone decay analysis with rho-lambda mixing solutions in [5].

questions.question: What combined HQET and QCD-sum-rule treatment of 1/m_Q chromomagnetic splittings can predict charmed and bottom SU(3) multiplets consistently enough to discriminate competing light-diquark dynamics?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the model-discriminating bottom-baryon spectra in [1] and the HQET sum-rule chromomagnetic splitting analysis in [3].

node_c8ad2c1ea382.summary: These papers use Regge trajectories and quark-model calculations to organize meson and baryon spectra, test trajectory linearity, and predict excited hadron masses.

questions.question: Which observed anomalous meson or baryon states would most decisively falsify the assumption that radial and orbital Regge trajectories are linear, parallel, and approximately equidistant across light, heavy-light, and heavy-hadron sectors?
questions.rationale: This broad test follows from the trajectory linearity and parallelism claims for heavy baryons, light mesons, and heavy-light mesons in [1], [2], [3], and [4].
