questions.question: Can the low-mass nonlinearity of parent heavy-quarkonium Regge trajectories be traced to one-loop radiative corrections in the heavy-quark potential, relativistic dynamics, or state assignment ambiguities?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [5], which includes one-loop radiative corrections and finds nearly linear daughter trajectories but nonlinear parent trajectories in the low-mass region.

questions.question: Do the anomalous Ds0*(2317), Ds1(2460), and DsJ*(2860) masses require physics outside the relativistic quark-model Regge classification, or can revised trajectory assignments and slope relations accommodate them?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [4], where the heavy-light Regge analysis agrees with most data except these anomalous D_s states.

node_586a764fbfee.summary: These works investigate the possible H-dibaryon and related dibaryon bound states using lattice QCD potentials, spectra, finite-volume behavior, and extrapolations toward the physical point.

questions.question: Does the lattice evidence for a bound H-dibaryon at heavy pion masses survive controlled extrapolation to physical quark masses and broken SU(3) flavor symmetry?
questions.rationale: This follows from bound H-dibaryon signals in the SU(3) limit and at m_pi about 389 MeV, with SU(3)-breaking effects still central [2].

questions.question: Can HAL QCD potentials and finite-volume spectra be reconciled into a common determination of whether the H-dibaryon is bound, resonant, or unbound near the Lambda-Lambda threshold?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in lattice potential studies finding attractive flavor-singlet channels and discussing possible H-dibaryon resonance behavior above threshold [4].

questions.question: Are near-unitary strange dibaryon systems such as OmegaOmega experimentally accessible through pair-momentum correlations, and can they calibrate lattice methods used for the H-dibaryon?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nearly physical OmegaOmega lattice result predicting weak binding near the unitary regime and proposing pair-momentum correlations as a search channel [5].

node_fd6ae828b518.summary: This cluster studies pion-pion, pion-nucleon, and meson scattering amplitudes using chiral perturbation theory, dispersion relations, unitarization, and lattice QCD.

questions.question: How can chiral perturbation theory, dispersion relations, and lattice-QCD extrapolations be combined to reduce the remaining uncertainty in low-energy pi-pi threshold parameters and light-quark-mass dependence?
questions.rationale: This follows from the high-precision chiral and dispersive pi-pi analysis, including threshold parameters and quark-mass dependence for lattice extrapolation, in [2].

questions.question: What first-principles amplitude constraints are sufficient to make pole extractions for broad scalar resonances such as the sigma and kappa stable across unitarized chiral and N/D approaches?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the coupled-channel chiral pole generation in [4], the N/D treatment of scalar amplitudes in [5], and the Snowmass call for robust amplitude analysis [S2].

questions.question: Can chiral EFT for one, two, and many nucleons be connected quantitatively to meson-meson and meson-baryon scattering amplitudes within a common uncertainty framework?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the chiral dynamics of nucleons and nuclei reviewed in [1] and the broader EFT research framing in [S1].

node_7833da7e6032.summary: These papers apply finite-volume lattice methods to extract pion-pion and coupled-channel meson scattering lengths, phase shifts, resonance properties, and related multi-particle amplitudes.

questions.question: How can moving-frame finite-volume spectra be combined with coupled-channel Lellouch-Luscher factors to extract resonance and weak-decay amplitudes with controlled S-matrix constraints?
questions.rationale: This derives from the moving-frame generalizations of Luscher quantization and the multiple-channel Lellouch-Luscher formula, together with the Snowmass emphasis on first-principles amplitude analysis [1], [5], and [S1].

questions.question: Which finite-volume observables most robustly distinguish genuine resonance poles from parametrization artifacts when lattice spectra are available at several volumes and total momenta?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the use of finite-volume spectra to infer hadron resonances and the need for comprehensive amplitude-analysis methods constrained by QCD and S-matrix theory [3], [4], and [S1].

node_be71be5bf359.summary: These works develop quantization conditions and numerical frameworks connecting finite-volume three-particle spectra to infinite-volume scattering amplitudes for lattice QCD.

questions.question: Can the relativistic three-particle quantization condition be made numerically practical for realistic lattice QCD spectra with coupled two-body subchannels and moving frames?
questions.rationale: This follows from the three-particle finite-volume condition depending on both the two-to-two K matrix and a nonstandard three-to-three K matrix, together with moving multichannel two-body formalisms [5], [4].

questions.question: What is the three-body analogue of a Lellouch-Luscher relation that converts finite-volume matrix elements into physical transition amplitudes without analytic continuation?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the original finite-volume weak-transition relation and its multiple-channel two-body generalization [1], [3].

questions.question: How can exponential finite-volume corrections and partial-wave mixing be bounded well enough to extract infinite-volume three-particle amplitudes from finite cubic volumes?
questions.rationale: This derives from the two-body moving-frame field-theory treatment accurate up to exponential corrections and the three-particle extension of finite-volume spectral analysis [2], [5].

node_1273b3e1a7f5.summary: This cluster focuses on relativistic and effective-field-theory formalisms for extracting two- and three-particle scattering information from finite-volume lattice spectra.

questions.question: How can the nonstandard three-to-three K-matrix in relativistic three-particle finite-volume quantization be related most cleanly to physical three-body scattering amplitudes in practical lattice QCD analyses?
questions.rationale: The need for both the two-to-two K-matrix and a nonstandard three-to-three K-matrix is the central structural feature of the relativistic three-particle quantization condition [5].

questions.question: Can Lellouch-Luscher-type finite-volume matrix-element relations be generalized in a numerically stable way from coupled two-channel systems to three-particle final states with arbitrary total momentum?
questions.rationale: This extends the finite-volume weak matrix-element program from two-body decays [1], moving frames [2], and multichannel Lellouch-Luscher formulae [3].

questions.question: What finite-volume observables best separate genuine three-body interactions from two-body rescattering effects when extracting scattering information from lattice spectra?
questions.rationale: The issue follows from the all-orders finite-volume analysis in which three-particle energies depend on both two-body scattering input and an independent three-body quantity [5].

node_8b176b564837.summary: These papers compute two-nucleon and light-nucleus binding energies in lattice QCD while using volume dependence to distinguish true bound states from attractive scattering states.

questions.question: At what pion mass and volume precision does the lattice evidence for bound deuteron and dineutron states transition from heavy-quark artifacts to quantitatively reliable statements about physical nuclear binding?
questions.rationale: Existing calculations find bound two-nucleon and light-nucleus systems at pion masses near 390, 450, and 510 MeV using volume dependence to separate bound states from scattering states [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: Can boosted-frame finite-volume corrections reduce the dominant systematic uncertainty in lattice extractions of shallow two-body nuclear binding energies enough to resolve near-threshold states?
questions.rationale: The finite-volume formalism shows that binding-energy shifts depend on total momentum and exponentially on L relative to the bound-state size [4].

node_57d75473e06b.summary: This cluster uses Lüscher finite-volume methods and lattice QCD correlators to determine pion-pion scattering lengths, phase shifts, and related hadron scattering observables.

questions.question: How precisely can moving-frame finite-volume spectra determine pi pi S- and D-wave phase shifts at physical pion mass while controlling partial-wave mixing in cubic irreducible representations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the moving-frame generalization of Luescher methods in [2] and the variational extraction of I=2 pi pi S- and D-wave phases in [4].

questions.question: Can coupled-channel finite-volume quantization be made practical for pion scattering near inelastic thresholds using the same energy-level-to-S-matrix logic as two-channel scattering models?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the two-channel finite-volume relation to continuum S-matrix elements developed in [5].

questions.question: Do gauge-unfixed wall-source methods and disconnected-loop extensions reduce statistical and systematic errors enough to broaden pion-scattering calculations beyond channels without disconnected contractions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the wall-source method and its proposed gauge-unfixed extension to disconnected quark-loop contributions in [1].

node_219464e74132.summary: These works calculate low-energy pion-pion, pion-kaon, and other hadron scattering lengths in lattice QCD and compare them with chiral perturbation theory.

questions.question: What lattice volumes and source strategies are sufficient to extract reliable scattering lengths in channels with unnaturally large S-wave lengths, especially two-nucleon channels near the infrared fixed point?
questions.rationale: The two-nucleon work argues that rigorous nuclear information may be extracted from lattices smaller than the scattering length, while the wall-source method targets efficient scattering-length calculations [1], [2].

questions.question: Can complex antikaon-nucleon scattering lengths and the Lambda(1405) pole be determined on the lattice with controlled inelastic-channel systematics?
questions.rationale: The proposed lattice method generalizes Luscher's approach to inelastic channels and aims to locate the S-matrix pole associated with Lambda(1405) [3].

questions.question: Which low-energy hadron scattering lengths provide the cleanest test of unitarized chiral perturbation theory against fully dynamical lattice QCD as quark masses are varied?
questions.rationale: The heavy-meson Goldstone-boson study found that unitarized chiral perturbation theory reproduces lattice quark-mass dependence and can signal possible bound states [4], [5].

node_a8a4290d6e96.summary: This cluster develops and applies finite-volume quantization methods to extract elastic two-particle scattering phase shifts, especially isospin-2 pion-pion channels.

questions.question: How precisely can moving-frame finite-volume spectra disentangle S-, P-, and D-wave phase shifts when cubic irreducible representations mix partial waves?
questions.rationale: The moving-frame generalization of Luscher's method was built for S-, P-, and D-wave meson and baryon resonances at general total momenta [1].

questions.question: For isospin-2 pi-pi scattering, can variational operator bases in flight determine D-wave phase shifts accurately enough to quantify their contamination of S-wave extractions?
questions.rationale: The isospin-2 pi-pi calculation used large correlator matrices and moving multi-hadron operators to extract S- and D-wave phase shifts at many elastic kinematic points [2].

questions.question: What is the minimal finite-volume spectrum needed to reconstruct coupled-channel S-matrix elements for two-particle scattering in moving frames?
questions.rationale: The two-channel finite-box and torus formalisms generalized Luscher relations to coupled-channel S-matrix elements and discussed extraction strategies from discrete spectra [3], [5].

node_e812ab4a6472.summary: These papers determine rho-meson and related meson resonance parameters from lattice QCD calculations of P-wave pion-pion and coupled-channel scattering.

questions.question: How can moving-frame finite-volume spectra, large pi pi, K Kbar, and q qbar operator bases, and cubic-group irreducible representations be optimized to determine the rho P-wave phase shift at physical pion mass?
questions.rationale: This follows from the moving-frame Lüscher extension in [1] and the large-operator-basis rho phase-shift calculations in [3] and [4].

questions.question: What amplitude parameterizations constrained by unitarity and S-matrix principles minimize model dependence in extracting the rho pole and its small coupling to K Kbar from coupled-channel lattice spectra?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the coupled pi pi, K Kbar rho analysis in [4] and the Snowmass emphasis on first-principles amplitude analysis in [S1].

questions.question: How should lattice studies propagate finite-volume, discretization, pion-mass, and phase-shift-parametrization uncertainties into resonance masses and widths obtained through Lüscher-type analyses?
questions.rationale: This derives from the general resonance-from-lattice-QCD challenges in [2] and the extraction of rho resonance parameters from finite-volume spectra in [5].

node_45f577d77c32.summary: This cluster analyzes pion-pion and pion-nucleon scattering with chiral perturbation theory, Roy equations, dispersion relations, and unitarization to constrain low-energy amplitudes.

questions.question: What new low-energy pi-pi measurement or lattice input would most sharply test the Roy-equation claim that the S- and P-wave amplitudes near threshold are essentially fixed by a0^0 and a0^2?
questions.rationale: The Roy-equation analyses identify the two S-wave scattering lengths as the essential low-energy parameters controlling threshold behavior and higher partial-wave threshold parameters [1][5].

questions.question: Can unitarized chiral N/D methods and model-independent Roy-equation pole extractions be reconciled into a single uncertainty framework for the sigma, kappa, and a0(980) scalar resonances?
questions.rationale: This question connects the N/D chiral-unitary description of scalar meson-meson states [2] with the Roy-equation determination of the sigma pole without model parametrizations [4].

node_954e10c574f2.summary: These papers develop higher-order chiral perturbation theory descriptions of low-energy pion-nucleon scattering, including heavy-baryon, covariant, Delta-resonance, phase-shift, and sigma-term analyses.

questions.question: Can Lorentz-covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory with explicit Delta(1232) degrees of freedom determine the pion-nucleon sigma term consistently across Karlsruhe-Helsinki, George-Washington, and low-energy phase-shift inputs?
questions.rationale: This derives from the EOMS pi-N amplitude with Delta effects and comparisons among phase-shift solutions in [5].

questions.question: What dispersive or unitarized chiral framework best preserves the analytic structure of low-energy pion-nucleon amplitudes while connecting to resonance-region behavior?
questions.rationale: This follows from the success of dispersive and inverse-amplitude methods in meson scattering in [1], [2], and [4], and the analytic-property requirements emphasized for pi-N scattering in [5].

questions.question: Can chiral effective Lagrangians for pion-nucleon systems predict pion-nucleus scattering lengths and three-body pion-nucleon interactions with uncertainties competitive with modern low-energy data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the chiral-invariant calculation of three-body interactions among pions and nucleons and the pion-nucleus scattering length in [3].

node_ba21e4564bb5.summary: This cluster focuses on chiral perturbation theory calculations of pion-pion scattering amplitudes, scattering lengths, threshold parameters, and related low-energy pion production constraints.

questions.question: What new low-energy pi pi measurement would most sharply test the ChPT determination of S-, P-, D-, and F-wave threshold parameters against dispersive input?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that chiral symmetry plus experimental information fixes the low-energy pi pi amplitude with very small uncertainties [1].

questions.question: Can two-loop ChPT and lattice extrapolations jointly determine the O(p^6) low-energy constants without relying heavily on higher-energy pi pi scattering sum-rule input?
questions.rationale: This derives from the two-loop amplitude calculations, O(p^6) constant estimates, and the use of higher-energy sum rules to fix low-energy constants [3],[4].

questions.question: Where does the simple resonance-plus-current-algebra description up to 1 GeV cease to be a reliable substitute for systematic ChPT plus unitarity and crossing constraints?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the 1/Nc-inspired model that preserves unitarity and crossing up to 1.2 GeV using contact and resonance terms [5].

node_58d395987de7.summary: These works use heavy-baryon and covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory, often with explicit Delta degrees of freedom, to fit pion-nucleon elastic and inelastic scattering data.

questions.question: Can covariant EOMS baryon ChPT with explicit Delta(1232) degrees of freedom resolve the spread among Karlsruhe-Helsinki, George-Washington, and Matsinos pi N phase-shift inputs in the sigma term extraction?
questions.rationale: The covariant O(p^3) analysis with Delta effects fits multiple empirical phase-shift solutions and uses them to determine low-energy constants and the pion-nucleon sigma term [2].

questions.question: At what chiral order do the heavy-baryon and relativistic formulations give stable, mutually consistent threshold parameters and P-wave scattering volumes?
questions.rationale: Third-order work showed recovery of the relativistic Born-graph 1/m expansion in heavy-baryon ChPT, while later analyses studied P-wave scattering-volume convergence [3].

questions.question: Which subset of the many fourth-order pion-nucleon low-energy constants can be constrained by existing low-energy scattering observables without relying strongly on resonance-saturation assumptions?
questions.rationale: The fourth-order chiral pion-nucleon Lagrangian contains 118 measurable terms, while lower-order analyses used selected observables and resonance exchange to understand finite constants [5].

node_300ce80483db.summary: This cluster studies inverse-amplitude, Bethe-Salpeter, and N/D unitarization methods that extend chiral perturbation theory into resonance regions while preserving analyticity and unitarity.

questions.question: Which resonance pole properties are invariant under changes among N/D, inverse-amplitude, Bethe-Salpeter, and Chew-Mandelstam parameterizations once analyticity, unitarity, and chiral matching are imposed?
questions.rationale: T-matrix pole locations were found to be more stable than eigenphases under different pi-N parameterizations, while several unitarization schemes claim controlled analytic structure [2], [4].

questions.question: How can crossing constraints and left-hand cuts be incorporated systematically into coupled-channel unitarized chiral amplitudes without losing the phenomenological success in the scalar and vector resonance regions?
questions.rationale: The N/D construction neglects unphysical cuts, whereas the Bethe-Salpeter approach emphasizes exact unitarity with crossing constraints imposed order by order [1], [3].

node_0918f2e37d3a.summary: These papers build data-driven pion-pion and pion-kaon scattering amplitudes constrained by analyticity, unitarity, crossing symmetry, Roy equations, and forward dispersion relations.

questions.question: What new combination of threshold scattering-length measurements and high-energy input would most decisively test whether the Roy-equation allowed band in (a_0^0, a_0^2) is complete?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finding that the low-energy pi-pi amplitude is essentially fixed once the two S-wave scattering lengths and experimental input are specified [1].

questions.question: Do once-subtracted Roy-like equations reveal a genuinely unique S0-wave amplitude up to 1100 MeV, or do residual parametrization choices still dominate the uncertainty?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the stronger constraints from once-subtracted dispersion relations and the need for an improved S0-wave description [2].

questions.question: Which missing pi-K data below 1 GeV would most reduce the multiplicity of Roy-Steiner solutions and sharpen constraints on OZI-suppressed chiral couplings?
questions.rationale: The pi-K Roy-Steiner analysis found a narrow scattering-length region but noted that present below-1-GeV data are limiting [3].

node_0918f2e37d3a_1.summary: This cluster emphasizes Roy and Roy-like dispersion-equation analyses of pion-pion scattering, with extensions to pion-kaon amplitudes and precise low-energy parametrizations.

questions.question: What new low-energy pi pi data would most reduce the remaining allowed band in the (a_0^0, a_0^2) Roy-equation solution space?
questions.rationale: The Roy analysis shows that the two S-wave scattering lengths essentially determine low-energy pi pi amplitudes within a physically acceptable band [1].

questions.question: Can once-subtracted Roy-like equations up to 1100 MeV provide a stable bridge between threshold chiral constraints and resonance-region S0-wave parametrizations?
questions.rationale: The improved once-subtracted Roy-like analysis extends constrained pi pi amplitudes to 1100 MeV and requires improved treatment of the S0 wave [2].

questions.question: How should Roy-Steiner inputs above 1 GeV be optimized to reduce ambiguities in pi K S- and P-wave amplitudes and the resulting OZI-suppressed chiral couplings?
questions.rationale: The pi K Roy-Steiner study derives six equations to constrain OZI-suppressed chiral couplings and uses high-energy pi K and pi pi -> K Kbar inputs to obtain low-energy solutions [3].

node_a58160bb5b2a.summary: These works extract and interpret light meson resonance poles such as kappa, sigma, f0, a0, rho, and K* states from pion-pion and pion-kaon scattering using dispersive, Padé, and unitarized approaches.

questions.question: Can once- and twice-subtracted dispersive analyses further reduce the model-independent uncertainties on the f0(600), f0(980), and kappa pole positions when new pi pi and pi K data are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the precise pole extraction of f0(600) and f0(980) using dispersive pion-pion amplitudes and the Roy-Steiner proof of the kappa pole in pi K scattering [1,3].

questions.question: How can conflicting high-energy K pi scattering data above 1 GeV be resolved well enough to determine the scalar resonance spectrum up to 2 GeV within resonance chiral Lagrangian and unitarized frameworks?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the S-wave K pi analysis noting partly conflicting data and the need for better high-energy cross-section information to determine scalar masses and widths [2].

questions.question: Which low-energy chiral constraints, especially the I = 1/2, J = 0 pi K scattering length, are most decisive for stabilizing the kappa pole against model dependence in unitarized amplitudes?
questions.rationale: This derives from the result that the kappa resonance appears if the relevant scattering length remains close to the chiral perturbation theory prediction [5].

node_6e24b8fa317c.summary: This cluster analyzes pion-pion and pion-kaon S-wave phase-shift data from production reactions to identify sigma and kappa scalar resonances and their interference patterns.

questions.question: What model-independent analytic continuation strategy can reconcile Roy-equation sigma pole determinations with older interfering-amplitude fits to pi-pi S-wave phase shifts?
questions.rationale: This follows from the precise Roy-equation determination of the sigma pole and the earlier unitary interfering-amplitude reanalysis suggesting a sigma near 555 MeV [1], [2].

questions.question: Can the evidence for the kappa in K-pi scattering be put on the same dispersive footing as the sigma evidence in pi-pi scattering?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the kappa claim from K-pi S-wave phase-shift reanalysis and the model-independent sigma extraction from pi-pi scattering [1], [3].

questions.question: How much do a1-exchange contamination and polarized-target amplitude separation shift the extracted scalar-isoscalar pi-pi phase below and above the KK threshold?
questions.rationale: This derives from the polarized-target analysis showing that the a1-exchange amplitude cannot be neglected near 1000 and 1500 MeV [4].

node_9c433ad81ac0.summary: These papers use lattice QCD, especially the HAL QCD method, to derive baryon-baryon interactions, nuclear forces, hyperon interactions, and few-body nuclear properties from first principles.

questions.question: What first-principles benchmark would most decisively connect lattice-QCD baryon-baryon potentials to chiral EFT nuclear forces with controlled power counting and regulator uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This frames the relation between chiral two-nucleon potentials fitted to phase shifts in [1] and the EFT power-counting program summarized in [2], [3], and [S1].

questions.question: Can semilocal momentum-space regularization and the removal of redundant fourth-order contact terms be matched to lattice-extracted nuclear forces without spoiling long-range pion physics?
questions.rationale: This question is based on the fifth-order semilocal chiral potentials and unitary removal of redundant contact terms in [4].

questions.question: Where does the boundary lie between perturbative and nonperturbative nuclear interactions when QMC calculations use local chiral EFT forces through next-to-next-to-leading order?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [5], which uses AFDMC to benchmark neutron matter and tests when softer chiral interactions agree with perturbative calculations.

node_9b543821f26c.summary: This cluster examines how chiral effective field theory, power counting, renormalization, and lattice-informed EFT connect nucleon-nucleon interactions to nuclear binding and structure.

questions.question: What single comparison between lattice-informed nuclear binding, scattering phase shifts, and chiral EFT order-by-order convergence would most clearly settle whether current power counting is adequate for light nuclei?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question is rooted in the original chiral two-nucleon potential fit to scattering and bound states in [1] and the Snowmass emphasis on EFT development in [S1].

questions.question: Do semilocal momentum-space regulators that preserve long-range pion exchange lead to regulator-independent many-body predictions once redundant fourth-order contact terms are removed?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from [4], which introduces semilocal momentum-space regularization and eliminates redundant fourth-order contact interactions.

questions.question: Where is the boundary between perturbative and nonperturbative treatments of chiral EFT interactions in neutron matter and finite nuclei?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [5], where QMC benchmarks show perturbative agreement for softer interactions and systematic order-by-order convergence in neutron matter.

node_c1c24fb59e32.summary: These works focus on renormalization, cutoff dependence, power counting, relativistic formulations, and regularized chiral potentials for effective field theories of nucleon-nucleon scattering.

questions.question: What cutoff-variation and phase-shift benchmark would settle whether present chiral two-nucleon potentials are genuinely renormalized EFTs or regulator-dependent parametrizations below about 100 MeV?
questions.rationale: The original chiral two-nucleon potential achieved phase-shift fits up to about 100 MeV, while EFT lectures emphasize renormalization and power counting as the organizing principles [1].

questions.question: Can semilocal momentum-space regularization preserve the long-range pion-exchange interaction while producing order-by-order convergence and perturbative softness in two- and many-body forces and currents?
questions.rationale: The fifth-order semilocal potentials were designed to preserve long-range physics, simplify contact fits, and yield softer interactions extendable to many-body forces and currents [4].

questions.question: How should Bayesian EFT truncation-error priors be tied to naturalness and power counting so that degree-of-belief intervals expose missing counterterms or inadequate regulator choices?
questions.rationale: The Bayesian truncation-error framework makes uncertainty estimates depend explicitly on priors for natural EFT expansion coefficients [5].

node_da82cf3e591d.summary: This cluster reviews and develops approaches combining lattice QCD, chiral EFT, pionless EFT, and nuclear lattice simulations to ground few- and many-nucleon physics in QCD.

questions.question: Where do local chiral-EFT quantum Monte Carlo benchmarks and perturbative many-body calculations first diverge as regulator choices, cutoffs, and density are varied toward saturation density?
questions.rationale: This follows from the order-by-order AFDMC benchmarks and cutoff comparisons in [1] and [2].

questions.question: What lattice-QCD precision and computational scale are needed before extracted low-energy scattering amplitudes can become routine inputs to predictive few- and many-nucleon EFT calculations?
questions.rationale: The roadmap from lattice-QCD scattering amplitudes to nuclear physics predictions is reviewed in [3].

questions.question: Is the sign change of effective multi-nucleon forces in medium-mass NLEFT a regulator artifact, a missing higher-order force, or evidence for an essential four-nucleon interaction?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the NLEFT finding that an effective four-nucleon interaction approximates the needed sign-changing multi-nucleon contribution in [5].

node_4bf3905188c7.summary: This cluster centers on using the HAL QCD method and Nambu-Bethe-Salpeter wave functions to extract baryon-baryon and hadron-hadron potentials directly from lattice QCD.

questions.question: How rapidly does the HAL QCD velocity expansion converge for central and tensor nucleon-nucleon potentials near physical quark masses?
questions.rationale: The original HAL QCD extraction obtained central and tensor potentials at leading order in the velocity expansion and analyzed their quark-mass dependence [1].

questions.question: Can the imaginary-time NBS method eliminate ground-state-saturation systematics across coupled baryon-baryon channels, not only in the NN 1S0 benchmark?
questions.rationale: The imaginary-time NBS approach was introduced specifically to avoid ground-state saturation and was demonstrated for the NN 1S0 channel [2].

questions.question: Is the near-unitary NXi interaction in the spin-singlet isospin-singlet channel stable under improved physical-point simulations and alternative analytic parametrizations of the HAL QCD potential?
questions.rationale: The physical-point coupled-channel study found weak LambdaLambda attraction but a strongly attractive NXi channel near unitarity [5].

node_a7803cf3453f.summary: These papers develop and apply lattice QCD techniques to compute nucleon-nucleon, hyperon-nucleon, charmonium-nucleon, and three-nucleon potentials.

questions.question: How accurately can the HAL QCD velocity expansion of the nonlocal NN potential reproduce central, tensor, and three-nucleon forces as simulations approach physical quark masses?
questions.rationale: The Bethe-Salpeter-amplitude method extracts central and tensor NN potentials at leading order in the velocity expansion [1], while exploratory three-nucleon forces were computed at heavy pion mass [3].

questions.question: Can lattice-extracted two- and three-nucleon potentials be matched to chiral EFT low-energy constants with controlled truncation, statistical, and finite-volume uncertainties?
questions.rationale: Lattice studies define NN and 3NF potentials from QCD [1][3], while rigorous few-body analyses show that chiral-EFT truncation errors are essential for constraining 3NF constants [4].

questions.question: What lattice observables can determine whether quarkonium-nucleus binding is dominated by two-gluon scale-anomaly matrix elements or by confinement corrections beyond the heavy-quark Coulombic limit?
questions.rationale: Quarkonium binding in nuclei is exactly computable in the m_Q -> infinity limit from two-gluon operators, but J/psi binding may receive large confinement corrections [2].

node_1b29f8ace7df.summary: This cluster focuses on near-physical lattice QCD studies of strange baryon interactions, coupled-channel systems, and possible dibaryon states using HAL QCD.

questions.question: Can coupled-channel HAL QCD calculations at physical quark masses determine whether the attractive spin-singlet isospin-singlet N-Xi channel is truly near unitarity or supports an observable strange dibaryon signal?
questions.rationale: This follows from near-physical Lambda-Lambda and N-Xi lattice potentials showing weak Lambda-Lambda attraction but a strongly attractive N-Xi channel near unitarity [3].

questions.question: How large are the systematic effects from non-local potential truncation, finite volume, and omitted D-wave octet-baryon couplings in the near-threshold N-Omega dibaryon prediction?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the time-dependent HAL QCD extraction of an attractive N-Omega potential and quasi-bound state under the assumption of small D-wave octet-baryon couplings [1][2][4].

questions.question: Can hyperon-nucleon phase shifts from fully dynamical lattice QCD at heavier pion masses be continuously connected to physical-point HAL QCD potentials for strange-baryon interactions?
questions.rationale: This follows from fully dynamical hyperon-nucleon scattering calculations at pion masses of 350-590 MeV and near-physical HAL QCD studies of strange baryon systems [3][5].

node_dbf61f098344.summary: These works investigate the binding and structure of light hypernuclei containing Lambda, Xi, or charmed hyperons using ab initio, EFT, and lattice-informed interactions.

questions.question: How can lattice-QCD hypernuclear binding energies computed near SU(3)-flavor symmetry be connected quantitatively to physical-mass chiral EFT interactions for A<=4 systems with strangeness up to two?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the SU(3)-symmetric lattice-QCD calculation of light nuclei and hypernuclei [1] and the NLO chiral EFT hyperon-nucleon interaction with physical pseudoscalar masses [2].

questions.question: What hyperon-nucleon and Lambda-Sigma conversion terms are required to reproduce both s-shell charge-symmetry breaking and p-shell hypernuclear spectra in ab initio calculations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the no-core shell-model treatment with explicit Lambda-Sigma conversion in p-shell hypernuclei [4] and the revisited A=4 charge-symmetry-breaking binding differences [5].

questions.question: Can large-N spin-flavor symmetry reduce the parameter ambiguity in octet-decuplet interactions enough to make controlled predictions for hypernuclei and strange matter?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the large-N result expressing leading octet-decuplet interactions in terms of only two couplings and its implications for hypernuclei and neutron-star strangeness [3].

node_46a90e8ce7d2.summary: This cluster combines broad chiral perturbation theory with lattice and chiral analyses of nucleon, pion, and baryon sigma terms.

questions.question: What result would settle whether manifestly Lorentz-invariant baryon chiral perturbation theory is necessary for reliable sigma-term extrapolations near t=4 M_pi^2, rather than a repaired heavy-baryon expansion?
questions.rationale: This derives from the finding that the heavy-baryon expansion of the scalar form factor breaks down near threshold unless relativistic insertions are effectively summed [4].

questions.question: Which low-energy meson-baryon or nucleon-nucleus observables most directly fix the chiral low-energy constants needed for sigma terms while preserving Ward identities and chiral symmetry constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the broad ChPT framework connecting chiral symmetry, Ward identities, low-energy constants, and applications to mesons, baryons, nucleons, and nuclei [1], [2], [3], [5].

node_fc9447609d8f.summary: These papers provide introductory and review treatments of chiral perturbation theory as the low-energy effective field theory of QCD and the Standard Model.

questions.question: Where does chiral perturbation theory lose quantitative predictive control as it is extended from mesonic processes to one-, two-, and many-nucleon systems?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the review of chiral symmetry breaking implications for processes with one or more nucleons [1] and the meson-baryon scope limitations emphasized in the broader ChPT review [3].

questions.question: How can low-energy constants and renormalization prescriptions be made transferable across strong, electromagnetic, semileptonic, and nonleptonic weak ChPT applications beyond next-to-leading order?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the review coverage of strong, electromagnetic, and weak ChPT processes beyond NLO [3] and the EFT lectures on momentum expansion, renormalization, and weak transitions [5].

node_1d48696401f7.summary: This cluster studies nucleon and octet-baryon sigma terms by combining lattice QCD data, Feynman-Hellmann methods, and chiral extrapolations.

questions.question: What resolves the tension between Roy-Steiner and lattice determinations of sigma_piN near 59 MeV and direct chiral-fermion lattice results near 46 MeV?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the high-precision Roy-Steiner result and the physical-point chiral-fermion lattice calculation with continuum, volume, and excited-state corrections [1,5].

questions.question: Can a large pion-nucleon sigma term be reconciled with small nucleon strangeness in a way that is stable under SU(3) chiral extrapolation and explicit decuplet effects?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between large pi N sigma-term analyses implying implausibly large strangeness and covariant chiral perturbation theory showing that about 60 MeV need not conflict with small strangeness [2,4].

questions.question: How accurately can octet-baryon sigma terms be extracted from 2+1-flavor lattice baryon masses using low-order SU(3)-breaking expansions around the chiral limit?
questions.rationale: This derives from the octet-baryon mass analysis that used lattice results and a low-order SU(3) chiral expansion to evaluate sigma commutators for all octet baryons [3].

node_ec294084314e.summary: These works address power counting, renormalization schemes, and relativistic versus heavy-baryon formulations in baryon chiral perturbation theory.

questions.question: Can manifestly Lorentz-invariant baryon chiral perturbation theory provide a uniformly convergent description of sigma(t) through the two-pion threshold without sacrificing transparent power counting?
questions.rationale: This follows from the breakdown of the heavy-baryon expansion near t=4 M_pi^2 and the Lorentz-invariant remedy proposed for the scalar form factor [1].

questions.question: How do finite-subtraction renormalization schemes compare with infrared regularization for multiloop baryon observables such as the nucleon mass and scalar form factor?
questions.rationale: This derives from the power-counting-preserving relativistic renormalization scheme and its comparison with Becher-Leutwyler infrared regularization [2].

questions.question: Can octet baryon masses and pion/kaon-nucleon sigma terms fix scalar-isoscalar low-energy constants well enough to make decuplet-loop and two-loop corrections predictive?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the heavy-baryon analysis using octet masses and the pion-nucleon sigma term to constrain low-energy constants, including octet, decuplet, scalar-meson, and two-loop effects [3].

node_873075173758.summary: This cluster uses chiral effective theory to extrapolate lattice QCD results for nucleon masses, magnetic moments, axial couplings, and finite-volume effects.

questions.question: Over what pion-mass range do finite-range regulators provide regulator-independent chiral extrapolations of the nucleon mass once lattice data extend beyond the perturbative chiral regime?
questions.rationale: The convergence study compares dimensional and finite-range regularization schemes while matching to precise two-flavor lattice nucleon-mass data over varying quark-mass ranges [4].

questions.question: Can finite-volume corrections to the nucleon mass remain parameter-free at O(p4) when Delta(1232) degrees of freedom are included through the small-scale expansion?
questions.rationale: The finite-size analysis gives parameter-free O(p4) SU(2) baryon-chiral predictions, while the small-scale expansion provides the systematic formalism for including Delta interactions [1,3].

questions.question: What observable set can determine whether cloudy-bag-inspired extrapolation formulas for nucleon magnetic moments preserve the leading nonanalytic chiral behavior while correctly approaching the heavy-quark Dirac-moment limit?
questions.rationale: The magnetic-moment study proposes a compact formula that reproduces lattice data, leading nonanalytic chiral behavior, and the expected large-mpi Dirac moment behavior [5].

node_d375e3693ae7.summary: These papers apply unitarized chiral perturbation theory and related approaches to meson-meson scattering, light resonance generation, and mesonic low-energy constants.

questions.question: Are the sigma, kappa, f0, and a0 pole positions and widths stable under different unitarization choices once O(p^6) chiral constraints and coupled-channel data are imposed?
questions.rationale: The dynamically generated resonance poles in [1] and [3] raise the stability question, while [2] supplies the higher-order chiral operator basis.

questions.question: Can large-N_c trajectories of unitarized amplitudes distinguish molecular or tetraquark-like light scalars from q qbar states without the current ambiguity in the a0 channel?
questions.rationale: This follows from the large-N_c behavior of vectors and light scalars reported in [4] within the broader chiral-unitary framework of [5].

node_a1166d0c2f59.summary: This cluster emphasizes nonperturbative and large-N approaches to meson scattering amplitudes, dynamically generated resonances, and the nature of scalar and vector mesons.

questions.question: What observable feature of meson-meson scattering amplitudes most decisively separates dynamically generated light scalar resonances from conventional q-qbar vector mesons?
questions.rationale: This derives from coupled-channel chiral-unitary amplitudes generating scalar and vector poles [1,2] and the large-Nc behavior distinguishing vectors from light scalars [3].

questions.question: Can one-loop SU(3) chiral amplitudes unitarized by the inverse-amplitude method reproduce the same pole positions and scattering lengths as alternative coupled-channel schemes up to 1.2 GeV?
questions.rationale: This follows from the one-loop SU(3) IAM analysis [5] and earlier nonperturbative chiral coupled-channel fits to the same energy region [1,2].

node_30c462fa71bf.summary: These works construct higher-order mesonic chiral Lagrangians, analyze low-energy constants, and use resonance chiral theory to estimate their values.

questions.question: Can a process-organized minimal basis for the full even- and odd-intrinsic-parity O(p^6) mesonic chiral Lagrangian be turned into a global fit strategy that identifies which low-energy constants are actually measurable in current lattice and experimental data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the construction and redundancy reduction of the O(p^6) Lagrangians and the separation of terms by process complexity in [1] and [4].

questions.question: How stable are O(p^6) low-energy constant estimates when resonance chiral theory is constrained simultaneously by multiple short-distance Green functions rather than by selected channels such as VAP and SPP?
questions.rationale: This extends the resonance-matching program in [2] and the large-Nc lightest-resonance-plus-continuum construction in [3].

node_eacd52ed6b2f.summary: These papers calculate strong and electromagnetic isospin-violating corrections in low-energy pion, kaon, and pion-nucleon processes, including kaon decays and hadronic atom observables.

questions.question: What hadronic-atom measurement would most decisively fix low-energy kaon-nucleon or pion-nucleon scattering lengths once isospin-breaking corrections are included?
questions.rationale: This broad question is motivated by kaonic hydrogen extraction in [1] and pionic hydrogen energy-shift calculations in [4].

questions.question: Can modified Deser-type relations for kaonic hydrogen remain parameter-free beyond leading cusp-enhanced isospin-breaking corrections?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nonrelativistic effective-Lagrangian result that leading cusp corrections can be expressed solely through KN S-wave scattering lengths in [2].

questions.question: How can K to 3 pi cusp analyses combine analyticity, unitarity, and minimal theory input to extract a0-a2 at a precision competitive with other pi-pi scattering determinations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the cusp method for K+ to pi+ pi0 pi0 in [3] and the EFT framework respecting analyticity and unitarity in [5].

node_fca3f0b8a776.summary: This cluster studies the spectrum, mixing, decays, and internal structure of light scalar mesons using QCD factorization, chiral models, sum rules, and phenomenological analyses.

questions.question: What measurement would most clearly settle whether the sigma, f0(980), and a0(980) are primarily dynamically generated meson-meson resonances, distorted q anti-q nonet states, or threshold-dominated mixtures?
questions.rationale: The chiral coupled-channel approach generates scalar singularities from meson-meson potentials, while the unitarized quark model fits the same light scalars as a distorted 0++ q anti-q nonet with large K Kbar components [1,5].

questions.question: Can a unified description of light scalar amplitudes simultaneously enforce chiral symmetry, Adler zeroes, analyticity, flavor-symmetric couplings, and the observed gamma gamma decay widths?
questions.rationale: The representative scalar-meson analyses separately emphasize chiral constraints, gamma gamma decays, Adler zeroes, unitarity, analyticity, and flavor-symmetric couplings [1,5].

questions.question: How should scalar and pseudoscalar mixing schemes be matched to QCD current correlators and anomalies so that phenomenological decay constants, eta-eta-prime mixing, and chiral-restoration behavior are described consistently?
questions.rationale: The eta-eta-prime mixing paper uses axial-current divergences and the anomaly, while the hidden-local-symmetry framework matches current correlators to QCD through the operator-product expansion and tracks chiral restoration [2,3].

node_7ff1aedc35c1.summary: These works focus on whether states such as the sigma, f0(980), and a0(980) are conventional quark-antiquark mesons, tetraquarks, molecules, glue-rich states, or dynamically generated resonances.

questions.question: Can a single coupled-channel, chiral-unitary description quantitatively separate pole generation by meson-meson dynamics from pre-existing quark-antiquark seed states for the sigma, f0(980), and a0(980)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between poles generated from lowest-order chiral Lagrangians with one cutoff in [1] and a distorted quark-antiquark nonet with large K Kbar components in [2].

questions.question: What observable or pole-residue criterion can make Weinberg-type compositeness tests reliable for the unstable a0(980) and f0(980) near the K Kbar threshold?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the model-independent extension of Weinberg's compositeness criterion to unstable a0(980) and f0(980) resonances in [3].

questions.question: Can a two-nonet plus glueball chiral model reproduce both the precise dispersive sigma pole and the scalar spectrum up to 1.7 GeV without double counting molecular, tetraquark, and quark-antiquark components?
questions.rationale: This combines the dispersive precision on the f0(500) pole in [4] with the two-nonet-plus-glueball interpretation of scalar mesons below and above 1 GeV in [5].

node_d90984059e61.summary: This cluster gathers lattice, QCD sum-rule, and heavy-decay studies testing four-quark interpretations of light scalar mesons against spectra, couplings, and decay data.

questions.question: Can compositeness criteria for unstable a0(980) and f0(980) resonances distinguish meson-molecule dominance from compact qq qbar qbar or q qbar components using only pole positions and channel couplings?
questions.rationale: This follows from the generalized Weinberg compositeness approach applied to a0(980) and f0(980) to test whether they are elementary or governed by mesonic components [1].

questions.question: Do light scalar decay patterns require both diquark-antidiquark structure and instanton-induced six-fermion mixing with q qbar nonets, or can one mechanism alone fit masses and OZI-allowed decays?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the diquark-antidiquark nonet description and the later inclusion of an instanton-induced six-fermion interaction to improve scalar decay and mixing fits [2][4].

questions.question: Can lattice pseudoscalar-scattering calculations with dynamical quark loops and annihilation determine whether the non-exotic 0++ four-quark bound-state signal persists at physical quark masses?
questions.rationale: This derives from the lattice indication of a stable non-exotic 0++ four-quark bound state found while ignoring quark loops and annihilation and using sufficiently heavy quarks [5].

node_70b557f93c6f.summary: These papers use lattice QCD, sum rules, diquark models, and anomaly arguments to infer the quark, tetraquark, and gluonic components of low-mass scalar mesons.

questions.question: Can lattice finite-volume spectra with twisted boundary conditions distinguish a compact diquark-antidiquark scalar from a threshold-generated meson-meson state for f0(980) and a0(980)?
questions.rationale: This combines the tetraquark interpretation of light scalars in [1] with the proposed finite-volume and twisted-boundary diagnostics in [5].

questions.question: How universal is the threshold-coupling mechanism that relates Ds(2317), D0(2100-2300), and the light scalar nonet across strange, charm, and bottom scalar sectors?
questions.rationale: The unitarized meson model in [2] attributes Ds(2317) and the light scalar nonet to strong OZI-allowed coupling to nearby S-wave thresholds.

questions.question: Can instanton-induced six-fermion interactions and q qbar mixing be constrained independently enough to predict scalar decay amplitudes rather than merely fit the observed light-scalar spectrum?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] finds that instanton-induced interactions improve scalar decays and induce mixing with positive-parity q qbar states.

node_8f01a3eaa92e.summary: This cluster uses B, D, Ds, and phi decays involving scalar resonances to constrain the nature of f0(980), a0(980), sigma, and related light scalar states.

questions.question: Which decay observables in B, D, Ds, and phi channels can cleanly separate compact q qbar or four-quark components of f0(980) and a0(980) from meson-meson molecular components?
questions.rationale: The generalized Weinberg compositeness analysis was developed to decide whether a0(980) and f0(980) are governed by genuine quark states or mesonic components [1].

questions.question: Can QCD factorization predictions for charmless B decays to scalar plus pseudoscalar mesons be extended to a quantitative four-quark scalar framework without losing the successful explanation of large f0(980) K rates?
questions.rationale: Large f0(980)K rates were explained in a two-quark QCD-factorization treatment, while the authors noted the difficulty of making quantitative predictions in the four-quark picture [2].

questions.question: How can pole residues from dispersive pi pi amplitudes, two-photon couplings, and phi to pi0 pi0 gamma data be combined to determine the flavor, glue, and four-quark content of sigma and f0(980)?
questions.rationale: Roy-equation pole residues probe couplings to qbar q, alpha_s G^2, and photons, while KLOE and pi pi data were interpreted as evidence for four-quark sigma and f0(980) components [5].

node_34e9769111c4.summary: These works develop linear sigma models with chiral symmetry, vector mesons, and flavor mixing to describe scalar and pseudoscalar meson masses, form factors, and decay widths.

questions.question: Can a globally chirally invariant linear sigma model with vector and axial-vector mesons decisively determine whether the dominant q-qbar scalar nonet lies below or above 1 GeV?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the three-flavor global fit favoring scalar q-qbar states above 1 GeV [1] and the two-flavor test assigning f0(600) and a0(980) as q-qbar states [2].

questions.question: What is the minimal set of chirally invariant but nonrenormalizable effective operators needed for unitarized three-flavor pseudoscalar scattering to reproduce pi-pi, pi-K, and pi-eta data?
questions.rationale: This derives from the K-matrix unitarization study showing the renormalizable three-flavor model has the right structure but is not quite sufficient unless renormalizability is relaxed [4].

questions.question: How do vector and axial-vector mesons alter the extraction of nucleon and chiral-partner axial couplings and the chirally invariant mass term in mirror-assignment baryon sigma models?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the mirror-assignment linear sigma model where vector and axial-vector fields modify gA of the nucleon and N* and constrain the chirally invariant mass m0 [5].

node_3f93da8d50d5.summary: This cluster analyzes the sigma and related scalar resonances through chiral dynamics, coupled-channel meson scattering, pole motion, and phase-shift fits.

questions.question: Can coupled-channel chiral dynamics and dispersive analyses be unified into a single framework that preserves the precise f0(500) pole while also describing the f0(980), a0(980), and higher scalar pole structure?
questions.rationale: This question combines the chiral coupled-channel generation of sigma, f0, and a0 poles in [1] with the dispersive precision on the f0(500) pole emphasized in [2].

questions.question: Which features of scalar spectral functions are truly non-Breit-Wigner consequences of thresholds and subthreshold channels, rather than artifacts of a chosen separable-potential or Flatte-like parametrization?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the pole and bound-state interpretations in [4] and the non-Breit-Wigner and Flatte-like spectral-function behavior discussed in [5].

node_649563b78a66.summary: These papers organize scalar mesons below and above 1 GeV into mixed nonets, examining tetraquark, quark-antiquark, glueball, and unitarized interpretations.

questions.question: What coupled-channel data would decisively determine whether a0(980) and f0(980) are primarily distorted qqbar states with large K Kbar components or members of a four-quark light scalar nonet?
questions.rationale: This question reflects the competing interpretations of the sub-GeV scalars in the unitarized qqbar model [1] and the four-quark/two-nonet pictures in [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can a single effective chiral Lagrangian with two scalar nonets and U(1)_A-sensitive interactions reproduce the masses, mixings, and decay couplings of scalars below and above 1 GeV?
questions.rationale: This follows from the two-nonet plus glueball description in [2], the mixing mechanism between four-quark and p-wave qqbar nonets in [4], and the U(1)_A-motivated two-chiral-nonet model in [5].

questions.question: How do Adler zeroes, analyticity, and flavor-symmetric couplings constrain the amount of meson-meson versus compact quark substructure in the light scalar wave functions?
questions.rationale: The issue is grounded in the unitarized quark-model fit using two-pseudoscalar thresholds, Adler zeroes, unitarity, and analyticity [1].

node_2db5fd299166.summary: This cluster studies f0(980), a0(980), and related scalar resonances in heavy-hadron decays and isospin-violating mixing, often using chiral unitary final-state interactions.

questions.question: What precision treatment of rho-omega and rho-gamma mixing is needed for pion form-factor analyses to make e+e- and tau spectral-function inputs mutually consistent?
questions.rationale: This follows from the charge-symmetry-breaking role of rho-omega mixing reviewed in [1] and the claim in [2] that missing rho-gamma mixing reconciles tau- and e+e--based evaluations.

questions.question: Can dispersive three-pion final-state interactions and OPE-constrained odd-intrinsic-parity couplings replace phenomenological vector-meson-dominance assumptions in omega and phi decay amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the dispersive description of omega, phi -> 3pi decays in [3] and the short-distance constraints on odd-parity resonance couplings in [4].

node_7f6699535b3a.summary: These works model scalar-resonance production in Ds, B, and Lambda_c decays through pseudoscalar hadronization, coupled-channel rescattering, and f0-a0 isospin mixing.

questions.question: Which decay channel can provide the cleanest coupled-channel test of whether f0(500), f0(980), and a0(980) are dynamically generated meson-meson states rather than primarily quark-antiquark resonances?
questions.rationale: This broad comparative question is grounded in chiral-unitary scalar production in B decays [1], D decays [3], and benchmark a0-f0 mixing calculations [4].

questions.question: Can a unified chiral-unitary analysis of B, Bs, D0, eta(1405), and J/psi decays determine the primary hadronization weights and final-state rescattering amplitudes with enough precision to overconstrain scalar mixing?
questions.rationale: The question combines the hadronization-weight method in [1], the Cabibbo-allowed D0 scalar production in [3], and the eta(1405) mixing analysis in [2].

questions.question: What experimental resolution and background control are required to isolate the narrow a0(980)-f0(980) mixing peak from non-mixing mechanisms in J/psi to phi pi0 eta or related channels?
questions.rationale: This derives from the 8 MeV mixing-width signature and background estimates in [5] and the claim that a0-f0 mixing dominates isospin breaking near the resonance region in [4].

node_2d2f2f30318f.summary: This cluster examines rho-omega and rho-gamma mixing, vector meson dominance, and their impact on pion electromagnetic form factors and comparisons of e+e- and tau data.

questions.question: Can a single momentum-dependent rho-omega-rho-gamma mixing framework reconcile pion form-factor data from e+e- annihilation and tau decay without relying on constant mixing assumptions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the rho-gamma correction to tau versus e+e- comparisons in [2], the dynamical s-dependent HLS mixing scheme in [4], and the momentum-dependence constraint in [5].

questions.question: Which short-distance QCD constraints on odd-intrinsic-parity resonance couplings are essential for making rho-omega mixing and radiative-decay phenomenology mutually consistent?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the VVP Green-function OPE matching and omega to pion gamma predictions in [3] together with the vector-meson-dominance review in [1].

node_aaaf800d89f2.summary: These papers analyze J/psi and psi(2S) hadronic decays, emphasizing interference between strong and electromagnetic amplitudes, OZI effects, hadronic loops, and anomalously large relative phases.

questions.question: What measurement would most cleanly separate a long-distance amplitude that cancels the short-distance three-gluon psi(2S) decay amplitude from an intrinsic-charm explanation of the rho-pi puzzle?
questions.rationale: This compares the cancellation mechanism based on relative electromagnetic and gluonic phases in psi(2S) decay with the intrinsic-charm Fock-component explanation for J/psi and psi(2S) vector-pseudoscalar decays [4],[5].

questions.question: Can dispersive final-state-interaction methods for three-pion vector-meson decays be extended to charmonium hadronic decays strongly enough to fix the relative phases of electromagnetic, gluonic, and hadronic-loop amplitudes?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the dispersive treatment of omega and phi to 3pi final-state interactions and the anomalous amplitude-phase problem in psi(2S) decays [1],[5].

questions.question: How universal are OZI-violating effects across pbar p annihilation and J/psi -> phi pi pi or phi K K, once strange and non-strange scalar form factors and pseudoscalar rescattering are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: This follows from the channel-dependent intrinsic-strangeness interpretation of apparent OZI violation and the chiral-dynamics analysis of J/psi -> phi pi pi(K Kbar) using scalar form factors and rescattering [2],[3].

node_ed72e2206c7c.summary: This cluster studies eta and eta-prime mixing, axial anomaly effects, decay constants, gluonic content, and radiative or hadronic decay phenomenology within chiral and quark-model frameworks.

questions.question: Is quark-flavor-basis eta-eta' mixing with aligned decay-constant and state mixing genuinely process-independent across two-photon, vector radiative, J/psi, tensor-meson, and higher-spin decay data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the quark-flavor mixing scheme in [1] and [3], the process-independent parameter discussion in [2], and the broad phenomenological angle extraction in [5].

questions.question: Which decay observables best quantify possible gluonic content of eta and eta' while linking J/psi radiative decays, D_s enhancements, and glueball-candidate decays into eta eta' channels?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4], which connects eta-eta' mixing, axial anomalies, gluon-mediated processes, and glueball-candidate eta eta' decays.

questions.question: How should mixing with pi0 or eta_c be incorporated into eta-eta' phenomenology without introducing unconstrained parameters beyond the anomaly-fixed mass-matrix and decay-constant relations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the eta_c generalization in [1] and the discussion of mixing with pi0, eta_c, and other states in [2].

node_a9d2f2130624.summary: These works focus on extracting eta-eta-prime mixing angles, decay constants, and anomaly-driven constraints from two-photon, radiative, and meson transition data.

questions.question: Is the quark-flavor basis still the minimal process-independent parametrization of eta-eta-prime mixing once modern two-photon, radiative, and heavy-quarkonium decay data are combined?
questions.rationale: This follows from the quark-flavor decay-constant scheme proposed and tested in [1,3] and the process-independent mixing discussion in [2].

questions.question: What experimental pattern would unambiguously separate gluonic content in eta and eta-prime states from anomaly-driven quark-flavor mixing effects?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [4], which relates two-photon, radiative, J/psi, and glueball-candidate decays to electromagnetic and strong axial-current anomalies.

questions.question: Can the long-standing phenomenological range theta_P about -17 degrees to -13 degrees be sharpened without introducing convention-dependent mixing angles?
questions.rationale: This derives from the phenomenological extraction in [5] and the basis-convention issues emphasized in [2].

node_992c35c16d28.summary: This cluster examines eta and eta-prime decays into pion final states using chiral perturbation theory, dispersion relations, rescattering, and Dalitz-plot analyses to constrain light-quark mass ratios.

questions.question: Can eta to 3pi be turned into a precision determination of the light-quark mass ratio Q once Khuri-Treiman final-state interactions are matched consistently to two-loop chiral perturbation theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dispersive quark-mass extraction in [1], the rescattering corrections in [2], and the larger two-loop ChPT corrections in [4].

questions.question: Which measurements of charged and neutral Dalitz parameters, the neutral-to-charged rate ratio, and eta-eta-prime mixing most sharply test the residual theoretical uncertainties in eta and eta-prime hadronic decays?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Dalitz and rate predictions of [2] and [4] and the broader precision program for eta and eta-prime observables in [3].

node_660bdd3eb148.summary: These papers develop effective chiral descriptions of vector and axial-vector mesons, including hidden local symmetry, SU(3) breaking, loop corrections, and vector manifestation near chiral restoration.

questions.question: Is hidden local symmetry with vector manifestation the right effective paradigm for chiral restoration, or does its success depend too strongly on Wilsonian matching choices and quadratic divergences?
questions.rationale: This broad question derives from the loop-level HLS construction, Wilsonian matching, and chiral-restoration behavior in [1].

questions.question: What experimental observable in hot QCD can separate local parity-odd pion asymmetries from conventional reaction-plane correlations in heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed pion charge asymmetry with respect to the reaction plane in [2] and the observable construction in [3].

questions.question: Can one chiral SU(3) vector-meson Lagrangian consistently describe pion and kaon electromagnetic form factors, anomalous decays, and rho-omega-phi mixing without ad hoc vector-meson-dominance assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the effective-Lagrangian description of vector meson structure, decays, form factors, and mixing in [5].

node_e6bb554c0252.summary: This cluster studies radiative rho and phi decays and related photon-induced meson reactions as probes of light scalar mesons, final-state interactions, and scalar mixing.

questions.question: Which radiative phi decay observable most directly distinguishes compact four-quark, K Kbar molecular, and s sbar interpretations of f0(980) and a0(980)?
questions.rationale: This derives from the several-orders-of-magnitude model spread in phi to scalar gamma branching ratios and scalar-structure discussion in [1] and [3].

questions.question: Can a chiral-unitary treatment of final-state interactions predict the pi pi and pi eta invariant-mass spectra in rho and phi radiative decays without tuning scalar resonance shapes channel by channel?
questions.rationale: This follows from the chiral-unitary calculation where kaonic loops generate the f0(980) peak in phi radiative decay in [4].

questions.question: How tightly can gamma gamma to meson-pair amplitude analyses constrain scalar radiative couplings when angular coverage and polarization information are incomplete?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the near model-independent amplitude analysis imposing analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry in [5].

node_de659a3fd52f.summary: These works focus on phi radiative decays into kaon, pion, and eta channels to identify the roles of f0(980), a0(980), and sigma-like scalar resonances.

questions.question: Which measured photon-energy and invariant-mass distributions in phi to gamma pi pi and phi to gamma pi eta can decisively distinguish four-quark, K Kbar molecule, and two-quark assignments of f0(980) and a0(980)?
questions.rationale: This follows from the large model spread in phi to S gamma branching predictions and the explicit comparison of scalar-structure models in radiative phi decays [1],[3],[5].

questions.question: How reliably can chiral-unitary final-state interactions and kaonic-loop mechanisms reproduce both the f0(980) peak in pi pi spectra and the a0(980) signal in pi eta spectra?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the chiral-unitary calculation of phi radiative decays through kaonic loops and the interference analysis favoring one-loop production mechanisms [4],[5].

questions.question: Can gauge-invariant radiative-decay formalisms developed for axial-vector mesons constrain the model dependence in scalar radiative production at phi factories?
questions.rationale: This question extends the hidden-gauge formalism's explicit treatment of gauge invariance in radiative meson decays to the model-dependence problem emphasized for scalar phi radiative decays [1],[2].

node_c818e7118c2e.summary: This cluster analyzes gamma-gamma to meson-meson reactions, especially pi-pi and pi-eta channels, to extract scalar and tensor resonance properties and two-photon widths.

questions.question: What additional polarization or angular-coverage information is needed to make gamma gamma to pi pi and KK partial-wave amplitudes below 1.5 GeV genuinely model independent?
questions.rationale: The comprehensive amplitude analysis imposes analyticity, unitarity, and crossing to compensate for limited angular coverage and absent polarization information [1].

questions.question: Can two-photon widths of f0, sigma, and a0 states distinguish quark-model, molecule, and dynamically generated pole interpretations once final-state interactions are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: Two-photon scalar studies use gamma gamma to pi pi data as structural probes, while the unified meson-meson analysis shows that final-state interactions are essential, especially in the L=0 channel [3,4].

questions.question: How can radiative couplings extracted from pole residues in gamma pi to pi pi be cross-validated against vector-meson-dominance estimates for rho and rho3 contributions?
questions.rationale: The radiative-coupling study develops a pole-residue method for the rho and compares the rho3 radiative width to a vector-meson-dominance estimate [5].

node_eb9bb8e2a7bc.summary: These papers apply standard and extended Nambu-Jona-Lasinio models to tau decays and electron-positron annihilation involving pseudoscalar, vector, scalar, and excited meson intermediate states.

questions.question: Can a single nonlocal NJL form-factor scheme simultaneously reproduce radial excitation spectra, weak decay constants, and tau decay amplitudes involving pseudoscalar, vector, and scalar intermediate states?
questions.rationale: The extended NJL papers use related separable nonlocal form factors for excited pion, rho, omega, scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector nonets, while tau decays require coordinated intermediate-state dynamics [1], [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: How robust is the predicted smallness of the excited-pion leptonic decay constant once finite pion mass effects and the fitted pi-prime mass range are propagated into tau decay observables?
questions.rationale: The chiral Lagrangian for excited pions finds f_pi-prime vanishes in the chiral limit but studies finite pion masses and pi-prime masses from 750 to 1300 MeV [1].

questions.question: Can the u-d quark-mass-difference mechanism for suppressed tau to eta pi nu and eta-prime pi nu decays be cleanly separated from uncertainties in a0, rho(770), and rho(1450) intermediate-state modeling?
questions.rationale: The NJL calculation attributes these suppressed tau modes to the u-d quark mass difference while explicitly including scalar and vector intermediate states [5].

node_a0a898b975fc.summary: This broad baryon cluster covers large-Nc expansions, chiral approaches, Skyrme and quark models, and QCD sum rules for baryon spectra, masses, magnetic moments, and heavy-baryon properties.

questions.question: What experimental or lattice-QCD result would most clearly settle whether the exotic anti-decuplet predicted by chiral soliton models corresponds to real baryon spectroscopy?
questions.rationale: This broad question derives from the chiral-soliton prediction of a narrow exotic Z+ baryon near 1530 MeV and the statement that this mass region had avoided thorough searches [1].

questions.question: How far can large-Nc spin-flavor relations for baryon masses, axial couplings, magnetic moments, and SU(3) breaking be pushed before subleading corrections erase their predictive power?
questions.rationale: The 1/Nc expansion predicts baryon coupling ratios, masses, and magnetic moments with constrained SU(3) breaking [2], while quark-operator reduction rules systematize these observables at and beyond the SU(3) limit [4].

questions.question: Can the Skyrme, quark-operator, and NJL chiral-soliton descriptions be matched into a common operator basis for baryon structure observables?
questions.rationale: The connection between Skyrme and quark representations is made through all-orders operator relations [4], while NJL chiral quark solitons describe baryons with valence quarks and a polarized Dirac sea [3].

node_9e355df32c24.summary: These works calculate octet, decuplet, and heavy-baryon magnetic moments using chiral perturbation theory, chiral quark models, unquenched quark models, and light-cone QCD sum rules.

questions.question: What pattern in octet and decuplet magnetic moments would most cleanly reveal spin-dependent forces rather than quark-mass effects in baryon electromagnetic structure?
questions.rationale: This derives from the lattice decuplet study in [1], which finds opposing spin-dependent and mass effects in charge radii and baryon-dependent effective quark magnetic moments.

questions.question: Can chiral perturbation theory with octet and decuplet intermediate states produce a stable description of baryon magnetic moments once axial couplings are fixed consistently at one loop?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [2], where decuplet loop effects do not cancel octet effects and the quality of magnetic-moment fits depends strongly on the axial couplings used.

questions.question: How should quenched and unquenched lattice results for baryon magnetic moments be extrapolated when quenching changes the nonanalytic pion-mass dependence?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the quenched baryon chiral perturbation theory result in [4] that quenching modifies nonanalytic mass terms.

node_2163f3ceba15.summary: This cluster concentrates on chiral and quark-model treatments of octet and decuplet baryon magnetic moments, including sea-quark polarization, orbital effects, and SU(3)-breaking corrections.

questions.question: Why do covariant EOMS SU(3) chiral loops improve baryon magnetic-moment fits while heavy-baryon and infrared schemes struggle at leading SU(3)-breaking order?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between the EOMS improvement in [3] and the problematic lower-order chiral fits discussed in [2].

questions.question: Can lattice-QCD determinations of octet and decuplet magnetic moments, radii, and E2/M3 moments disentangle spin-dependent forces from quark-mass effects in chiral extrapolations?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the lattice decuplet study identifying spin-dependent forces, mass effects, and preliminary shape-sensitive E2 and M3 moments [1].

questions.question: Which magnetic-moment relations survive a simultaneous expansion in m_s and 1/N once q^4 counterterms and decuplet intermediate states are included?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nonanalytic decuplet-loop effects in [2], the q^4 counterterm fit in [4], and the m_s plus 1/N relation analysis in [5].

node_917d7eec7d34.summary: These papers compute octet and decuplet baryon magnetic moments in chiral perturbation theory, emphasizing SU(3)-breaking, loop effects, decuplet contributions, and lattice-QCD comparisons.

questions.question: Can covariant EOMS chiral perturbation theory with explicit decuplet intermediate states produce a convergent simultaneous description of octet and decuplet magnetic moments and lattice form factors?
questions.rationale: EOMS improves leading SU(3)-breaking fits in [3], while decuplet structure and M1 form factors are extracted from lattice QCD in [1].

questions.question: Which combination of q^4 counterterms and nonanalytic m_q^{1/2}, m_q ln m_q loop effects is required to preserve predictive magnetic-moment relations beyond the Coleman-Glashow limit?
questions.rationale: Large nonanalytic loop corrections and decuplet contributions are studied in [2], while q^4 counterterms restore fits with natural couplings in [4].

questions.question: Can a combined 1/N and m_s expansion explain why observed octet and decuplet magnetic-moment relations work while some SU(3) chiral loop fits fail at low order?
questions.rationale: The simultaneous 1/N and m_s expansion in [5] yields successful relations, whereas [2] reports poor fits for some one-loop axial-coupling inputs.

node_92c82cd077b8.summary: This cluster uses chiral, soliton, constituent, relativistic, and unquenched quark models to describe octet and decuplet baryon magnetic moments and spin structure.

questions.question: What measurement of charmed-baryon or transition magnetic moments would most sharply test the SU(4) chiral constituent quark model's separation of valence, sea-polarization, and orbital contributions?
questions.rationale: The SU(4) chiral constituent quark model in [1] explicitly decomposes these contributions for low-lying and charmed baryons and their transitions.

questions.question: Can configuration mixing in chiral quark-model wave functions explain the Coleman-Glashow sum-rule violation without spoiling successful decuplet magnetic-moment ratios?
questions.rationale: Configuration mixing is used in [5] to reproduce the octet violation, while [2] tests relativistic quark-model ratios for Delta++ and Omega- moments.

questions.question: Which magnetic-moment observable can distinguish a dynamically generated Lambda(1405) or Lambda(1670) from conventional quark-model resonance assignments?
questions.rationale: The unitarized chiral perturbation theory calculation in [4] predicts magnetic moments and transition moments that differ appreciably from existing quark models.

node_5fb894ab69ed.summary: These works calculate magnetic moments of single, double, and strange heavy baryons using light-cone QCD sum rules and relativistic three-quark models.
