questions.question: What measurement of a single, double, or triple heavy-baryon magnetic moment would most sharply discriminate relativistic three-quark, hypercentral potential, and light-cone QCD sum-rule descriptions?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the coexistence of relativistic three-quark, hypercentral, and light-cone sum-rule predictions for heavy-baryon magnetic observables [1,2,3].

questions.question: Can heavy-quark symmetry and chiral constraints be used to reduce the model dependence of baryonic three-quark currents in magnetic-moment predictions for charm and bottom baryons?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the relativistic three-quark model’s consistency with HQET and Heavy Hadron Chiral Perturbation Theory and its use of covariant baryonic currents [1].

questions.question: Can lattice-QCD methods that reproduce light-nucleus magnetic moments at heavy pion mass be extended to physical-mass heavy baryons and radiative heavy-baryon transitions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the lattice calculation of magnetic moments at m_pi around 800 MeV and the sum-rule calculations of transition magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments [3,4].

node_069195337442.summary: This cluster studies electromagnetic and axial form factors of octet baryons and decuplet-octet transitions through chiral quark models, lattice QCD, and chiral extrapolation.

questions.question: Can modern lattice calculations of octet and decuplet electromagnetic form factors isolate quenching artifacts well enough to test the nonanalytic M_pi, M_pi^2 log M_pi, and M_pi^3 structures predicted by quenched baryon chiral perturbation theory?
questions.rationale: Quenched baryon chiral perturbation theory predicts altered and additional nonanalytic mass dependences [1], while FLIC lattice studies compare octet electromagnetic properties extensively with quenched chiral perturbation theory [5].

questions.question: Which hyperon charge radii and octet-to-decuplet transition moments most sensitively distinguish relativistic baryon chiral perturbation theory from lattice quark-sector environment effects?
questions.rationale: Relativistic baryon chiral perturbation theory predicts octet electromagnetic form factors and hyperon charge radii [2], while lattice transition and octet studies reveal quark contribution patterns and environment sensitivity beyond simple quark-model expectations [4,5].

node_e7babaa8ae34.summary: These papers analyze octet and heavy-baryon mass splittings from isospin violation, SU(3) breaking, QED effects, lattice QCD, and chiral perturbation theory.

questions.question: How can lattice QCD plus QED calculations remove the remaining uncertainty from neglecting sea-quark electromagnetism in octet-baryon isospin splittings?
questions.rationale: This follows from the lattice QCD+QED calculation that controlled most systematics but still neglected electromagnetism in the sea [2].

questions.question: Which SU(3) chiral relations between octet mass splittings and CP-odd nucleon-meson couplings survive beyond next-to-next-to-leading order?
questions.rationale: This derives from the NNLO SU(3) chiral analysis showing that some theta-term relations are respected by loops while other leading-order relations are violated [3].

questions.question: Can decuplet intermediate states and discretization effects be incorporated consistently enough to reconcile chiral extrapolations of baryon masses with continuum lattice determinations of baryon structure observables?
questions.rationale: This combines the decuplet-renormalization issues in heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory with lattice evidence that apparent flavor-symmetry violations in baryon distribution amplitudes vanish in the continuum limit [1], [5].

node_f0a2b1ce5490.summary: This cluster develops the 1/Nc expansion and emergent spin-flavor symmetry as systematic tools for baryon masses, magnetic moments, axial couplings, and resonances.

questions.question: Which baryon observables provide the cleanest subleading tests of emergent SU(2N_f) spin-flavor symmetry once SU(3) breaking is included systematically?
questions.rationale: The question comes from the leading and subleading predictions for axial couplings, masses, and magnetic moments in [1] and the operator reduction rules with SU(3) breaking in [2].

questions.question: Can the large-N_c consistency conditions for pion-baryon couplings be embedded in chiral effective theory without conflicting with known large-N_c counting rules for mesonic couplings and anomalies?
questions.rationale: This connects the pion-baryon consistency conditions and Skyrme-model solution in [4] with the large-N_c chiral counting subtleties discussed in [3] and [5].

node_f0a2b1ce5490_1.summary: These papers apply large-Nc QCD and quark-operator methods to baryon spectra, excited states, spin-flavor structure, and SU(3)-breaking mass relations.

questions.question: What baryon spectroscopy measurement would most directly test whether leading large-Nc spin-flavor symmetry, rather than quark-model assumptions, controls the observed excited-baryon spectrum?
questions.rationale: The 1/Nc expansion predicts leading spin-flavor symmetry and subleading relations for baryon masses, axial couplings, and magnetic moments [1].

questions.question: How far can SU(3)-breaking baryon mass and coupling relations be pushed before the operator reduction rules of the quark-operator 1/Nc expansion lose predictive power?
questions.rationale: The quark-operator analysis derives operator identities and reduction rules for masses, magnetic moments, axial currents, and hyperon amplitudes with and without SU(3) breaking [2].

questions.question: Can large-Nc chiral perturbation theory provide a unified account of pion-baryon couplings and mesonic low-energy constants without conflicts such as Kaplan-Manohar-type ambiguities?
questions.rationale: Large-Nc chiral perturbation theory constrains effective couplings and suppresses the Kaplan-Manohar transformation, while pion-baryon consistency conditions uniquely reproduce Skyrme-model couplings [3,4].

node_b39d48eb34d3.summary: This cluster focuses on baryon axial currents in chiral perturbation theory and large-Nc QCD, including loop renormalization, decuplet effects, and flavor-symmetry breaking.

questions.question: Can large-Nc spin-flavor symmetry relations for baryon axial-current ratios remain stable once chiral loops, decuplet intermediate states, and SU(3)-breaking analytic terms are all included consistently?
questions.rationale: This combines the second-order 1/Nc violation result of [1] with the one-loop decuplet analysis of [2] and the SU(3)-breaking covariant calculation of [5].

questions.question: Which low-energy constants control the cancellations that make O(p^3) corrections to octet axial charges converge, and can lattice extrapolations determine them without relying only on non-analytic terms?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which finds good convergence due to cancellations and emphasizes that analytic terms at the same chiral order are essential.

questions.question: What dynamical ingredient explains the persistent discrepancy between quark-model N-Delta coupling predictions and experiment while preserving the Goldberger-Treiman relation in both NN and N-Delta sectors?
questions.rationale: This is based on [3], which finds experimental N-Delta values significantly above mass-corrected SU(6) predictions despite satisfaction of the Goldberger-Treiman relation.

node_b5fd43df8cde.summary: These works explore Skyrme and near-BPS Skyrme models for nuclei, dense matter, binding energies, vector-meson extensions, and topological soliton structure.

questions.question: Is the shell-like Skyrmion picture still the right nuclear paradigm once a nonzero pion mass is included, or do crystal-chunk configurations become the relevant minima for specific baryon numbers?
questions.rationale: This question follows from [4], which finds that nonzero pion mass can replace shell-like minima with crystal chunks and remove shell-like bound states at selected baryon numbers.

questions.question: Can the rho-meson truncation of the BPS-inspired infinite vector-meson tower reduce binding-energy problems while preserving realistic baryon-number one through four Skyrmion structures without adding free parameters?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], where truncating the vector-meson tower to a single rho meson yields a parameter-free extension studied for baryon numbers one to four.

questions.question: Which collective-coordinate manifold for baryon number two best captures the deuteron: toroidal minima, attractive-channel two-Skyrmion configurations, or a larger instanton-holonomy space?
questions.rationale: This derives from the M10 instanton-holonomy description of the deuteron in [5] and the orientation-dependent force tests in baby-Skyrmion dynamics in [1].

node_4485d58cc5b1.summary: This cluster centers on near-BPS and BPS Skyrme descriptions of nuclei, incorporating constant baryon density, Coulomb effects, quantization, and nuclear binding energies.

questions.question: Can near-BPS Skyrme models simultaneously reproduce small nuclear binding energies, realistic pion-mass-dependent shapes, and shell-to-crystal structural changes across baryon number?
questions.rationale: This combines the BPS-model success for heavier-nucleus binding energies with evidence that a nonzero pion mass can replace shell-like Skyrmions by crystal chunks [3],[2].

questions.question: How much of nuclear spectroscopy is fixed by truncating the vector-meson tower to the rho meson without introducing new free parameters?
questions.rationale: This follows from the truncated BPS theory in which a single rho meson extends the standard Skyrme model and is tested for baryon numbers one to four [1].

questions.question: Can collective-coordinate quantization on constrained Skyrmion manifolds produce quantitatively accurate few-body nuclei beyond the deuteron while remaining compatible with BPS binding-energy systematics?
questions.rationale: This derives from the ten-dimensional Skyrme-field description of the deuteron and from BPS-model binding-energy calculations using collective-coordinate corrections [4],[3].

node_3aa5dad5e053.summary: These papers study Skyrmions trapped, transformed, or stabilized by domain walls and related defects, including baby Skyrmions, sine-Gordon kinks, and chiral magnets.

questions.question: Which moduli and interaction terms on a non-Abelian domain-wall worldvolume control whether a sine-Gordon kink, baby Skyrmion, Q-lump, or instanton realizes the same 3+1-dimensional Skyrmion charge?
questions.rationale: This derives from constructions of lumps, baby Skyrmions, Q-lumps, and instantons inside domain walls as lower-dimensional realizations of higher-dimensional Skyrmions [2], [4].

questions.question: Can the nonlinear superposition law found for exact time-periodic Skyrmions be generalized to domain-wall-bound or nested Matryoshka Skyrmions without losing stability?
questions.rationale: The question combines the exact superposition phenomenon of Skyrme crystals with the stable nested domain-wall construction in hierarchical sigma models [3], [5].

questions.question: How do spin, relative orientation, and wall confinement modify the force law and scattering dynamics of baby Skyrmions embedded as constituents of higher-dimensional Skyrmions?
questions.rationale: This extends the numerical tests of spin and orientation effects in baby-Skyrmion dynamics to the domain-wall correspondence with 3D Skyrmions [1], [2].

node_770c344e2ed9.summary: This cluster investigates SU(2) and SU(3) multiskyrmions, their collective-coordinate quantization, strange multibaryons, dibaryon predictions, and topological baryon structure.

questions.question: Can collective-coordinate quantization of B=2 and B=3 skyrmions become predictive for deuteron-like states despite the strong sensitivity of spectra to model parameters?
questions.rationale: This follows from the B=2 and B=3 quantization study where the deuteron-like energy is highly parameter sensitive and large-amplitude fluctuations alter the intrinsic wave function [5].

questions.question: Which meson-sector constraints, including vector-meson symmetry-breaking terms and hidden-local-symmetry rho and omega dynamics, are sufficient for a near zero-parameter baryon and multibaryon Skyrme model?
questions.rationale: The question combines the program of fixing chiral Lagrangian parameters from meson data with the HLS result that Skyrmion properties can be made independent of the parameter a [1],[2],[3].

questions.question: Do Dirac and BFT-consistent quantization prescriptions change SU(2) or SU(3) Skyrmion static properties and multibaryon spectra enough to matter phenomenologically?
questions.rationale: This derives from the demonstration that Dirac quantization with generalized momenta yields an SU(2) Skyrmion spectrum consistent with the BFT formalism [4].

node_26bd07b33805.summary: These papers model baryons as chiral solitons in NJL, Skyrme, and related effective QCD theories, emphasizing large-N arguments, flavor quantization, spectra, and exotic states.

questions.question: Which observables or resonance assignments can remove the ambiguity in chiral-soliton predictions for exotic antidecuplet masses and widths?
questions.rationale: This follows from the original low-mass narrow exotic prediction in [1] and the later sensitivity to moment of inertia, pi-nucleon sigma term, singlet axial current, and resonance assignments in [5].

questions.question: Can the NJL chiral-quark-soliton picture with valence quarks plus polarized Dirac sea be matched quantitatively to large-Nc QCD constraints and the Skyrme limit for both N_f=2 and N_f=3 baryons?
questions.rationale: This derives from the NJL soliton review in [2] and the large-Nc, bosonization, and Skyrme-connection discussion in [3].

questions.question: How far can an effective action combining chiral and heavy-quark symmetry predict heavy-baryon solitons while preserving compatibility between the heavy-quark and large-Nc limits?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the heavy-quark-symmetric chiral effective action and its proposed use for heavy-baryon solitons in [4].

node_8ad2d22756b6.summary: This cluster focuses on chiral soliton descriptions of ordinary and heavy baryons, especially heavy meson bound states and heavy-quark symmetry in baryon spectra.

questions.question: Can a unified soliton description consistently combine the polarized Dirac sea, SU(3) flavor breaking, and heavy-quark symmetry to predict ordinary, strange, and heavy baryon spectra with one controlled set of parameters?
questions.rationale: This question joins the NJL/chiral-quark-soliton baryon framework in [1] and [2] with the heavy-quark-symmetric effective action of [3] and the three-flavor collective quantization reviewed in [5].

questions.question: Which observables in heavy baryons most cleanly test whether the large-Nc soliton limit and the heavy-quark limit commute beyond the meson-sector compatibility shown in effective-action constructions?
questions.rationale: The issue is motivated by [3], which shows compatibility of the heavy-quark and large-Nc limits in the meson sector and discusses relevance to heavy-baryon solitons.

node_52e10f3ca553.summary: These works use chiral soliton and chiral quark-soliton models to predict and interpret exotic baryon multiplets, pentaquark masses, widths, parities, and decay patterns.

questions.question: What single experimental observation would most cleanly validate or rule out the chiral-soliton antidecuplet interpretation: a narrow Theta+, the predicted Xi-- range, or the missing non-exotic N and Sigma partners?
questions.rationale: The soliton papers predict a narrow S=+1 Theta-like state, estimate Xi-- masses, and argue that antidecuplet consistency requires additional N and Sigma states [1,2,3].

questions.question: How much of the uncertainty in exotic baryon masses and widths comes from the pi-nucleon sigma term, the soliton moment of inertia, and the singlet axial-current matrix element?
questions.rationale: The reanalysis identifies these quantities as controlling the predicted antidecuplet mass ranges and suppressed decay rates [2].

questions.question: Can coupling between collective radial motion and SU(3) flavor rotations shift the predicted Z+ pentaquark enough to reconcile soliton spectra with low-lying baryon radial excitations?
questions.rationale: The extended Skyrme analysis treats radial and flavor-rotational collective coordinates together and predicts a Z+ mass near 1.58 GeV with estimated hadronic widths [5].

node_44b5e8d84a11.summary: This cluster studies magnetic moments and electromagnetic properties of hidden-charm, strange, doubly heavy, and molecular pentaquark candidates using QCD sum rules and model comparisons.

questions.question: For Pc(4440), Pc(4457), and Pcs(4459), which combination of magnetic dipole, electric quadrupole, and transition magnetic moments can unambiguously separate molecular, diquark-triquark, and diquark-diquark-antiquark assignments for the same J^P?
questions.rationale: This follows from model-dependent hidden-charm pentaquark magnetic moments across color-flavor structures [1] and light-cone QCD sum-rule calculations of magnetic dipole and quadrupole moments for Pc and Pcs states [4].

questions.question: How large are coupled-channel and D-wave corrections to transition magnetic moments and radiative widths across the Pc and Pcs spectrum, and do they remain small enough for electromagnetic moments to be structural diagnostics?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that coupled-channel effects shift most magnetic moments by 0.1-0.4 nuclear magnetons while D waves are typically below 0.03 nuclear magnetons [5].

node_c1194d382dd1.summary: These papers investigate gluonic hadrons, combining lattice QCD, phenomenology, and mixing analyses to identify glueballs and hybrid mesons beyond the conventional quark model.

questions.question: What combination of lattice glueball masses, continuum spin assignments, and finite-volume diagnostics would make an experimental glueball identification robust against contamination from two-glueball, torelon-pair, or conventional meson states?
questions.rationale: This follows from the anisotropic lattice study's care in distinguishing single glueballs from two-glueball and torelon-pair states while assigning continuum spin quantum numbers [1].

questions.question: Can glueball-to-vacuum matrix elements of local gluonic operators predict radiative J/psi branching ratios accurately enough to discriminate scalar, tensor, and pseudoscalar glueball candidates experimentally?
questions.rationale: The matrix-element study computes local gluonic-operator matrix elements specifically because they are needed to predict glueball branching ratios in J/psi radiative decays [4].

questions.question: How can effective-field-theory descriptions of QCD flux-tube hybrid excitations be matched to lattice static potentials strongly enough to predict which quarkonium-like states are genuine hybrids?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review connecting lattice QCD confining forces, static potentials, effective field theory methods, and hybrid excitations of the QCD flux tube [3].

node_d7e8a6cc0724.summary: This cluster centers on identifying the lightest scalar glueball through its mixing with isoscalar mesons, decay branching patterns, lattice predictions, and phenomenological fits.

questions.question: What combined pattern of scalar masses, mixing angles, and pseudoscalar decay branching fractions would decisively distinguish f0(1500) from f0(1710) as the state with the largest lightest-glueball component?
questions.rationale: The representative papers give competing glueball assignments to f0(1500) through mixing with the 0++ quarkonium nonet [1,3] and to f0(1710) through quenched lattice decay widths and mixing energies [2,5].

questions.question: Can unquenched lattice calculations of scalar glueball-quarkonium mixing and decay amplitudes resolve whether the predicted additional f0 state in the 1500-1800 MeV region couples dominantly to K Kbar, eta eta, and eta eta'?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the predicted extra scalar state and its characteristic decay modes in the f0(1500) glueball-mixing hypothesis [1,3].

questions.question: Can leading neutral clusters in high-energy gluon jets be turned into a quantitatively calibrated glueball-production observable rather than a qualitative excess over Monte Carlo expectations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review's report of a surplus of leading neutral clusters in LEP gluon jets and its suggestion of more energetic LHC jet studies [4].

node_d3086a808d4b.summary: These works review and calculate hybrid meson spectra, decay modes, and exotic quantum-number states using lattice QCD, Coulomb-gauge models, flux-tube ideas, and sum rules.

questions.question: Which decay-pattern observable can most cleanly distinguish light hybrid mesons from nearby conventional q qbar orbital excitations that populate the same mass region?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the overlap between missing L=2 and L=3 quarkonia and hybrid search channels discussed in [3] and the hybrid decay selection rules from flux-tube breaking in [4].

questions.question: How far can the adiabatic approximation and lattice QCD static potentials be pushed in predicting heavy-quark hybrid spectra before coupled-channel effects invalidate a potential description?
questions.rationale: The issue follows from the review of QCD confining potentials, hybrid flux-tube excitations, and the validity of nonrelativistic and adiabatic treatments in [2].

questions.question: Is the Y(4260) compatible with a unique hybrid-charmonium assignment once radiative, open-charm, and closed-charm hadronic transitions are analyzed alongside other gluonic excitations above 3 GeV?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the comparison of Y(4260) and related structures with hybrid charmonium expectations in [5].

node_79d2688cc830.summary: This cluster emphasizes lattice-QCD and phenomenological studies of light and heavy hybrid mesons, including spin-exotic candidates, gluonic excitations, and expected decay signatures.

questions.question: Which lattice-QCD hybrid static potentials and Born-Oppenheimer corrections are required before heavy-quark hybrid spectra can be compared unambiguously with Y(4260)-like charmonium structures?
questions.rationale: This derives from lattice studies of hybrid flux-tube excitations and effective-field-theory treatments of heavy-quark potentials, together with the proposed hybrid interpretation of Y(4260) [2][5].

questions.question: Can decay selection rules from flux-tube breaking be reconciled with observed channels where those rules appear significantly violated, and can such violations become positive diagnostics of hybrid mesons?
questions.rationale: This follows from the flux-tube-breaking calculation that predicts hybrid widths, branching ratios, production dynamics, and possible significant breaking of decay selection rules in specific channels [4].

questions.question: What combined spectrum-and-branching-fraction criterion best separates light spin-exotic hybrids from missing conventional quarkonia in the crowded 2 GeV region?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the warning that missing L=2 and L=3 quarkonia may decay into the same S+P and S+D modes targeted in hybrid searches [3].

node_fffba4a6bab1.summary: These papers use QCD spectral and Laplace sum rules with condensate corrections to predict masses of light, charmonium, bottomonium, and double-gluon hybrid mesons.

questions.question: How stable are QCD spectral-sum-rule hybrid mass predictions when dimension-six condensates, radiative corrections, and tachyonic-gluon-mass effects are varied across light, charmonium, and bottomonium channels?
questions.rationale: Light-hybrid analyses find small radiative and UV-renormalon-mimicking effects, while heavy-quarkonium hybrid spectra become stable only after including condensates up to dimension six [2,5].

questions.question: Can the color-octet JP=1+ gluonic excitation pattern seen in lattice hybrid baryons be quantitatively matched to the hybrid meson supermultiplet structure inferred from QCD sum rules?
questions.rationale: The lattice baryon study isolates positive-parity hybrid baryons compatible with a JP=1+ gluonic excitation, while the heavy-hybrid sum-rule work identifies lightest negative-parity supermultiplets [1,5].

questions.question: What experimental amplitude information would separate a 1-+ hybrid interpretation of pi1 candidates from molecule and four-quark alternatives in the mixed 1.3-1.8 GeV region?
questions.rationale: The 1-+ QCD sum-rule reanalysis finds nearby hybrid, four-quark, and molecular masses and suggests that pi1(1400) and pi1(1600) may involve two-component mixing [4].

node_89c24fd4f335.summary: This cluster focuses on numerical determinations of glueball masses and matrix elements in lattice Yang-Mills and QCD-like theories, including large-N and anisotropic-lattice studies.

questions.question: What lattice operator basis most reliably separates single-glueball states from two-glueball and torelon-pair contaminations below 4 GeV in continuum SU(3) Yang-Mills spectra?
questions.rationale: This follows from the anisotropic-lattice spectrum study that explicitly addressed discretization, finite-volume effects, spin identification, and multi-state contamination in [1].

questions.question: Can glueball-to-vacuum matrix elements of local gluonic operators be computed with enough control to predict J/psi radiative branching ratios that identify experimental glueball candidates?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the scalar, tensor, and pseudoscalar matrix-element calculations for J/psi radiative decay phenomenology in [2].

questions.question: Are spin-exotic glueballs genuinely absent below 3 GeV in continuum SU(3), or are current lattice signals limited by operator overlap and state identification?
questions.rationale: This extends the comprehensive lattice finding of no clear spin-exotic glueball signals below 3 GeV in [3].

node_9226934ae6e3.summary: These papers calculate and classify fully heavy, doubly heavy, hidden-charm, and open-flavor tetraquark spectra using quark models, diquark models, QCD sum rules, and four-body methods.

questions.question: What measurement would decisively distinguish compact diquark-antidiquark structure from deuteron-like hadronic molecules in heavy multiquark states such as X(3872), Z(4430), and doubly heavy tetraquarks?
questions.rationale: This is the central Snowmass framing question about whether multiquark hadrons are compact color-bound objects with diquarks or hadronic molecules bound by light-meson exchange [S1].

questions.question: Are the predicted strong- and electromagnetic-stable double-bottom tetraquarks robust once finite-heavy-mass corrections, heavy-light thresholds, and weak-decay discovery channels are treated in one framework?
questions.rationale: The question follows from predictions that bb anti-u anti-d tetraquarks are below B B* and radiative thresholds and stable except for weak decay, while related cc and bc states are not similarly stable [2][3].

questions.question: Can spin-spin interaction models of S- and P-wave tetraquarks explain both the observed charged sectors and the apparent absence of complete isospin multiplets without adding unsupported states?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the type-II diquark-antidiquark model's success for Z and Y sectors and its stated unresolved difficulty with incomplete isospin multiplets [4].

node_633068ef56ec.summary: This cluster studies heavy-flavor tetraquarks in quark-model frameworks, comparing meson-meson and diquark-antidiquark configurations to explain observed exotic charmonium-like states.

questions.question: What mass splittings, charged partners, and incomplete isospin multiplets around X(3872), X(3940), and Z(4430) would decisively falsify compact diquark-antidiquark spin models relative to molecular organization?
questions.rationale: This question is drawn from the diquark-antidiquark interpretation of X(3872), the type-II tetraquark spin model for Z(4430), and the Snowmass compact-versus-molecular framing [1], [4], and [S1].

questions.question: How reliable are heavy-quark-symmetry plus finite-mass-correction predictions that bb anti-u anti-d is stable below B B* thresholds while cc and bc analogues dissociate into heavy-light mesons?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the doubly heavy tetraquark stability predictions tied to Xi_cc and heavy-quark-symmetry finite-mass corrections [2] and [3].

node_21d52bdfb581.summary: These papers use constituent, chiral, relativistic, and potential quark models to predict spectra and structures of fully heavy, doubly heavy, hidden-charm, and open-flavor tetraquarks.

questions.question: Which spin-spin interaction pattern in diquark-antidiquark Hamiltonians can simultaneously reproduce X(3872), charged Z states, Y resonances, and the observed incompleteness of isospin multiplets?
questions.rationale: The unresolved isospin-multiplet problem is central to the type-II tetraquark spin-interaction model proposed in [3].

questions.question: How large are finite-heavy-mass corrections to the heavy-quark-symmetry prediction that only selected double-bottom Q_i Q_j anti-q_k anti-q_l tetraquarks are stable against strong decays?
questions.rationale: The stability pattern of double-bottom versus double-charm and bc tetraquarks is derived from heavy-quark symmetry plus finite-mass corrections in [2].

questions.question: Can relativistic quark models with non-pointlike diquark form factors make parameter-stable predictions for hidden-bottom, open-bottom, and double-heavy tetraquark masses across all relevant meson thresholds?
questions.rationale: The relativistic calculations in [4] and [5] hinge on internal diquark structure encoded by diquark-gluon form factors and compare masses to open-flavor thresholds.

node_9accb40a73f2.summary: This cluster focuses on mass spectra of fully heavy and hidden-heavy tetraquarks in diquark-antidiquark quark models, often connecting predicted states to LHC charmonium-like signals.

questions.question: Which spin-spin, color-magnetic, and relativistic diquark form-factor effects are essential for a stable prediction of fully heavy QQbarQbarQ spectra across ccbarcbarc, bcbarbbarc, and bbbarbbarc systems?
questions.rationale: This question connects the constituent spin-spin spectra in [1], the relativistic diquark form-factor treatment in [3] and [4], and the color-magnetic fully heavy analysis in [5].

questions.question: Can predicted narrow bbbarbbarc and bcbarbbarc tetraquarks be separated experimentally from threshold cusps by their strong-decay patterns and heavy-quark spin multiplet structure?
questions.rationale: The possibility of stable or narrow fully heavy states and their strong decay patterns is explicitly raised in [5].

questions.question: What mechanism explains incomplete isospin multiplets in diquark-antidiquark spectroscopy without spoiling the successful assignments of X(3872), Z(4430), and Y-sector states?
questions.rationale: The unresolved problem of incomplete isospin multiplets is identified in the type-II tetraquark model of [2], while [1] uses X(3872) as an input to build broader spectra.

node_0b0a4949230e.summary: These works calculate ground and excited charm-only and bottom-only tetraquark states using relativistic, nonrelativistic, and QCD-sum-rule approaches to interpret structures such as X(6900).

questions.question: What experimental pattern of masses and widths among cc cbar cbar, bb bbar bbar, and bc bbar cbar excitations would discriminate relativized diquark-antidiquark spectra from color-magnetic interaction predictions?
questions.rationale: Fully heavy tetraquark spectra are computed in both relativized diquark Hamiltonians [5] and color-magnetic interaction models with predicted decay patterns [3].

questions.question: How large are spin-spin, spin-orbit, tensor, and finite-diquark-size effects in excited fully charmed tetraquarks near the observed charmonium-like structures?
questions.rationale: The nonrelativistic cc cbar cbar model finds sizable spin-dependent interactions and finite diquark size effects despite the heavy diquark mass [4].

node_9c084d775ce2.summary: This cluster studies hidden-charm and hidden-strangeness tetraquarks in diquark-antidiquark models to classify X, Y, and Z resonances and predict related open-strange exotic partners.

questions.question: Can a single hidden-charm diquark-antidiquark Hamiltonian combining type-II intra-diquark spin interactions with relativistic heavy-light diquark dynamics reproduce the X(3872), Z(4430/4433), Y(4260), Y(4360), and Y(4660) spectrum while also predicting which 1++ and 1-- isospin partners should be missing or observed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the type-II spin-interaction model's success in the 1++ and 1-- sectors but unresolved incomplete isospin multiplets [2], together with the relativistic diquark spectrum assignments for the same hidden-charm states [3].

questions.question: In lattice QCD, does the X(3872) emerge as a genuine compact diquark-antidiquark eigenstate, or only as a mixed state requiring simultaneous ccbar and D D* interpolating operators, and how does this conclusion change for c cbar s sbar candidates such as Y(4140)?
questions.rationale: The lattice study found an I=0 X(3872) candidate only when both ccbar and D D* operators were included, and not from diquark-antidiquark plus D D* operators without ccbar [4].

questions.question: If Z(4433) is the first radial excitation of the tetraquark supermultiplet containing X(3872) and X(3876), what quantitative radial mass splittings and charged-partner pattern distinguish this assignment from alternative S- or P-wave hidden-charm tetraquark classifications?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the proposed identification of Z(4433) as a first radial excitation of the X(3872)/X(3876) tetraquark supermultiplet and the associated experimental predictions [5].

node_178cc6dfaebd.summary: These papers investigate bound and resonant QQ anti-q anti-q tetraquark states, especially Tcc and Tbb systems, using chiral, constituent, molecular, and heavy-diquark symmetry models.

questions.question: Which finite-heavy-quark-mass corrections decide the boundary between strongly stable bb qbar qbar tetraquarks and dissociating cc or bc analogues?
questions.rationale: This follows from heavy-quark-symmetry predictions that double-beauty states are stable while double-charm and mixed beauty-charm states generally dissociate [1].

questions.question: Can flux-tube diffusion Monte Carlo, chiral constituent quark models, and color-screening models be reconciled on whether full-beauty bbbb states are bound, broad resonances, or absent?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in conflicting model outcomes for bbbb states, including a bound 0++ state, possible wide resonances, and no bound state in different quark models [3][5].

questions.question: What decay and production channels best distinguish compact diquark-antidiquark full-heavy tetraquarks from meson-meson threshold resonances in ccbarccbar and bbbarbbbar systems?
questions.rationale: This derives from proposed production and observation channels for fully heavy resonances and model comparisons of meson-meson versus diquark-antidiquark structures [2][5].

node_4e7200ba4e7a.summary: This cluster examines production mechanisms and phenomenology for heavy tetraquarks at colliders, especially fully charmed states produced through NRQCD fragmentation at the LHC and FCC.

questions.question: Can collider production rates and invariant-mass spectra distinguish compact fully heavy tetraquarks from nonresonant double-quarkonium production in the 2 J/psi channel?
questions.rationale: This follows from the predicted T4c peaks in heavy-quarkonium-pair spectra in [2] and the double-J/psi production estimates with possible tetraquark contributions in [3].

questions.question: What production and decay channels provide the cleanest test of whether a bb anti-u anti-d tetraquark is strong- and electromagnetic-stable as predicted from doubly heavy baryon mass systematics?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the stable T(bb anti-u anti-d) prediction inferred from the Xi_cc discovery in [1].

questions.question: Can spin-symmetry multiplet assignments connect Zc and Zb spectroscopy to collider searches for heavier tetraquark and hybrid analogs?
questions.rationale: This derives from the hybrid-tetraquark multiplet interpretation in [4] and the Zb tetraquark interpretation tested against Belle data in [5].

node_9b9b6ac91c87.summary: These works review and model the stability of exotic multiquark hadrons using bag, string, hyperspherical, and diquark pictures, with emphasis on heavy-quark configurations near strong-decay thresholds.

questions.question: What minimal experimental pattern of masses, quantum numbers, and decay thresholds would decide whether heavy multiquark states are compact color-bound objects or deuteron-like hadronic molecules?
questions.rationale: This is the central structural question identified in the Snowmass framing paper and is echoed by model comparisons between compact and molecular four-quark candidates [S1],[3].

questions.question: Across hyperspherical, diquark, string, bag, and chiral quark-model descriptions, which predicted heavy-quark flavor configurations remain stable against strong decay under changes of the hyperfine interaction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the hyperspherical stability results for selected J^PC channels, diquark-model stable heavy configurations, and the contrasting chiral quark-model binding of QQ qbar qbar systems [2],[4],[5].

questions.question: Can unexplored flavor configurations with one or more heavy quarks provide a sharper test of multiquark stability models than already observed near-threshold exotic candidates?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review emphasis on flavor configurations not yet investigated and the Snowmass question of what other multiquark states should be expected [1],[S1].

node_ba5e7669e943.summary: This cluster applies QCD sum rules to compute masses, pole residues, and quantum-number assignments for hidden-charm, fully heavy, fully strange, and light tetraquark candidates.

questions.question: Can QCD sum rules distinguish compact diquark-antidiquark tetraquarks from molecular or threshold-dominated states once pole residues, continuum thresholds, and high-dimension condensates are varied systematically?
questions.rationale: This follows from X(3872) and Zc axial-vector sum-rule assignments using high-dimension condensates and scale dependence [1] and [3].

questions.question: Which sum-rule stability criteria can decide whether fully heavy ccbarccbar and bbarbbb tetraquark currents correspond to observable resonances rather than states above spontaneous two-quarkonium dissociation thresholds?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the moment sum-rule analysis and threshold comparison for fully heavy tetraquarks in [4].

node_ba5e7669e943_1.summary: These papers construct interpolating currents for S-wave and P-wave tetraquarks and use QCD sum rules to assign observed X, Y, Z, fully heavy, and fully strange resonances.

questions.question: Can a common QCD sum-rule criterion distinguish compact diquark-antidiquark assignments from molecular or mixed components for X(3872), Zc(3900), and Y-family states?
questions.rationale: Different sum-rule analyses support axial-vector tetraquark assignments for X(3872) and Zc states, while other currents place related charmonium-like masses above X(3872) [1,2,4].

questions.question: How stable are tetraquark mass assignments under dimension-10 condensates, energy-scale choices, and pole-residue criteria in the operator product expansion?
questions.rationale: The axial-vector X and Zc analysis emphasizes consistent dimension-10 condensates and detailed energy-scale dependence as central to the assignment [2].

questions.question: For fully heavy tetraquark currents, can moment QCD sum rules predict which states are true resonances rather than configurations lying above spontaneous two-quarkonium dissociation thresholds?
questions.rationale: Moment sum rules with inequalities find most cc cbar cbar masses above two-charmonium thresholds while bottom analogs can lie near or below bottomonium thresholds [3].

node_7a45d19c66e4.summary: This cluster uses two-point and three-point QCD sum rules to estimate masses, couplings, and strong decay widths of double-heavy, fully heavy, and charmonium-like tetraquark candidates.

questions.question: Can two-point and three-point QCD sum rules produce stable, experimentally discriminating predictions for both masses and partial widths of double-heavy and charmonium-like tetraquarks using the same interpolating-current assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of two-point sum rules for tetraquark masses and three-point functions for strong couplings and decay widths [2,4,5].

questions.question: Which decay channel among J/psi pi, eta_c rho, open-heavy meson pairs, and isospin-violating Ds pi modes most cleanly tests whether a candidate is a compact diquark-antidiquark tetraquark?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the proposed four-quark decay modes for Ds(2320), the Zc(3900) width calculation, and the review of dominant strong tetraquark decays [1,3,4,5].

questions.question: Do higher-dimensional condensates and leading-order alpha_s approximations allow a robust conclusion that Tbb lies below the BB* threshold while Tcc remains near 4 GeV?
questions.rationale: This directly derives from the QQ anti-u anti-d sum-rule prediction using condensates up to dimension eight at leading order in alpha_s [2].

node_a89754b5821d.summary: These studies use lattice QCD and lattice NRQCD to search for bound doubly heavy tetraquarks, especially bottom-bottom and bottom-charm light-antiquark systems with axial-vector quantum numbers.

questions.question: What lattice setup can resolve whether the cc anti-u anti-d near-threshold pole is a virtual state, a shallow bound tetraquark, or a finite-volume artifact after extrapolation to physical pion mass and continuum spacing?
questions.rationale: The DD* Luescher analysis finds an l=0 virtual bound-state pole near threshold at m_pi about 280 MeV and two charm masses, leaving the physical-limit pole nature open [4].

questions.question: How do diquark-antidiquark and nonlocal meson-meson interpolators change extracted binding energies for ud anti-b anti-b and ls anti-b anti-b channels in a combined continuum, volume, and NRQCD-systematics analysis?
questions.rationale: Deep binding was found using diquark and meson-meson operators with NRQCD bottom quarks, while later work improved the analysis with nonlocal two-meson interpolators and Luescher extrapolation [2], [5].

questions.question: Can lattice QCD map the heavy-quark-mass dependence from charm to bottom well enough to connect pion-exchange binding in the infinite-heavy limit to the observed hierarchy of bb, bc, and cc tetraquark candidates?
questions.rationale: The heavy-quark-limit argument predicts stable QQ anti-q anti-q states through one-pion exchange, while lattice studies compare bottom and charm heavy sectors with varying light-quark content [1], [3].

node_632280afb346.summary: This cluster centers on QCD sum-rule determinations of heavy-light meson decay constants and related hadronic couplings, with careful treatment of perturbative corrections and condensate uncertainties.

questions.question: Can light-cone QCD sum rules for D*Dpi and B*Bpi couplings be made precise enough that pion two- and three-particle twist-2, twist-3, and twist-4 wave-function uncertainties no longer dominate semileptonic pole-dominance tests?
questions.rationale: The light-cone sum-rule calculation of D*Dpi and B*Bpi couplings explicitly includes pion wave functions through twist 4 and uses the couplings in pole-dominance estimates for B to pi and D to pi transitions [2].

questions.question: How can heavy-quark effective theory sum rules consistently combine perturbative corrections, condensate inputs, and chromomagnetic operators to predict vector-pseudoscalar heavy-light meson splittings across charm and beauty?
questions.rationale: The HQET sum-rule study computes chromomagnetic splittings and the heavy-quark kinetic-energy matrix element, finding agreement with charm and beauty data [5].

questions.question: Can in-medium current-current correlation functions from effective chiral SU(3) dynamics and vector-meson dominance be reconciled with QCD sum-rule constraints on rho and omega spectral changes in baryonic matter?
questions.rationale: The in-medium vector-meson study uses effective scattering amplitudes as input to QCD sum rules and finds different rho and omega spectral modifications [3].

node_730328794be5.summary: These papers study how nuclear or strange hadronic matter modifies meson masses, condensates, decay constants, optical potentials, and possible bound states using QCD sum rules and effective hadronic models.

questions.question: Which in-medium spectral features, rather than mass shifts alone, provide the most discriminating test of QCD-sum-rule descriptions of rho and omega propagation in baryonic matter?
questions.rationale: The vector-meson sum-rule study finds enhanced low-mass isovector spectral density with little rho mass shift but a downward omega peak shift and moderate broadening [1].

questions.question: Can QMC scaling relations for in-medium hadron masses and form factors be reconciled quantitatively with finite-density QCD condensate sum rules for baryon self-energies and optical potentials?
questions.rationale: The QMC review predicts simple medium scaling and form-factor changes, while the QCD-sum-rule review relates in-medium hadron spectral properties to condensates [2].

questions.question: What experimental observable would most directly validate self-consistent coupled-channel predictions for D-meson optical potentials and possible D-nuclear bound states?
questions.rationale: The DN coupled-channel study computes in-medium D-meson behavior in isosymmetric nuclear matter using a self-consistent meson-baryon interaction [4].

node_b35422a143d5.summary: This cluster focuses on applying QCD sum rules to hadrons in baryonic or nuclear matter, linking in-medium spectral changes and scattering lengths to quark and gluon condensates.

questions.question: Can finite-density QCD sum rules disentangle genuine in-medium pole shifts from low-energy spectral-density enhancements in the rho and omega channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast in [1] between strong sub-rho spectral enhancement in the isovector channel and a downward omega peak shift in the isoscalar channel.

questions.question: Which density-dependent condensates most strongly control baryon self-energies and optical potentials, and can they be constrained independently enough to make nuclear-matter sum-rule predictions predictive rather than phenomenological?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2], which relates quasinucleon optical potentials and baryon self-energies to finite-density QCD condensates.

questions.question: Can QCD-sum-rule treatments of heavy hadrons in nuclear matter be consistently matched to coupled-channel DN and heavy-quark-spin-symmetric effective-Lagrangian descriptions?
questions.rationale: This combines the self-consistent DN coupled-channel treatment in [3] with the heavy-hadron nuclear-matter framework emphasizing chiral and heavy-quark spin symmetries in [5].

node_04a8a4f01629.summary: These works analyze how strong magnetic fields and asymmetric hadronic matter alter open heavy mesons, charmonia, bottomonia, masses, mixing, and decay widths.

questions.question: How can QCD sum-rule spectral ansaetze disentangle pseudoscalar-vector mixing, Landau levels, and genuine OPE-induced mass shifts for charged and neutral open-heavy mesons in strong magnetic fields?
questions.rationale: The D-meson sum-rule study finds that charged states are largely saturated by Landau-level and mixing effects, whereas neutral D mesons receive significant additional positive mass shifts [4].

questions.question: What observable consequence follows from the failure of center-of-mass and internal motion to decouple for quarkonia labeled by pseudomomentum in a magnetic field?
questions.rationale: The quarkonium magnetic-field analysis shows that pseudomomentum replaces conserved center-of-mass momentum and makes quarkonium properties depend on the state motion [1].

questions.question: Can lattice-inspired anisotropic static potentials and QCD-sum-rule mixing effects be combined into a common prediction for J/psi, eta_c, Upsilon, and open-heavy-meson production changes in heavy-ion magnetic fields?
questions.rationale: Potential-model studies include anisotropic Cornell-like potentials, while sum-rule and color-evaporation analyses connect magnetic-field-induced mass shifts to charmonium and bottomonium production [2,3,5].

node_b69c1147b87c.summary: This cluster examines how nuclear matter changes pion form factors, decay constants, valence-quark distributions, wave functions, and related hadron structure observables.

questions.question: Which observable would most cleanly decide whether near-threshold scalar-isoscalar pi-pi enhancement in nuclear matter is driven by partial chiral restoration rather than ordinary many-body dynamics?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that reduced chiral condensate enhances the I=J=0 pi-pi cross section near the two-pion threshold in both linear and nonlinear chiral models [2].

questions.question: Can one build a quantitatively consistent in-medium description that links QMC scaling of hadron masses and form factors with soliton-model changes in energy-momentum-tensor form factors?
questions.rationale: The question combines the QMC prediction of medium-modified masses and form factors with Skyrme and pi-rho-omega soliton calculations of in-medium EMT form factors and D-term changes [1],[3],[5].

questions.question: How do isoscalar and isovector effective-mass constraints from giant resonances feed into predictions for pion-mediated structure changes in asymmetric nuclear matter?
questions.rationale: This follows from the extraction of isoscalar and isovector effective masses in Pb-208 and the broader program of modeling medium-modified hadron structure [4],[1].

node_090f8cc47ce9.summary: These papers investigate eta, eta-prime, and eta_c interactions with nuclei, emphasizing optical potentials, mesic bound states, axial anomaly dynamics, and medium-modified meson-baryon amplitudes.

questions.question: Can measurements of eta bound states in nuclei determine the eta singlet component and thereby constrain axial U(1) dynamics and glue contributions to eta-nucleon scattering?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from [1], which argues that eta nuclear binding is sensitive to the flavor-singlet component and eta-eta-prime mixing.

questions.question: How can strongly energy-dependent eta optical potentials from self-consistent chiral unitary calculations be tested against formation spectra of eta or eta-prime mesic nuclei?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the energy-dependent eta optical potential of [2] and the Green-function formation-spectrum program for eta-prime bound states in [4].

questions.question: Which combination of eta-prime scattering-length measurements, transparency ratios, and pion- or photon-induced formation reactions can reduce the present uncertainty in the eta-prime-nucleus optical potential?
questions.rationale: This derives from [5], which identifies the poorly known eta-prime-nucleon interaction, scattering length, and transparency ratios as limiting inputs.

node_632280afb346_1.summary: This cluster centers on high-precision QCD sum-rule determinations of heavy-light pseudoscalar and vector meson decay constants with improved perturbative and condensate corrections.

questions.question: Can heavy-light decay-constant sum rules be made systematically stable by using short-distance heavy-quark masses while propagating three-loop perturbative and condensate uncertainties into f_B and f_Bs?
questions.rationale: This directly extends the finding in [3] that pole-mass sum rules are unreliable while the MSbar scheme gives controlled determinations, within the broader sum-rule framework of [1].

questions.question: What sum-rule strategy can simultaneously describe pseudoscalar-vector splittings, HQET kinetic and chromomagnetic matrix elements, and light-cone heavy-decay amplitudes without relying on fragile resonance-dominance assumptions?
questions.rationale: This combines the HQET splitting calculation in [2], the light-cone sum-rule program in [5], and the failure of lowest-resonance dominance in related QCD sum-rule constraints in [4].

node_a06c74560799.summary: These works use QCD sum rules to extract heavy-light meson masses, decay constants, and ratios while controlling uncertainties from operator expansions, heavy-quark masses, and continuum thresholds.

questions.question: Can heavy-light decay-constant sum rules be made insensitive to heavy-quark mass schemes by consistently avoiding pole-mass inputs in favor of short-distance masses?
questions.rationale: The f_B and f_Bs analysis finds pole-mass sum rules unreliable because of large higher-order corrections, while the MS-bar scheme gives controlled results [2].

questions.question: Which O(alpha_s^2) perturbative and O(alpha_s) condensate contributions dominate the uncertainty in vector-to-pseudoscalar decay-constant ratios such as f_B*/f_B and f_D*/f_D?
questions.rationale: The vector-meson decay-constant study improves the OPE with alpha_s^2 perturbative terms and alpha_s quark-condensate corrections to predict these ratios [3].

questions.question: How robust are QCD spectral sum-rule predictions for scalar-pseudoscalar open-charm and open-beauty splittings against assumptions about the chiral condensate and continuum threshold?
questions.rationale: The chiral-multiplet study identifies the chiral condensate as central to scalar-pseudoscalar mass splittings and fixes sum-rule parameters from known D and Ds masses [4].

node_d3b07ff061d2.summary: This cluster reviews and tests QCD sum-rule techniques, including condensate inputs, effective continuum thresholds, dispersive methods, and systematic uncertainties in hadron parameter extraction.

questions.question: How can QCD sum rules assign systematic uncertainties to effective continuum thresholds and condensate inputs so that extracted heavy-flavor decay constants and form factors are reproducible across channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the broad methodological review in [1], the vacuum-condensate and OPE foundations in [4], and the heavy-flavor QSSR comparisons in [5].

questions.question: When do lowest-resonance dominance assumptions fail in dispersive or resonance-interpolant sum rules, and what asymptotic constraints are needed to prevent biased low-energy constants?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Dashen-theorem sum-rule analysis in [2], which shows failures of lowest-resonance dominance under QCD asymptotic constraints.

node_0d8305d4e19c.summary: These papers calculate heavy-meson strong form factors and coupling constants at meson vertices using three-point and light-cone QCD sum rules.

questions.question: How can three-point and light-cone QCD sum-rule extractions of H^*H pi couplings be made insensitive to the choice of off-shell meson and extrapolation from the deep Euclidean region?
questions.rationale: The D*Dpi form-factor studies find different momentum dependence for D- and pion-off-shell form factors but the same coupling, and the review highlights extrapolation to time-like poles as a key uncertainty [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: Can the heavy-quark limit reconcile QCD sum-rule and light-cone sum-rule predictions for strong couplings of excited positive-parity heavy mesons while preserving reliable finite-charm and finite-bottom widths?
questions.rationale: The excited-heavy-meson paper finds compatible QCD and light-cone sum-rule results in the m_Q -> infinity limit and applies them to B and D positive-parity hadronic widths [4].

questions.question: Which pion distribution amplitudes and higher-twist contributions dominate the uncertainty in g_{D^*Dpi} and g_{B^*Bpi}, and how would improved inputs affect semileptonic pole-dominance applications?
questions.rationale: The light-cone sum-rule calculation includes two- and three-particle pion wave functions of twists 2, 3, and 4 and uses the extracted couplings in pole-dominance models for B -> pi and D -> pi semileptonic form factors [1].

node_5f05681c7b7f.summary: This cluster studies pion-nucleon and pion-baryon coupling constants, scattering constraints, and parity-violating hadronic interactions through QCD sum rules, lattice QCD, and phenomenology.

questions.question: How can pionic-atom scattering lengths, the isovector GMO sum rule, and backward neutron-proton scattering be reconciled into a single charged pion-nucleon coupling determination with controlled systematics?
questions.rationale: The tension among direct data, indirect methods, and backward np determinations is explicitly discussed in [2].

questions.question: Can an EFT description of strangeness-conserving hadronic parity violation connect meson-exchange couplings and lattice QCD well enough to explain the suppressed weak pion-nucleon coupling?
questions.rationale: The need for a model-independent EFT framework in [3] and the suppressed parity-nonconserving pion-nucleon coupling in [4] motivate this question.

questions.question: Which O(p^6) chiral low-energy constants in two-loop vector and axial correlators most limit chiral sum rules and precision pion-baryon coupling extractions?
questions.rationale: The two-loop ChPT calculations and new O(p^6) constants in [1] and [5] set the theoretical systematics for such low-energy analyses.

node_ef09549e39a8.summary: These papers model pion production in neutrino, photon, and nucleon reactions, including resonant and nonresonant amplitudes, coherent nuclear production, and final-state interactions.

questions.question: What experimental observable would most cleanly separate resonant Delta-pole pion production from the chiral-symmetry-required background terms in weak pion production off nucleons?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] finds that background terms significantly alter neutrino and antineutrino pion-production cross sections after refitting the C5A form factor.

questions.question: Can transport models such as GiBUU provide a unified treatment of pion-induced, photon-induced, electron-induced, and neutrino-induced nuclear reactions once off-shell propagation and in-medium collision terms are constrained by data?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] presents GiBUU as a transport framework spanning these reaction classes, with off-shell transport and in-medium modifications as central ingredients.

questions.question: How consistently can multichannel partial-wave and dynamical coupled-channel analyses extract nucleon and Delta resonance properties when pion, eta, kaon, photon, and pi-pi-N channels are fitted simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows from the multichannel resonance program in [3] and the coupled-channel integral-equation treatment of pi N and gamma N reactions in [5].

node_8b31ab1e76cf.summary: This cluster analyzes kaon, hyperon, and vector-meson photoproduction reactions to extract nucleon and hyperon resonance contributions using effective Lagrangian and coupled-channel approaches.

questions.question: Can a coupled-channel analysis of gamma N and pi N reactions up to W = 2 GeV determine which kaon and eta photoproduction structures are genuine nucleon resonances rather than model-dependent meson-baryon final-state interactions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dynamical coupled-channel framework with pi N, eta N, K Lambda, K Sigma, and pi pi N channels in [2] and the effective-Lagrangian eta-photoproduction analysis in [3].

questions.question: How model-independent can extractions of the two Lambda(1405) poles and possible isospin-1 pi Sigma amplitudes become using Jefferson Lab photoproduction data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the chiral coupled-channel generation of Lambda(1405) [1] and the pi Sigma photoproduction strategy for extracting isospin 0 and 1 components [5].

node_6b9176fd17fd.summary: These papers model kaon and K-star photoproduction of Lambda and Sigma hyperons to determine the roles of nucleon, Delta, and exchange contributions in strangeness production.

questions.question: Can pi Sigma photoproduction data determine both isospin-0 Lambda(1405) poles and the isospin-1 amplitude with enough model independence to discriminate chiral-unitary descriptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the strategy of fitting gamma p to K+ pi Sigma channels with minimally model-dependent production mechanisms and chiral-unitary final-state interactions [1].

questions.question: Which polarization or angular observables in K* Lambda photoproduction can establish whether D13(2080), rather than D15(2200), drives the near-threshold enhancement?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the effective-Lagrangian finding that D13(2080) is crucial for the near-threshold production rate while D15(2200) is small [5].

questions.question: How can low-energy effective-Lagrangian mechanisms and higher-energy Regge or quark-gluon-string descriptions be matched in Lambda(1520) photoproduction where K exchange dominates over K* exchange?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Lambda(1520) study finding small dynamically generated N Kbar* coupling, K-exchange dominance near threshold, and K-Regge success at higher energies [4].

node_b2e383517aca.summary: These studies analyze antikaon-proton and related hadronic reactions to extract Lambda, Sigma, Xi, and charmed hyperon resonance properties using coupled-channel and effective Lagrangian methods.

questions.question: Which new K^- p measurements in eta Lambda, K Xi, pi pi Lambda, or pi anti-K N channels would most reduce model dependence in extracting Lambda* and Sigma* pole positions and residues below W = 2.1 GeV?
questions.rationale: The dynamical coupled-channels program extracts hyperon poles using two- and three-body channel spaces [1,2], while unitary multichannel analyses find important differences among existing fits and call for more anti-K N data [3].

questions.question: Can the proposed narrow J^P = 3/2+ Lambda resonance strongly coupled to eta Lambda be confirmed through amplitude analyses that preserve unitarity, analyticity, and correct threshold behavior?
questions.rationale: A dynamical coupled-channels extraction proposes a new narrow 3/2+ Lambda resonance with strong eta Lambda coupling [1], while a separate multichannel model emphasizes unitarity, analytic continuation, and threshold behavior [3].

node_b0329137d938.summary: This cluster uses eta and eta-prime photo-, electro-, and hadroproduction to constrain N-star resonance spectra and production mechanisms in nucleon reactions.

questions.question: Can eta and kaon photoproduction data in a single SU(3) coupled-channel fit determine whether the S11(1535) is predominantly a dynamically generated quasi-bound state or requires an explicit bare nucleon resonance?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] obtains the S11(1535) as a kaon-Sigma quasi-bound state in an SU(3) chiral coupled-channel framework, while [3] treats it as the dominant explicit resonance in an effective Lagrangian approach.

questions.question: Which meson-baryon channel data below W=2 GeV most reduce the ambiguity in extracted N* pole parameters when piN, etaN, KLambda, KSigma, and pi-pi-N channels are all coupled?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] fits a dynamical coupled-channel model including these channels, and [5] extracts resonance parameters from a unitary multichannel parametrization.

questions.question: Can photoproduction off proton targets distinguish genuine exotic baryon resonances from kinematic effects using the same coupled-channel discipline developed for eta photoproduction?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] proposes J/psi p photoproduction as a crucial resonant-nature test for LHCb exotic states, while [1] and [2] show how photoproduction constrains resonance dynamics.

node_8e14e6fd852e.summary: These papers study near-threshold pion photo- and electroproduction with chiral perturbation theory, emphasizing multipoles, low-energy constants, and Delta resonance effects.

questions.question: Which threshold pion photo- and electroproduction multipoles are genuinely controlled by fast-converging chiral low-energy theorems rather than by slowly convergent E0+ expansions?
questions.rationale: Heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory found slow convergence for E0+ but fast-converging P-wave low-energy theorems useful for data analysis [2].

questions.question: How can Chew-Mandelstam, dynamical coupled-channel, and chiral Delta-region analyses be reconciled in their extraction of photocouplings, pole residues, and gamma N to Delta transition strengths?
questions.rationale: SAID uses a unitary Chew-Mandelstam parametrization, the Delta-region EFT fits M1, E2, and C2 low-energy constants, and the Juelich model extracts photocouplings at resonance poles [1], [3], [5].

questions.question: Which polarization observables near threshold would most strongly constrain the poorly determined neutral-pion multipoles and gamma n to pi0 n amplitudes?
questions.rationale: The neutral-pion photoproduction analysis stresses polarization observables as essential for pinning down certain multipoles and gives predictions for gamma n to pi0 n [2].

node_8e14e6fd852e_1.summary: This cluster focuses on neutral pion photo- and electroproduction near threshold as a test of chiral dynamics, loop corrections, and Delta-inclusive effective theories.

questions.question: Which near-threshold neutral-pion observables provide the cleanest test of chiral dynamics if the E0+ electric dipole amplitude is slowly convergent and therefore a weak discriminator?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the heavy-baryon chiral perturbation theory result that E0+ converges slowly while P-wave low-energy theorems converge rapidly [2].

questions.question: How can polarization observables be combined with unitary Chew-Mandelstam or dynamical coupled-channel analyses to reduce ambiguities in threshold multipoles and photocouplings at resonance poles?
questions.rationale: This derives from the need for polarization data to pin down multipoles [2], the unitary SAID Chew-Mandelstam analysis [1], and pole photocoupling extraction in a dynamical coupled-channel framework [5].

questions.question: Can Delta-inclusive chiral EFT in the delta expansion be matched smoothly onto threshold neutral-pion photoproduction and higher-energy coupled-channel descriptions without double counting resonance effects?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the Delta-region electroproduction calculation with fitted M1, E2, and C2 transition constants [3] and the resonance mechanisms needed in pion photoproduction channels [4].

node_a4da7f1812c0.summary: These works apply Regge pole, cut, and exchange models to high-energy pion, eta, omega, and related meson photoproduction and scattering at forward or backward angles.

questions.question: What minimal set of Regge poles, cuts, and gauge-restoring terms can describe forward-angle pion, neutral-pion, and strangeness photoproduction without channel-by-channel refitting?
questions.rationale: Parameter-sparse Regge descriptions succeed for pion photoproduction [5], neutral pion production [4], and strangeness electroproduction when gauge invariance is handled carefully [2],[3].

questions.question: Which spin-transfer or polarization observables most decisively test Regge-pole dominance and factorization above the resonance region?
questions.rationale: Regge factorization was checked precisely in scattering amplitudes [1], and spin-transfer observables were identified as sensitive discriminants among strangeness electroproduction models [3].

node_8c7c02950994.summary: This cluster develops models for single and coherent pion production in neutrino-nucleon and neutrino-nucleus scattering, including Delta dominance, background terms, PCAC, and nuclear effects.

questions.question: How large are chiral-symmetry-required background terms relative to Delta-pole dominance across neutrino and antineutrino single-pion channels on free nucleons and nuclei?
questions.rationale: The weak pion production model refits C5A and finds a smaller Delta-pole contribution than traditionally assumed, with significant background terms required by chiral symmetry [2].

questions.question: Can PCAC-based coherent pion production be reconciled with MiniBooNE neutral-pion data while retaining the lepton-mass suppression that agrees with charged-pion upper limits?
questions.rationale: The PCAC analysis agrees with published pi+ upper limits after including lepton-mass suppression but predicts pi0 production well below the MiniBooNE result [5].

questions.question: How do off-shell transport, in-medium collision terms, and final-state interactions modify neutrino-induced pion observables in the few-GeV energy range relevant to GiBUU applications?
questions.rationale: The GiBUU review emphasizes off-shell transport, potentials, in-medium collision terms, and applications to photon-, electron-, and neutrino-induced nuclear reactions [1].

node_64c952e8d768.summary: These papers develop and apply partial-wave analysis methods to baryon and meson spectroscopy, extracting resonance properties from pion, photon, charmonium, and diffractive production data.

questions.question: How can multichannel partial-wave analyses quantify the statistical necessity of weakly coupled inelastic channels in extracting baryon resonance pole positions and residues?
questions.rationale: The multichannel baryon analysis studies the statistical significance of pion- and photo-induced inelastic reactions, and the Roper study uses combined pion- and photo-induced data to determine P11 poles [1], [4].

questions.question: Can covariant tensor PWA formulae for J/psi and psi-prime decays be integrated with analyticity and unitarity constraints to reduce ambiguities in glueball, hybrid, and flavor-component assignments?
questions.rationale: The covariant tensor formalism supplies explicit decay formulae for meson spectroscopy, while the operator-expansion approach imposes analyticity and unitarity in combined production analyses [2], [3].

questions.question: Which resonance-model assumptions most affect the extraction of spin-exotic 1-+ light-meson signals from high-statistics diffractive three-pion data binned in mass and momentum transfer?
questions.rationale: The COMPASS-style analysis fits 14 selected waves across m_3pi and t-prime bins using Breit-Wigner amplitudes including spin-exotic quantum numbers [5].

node_e92caaeec6d8.summary: This cluster examines proton-antiproton threshold enhancements in J/psi, B, and electron-positron reactions, often interpreting them through final-state interactions or baryonium-like dynamics.

questions.question: Can one NNbar final-state-interaction framework reproduce the p pbar threshold enhancement in J/psi to gamma p pbar while explaining its absence in J/psi to pi0 p pbar?
questions.rationale: The contrast between the gamma and pi0 channels and the limits of current NNbar interaction knowledge are emphasized in [1] and [4].

questions.question: Which observables discriminate S-wave one-pion-exchange or G-parity-induced p pbar attraction from a narrow baryonium X(1860) quasi-bound state?
questions.rationale: The FSI explanations in [2] and [4] compete with the baryonium interpretation and decay criteria discussed in [5].

questions.question: How do Coulomb final-state interactions and baryon form factors explain non-vanishing e+e- to p pbar and Lambda anti-Lambda cross sections at threshold?
questions.rationale: The threshold behavior and Coulomb enhancement factor are the key unexpected features analyzed in [3].

node_47d5d1f3d9a0.summary: These studies use Compton scattering, dispersion relations, chiral perturbation theory, and lattice QCD to determine electromagnetic polarizabilities of pions, nucleons, and other hadrons.

questions.question: What combination of real and virtual Compton-scattering data would most decisively reduce the dispersion-relation uncertainty in nucleon dipole, spin, dispersion, and quadrupole polarizabilities?
questions.rationale: The dispersion-relation review [1] connects polarizabilities and sum rules to the nucleon excitation spectrum, while [4] identifies large-angle Compton experiments as especially important for uncertain structure parameters.

questions.question: Can the tension between two-loop chiral predictions and recent charged-pion dipole-polarizability measurements be resolved by improved low-energy constants, dispersion input, or a reassessment of the experimental extraction?
questions.rationale: The recalculation of gamma gamma -> pi+ pi- in [5] finds agreement with earlier theory for common LECs but conflict with the MAMI experimental result.

questions.question: How robust is resonance saturation for the p^6 counterterms entering neutral pion polarizabilities when confronted with dispersion-theory calculations and photon-photon data above threshold?
questions.rationale: The two-loop gamma gamma -> pi0 pi0 calculation [2] estimates three new counterterms with resonance saturation and compares favorably with data and dispersion calculations even above threshold.

node_aa053feb41f8.summary: This cluster centers on extracting nucleon electric, magnetic, and spin polarizabilities from real and virtual Compton scattering using dispersion relations and chiral effective theory.

questions.question: Which large-angle polarized Compton-scattering measurements would most reduce the uncertainty in nucleon spin polarizabilities and test the convergence of the low-energy expansion through order omega-four?
questions.rationale: The low-energy expansion analysis emphasizes that large-angle experiments can fix the most uncertain structure parameters and tests convergence of the expansion [2].

questions.question: Can fixed-t and fixed-theta dispersion relations be combined into a controlled extraction pipeline that consistently determines proton and neutron electric, magnetic, and spin polarizabilities across the first resonance region?
questions.rationale: The complementary roles of fixed-t and fixed-theta non-subtracted dispersion theories are presented as central tools for reproducing cross sections and extracting polarizabilities [4].

questions.question: How can chiral perturbation theory and dispersion-relation analyses isolate the Delta(1232) and non-analytic pion-loop contributions to the small empirical magnetic polarizability?
questions.rationale: The beyond-NLO chiral calculation identifies a cancellation between the positive Delta(1232) contribution and a non-analytic log pion-mass loop term [3].

node_4a228a84ff0c.summary: These papers compute electric and magnetic polarizabilities of neutrons, pions, kaons, and other hadrons in lattice QCD using background electromagnetic fields.

questions.question: What lattice strategy can reduce the dominant finite-volume and quark-mass extrapolation uncertainties in background-field determinations of nucleon electromagnetic and spin polarizabilities to the level needed for direct comparison with experiment?
questions.rationale: Finite-volume chiral perturbation theory found order-10% volume and quark-mass effects for current polarizability calculations [2].

questions.question: Can charged-hadron polarizabilities be extracted systematically across electric and magnetic background fields once Landau-level structure, boundary flux quantization, and Born-term-like magnetic-moment effects are treated in a unified analysis?
questions.rationale: This combines the nontrivial Landau-level treatment required for charged states [1], quantized uniform electric fields for charged mesons [4], and the need to separate magnetic moments from electric polarizabilities [3].

questions.question: Which features of the SU(3)-symmetric heavy-pion calculations of light nuclei survive toward physical quark masses, especially the apparent similarity between lattice nucleon magnetic polarizabilities and their physical values?
questions.rationale: The question follows from lattice calculations at m_pi around 806 MeV that found nucleon and light-nuclear magnetic properties, including polarizabilities, comparable in size to physical values [1].

node_80774e7a1f63.summary: These papers use chiral perturbation theory, dispersion relations, and photon-photon or Compton scattering data to determine charged and neutral pion electromagnetic polarizabilities.

questions.question: Can two-loop chiral perturbation theory with updated low-energy constants and Muskhelishvili-Omnes dispersive constraints resolve the charged-pion dipole-polarizability conflict with the MAMI result?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3], which finds a charged-pion polarizability prediction conflicting with MAMI, and [5], which applies MO representations to high-statistics Belle gamma gamma to pi pi data.

questions.question: How precisely must p^6 counterterms, resonance saturation estimates, and 1/Nc inputs be constrained to give consistent charged and neutral pion polarizabilities across gamma gamma to pi pi and gamma pi Compton channels?
questions.rationale: This combines the two-loop neutral and charged calculations in [1,4] with the 1/Nc estimates of electromagnetic constants and polarizabilities in [2].

questions.question: Can MO representations including KKbar inelasticity above 1 GeV cleanly separate subtraction constants tied to pion polarizabilities from left-hand-cut modeling?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [5], which extends the MO formalism beyond 1 GeV, includes KKbar inelasticity, and relates subtraction constants simply to pion polarizabilities.

node_72c9498d2bd7.summary: This broad cluster covers theoretical and phenomenological dark matter candidates, including dark photons, neutralinos, Higgs portals, self-interactions, gamma-ray signals, and links to neutrino mass.

questions.question: After null ton-scale WIMP searches, what portfolio of direct, indirect, collider, and astrophysical measurements would most efficiently decide whether the classic neutralino/Kaluza-Klein WIMP paradigm remains viable?
questions.rationale: This follows from broad WIMP candidate reviews and XENON1T's exclusion of new spin-independent WIMP-nucleon parameter space, together with Snowmass's call to search both deep and wide [1], [2], [3], [S1].
