questions.rationale: This directly synthesizes the small-scale Lambda-CDM tensions [1], the multi-scale SIDM program [2], the preferred velocity dependence from halo fits [3], and resonant angular-dependent scattering [4].

questions.question: Which halo observables can break the degeneracy between particle-physics self-interactions and baryonic explanations of cusp-core, missing-satellite, and too-big-to-fail tensions?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the review of small-scale challenges [1] and the SIDM claim of a universal explanation across mass scales [2].

node_cb7513cac156.summary: This cluster uses dwarf galaxies, satellite halos, colliding clusters, groups, and galaxy clusters to test velocity-dependent self-interacting dark matter models.

questions.question: Can a single velocity-dependent SIDM cross section sigma/m(v) inferred from dwarfs, low- and high-surface-brightness galaxies, groups, and clusters explain halo diversity after baryonic effects and selection functions are marginalized?
questions.rationale: This follows from the SIDM review across mass scales in [2] and the dwarf-to-cluster cross-section inference in [3].

questions.question: Which astrophysical systems most sharply distinguish elastic SIDM from dissipative hidden-sector or partially interacting double-disk dark matter while respecting BBN, recombination, and large-scale-structure constraints?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the dissipative hidden-sector constraints in [4] and the partially interacting double-disk scenario in [5].

questions.question: What joint likelihood over cusp-core, missing-satellites, and too-big-to-fail observables would decide whether small-scale tensions require self-interactions or can be absorbed within collisionless LambdaCDM systematics?
questions.rationale: This derives from the small-scale LambdaCDM challenges summarized in [1] and the SIDM interpretation of those challenges in [2].

node_cf5b44d5c482.summary: These works analyze light-mediator, Higgs-portal, and scalar-mediator self-interacting dark matter models under relic-density, direct-detection, indirect-detection, and cosmological constraints.

questions.question: Can velocity- and angle-dependent self-scattering in the quantum resonant regime be mapped accurately enough to predict dwarf, galaxy, and cluster halo structure from one particle model?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which develops methods for light-mediator SIDM beyond constant or classical cross-section regimes.

questions.question: Which combinations of relic-density, direct-detection, indirect-detection, and halo bounds still allow a single dark-force coupling to explain both thermal abundance and small-scale structure?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3] and [5], which connect Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation, self-scattering bounds, resonances, relic density, and halo phenomenology.

questions.question: How coarse can the ETHOS effective-parameter mapping be before microphysically distinct SIDM models cease to give similar linear power spectra and transfer cross sections?
questions.rationale: This derives from [4], which maps dark-sector microphysics into effective parameters for linear matter power and nonrelativistic self-interaction transfer cross sections.

node_02dcfeba27db.summary: These papers use rotation curves, stellar tracers, Gaia data, and modified-gravity comparisons to infer the Milky Way dark matter profile and test alternatives.

questions.question: Can Gaia-era non-axisymmetric and disequilibrium modeling reconcile the lower local dark-matter densities preferred by global Milky Way fits with the higher values from local analyses?
questions.rationale: Recent reviews report a persistent offset between local and global determinations and stress the need to go beyond the steady, axisymmetric Ideal Galaxy approximation [5].

questions.question: Which stellar tracer populations and velocity-anisotropy priors most strongly determine whether the Milky Way halo is inferred to be cored Burkert-like or cuspy NFW/Einasto-like?
questions.rationale: Cored-halo fits use terminal velocities, masers, and stellar-halo tracers with anisotropy freedom, while global analyses fit NFW or Einasto profiles with baryonic morphology uncertainties [1,4].

questions.question: Can abundance-selected distribution-function analyses over 4-12 kpc be extended to the inner Galaxy to decide where baryonic mass models fail to explain the rotation curve without dark matter?
questions.rationale: Action-based modeling of SEGUE mono-abundance populations tightly constrains disk and dark matter profiles, while rotation-curve compilations show inner-Galaxy evidence against baryons alone [2,3].

node_83d1e6d988bc.summary: This cluster focuses on measuring the Milky Way's local and inner dark matter density and velocity structure using stellar kinematics, Gaia observations, and dynamical modeling.

questions.question: How can Gaia-era local analyses and global rotation-curve analyses be combined without assuming an Ideal Galaxy, so that the local dark matter density tension between roughly 0.4-0.6 and 0.3-0.5 GeV/cm^3 is resolved?
questions.rationale: This question is directly motivated by the local-versus-global density ranges and Ideal Galaxy caveat in [5].

questions.question: Which stellar tracer populations and action-based distribution functions best break the degeneracy between disk surface density, halo shape, velocity anisotropy, and the local dark matter profile at 4-12 kpc?
questions.rationale: This follows from the abundance-selected SEGUE MAP modeling in [2] and the Jeans-equation treatment of halo-tracer anisotropies in [1].

questions.question: Can inner-Milky-Way rotation-curve evidence for dark matter discriminate between cored Burkert, generalized NFW, and Einasto profiles once baryonic bulge, disk, and gas morphologies are varied observationally?
questions.rationale: The profile-discrimination issue is grounded in the Burkert-versus-NFW comparison in [1], the baryon-only rejection in [3], and generalized NFW/Einasto fits in [4].

node_6a0dad2c4c56.summary: These works examine MOND, MOND-like dark matter, and other modified-gravity ideas through galactic rotation curves, acceleration relations, and Milky Way observables.

questions.question: What observation of galaxy rotation curves or acceleration relations would decisively distinguish MOND's low-acceleration scale invariance from dark-sector models engineered to reproduce MOND-like force laws on nonlinear scales?
questions.rationale: This derives from MOND's scale-invariant low-acceleration tenets in [2] and the MOND-like dark matter fluid construction in [5].

questions.question: Can the baryonic mass fraction and radial concentration inferred from flat rotation curves in ultra-light boson halo models reproduce the same regularities that MOND attributes to the acceleration constant a0?
questions.rationale: The question links the visible-matter fractions and extents in the late-time phase-transition boson halo model of [1] with the special role of a0 in [2].

questions.question: Do high-quality outer rotation-curve measurements reveal the predicted departure from asymptotic flatness in linear-potential conformal gravity, and how would that compare with MOND and LCDM interpretations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the claim in [4] that flatness may be only intermediate, set against the MOND-LCDM paradigm tension reviewed in [3].

node_88a5f3609c45.summary: This cluster studies ultralight or fuzzy dark matter models and constrains them using dwarf galaxies, soliton-halo relations, stellar heating, and galactic rotation curves.

questions.question: Can the Milky Way satellite census separate the fuzzy-dark-matter cutoff in halo formation from uncertainties in galaxy-halo mapping, disk disruption, and survey selection?
questions.rationale: Satellite-count analyses marginalize over detectability, galaxy-halo mapping, Milky Way properties, and disk disruption while setting strong fuzzy dark matter constraints [3].

questions.question: Do ultra-faint dwarfs and rotation-curve ripple searches favor the soliton-plus-CDM-like-envelope picture or the older Bose-liquid density-wave phenomenology?
questions.rationale: FDM predicts soliton cores with CDM-like envelopes and a minimum halo mass, while Bose-liquid models predict r^-1.6 profiles and ripple-like fine structures in rotation curves [1,2,4].

questions.question: How can dwarf-spheroidal phase-space bounds be consistently combined with wave-mechanical FDM constraints when the underlying assumptions differ between fermionic and bosonic dark matter?
questions.rationale: Dwarf phase-space methods give lower bounds for fermionic or model-dependent dark matter, whereas FDM constraints arise from de Broglie-scale suppression and soliton dynamics [1,5].

node_88a5f3609c45_1.summary: These papers test ultralight dark matter against Milky Way satellite galaxies and ultrafaint dwarfs, emphasizing limits from halo structure, stellar dynamics, and satellite counts.

questions.question: How robust are fuzzy-dark-matter lower bounds from the Milky Way satellite census once soliton-envelope halo structure, the minimum halo mass, disk disruption, detectability inhomogeneity, and galaxy-halo mapping uncertainties are treated together?
questions.rationale: This combines the FDM prediction of suppressed halo formation and soliton cores [1] with the satellite-census marginalization over detectability, galaxy-halo mapping, Milky Way properties, and disk disruption [2].

questions.question: Can core-oscillation heating of old star clusters in ultrafaint dwarfs be calibrated well enough to distinguish the FDM particle mass and fraction from conventional stellar-dynamical uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Eridanus II constraint based on density fluctuations, core oscillations, and star-cluster survival [5].

questions.question: Will new DES-like ultrafaint candidates, after completeness corrections, provide a decisive number-count test between CDM and small-scale-suppressed dark matter models?
questions.rationale: The question follows from DES ultrafaint discoveries [3], the completeness-corrected resolution of the missing-satellites problem in CDM [4], and the satellite-count constraints on warm, interacting, and fuzzy dark matter [2].

node_6b827ebdb009.summary: This cluster develops superfluid dark matter models in which condensed axion-like particles reproduce MOND-like galaxy dynamics while retaining cosmological dark matter behavior.

questions.question: Can one dark matter superfluid model simultaneously reproduce MOND-like phonon forces in galaxies and LambdaCDM-like behavior on cosmological scales without violating dwarf-galaxy phase-space bounds?
questions.rationale: Superfluid dark matter aims to unify MOND phenomenology and cosmological dark matter [3], while dwarf spheroidals impose lower bounds on allowed dark matter particle masses [2].

questions.question: What observable rotation-curve features would distinguish ripple-like Bose-liquid halo structure from solitonic cores in ultralight scalar-field dark matter?
questions.rationale: Late-transition Bose-liquid halos predict ripple-like rotation-curve fine structure [1], while scalar-field dark matter simulations predict soliton-dominated central density profiles [5].

questions.question: How do self-interaction strength, particle mass, and halo virial mass determine whether a galactic halo forms a superfluid core rather than a CDM-like outer profile?
questions.rationale: The superfluid theory uses eV-scale axion-like particles with strong self-interactions and a polytropic equation of state, while scalar-field halo profiles interpolate between cores and CDM-like outskirts [3],[5].

node_a0c7fd6e2453.summary: These papers investigate light neutralino dark matter in MSSM and NMSSM scenarios under relic-density, collider, Higgs, flavor, and direct-detection constraints.

questions.question: In light neutralino scenarios, what combination of relic density, direct detection, indirect detection, collider, Higgs, and flavor constraints would actually falsify the neutralino paradigm rather than only exclude individual MSSM or NMSSM parameter regions?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from dark-matter reviews emphasizing neutralinos as a leading WIMP candidate and from the Snowmass NMSSM study of post-Higgs relic abundance and detection constraints [1][2][S1].

questions.question: How accurately must coannihilation, resonant annihilation, and threshold effects be modeled to decide whether a light neutralino with mixed bino-higgsino or singlino composition can match the observed relic abundance?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the relic-density calculation showing that neutralino-chargino coannihilations, resonances, thresholds, and one-loop mass corrections can be essential across neutralino compositions [4].

questions.question: Can generic relic-density tools such as micrOMEGAs reliably compare MSSM, complex-phase MSSM, and NMSSM light-neutralino models when all annihilation and coannihilation channels feed both cosmology and indirect-detection predictions?
questions.rationale: The question derives from micrOMEGAs 2.0 automatically including annihilation and coannihilation channels in MSSM, complex MSSM, NMSSM, and other models, including v=0 cross sections for indirect detection [5].

node_8e9847973a10.summary: This cluster reviews supersymmetric neutralino dark matter and compares its discovery prospects across direct detection, indirect cosmic signals, and collider searches.

questions.question: What combination of direct detection, neutrino-based indirect detection, and collider measurements could decisively confirm or exclude neutralino dark matter once relic-density bounds narrow supersymmetric parameter space?
questions.rationale: This derives from neutralino dark-matter reviews comparing direct and indirect searches and from WMAP-era constraints reducing the CMSSM LSP mass range [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: How should neutralino search strategies change if the relevant supersymmetric dark matter is instead produced through late WIMP decays into superWIMPs, making conventional WIMP searches ineffective?
questions.rationale: This follows from superWIMP studies showing that such candidates evade conventional searches but affect BBN, the CMB, substructure, and collider signatures [4], [S1].

node_674f66027eb0.summary: These works connect supersymmetric dark matter candidates with LHC searches, cosmological constraints, and direct or indirect detection experiments.

questions.question: Which combination of collider limits, relic-density constraints, and direct or indirect searches can still distinguish neutralino WIMPs from superWIMP scenarios that evade conventional detection?
questions.rationale: The dark-matter reviews emphasize neutralino direct and indirect searches, while the superWIMP papers stress that gravitino or graviton superWIMPs can be invisible to conventional searches [1,2,4,S1].

questions.question: How robust are CMSSM upper limits on the LSP mass once WMAP-like relic-density restrictions are combined with current non-observation in laboratory dark-matter searches?
questions.rationale: The WMAP-era CMSSM study found that the allowed relic-density range significantly reduced the upper limit on the neutralino LSP mass [5].

questions.question: Can late-decaying WIMP scenarios simultaneously satisfy Big Bang nucleosynthesis, CMB, and small-scale-structure constraints while producing collider signatures distinct from standard supersymmetric dark matter?
questions.rationale: The superWIMP papers identify late decays, BBN, CMB distortions, galactic substructure, and collider signatures as defining tests [4,S1].

node_2a475394f275.summary: This cluster centers on calculating neutralino-nucleon scattering rates in MSSM and supergravity models and assessing their implications for direct detection experiments.

questions.question: Which hadronic matrix element measurement would most reduce the uncertainty in spin-independent neutralino-nucleon cross sections across MSSM and supergravity parameter scans?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by [2], which identifies the pi-nucleon sigma term and scalar matrix elements as the dominant uncertainty.

questions.question: Can twist-2, heavy-Higgs, and left-right squark-mixing contributions be organized into a standard calculation precise enough to compare direct-detection exclusions across constrained and non-universal Higgs MSSM models?
questions.rationale: The refined neutralino-nucleon amplitude in [3] and the NUHM1/NUHM2 phenomenology in [4] motivate this calculation-level question.

questions.question: Do current direct-detection limits still leave parameter regions where neutralino scattering would be the first evidence for supersymmetry rather than collider production?
questions.rationale: This updates the comparison between direct detection and collider searches emphasized in [5] and the lower cross-section bands found in [1].

node_49fe03b72716.summary: These papers study neutralino dark matter signals in neutrino telescopes and cosmic channels while comparing them with direct-detection anomalies and relic-density constraints.

questions.question: What neutralino spectra remain testable only through indirect neutrino signals from the Sun or Earth once relic density, direct detection, and 14 TeV or 100 TeV collider reach are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: Neutralino studies compare relic-density regions, direct searches, collider reach, and neutrino-telescope complementarity [1,3,4,5].

questions.question: How does the trade-off between kilometer-scale neutrino-telescope area and higher muon-energy threshold change for higgsino-like or coannihilating neutralinos favored by precision cosmological relic-density constraints?
questions.rationale: WMAP-era mSUGRA work highlights higgsino-like and coannihilating neutralinos, while neutrino-telescope studies emphasize the area-threshold trade-off for captured neutralino annihilation [2,5].

questions.question: Can relic-density calculations that avoid low-velocity expansions materially shift the indirect-detection expectations near annihilation thresholds and Breit-Wigner poles?
questions.rationale: The mSUGRA relic-density calculation explicitly includes relativistic Boltzmann averaging, threshold effects, and Breit-Wigner pole integration rather than a velocity expansion [1].

node_6919002be7d5.summary: This cluster examines low-mass neutralino dark matter in MSSM and NMSSM frameworks, focusing on viability after collider, Higgs, flavor, relic-abundance, and direct-detection bounds.

questions.question: After Higgs, collider, flavor, relic-density, and direct-detection constraints, is a low-mass neutralino still naturally viable, or only viable through well-tempered, focus-point, singlino, bino, or coannihilation special regions?
questions.rationale: This combines the well-tempered neutralino fine-tuning argument [2], focus-point mixed gaugino-Higgsino viability [3], Higgs-mass implications for SUSY spectra [4], and NMSSM Snowmass scenarios [S1].

questions.question: Can collider measurements determine neutralino mixing and superpartner masses accurately enough to predict the relic density and direct-detection cross sections at the precision required by astrophysical searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from the collider dark-matter study showing that accelerator measurements can infer cosmic density, annihilation rates, and direct-detection cross sections, with the ILC playing a key role [5].

questions.question: Which annihilation channels and soft-parameter relations most control whether minimal supergravity models overclose the universe or yield a cosmologically interesting neutralino abundance?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the mSUGRA relic-density calculation that included all neutralino annihilation processes for general mixed neutralino states and broad Planck-scale soft parameters [1].

node_35997bdbcc3c.summary: These papers test whether very light MSSM or NMSSM neutralinos can satisfy relic-density, collider, flavor, and direct or indirect detection constraints, often using light Higgs or near-degenerate superpartner annihilation channels.

questions.question: Is the well-tempered neutralino still the most plausible path to the correct relic density once Higgs-mass, LEP, LHC, and direct-detection constraints are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that LEP constraints make the correct relic density require sensitive parameter relations and from later implications of a 125 GeV Higgs for SUSY spectra [2], [4].

questions.question: Can focus-point or mixed gaugino-Higgsino scenarios preserve robust neutralino dark matter while pushing scalar superpartners to multi-TeV masses?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by focus-point supersymmetry, where multi-TeV scalars and mixed gaugino-Higgsino neutralinos remain compatible with relic density and direct-detection prospects [3].

questions.question: What collider measurements would determine neutralino microscopic properties accurately enough to predict relic density and detection cross sections without assuming a tightly constrained SUSY model?
questions.rationale: This derives from studies showing how high-energy collider data, especially from the ILC, could determine dark matter density and scattering or annihilation rates in neutralino models [5].

node_43651d5ed81a.summary: This cluster studies NMSSM scenarios where singlino-like or higgsino-like neutralinos provide dark matter while remaining compatible with Higgs measurements, naturalness, collider searches, and direct detection limits.

questions.question: Where in singlino-bino-higgsino neutralino parameter space do Higgs-sector blind spots suppress spin-independent direct detection while preserving the observed relic density and post-Higgs collider constraints?
questions.rationale: This combines MSSM blind-spot cancellations in Higgs exchange [4], Snowmass NMSSM coverage of singlino, bino, and higgsino dark matter [S1], and near-PQ NMSSM singlino dark matter [5].

questions.question: Can the near-Peccei-Quinn NMSSM window with light scalar, pseudoscalar, and singlino states still achieve relic density through pseudoscalar annihilation and scalar-mediated nucleon scattering under current searches?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the Dark Light Higgs scenario with 0.1-10 GeV singlet-like states, singlino dark matter, pseudoscalar annihilation, and scalar exchange with nucleons [5].

questions.question: Which combination of inelastic scattering, EDMs, LHC higgsino production, IceCube sensitivity, and direct detection can distinguish high-scale higgsino or mixed bino-higgsino dark matter from singlino NMSSM dark matter?
questions.rationale: This follows from mixed bino-higgsino detection prospects [2], high-scale higgsino constraints from inelastic scattering, EDMs, and production [3], and Snowmass NMSSM detection channels [S1].

node_b4a6e9b89969.summary: These works compute neutralino relic abundances including coannihilations with sleptons, charginos, squarks, stops, and other superpartners, showing how near-degenerate spectra reshape cosmologically allowed MSSM and NMSSM parameter space.

questions.question: How accurately must near-degenerate neutralino, chargino, slepton, squark, and gluino spectra be computed for coannihilation thresholds and resonances to determine the relic density?
questions.rationale: The neutralino relic-density and micrOMEGAs papers stress exact coannihilation channels, loop-corrected masses, and careful treatment of poles and thresholds [1],[3],[5].

questions.question: Can automated relic-density tools maintain reliable uncertainties when extended from MSSM and NMSSM coannihilation to arbitrary R-parity-like dark-sector models?
questions.rationale: micrOMEGAs 2.0 generalizes automatic annihilation and coannihilation calculations to arbitrary models implemented in CalcHEP under a stabilizing conservation law [2].

questions.question: What observational signature would distinguish thermally underabundant wino dark matter from wino dark matter replenished by pre-BBN moduli decay?
questions.rationale: The anomaly-mediated wino scenario finds thermal wino relic density too small but moduli decays before BBN can produce enough winos for cold dark matter [4].

node_9dfa55ec1a58.summary: This cluster centers on accurate computational treatments of neutralino dark matter relic density, especially micrOMEGAs-style calculations including annihilation and coannihilation channels across supersymmetric models.

questions.question: How large are the relic-density errors from treating near-threshold, resonant, and coannihilation channels at tree level in automated tools for neutralino-like dark matter?
questions.rationale: This follows from the careful pole, threshold, and exact tree-level coannihilation treatments in [1], [3], and [4].

questions.question: Can a model-independent relic-density code interface automatically determine when all coannihilations are required, analogous to the MSSM criterion |mu| less than about 2|M1|?
questions.rationale: The need is motivated by the all-channel automation of micrOMEGAs2.0 in [2] and the neutralino-chargino coannihilation criterion found in [1].

questions.question: Which analytically controlled coannihilation sectors should be used as benchmark tests for future relic-density tools beyond the CMSSM?
questions.rationale: Neutralino-stau, selectron, and smuon coannihilation channels provide detailed analytic and numerical benchmarks in [5].

node_40b4c5033d7b.summary: These papers evaluate QCD, SUSY-QCD, electroweak, and higher-order loop corrections to neutralino annihilation or coannihilation processes and their impact on relic density and gamma-ray signals.

questions.question: At what neutralino masses and compositions must one replace fixed one-loop gamma-line annihilation calculations by a nonrelativistic all-order treatment to preserve unitarity?
questions.rationale: The higher-order study finds that heavy wino-like and Higgsino-like neutralinos can violate unitarity at one loop and require multi-state nonrelativistic corrections [3].

questions.question: How should loop-induced two-photon and Z-gamma line rates be combined with Sommerfeld-enhanced coannihilation in relic-density calculations for arbitrary MSSM neutralino mixtures?
questions.rationale: Full one-loop gamma-line calculations and multi-state Sommerfeld relic-density formalism both produce order-level changes in relevant neutralino parameter regions [1].

node_d963f086139b.summary: This cluster analyzes loop-induced and QCD-corrected dark-matter scattering or annihilation signals, especially for wino, higgsino, electroweak multiplet, and pseudoscalar-mediator dark matter models.

questions.question: Can loop-level direct-detection predictions for pure electroweak multiplet dark matter be pushed beyond leading order enough to resolve the accidental cancellation between quark and gluon contributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which finds comparable one- and two-loop contributions to nucleon scattering with an accidental cancellation in the spin-independent cross section.

questions.question: How do Sommerfeld enhancement, gamma-ray line limits, and halo-profile uncertainties jointly determine whether thermal or nonthermal wino dark matter survives indirect detection?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the relic-density Sommerfeld effect in [2] and the H.E.S.S. and Fermi constraints in [3] and [4].

questions.question: Can nonthermal moduli decay histories produce the correct wino abundance while evading both BBN reheating constraints and the current continuum and line gamma-ray bounds?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], which motivates wino production from moduli decays before BBN, and [4], which stresses strong indirect limits on light nonthermal winos.

node_030e2100983d.summary: These papers survey heavy neutral Z-prime gauge bosons, covering theoretical motivations, electroweak precision constraints, collider discovery prospects, coupling measurements, and possible flavor-anomaly interpretations.

questions.question: If a heavy neutral resonance is discovered, which minimal set of collider observables can determine whether it is a Z' gauge boson and distinguish among anomaly-free U(1)' benchmark models?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass diagnosis study focuses on measuring mass, width, and asymmetries at the LHC and ILC to distinguish benchmark Z' models after discovery [S1].

questions.question: How model-independent can Z' limits remain when electroweak precision constraints, Z-Z' mixing, branching fractions to leptons, and quark-coupling assumptions are varied simultaneously?
questions.rationale: Tevatron and general phenomenology papers emphasize parametrized dilepton signals, Z-Z' mixing limits, radiative corrections, systematic errors, kinematic cuts, and model assumptions in deriving constraints [2,3].

questions.question: Can a single renormalizable Z' framework explain flavor anomalies or hidden-sector dark matter while surviving meson mixing and precision Z-pole constraints?
questions.rationale: L_mu-L_tau models address B -> K* mu+ mu- tensions subject to light-flavor meson-mixing constraints, while Stueckelberg kinetic-mixing models fit precision LEP data and allow hidden-sector milli-charged matter [4,5].

node_d19987f9de0b.summary: This cluster focuses on how Tevatron, LHC, and future collider observables can discover, constrain, and distinguish Z-prime bosons through dilepton signals, cross sections, asymmetries, and coupling measurements.

questions.question: If a dilepton resonance is discovered, which minimal set of LHC and ILC observables can determine the Z-prime mass, width, quark couplings, lepton couplings, and kinetic mixing well enough to distinguish anomaly-free U(1)' models?
questions.rationale: Z-prime reviews emphasize masses, couplings, anomaly-free models, collider diagnostics, and kinetic mixing, while Snowmass studies focus on mass, width, and asymmetry measurements at the LHC and ILC [1][3][4][S1].

questions.question: How model independent can hadron-collider Z-prime exclusion reaches be when branching fractions to leptons, exotic fermions, extended Higgs sectors, or neutralinos vary across viable U(1)' scenarios?
questions.rationale: The Tevatron parametrization separates mass, leptonic branching fraction, and average quark couplings, while general Z-prime models may include exotic fermions, extended Higgs sectors, and neutralino sectors [1][2][5].

node_d19987f9de0b_1.summary: These works combine electroweak precision data, LEP measurements, atomic parity violation, and collider searches to constrain extra neutral gauge bosons and their mixing with the Standard Model Z.

questions.question: What model-independent combination of dilepton resonance data, electroweak precision observables, and low-energy parity measurements would most decisively separate a true U(1)' gauge boson from benchmark-model assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the tension between canonical Z' benchmarks and the more general constraints from collider, Z-pole, and low-energy data discussed in [3] and [4].

questions.question: If a TeV-scale neutral resonance is found, which small set of LHC and ILC observables can robustly diagnose its mass, width, quark couplings, lepton couplings, and possible Z-Z' mixing?
questions.rationale: Snowmass studies emphasize that discovery is not enough and that asymmetries, widths, and collider complementarity are needed to distinguish Z' models [S1].

questions.question: How much of the viable nonexotic, anomaly-free U(1)' parameter space remains after simultaneously imposing fermion-mass generation, right-handed neutrino requirements, kinetic mixing, and current collider bounds?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the two-parameter anomaly-free charge families and mass-coupling bounds derived for nonexotic neutral gauge bosons [5].

node_cd0b4425fcff.summary: This cluster develops collider strategies and minimal or model-independent parameterizations for detecting Z-prime bosons and extracting their couplings across broad classes of electroweak extensions.

questions.question: What minimal set of resonance and angular observables would turn a dilepton Z-prime discovery into a model-independent determination of normalized quark and lepton couplings?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1], [3], and [S1] emphasize parametrizations bridging collider searches to models and the use of asymmetries, width, and coupling measurements for diagnosis.

questions.question: How robust are the c_u and c_d narrow-width parameterizations once Z-Z-prime mixing, kinetic mixing, and finite-width effects become non-negligible?
questions.rationale: Refs. [4] and [5] use c_u, c_d or minimal three-parameter descriptions while noting mass and kinetic mixing effects can be sizable.

questions.question: If no clear resonance is accessible, which collider combination most efficiently converts indirect dilepton deviations into exclusions across broad U(1)' benchmark families?
questions.rationale: Refs. [S1] and [S2] frame the complementarity of LHC, high-luminosity or higher-energy hadron colliders, and the ILC for Z-prime exclusion or diagnosis.

node_b06f1b7c1267.summary: These papers emphasize indirect precision constraints on extra U(1) or E6-inspired Z-prime bosons, especially bounds on their masses, mixings, and effects in low-energy neutral-current observables.

questions.question: What model-independent electroweak observable would most cleanly separate Z-Z-prime mass mixing from U(1) gauge kinetic mixing in extra neutral gauge boson searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from the general renormalizable SU(2)xU(1)xU(1) treatment emphasizing kinetic mixing and low-energy plus Z-pole constraints [3].

questions.question: How robust are indirect TeV-scale Z-prime mass limits once anomaly cancellation, generation-independent charges, radiative corrections, systematic errors, and collider cuts are varied together?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in reviews stressing model assumptions, radiative corrections, systematics, and the two-parameter nonexotic charge family for neutral gauge bosons [2],[4],[5].

node_c8e15065e3b2.summary: This cluster studies W-prime and associated Z-prime bosons in left-right or SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) models, particularly interpretations of early LHC diboson, dijet, Wh, and eejj excesses near 2 TeV.

questions.question: What correlated Wprime, Zprime, dijet, dilepton, Wh, and eejj signal pattern would survive current precision bounds in a general SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) model?
questions.rationale: The global G(221) analysis constrains heavy gauge bosons with electroweak precision data, while the 2 TeV Wprime model predicts associated Zprime signals and multiple LHC final states [1,2].

questions.question: Can a charged Wprime near 2 TeV be interpreted without a nearly degenerate or heavier neutral companion once combined lepton-plus-missing-energy and dilepton searches are imposed?
questions.rationale: The model-independent vector-boson analysis argues that observable Wprime signals with leptonic final states generically correlate with companion Zprime states and improve limits when searches are combined [3].

questions.question: Do heavy-Higgs cascade decays provide a viable explanation of the historical 2 TeV Wprime excesses without conflicting with dijet and diboson constraints?
questions.rationale: The left-right model study finds sizable Wprime branching fractions into heavy Higgs bosons and relates them to same-sign lepton plus b-jet excess interpretations [5].

node_7b4f74a46bfd.summary: These papers study nonuniversal Z′ and related gauge extensions that generate b→sℓℓ flavor-changing currents to explain LHCb B-decay anomalies and sometimes the muon g−2 discrepancy under collider and flavor constraints.

questions.question: What single pattern across B→K(*)μμ angular observables, R(K), τ→3μ, and pp→Z′→μμ would distinguish an L_mu-L_tau Z′ from more generic family-nonuniversal Z′ explanations of the flavor anomalies?
questions.rationale: The L_mu-L_tau model links B→K*μμ and τ decay tensions, while the horizontal-gauge model connects B anomalies, h→μτ, τ→3μ, and direct dimuon searches [1].

questions.question: Can anomaly-free ultraviolet completions with heavy fermions keep the needed b→sμμ coupling while satisfying light-meson mixing, Z-Z′ mixing, and direct low-mass muonic-force bounds?
questions.rationale: The quark-transition study constructs an anomaly-free heavy-fermion completion and emphasizes meson-mixing constraints, while BABAR excludes parts of the low-mass muonic Z′ parameter space [1].

node_38c1c972f2b8.summary: This cluster focuses on gauged Lμ−Lτ and flavored U(1)′ Z′ models linking B-meson lepton-universality anomalies with muon g−2 while testing their viability against LHC, electroweak, and mixing bounds.

questions.question: Can an anomaly-free gauged Lμ-Lτ framework with quark couplings provide a single coherent fit to B -> K* mu+mu-, R(K), tau -> mu nu nu, and muon g-2 once meson mixing and dimuon-resonance bounds are imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the combined anomaly targets, renormalizable quark-coupling construction, flavor constraints, and g-2 motivation in [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Which renormalizable UV completions with heavy fermions or horizontal charges predict sufficiently aligned quark-Z' couplings, rather than arbitrary flavor structures, while still generating realistic fermion mixing matrices?
questions.rationale: This derives from the heavy-fermion completion of quark transitions in [1] and the horizontal U(1)' flavor construction in [2].

questions.question: What low-mass muonic-Z' or pp -> Z' -> mu+mu- result would decisively close, or isolate, the parameter space relevant to the B-anomaly and muon-sector interpretations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the BABAR muonic dark-force limits in [3] and the direct LHC dimuon constraints emphasized in [2].

node_e28e92d817b2.summary: These works examine light or weakly coupled Lμ−Lτ Z′ bosons motivated by muon g−2 and flavor anomalies, emphasizing kinetic mixing and searches at Belle II, electron colliders, and the LHC.

questions.question: Can a light or weakly coupled L_mu - L_tau gauge boson still explain the muon g-2 discrepancy once BABAR muonic dark-force bounds and neutrino constraints are combined over the full 0.212-10 GeV mass range?
questions.rationale: This follows from the original L_mu - L_tau g-2 parameter regions and the BABAR exclusion limits on e+e- -> mu+mu- Z', Z' -> mu+mu- [2,3].

questions.question: What renormalizable anomaly-free completion of L_mu - L_tau with heavy fermions can generate the quark couplings needed for b -> s mu+ mu- anomalies while satisfying light-meson mixing and tau-decay constraints?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the construction where heavy fermions induce quark couplings for an L_mu - L_tau Z' and are restricted by flavor mixing and tau decay data [1].

questions.question: Can searches for lepton-flavor-violating B decays distinguish generic Z' explanations of b -> s mu+ mu- anomalies from specifically L_mu - L_tau motivated models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the study of B -> K(*) tau mu, Bs -> tau mu, and related lepton-flavor-violating modes in generic Z' models motivated by LHCb anomalies [4].

node_c3ed81d6f72a.summary: This cluster develops anomaly-free flavored U(1)′ extensions with generation-dependent charges, vectorlike matter, or hidden sectors to explain RK, RK*, RD, and related B-meson anomalies.

questions.question: What minimal anomaly-free flavored U(1)' charge structure can still reproduce the observed b -> s l+l- Wilson-coefficient pattern while satisfying flavor constraints and direct pp -> Z' -> mu+mu- searches?
questions.rationale: This follows from the flavored horizontal U(1)' explanation of B -> K* mu+mu-, R(K), and related LHC dimuon constraints in [1] and the predictive Wilson-coefficient correlations in [3].

questions.question: Do light flavored or baryonic U(1)' models remain viable once heavy-fermion anomaly cancellation is integrated out, or do Wess-Zumino interactions make Z decays and FCNC meson decays decisive?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the anomaly-induced Wess-Zumino interactions and longitudinal-vector enhancements derived for light vectors coupled to anomalous currents in [4].

questions.question: Which experimentally accessible correlation would best distinguish leptophobic Z-Z' mixing explanations from family-nonuniversal U(1)' models: LEP-style R_b/R_c shifts, lepton-universality-violating Z' decays, or B-anomaly observables?
questions.rationale: This compares the leptophobic generation-independent Z-Z' mixing constructions of [2] with the family-nonuniversal flavor-changing models and Z' decay tests of [3].

node_e351c5cc14b4.summary: These papers analyze how family nonuniversal Z′ bosons with tree-level flavor-changing neutral currents affect rare B decays, B mixing, CP asymmetries, and long-standing B→πK puzzles.

questions.question: Can Delta F=2 observables and b to s mu+mu- angular and branching data overconstrain left-handed Z-prime flavor-changing couplings and distinguish them from anomalous Z-penguin scenarios?
questions.rationale: This is based on the sensitivity of rare semileptonic b to s transitions to nonstandard Z couplings [2] and the program for determining left-handed Z-prime or Z FCNC couplings from Delta F=2 and b to s mu+mu- observables [4].

questions.question: Which family-nonuniversal Z-prime coupling textures can solve the B to pi K electroweak-penguin puzzle while remaining compatible with B to phi K_S CP asymmetries, B_s,d to mu+mu-, LEP-II, and LHC constraints?
questions.rationale: The question combines the general formalism for family-nonuniversal Z-prime flavor violation [1], the B to pi K solution via enhanced electroweak penguins [5], and 331-model constraints from rare B data and collider bounds [3].

node_dc026672d180.summary: This cluster explores particle-physics explanations of the ATOMKI 8Be electron-positron excess using a roughly 17 MeV X boson with protophobic, axial-vector, or pseudoscalar couplings.

questions.question: Which spin-parity assignment for a 17 MeV boson can simultaneously fit the 8Be pair-production anomaly, the absence of related nuclear-transition anomalies, and existing beam-dump and flavor constraints?
questions.rationale: Vector, pseudoscalar, and axial-vector explanations face different nuclear matrix-element, beam-dump, and flavor constraints across [1],[2],[3],[4].

questions.question: Can ab initio nuclear calculations reduce the uncertainty in 8Be transition matrix elements enough to distinguish protophobic vector couplings from primarily axial light-quark couplings?
questions.rationale: The axial-vector interpretation depends on ab initio 8Be matrix elements from chiral EFT and in-medium similarity renormalization group calculations [4], while the protophobic model relies on specific suppressed proton and enhanced neutron couplings [1].

node_21d1ab0a0448.summary: These works interpret the CDF II W-boson mass discrepancy through electroweak fits and new physics such as extended Higgs sectors, triplet seesaws, singlets, vectorlike leptons, dark matter, and muon g−2 connections.

questions.question: Can the CDF II W-mass shift be reconciled with global electroweak precision data by a Stueckelberg Z-prime sector without spoiling LEP Z-pole fits and hidden-sector millicharge constraints?
questions.rationale: Stueckelberg extensions with kinetic mixing can fit LEP precision data closely and generate hidden-sector millicharges, while the CDF II W mass motivates new oblique-parameter fits [1], [4].

questions.question: Which pattern of S, T, and U deviations would distinguish non-degenerate multiplets from real-singlet scalar extensions as an explanation of the W-boson mass anomaly?
questions.rationale: The electroweak fit points to oblique parameters consistent with non-degenerate multiplets, while the singlet extension constrains Delta r and the corresponding W-mass prediction [4], [5].

questions.question: Do low-mass Stueckelberg Z-prime resonances with uniquely suppressed vector and axial couplings remain viable once W-mass, forward-backward asymmetry, and fermion-branching-ratio data are fit simultaneously?
questions.rationale: The Stueckelberg model predicts a massive Z-prime with mixing-suppressed fermion couplings, distinctive branching ratios, and forward-backward asymmetries [2], [3].

node_d3fdaef7abdb.summary: This broad cluster covers collider searches for long-lived particles and heavy Majorana neutrinos, including displaced decays, lepton-number violation, same-sign dileptons, and dedicated lifetime-frontier detectors.

questions.question: Which lifetime and mass regions for heavy neutral leptons remain uncovered when rare meson and tau decays, main LHC displaced searches, MATHUSLA-like detectors, and EIC prompt/displaced strategies are combined?
questions.rationale: This combines resonant Majorana-neutrino bounds from rare decays in [1], LLP detector motivation in [2], LHC displaced-signature coverage in [3], and EIC reach projections in [S1].

questions.question: What experimental signature would most cleanly establish the Majorana nature of a long-lived neutral lepton rather than merely discovering a displaced neutral particle?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which emphasizes that Majorana neutrinos are experimentally verified through charged-lepton lepton-number-violating processes.

questions.question: Can neutral-lepton searches motivated by the nuMSM simultaneously satisfy oscillation, dark-matter, baryogenesis, and cosmological interaction-strength bounds while remaining observable in meson decays or pp collisions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nuMSM analysis in [5], which links neutrino oscillations, dark matter, baryon asymmetry, cosmological bounds, and production in meson decays and pp collisions.

node_ddc17d0f2c40.summary: These papers study lepton-number-violating signatures of heavy Majorana neutrinos in meson, tau, top, hadron-collider, lepton-collider, and lepton-proton processes.

questions.question: How can mass-mixing constraints on heavy Majorana neutrinos be consistently combined across resonant 100 MeV to 5 GeV meson and tau decays and 10 to 400 GeV collider production?
questions.rationale: This follows from the resonant rare-decay program in [1], the global heavy-neutrino mixing fit in [2], and the hadron-collider mass ranges studied in [3].

questions.question: What analysis strategy can control like-sign dilepton backgrounds enough for pp -> W -> l N -> l l jj searches to reach their true LHC sensitivity?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4], which shows that like-sign dilepton backgrounds are much larger than simple parton-level estimates and require likelihood analysis.

questions.question: How complementary are FCC-ee neutrino counting and direct heavy-neutrino decay searches with rare Delta L=2 meson and tau decays in verifying the Majorana nature of neutrinos?
questions.rationale: This derives from the statement in [1] that Majorana nature requires charged-lepton lepton-number violation and from the FCC-ee counting/direct-search sensitivities in [5].

node_5934887a8a11.summary: This cluster emphasizes collider production of heavy Majorana neutrinos through like-sign dilepton plus jets and related channels at hadron, lepton, and lepton-proton machines.

questions.question: Across the 100 MeV to few-hundred-GeV mass range, how can collider and rare-decay searches be combined into a single heavy Majorana neutrino mixing analysis without losing sensitivity to resonant lepton-number violation?
questions.rationale: Rare tau and meson decays constrain resonant Majorana neutrinos in [1], while hadron and lepton collider searches are developed in [3], [4], and [5].

questions.question: What analysis strategy for like-sign dilepton plus jets can robustly recover LHC sensitivity after realistic detector backgrounds reduce the reach relative to parton-level estimates?
questions.rationale: The fast-simulation study in [4] found like-sign dilepton backgrounds 100 to 1000 times larger than assumed in earlier estimates such as [3].

questions.question: How should FCC-ee neutrino counting and direct heavy-neutrino decay searches be combined with electroweak precision and flavor constraints to identify viable seesaw parameter regions?
questions.rationale: FCC-ee sensitivities in [5] probe heavy neutral leptons directly, while [2] shows that electroweak precision, flavor, CKM unitarity, and universality data impose correlated mixing limits.

node_c18bd1f177ff.summary: These works focus on heavy Majorana neutrino discovery at proton colliders via lepton-number-violating same-sign dilepton and multilepton final states with realistic backgrounds and mixing limits.

questions.question: What analysis strategy can recover heavy Majorana neutrino sensitivity in same-sign dilepton plus jets final states once realistic like-sign lepton backgrounds are included?
questions.rationale: Fast detector studies found that backgrounds are 10^2-10^3 larger than earlier parton-level estimates and cannot be removed by simple sequential cuts [3].

questions.question: How can collider same-sign dilepton searches be consistently combined with rare meson and tau decay bounds across the 100 MeV to sub-TeV Majorana-neutrino mass range?
questions.rationale: Rare meson and tau decays constrain resonant Majorana neutrinos below a few GeV, while hadron-collider studies target heavier resonant production [1], [2].

questions.question: Which dimension-six effective operators involving sub-TeV Majorana neutrinos produce distinguishable same-sign dilepton signatures beyond minimal mixing-driven production?
questions.rationale: The effective-Lagrangian study shows that leading operators can generate large same-sign lepton-number-violating l+l+jj event rates at the LHC [4].

node_4b4063a0a130.summary: This cluster studies prospects for detecting heavy Dirac or Majorana neutrinos at future e+e− and e−e− colliders through single production, pair production, and lepton-number-violating final states.

questions.question: How can future e+e- collider searches combine neutrino counting, direct heavy-neutrino decays, and electroweak/flavor-universality data to distinguish generic heavy-neutrino mixing from the correlated three-heavy-state seesaw case?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between global-fit constraints on general versus minimal heavy-neutrino scenarios in [1] and the FCC-ee neutrino-counting and direct-search program in [2].

questions.question: What mix of e+e- channels such as e+2j+missing energy and lepton-number-violating same-sign dileptons with jets gives the best simultaneous reach for heavy-neutrino discovery and for establishing Majorana rather than Dirac character?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] identifies e+2j+missing energy as the strongest discovery mode but emphasizes that same-sign dilepton channels are needed to probe lepton-number violation.

questions.question: Can tau-flavor heavy-neutrino mixing be constrained at future lepton colliders in a way that closes the gap between low-mass beam-dump limits and electroweak-scale Majorana-neutrino searches?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the tau-mixing limits from CHARM in [4] and the electroweak-scale seesaw collider regions mapped in [5].

node_e16324a94737.summary: These papers study lepton-number-violating rare decays of mesons, baryons, top quarks, and W bosons mediated by resonant heavy Majorana neutrinos.

questions.question: Across rare K, D, B, B_c, W, and collider displaced-vertex channels, which mass-mixing region for an intermediate Majorana neutrino gives the strongest realistic discovery reach for lepton-number violation rather than only improved exclusion limits?
questions.rationale: Resonant meson-decay reach in the intermediate mass window is studied in [1], while the collider mass-mixing regimes for observable LNV are classified in [5].

questions.question: Can nearly degenerate heavy neutrinos produce simultaneously observable CP asymmetries and resolvable neutrino-antineutrino oscillations, and what relation between mass splitting, width, and lifetime is required?
questions.rationale: Large resonant CP asymmetries for Delta m_N comparable to Gamma_N are derived in [2], while displaced heavy-neutrino oscillations are proposed in [4].

node_a67fb872e7e4.summary: This cluster surveys theoretical motivations, collider signatures, and proposed LHC detector strategies for discovering beyond-Standard-Model long-lived particles.

questions.question: What detector configuration closes the lifetime gap for neutral, non-hadronic LLPs with c tau near the BBN limit that main LHC detectors cannot efficiently trigger on or reconstruct?
questions.rationale: The MATHUSLA papers argue that neutral LLPs with lifetimes above about 100 m, especially near c tau up to 10^7-10^8 m, are poorly covered by main detectors and motivate a surface detector [1], [4].

questions.question: How should LHC LLP searches be organized so that displaced vertices, atypical tracks, short track segments, and far-detector decays cover the same benchmark models without blind spots?
questions.rationale: The collider review stresses that LLPs require customized reconstruction for displaced vertices, unusual tracks, and short segments, while MATHUSLA and CODEX-b target complementary far-detector signatures [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: For Higgs-portal dark photons and B-meson decays through a Higgs mixing portal, what determines whether LHCb-based compact detectors outperform or complement SHiP and MATHUSLA?
questions.rationale: The CODEX-b proposal studies Higgs decays to dark photons and B decays via a Higgs mixing portal and compares its reach and complementarity with SHiP and MATHUSLA [3].

node_ab27e88f7546.summary: These works review and model heavy neutral lepton production, decay, constraints, and future sensitivity across collider, fixed-target, beta-decay, astrophysical, and cosmological probes.

questions.question: Can a global HNL sensitivity framework consistently combine meson-decay, pp-collision, beta-decay, collider, fixed-target, astrophysical, and cosmological constraints for arbitrary flavor-mixing patterns rather than benchmark dominance assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from nuMSM production and decay bounds [1], the broad experimental status review [2], GeV-scale channel refinements [3], and SHiP tools for arbitrary flavor mixings [4].

questions.question: Which production and decay channels around the GeV scale dominate HNL reach once QCD corrections and detector acceptance for prompt versus displaced searches are included experiment by experiment?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in revised GeV-scale HNL phenomenology with QCD corrections [3], SHiP displaced-decay sensitivity over long baselines [4], and EIC prompt/displaced strategies with detector thresholds and geometry [S1].

node_7a94ee1d7d1c.summary: This cluster focuses on displaced-vertex collider signatures from long-lived heavy neutrinos, exotic Higgs decays, doubly charged scalars, supersymmetric states, and baryogenesis-motivated particles.

questions.question: What displaced-vertex search strategy gives simultaneous coverage of exotic Higgs decays, heavy neutrinos, R-parity violation, and baryogenesis-motivated weak-scale decays without losing efficiency to standard track-quality cuts?
questions.rationale: The common detector-scale displaced-vertex challenge appears in Higgs decays [1], B-L heavy neutrinos [2], displaced supersymmetry [3], and baryogenesis models [4].

questions.question: Can measurements of heavy-neutrino mass, decay length, and flavor-specific final states at ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb be combined to infer the light-neutrino mass scale or mixing pattern?
questions.rationale: The possibility of estimating the parent light-neutrino mass from heavy-neutrino mass and decay length is raised in [2], and detector sensitivities are quantified in [5].

questions.question: How much sensitivity is gained by extending displaced heavy-neutrino searches beyond the tracker into muon chambers, and what backgrounds ultimately limit that program at the HL-LHC?
questions.rationale: A muon-chamber displaced search for heavy neutrino decays outside the tracker is proposed in [5].

node_d2a56b1aa79f.summary: These papers examine left-right symmetric theories, including their LHC signals, CP and flavor constraints, supersymmetric variants, neutrino mass generation, baryogenesis, Higgs sectors, and dark matter candidates.

questions.question: Can mirror- or twin-sector constructions provide a unified and testable paradigm for natural electroweak symmetry breaking, sterile-neutrino lightness, and cosmological consistency without introducing visible colored top partners?
questions.rationale: This question synthesizes the mirror-sector sterile-neutrino motivation in [2], asymmetric reheating solution to nucleosynthesis constraints in [3], and Standard-Model-neutral twin top partners in [1] and [4].

questions.question: What collider observation would most decisively distinguish dark naturalness via exotic Higgs decays to displaced twin hadrons from conventional left-right symmetry breaking with low- or intermediate-scale composite scalars?
questions.rationale: The contrast follows from the displaced Higgs-decay phenomenology emphasized in [4] and the extra scalar and lepton-flavor-violation signatures predicted in the dynamical left-right model of [5].

questions.question: How low can the right-handed or mirror-sector symmetry-breaking scale be while remaining compatible with neutrino data, big-bang nucleosynthesis, precision electroweak constraints, and low-energy lepton-flavor bounds?
questions.rationale: This combines the larger mirror electroweak scale used for neutrino puzzles in [2], asymmetric reheating in [3], precision-safe twin Higgs construction in [1], and the approximately 20 TeV right-handed scale discussed in [5].

node_eb1c2d1bbf08.summary: This cluster studies supersymmetric and related left-right models with R-parity, Higgs-sector structure, doubly charged states, neutrino masses, baryogenesis, and dark matter.

questions.question: What experimental signal would most clearly distinguish a supersymmetric left-right model with automatic R-parity conservation from a nonsupersymmetric or dynamically broken left-right theory?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from minimal supersymmetric left-right models predicting exact R-parity and light charged or doubly charged Higgs states, contrasted with dynamical composite-Higgs left-right scenarios [1],[3],[4].

questions.question: Can parity breaking, B-L breaking, and electroweak breaking be generated in a single natural hierarchy while keeping the right-handed scale accessible and avoiding electromagnetic symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This derives from dynamical and NJL approaches to tumbling symmetry breaking and from supersymmetric constructions where parity can break while preserving electromagnetic gauge invariance [2],[3].

questions.question: How does the QCD phase transition quantitatively affect entropy dilution for keV right-handed-neutrino warm dark matter in low-scale left-right theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the warm-dark-matter analysis where right-handed charge-current interactions near the QCD phase transition control the late-entropy dilution needed for the relic density [5].

node_7b0c164e0d08.summary: These works develop left-right symmetric mechanisms for generating light neutrino masses, including type-I, new, Dirac, pseudo-Dirac, radiative, and low-scale seesaw scenarios.

questions.question: Can TeV-scale left-right seesaw models naturally maintain large light-heavy neutrino mixing while surviving improved limits from mu to e gamma, mu to 3e, mu-e conversion, neutrinoless double beta decay, and LHC searches?
questions.rationale: This is the experimental consistency problem posed in [1], where discrete symmetries keep neutrino masses small despite large light-heavy mixing.

questions.question: How completely can collider measurements of heavy neutrino masses and mixings reconstruct the Dirac Yukawa matrix in the minimal left-right symmetric model?
questions.rationale: This follows from [2], which shows that light and heavy neutrino data determine Dirac Yukawa couplings and discusses their reconstruction at the LHC.

questions.question: Can pseudo-Dirac, linear-seesaw, and radiative Dirac-neutrino left-right scenarios be distinguished by their correlated predictions for right-handed currents, neutrinoless double beta decay, and N_eff constraints?
questions.rationale: This connects the pseudo-Dirac linear seesaw and right-handed-current effects in [4] with the one-loop Dirac neutrino scenario and N_eff bounds in [5].

node_c2cd9ae0d48a.summary: This cluster analyzes symmetry breaking and Higgs-sector dynamics in left-right models, including supersymmetric, bidoublet-free, composite, and dynamical scalar constructions.

questions.question: Is dynamical left-right symmetry breaking with composite Higgs fields a viable alternative to elementary scalar sectors once the predicted low-scale scalars and lepton-flavor-violating effects are included?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1] and [2], where left-right breaking arises from four-fermion dynamics and predicts intermediate or low-scale composite scalar states.

questions.question: Why do composite triplet and doublet realizations differ so sharply in their ability to break parity, and can this be made into a model-independent criterion for left-right Higgs sectors?
questions.rationale: This follows from [2], where triplet composite models fail to break parity at low energies while doublet models break it automatically.

questions.question: Can minimal supersymmetric left-right models predict experimentally accessible charged or doubly charged Higgs multiplets while keeping R-parity exact and the parity-breaking scale in the required intermediate range?
questions.rationale: This combines the non-renormalizable and renormalizable SUSY left-right predictions for exact R-parity, intermediate parity breaking, and light charged multiplets in [3], [4], and [5].

node_0bf56b5fe6f2.summary: These papers explore dark matter candidates in left-right symmetric theories, including stable multiplets, keV right-handed neutrinos, singlet fermions, multi-component sectors, and collider excess interpretations.

questions.question: Is a keV right-handed neutrino still the unique viable warm-dark-matter candidate in minimal low-scale left-right symmetry after QCD-era charge-current interactions and late entropy production are modeled with full Boltzmann evolution?
questions.rationale: This derives from the claim that the lightest right-handed neutrino near keV mass is the only viable minimal candidate and that QCD-transition dynamics controls the required dilution [1].

questions.question: Can stable TeV multiplet dark matter from accidental stability or residual B-L parity coexist with the W_R resonance patterns used to motivate left-right collider scenarios?
questions.rationale: This question links minimal left-right dark matter triplets or quintuplets with left-right models invoked to explain eejj, diboson, and dijet resonance patterns [2],[4].

questions.question: Which symmetry and loop structures make scalar diphoton-type signals compatible or incompatible with left-right dark-matter relic density and muon g-2 requirements?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dark left-right model where a global symmetry stabilizes dark matter and enhances diphoton branching, contrasted with minimal left-right explanations whose cross section was not consistent [3],[5].

node_8b8fba00b93a.summary: This cluster studies bounds and signals for right-handed gauge bosons in left-right models using LHC searches, low-energy precision data, meson mixing, CP violation, and leptogenesis.

questions.question: Can a combined fit to K-meson mixing, low-energy CP-violating observables, radiative B-decay CP asymmetries, and LHC dilepton-plus-dijet searches determine whether the canonical M_WR lower bound near 2.5 TeV is robust or can still be weakened by right-handed mixing structure?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the tension between the K-mixing lower bound and possible reductions from the mismatch of left- and right-handed quark mixings in minimal LRSM analyses [2,3].

questions.question: Which regions of right-handed lepton mixing and heavy-neutrino masses make LHC lepton-flavour-violating heavy-neutrino signals more constraining than low-energy LFV searches?
questions.rationale: The LHC and low-energy complementarity in heavy right-handed neutrino production and decay is explicitly identified as a parameter-space question in [4].

questions.question: Could a large mixing-induced CP asymmetry in radiative b -> s gamma or b -> d gamma decays survive present rate constraints while pointing uniquely to LRSM right-handed photon amplitudes?
questions.rationale: Radiative B decays can have SM-like rates but asymmetries above 50% in LRSM because right-handed photon amplitudes are enhanced by heavy virtual fermion masses [1].

node_f5c40fc8eb3f.summary: These works focus on collider searches for TeV-scale right-handed W bosons and associated heavy neutrinos, including dilepton-plus-jets, neutrino-jet, flavor-violating, and leptogenesis-related signatures.

questions.question: How robust are LHC limits on W_R masses once the right-handed quark mixing matrix, the definition of left-right symmetry as parity or charge conjugation, and unconstrained bidoublet VEV ratios are varied?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which shows that the usual W_R lower bound depends on the right-handed mixing structure and the parity-versus-charge-conjugation choice.

questions.question: Can lepton-flavor-violating heavy-neutrino production at the LHC and low-energy LFV searches jointly determine the right-handed neutrino mixing matrix?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by [2], which compares LHC sensitivity to heavy-neutrino flavor violation with low-energy LFV constraints.

questions.question: What pattern of opposite-sign versus same-sign dilepton-plus-jets events would distinguish Majorana, pseudo-Dirac, non-degenerate, and CP-phased heavy neutrinos in minimal left-right models?
questions.rationale: This derives from [5], where CP phases and non-degenerate heavy neutrinos can explain the OS-to-SS ratio and flavor pattern in pp to lljj data.

node_3fb59b1859d4.summary: This cluster examines CP violation, right-handed quark mixing, flavor observables, meson mixing, electric dipole moments, and semileptonic anomalies in left-right and right-handed-current frameworks.

questions.question: What set of flavor observables would decisively separate right-handed charged-current effects from hadronic or CKM-fit uncertainties in radiative, semileptonic, and meson-mixing data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the large possible radiative-B CP asymmetries in [1], the right-handed-current explanation of Vub and Vcb tensions in [5], and the SMEFT degeneracy analysis in [4].

questions.question: How stable are lower bounds on the W_R scale once gauge-independent flavor-changing neutral-Higgs contributions and updated K and B mixing inputs are treated together?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the analytic right-handed mixing-matrix constraints of [2] and the gauge-independence corrections to Delta F=2 amplitudes in [3].

questions.question: Can mixing-induced CP asymmetries in b -> s gamma and b -> d gamma provide a cleaner discovery channel for right-handed photons than total radiative decay rates?
questions.rationale: This derives from the observation in [1] that radiative rates can look Standard-Model-like while right-handed amplitudes generate large CP asymmetries.

node_8f08e6625be6.summary: These papers explore parallel mirror sectors, their cosmological evolution, neutrino mixing, baryogenesis, dark matter, parity restoration, and collider signatures.

questions.question: What observational result would most decisively test the broad mirror-world cosmology picture: sterile-neutrino mixing, asymmetric reheating, mirror baryon dark matter, or deviations in nucleosynthesis?
questions.rationale: Mirror-sector models connect sterile neutrino puzzles, lower mirror reheating temperatures, altered nucleosynthesis, baryogenesis, and mirror baryon dark matter [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Can explicit asymmetric reheating models naturally produce the temperature hierarchy required by nucleosynthesis while also yielding a mirror baryon asymmetry large enough for mirror baryons to dominate dark matter?
questions.rationale: Asymmetric reheating was proposed to satisfy nucleosynthesis bounds, and early mirror-universe studies found mirror baryon asymmetries can exceed the ordinary one [2] and [3].

questions.question: How much breaking of exact mirror parity, such as a larger mirror electroweak scale, is compatible with explaining sterile-neutrino masses while preserving the cosmological role of the mirror sector?
questions.rationale: One model explains solar, atmospheric, LSND, and hot-dark-matter neutrino puzzles using a mirror electroweak scale larger by about a factor of 30 [1].

node_4433d0a6b3d1.summary: These works study Twin Higgs models where mirror or twin sectors protect the electroweak scale while producing distinctive dark matter, cosmological, and collider phenomenology.

questions.question: What minimal twin-sector content and Z2-breaking pattern preserves Higgs naturalness while avoiding a massless twin photon and satisfying dark-matter cosmology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Fraternal Twin Higgs dark-matter construction and the composite Twin Higgs observation that not gauging twin hypercharge can remove a massless twin photon [4].

questions.question: Can exotic Higgs decays to twin hadrons, especially displaced visible decays, cover the parameter space where SM-neutral top partners and twin QCD provide dark naturalness?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the finding that natural Twin Higgs models generically produce Hidden Valley phenomenology through Higgs-portal decays to twin hadrons [2].

questions.question: In left-right or composite Twin Higgs UV completions, which symmetry and selection-rule conditions are truly necessary for one-loop quadratic-divergence cancellation and precision-electroweak viability?
questions.rationale: This derives from the original mirror-symmetry cancellation mechanism, its left-right realization, and the composite-model warning that protection works only under certain conditions [3].

node_98c0076edea4.summary: These papers investigate quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions through hydrodynamics, jet quenching, transport coefficients, heavy-quark diffusion, and critical-point observables.

questions.question: What measurements would establish whether collective hadronization in small high-density pp systems is the same physical phenomenon as flow in large heavy-ion fireballs?
questions.rationale: EPOS LHC introduced different flow parametrization for small high-density pp cores versus large heavy-ion volumes to reproduce LHC pp, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb data [3].

questions.question: How can transport models, saturation initial conditions, and quarkonium observables be combined into a unified test of QGP formation and evolution across pp, pA, and AA collisions?
questions.rationale: UrQMD models pp, pA, and AA collisions via hadronic interactions and strings, CGC describes saturated gluons in high-energy wavefunctions, and quarkonium reviews emphasize heavy-ion production as a continuing puzzle [2], [4], [1].

questions.question: Which parts of nonlinear small-x evolution are essential for quantitatively reliable initial conditions in heavy-ion phenomenology?
questions.rationale: The CGC overview and JIMWLK-type nonlinear evolution derivation frame high-density small-x gluons through a functional Fokker-Planck equation with coefficients needed to all orders in source strength [4], [5].

node_18f82aaae0ad.summary: These works use Tsallis and statistical-thermal models to fit transverse-momentum spectra and hadron yields in pp, p-Pb, and heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: Can a single phenomenological framework distinguish genuine collective hadronization in high-multiplicity pp collisions from non-thermal string-fragmentation or Pomeron-based descriptions of the same hadron spectra?
questions.rationale: EPOS LHC attributes small-system data to collective hadronization, while UrQMD and QGSJET-II emphasize string fragmentation and enhanced-Pomeron dynamics [1], [2], [3].

questions.question: Which precision hadron-hadron or pA measurements would most decisively test whether Tsallis-like spectral fits encode thermalized QCD matter or merely effective parameters of microscopic transport and fragmentation?
questions.rationale: UrQMD notes that higher-precision hadronic reaction data are needed, while the heavy-ion overview frames thermalization and QGP formation as central unresolved issues [1], [4].

questions.question: How can chemical freeze-out criteria based on fixed energy per particle, baryon density, entropy density, or percolation be consistently combined with transverse-momentum spectral systematics across pp, p-Pb, and heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: The freeze-out comparison found successful but parameter-sensitive regularities in yields, while LHC event-generator studies extend the same phenomenology across pp, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb systems [2], [5].

node_d150ff23253d.summary: These papers analyze hadron multiplicities and strange-particle yields in nuclear collisions to extract chemical freeze-out conditions and strangeness equilibration.

questions.question: Which multistrange baryon-to-meson yield ratios most sharply discriminate fixed energy per particle, baryon-density, entropy-density, and percolation criteria for chemical freeze-out?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the comparison of freeze-out criteria and the RHIC thermal-model fit noting that multistrange ratios are needed to further constrain freeze-out conditions [2] and [3].

questions.question: Does collective hadronization in high-density small-volume pp and p-Pb cores obey the same T, mu_B, and strangeness-under-saturation systematics extracted from A-A collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from EPOS LHC's collective-hadronization interpretation in pp and the observed smooth freeze-out dependence on energy and system size [1] and [5].

node_cceb96ebe8a3.summary: These works focus on canonical statistical descriptions of strange and multistrange hadron enhancement across pp, pA, and nucleus-nucleus collisions.

questions.question: Can canonical strangeness suppression and collective hadronization be separated experimentally across pp, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb by using multistrange yields at fixed multiplicity and system size?
questions.rationale: EPOS-LHC attributes small-system data to collective hadronization in high-density cores [1], while thermal analyses require additional strangeness suppression to describe multiplicities [3].

questions.question: Which beam-energy dependence of pion and strangeness production would uniquely identify the onset of deconfinement rather than a smooth change in hadronic freeze-out parameters?
questions.rationale: The statistical early-stage model predicts characteristic energy behavior of pion and strangeness production as a deconfinement signal [2].

questions.question: Can transport calculations with detailed balance reproduce the same strange-hadron chemical equilibration patterns inferred from canonical thermal fits at low beam energies?
questions.rationale: SMASH validates microscopic transport through detailed balance and low-energy particle production [4], while [3] extracts thermal parameters and strangeness suppression from heavy-ion yields.

node_34e9471fe8e4.summary: These papers compare strange-hadron production across collision systems and energies, emphasizing suppression, enhancement, and event-generator modeling from SPS to LHC regimes.

questions.question: Can collective hadronization in small high-density pp systems be distinguished experimentally from rope or overlapping-string mechanisms as the origin of enhanced strangeness and baryon production?
questions.rationale: This question links the EPOS LHC interpretation of collective hadronization in pp [1] with the rope-formation expectation of increased strange particles and baryons [4].

questions.question: How does the strangeness saturation factor gamma_S evolve with collision energy and system size, and where does a thermal model with partial strangeness saturation cease to describe fully integrated multiplicities?
questions.rationale: This derives from thermal-model analyses requiring additional or partial strangeness suppression from pp to heavy-ion systems [2,5].

questions.question: Can hadronic transport approaches validated at low beam energies be extended to strange-particle production while preserving detailed balance and agreement with elementary cross sections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the SMASH transport construction and validation for non-strange production and equilibrium properties at low beam energies [3].

node_6d8982906947.summary: These works interpret strange-hadron yields and chemical nonequilibrium as signatures of quark-gluon plasma hadronization in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: Can the energy dependence of pion and strangeness production locate a unique deconfinement transition region, or can statistical hadronization with canonical or partial chemical equilibrium mimic the same scaling?
questions.rationale: The early-stage model interprets SPS pion and strangeness scaling as evidence for QGP creation, while statistical hadronization analyses test equilibrium and strangeness undersaturation across beam energies [1][4][5].

questions.question: How do pionic Mott-temperature suppression, hadronization times of quark-to-meson processes, and the near-universal 170 MeV hadronization temperature fit into one freeze-out description?
questions.rationale: This question connects NJL calculations of hadronization rates and Mott suppression with thermal pp and p-pbar evidence for a nearly constant hadronization temperature around 170 MeV [2][3].

questions.question: Which yield ratios, measured consistently in full phase space rather than only at midrapidity, most robustly diagnose strangeness under-saturation in relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the statistical-model warning that midrapidity yields can artificially enhance inferred strangeness production and mislead conclusions about chemical equilibrium [5].
