node_0a3766bf7429.summary: These papers examine why hadron production appears thermal, using canonical and microcanonical models as well as Hawking-Unruh-inspired confinement scenarios.

questions.question: What cross-system measurement of the same hadron species with comparable uncertainties in e+e-, pp, and AA collisions would falsify the claim that statistical hadronization is equally successful in elementary and nuclear reactions?
questions.rationale: This is the broad test demanded by the comparative statistical-model analysis in [5].

questions.question: Can the Hawking-Unruh confinement-horizon mechanism quantitatively predict a common hadronization temperature while enforcing color neutrality and strangeness systematics from elementary collisions to heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the confinement-horizon thermalization conjecture in [1] and its Color Glass Condensate extension in [2].

questions.question: How can resonance yields and spectra after rescattering between chemical and thermal freeze-out be used to separate primordial thermal production from hadronic evolution effects?
questions.rationale: The use of Lambda(1520), K0(892), Phi, and Delta(1232) resonances as freeze-out probes is developed in [3].

node_ac91cd1aebeb.summary: These works determine heavy-ion chemical freeze-out parameters from hadron yields, resonance-gas models, lattice-QCD fluctuation ratios, and beam-energy systematics.

questions.question: Can lattice-QCD cumulant ratios of conserved-charge fluctuations determine T, mu_B, mu_Q, and mu_S at freeze-out with less model dependence than hadron-yield fits?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of net-electric-charge cumulant ratios and Taylor-expanded lattice QCD to determine freeze-out conditions in [5].

questions.question: Which proposed freeze-out criterion remains valid when beam energy, system size, strangeness undersaturation, and multistrange baryon-to-meson ratios are all included?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the comparison of freeze-out criteria in [1], the RHIC need for multistrange ratios in [2], and the energy/system-size study in [3].

questions.question: How should thermal-model analysis packages incorporate correlated yield uncertainties, resonance-gas assumptions, and lattice fluctuation constraints to make freeze-out systematics reproducible?
questions.rationale: This derives from the THERMUS thermal-model framework in [4] and the hadron-resonance-gas comparison to lattice QCD freeze-out parameters in [5].

node_62bac6413c2a.summary: These papers model charged-particle, baryon, and strangeness production in hadronic and nuclear collisions using diffusion, string, participant, and transport approaches.

questions.question: Which hadron-production data would most clearly separate transport models with string fragmentation, enhanced-Pomeron Monte Carlo generators, and three-dimensional dynamical initial-state models across pp, pA, and AA systems?
questions.rationale: This broad comparison is grounded in UrQMD string fragmentation at high energy [1], QGSJET-II enhanced-Pomeron final-state generation [2], DPMJET-III's unified collision coverage [3], and dynamical initial conditions in [5].

questions.question: Can net-baryon rapidity distributions, two-particle rapidity correlations, and rapidity decorrelation provide a common calibration of participant deceleration and energy deposition in heavy-ion initial-state models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the dynamical initial-state model's explicit treatment of participant deceleration, string energy deposition, and these rapidity-sensitive observables in [5].

node_8d8bf3d1de0e.summary: These works study charged-particle multiplicities and pseudorapidity distributions across pp, pA, and heavy-ion collisions from RHIC to LHC energies.

questions.question: Which ingredient is chiefly responsible for current differences among UrQMD, QGSJET-II, DPMJET-III, FLUKA, and HIJING predictions of charged-particle pseudorapidity densities: string fragmentation, enhanced Pomeron resummation, minijet parameters, or nuclear-collision modeling?
questions.rationale: This question compares the mechanisms emphasized across the transport, Reggeon-field-theory, dual-parton, FLUKA, and HIJING generator descriptions [1][2][3][4][5].

questions.question: Can one construct a common benchmark dataset across pp, pA, and AA collisions that constrains both low-energy resonance transport and high-energy string or semihard Pomeron particle production in the same generator tune?
questions.rationale: This follows from UrQMD's need for precise hadronic data across energies and DPMJET-III's unified treatment of hadron, photon, and nuclear interactions from a few GeV to cosmic-ray energies [1][3].

questions.question: How do updated parton distributions and two-component minijet parameters propagate into uncertainties on central multiplicity and rapidity distributions for p+Pb and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC energies?
questions.rationale: This derives from HIJING 2.0, where updated PDFs and minijet parameters control total pp cross sections and central pseudorapidity density before predictions are made for pp, p+Pb, and Pb+Pb [5].

node_8c32cb2491d8.summary: These papers model charged-particle pseudorapidity densities, transverse energy, and centrality trends across pp, pA, and heavy-ion collisions from RHIC to LHC energies.

questions.question: Can one scaling framework relate charged-particle mean multiplicity and midrapidity pseudorapidity density across pp, pA, and AA collisions using participant energy and constituent-quark variables?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the model connecting hadronic and nuclear collision multiplicities through dissipating participant energy, constituent quarks, and Landau hydrodynamics [4].

questions.question: Where do saturation-based perturbative QCD predictions for centrality-dependent multiplicities fail once nuclear geometry and changing collision energy are confronted with RHIC-to-LHC data?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the pQCD saturated-gluon calculation of centrality-dependent multiplicities in ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions [5].

questions.question: Can low-pT hydrodynamic spectra and high-pT pQCD quenching calculations be matched consistently enough to predict charged-hadron spectra without retuning the decoupling temperature at each energy?
questions.rationale: This derives from the RHIC-tested prediction combining boost-invariant hydrodynamics, pQCD cross sections, nuclear PDFs, fragmentation, and quenching weights [2].

node_17edaef59045.summary: This cluster focuses on transport and Monte Carlo models such as UrQMD, DPMJET, QGSJET, and wounded-nucleon approaches for simulating hadronic and nuclear collision observables.

questions.question: What minimal benchmark data set across pp, pA, AA, photon-hadron, and cosmic-ray energies would expose whether UrQMD, DPMJET, QGSJET-II, and HIJING are failing in cross sections, multiplicities, spectra, or rapidity distributions?
questions.rationale: The event-generator papers emphasize broad applicability but rely on different dynamical ingredients and repeatedly call for precise hadronic reaction data and comparisons to measured spectra [1], [2], [3], [4], [5].

questions.question: How should enhanced Pomeron resummation, semihard minijets, color-string fragmentation, and hadronic transport be matched in a single generator without double counting particle production mechanisms?
questions.rationale: QGSJET-II builds final states from resummed enhanced Pomeron diagrams, HIJING uses a two-component minijet model, and UrQMD switches from hadron resonances to string excitation above sqrt(s) about 5 GeV [1], [2], [4].

node_8791f83dd165.summary: These works study baryon and strange-baryon production using quark-gluon string and fragmentation models, emphasizing string-junction transport of baryon number in rapidity.

questions.question: Which baryon-antibaryon correlations would most directly test whether string-fragmentation popcorn mechanisms, rather than late hadronic reactions, control baryon production rates and momentum distributions?
questions.rationale: The improved popcorn model reproduces baryon species rates and momentum distributions and makes predictions for baryon-antibaryon correlations [5].

questions.question: Can a single baryon-stopping model describe antiparticle-to-particle ratios from hadron-hadron and d-Au collisions through heavy-ion systems as matter-antimatter symmetry emerges at higher beam energy?
questions.rationale: DPMJET-III is used to analyze baryon stopping in hadron-hadron and d-Au data, while antimatter studies quantify the energy dependence toward matter-antimatter symmetry [3,4].

questions.question: How much of the antiproton yield at SPS energies is fixed by thermal backward multi-pion reactions rather than initial string-junction baryon transport?
questions.rationale: The antiproton puzzle paper argues that including the backward p pbar to n pion reaction in a thermal framework maintains the antiproton abundance to decoupling [2].

node_befcba1a1bb3.summary: This cluster examines net-baryon rapidity loss and stopping in relativistic heavy-ion collisions as probes of saturation, deconfinement, initial-state dynamics, and limiting-fragmentation behavior.

questions.question: Can dynamical deceleration initial-state models and finite-baryon hydrodynamics be constrained enough by net-baryon rapidity distributions and rapidity correlations to identify the dominant stopping mechanism?
questions.rationale: The three-dimensional initial-state model predicts net-baryon rapidity distributions, two-particle rapidity correlations, and decorrelation observables from participant deceleration [1].

questions.question: How can measurements across RHIC BES, NA61/SHINE, and LHC energies separate limiting-fragmentation dynamics from diquark-breaking baryon stopping?
questions.rationale: Limiting fragmentation is described using Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution, while diquark breaking predicts increasing midrapidity stopping with energy, system size, and centrality [5].

node_a850278e66c4.summary: These papers apply Tsallis and other nonextensive statistical forms to transverse-momentum spectra in pp, pA, and heavy-ion collisions, extracting temperature, flow, and nonextensivity parameters.

questions.question: Can the Tsallis nonextensivity parameter q be operationally separated into temperature fluctuations, intrinsic power-law dynamics, and collective flow across pp, pA, and heavy-ion transverse-momentum spectra?
questions.rationale: This follows from the interpretation of q as fluctuations of an exponential distribution in [1], the power-law fluctuation review in [4], and the thermodynamically consistent pT fits in [2] and [3].

questions.question: What data or consistency condition would decide whether nonextensive hadron spectra are a genuine thermodynamic description of quark matter or only an effective parametrization of final-state hadron production?
questions.rationale: This broad disagreement-calibrated question is grounded in the thermodynamic-consistency issues of Tsallis distributions in [2] and [3] and the nonextensive quark-matter/coalescence framework in [5].

node_21de3b627da7.summary: This cluster centers on thermodynamically consistent Tsallis fits to high-pT charged-particle and hadron spectra at RHIC and LHC energies, especially in pp and p-Pb collisions.

questions.question: Can the Tsallis nonextensivity parameter q be quantitatively decomposed into initial-state, event-by-event, and hard-scattering fluctuations across RHIC and LHC spectra, rather than treated as a single phenomenological fit parameter?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the interpretation of q as arising from fluctuations of an underlying exponential distribution [1] and by systematic beam-energy trends in q [4].

questions.question: What observable comparison between identified hadrons and jets can decide whether the high-pT Tsallis power law is primarily thermodynamic or instead generated by multiple hard scattering and parton showering?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the empirical finding that hadron and jet spectra both show power laws but with systematically different high-pT indices [5].

node_efca291219d0.summary: These works analyze how Tsallis temperatures, nonextensivity parameters, volumes, and rapidity distributions vary with collision energy in high-energy pp and p-Pb data.

questions.question: Can the weak rise of the Tsallis nonextensivity parameter q with pp collision energy be quantitatively mapped to fluctuations of an underlying exponential parameter, rather than treated only as a fit trend?
questions.rationale: The interpretation of q greater than one as entirely due to fluctuations of exponential-distribution parameters directly motivates testing the observed energy dependence of q [1].

questions.question: Are the apparently energy-independent Tsallis temperature and volume robust under thermodynamically consistent relativistic quantum-distribution fits to identified-particle spectra?
questions.rationale: Thermodynamically consistent Tsallis forms were proposed for high-energy transverse-momentum spectra, while systematic pp fits found T and volume consistent with no beam-energy dependence [2].

questions.question: Can a single Tsallis temperature and near-universal entropic index describe both transverse-momentum and rapidity distributions once correlations among particle species and beam energies are fitted globally?
questions.rationale: A combined analysis reported one temperature of about 68 MeV and q close to 1.146 for many pp spectra, then used two Tsallis fireballs to describe rapidity distributions [5].

node_6ec7e42348b0.summary: This cluster compares phenomenological thermal, multisource, Hagedorn, and Tsallis-like descriptions of identified-particle transverse-momentum spectra across pp, pA, and nucleus-nucleus systems.

questions.question: What physical mechanism, if any, makes the two-parameter Tsallis form describe identified-hadron pT spectra in pp collisions over such a wide momentum range?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] asks whether Tsallis parameters arise from hard parton scattering, multiple scattering, and showering, while [4] documents systematic two-parameter fits across RHIC and LHC pp data.

questions.question: Can one construct a unified identified-particle spectrum formula whose parameters continuously separate hard-scattering power laws, collective flow, and temperature fluctuations across pp, pA, and AA systems?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] introduces a flow-modified Tsallis form for Au+Au spectra, and [5] modifies the Hagedorn formula with temperature fluctuations to fit the full pT range.

questions.question: Is the very-low-pT pion enhancement in LHC heavy-ion collisions better interpreted as chemical non-equilibrium and onset of pion condensation, or can Tsallis-like phenomenology reproduce it with comparable predictive power?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] attributes the low-pT pion enhancement to chemical non-equilibrium and possible pion condensation, while [2] and [4] motivate Tsallis-based alternatives for identified spectra.

node_9b29fd39ba38.summary: These papers interpret power-law hadron spectra through nonextensive statistical mechanics, linking deviations from Boltzmann-Gibbs behavior to fluctuations, finite-size effects, and hadronization.

questions.question: Can the Tsallis nonextensivity parameter q be tied to a measurable fluctuation source rather than serving mainly as a fit parameter for power-law hadron spectra?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which interprets power laws in elementary and heavy-ion collisions as possible reflections of intrinsic fluctuations encoded by q.

questions.question: Where is the boundary between QCD hard-scattering dominance and nonextensive thermal interpretation in transverse-momentum spectra spanning low to high pT?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [4], which connects QCD hard-scattering power laws with nonextensive statistical descriptions over wide pT ranges.

questions.question: Can nonextensive quark coalescence produce thermodynamically consistent hadron spectra across elementary and heavy-ion collisions with a common energy dependence of q and temperature?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2] on relativistic generalized Boltzmann equations and quark coalescence, together with [3,5] on e+e- spectra, q dependence, and energy-independent fitted temperatures.

node_ed53385a5b60.summary: This cluster extracts kinetic freeze-out temperature, transverse flow velocity, and freeze-out volume from identified-particle spectra using blast-wave, Tsallis, and related thermal models.

questions.question: Can a common freeze-out analysis disentangle true kinetic freeze-out temperature from non-equilibrium effective temperatures when different local momentum variables give incompatible temperature extractions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the AMPT study finding that effective temperatures extracted from different rest-frame variables differ substantially, signaling that the parton system is not in local thermal equilibrium [1].

questions.question: Is the observed mass-dependent differential freeze-out a genuine species-dependent decoupling pattern, or an artifact of fitting identified spectra with Tsallis and blast-wave parametrizations?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the reported mass-dependent freeze-out volume, temperature, chemical potential, and radial flow velocity, including a radial-flow mass hierarchy [2].

questions.question: What observable combination of spectra, multiplicities, rapidity distributions, and phase-space densities can resolve contradictory central-versus-peripheral kinetic freeze-out temperatures across BGBW, TBW, improved Tsallis, and intercept methods?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the finding that different extraction methods give contradictory centrality ordering of kinetic freeze-out temperatures, while hydrodynamic initial-volume choices affect simultaneous fits to effective temperatures and bulk data [3,5].

node_053b1abf5ae9.summary: These works explain enhanced charm-baryon yields and charm-hadron ratios in pp and heavy-ion collisions through statistical hadronization, coalescence, fragmentation, and color-reconnection mechanisms.

questions.question: Can charm-baryon enhancement in pp and heavy-ion collisions be explained by a universal hadronization mechanism, or does the heavy-quark flavor composition necessarily depend on the production environment?
questions.rationale: This follows from [5], which argues that charm and bottom hadronization depends on the string environment and can yield non-universal flavor composition.

questions.question: Which measurements can separate baryon enhancement from beyond-leading-colour string formation, soft colour reconnection, and cluster models with explicit diquark degrees of freedom?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the SU(3) multiplet string-minimization model in [1], the modified cluster model with diquarks in [2], and Herwig++ colour reconnection in [3].

questions.question: How do multi-parton interactions in pp collisions overcome nominal subleading-colour suppression to favor baryonic string topologies relevant for charm-hadron ratios?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], which states that multi-parton interactions increase possible subleading connections and kinematically favor those reducing total string length.

node_053b1abf5ae9_1.summary: This cluster studies charm and heavy-quark hadron formation across collision environments using coalescence, fragmentation, Lund string dynamics, and extended charmed-hadron state spectra.

questions.question: Across e+e-, pp, and heavy-ion environments, what observable combination of charm baryon-to-meson ratios and pT spectra can separate non-universal string drag or string collapse from genuine coalescence with flowing QGP partons?
questions.rationale: This combines the environment-dependent string-model hadronization and string collapse effects in heavy-quark fragmentation with coalescence-plus-fragmentation predictions for D0, Ds, and Lambda_c production [2], [3].

questions.question: How much of the observed charm baryon enhancement can be attributed to an extended spectrum of heavy-hadron resonances rather than to modified coalescence parameters or subleading-color string connections?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the inclusion of heavy-hadron resonance decays in coalescence calculations and in the PYTHIA model where beyond-leading-color correlations alter string formation in pp collisions [1], [3].

questions.question: Can a four-momentum-conserving recombination model with space-momentum correlations reproduce heavy-flavor hadrochemistry from RHIC to LHC without retuning while remaining consistent with exact charm conservation constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the recombination model that recovers thermal and chemical equilibrium limits with space-momentum correlations and from the canonical statistical coalescence treatment with exact charm conservation [4], [5].

node_9cf103dc95c9.summary: These papers study how color reconnection and related final-state effects reshape hadronization, particle yields, underlying-event observables, and precision measurements in event generators and collider data.

questions.question: Which identified-hadron yield ratios as functions of charged multiplicity can distinguish PYTHIA color reconnection from DIPSY rope hadronization, especially for baryon and strangeness enhancement?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison showing that both models enhance baryons with multiplicity but only DIPSY rope hadronization produces strangeness enhancement [5].

questions.question: Can cluster-hadronization models with soft color reconnection and baryonic clusters simultaneously describe underlying-event data, minimum-bias observables, and charm-baryon enhancement without retuning unrelated fragmentation parameters?
questions.rationale: The question combines the modified cluster model with baryonic quantum-number clusters [1] and the Herwig++ color-reconnection improvement of minimum-bias and underlying-event data [2].

questions.question: What event-shape or identified-particle observable can separate genuine collective flow from flow-like patterns generated by color reconnection among independent hard subcollisions in pp events?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by PYTHIA 8 studies showing flow-like effects from color string formations due to color reconnection in multiple-hard-scattering events [4].

node_c081aa98b3a3.summary: This cluster reviews the formation, properties, signatures, and theoretical interpretation of quark-gluon plasma in heavy-ion and small-system collisions.

questions.question: What minimal set of final-state observables can establish QGP formation while simultaneously constraining thermalization, the equation of state, and transport properties across A-A, p-A, and high-multiplicity pp systems?
questions.rationale: This follows from the broad-signature program reviewed in [1] and [2], the small-to-large system agenda in [3], and the extraction of bulk properties in [5].

questions.question: How can soft collective flow, jet modification, quarkonia, dileptons, and fluctuations be combined into a single multi-scale inference framework for QCD medium properties?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the multi-scale QCD description in [1] and the range of bulk, electromagnetic, heavy-flavor, and fluctuation observables reviewed in [5].

node_fcaf8e5809e1.summary: These works focus on experimental and theoretical evidence for quark-gluon plasma formation, including collective expansion, thermal emission, hadronization patterns, and proposed diagnostic observables.

questions.question: Which combination of bulk observables, thermal electromagnetic probes, jet quenching, heavy flavor, and quarkonium measurements can most cleanly separate QGP formation from hadronic or initial-state alternatives?
questions.rationale: This reflects the critical reviews of proposed QGP signatures and the modern emphasis on combining soft, hard, and penetrating probes [2],[4],[5].

questions.question: Can a single multi-scale QCD framework quantitatively connect early thermalization, near-minimal viscosity, collective expansion, and jet energy loss in the same heavy-ion events?
questions.rationale: This extends the big-picture description of QGP as a rapidly thermalizing low-viscosity droplet traversed by energetic partons [1].

questions.question: What observable would most directly reveal the microscopic constituents of the QGP at different wavelength scales using jets and heavy quarks?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the review's claim that high-momentum probes are needed to unveil QGP constituents at different wavelengths while its fast evolution remains elusive [5].

node_205cac7dadc1.summary: This cluster surveys theoretical concepts, open questions, and RHIC-to-LHC developments in hot and dense QCD matter produced by relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: What combined set of RHIC and LHC observables can separate macroscopic QGP transport properties from the microscopic parton dynamics that generate them?
questions.rationale: This follows from the stated LHC goal of characterizing long-wavelength QGP properties while also identifying the underlying parton dynamics [1].

questions.question: Can one construct a unified particle-production framework that quantitatively describes high-multiplicity pp, p-Pb, and Pb-Pb collisions without obscuring where genuine deconfinement begins?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the Working Group goal of unifying QCD dynamics from small to large systems and in the p+A role as a reference for nucleus-nucleus data [1], [5].

questions.question: Which measurements most cleanly distinguish low-x nuclear saturation effects from final-state hot-medium effects in proton-nucleus collisions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the use of p+A collisions to probe small-x partonic structure while also serving as the baseline for heavy-ion interpretation [5].

node_34fba77ba1a0.summary: These papers develop color-string fusion and percolation models to explain multiplicities, transverse momentum trends, correlations, and possible QGP-like transitions in hadronic and nuclear collisions.

questions.question: Which combined measurements of near-side ridge correlations, multiplicity damping, and average-pT correlations can cleanly distinguish string percolation collectivity from hydrodynamic plasma flow in high-multiplicity pp and heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the string-pressure explanation of the pp ridge in [1] and the percolation predictions for multiplicities, transverse momentum, and long-range correlations in [3] and [5].

questions.question: Does the predicted scaling of multiplicity-multiplicity and pT^2-multiplicity correlations only with string density survive realistic event-by-event geometry fluctuations and alternative fused-cluster dynamics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the reported insensitivity of these correlations to string-interaction dynamics and cluster geometry in [5].

questions.question: Can Gaussian string-tension fluctuations that generate thermal transverse-mass spectra be consistently combined with transverse string pressure and expansion without double counting thermal-like behavior?
questions.rationale: This derives from the string-tension fluctuation explanation of thermal mT spectra in [2] and the pressure-driven string-expansion model implemented in PYTHIA8 in [1].

node_64e5be8463a3.summary: This cluster compares thermal, coalescence, transport, and afterburner descriptions of deuteron, triton, helium, hypertriton, and antinucleus production in relativistic collisions.

questions.question: What microscopic reaction network reconciles thermal deuteron yields at T = 155 MeV with the survival and regeneration of weakly bound nuclei during the hadronic afterburner stage?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3], which explains the snowballs in hell puzzle using hydrodynamics plus hadronic reactions such as pi d <-> pi n p without free parameters.

questions.question: Can the p-d-t yield ratio remain an unambiguous QCD critical-fluctuation probe after source-size suppression and finite nuclear wave-function overlap are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the neutron-density fluctuation observable proposed in [4] and the small-system coalescence suppression from finite light-nucleus size in [5].

questions.question: How should microscopic cluster wave functions from ab initio light-nuclei theory be incorporated into coalescence, transport, and antinucleus production predictions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the survey of microscopic clustering methods in [1], antinucleus phenomenology in [2], and wave-function-overlap effects in [5].

node_073c405ea753.summary: These papers study how energetic partons lose energy through radiative and collisional processes in QCD matter, modifying jets and high-momentum hadron suppression in heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: What experimental observable can most directly discriminate the predicted L, L^2, and energy-dependent crossover behavior of medium-induced radiative energy loss in finite QCD matter?
questions.rationale: The representative energy-loss calculations variously predict dE/dz growing with L, total induced energy loss scaling as L^2, and a transition from L^2 to L behavior as the quark energy decreases [1,2,5].

questions.question: Can pT broadening and radiative energy loss be related in hot expanding matter as robustly as in the large-nucleus result dE/dz = (1/8) alpha_s N_c p_perpW^2, or do expansion and finite-volume effects break that universality?
questions.rationale: The broadening-loss relation was derived for large nuclei, while later work treats finite-volume quark-gluon plasma and longitudinally expanding media [1,2,4].

questions.question: How precisely can heavy-to-light observables such as D/pi at moderate transverse momentum be converted into a color-charge-density measurement of QCD matter, given their exponential sensitivity to the medium?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark colorimetry predicts a mass-driven enhancement of the D/pi ratio at 5-10 GeV whose magnitude and shape are exponentially sensitive to the density of color charges [3].

node_6eb6c6816dbc.summary: This cluster centers on perturbative and Monte Carlo modeling of jet quenching, including medium-modified fragmentation, multistage shower evolution, and comparisons with RHIC and LHC observables.

questions.question: Can higher-twist modified fragmentation functions from cold nuclear DIS be quantitatively continued to hot QCD media while preserving the LPM interference pattern and the A^{2/3} nuclear-size scaling limit?
questions.rationale: This derives from the modified fragmentation-function evolution and LPM structure in [1] and [4].

questions.question: What common definition of the jet transport coefficient qhat allows BDMPS-Z quenching weights, opacity expansions, and hydrodynamic medium extractions to be compared without model-dependent normalization shifts?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the quenching-weight comparison between multiple-soft and single-hard scattering in [3] and the multi-model qhat extraction in [5].

questions.question: How can nuclear PDF effects in proton-nucleus production be separated from final-state parton energy loss when interpreting quarkonium, D, and B meson nuclear modification factors?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the model-independent nuclear-gluon-density procedure for heavy-flavor production in [2] and the energy-loss framework of [1], [3], and [5].

node_6eb6c6816dbc_1.summary: These works describe theoretical frameworks and event-generator approaches for jet evolution through dense QCD matter and the resulting suppression of jets and leading hadrons.

questions.question: Can higher-twist modified fragmentation-function evolution be embedded in event-level hot-medium jet showers while preserving LPM interference and the role of diagonal and off-diagonal twist-four distributions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the derivation of modified fragmentation functions and QCD evolution equations with LPM interference in nuclear DIS [1].

questions.question: Which medium properties can be extracted uniquely by comparing pQCD multiple-scattering energy-loss formalisms with RHIC and LHC high-pT hadron and jet spectra, given Monte Carlo model dependence?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the jet-quenching review of multiple approaches and the fast Monte Carlo model used to modify PYTHIA jets in heavy-ion events [4].

questions.question: How should the A^(2/3) nuclear-size modification predicted in eA DIS be generalized to time-dependent hot QCD media coupled to hydrodynamic backgrounds?
questions.rationale: This comes from the predicted quadratic nuclear-size dependence of modified fragmentation in eA scattering and the subsequent generalization toward hot media and heavy-ion modeling [2].

node_4a55b0894d88.summary: This cluster focuses on how dense QCD matter alters parton showers, jet shapes, fragmentation patterns, and jet substructure using analytic and multistage simulation frameworks.

questions.question: Can modified fragmentation-function evolution with diagonal and off-diagonal twist-four nuclear distributions be generalized quantitatively from cold DIS nuclei to hot QCD media probed by full reconstructed jets?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1] and [2] derive medium-modified quark fragmentation functions and evolution equations in DIS with twist-four distributions and discuss generalization to hot QCD matter.

questions.question: Which jet-shape or substructure observable most directly isolates Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference from standard DGLAP showering and classical cascade expectations in a thin quark-gluon plasma?
questions.rationale: Ref. [4] shows that interference among hard radiation, induced Gunion-Bertsch radiation, and gluon rescattering yields angular distributions distinct from DGLAP and classical cascading.

questions.question: How can quenching-factor formalisms incorporate large-distance sensitivity without reducing medium modification to an inadequate mean-energy-loss shift of the hard parton spectrum?
questions.rationale: Ref. [5] finds that the quenching factor is perturbatively safe but highly sensitive to large distances and that simple p_T-shift models are inadequate.

node_4a55b0894d88_1.summary: These papers emphasize Monte Carlo and perturbative descriptions of jet rescattering, shower modification, fragmentation distortion, and observable jet-shape changes in heavy-ion environments.

questions.question: How can Monte Carlo jet-quenching generators encode twist-four diagonal and off-diagonal nuclear matrix elements while preserving the LPM interference pattern in medium-modified fragmentation functions?
questions.rationale: The higher-twist DIS calculations show that modified fragmentation and its evolution depend on both diagonal and off-diagonal twist-four distributions and exhibit LPM interference [1],[2].

questions.question: Which jet-shape or hadron-spectrum observables most cleanly expose the failure of mean-energy-loss shift models in the pT range relevant to heavy-ion data?
questions.rationale: The quenching factor is perturbatively safe but highly sensitive to large distances, and simple pT-shift modeling by mean energy loss is found to be inadequate [5].

node_1d775fc6b0ba.summary: This cluster studies groomed and hard jet-substructure observables as probes of QGP resolution length, medium response, and medium-induced radiation in heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: Which groomed jet-substructure observables can separately constrain medium-induced bremsstrahlung, color decoherence, and soft-background contamination in heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from soft-drop studies of hard medium-induced gluon radiation and their discussion of decoherence and grooming contamination [2].

questions.question: Can simultaneous measurements of zg, subjet girth, and subjet separation identify jet-induced medium response independently of a recoilless energy-loss baseline?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that groomed momentum sharing and subjet girths show recoil dependencies absent in recoilless baselines [3].

questions.question: How can jet-substructure data determine the QGP resolution length and its time dependence during the pre-equilibrium stage of heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This combines the resolution-length proposal for quenched jet substructure with evidence that jet-quenching observables can act as chronometers of the initial stages [4],[5].

node_dd377dbdf45f.summary: These papers develop and compare theoretical and phenomenological descriptions of parton energy loss and jet suppression as probes of quark-gluon plasma at RHIC and the LHC.

questions.question: Can jet-quenching phenomenology extract a medium transport picture that simultaneously describes radiative loss, collisional loss, transverse momentum broadening, and recoil-modified jet shapes at RHIC and LHC?
questions.rationale: This combines the comparative treatment of radiative and collisional energy loss [5] with Linear Boltzmann Transport including elastic processes and thermal recoil partons [4].

questions.question: Which photon-tagged fragmentation observables most directly determine jet energy loss and the parton mean free path after realistic heavy-ion background subtraction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal to use direct-photon-tagged away-side hadron spectra to compare AA and pp fragmentation functions [3].

questions.question: How much of the nuclear modification factor RAA can be fixed by leading-order microscopic energy-loss rates, and how much remains model-dependent through hydrodynamic background and Monte Carlo implementation choices?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the PYTHIA-plus-hydro Monte Carlo quenching model [1] and the review of multiple-scattering and energy-loss implementations [2].

node_e54a27f9d53c.summary: This cluster studies dijet asymmetry, photon-hadron correlations, and back-to-back observables as differential tools for diagnosing how jets lose energy in the medium.

questions.question: Can dijet imbalance be made tomographic once proton-proton recoil fluctuations, out-of-cone radiation, energy-loss fluctuations, and path-length differences are separated experimentally?
questions.rationale: The JEWEL study found that dijet asymmetry is dominated by fluctuations in both proton-proton and heavy-ion collisions, with path-length differences subleading [5].

questions.question: Which jet-cone and time-evolution observables can distinguish early medium modification of vacuum radiation from late medium-induced radiation in Pb+Pb collisions?
questions.rationale: The di-jet asymmetry calculation found early-time energy loss dominated by medium effects on vacuum radiation and late-time loss dominated by medium-induced radiation [1].

questions.question: Do photon-tagged jet momentum imbalances provide a more quantitative calibration of parton-shower dissipation than inclusive dijets across RHIC and LHC energies?
questions.rationale: The isolated-photon-tagged jet study proposed gamma+jet imbalance as a way to compare shower formation and propagation in strongly interacting matter at different center-of-mass energies [3].

node_a66ead0ee716.summary: These works use hadron, dihadron, photon-hadron, and flavor-dependent suppression data with transport and hydrodynamic models to constrain the jet transport coefficient qhat.

questions.question: How can extractions of qhat from single-hadron R_AA be made robust against competing initial-state effects such as nuclear shadowing and the Cronin effect?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3], which extracts qhat from high-p_T hadron suppression, and [4], which emphasizes disentangling initial- and final-state nuclear effects using d+Au and Au+Au data.

questions.question: Can quenching-weight formalisms based on multiple soft scattering and single hard opacity be reconciled into a universal qhat definition for expanding hydrodynamic media?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [2], which compares BDMPS-Z and N=1 opacity quenching weights and relates qhat, Debye mass, and opacity for finite and expanding media.

questions.question: Which set of hadron, dihadron, photon-hadron, and flavor-dependent observables is needed to determine the path-length, energy, and temperature dependence of qhat rather than only its central-collision normalization?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3], where several energy-loss models extract central qhat values, and [5], where one tuned parameter is tested across centrality, correlations, and azimuthal anisotropies.

node_4a1c9b58acf5.summary: This cluster focuses on nuclear modification factors for high-pT hadrons, photons, and jets, separating hot-medium quenching from cold nuclear matter effects across RHIC and LHC systems.

questions.question: How can p+A or d+A nuclear modification factors constrained by gluon nPDFs be combined with A+A high-pT suppression to isolate shadowing, Cronin enhancement, and final-state jet energy loss?
questions.rationale: This follows from the nPDF-based p+A procedure in [1] and the initial-versus-final-state disentangling strategy in [2].

questions.question: Which observables beyond inclusive high-pT R_AA retain sensitivity to the jet transport coefficient once leading-particle suppression becomes fragile at large medium density?
questions.rationale: The loss of R_AA sensitivity is emphasized in [4], while centrality evolution, away-side correlations, and azimuthal anisotropies are used in [3].

questions.question: Can event generators that combine evolving soft backgrounds with radiative and elastic parton evolution reproduce RHIC and LHC high-pT hadron suppression without retuning a single quenching parameter?
questions.rationale: This question combines the one-parameter PQM strategy in [3] with the MARTINI event-generator framework in [5].

node_f0e25b863f26.summary: These papers examine how light, charm, and bottom partons are quenched differently and how their suppression patterns constrain qhat and jet-medium interaction dynamics.

questions.question: Can a single temperature-, energy-, and virtuality-dependent qhat describe light-hadron R_AA, D-meson suppression, and heavy-flavor elliptic flow across RHIC and LHC within a multi-stage jet evolution framework?
questions.rationale: This question combines JETSCAPE Bayesian qhat extraction using MATTER+LBT with LBT descriptions of heavy and light flavor suppression and flow [3][4][5].

questions.question: How much of the observed flavor hierarchy in nuclear modification factors is fixed by partonic energy loss, and how much by initial spectra, fragmentation functions, coalescence, and radial flow?
questions.rationale: LBT studies identify sensitivity to elastic and inelastic energy loss, hybrid fragmentation-coalescence hadronization, transport-coefficient dependence, radial flow, initial spectra, and fragmentation shapes [3][5].

questions.question: Can quenching-weight formalisms in the multiple-soft and single-hard limits be embedded consistently into modern event-by-event hydrodynamic extractions of flavor-dependent qhat?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the relation among transport coefficient, Debye mass, and opacity in quenching-weight calculations and from phenomenological qhat extraction in hydrodynamic media [1][2].

node_ee1972983059.summary: This cluster compares radiative gluon emission and elastic collisional mechanisms for light and heavy parton energy loss in static, expanding, and finite quark-gluon plasma.

questions.question: Which jet-quenching observables can separate L, L^2, and energy-dependent crossover behavior in radiative energy loss from collisional energy loss in finite and longitudinally expanding QCD media?
questions.rationale: This derives from the different path-length dependences and medium models discussed for radiative loss, pT broadening, finite volumes, and expanding plasmas [1], [2], [4], [5].

questions.question: How do finite heavy-quark mass effects modify medium-induced radiation and the predicted heavy-to-light D/pi enhancement at 5-10 GeV when the color-charge density and pT broadening are constrained together?
questions.rationale: This follows from the heavy-quark colorimetry proposal and the relation between radiative loss and transverse broadening in QCD matter [1], [3].

node_decbc2dcd928.summary: These works emphasize charm and heavy-quark energy loss, assessing the competing roles of collisional scattering, radiative emission, finite-size effects, and plasma response.

questions.question: What measurement can quantitatively separate radiative from collisional heavy-quark energy loss in hot QCD matter over the 5-10 GeV transverse-momentum range?
questions.rationale: This follows from reviews of collisional and radiative loss and the prediction that finite heavy-quark mass changes heavy-to-light observables such as the D/pi ratio at moderate pT [3], [4].

questions.question: Where is the transition between L2 and L scaling of finite-size radiative energy loss for heavy and light quarks in realistic expanding media?
questions.rationale: This derives from finite-volume calculations predicting L2 energy loss for energetic quarks and a turn to approximately L scaling as the quark energy decreases [2], [5].

questions.question: Can pT broadening and induced gluon radiation be related in hot matter as universally as in the large-nucleus calculation, independent of microscopic scattering details?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the result that dE/dz is proportional to alpha_s Nc times transverse-momentum broadening in large nuclei under broad conditions [1].

node_41a387b5a3a7.summary: This cluster develops perturbative treatments of medium-induced radiation and its path-length dependence for energetic partons traversing finite or expanding QCD matter.

questions.question: What observable can distinguish the L^2 finite-volume radiative energy-loss regime from the L-linear regime caused by finite parton energy or cold nuclear matter effects?
questions.rationale: Papers [2] and [4] predict Delta E proportional to L^2 in finite hot media but note transitions toward L-linear behavior at lower quark energy or in nuclei.

questions.question: Can p_perp broadening and induced gluon radiation be unified experimentally through the relation dE/dz = (1/8) alpha_s N_c p_perpW^2 in realistic expanding QCD matter?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] derives this relation for large nuclear matter under multiple scattering and suggests enhanced effects in hot matter.

questions.question: How should the non-abelian LPM formation time, color representation dependence, and longitudinal plasma expansion be combined into jet-quenching predictions with controlled theoretical uncertainty?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] derives color-dependent LPM suppression, while [3] compares approaches and treats longitudinally expanding QCD plasma.

node_00569f7ecd3b.summary: These papers model charm and bottom quark energy loss, hadronization, and heavy-meson suppression to interpret B, D, quarkonium, and heavy-to-light measurements.

questions.question: At which transverse momenta do charm and bottom quarks stop exhibiting mass-dependent energy loss and become effectively light-parton probes in heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: The heavy-to-light ratio study found charm behaves essentially like light quarks for experimentally accessible high-pT D mesons at the LHC, while heavy-to-light ratios test mass and color-charge dependence [2].

questions.question: Can a unified treatment of running-coupling collisional loss, radiative loss, and hadronization reproduce both heavy-flavor R_AA and v_2 without tuning separate mechanisms for each observable?
questions.rationale: The RHIC single-electron analysis found fixed-coupling pQCD insufficient, while running coupling and HTL screening substantially increased collisional energy loss and improved both R_AA and v_2 [3].

questions.question: How can cold-nuclear-matter energy loss that scales with quarkonium energy be separated from hot-medium suppression in interpreting J/psi and Upsilon data across p-A and A-A systems?
questions.rationale: The p-A quarkonium study argued from first principles that medium-induced energy loss scales as E and can reproduce J/psi and Upsilon suppression with a single parameter [4].

node_3e86b89d4e7d.summary: This cluster applies AdS/CFT, hybrid strong/weak coupling models, and plasma wake calculations to describe jet and heavy-quark energy loss in strongly coupled media.

questions.question: Can the light-like Wilson-loop definition of qhat be matched quantitatively between strongly coupled N=4 SYM, flowing plasma backgrounds, and phenomenological QCD jet-quenching extractions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the AdS/CFT calculation of qhat from a light-like Wilson loop [1] and its extension to moving plasmas and related Wilson loops [4].

questions.question: How should hybrid strong/weak jet-quenching models incorporate the hydrodynamic wake and conical-flow response of the medium without double counting perturbative shower evolution?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the hybrid treatment of hard shower evolution and soft strong-coupling energy loss [3] together with conical flow and plasma-wake analyses [2,5].

node_f13ca8b9dd2d.summary: These works analyze transverse momentum broadening and qhat in anisotropic, flowing, expanding, unstable, pre-equilibrium, and dense QCD media.

questions.question: Can the soft contribution to the jet-quenching parameter qhat be determined with controlled matching between SCET Glauber-Wilson-line definitions, electrostatic-QCD lattice calculations, and weak-coupling NLO plasma corrections?
questions.rationale: SCET expresses transverse momentum broadening through separated lightlike Wilson lines, while EQCD lattice simulations and O(g) plasma corrections show large soft contributions to qhat [2], [3], [4].

questions.question: How do anisotropy, non-equilibrium dynamics, and next-to-leading self-energy effects modify the tensor structure of momentum broadening beyond isotropic equilibrium qhat?
questions.rationale: In anisotropic plasma, next-to-leading self-energy effects regulate singularities and produce larger broadening along the beam axis than in the transverse plane [5].

questions.question: Can recoil-sensitive single-logarithmic resummation of jet broadening be consistently connected to medium-induced transverse-momentum broadening in heavy-ion jet observables?
questions.rationale: Precise small-B jet-broadening resummation requires proper treatment of quark recoil, while medium studies define transverse momentum broadening through parton interactions with QCD matter [1], [3].

node_380ae7629bf5.summary: This cluster develops formalisms for gluon radiation induced by multiple scattering, including coherence, decoherence, opacity expansion, antenna interference, and medium-induced branching.

questions.question: Can opacity-expansion and path-integral formalisms give quantitatively identical kt-differential medium-induced gluon spectra once realistic finite media and regularization prescriptions are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proof of equivalence between BDMPS and Zakharov formalisms for kt-differential radiation after resumming opacity terms [1].

questions.question: Where is the boundary between coherent LPM suppression and independent Bethe-Heitler-like emissions for gluon radiation in QCD matter with finite path length and density?
questions.rationale: This derives from the role of large formation times in suppressing radiation relative to independent emissions in the BDMPS picture [2].

questions.question: How does medium filling of the heavy-quark dead cone propagate into experimentally robust differences between charm, bottom, and light-parton energy loss?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the calculation that medium-induced radiation fills the dead cone while reducing large-energy gluon radiation from massive quarks [3].

node_f50cdc226c50.summary: These papers use nuclear Drell-Yan production to separate shadowing, nuclear PDFs, and initial-state quark energy loss in cold nuclear matter.

questions.question: Can lower-energy fixed-target Drell-Yan measurements at large xF separate initial-state quark energy loss from nuclear shadowing well enough to determine the quark radiation length in cold nuclear matter?
questions.rationale: This follows from the E906-focused proposal in [4] and the E772/E866 shadowing-versus-energy-loss analysis in [5].

questions.question: How do generalized-factorization corrections beyond the soft-bremsstrahlung approximation change the energy-loss values inferred from nuclear DIS and Drell-Yan attenuation?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which reduces effective energy loss by 5/6 beyond the helicity-amplitude approximation, and [2], which tests nuclear hadronization dynamics in DIS.

questions.question: Which high-xF nuclear suppression data can falsify energy-loss explanations in favor of other nuclear mechanisms?
questions.rationale: This derives from [3], which gives a quantum-mechanical upper bound on radiative energy loss and argues that quarkonium suppression at high xF cannot be explained by parton energy loss.

node_47a76a49b9b0.summary: This cluster studies shear and bulk viscosities, conductivities, and relativistic viscous hydrodynamics for quark-gluon plasma and hot hadronic matter.

questions.question: How can RHIC- and LHC-scale flow data quantitatively resolve the tension between weak-coupling transport-coefficient calculations and the strongly coupled sQGP interpretation?
questions.rationale: The tension is between leading-order high-temperature gauge-theory transport coefficients [1,3] and the RHIC conclusion that collective flow requires much larger rescattering than perturbative QCD suggests [2].

questions.question: What precision in extracting eta/s, bulk viscosity, conductivity, and diffusion constants from 3+1D viscous hydrodynamics is required before numerical viscosity and freeze-out systematics stop dominating the comparison to microscopic theory?
questions.rationale: MUSIC emphasizes small numerical viscosity and detailed freeze-out reconstruction [4], while modern viscous hydrodynamics connects second-order fluid equations to weakly and strongly coupled systems [5].

questions.question: Do next-to-leading-log approximations remain reliable for QGP phenomenology in the temperature range where the Debye mass is not parametrically smaller than T?
questions.rationale: The beyond-leading-log calculation finds next-to-leading-log results approximate full leading order well when the Debye mass is less than the temperature [3], while phenomenology points to a strongly coupled regime for T_c < T < 4T_c [2].

node_415bdd985266.summary: These works examine when far-from-equilibrium kinetic systems in heavy-ion collisions become accurately described by viscous or anisotropic relativistic hydrodynamics.

questions.question: What quantitative criterion marks the onset of hydrodynamic applicability in far-from-equilibrium heavy-ion matter: small gradients, bounded viscous corrections, or approach to a non-equilibrium attractor?
questions.rationale: Modern viscous hydrodynamics has multiple derivations with limited applicability, while the non-equilibrium review emphasizes divergent gradient expansions and attractor solutions [2], [5].

questions.question: How do hydrodynamic fluctuations and derivative-expansion breakdown modify eta/s extraction from event-by-event hydrodynamic and hadronic-cascade simulations?
questions.rationale: Hydrodynamic fluctuations cause derivative-expansion breakdown, and iEBE-VISHNU is designed for event-by-event model-data comparisons of heavy-ion collisions [3], [4].

questions.question: Can 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic codes with low numerical viscosity and realistic freeze-out be benchmarked against kinetic-theory derivations to separate physical hydrodynamization from numerical artifacts?
questions.rationale: MUSIC emphasizes low numerical viscosity and freeze-out construction, while viscous hydrodynamics is derived partly from kinetic theory with specified domains of validity [1], [2].

node_44c09d86e5bf.summary: This cluster develops and analyzes relativistic dissipative hydrodynamic theories, emphasizing kinetic derivations, second-order corrections, stability, and causality.

questions.question: Can first-order stable-frame relativistic viscous hydrodynamics reproduce the same nonlinear fluctuation, causality, and existence properties as second-order Israel-Stewart-like theories when coupled to realistic QGP transport coefficients?
questions.rationale: This follows from the result that first-order hydrodynamics has stable frames and from the nonlinear causality and existence proof for a second-order conformal viscous theory coupled to gravity [4][5].

questions.question: How can the local KMS symmetry and nonlinear Onsager relations in dissipative-fluid effective field theory be matched quantitatively onto kinetic-theory integral equations for transport coefficients?
questions.rationale: This question connects the EFT formulation of dissipative fluids with local KMS constraints to the weak-coupling scalar-field result reducible to the linearized Boltzmann equation [2][3].

questions.question: At what order and fluctuation strength does the hydrodynamic derivative expansion break down in relativistic fluids, and how should that breakdown be incorporated in phenomenological hydrodynamization models?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the lectures' emphasis on hydrodynamic-mode interactions, fluctuating hydrodynamics, and the breakdown of the derivative expansion [1].

node_c021d4b5eebb.summary: These papers derive second-order dissipative, multicomponent, and magnetohydrodynamic transport equations and coefficients from Boltzmann kinetic theory.

questions.question: Can the equivalence between leading weak-coupling diagram resummation and a linearized Boltzmann equation be extended from scalar theory to full non-Abelian plasmas with quasiparticle masses and scattering amplitudes treated consistently at second order?
questions.rationale: This follows from the scalar-field result that an infinite leading diagram class reduces to the same linear integral equation as an effective Boltzmann description [1].

questions.question: Which second- and third-order gradient structures are actually required to reproduce exact kinetic-theory evolution of pressure anisotropy beyond one-dimensional scaling expansion?
questions.rationale: The relaxation-time Chapman-Enskog derivations show improved agreement with exact Boltzmann solutions when higher-order viscous corrections are included [3], [5].

questions.question: Can dissipative magnetohydrodynamic transport coefficients derived from generalized global symmetry be matched to microscopic kinetic coefficients, including a Kubo definition of resistivity, in weakly coupled plasmas?
questions.rationale: The generalized-symmetry construction gives seven first-order MHD transport coefficients and a Kubo formula for resistivity, while the kinetic papers compute microscopic transport coefficients [2], [4].

node_4b853489d54a.summary: This cluster focuses on the conditions under which relativistic Navier-Stokes and viscous hydrodynamic theories remain stable, causal, and well posed.

questions.question: What are the necessary and sufficient inequalities on first-order transport coefficients and frame choices for nonlinear causality, strong hyperbolicity, equilibrium stability, and non-negative entropy production with shear, bulk viscosity, heat conduction, and baryon density?
questions.rationale: This extends the stable-frame parameter-space result of [1] to the full first-order general-relativistic viscous theory with all dissipative channels in [3].

questions.question: Can stable-frame first-order relativistic Navier-Stokes theory be derived systematically from kinetic theory beyond neutral conformal fluids while remaining causal when coupled to Einstein equations?
questions.rationale: The conformal kinetic-theory derivation and nonlinear existence proof with gravity in [2] motivate testing the broader first-order stable-frame program of [5].

questions.question: How should asymptotic causality conditions such as tau_pi/Gamma_s be related to finite-wavenumber boosted-frame spectra so that stability criteria do not misidentify superluminal group velocities as acausality?
questions.rationale: The distinction between boosted-frame stability, asymptotic causality, and finite-wavenumber group velocity is analyzed in [4].

node_e832954c0819.summary: These works formulate stochastic and Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions for relativistic dissipative fluids including thermal fluctuations and correlation functions.

questions.question: Can Schwinger-Keldysh hydrodynamic effective actions with dynamical KMS symmetry provide a complete renormalized treatment of fluctuation-induced breakdown of the derivative expansion in relativistic fluids?
questions.rationale: Hydrodynamic fluctuations cause derivative-expansion breakdown, while dissipative-fluid EFTs impose local or dynamical KMS symmetry to organize noise, nonlinear interactions, and entropy constraints [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: How are frame choices, field redefinitions, and non-equilibrium entropy currents constrained beyond second order when dissipative hydrodynamics is derived from an open-system effective action?
questions.rationale: The action-based formulation clarifies field redefinitions and frames, while second-order viscous hydrodynamics relates transport coefficients through positivity of entropy production [3], [4], [5].

node_254ad9d1223e.summary: This cluster reviews and develops relativistic hydrodynamic descriptions of quark-gluon plasma evolution in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions.

questions.question: How can event-by-event 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic simulations quantify the separate uncertainties from numerical viscosity, freeze-out surface reconstruction, and the lattice-based equation of state in predictions for v2 and v4 versus pT and pseudorapidity?
questions.rationale: MUSIC emphasizes low numerical viscosity, shock handling, triangulated freeze-out, a lattice equation of state, and precision flow predictions [1].

questions.question: Which second-order transport coefficients and transient modes are actually constrained by heavy-ion data once hydrodynamization, divergent gradient expansions, attractors, and thermal fluctuations are included consistently?
questions.rationale: The reviews connect second-order viscous hydrodynamics to kinetic theory, effective field theory, gradient divergence, attractors, and transient modes [2,4,5].

questions.question: Can hybrid hydrodynamics plus hadronic cascade frameworks extract medium evolution in a way that is simultaneously compatible with bulk hadrons, thermal photons, jet energy loss, and heavy-quark diffusion?
questions.rationale: iEBE-VISHNU was built for event-by-event model-data comparisons and includes interfaces for thermal photons and other rare probes coupled to temperature and flow evolution [3].

node_e121ca204bd9.summary: These papers study universal far-from-equilibrium attractor solutions that explain early hydrodynamic behavior in Bjorken-expanding quark-gluon plasma systems.

questions.question: What is the precise transseries structure connecting nonhydrodynamic modes, Borel singularities, and the universal attractor in kinetic theory beyond relaxation-time approximation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the resurgence and Borel-summation interpretation of attractors and the finding that not all Borel singularities in RTA kinetic theory correspond to transient modes [1,3].

questions.question: Can aHydro's simultaneous resummation of Knudsen and inverse Reynolds effects be generalized to realistic 3+1D heavy-ion initial conditions while preserving positive longitudinal pressure?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the anisotropic-hydrodynamics attractor result that resums infinitely many inverse-Reynolds terms and closely matches the exact Boltzmann attractor with positive pressure ratio [4].

questions.question: What separates early-time attraction from late-time hydrodynamization in phenomenologically relevant boost-invariant 3+1D systems?
questions.rationale: This derives from the observation that early-time approach to the attractor can occur before hydrodynamization and follows different power-law dynamics than late-time exponential approach [5].

node_2a4c10a0929e.summary: This cluster compares exact relaxation-time Boltzmann solutions with viscous and anisotropic hydrodynamic approximations for rapidly expanding relativistic systems.

questions.question: What is the minimal second-order anisotropic hydrodynamic closure that remains quantitatively accurate against exact relaxation-time Boltzmann solutions for arbitrary initial momentum anisotropy and shear viscosity?
questions.rationale: Exact boost-invariant RTA solutions showed that anisotropic hydrodynamics can closely approximate kinetic theory when relaxation times are matched appropriately [2].

questions.question: Can the de Sitter-space formulation of conformal flow be used to derive controlled tests of anisotropic hydrodynamics with transverse expansion and perturbations beyond Bjorken symmetry?
questions.rationale: Gubser-type conformal flow is fixed by symmetry and becomes static in de Sitter space, enabling viscous corrections and linearized perturbations [1][3].

questions.question: How should deviations from a spheroidal one-particle distribution be organized so that second-order anisotropic hydrodynamics remains stable and predictive in full 2+1-dimensional expansion?
questions.rationale: The second-order 2+1-dimensional formulation introduced additional viscous tensor components generated by deviations from the leading spheroidal ansatz [4].

node_cb54d04c40df.summary: These works compute shear and bulk viscosity and related transport coefficients in QCD matter using lattice, perturbative, quasiparticle, and hadron-gas methods.

questions.question: Can lattice spectral-function extractions, leading-order kinetic theory, and Bayesian heavy-ion calibrations be brought to a common temperature-dependent parametrization of eta/s and zeta/s with controlled uncertainties near the QCD crossover?
questions.rationale: The tension between perturbative transport calculations [1][2], lattice estimates relying on spectral smoothness [4], and phenomenological Bayesian extraction of temperature-dependent viscosities [3][5] motivates this question.

questions.question: Which experimental observables can break the degeneracy between initial-state entropy deposition and the minimum and slope of the QGP specific shear viscosity inferred from hydrodynamic model-to-data comparisons?
questions.rationale: The Bayesian TRENTO plus hybrid-hydrodynamics analysis finds correlated constraints on initial conditions and temperature-dependent shear viscosity, including a relation between the minimum and slope [3].

node_88fca9c9d6dc.summary: This cluster estimates viscosities, conductivities, and other transport coefficients of hot and dense quark-gluon matter at finite temperature and chemical potential.

questions.question: Can weak-coupling leading-order transport calculations and lattice spectral-function extractions be reconciled into a controlled description of eta/s across the temperature range where QGP behaves nearly perfectly?
questions.rationale: This question connects the full leading-order shear-viscosity calculations in [1] and [2] with the lattice SU(3) estimate of eta/s near 1.65 Tc in [3] and the nearly perfect fluidity review in [5].

questions.question: How do finite baryon density and light-quark effects modify the expected critical enhancement of bulk viscosity near O(4) or Z(2) QCD critical behavior?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [4], which extends bulk-viscosity sum-rule analysis to light quarks and discusses O(4) and Z(2) universal behavior near QCD phase transitions.

questions.question: Which transport coefficients at finite temperature and chemical potential are most sensitive to the breakdown of the 1/log(1/g) expansion used in high-temperature gauge theories?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [2], which evaluates shear viscosity, flavor diffusion, and electrical conductivity beyond leading log and tests the usefulness of the 1/log(1/g) expansion.

node_8c20cdfc8d13.summary: Studies compute shear and bulk viscosity of quark-gluon and pure-glue plasmas using perturbative, lattice, quasiparticle, and sum-rule methods, emphasizing temperature, chemical-potential, and critical behavior.

questions.question: Can lattice spectral-function reconstructions of the shear channel reach the precision needed to distinguish eta/s near the proposed quantum lower bound from perturbative leading-order and next-to-leading-log expectations?
questions.rationale: This question links the perturbative transport calculations in [1] and [2] with the lattice SU(3) shear-viscosity estimate and spectral smoothness assumption in [3].

questions.question: How does bulk viscosity scale near the O(4) chiral transition and Z(2) critical point once realistic light-quark masses and finite baryon density are included?
questions.rationale: The critical and universal behavior of bulk viscosity near QCD phase transitions is the focus of [4].

questions.question: What controlled matching connects weak-coupling kinetic theory, lattice Euclidean correlators, and phenomenological nearly perfect fluid behavior across the temperature range probed by heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the weak-coupling transport results of [1] and [2], the lattice calculation in [3], and the cross-system nearly perfect fluidity review in [5].

node_c3ee75ecdc9f.summary: This cluster focuses on bulk viscosity in hot QCD matter near phase transitions and criticality, including its relation to shear viscosity and extraction from lattice, hydrodynamic, and strongly coupled models.

questions.question: Can lattice equation-of-state data and sum rules determine whether bulk viscosity near the QCD transition shows the universal critical behavior expected for O(4) or Z(2) dynamics?
questions.rationale: This follows from the light-quark sum-rule extraction and universality arguments for bulk viscosity near chiral and critical-point transitions in [1].

questions.question: How does the microscopic origin of bulk viscosity change between weakly coupled high-temperature QCD, where zeta is small relative to eta, and near-transition matter used in heavy-ion hydrodynamics?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the weak-coupling QCD calculation in [4], the kinetic-theory distinction between shear and bulk processes in [3], and the nearly perfect fluid context in [2].

questions.question: Can holographic QCD-like models with crossover equations of state be calibrated to lattice thermodynamics tightly enough to make quantitative predictions for zeta/s near T_c?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the black-hole dual calculations showing different zeta/s behavior for first-order transitions and smooth crossovers in [5].

node_03ea4bffe83e.summary: Papers determine shear and bulk viscosities and related spectral functions of pure-glue or quenched QCD plasmas from lattice correlators, Kubo formulas, and nonperturbative reconstruction methods.

questions.question: Can lattice reconstructions of the energy-momentum tensor spectral function determine whether the low-frequency smoothness assumption used to extract eta/s in SU(3) gluodynamics is quantitatively reliable?
questions.rationale: This targets the key assumption behind the eta/s estimate from high-precision lattice tensor correlators in SU(3) gauge theory [2].

questions.question: What nonperturbative feature of the scalar trace-anomaly correlator drives the rapid rise of zeta/s just above Tc, and can it be separated from analytic-continuation systematics?
questions.rationale: This follows from the strong temperature dependence and near-Tc enhancement of bulk viscosity found in SU(3) gluodynamics [3].

questions.question: How can hydrodynamic pole constraints, sum rules, and lattice correlator data be combined to reduce the degeneracy of small-frequency transport spectral functions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the review emphasis that Euclidean conserved-current correlators determine transport only through an ill-posed integral transform constrained by hydrodynamic pole structure [5].

node_f580b2d8b82a.summary: This cluster develops Kubo, real-time finite-temperature, ladder-resummation, and kinetic approaches for computing shear viscosity in weakly coupled gauge and scalar theories.

questions.question: What missing NLO contributions to QCD shear viscosity are needed to decide whether the weak-coupling expansion is quantitatively useful at physically relevant temperatures?
questions.rationale: This follows from the almost-NLO QCD calculation finding large corrections, dominant qhat effects, and problematic convergence even near T≈100 GeV [2].

questions.question: Can ladder-resummed Kubo and kinetic-theory formulations be matched term by term for gauge theories beyond leading order, including Coulomb logarithms and soft momentum diffusion?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by full leading-order transport calculations beyond leading log and the diagrammatic resummations required for viscosity [1].

questions.question: How universal is the relation between 2PI ladder integral equations and weak-coupling variational solutions across O(N), QCD, QED, and weakly coupled N=4 SYM shear viscosity?
questions.rationale: This connects the 2PI-1/N treatment of O(N) viscosity with weak-coupling comparisons among QCD, QED, and N=4 SYM [4],[5].

node_cb27230510ac.summary: These papers estimate viscosities, conductivities, and thermal transport in hot and dense quark matter using NJL, PNJL, quasiparticle, relaxation-time, and magnetic-field frameworks.

questions.question: Can NJL, PNJL, DQPM, and quasiparticle descriptions be calibrated to lattice thermodynamics in a way that yields predictive shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, electric conductivity, and heat conductivity above the critical temperature?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison showing limited NJL predictive power above Tc while PNJL and DQPM better reproduce thermodynamic and transport quantities [1].

questions.question: Which transport coefficient is the most sensitive probe of the order of the chiral phase transition and the location of a critical end point in finite-temperature, finite-density quark matter?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the calculation of shear and bulk viscosities near the chiral phase boundary and their proposed sensitivity to the critical end point [3].

questions.question: How do magnetic-field-induced anisotropic viscosities and anomalous color-field viscosities combine in rapidly expanding QGP, and can their relative size explain nearly perfect liquidity without assuming a uniformly strong-coupling plasma?
questions.rationale: This question links the five-shear-coefficient tensor structure in magnetized plasma to anomalous viscosity from dynamically generated color fields in anisotropic expansion [4,5].

node_2d9c493f6c28.summary: This cluster combines hadron-gas, quasiparticle, hydrodynamic, transport, and Bayesian analyses to constrain QCD matter transport coefficients across temperature and baryon-density regimes.

questions.question: How tightly can Bayesian heavy-ion analyses constrain temperature- and baryon-density-dependent shear and bulk viscosities once RHIC, LHC, and lower-energy observables are calibrated in a common multi-stage framework?
questions.rationale: This extends the Bayesian transport-coefficient extraction of [1] and the multisystem RHIC/LHC constraints of [3] toward the finite-density regimes summarized by the node.

questions.question: Which observables most cleanly break degeneracies between initial entropy deposition, free-streaming parameters, and the bulk-viscosity peak near the QCD crossover?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the initial-condition and viscosity degeneracies studied in [1], the phenomenological importance of bulk viscosity in [2], and the variable free-streaming stage in [5].

questions.question: Can closure-tested emulators remain reliable when extrapolating transport-coefficient posteriors from collider energies to finite-baryon-density heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the closure-test emphasis in [3] and [5], where emulator validation is central before comparing multi-parameter models to data.

node_d56026ee8494.summary: Papers review and model the nearly ideal-fluid behavior, early thermalization, and hydrodynamic evolution of strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma using RHIC/LHC data and gauge-gravity methods.

questions.question: What observable can distinguish early hydrodynamization or isotropization from full thermal equilibration in strongly coupled plasma, and can gauge-gravity horizon-formation calculations provide quantitative priors for heavy-ion initial conditions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the near-ideal hydrodynamic behavior reported in [1] and the far-from-equilibrium isotropization study in [4].

questions.question: Can second-order transport coefficients from charged AdS_5 black-hole hydrodynamics be mapped onto QCD matter near T_c < T < 4 T_c in a way consistent with lattice equations of state and RHIC/LHC flow data?
questions.rationale: This connects the transport-coefficient calculation in [2] with the lattice-EoS and collective-flow phenomenology emphasized in [1] and [3].

questions.question: What experimental signatures would discriminate a strongly coupled bound-state or electric-magnetic description of sQGP from a weakly coupled quasiparticle gas with anomalously large rescattering?
questions.rationale: This follows from the contrast between weakly coupled expectations and strong-coupling interpretations in [3] and the electric-magnetic discussion in [5].

node_909dac263201.summary: This cluster addresses how strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma forms, thermalizes, and enters hydrodynamic flow in heavy-ion collisions, with emphasis on AdS/CFT and RHIC/LHC phenomenology.

questions.question: What minimum set of early-time observables can distinguish true hydrodynamization of the QGP from mere momentum-space isotropization in strongly coupled plasma formation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the AdS/CFT study of anisotropic plasma evolution and horizon formation as a model of far-from-equilibrium isotropization [3].
