questions.rationale: This follows from the reported strong volume dependence of the critical endpoint position in two-flavor lattice Taylor-expansion studies [1].
kg_prereqs: Taylor expansion at finite chemical potential

questions.question: How can boundary-condition, pion-mass, and mesonic fluctuation effects be folded into a controlled extrapolation of the chiral-transition curvature from finite lattice volumes to infinite-volume QCD?
questions.rationale: Functional RG quark-meson studies find pronounced finite-volume effects on the transition curvature that depend on boundary conditions and pion mass [2].

node_68d97ff57309.summary: This cluster centers on lattice determinations and phenomenological modeling of the QCD equation of state across temperature and chemical-potential regimes relevant to hot dense matter.

questions.question: Can different improved staggered-fermion discretizations produce a single continuum QCD equation of state with quantified correlations among pressure, interaction measure, energy density, entropy density, and speed of sound?
questions.rationale: The HISQ, stout, asqtad, and p4 equation-of-state studies compare discretizations, continuum extrapolations, and thermodynamic observables over overlapping temperature ranges [1][2][3][5].

questions.question: How should lattice equation-of-state parameterizations near the chiral crossover be extended to finite baryon density while preserving consistency with deconfinement and chiral-restoration observables?
questions.rationale: The finite-temperature equation-of-state papers provide continuum parameterizations around the crossover, while the finite-temperature and density review frames the deconfining, chiral, and high-temperature thermodynamic aspects of the phase diagram [1][4][5].

node_667b27a44cbc.summary: These papers formulate thermodynamically consistent quasiparticle descriptions of the quark-gluon plasma that reproduce lattice QCD thermodynamics and extend them to finite chemical potential.

questions.question: Can a single thermodynamically consistent quasiparticle framework reproduce lattice pressure, quasiparticle masses, static-quark free energies, and spectral-density evidence for bound states near 1-3 T_c?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which connects lattice spectral functions, static-quark free energies, quasiparticle masses, and bulk thermodynamics in the strongly interacting QGP.

questions.question: How unique is the finite-chemical-potential equation of state obtained by extending zero-density lattice fits through Maxwell-relation flow equations?
questions.rationale: This derives from [3] and [5], which extend quasiparticle models from zero to nonzero chemical potential using thermodynamic self-consistency.

questions.question: Can interacting cold-quark-matter equations of state calibrated to perturbative QCD and lattice-motivated quasiparticles yield compact-star predictions with controlled systematic uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4], which constructs a practical interacting quark-matter EOS with built-in uncertainty estimates for compact-star applications.

node_d15d27781a1b.summary: This cluster reports continuum-oriented lattice QCD equation-of-state calculations with improved actions, dynamical quarks, and near-physical or physical quark masses.

questions.question: What residual discretization and action-dependence uncertainties limit the continuum 2+1-flavor QCD equation of state in the crossover region after HISQ, stout, asqtad, and p4 calculations are compared at physical quark masses?
questions.rationale: This is derived from the continuum-oriented physical-mass equation-of-state calculations and cross-action comparisons in the representative lattice studies [1,2,3,4].

questions.question: Can the pressure parameterizations and tabulated physical-mass equation-of-state results be sharpened enough to determine the speed of sound and interaction measure across 130-400 MeV at a precision useful for phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the HISQ parameterization of pressure and thermodynamic observables and the published tabulated 2+1-flavor equation-of-state results [1,2].

questions.question: How should high-temperature cutoff effects above several hundred MeV be controlled when extending physical-mass 2+1-flavor thermodynamics toward the 800-1000 MeV range?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the high-temperature ranges and explicit discussion of significant finite-cutoff effects in physical or almost-physical mass equation-of-state studies [3,5].

node_11bdbfb82f84.summary: These review papers summarize lattice QCD results on finite-temperature and finite-density thermodynamics, including phase transitions, equations of state, and quark-gluon plasma observables.

questions.question: What single lattice observable, or combination of observables, would most sharply distinguish chiral restoration from deconfinement in the finite-temperature QCD crossover?
questions.rationale: Papers [1], [2], and [4] review the parallel but distinct deconfining and chiral features of the QCD transition.

questions.question: How can finite-density lattice methods at small baryon chemical potential be benchmarked so that equation-of-state, conserved-charge fluctuation, and heavy-ion interpretations share controlled systematic errors?
questions.rationale: Papers [3] and [4] emphasize finite-density simulations, bulk thermodynamics, and conserved-charge fluctuations as inputs to heavy-ion phenomenology.

questions.question: Can lattice spectral-density and screening-length calculations deliver transport and in-medium hadron information precise enough to constrain quark-gluon-plasma observables independently of model assumptions?
questions.rationale: Papers [3], [4], and [5] identify transport properties, spectral densities, screening, and thermal hadron modifications as central but difficult lattice targets.

node_5a3066088285.summary: This cluster uses Taylor expansion and analytic-continuation methods to estimate the QCD equation of state, susceptibilities, and transition behavior at nonzero chemical potential.

questions.question: How far in mu_B/T can Taylor-expanded lattice QCD be pushed before sixth-order and higher coefficients cease to give controlled estimates of pressure, density, and susceptibilities?
questions.rationale: This follows from fourth- and sixth-order Taylor calculations of thermodynamic observables and their use in estimating the radius of convergence [1], [2].

questions.question: Which observables provide the most reliable radius-of-convergence signal for a chiral critical point when bulk thermodynamic quantities remain inconclusive?
questions.rationale: This derives from the observation that baryon and isospin fluctuations can be related to the convergence radius while bulk observables did not yet show decisive critical behavior [1].

questions.question: How should continuum finite-mu lattice equations of state incorporate charm-threshold effects when used for expansion-rate calculations between the QCD and electroweak scales?
questions.rationale: This combines continuum physical-mass Taylor results at nonzero chemical potential with evidence that charm contributes visibly to thermodynamics at unexpectedly low temperatures [3], [4].

node_aec485a5898c.summary: These papers construct lattice-informed QCD equations of state for heavy-ion collisions, incorporating baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials and sometimes critical-point behavior.

questions.question: How much do sixth-order baryon, strangeness, and electric-charge chemical-potential terms change hydrodynamic predictions relative to equations of state matched only through O(mu_B4)?
questions.rationale: This follows from lattice calculations of the QCD equation of state through O(mu_B6) and critical-point equations of state matched to O(mu_B4) lattice data [1], [2].

questions.question: Which mapping choices from the 3D Ising model to QCD leave observable imprints on pressure, speed of sound, and baryon density in Beam Energy Scan simulations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the construction of lattice-matched QCD equations of state with a tunable critical point and free Ising-to-QCD mapping parameters [2].

questions.question: How large are the combined effects of strangeness neutrality, fixed charge-to-baryon ratio, and additional strange resonances on multiparticle correlations in heavy-ion collisions?
questions.rationale: This follows from finite-density equations of state enforcing heavy-ion charge constraints and from studies of new strange resonances in the equation of state and hadronic afterburners [4], [5].

node_27c6221bfea1.summary: This cluster computes lattice QCD fluctuations and correlations of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness to characterize deconfinement, hadronic matter, and critical behavior.

questions.question: Which continuum-extrapolated combinations of baryon, charge, and strangeness susceptibilities most cleanly isolate missing hadron-resonance content from genuine deconfinement physics near 150-250 MeV?
questions.rationale: The HISQ fluctuation study compares continuum-extrapolated conserved-charge susceptibilities with the hadron resonance gas in this temperature interval [2].

questions.question: Can finite-density Taylor coefficients of conserved-charge fluctuations separate O(4), critical-end-point, and hidden-tricritical scaling before analytic continuation or sign-problem limitations dominate?
questions.rationale: The universality study argues that a hidden tricritical point can affect quark-number susceptibility near the critical end point and change the effective critical exponent [4].

questions.question: How accurately must lattice spacing, quark-mass dependence, and resonance-spectrum distortions be controlled before HRG-lattice discrepancies can be interpreted as evidence for new thermodynamic degrees of freedom?
questions.rationale: The equation-of-state comparison shows that HRG-lattice discrepancies are largely reduced after accounting for heavier lattice quark masses and finite-spacing errors [1].

node_587a49f35175.summary: These studies use high-order baryon and conserved-charge cumulants from lattice, Dyson-Schwinger, and effective models to probe the QCD phase diagram and possible critical endpoint.

questions.question: Can continuum-extrapolated sixth- and eighth-order baryon cumulant ratios under strangeness-neutral heavy-ion conditions provide an unambiguous lattice-QCD signature of proximity to a critical endpoint?
questions.rationale: This derives from the rapid transition-region behavior of sixth- and eighth-order moments in [4] and the strangeness-neutral cumulant-ratio construction in [5].

questions.question: Where exactly do hadron-resonance-gas descriptions of conserved-charge fluctuations fail as temperature rises, and which charge correlations best identify the change in microscopic degrees of freedom?
questions.rationale: This follows from lattice-HRG comparisons of quadratic fluctuations and charge correlations in [1] and the degree-of-freedom interpretation of quartic-to-quadratic ratios in [3].

questions.question: How can imaginary-chemical-potential lattice methods be extended or cross-checked to control uncertainties in high-order conserved-charge correlations at nonzero baryon chemical potential?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the use of imaginary chemical potential to obtain higher-order fluctuations and correlations in [5].

node_7a9aad4eeeb2.summary: This cluster examines second- and higher-order fluctuations of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness as signals of changing degrees of freedom near the QCD transition.

questions.question: Which continuum-extrapolated combinations of baryon, charge, and strangeness susceptibilities most sharply locate the change from hadron-resonance-gas degrees of freedom to quark-like carriers near the QCD transition?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the lattice-HRG comparisons of quadratic fluctuations and charge correlations in [1] and [2].

questions.question: Can higher-order cumulant ratios computed at imaginary chemical potential under strangeness neutrality and fixed charge-to-baryon ratio quantitatively predict the STAR net-charge and net-baryon fluctuation systematics?
questions.rationale: The construction of experimentally constrained cumulant ratios from imaginary-chemical-potential lattice data is described in [4].

questions.question: How consistently can freeze-out temperature and chemical potential be extracted independently from net-electric-charge and net-baryon higher moments once both lattice and experimental uncertainties are propagated?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed first-principles freeze-out extraction using higher-order charge and baryon fluctuations in [5].

node_0fdd1c5e08f5.summary: These papers use lattice QCD, effective models, and functional methods to study high-order net-baryon cumulants as probes of the QCD transition, critical endpoint, and heavy-ion freeze-out.

questions.question: Can lattice-QCD calculations of chi_6^B, chi_8^B, and chi_10^B along realistic freeze-out trajectories separate a true critical endpoint signal from non-monotonic behavior generated in the crossover region?
questions.rationale: High-order cumulants change rapidly near the transition [1], while hyper-order calculations show that non-monotonic energy dependence can arise even in a non-critical crossover [5].

questions.question: How stable is the parameter-free comparison between lattice net-baryon cumulants and experimental net-proton cumulants once acceptance, volume fluctuations, and baryon-to-proton mapping uncertainties are treated together?
questions.rationale: The lattice comparison to high-statistics STAR cumulants uses ratios expressed through chi_1^B/chi_2^B [2], while volume fluctuations can enhance and modify higher cumulants [4].

questions.question: At what order in mu_B/T do Taylor expansions around zero density cease to be reliable for cumulant ratios used in Beam Energy Scan freeze-out analyses?
questions.rationale: Direct finite-density effective-theory calculations up to tenth order were used to assess the applicability of expansions about vanishing density [5].

node_1ea93fa93127.summary: These works compare and extend hadron resonance gas models against lattice QCD thermodynamics to constrain the hadron spectrum, interactions, equation of state, and strangeness freeze-out.

questions.question: Which modifications to the hadron spectrum are required for an HRG model to reproduce lattice trace anomaly, baryon fluctuations, and strangeness fluctuations near the crossover at physical quark masses?
questions.rationale: The equation-of-state study shows discrepancies reduced by accounting for lattice quark-mass and cutoff effects, while later fluctuation work confirms HRG agreement in the confined phase [1,4].

questions.question: Can lattice strangeness-baryon correlations determine whether additional uncharted strange hadrons are thermodynamically required below the QCD crossover?
questions.rationale: The strange-hadron study finds that conventional HRG fails near the crossover and that quark-model or lattice-spectrum strange states improve agreement [5].

questions.question: How large are Taylor-truncation and unphysical-quark-mass errors when HRG thermodynamics is used to model nonzero-baryon-density lattice results below T_c?
questions.rationale: The nonzero-density comparison estimates truncation errors in mu expansions and studies the influence of heavy quark masses on the equation of state and critical conditions [3].

node_d43ec48a6a79.summary: This cluster studies diagonal and off-diagonal quark-number susceptibilities in hot QCD using lattice simulations, HTL resummation, perturbation theory, and critical-scaling arguments.

questions.question: Can continuum-extrapolated physical-mass 2+1 flavor susceptibilities resolve the 5-10 percent mismatch between HTL-resummed diagonal quark susceptibilities and lattice data at 1.5 to 5 Tc?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Wuppertal-Budapest continuum results for diagonal and non-diagonal susceptibilities and the HTL calculation that tracks lattice trends but overshoots them [1],[4].

questions.question: How does hidden tricriticality modify the scaling of quark-number susceptibility near the QCD critical endpoint, and can path-dependent critical exponents be separated from crossover behavior?
questions.rationale: This derives from universality and model studies showing crossover between CEP and TCP exponents and path-dependent critical behavior near critical regions [2],[3],[5].

questions.question: Which higher non-Gaussian conserved-charge moments remain robust probes of the critical endpoint after including matter back-reaction, renormalized vacuum terms, and continuum lattice constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from three-flavor model studies of higher moments near the critical point and from lattice constraints on conserved-charge fluctuations [1],[5].

node_d83646778c83.summary: These papers develop and review lattice strategies such as imaginary chemical potential, reweighting, density-of-states, and cumulant expansions for exploring finite-density QCD despite the sign problem.

questions.question: Can imaginary-chemical-potential continuation, Taylor expansion at mu=0, and multi-parameter reweighting be combined into a controlled continuum strategy for T_c(mu_B) beyond mu_B about 500 MeV?
questions.rationale: This question comes from the analyticity and continuation limits in [1] and [3], the small-mu Taylor method in [2], and reweighting in [5].

questions.question: What quantitative diagnostic can determine whether a proposed finite-density lattice method is finding a genuine QCD critical point rather than the boundary of its sign-problem-controlled accessible region?
questions.rationale: The need for such a diagnostic is explicit in the review of sign-problem severity, accessible baryon densities, and critical-point searches [4].

node_2d845eb7da3b.summary: This cluster focuses on the origin, severity, diagnostics, and mitigation of the complex fermion determinant sign problem in finite-density lattice QCD.

questions.question: Can analytic severity diagnostics for the complex fermion determinant be turned into quantitative criteria that predict, before simulation, the maximum baryon chemical potential accessible to reweighting, imaginary-chemical-potential continuation, or other nonstandard finite-density methods?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review emphasis on predicting the severity of the sign problem and the numerically accessible density range, while comparing small-chemical-potential workarounds [1].

questions.question: Which finite-volume and continuum-scaling observables can separate genuine critical-point signals from overlap failure in multi-parameter reweighting studies of finite-temperature QCD?
questions.rationale: The overlap-improving reweighting method was used to infer a four-flavor phase diagram from limited lattice volumes, making the distinction between physical critical behavior and reweighting artifacts central [2].

questions.question: Can matrix-model descriptions in which dense quarks generate a complex background Z(N) field suggest lattice observables or contour choices that reduce the sign problem without erasing the unequal behavior of Polyakov loops and conjugate loops?
questions.rationale: The SU(N) matrix model finds a real but non-positive measure and unequal real expectation values for the loop and conjugate loop, proposed as insight into the lattice sign problem [5].

node_1c81aef75329.summary: These works use imaginary chemical potentials, canonical partition functions, and analytic continuation to infer the finite-density QCD phase diagram and thermodynamics.

questions.question: Can imaginary-chemical-potential simulations at physical quark masses and controlled continuum spacing determine the radius of analyticity of T_c(mu_B) beyond the rapidly convergent mu_I/T <= pi/3 regime?
questions.rationale: This follows from the analytic-continuation strategy and observed rapid Taylor convergence for T_c(mu_I) in the small-density phase diagram study [1].

questions.question: How consistently do Taylor expansion, imaginary-mu analytic continuation, exact reweighting, and canonical-partition-function reconstructions predict the low-density critical curve and possible first-order region?
questions.rationale: The comparison of Taylor results with reweighting [2] and the canonical effective-potential indication of a first-order transition [4] motivate a systematic cross-method benchmark.

questions.question: Which ansatz classes for continuing chiral observables from imaginary to real mu_B remain stable when constrained simultaneously by chiral condensates, T_c(mu), and canonical density observables?
questions.rationale: The four-flavor analytic-continuation work tested theory- and model-motivated ansatze for the critical line and chiral condensate up to mu_B approximately 500 MeV [3].

node_d7d1ef736562.summary: This cluster searches for the QCD critical point by extracting Lee-Yang edge singularities in the complex chemical-potential plane using lattice data and Padé-based analytic continuation.

questions.question: Can multipoint Pade extractions of Lee-Yang edge singularities from imaginary-mu_B lattice data be made robust enough to distinguish a true QCD critical endpoint from rational-approximation poles?
questions.rationale: Refs. [3] and [5] use rational approximations to locate complex chemical-potential singularities, making pole stability central to the method.

questions.question: How do finite-volume sign-problem effects bias the scaling of Lee-Yang zeros toward the real axis, and what diagnostics can separate this artifact from genuine critical behavior?
questions.rationale: Ref. [4] warns that the sign problem can force Lee-Yang zeros toward the real axis in the thermodynamic limit and obscure crossover scaling.

questions.question: Are the complex-mu_B singularities inferred near the Roberge-Weiss and chiral regimes quantitatively consistent with a single universal scaling ansatz extrapolating to real chemical potential?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1], [3], and [5] connect complex chemical-potential singularities to universality, Roberge-Weiss behavior, and CEP extrapolation.

node_7ce7c20670ab.summary: This broad cluster covers finite-temperature QCD phenomena including quarkonium survival, spectral-function reconstruction, QCD sum rules, and hard-thermal-loop descriptions of quark-gluon plasma dynamics.

questions.question: What lattice real-time reconstruction strategy can decisively separate quarkonium melting caused by Debye screening from melting caused by the imaginary thermal width of the static potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from the MEM program for extracting spectral functions from Euclidean correlators [2] and the finding that the hot-QCD static potential acquires an imaginary part that broadens quarkonium peaks [5].

questions.question: How does the quark-mass and flavor dependence of the QCD pseudo-critical temperature propagate into heavy-quark potential screening and the survival pattern of quarkonium states?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the reported flavor dependence of T_c and dynamical-quark effects on heavy-quark screening [1], together with the use of the screened real-time potential for quarkonium melting [5].

questions.question: Can dimensional-reduction and HTL effective descriptions be matched to lattice spectral observables well enough to identify where weak-coupling collective-mode physics breaks down near the transition region?
questions.rationale: Dimensional reduction constructs finite-temperature effective theories by matching Green's functions [3], while HTL theory describes collective QGP excitations at the scale gT in the weak-coupling regime [4].

node_c2301a4c1457.summary: These papers develop HTL and weak-coupling effective descriptions of hot QCD thermodynamics, collective modes, screening, quasiparticles, and high-temperature pressure.

questions.question: Can the unknown order-g^6 constant and the nonperturbative g^2 T magnetic-scale contribution be determined with enough precision to make the high-temperature QCD pressure predictive at temperatures relevant to heavy-ion phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the separation of T, gT, and g^2T contributions in [3] and [5], and from the perturbative g^6 ln(1/g) pressure calculation in [2].

questions.question: How can hard-thermal-loop kinetic theory and resummed perturbation theory be extended to quantify damping, screening, and collective-mode observables beyond leading order while maintaining gauge covariance?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the gauge-covariant HTL effective theory for collective excitations in [1] and the resummed finite-temperature self-energy and damping-rate analysis in [4].

node_ccfcc4fadfa3.summary: This cluster examines the gauge structure, transport-theory derivations, higher-order refinements, and effective actions underlying hard thermal loops in hot gauge theories.

questions.question: Can the gauge-covariant kinetic-equation derivation of hard thermal loops be extended into a controlled hierarchy connecting gT collective modes to g^2 T ultrasoft non-Abelian dynamics?
questions.rationale: This follows from the HTL kinetic theory for gT collective excitations in [1,4] and the ultrasoft effective theory derived in [2].

questions.question: What is the minimal effective action that preserves gauge invariance, infrared finiteness, and correct unequal-time correlations for hot soft non-Abelian fields?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by [2], which derives a local Langevin theory for soft fields, and [3], which reviews unresolved effective-field-theory issues in perturbative thermal gauge theory.

questions.question: Can color conductivity and logarithmic enhancements of baryon-number-violation rates be computed in a way that removes residual ambiguities between classical lattice and effective-theory treatments?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2] and [5], which connect soft non-Abelian dynamics, color conductivity, and rates scaling with logarithmic factors.

node_20f49212c1c2.summary: These works apply hard-thermal-loop perturbation theory and self-consistent resummations to compute quark-gluon plasma pressure, entropy, energy density, and trace anomaly beyond leading order.

questions.question: Can HTL perturbation theory and dimensionally reduced effective theory be matched into a single thermodynamic description that controls the T, gT, and nonperturbative g^2 T contributions near phenomenological QCD temperatures?
questions.rationale: This follows from the scale-separation framework of [1] and [2] and the lattice-agreement window reported for three-loop HTLpt in [5].

questions.question: What is the minimal self-consistent resummation that reproduces LO and NLO entropy and density effects while avoiding unjustified use of HTL/HDL approximations outside their kinematic domain?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the approximately self-consistent entropy and density resummation proposed in [3].

questions.question: How do finite chemical potentials affect the convergence and uncertainty estimates of three-loop HTLpt predictions for susceptibilities, trace anomaly, and speed of sound?
questions.rationale: This derives from the finite-temperature and finite-chemical-potential three-loop HTLpt thermodynamic potential and observables computed in [5].

node_6f6bca069f15.summary: This cluster studies damping rates and lifetimes of fermions, photons, quarks, and gluons in hot or dense relativistic plasmas, emphasizing infrared effects and resummation.

questions.question: What is the gauge-theory analogue of a controlled resummed expansion that yields finite thermal quasiparticle damping rates while preserving the non-exponential long-time behavior caused by unscreened magnetostatic modes?
questions.rationale: Scalar thermal mass and damping can be obtained through a resummed expansion [1], whereas hot QED fermion lifetimes require Bloch-Nordsieck resummation and produce non-exponential damping from unscreened magnetic photons [2].

questions.question: How can perturbation theory, kinetic theory, and hydrodynamics be stitched into a quantitative real-time correlator that captures both quasiparticle damping at intermediate times and hydrodynamic power-law tails at late times?
questions.rationale: Effective-theory analyses of real-time plasma correlations show that perturbation theory, kinetic theory, linearized kinetic theory, and hydrodynamics control different time ranges, with nonlinear hydrodynamic modes generating late-time power laws [5].

node_bbecc7b97ace.summary: These papers compute the QCD equation of state in the deconfined phase using high-order perturbation theory, finite chemical potentials, large-flavor limits, and hard-thermal-loop resummation.

questions.question: Can the unknown perturbative and nonperturbative g^6 contributions to the hot-QCD pressure be fixed tightly enough to determine the temperature where the weak-coupling series becomes quantitatively reliable?
questions.rationale: The g^6 ln(1/g) calculation noted that applicability to surprisingly low temperatures depends on the unknown perturbative and nonperturbative g^6 terms [1].

questions.question: How far can finite-temperature and finite-chemical-potential dimensional-reduction predictions for quark-number susceptibilities be pushed before lattice agreement breaks down?
questions.rationale: The finite-T and finite-mu pressure calculation found excellent agreement with lattice simulations, especially for chemical-potential-dependent parts of the pressure [2].

questions.question: Do HTL-resummed soft-sector contributions remain well behaved for cold dense quark matter beyond the leading logarithmic NNNLO terms relevant to neutron-star-core equations of state?
questions.rationale: Cold-quark-matter studies used HTL methods to compute soft long-wavelength contributions and the alpha_s^3 ln^2 alpha_s leading logarithm, finding the new term small and the soft sector well behaved [4][5].

node_53b0709c512d.summary: This cluster studies charmonium and bottomonium correlators, spectral functions, and in-medium survival using lattice QCD, maximum entropy methods, potentials, and effective heavy-quark theories.

questions.question: To what extent can MEM or Bayesian extraction from finite-temperature correlators distinguish true survival of 1S quarkonium states from artifacts of limited temporal data, lattice spacing, and spectral priors?
questions.rationale: This derives from MEM methodology and finite-temperature lattice claims that J/psi, eta_c, and 1S quarkonium survive above deconfinement while temporal resolution is crucial [1], [3], [5].

questions.question: How can the imaginary part of the real-time static potential be connected quantitatively to lattice spectral widths and the observed melting hierarchy of charmonium and bottomonium channels?
questions.rationale: This follows from the HTL-derived complex static potential and lattice observations of different survival temperatures for 1S, 1P, scalar, and axial-vector states [2], [3], [4], [5].

node_4a7a042de28a.summary: These works focus on bottomonium and heavy-quark potentials in the quark-gluon plasma, combining lattice NRQCD, complex potentials, and spectral analyses to track screening and melting.

questions.question: Can lattice extractions of the complex heavy-quark potential determine the r and T dependence of the imaginary part with enough precision to predict bottomonium widths rather than only melting thresholds?
questions.rationale: The real-time HTL calculation and lattice Wilson-loop spectral analysis both find an imaginary potential component associated with thermal quarkonium width [1,2].

questions.question: How can potential-model spectral functions reconcile the apparent survival of bottomonium ground states with the strong suppression or dissolution of excited states across Tc to about 2Tc?
questions.rationale: Potential-model work finds most states dissolve below 1.5Tc except 1S bottomonium, while lattice NRQCD finds ground states survive and excited states are suppressed with temperature [4,5].

questions.question: What definition of the in-medium heavy-quark potential best connects Debye-screened lattice free energies, real-time EFT potentials, and measured quarkonium correlation functions?
questions.rationale: The quenched-QCD potential study finds Debye screening above Tc, while the survival study uses lattice free energies in potential models that reproduce correlators despite differing spectral conclusions [3,4].

node_33f98d520ec7.summary: This cluster examines whether charmonium states persist above deconfinement by reconstructing finite-temperature lattice correlators and spectral functions in quenched and two-flavor QCD.

questions.question: Can finite-temperature lattice charmonium spectral reconstructions determine whether J/psi and eta_c truly survive to about 1.6-2 Tc or whether the apparent survival is a MEM and temporal-resolution artifact?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the MEM-based survival claims and the explicit emphasis on sufficient temporal data points and cutoff control [1,3].

questions.question: What causes the spread between studies finding S-wave charmonium dissociation near 1.5 Tc, between 1.6 and 1.9 Tc, close to 2 Tc, or only gradually by 3 Tc?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the different dissociation temperatures reported across quenched, two-flavor, anisotropic, and fine-lattice charmonium studies [1,2,4,5].

questions.question: Can a combined analysis of S-wave survival, P-wave melting near Tc, and the charm diffusion coefficient provide one consistent picture of charm transport and charmonium binding in the deconfined plasma?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reported survival of S waves, early modification or melting of P waves, and Kubo-formula estimates of the charm diffusion coefficient [2,3,4,5].

node_6253a362f15d.summary: These papers develop and compare Bayesian, maximum-entropy, machine-learning, and smearing-based methods for extracting real-time spectral functions from Euclidean correlators.

questions.question: Can Bayesian, Tikhonov, and smearing-first reconstructions be benchmarked on common lattice correlators to identify which spectral features are data-driven and which are prior- or regulator-driven?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in MEM's Bayesian claims in [1], the modified Bayesian prior in [2], the smearing-function method in [4], and Tikhonov regularization in [5].

questions.question: What minimum Euclidean time resolution, statistical accuracy, and threshold information are required to reconstruct real-time quarkonium or gluon spectral densities with quantitatively reliable uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This derives from the data-point and accuracy requirements found using mock heavy-quark-potential correlators in [2] and the unknown-threshold issue emphasized in [5].

node_45034c80212e.summary: This cluster develops finite-temperature field-theory tools for analytic continuation, real-time contours, retarded correlators, cutting rules, and spectral functions.

questions.question: Can functional-renormalization-group analytic continuation with Baym-Mermin boundary conditions be made systematically improvable for QCD spectral functions at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from the FRG construction of finite-temperature and finite-density spectral functions using analytically continued external frequencies and Baym-Mermin boundary conditions in [2].

questions.question: How does the critical soft mode evolve from sigma-like scalar fluctuations to hydrodynamic density fluctuations in real-time correlators near the QCD critical line?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the Ginzburg-Landau and NJL analysis of sigma and hydrodynamic modes along the critical line in [3].

questions.question: What real-time simulation algorithm can include hard-thermal-loop physics while avoiding ultraviolet divergences in classical thermal evolutions of anomalous or baryon-number-violating processes?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the modified hard-thermal-loop Hamiltonian algorithm proposed to cure ultraviolet problems in classical real-time thermal simulations in [4].

node_a3b10a2d8997.summary: These works analyze the foundations and diagrammatics of real-time thermal field theory, including path contours, causal Green functions, gauge choices, and finite-temperature cutting rules.

questions.question: Can a single basis choice for real-time thermal n-point functions minimize diagrammatic complexity while preserving transparent relations to imaginary-time analytic continuations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison of Keldysh, retarded/advanced, and Feynman-like bases for real-time finite-temperature Feynman rules [4].

questions.question: How far can Cutkosky-like rules derived from imaginary-time diagrams replace direct real-time perturbation theory in practical computations of transport spectral densities?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the derivation of finite-temperature spectral-density rules that avoid real-time perturbation theory complications and their proposed use for transport coefficients [2].

node_71974ebf259a.summary: This cluster uses functional renormalization group and related finite-temperature approaches to compute bosonic and fermionic spectral functions, quasiparticle modes, and chiral-transition excitations.

questions.question: Can FRG truncations with Baym-Mermin analytic continuation reproduce the sigma-to-hydrodynamic soft-mode evolution expected along the finite-mass QCD critical line?
questions.rationale: This combines the thermodynamically consistent FRG spectral construction of [1] with the soft-mode interpolation between sigma-like and hydrodynamic modes in [2].

questions.question: What regulator choices allow direct real-time FRG calculations to preserve spacetime symmetries while retaining quantitatively stable spectral functions at finite temperature and density?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the real-time FRG regulator program in [4] and the finite-density spectral-function calculation demonstrated in [1].

questions.question: How should collective fermionic branches at large chemical potential be incorporated into nonperturbative thermal spectral calculations beyond quasiparticle approximations?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the explicit construction of two collective fermionic excitation branches in [5] and the nonperturbative real-time methods discussed in [1] and [4].

node_a2f4b22b8c5c.summary: These papers study QED effective actions, photon self-energies, thermal running couplings, and electromagnetic properties of plasmas across low- and high-temperature regimes.

questions.question: Can finite-temperature QED effective actions be formulated so that electric and magnetic weak-field couplings, Debye screening, and gauge restrictions in imaginary time are treated within one consistent renormalization prescription?
questions.rationale: Real-time calculations find different high-temperature behavior for electric and magnetic effective couplings [4], while imaginary-time work identifies an additional gauge-invariant quantity related to chemical potential and Debye screening [5].

questions.question: At low temperature, why do thermally excited internal photons make the two-loop QED effective action dominate the one-loop thermal correction, and how does this affect light propagation, photon splitting, and pair production?
questions.rationale: The two-loop finite-temperature QED effective action was found to exceed the one-loop contribution at T much smaller than the electron mass and to induce effects in light propagation, photon splitting, and electric-field pair production [2].

node_789cd5baff19.summary: This cluster investigates electric, magnetic, Polyakov-loop, gluon, and mesonic screening masses in hot QCD using lattice simulations, perturbation theory, and hard-thermal-loop methods.

questions.question: How do dynamical quark masses and the number of light flavors quantitatively shift electric screening, the heavy-quark free energy, and the pseudo-critical temperature near the QCD transition?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the quark-mass and flavor dependence of Tc and heavy-quark-potential screening analyzed in [1].

questions.question: Can dimensionally reduced three-dimensional effective theories reproduce lattice electric and magnetic screening masses across the temperature range where perturbation theory begins to fail?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the Green-function matching rules for high-temperature dimensional reduction in [2] and the scale sensitivity of high-temperature pure-gauge thermodynamics in [5].

questions.question: What renormalization prescription for Polyakov-loop and color-singlet free energies best connects short-distance zero-temperature potentials to continuum finite-temperature screening observables?
questions.rationale: This derives from the renormalized heavy-quark free-energy and Polyakov-loop construction in [4] and the finite-temperature running-coupling analysis in [3].

node_6cc3769380fc.summary: These works analyze chromoelectric and chromomagnetic screening in high-temperature non-Abelian gauge theories, emphasizing Debye masses, dimensional reduction, and nonperturbative magnetic effects.

questions.question: Can the gauge-invariant nonperturbative definition of the Debye mass be matched quantitatively to dimensionally reduced effective theories across the temperature range where O(g^2) corrections are large?
questions.rationale: Dimensional reduction provides the effective-theory matching framework [1], while lattice studies using a gauge-invariant Debye mass find large O(g^2) corrections [5].

questions.question: How should the logarithmic sensitivity of the NLO non-Abelian Debye mass to magnetic screening be incorporated into a controlled hierarchy of chromoelectric and chromomagnetic correlation lengths?
questions.rationale: The NLO Debye mass is logarithmically sensitive to the nonperturbative magnetic mass [2], and the nonperturbative lattice result modifies the standard power-counting hierarchy [5].

questions.question: Do multiscalar theories such as the MSSM, 2HDM, and NMSSM preserve the same universal reduced-theory structure for screening observables once successive heavy modes are integrated out?
questions.rationale: The generic and electroweak dimensional-reduction rules [1] are extended to MSSM, 2HDM, and NMSSM multiscalar models with staged integration of massive particles [4].

node_4555fcc0e076.summary: This cluster focuses on lattice and perturbative calculations of light, strange, and charmonium meson screening masses across the QCD crossover and high-temperature regimes.

questions.question: Can continuum-extrapolated meson screening masses in 2+1-flavor QCD quantify the temperature at which chiral, axial, and other symmetry-restoration patterns become effectively indistinguishable in light and strange channels?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the HISQ continuum-extrapolated screening-mass study and its discussion of symmetry restoration in the high-temperature phase [4].

questions.question: How do light-quark mass, strange-quark mass, and flavor number shift the screening spectrum and pseudo-critical temperature from the crossover region to the approach toward the perturbative limit?
questions.rationale: The question follows from studies of quark-mass and flavor dependence of the QCD transition and 2+1-flavor screening masses over broad temperature ranges [1,4,5].

questions.question: Can effective-theory and three-dimensional lattice calculations of static correlation lengths at finite chemical potential be matched quantitatively to thermal meson screening channels at T greater than about 2 Tc?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the perturbative effective-theory determination of high-temperature static correlation lengths at finite density and the lattice meson screening calculations [3,4,5].

node_345d9a6b948e.summary: These papers study static heavy quark-antiquark free energies, screening, entropy, and renormalized Polyakov loops in finite-temperature QCD and related gauge theories.

questions.question: What is the most reliable gauge-invariant relation between static singlet free energies, renormalized Polyakov loops, and the in-medium heavy-quark potential relevant for quarkonium binding near T_c?
questions.rationale: Static singlet and color-averaged free energies are renormalized using the zero-temperature potential in [2], while [1] connects their temperature dependence to quarkonium binding and screening scales.

questions.question: How should one separate remnants of the confining force from genuinely Coulombic nonperturbative interactions when defining a finite-temperature running coupling from static quark-antiquark free energies?
questions.rationale: The quenched analysis argues that near T_c the plasma is better characterized by remnants of confinement than by a strong Coulombic force, and notes ambiguities in coupling definitions beyond perturbation theory [5].

node_dfaa4c2a33e8.summary: This cluster applies finite-temperature QCD sum rules to mesons and quarkonia, extracting masses, decay constants, widths, spectral changes, and chiral-restoration constraints.

questions.question: Can finite-temperature Weinberg and QCD sum rules determine whether rho-meson melting alone is compatible with chiral restoration, or is a constrained in-medium axial-vector spectral function required?
questions.rationale: The rho-melting study tests in-medium vector spectral functions against QCD and Weinberg sum rules while modeling the poorly known axial-vector channel [2].

questions.question: How should transverse and longitudinal finite-temperature spectral densities at nonzero momentum be constrained jointly by OPE condensates, lattice inputs, and functional-renormalization-group spectral functions?
questions.rationale: Finite-temperature Weinberg sum rules involve transverse and longitudinal spectral densities at each momentum, while FRG calculations provide momentum-dependent rho and a1 spectral functions [1], [3].

questions.question: Where does the OPE-based charmonium sum-rule description lose predictive power near Tc, and can lattice gluon-condensate inputs stabilize mass-width extractions above the reported breakdown temperatures?
questions.rationale: The charmonium QCD sum-rule analysis finds rapid spectral changes near Tc but reports loss of OPE stability above about 1.04-1.06 Tc [4].

node_32d57515f6b1.summary: These works use NJL, PNJL, and related effective models to map chiral restoration, deconfinement, pion condensation, and dense-matter phases across temperature and chemical potential.

questions.question: What observable would most decisively show whether NJL, PNJL, or PQM models capture the same chiral-restoration and deconfinement physics as finite-density lattice QCD?
questions.rationale: The question follows from comparisons of PNJL thermodynamics with lattice pressure and quark-number density [3] and from PQM studies of chiral and Polyakov-loop behavior at finite chemical potential [5].

questions.question: Can a Polyakov-loop effective potential with explicit chemical-potential and N_f dependence lock the chiral and deconfinement crossovers without overfitting pure-gauge input?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed mechanism for simultaneous chiral and deconfinement crossovers [2] and the RG-motivated N_f- and chemical-potential-dependent Polyakov potential in the PQM model [5].

questions.question: Is the smooth hadron-to-quark continuity found at finite isospin density reproducible in chiral effective phase models across temperature, isospin chemical potential, and baryon chemical potential?
questions.rationale: The finite-isospin analysis finds a pion-condensed low-density phase, high-density Cooper pairing with the same quantum numbers, and a conjectured smooth transition [4], while NJL-type models are used to map finite-temperature and finite-density QCD phases [1].

node_32d57515f6b1_1.summary: This cluster focuses on Polyakov-loop-extended NJL models of two- and three-flavor QCD phase structure, comparing chiral and deconfinement transitions with lattice constraints.

questions.question: Can lattice thermodynamics at finite chemical potential fix the Polyakov-loop effective potential, including prescription, N_f, and chemical-potential dependence, well enough for PNJL and PQM models to make stable predictions for the equation of state and quark number density?
questions.rationale: This derives from comparisons of PNJL/PQM thermodynamics with lattice data and from proposed modifications of the Polyakov-loop potential [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: What dynamical condition actually locks the chiral and deconfinement crossovers: a finite condensate at vanishing Polyakov loop, quark coupling to the temporal gauge background, or additional model constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed mechanism for simultaneous crossovers and the need for further constraints to achieve perfect locking [1], [2].

questions.question: How do effective U_A(1) restoration, induced vector-channel interactions, diquark degrees of freedom, and quark-mass variation move the QCD critical point in PNJL phase diagrams?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in PNJL studies of diquarks, Polyakov-loop dynamics, quark masses, U_A(1) restoration, and vector interactions near the critical point [4], [5].

node_32d57515f6b1_2.summary: These papers use PNJL models at real and imaginary chemical potential to study Roberge-Weiss periodicity, extended Z3 symmetry, and the QCD phase diagram.

questions.question: Can PNJL models constrained at imaginary chemical potential and by Roberge-Weiss or extended Z3 symmetry predict the real-mu critical point without prescription dependence in the Polyakov-loop potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from PNJL comparisons to lattice thermodynamics, the documented prescription dependence of the Polyakov-loop effective potential, and the central role of Z3 Polyakov-loop phases [1], [3], [4].

questions.question: How do diquark degrees of freedom, vector-channel interactions, and effective U_A(1) restoration jointly shift the PNJL phase diagram and critical point?
questions.rationale: This derives from PNJL studies adding explicit diquarks and examining how U_A(1) restoration and induced vector interactions affect the critical point [2], [3].

questions.question: Are high-order Taylor coefficients, susceptibilities, and speed of sound in PNJL models sufficient to match lattice QCD thermodynamics beyond small chemical potential?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by PNJL calculations of pressure coefficients up to eighth order and derived thermodynamic quantities compared with lattice estimates [5].

node_32d57515f6b1_3.summary: This cluster examines how Polyakov-loop dynamics in NJL-type models couples deconfinement to chiral restoration in finite-temperature and finite-density QCD.

questions.question: How uniquely can lattice thermodynamics at finite chemical potential fix the Polyakov-loop effective potential used in PNJL models once pressure, quark density, and chiral condensate data are all imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison of PNJL thermodynamics with lattice QCD using a Polyakov potential fixed in the pure-gauge sector [1].

questions.question: How sensitive are PNJL critical-point predictions to the prescription for the Polyakov-loop potential, effective UA(1) restoration, and induced vector-channel interactions at finite density?
questions.rationale: This derives from three-flavor PNJL studies emphasizing prescription dependence, UA(1) restoration, and vector-channel effects on the QCD critical point [3].

questions.question: Can PNJL Taylor coefficients through eighth order, the speed of sound, and the conformal measure provide a quantitative test of deconfinement-chiral coupling beyond fitting transition temperatures?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in PNJL calculations of pressure expansion coefficients, specific heat, speed of sound, and conformal measure compared with lattice estimates [5].

node_bbbae2b0cb43.summary: These works emphasize imaginary chemical potentials, Z3 symmetry, Roberge-Weiss structure, confinement mechanisms, and quarkyonic matter within PNJL-based phase diagrams.

questions.question: Can an entangled PNJL or nonlocal Polyakov-loop potential simultaneously reproduce Roberge-Weiss periodicity and endpoint mass dependence at imaginary chemical potential while retaining the mu-dependent deconfinement scale needed for quarkyonic thermodynamics at real chemical potential?
questions.rationale: This combines the mu-dependent Polyakov-scale issue in quarkyonic PNJL phase diagrams with the EPNJL fit to lattice Roberge-Weiss endpoint behavior [2][4].

questions.question: What Polyakov-loop-dependent four-quark vertex is required for chiral-deconfinement entanglement to match lattice magnetic-field condensate splitting while preserving the Z3 phase dependence of chiral restoration?
questions.rationale: The Z3 dependence of the chiral condensate and the magnetic-field comparison of PNJL versus EPNJL motivate a concrete test of the entanglement interaction [1][5].

questions.question: How do the predicted critical endpoint and tricritical point move when Roberge-Weiss constraints, entanglement interactions, and Z3-neutral quarkyonic contributions are imposed in the same PNJL framework?
questions.rationale: The location of the critical endpoint and tricritical point is explicitly tied to quarkyonic matter, large-Nc behavior, and EPNJL entanglement effects [2][3][4].

node_89a7032a8d7f.summary: This cluster develops local and nonlocal PNJL thermodynamics, including running couplings, wave-function renormalization, axial anomaly effects, and lattice-motivated phase behavior.

questions.question: Can nonlocal or generalized PNJL parameterizations fit lattice pressure, quark-number susceptibilities through eighth order, and the strange-quark susceptibility inflection point with a single Polyakov-loop potential fixed from the pure-gauge sector?
questions.rationale: The PNJL thermodynamics program fixes the Polyakov potential from pure gauge data and compares pressure, density, Taylor coefficients, and strange susceptibility with lattice QCD [1][4][5].

questions.question: How do explicit diquark degrees of freedom, effective U_A(1) restoration, and induced vector-channel interactions shift or remove the QCD critical point in two- and 2+1-flavor PNJL phase diagrams?
questions.rationale: The two-flavor PNJL model studies diquarks and critical-point dependence, while the three-flavor PNJL analysis focuses on U_A(1) restoration and vector interactions at finite density [2][3].

questions.question: What model-independent constraints on the Polyakov-loop effective potential follow from requiring consistency among the equation of state, pressure differences, speed of sound, and conformal measure at finite chemical potential?
questions.rationale: The representative thermodynamics studies compare PNJL equation-of-state observables and higher Taylor coefficients with lattice QCD at finite chemical potential [1][4].

node_de63b7d1faf3.summary: These papers investigate the QCD critical endpoint and nearby critical behavior in NJL and PNJL models, including vector interactions, axial anomaly effects, and spinodal physics.

questions.question: What lattice-constrained range of isoscalar vector coupling in NJL or PNJL models eliminates the critical endpoint, and how does that range shift when axial-anomaly and eight-quark interactions are included consistently?
questions.rationale: Vector interactions can remove the first-order transition and CEP, while axial-anomaly and sigma-four or vector interactions move the CEP in opposite directions [2], [3], [5].

questions.question: How does the Lifshitz point of one-dimensional inhomogeneous chiral phases remain stable or move under Polyakov-loop dynamics and repulsive vector interactions compared with the homogeneous chiral transition line?
questions.rationale: The inhomogeneous-phase study finds that the Polyakov loop gives quantitative changes while vector interactions qualitatively weaken homogeneous first-order transitions but less strongly affect inhomogeneous domains [1].

questions.question: Can quark-number, isovector, and off-diagonal flavor susceptibilities provide a model-independent discriminator between a true CEP and a vector-weakened crossover in effective QCD phase diagrams?
questions.rationale: NJL studies compare quark flavor susceptibilities at finite chemical potential with lattice results and examine their dependence on vector couplings and quark masses [4], [5].

node_8157f2cc2faa.summary: This cluster studies PQM and quark-meson models of QCD thermodynamics, highlighting mesonic and fermionic fluctuations, functional renormalization group treatments, and phase-boundary shifts.

questions.question: What dynamical constraint is still missing for perfect locking of chiral restoration and deconfinement crossovers in Polyakov-loop-extended chiral models?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] proposes a mechanism for simultaneous crossovers but states that further constraints are needed for perfect locking.

questions.question: How much do mesonic and fermionic fluctuations, including matter backreaction on the Yang-Mills sector, shift the PQM critical endpoint relative to mean-field predictions?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] goes beyond mean field by including matter fluctuations and backreaction, while [2] presents the phase structure from minimizing the PQM thermodynamic potential.

questions.question: Can susceptibilities of approximate order parameters discriminate Polyakov cooling and triality conservation effects from ordinary constituent-quark mass suppression in finite-temperature chiral observables?
questions.rationale: Papers [3] and [5] discuss order-parameter fluctuations, susceptibilities, triality conservation, and Polyakov-loop suppression of thermal effects.

node_3b5fd82a83c3.summary: These works analyze mesonic correlations, pseudoscalar and scalar meson properties, and quark-hadron phase transitions in hot or dense NJL and PNJL matter.

questions.question: Can PNJL calculations with mesonic ring correlations reproduce both the pion-dominated pressure below the transition and the merging of pion and sigma spectral functions at chiral restoration in one consistent finite-temperature framework?
questions.rationale: Mesonic correlations dominate the pressure below T_c [2], while PNJL-RPA correlators predict pion-sigma spectral merging when chiral symmetry is restored [1].

questions.question: How should the Beth-Uhlenbeck phase-shift treatment of Mott dissociation be extended to quantify meson-diquark mixing in the 2SC phase at finite temperature and chemical potential?
questions.rationale: The generalized Beth-Uhlenbeck approach frames bound-state dissociation through in-medium phase shifts and highlights scalar meson-diquark mixing in the 2SC phase [4].

questions.question: Which pseudoscalar-meson observables most cleanly separate U_A(1) restoration effects from changes induced by strangeness content and beta equilibrium in dense matter?
questions.rationale: Three-flavor NJL studies find eta, eta prime, kaon, and pion behavior changes with density, strangeness content, and the 't Hooft U_A(1)-breaking interaction [3],[5].

node_1d2723427361.summary: This cluster uses linear and nonlinear sigma models plus chiral perturbation theory to study finite-temperature chiral symmetry restoration and pion dynamics.

questions.question: How sensitive are the critical end point and chiral critical surface in three-flavor linear sigma models to the sigma mass, axial anomaly strength, and strange-condensate dynamics?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which studies the sigma-mass dependence, axial anomaly, nonstrange and strange condensates, and the critical surface in hot and dense QCD matter.

questions.question: Can finite-temperature pion observables reconcile the linear and nonlinear sigma-model descriptions of chiral restoration beyond the approximations where their critical temperatures and field-redefinition-independent quantities agree?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [5], which compares linear and nonlinear O(N) sigma models, and [2], which derives finite-temperature pion velocity and static versus dynamic pion masses.

questions.question: How does finite isospin chemical potential shift pion condensation and pion decay constants at nonzero temperature, and can those shifts be embedded consistently in Polyakov linear sigma-model phase diagrams?
questions.rationale: This derives from the thermal and isospin-density pion corrections in [3] and the PLSM finite-temperature and density phase structure in [4].

node_412c4bbdf5a9.summary: These papers study pion masses, decay constants, dispersion relations, and chiral Ward identities in finite-temperature chiral effective theories such as the linear sigma model and ChPT.

questions.question: Can lattice-determined static correlators pin down the real-time soft-pion dispersion relation, including pion velocity, pole mass, screening mass, decay constant, and axial isospin susceptibility, near the chiral transition?
questions.rationale: Real-time pion propagation is argued to be expressible entirely through static correlators [3], with critical behavior predicting decreasing pion velocity and pole mass near T_c [4].

questions.question: How do finite isospin chemical potential and finite temperature jointly shift the charged-pion condensation threshold away from mu_I = ±m_pi?
questions.rationale: Thermal ChPT finds that the zero-temperature charged-pion condensation condition is modified once temperature and isospin chemical potential are both present [2].

questions.question: What is the precise finite-temperature form of GMOR when Lorentz symmetry breaking separates static and dynamic pion masses and decay constants?
questions.rationale: Finite-temperature pion studies derive distinct static and dynamic mass relations [1] and examine the validity and meaning of GMOR at finite temperature [3,5].

node_cf0418a097c0.summary: These works use linear sigma, quark-meson, and Polyakov-extended models to map chiral symmetry restoration and critical behavior at finite temperature and density.

questions.question: How robust is the predicted critical endpoint location in three-flavor linear sigma and Polyakov linear sigma models once sigma-mass choices, axial-anomaly strength, vector and axial-vector mesons, and fermionic vacuum fluctuations are varied within phenomenologically fitted ranges?
questions.rationale: The CEP sensitivity to sigma mass and anomaly effects is emphasized in [1], while [5] shows that vector mesons and vacuum fluctuations can alter the same phase-structure question.

questions.question: Can the apparently independent light-quark chiral restoration, strange-quark chiral restoration, and deconfinement transitions in the PLSM be tied to model-independent observables that survive beyond mean-field treatment?
questions.rationale: The independence of the three transitions and quarkyonic phases is a central result of [2], while [3] highlights how treatment of fluctuations and field definitions affects chiral observables.

node_df2714b7c8ca.summary: This cluster centers on NJL-type effective descriptions of low-energy QCD, including dynamical chiral symmetry breaking, meson spectra, phase diagrams, regularization choices, and loop corrections.

questions.question: Which NJL extensions can simultaneously reproduce O(p^4) chiral low-energy constants, short-distance QCD constraints, and realistic scalar, vector, and axial-vector spectra without overfitting regulator-dependent parameters?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in ENJL derivations of the O(p^4) effective action and their links to chiral Lagrangians, VMD, and short-distance relations [2],[3].

questions.question: Is an infrared cutoff, nonlocal form factor, or another confinement-motivated prescription the least ambiguous way to remove unphysical q-anti-q thresholds while preserving pion chiral relations and heavy-meson phenomenology?
questions.rationale: The question combines the two-cutoff extended NJL treatment of light and heavy mesons with nonlocal NJL models that preserve GMOR and exhibit confinement-like behavior [4],[5].

questions.question: How can the axial anomaly and current-quark mass effects be incorporated in NJL phenomenology so that flavor mixing, OZI violation, and finite-temperature or finite-density phase behavior are constrained by the same parameter set?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review's emphasis on the interplay between axial anomaly, quark masses, hadron contents, and applications at finite T and density [1].

node_88a12027f83f.summary: These papers derive, review, and test NJL-like models as low-energy limits of QCD, including lattice formulations and finite-temperature chiral behavior.

questions.question: What observable would most sharply test whether NJL-like models are reliable low-energy limits of QCD rather than phenomenological parametrizations of chiral symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This broad foundational question follows from the QCD low-energy effective-action derivation in [2] and the NJL phenomenology review in [1].

questions.question: Can a nonlocal NJL extension simultaneously reproduce meson spectra, radial excitations, Gell-Mann-Oakes-Renner pion properties, and quark-confinement-like behavior without losing the successful local-model description of ground-state nonets?
questions.rationale: This combines the need for nonlocality in radial excitations and confinement stated in [5] with the nonlocal covariant NJL construction and GMOR result in [4].

questions.question: How should the axial anomaly, current-quark masses, and vector-meson-dominance constraints be implemented so that the order-p4 chiral action and flavor anomaly remain consistent across NJL-like regularizations?
questions.rationale: The issue is grounded in the anomaly and quark-mass interplay emphasized in [1] and the heat-kernel and flavor-anomaly prescription discussed in [3].

node_1467af4a013f.summary: These studies analyze how cutoff, dimensional, thermal, and magnetic-field regularization prescriptions affect NJL model parameters, meson properties, condensates, and phase structure.

questions.question: Can one define a regulator-independent diagnostic for which NJL predictions for meson thresholds, condensates, and finite-temperature chiral melting are artifacts of ultraviolet, infrared, mesonic, or light-cone cutoffs?
questions.rationale: This follows from the threshold removal by an infrared cutoff in [1], the regulator-dependent sign of 1/Nc corrections in [3], and the light-cone cutoff comparisons in [5].

questions.question: How stable is the identification of the critical-end-point soft mode as scalar density fluctuation once next-to-leading 1/Nc meson-loop effects are included with different regularization prescriptions?
questions.rationale: The scalar-density soft mode in [2] should be tested against the substantial symmetry-preserving meson-loop corrections described in [4] and the beyond-mean-field regularization effects in [3].

questions.question: Is there a matching prescription between local, nonlocal, and light-cone NJL formulations that preserves Goldstone, Goldberger-Treiman, and GMOR relations while giving consistent pion structure functions?
questions.rationale: This question links the symmetry-preserving next-to-leading treatment in [4] with the nonlocal beyond-mean-field refit in [3] and the light-cone pion-structure calculation in [5].

node_2312eb7a3009.summary: This cluster examines pion condensation and superfluid phases in QCD and NJL models under isospin, baryon, and charge-neutrality constraints.

questions.question: Is the hadron-to-quark crossover at finite isospin density truly smooth once lattice simulations connect the pion-condensed BEC regime to the high-density BCS paired regime at nonzero temperature?
questions.rationale: This follows from the conjectured smooth transition between pion condensation and quark-antiquark Cooper pairing and from lattice evidence connecting deconfinement to the BEC-BCS crossover [1],[3],[4].

questions.question: How does the vanishing explicit isospin-breaking extrapolation affect the inferred boundary of the pion-condensed phase and the claim that pion condensation disappears above about 160 MeV?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in continuum-extrapolated lattice simulations that use a small explicit breaking parameter and a singular-value improvement program to reach the zero-breaking limit [4].

questions.question: Can NJL and lattice descriptions agree on whether flavor-mixing instanton interactions merge or split chiral, deconfinement, and pion-superfluid transitions in the mu_B-T plane at fixed isospin chemical potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from NJL studies of pion superfluidity and from the finding that flavor-mixing interactions can remove the two-transition structure [2],[5].

node_c450c004fd96.summary: These works study QCD at nonzero isospin chemical potential using chiral perturbation theory, lattice methods, and sigma models to characterize charged-pion Bose condensation.

questions.question: Is the conjectured smooth continuity between the low-mu_I pion-condensed superfluid and the high-mu_I quark-antiquark paired Fermi liquid quantitatively preserved in continuum-extrapolated lattice QCD across the BEC-BCS crossover?
questions.rationale: This directly extends the pion-condensate to Cooper-pairing continuity conjecture and the lattice indication that deconfinement connects to the BEC-BCS crossover [1],[3].

questions.question: How sharply can the pion-condensation boundary near T approximately 160 MeV be defined after extrapolating the explicit isospin-breaking source to zero using Dirac singular-value methods?
questions.rationale: This is based on the continuum staggered-quark study that used a small explicit breaking parameter and singular-value improvement to locate the normal-to-pion-condensed phase boundary [3].

questions.question: How are the pion and kaon superfluid phases reorganized when small independent light-quark chemical potentials, baryon density, and finite quark masses are included in a single effective description?
questions.rationale: This combines the symmetry-based EFT phase structure with pion and kaon superfluids and the strong-coupling lattice treatment of finite baryon and isospin density [4],[5].

node_2e03c9111f8c.summary: These papers focus on charged pion condensation in NJL-type dense quark matter, emphasizing neutrality, chiral imbalance, dualities, inhomogeneity, and finite-temperature phase structure.

questions.question: Which ingredient determines whether finite isospin chemical potential produces one or two chiral phase transitions in the muB-T plane: explicit flavor mixing, neutrality, or mesonic fluctuations?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] finds two first-order transitions and two endpoints at small isospin chemical potential, while [3] shows that flavor-mixing interactions can remove the two-transition structure.

questions.question: Under what model-independent conditions does the pion-condensation threshold remain exactly at the vacuum pion mass when baryon density, temperature, and neutrality constraints are included?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] finds the critical isospin chemical potential equals the vacuum pion mass in mean-field NJL, while [5] shows neutrality can allow or forbid pion condensation depending on parameters.

questions.question: Can the Goldstone mode formed from sigma and charged-pion mixing in the pion-superfluid phase be connected to observable equation-of-state changes in dense isospin-asymmetric matter?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] identifies a mixed sigma-charged-pion Goldstone mode and computes meson spectra and the equation of state in the pion-superfluid phase.

node_66f65be7e9d0.summary: This cluster investigates Gross-Neveu and chiral NJL models with finite temperature, density, and flavor number, especially spatially modulated condensates and crystalline phases.

questions.question: What single calculation would settle whether the first-order chiral transition line in QCD-like phase diagrams is generically replaced by an inhomogeneous phase?
questions.rationale: This broad question derives from the replacement of the homogeneous first-order line by an inhomogeneous phase in NJL and quark-meson models in [2].

questions.question: Which modulation geometry is thermodynamically preferred near the chiral critical point: one-dimensional kink crystals, chiral spirals, or higher-dimensional condensate lattices?
questions.rationale: This follows from the open issue of modulation shape and dimensionality in [1], the chiral spiral in [3], and possible domain-wall-soliton lattices in [4].

questions.question: Can the exactly solved large-N Gross-Neveu phase diagram serve as a quantitative benchmark for algorithms intended to find inhomogeneous phases in higher-dimensional QCD effective models?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the use of the complete 1+1-dimensional Gross-Neveu phase diagram as a testing ground for algorithms and theoretical ideas in [5].

node_9c682862f509.summary: These papers use lattice QCD with domain-wall or overlap fermions to test axial U(1) anomaly effects and possible effective restoration near and above the chiral transition.

questions.question: In the thermodynamic and chiral limits, does the near-zero Dirac eigenvalue density vanish strongly enough above T_c to make U(1)_A invisible in scalar and pseudoscalar susceptibilities?
questions.rationale: Overlap-fermion constraints on the eigenvalue density and its derivatives imply invisibility of U(1)_A breaking in susceptibilities in [5].

questions.question: Can domain-wall and overlap simulations with physical light quark masses reconcile meson-correlator evidence for U(1)_A restoration with possible anomaly effects at the chiral transition?
questions.rationale: Domain-wall finite-temperature studies in [1] and overlap correlator studies in [4] directly test effective U(1)_A restoration near T_c.

questions.question: If U(1)_A is effectively restored at T_c, what lattice observables can determine whether the two-flavor chiral transition lies inside the stable U(2)_L x U(2)_R fixed-point attraction domain?
questions.rationale: A stable RG fixed point for the U(2)_L x U(2)_R to U(2)_V scenario is found in [2].

node_9c682862f509_1.summary: This cluster studies whether axial U(1) symmetry is effectively restored in high-temperature two-flavor QCD through Dirac eigenvalue spectra, susceptibilities, and chiral lattice fermions.

questions.question: Is U(1)A effectively restored at the two-flavor chiral transition in the thermodynamic and chiral limits, or do low-lying Dirac modes preserve anomaly effects that finite-volume simulations underresolve?
questions.rationale: This question follows from domain-wall and overlap studies of U(1)A restoration through susceptibilities and low-lying Dirac spectra near Tc [1,3,5].

questions.question: Can lattice calculations verify the predicted vanishing of the Dirac eigenvalue density at the origin and its first two derivatives while controlling ultraviolet divergences and Ginsparg-Wilson relation violations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the overlap-operator constraint analysis and the Mobius domain-wall finding that Ginsparg-Wilson violations can dominate apparent U(1)A-breaking signals [4,5].

questions.question: If U(1)A breaking is effectively suppressed at Tc, does the two-flavor chiral transition follow the U(2)L x U(2)R to U(2)V fixed-point scenario, and what bare quartic parameters place QCD in its attraction domain?
questions.rationale: This follows from the high-order RG study of the three-dimensional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson theory with restored U(1)A symmetry and a stable fixed point [2].

node_bd7d4b2376e3.summary: These works examine how the axial U(1) anomaly and topological susceptibility affect chiral restoration, scalar-pseudoscalar meson spectra, and QCD phase transitions at finite temperature or density.

questions.question: What lattice observable set can decisively determine whether U(1)_A symmetry is effectively restored at the SU(2)_A chiral crossover temperature?
questions.rationale: The core unresolved issue is whether U(1)_A is restored at T_c, with screening spectra giving evidence for SU(2)_A restoration but not axial restoration [1][3].

questions.question: How sensitive are eta and eta-prime chiral-partner assignments to fluctuation-induced modifications of quark-meson correlations in the presence of a temperature-dependent U(1)_A anomaly?
questions.rationale: Functional RG work finds the pseudoscalar eta, eta-prime flavor composition to be drastically sensitive to fluctuation-induced effects when the axial anomaly is present [5].

node_1c9c935e9772.summary: This cluster centers on lattice studies of finite-temperature phase transitions, especially deconfinement in SU(N) Yang-Mills and related electroweak or gauge-Higgs systems, extracting critical behavior and thermodynamics.

questions.question: What continuum-extrapolated lattice observables most sharply determine whether finite-temperature SU(N) gauge theories undergo first-order, second-order, or crossover behavior as the gauge group and matter content vary?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the SU(3) thermodynamic continuum extrapolation and critical-temperature extraction in [1] and the SU(2)-Higgs endpoint studies in [2,3].

questions.question: Can effective theories of thermal Wilson lines predict the order and dominant correlation length of deconfinement transitions quantitatively enough to replace purely numerical classification?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal that SU(N) Wilson-line behavior governs Z(N) deconfinement transitions and correlation-length growth near finite-temperature transitions [4].

questions.question: How reliably can Landau-gauge ghost and gluon propagators, through functional-RG order-parameter potentials, reproduce lattice critical temperatures and transition orders for SU(2), SU(3), and theories with dynamical matter?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the confinement criterion based on ghost/gluon infrared behavior and functional-RG prediction of SU(2) and SU(3) deconfinement properties [5].

node_9310bcebfc9b.summary: These papers analyze deconfinement transitions in SU(N) lattice Yang-Mills theories across N, determining transition order, latent heat, continuum scaling, and Polyakov-loop effective descriptions.
