questions.question: Can relaxion models raise the technically natural cutoff beyond 10^8 GeV without introducing new fine tuning, anthropic selection, or uncontrolled inflation-sector assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the cutoff limitation and early-universe scanning mechanism in the original cosmological relaxation proposal [1].

questions.question: Does renormalization-group running of vacuum and gravitational terms in curved-space Standard Model calculations lead to observable cosmological effects without spoiling primordial nucleosynthesis?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [2], which computes Standard Model contributions to running cosmological and gravitational constants and tests nucleosynthesis constraints.

questions.question: Can any global modification such as sequestering evade Weinberg-type no-go arguments while remaining compatible with low-energy effective field theory and string-theory expectations?
questions.rationale: This combines the no-go and sequestering discussion in [3] with the string-theory view that the cosmological constant obstructs realistic low-energy models in [5].

node_378803a7200c.summary: These papers propose mechanisms such as scale invariance, string-theory vacua, quantum gravity suppression, nonlocal constraints, renormalization running, and quantum discharge to explain the small cosmological constant.

questions.question: What empirical or theoretical criterion could decide whether the cosmological constant problem should be addressed by running vacuum terms, global constraints such as sequestering, string vacua, or abandoning radiative stability as a guide?
questions.rationale: This broad question reflects the surveyed alternatives and the emphasis that radiative instability and Weinberg's no-go theorem make local microphysical solutions difficult [2][3][5].

questions.question: Can renormalization-group running of the cosmological and gravitational constants be formulated in a way that is simultaneously compatible with Standard Model thresholds, curved-space QFT, and primordial nucleosynthesis constraints?
questions.rationale: This derives from calculations of Standard Model particle contributions to running vacuum and gravitational terms and their possible impact on primordial nucleosynthesis [1].

questions.question: If Standard Model symmetry breaking induces a large vacuum term that is cancelled only in the far infrared, what observable new light degrees of freedom or forces are unavoidable near the scale where the cancellation fails?
questions.rationale: This follows from the argument that running Higgs parameters and the vacuum term can generate a nonzero observable cosmological constant near an electron-neutrino-mass scale, suggesting new forces or light degrees of freedom [4].

node_023615ac83fc.summary: This cluster focuses on the cosmological constant problem and surveys or develops symmetry-based, nonlocal, quantum-gravity, and modified-geometry approaches to reducing gravitational vacuum energy.

questions.question: Can any vacuum-energy suppression mechanism evade radiative instability without effectively introducing a global modification of gravity or repeated retuning across effective field theory thresholds?
questions.rationale: Paper [2] emphasizes radiative instability, Weinberg's no-go theorem, and the appeal of global modifications such as sequestering.

questions.question: Do renormalization-group running G(mu) and Lambda(mu) models produce observable cosmological evolution while remaining consistent with primordial nucleosynthesis and low-energy gravitational constraints?
questions.rationale: Papers [1] and [4] compute running cosmological and gravitational constants and assess cosmological implications including nucleosynthesis.

questions.question: Can the quantum break-time of de Sitter space be connected to a concrete suppression or relaxation of vacuum energy rather than only to the limits of classical mean-field evolution?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] formulates de Sitter as a graviton coherent state and derives a quantum break-time for departure from classical evolution.

node_b418abdd397f.summary: These works examine small cosmological constants in scale-invariant, string, and supergravity models, often invoking degenerate vacua, radiative constraints, or the multiple point principle.

questions.question: Can any scale-invariant or supersymmetric framework cancel the Standard Model vacuum energy across running scales without introducing hidden tunings or new light forces already excluded experimentally?
questions.rationale: The running cosmological-constant problem in [2] and the SLED objections reviewed in [3] define this broad unresolved challenge.

questions.question: Is an unbroken-supersymmetry vacuum interpretation of the real world compatible with string-theory model building and the observed extremely small positive vacuum energy?
questions.rationale: The string-theory review in [1] identifies the cosmological constant as a central obstacle and asks whether the real world can be interpreted through an unbroken-supersymmetry vacuum.

questions.question: Does the near-critical running of the Higgs sector toward the Planck scale provide an actual dynamical trigger for electroweak symmetry breaking or only a boundary-condition coincidence?
questions.rationale: The Standard Model effective-theory discussion in [5] links the 126 GeV Higgs mass, Planck-scale vacuum stability, running masses, and the sign change of quadratic-divergence coefficients.

node_351e967025a2.summary: This cluster studies exact or dynamically broken quantum scale invariance as a route to the hierarchy problem, dilaton physics, electroweak stability, dark matter, inflation, and cosmology.

questions.question: Can exact quantum scale invariance protect the electroweak scale while also producing a phenomenologically acceptable cosmological constant or dark-energy sector?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from [1], which constructs all-order quantum scale-invariant theories and applies them to the hierarchy, cosmological constant, and dark-energy problems.

questions.question: How tightly does Higgs-dilaton cosmology link inflationary observables such as n_s and its running to the present dark-energy equation of state?
questions.rationale: This derives from [2], which predicts relations among the scalar tilt, its running, and the current dark-energy equation-of-state parameter.

questions.question: Can hidden-sector Coleman-Weinberg scale generation transmit the weak scale through the Higgs portal without spoiling technical naturalness through residual couplings to the visible sector?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [4] and [5], where the weak and Planck hierarchy emerges from a nearly decoupled hidden sector or Higgs-portal dimensional transmutation.

node_08e0e90dbd57.summary: These papers center on scale-invariant gravitational theories, dilaton dynamics, unimodular gravity, lattice definitions, and cosmological breaking of scale symmetry.

questions.question: Can quantum scale invariance be maintained beyond perturbation theory in scale-invariant gravity models while keeping the dilaton exactly or nearly massless enough to address both the hierarchy and cosmological constant problems?
questions.rationale: This derives from the all-orders perturbative quantum scale invariance and massless-dilaton mechanism proposed in [1] and its cosmological use in [3].

questions.question: How robust is the Higgs-dilaton relation between the scalar tilt n_s, its running, and the present dark-energy equation of state once the full post-inflationary cosmological evolution is included?
questions.rationale: The specific link between inflationary predictions and late-time dark energy is a central prediction of Higgs-dilaton cosmology in [2].

questions.question: Can hidden-sector decoupling models that generate the weak/Planck hierarchy be embedded in dynamically induced Planck-scale inflation without spoiling the predicted range of tensor-to-scalar ratios?
questions.rationale: This combines the technically natural hidden-sector hierarchy mechanism of [4] with the dynamically generated Planck scale and inflationary predictions of [5].

node_210780d5622c.summary: This cluster explores mechanisms for generating or selecting the weak scale through broken scale invariance, Higgs portal dynamics, dark technicolor, anthropic arguments, entropy principles, and cosmological constraints.

questions.question: What single experimental or cosmological signature would most sharply discriminate among Higgs-portal Coleman-Weinberg scale generation, reheating selection with many Standard Model copies, dark technicolor, and pseudo-dilaton Higgs scenarios?
questions.rationale: The node contains competing weak-scale origin mechanisms whose testability is tied respectively to hidden-sector portals, modified reheating, dark-sector confinement, and broken scale invariance [1], [2], [3], [4].

questions.question: Can classically conformal B-L or hidden-sector models generate the observed Higgs mass and electroweak vacuum expectation value while remaining compatible with RG running near the Planck scale and current null searches for new physics?
questions.rationale: Coleman-Weinberg hidden-sector and B-L models use radiative symmetry breaking to transmit a scale to the Higgs sector, motivated by the observed Higgs mass and near-Planck-scale quartic behavior [1], [5].

node_ee5bc327e21e.summary: These works develop and critique cosmological relaxation scenarios in which a rolling axion-like field dynamically selects the electroweak scale and may connect to inflation, reheating, dark matter, and strong CP physics.

questions.question: Is there a technically natural relaxion construction that raises the cutoff well above the electroweak scale while respecting the gauge redundancy expected of axion-like pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons?
questions.rationale: The original relaxation model achieved cutoffs up to 10^8 GeV [1], but the axion interpretation has been challenged on gauge-symmetry and technical-naturalness grounds [5].

questions.question: Can multi-axion or clockwork realizations generate the exponentially long relaxion field range without introducing fine tuning in the Higgs-mixing phenomenology that experiments already probe?
questions.rationale: Multi-axion models produce long helical flat directions [2], while relaxion-Higgs mixing opens broad experimental constraints and reveals mild tuning in simple clockwork completions [3].

questions.question: What particle-production friction mechanisms can stop the relaxion before, during, or after inflation while avoiding both super-Planckian excursions and conflict with the strong CP problem?
questions.rationale: Particle production was proposed as a relaxion friction force that can avoid super-Planckian motion and decouple the mechanism from inflationary timing [4].

node_d479db3a7be6.summary: This cluster studies local conformal symmetry, Weyl geometry, Stueckelberg breaking, Coleman-Weinberg generation of the Planck scale, torsion effects, and quantum-gravity constraints on symmetries.

questions.question: Which low-energy scale-invariant or Weyl-geometric gravity models survive quantum-gravity consistency conditions requiring no global symmetries, compact gauge groups, and a complete charged spectrum?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from the quantum-gravity symmetry constraints established using AdS/CFT and effective arguments [1,2,3] and emphasized for particle-physics model building [S1].

questions.question: Can generalized or discrete gauge symmetries provide a consistent replacement for would-be global scale or matter symmetries in conformal gravity model building?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the emergence of one-form gauge symmetry in discrete gauge theories [1] and by the generalized-symmetry framework for gauging discrete symmetries [4].

questions.question: Are scalar-nonmetricity theories cosmologically distinguishable from scalar-curvature or scalar-torsion theories once conformal transformations, connection dynamics, and f(Q) relations are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: This derives from the nonmetricity formulation's comparison of scalar-Q, scalar-R, and scalar-T theories and its observation that flat-universe equations coincide with teleparallel dark energy [5].

node_735871449611.summary: These papers apply Weyl conformal geometry and local scale symmetry to gravity, the Standard Model, inflation, B-L extensions, geodesically complete cosmologies, and spontaneous Planck-scale generation.

questions.question: Can scalar-nonmetricity Q theories be observationally separated from scalar-curvature and scalar-torsion dark-energy models once the connection, conformal transformations, and f(Q) relation are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comparison of scalar-nonmetricity, scalar-curvature, scalar-torsion, conformal-frame, and cosmological structures in [1].

questions.question: Under what conditions does lifting the Standard Model plus gravity to a locally conformal theory yield geodesically complete FRW crunch-bang cosmologies without losing analytic control after symmetry breaking?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the Weyl-invariant Standard Model plus gravity construction and geodesically complete cosmologies described in [2].

questions.question: Can conformal symmetry or agravity genuinely stabilize the weak scale up to infinite energy when running couplings must avoid Landau poles, scalar instabilities, and large physical Higgs-mass corrections?
questions.rationale: This derives from the conformal-anomaly hierarchy argument in [3] and the fixed-point and conformal-gravity flow conditions for agravity in [4].

node_00c129e6de19.summary: This cluster examines gauge-theoretic unification of gravity with particle interactions, generalized symmetries, quantum-gravity restrictions on global symmetries, and higher-dimensional or internal-space formulations.

questions.question: What observable low-energy criterion can decide whether a proposed gauge-gravity unification model has successfully eliminated all ordinary, discrete, and generalized global symmetries?
questions.rationale: This broad test follows from the no-global-symmetry constraints in quantum gravity in [1], [2], [3], and the Snowmass framing in [S1].

questions.question: How are Chern-Weil global symmetries such as tr(F_2^2) broken or gauged in concrete particle-physics EFTs coupled to gravity without spoiling their gauge-theory phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This is directly motivated by [5], which identifies Chern-Weil currents as ubiquitous and hard-to-break generalized global symmetries.

questions.question: Can compactness of gauge groups and the requirement of dynamical objects in every allowed representation be turned into practical constraints on BSM model building?
questions.rationale: This derives from the AdS/CFT arguments for compact gauge groups and complete charge spectra in [2] and [3], with phenomenological motivation from [S1].

node_9250d6dee3a1.summary: These works analyze torsion as an effective gravitational field coupled to fermions, including its renormalizable actions, collider bounds, extra-dimensional effects, leptogenesis, neutrino masses, and fermion condensation.

questions.question: Can torsion be made a predictive low-energy field theory beyond fermion-torsion systems, or do scalar couplings inevitably reintroduce unitarity or renormalizability problems?
questions.rationale: This comes from [2], where antisymmetric torsion is equivalent to a massive axial vector and scalar couplings generate serious two-loop divergence problems.

questions.question: Does projective symmetry in scalar-metric-affine gravity provide a general ghost-free principle for torsionful connections once the connection acquires dynamics or couples to matter sectors beyond the unitary-gauge construction?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by [1], where projective symmetry absorbs a ghostly scalar derivative sector when the connection has no kinetic term.

questions.question: Can Kalb-Ramond or torsion-descent axion backgrounds generate realistic leptogenesis or right-handed Majorana neutrino masses without conflicting with the derivative shift symmetry of perturbative torsion couplings?
questions.rationale: This links tree-level leptogenesis from torsion backgrounds in [3] with two-loop Majorana mass generation after shift-symmetry breaking in [5].

node_10b2b9b7051a.summary: This cluster focuses on phenomenological consequences of quantum gravity, especially generalized uncertainty principles, minimum or maximum length scales, higher-derivative unitarity, and constraints from low-energy experiments or gravitational waves.

questions.question: Which low-energy observable could turn generalized-uncertainty-principle Hamiltonian corrections from broad upper bounds into a falsifiable quantum-gravity signal?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the Lamb-shift, Landau-level, STM, and tunneling corrections found to be tiny but bound-setting in [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can any quantum-gravity effective theory with ghosts or higher derivatives remain phenomenologically viable while satisfying unitarity, radiative stability, and low-energy gravitational-EFT constraints?
questions.rationale: This contrasts the severe ghost-instability bounds in [1] with the ghost-free super-renormalizable gravity constructions in [4] and the EFT viewpoint of [5].

node_35f3d528edd2.summary: These papers study higher-derivative, nonlocal, Lee-Wick, fakeon, and quadratic gravity approaches aimed at making quantum gravity unitary, renormalizable, or finite.

questions.question: Can higher-derivative or nonlocal gravity be made finite and ghost-free while satisfying low-energy causality bounds on graviton scattering Wilson coefficients?
questions.rationale: This combines the finite ghost-free non-polynomial gravity program in [2] with the causality and unitarity dispersion-relation constraints of [5].

questions.question: Are unstable ghost-like resonances in quadratic or Lee-Wick gravity truly absent from the asymptotic spectrum beyond perturbative examples, and what observable remnants remain in loop amplitudes?
questions.rationale: This follows from [4], which argues that unstable ghost resonances preserve all-order unitarity when only stable-state cuts enter the unitarity sum.

questions.question: What ultraviolet cutoff or Lorentz-violation structure is required for low-energy ghost effective theories to avoid catastrophic vacuum decay while remaining compatible with gravitational interactions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which derives gamma-ray-background bounds on ghost effective theories and excludes Lorentz-conserving cutoffs.

node_d5e3cc4602e5.summary: This cluster examines generalized uncertainty principles from quantum gravity and their observable consequences for quantum systems, black holes, cosmology, and gravitational waves.

questions.question: Is generalized-uncertainty phenomenology better framed as a universal Hamiltonian correction or as a device-independent measurement limit, and what single class of measurements could distinguish the two?
questions.rationale: This question contrasts universal GUP-induced corrections to quantum Hamiltonians with the device-independent Planck-scale position-measurement limit argued from quantum mechanics and general relativity [1],[3].

questions.question: What sign and magnitude of the GUP parameter can preserve black-hole-remnant or minimum-length physics without eliminating the Chandrasekhar limit for white dwarfs?
questions.rationale: This follows from the observation that a positive GUP parameter can permit arbitrarily large white dwarfs, while a negative parameter may resolve the astrophysical conflict [4].

questions.question: Can GUP-modified phase space explain small-scale weak-equivalence-principle anomalies while remaining compatible with Lamb-shift, Landau-level, tunneling, and STM bounds?
questions.rationale: The question combines proposed GUP effects on equivalence-principle tests and invariant phase space with laboratory bounds from corrected quantum Hamiltonians [1],[2],[5].

node_2d9b4e17b462.summary: These works apply string swampland conjectures to inflation, dark energy, Higgs physics, and particle phenomenology, testing which effective theories can couple consistently to quantum gravity.

questions.question: What observation of r, dark-energy equation of state, or scalar-field range would most directly distinguish refined de Sitter swampland bounds from the trans-Planckian censorship conjecture?
questions.rationale: The cosmological swampland and TCC papers both constrain slow roll and positive potentials but motivate different observational tests involving r, dark energy, and field excursions [2],[3].

questions.question: Can explicit string compactifications realize quintessence potentials satisfying both field-range and gradient bounds while remaining compatible with current cosmological data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the claim that inflation is generically in tension with the swampland criteria while some quintessence models may satisfy both the criteria and observations [2].

questions.question: Is there a model-independent link between the instability of non-supersymmetric AdS flux vacua and the refined de Sitter constraints used in cosmology?
questions.rationale: The question connects the proposed instability of non-supersymmetric AdS flux vacua with the broader web of weak-gravity and de Sitter swampland conjectures [4],[5].

node_0c119f891bb2.summary: This cluster focuses on quantum-gravity signatures in the early universe, especially loop quantum cosmology bounces, inflationary perturbations, primordial spectra, and quantum correlations.

questions.question: What observable would most cleanly distinguish quantum-gravitational slowing of inflation from conventional slow-roll dynamics or stochastic super-Hubble decoherence?
questions.rationale: Two-loop back-reaction calculations predict a late-time, nonperturbatively large slowing of inflation, while open-system EFT describes super-Hubble evolution through a Lindblad/Fokker-Planck limit [1,2,4].

questions.question: Can inflationary non-Gaussianity or unequal-time two-point functions provide a practical test of the large quantum discord predicted for primordial perturbations?
questions.rationale: The power spectrum alone can be reproduced by non-discordant classical states, but [5] argues this requires errors in other two-point correlators and intrinsic non-Gaussianity.

questions.question: Can the graviton-constituent large-N picture be matched quantitatively to semiclassical inflationary EFT predictions, including the history-dependent corrections absent in standard metric treatments?
questions.rationale: The compositeness picture reproduces known inflationary parameters but predicts additional corrections sensitive to inflationary history [3].

node_9f10649385d4.summary: These papers develop asymptotic safety as a UV completion of quantum gravity and matter using renormalization-group fixed points and their implications for Standard Model couplings.

questions.question: Is asymptotic safety predictive enough to fix low-energy Standard Model couplings, and which fixed-point properties distinguish true predictions from free infrared parameters?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Higgs-mass prediction mechanism tied to a gravity-induced quartic fixed point in [1] and the two QED-plus-gravity fixed points with either free or predicted fine-structure constant in [5].

questions.question: What matter-content boundary in scalars, fermions, and gauge fields separates asymptotically safe Standard Model extensions from disfavored GUT, supersymmetric, or extra-dimensional spectra?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the matter-degree-of-freedom bounds found with functional RG methods in [2] and the model-building overview in [3].

questions.question: Does the near-Gaussian irrelevance of high-order Ricci-scalar invariants persist when the bootstrap search is extended to the full metric theory with realistic matter?
questions.rationale: This derives from the high-order Ricci-scalar polynomial bootstrap in [4] and the gravity-matter asymptotic-safety program reviewed in [3].

node_3bf2abd7a299.summary: This cluster studies light dilatons from broken scale invariance, their effective couplings, and how LHC data can distinguish them from or constrain Higgs-like scalars.

questions.question: What LHC or ILC measurement of Higgs-like scalar couplings would most cleanly distinguish a pseudo-dilaton from a minimal Standard Model Higgs when the dilaton scale is near the weak scale?
questions.rationale: The collider discriminants and higgslike dilaton scenario are developed in [2] and [4].

questions.question: Is a naturally light dilaton compatible with strong conformal dynamics for electroweak symmetry breaking without mild tuning, or is near-marginality generically insufficient?
questions.rationale: The effective light-dilaton analysis in [5] states that near-marginality can help but is often not satisfied in EWSB scenarios, matching the tuning concern in [4].

questions.question: Can clockwork or linear-dilaton constructions and least-coupling cosmological dynamics produce suppressed dilaton interactions while preserving collider-accessible deviations from Higgs behavior?
questions.rationale: This question links the least-coupling principle of [1] with the clockwork and continuum linear-dilaton framework of [3].

node_9e0450660a5d.summary: These works build inflationary scenarios within supersymmetry and supergravity, including hybrid, chaotic, no-scale, and nilpotent-superfield models matched to cosmological observables.

questions.question: Which observable would most sharply separate supersymmetric GUT-scale inflation, natural-inflation axion potentials, and many-axion N-flation: the spectral index n(k), reheating requirements, tensor power, or residual isocurvature?
questions.rationale: The supplied models emphasize n(k) as a discriminator, GUT-scale amplitudes, natural-inflation reheating bounds, and radiatively stable many-axion chaotic inflation [1,3,4,5].

questions.question: Can supersymmetric inflation models remain cosmologically viable after imposing both precision density-perturbation constraints and thermal gravitino production limits on the reheating temperature?
questions.rationale: Inflationary model predictions for the primordial perturbation must be combined with high-temperature gravitino production, whose rate affects dark-matter and cosmological constraints [1,2].

questions.question: Is the absence of fine tuning in realistic supersymmetric GUT inflation stable once the amplitude proportional to (M_X/M_P)^2 is confronted with modern constraints on n, dark matter composition, and reheating?
questions.rationale: The classic supersymmetric GUT model avoids usual fine tuning by tying fluctuation amplitudes to the GUT-to-Planck scale ratio and predicts n = 0.98 with assumptions about dark matter [3].

node_cbd7cbc14082.summary: This cluster centers on no-scale supergravity realizations of inflation, including Starobinsky-like potentials, superconformal constructions, and stabilized modulus or matter inflatons.

questions.question: Which Kähler-potential symmetries and controlled superpotential breaking terms can keep a supergravity inflaton flat beyond the Planck scale while matching precision spectral-index and density-perturbation constraints?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the shift-symmetric supergravity chaotic-inflation construction and the review emphasis on spectral-index discrimination among particle-physics inflation models [1] and [5].

questions.question: Can supersymmetric GUT or no-scale inflation link the perturbation amplitude to (M_X/M_P)^2 without fine tuning while maintaining viable reheating, baryogenesis, and moduli cosmology?
questions.rationale: This follows from the SUSY GUT inflation model with amplitude proportional to the GUT-to-Planck scale ratio and the cosmological constraints on moduli and dynamical SUSY breaking [2] and [4].

node_96cdb491448a.summary: These papers explore inflation in supersymmetric and no-scale supergravity frameworks, emphasizing natural potentials, supersymmetry breaking, and predictions for spectral tilt and tensor modes.

questions.question: In minimal supergravity vector-multiplet inflation, what restrictions on the Jordan-frame function are imposed by spectral-index and tensor-mode constraints while avoiding extra scalar stabilization problems?
questions.rationale: This follows from the superconformal master-action construction whose single real scalar can realize arbitrary inflaton potentials without stabilizing chiral extra scalars [5].

questions.question: Can supersymmetric GUT or natural-inflation constructions generate the observed density-perturbation amplitude and tilt without fine tuning while also satisfying reheating, baryogenesis, and moduli or gravitino cosmology constraints?
questions.rationale: The question combines the no-fine-tuning supersymmetric GUT inflation proposal, natural-inflation reheating requirements, and cosmological constraints on dynamical supersymmetry breaking [4].

questions.question: For multi-component supersymmetric inflaton sectors, how does the separate evolution of causally disconnected regions modify spectral-index predictions relative to single-component formulas?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review's emphasis on the extension of the spectral-index formula to multi-component inflaton dynamics [1].

node_96cdb491448a_1.summary: These papers explore inflation in supersymmetric and no-scale supergravity frameworks, emphasizing natural potentials, supersymmetry breaking, and predictions for spectral tilt and tensor modes.

questions.question: Which no-scale or minimal-supergravity inflation constructions can produce the observed spectral tilt while avoiding extra-scalar stabilization problems inherent to chiral-multiplet inflaton models?
questions.rationale: Ref. [5] presents single-real-scalar supergravity inflation in vector or tensor multiplet formulations where supersymmetric partner fields need not acquire vevs during inflation.

questions.question: Can supersymmetric GUT inflation models retain natural density-perturbation amplitudes proportional to (M_X/M_P)^2 while satisfying modern constraints on reheating and dark-matter content?
questions.rationale: Ref. [2] proposes supersymmetric GUT inflation without usual fine tuning, with fluctuation amplitude tied to the GUT-to-Planck scale ratio and n=0.98.

questions.question: How do dynamical supersymmetry-breaking sectors consistent with nucleosynthesis constraints feed back into viable inflaton potentials and post-inflationary cosmology?
questions.rationale: Ref. [4] argues that moduli-like gravitationally coupled supersymmetry-breaking fields are inconsistent with standard nucleosynthesis unless the gravitino is very heavy, while renormalizable flat-space breaking avoids the issue.

node_3d8afd88f9b3.summary: This cluster links inflation to supersymmetry breaking sectors, including sgoldstino, dynamical SUSY-breaking, low-scale SUSY, and natural models without extremely small parameters.

questions.question: Which inflationary observables can robustly distinguish SUSY-breaking sectors that are cosmologically safe from moduli-like hidden sectors that fail nucleosynthesis constraints?
questions.rationale: Dynamical SUSY-breaking models divide into sectors with and without serious cosmological problems [4], while inflationary density perturbations and spectral indices are emphasized as model discriminants [1].

questions.question: Can squeezed-limit non-Gaussianity from Hubble-mass supermultiplets provide a practical test of the supersymmetric naturalness structure of inflation?
questions.rationale: The question is based on the supersymmetric effective theory linking Hubble-scale fields, radiative stability, and squeezed-limit three-point signatures [5].

node_495540bfc97e.summary: These works study Starobinsky and R-squared inflation embedded in old-minimal, new-minimal, higher-derivative, and no-scale supergravity formulations.

questions.question: Which observables beyond leading n_s and r can discriminate genuine R+R^2 supergravity from no-scale and universal-attractor descendants that share the Starobinsky large-field potential but differ in small-field behavior and ultraviolet cutoff scale?
questions.rationale: No-scale Starobinsky-like models and Starobinsky descendants can share large-field predictions while differing in n_s-r-N_* relations and small-field ultraviolet behavior [3][5].

questions.question: Can constrained-multiplet formulations with X^2=0 or R^2=0 be embedded consistently in vector or linear multiplet supergravity while avoiding extra light scalar, axion, vector, or tensor directions during inflation?
questions.rationale: Minimal supergravity inflation avoids stabilizing chiral extra scalars, while Volkov-Akulov-Starobinsky supergravity makes the axion heavy using constrained superfields [1][4].

questions.question: Can scale-free agravity or no-scale supergravity produce the Starobinsky plateau dynamically while maintaining the required Planck-scale boundary conditions and modulus stabilization?
questions.rationale: Agravity links inflationary slow-roll to beta functions and dynamical scale generation, while no-scale supergravity requires controlled modulus or matter-inflaton stabilization [2][3].

node_e31cf009844a.summary: These papers study how MSSM LLe and udd flat directions can drive low-scale A-term inflation and affect reheating, stability, and SUSY-breaking corrections.

questions.question: Can MSSM LLe and udd flat-direction inflation remain predictive once radiative corrections, saddle-point tuning, and collider-measurable slepton or squark soft masses are treated in a single renormalization-group analysis?
questions.rationale: The slow-roll and reheating study found radiative corrections require modest saddle-point tuning and related the inflaton mass running to slepton masses testable outside cosmology [3].

questions.question: What reheating and thermalization history is unique to visible-sector MSSM inflatons, and can it avoid both gravitino overproduction and conflicts with Big Bang nucleosynthesis?
questions.rationale: MSSM flat-direction models predict rapid inflaton decay but delayed full thermalization, with temperatures arranged to avoid the gravitino problem [3].

questions.question: Can a right-handed sneutrino-Higgs-slepton flat direction link the observed neutrino mass scale to the amplitude and tilt of primordial perturbations without adding hidden-sector inflation ingredients?
questions.rationale: The A-term inflation model with small Dirac neutrino masses relates the flat-direction Yukawa coupling, microwave background anisotropy, tilted spectrum, and neutrino masses [5].

node_2ac06e756de2.summary: These works construct chaotic, Starobinsky-like, and plateau inflaton potentials in supergravity using shift-symmetric Kahler structures, stabilized chiral fields, and observational fits.

questions.question: What classes of Kahler potentials and superpotentials simultaneously solve the supergravity eta problem, stabilize all noninflaton scalars, and realize controlled chaotic or arbitrary inflaton potentials?
questions.rationale: This combines the shift-symmetric chaotic construction in [1], the eta-problem conditions in [3], and the stabilization method for arbitrary potentials in [4].

questions.question: Can superconformal Starobinsky and canonical superconformal supergravity embeddings produce observationally distinct spectral-index and tensor predictions while preserving their simple Jordan-frame structure?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the superconformal Starobinsky construction in [2] and the CSS embedding with canonical Jordan-frame kinetic terms in [5].

questions.question: How robust is trans-Planckian chaotic inflation in supergravity to the small shift-symmetry-breaking superpotential terms required to generate the inflaton potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], where flatness beyond the Planck scale is protected by a shift symmetry that must be weakly broken in the superpotential.

node_82e914aaea9c.summary: These papers analyze thermal and nonthermal gravitino production after inflation, its dark matter role, and constraints from reheating, nucleosynthesis, leptogenesis, and cosmic-ray signals.

questions.question: What reheating-temperature window remains simultaneously compatible with thermal gravitino production, BBN light-element bounds, and the temperatures required for thermal leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: Thermal production calculations motivate gravitino dark matter, while BBN and leptogenesis studies turn the relic density and decay effects into reheating-temperature constraints [1].

questions.question: Can collider measurements of gaugino, NLSP, and gravitino-sector parameters make the thermal gravitino relic-density calculation predictive enough to test leptogenesis in the laboratory?
questions.rationale: The collider-test paper gives a gauge-invariant leading-order relic-density result and argues that gaugino mass bounds and a gravitino mass determination can test thermal leptogenesis [4].

questions.question: In R-parity-breaking vacua, what correlated pattern of displaced NLSP decays and diffuse gamma-ray signatures would distinguish metastable gravitino dark matter from conventional stable-gravitino scenarios?
questions.rationale: The R-parity-breaking study predicts centimeter-scale NLSP decay lengths and photon fluxes from relic gravitino decays while preserving BBN and leptogenesis consistency [5].

node_f973276a3134.summary: These studies focus on gravitino LSP scenarios in constrained supersymmetry, combining thermal and NLSP-decay relic abundance with BBN limits and reheating-temperature bounds.

questions.question: Can CMSSM gravitino dark matter remain compatible with thermal leptogenesis once leading-order thermal production, gaugino-mass bounds, and electromagnetic plus hadronic BBN limits on NLSP decays are imposed together?
questions.rationale: This combines thermal production in [1], leptogenesis-linked gaugino bounds in [3], and BBN constraints on gravitino or NLSP decays in [2,4,5].

questions.question: Which NLSP identity, Bino, stau, or sneutrino, leaves the largest viable CMSSM region after relic NSP density, late-decay light-element constraints, and collider-accessible superpartner masses are treated consistently?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the NLSP-specific stable-gravitino constraints in [2,4] and the limited allowed CMSSM parameter space found in [5].

node_ac660b69b3ee.summary: These papers examine gravitino dark matter with late NLSP decays, BBN and lithium constraints, reheating limits, and possible collider signatures of light gravitinos.

questions.question: Which NLSP identity and lifetime range leaves a viable gravitino-LSP dark-matter region after simultaneously applying electromagnetic, hadronic, CMB, relic-density, and structure-formation bounds?
questions.rationale: This follows from studies of bino, stau, sneutrino, slepton, and sneutrino NLSP decays under BBN, CMB, relic-density, and free-streaming constraints [1],[2],[4],[5].

questions.question: Can updated light-element abundance data and full multi-body NLSP decay calculations reopen or close the limited CMSSM regions where gravitinos constitute all dark matter?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in CMSSM gravitino studies and improved BBN analyses including hadronic three- and four-body NLSP decay modes [1],[3],[4],[5].

questions.question: What reheating-temperature upper bounds remain for unstable or stable gravitinos once longitudinal gravitino production and thermal scattering contributions are included consistently?
questions.rationale: This derives from BBN constraints that include longitudinal gravitino production and thermal scattering sources of gravitino abundance [1],[4].

node_f830af8e55d0.summary: These works study gravitino dark matter in gauge-mediated supersymmetry, emphasizing messenger-sector effects on thermal production, entropy dilution, leptogenesis compatibility, and reheating bounds.

questions.question: In gauge-mediated models with thermalized gravitinos and messengers, how model-independent is late-time messenger entropy dilution as a way to remove the reheating-temperature upper bound while preserving thermal leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the claim that messenger decays can naturally dilute gravitino relics independently of gravitino mass and reheating temperature [5], in tension with reheating bounds in gravitino dark matter cosmology [3].

questions.question: Can collider determinations of gaugino masses and a gravitino mass distinguish pure thermal gravitino production from mixed thermal plus nonthermal gravitino dark matter in gauge-mediated scenarios?
questions.rationale: Thermal production links gaugino masses and leptogenesis tests [2], while next-to-lightest-superparticle decays can generate a hot nonthermal gravitino component [4].

node_84a314b2f2ad.summary: These papers investigate gravitino and inflatino production during reheating and preheating, including thermal yields, inflaton decay channels, and ways to evade overproduction constraints.

questions.question: What reheating-temperature bound survives when thermal scattering, thermal-mass decays, top-Yukawa production, and the finite duration of reheating are all included consistently?
questions.rationale: This follows from the classic BBN reheating-temperature constraints in [1] and [5] and the enlarged thermal production rate in [2].

questions.question: In which supergravity models is nonthermal gravitino production during preheating genuinely unsuppressed by gravitational coupling, and how can those cases evade overproduction?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the model-sensitive nonthermal production mechanism after inflation described in [3].

questions.question: How do detailed gravitino decay spectra, including hadronic and photodissociation channels, propagate into light-element abundance limits for gravitino masses below about 10 TeV?
questions.rationale: This derives from the detailed BBN treatment of unstable gravitino lifetimes, branching ratios, and hadron spectra in [4].

node_2d97c57a6cb1.summary: These studies explore metastable gravitino dark matter with small R-parity violation, linking neutrino masses, NLSP decays, gamma rays, cosmic rays, and collider signatures.

questions.question: Can small R-parity violation simultaneously satisfy thermal leptogenesis, big-bang nucleosynthesis, neutrino-mass generation, and a gravitino lifetime longer than the age of the Universe over a broad gravitino-mass range?
questions.rationale: R-parity-breaking gravitino models were argued to reconcile BBN, leptogenesis, and dark matter for sufficiently small lepton-number-violating couplings [1],[2].

questions.question: What combination of displaced NLSP decays at colliders and MeV-to-GeV gamma-ray line searches can distinguish bilinear R-parity violation from the mu nu SSM realization of gravitino dark matter?
questions.rationale: The framework predicts long-lived NLSP signatures [1], while Fermi-LAT line searches and mu nu SSM studies constrain radiative gravitino decay [4],[5].

questions.question: Do updated diffuse gamma-ray and positron data leave viable parameter space where gravitino decays explain high-energy cosmic-ray excesses without overproducing the isotropic photon background?
questions.rationale: Gravitino decay was proposed as a source of gamma-ray and positron excesses [3], but diffuse photon measurements disfavor parts of the mass range in concrete models [5].

node_e2c5656d8746.summary: These papers develop F-term, D-term, and smooth supersymmetric hybrid inflation models, including supergravity corrections, soft terms, cosmic strings, and CMB constraints.

questions.question: Under what supergravity and gauge-charge conditions do D-term hybrid-inflation models genuinely avoid an inflaton mass of order the Hubble scale while still producing the observed density perturbations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the D-term solution to the supergravity slow-roll problem in [1] and the anomalous-D-term supergravity toy model in [3].

questions.question: Are cosmic strings unavoidable in acceptable SUSY GUT hybrid-inflation models once monopole avoidance, baryogenesis, proton lifetime, and end-of-inflation symmetry breaking are imposed?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the systematic SUSY-GUT string-formation result in [2] and the monopole-avoiding nonrenormalizable inflationary valley in [5].

questions.question: Can supergravity hybrid models with natural couplings simultaneously achieve a spectral index near 0.9 to 1, acceptable string or monopole phenomenology, and the Peccei-Quinn or mu-term structure required by the particle model?
questions.rationale: This derives from the blue-spectrum and heavy-string supergravity model in [4] and the Pati-Salam construction with natural couplings, monopole avoidance, PQ symmetry, and mu-term generation in [5].

node_55445de2441b.summary: These works emphasize minimal and extended supersymmetric hybrid inflation, its R-symmetric superpotential structure, soft-breaking effects, GUT-scale phase transitions, and Planck-era parameter constraints.

questions.question: Can F-term hybrid inflation be made compatible with present spectral-index and defect constraints without introducing small parameters that undermine its original supergravity motivation?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the early supergravity realization predicting a blue spectrum and possible heavy cosmic strings [1], compared with later smooth models that avoid topological defects [3].

questions.question: How generic is the use of nonrenormalizable superpotential terms to break GUT symmetries during inflation and thereby avoid monopole production at the waterfall transition?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Pati-Salam model where a nonrenormalizable term creates an inflationary valley with G_PS already broken, preventing monopole production at the end of inflation [2].

questions.question: What initial Higgs-field fluctuation spectrum should be passed from the quantum linear regime to nonlinear lattice simulations in realistic F-term hybrid-inflation waterfall transitions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the analysis showing that Higgs fluctuations become classical Gaussian lumps before bubble growth and collision after hybrid inflation [4].

node_cb19849df64e.summary: These papers analyze D-term hybrid inflation in supergravity and string-inspired settings, focusing on Fayet-Iliopoulos terms, slow-roll viability, and cosmic-string CMB constraints.

questions.question: Can D-term hybrid inflation remain a viable slow-roll mechanism in quantum gravity if conventional Fayet-Iliopoulos terms require exact continuous global symmetries?
questions.rationale: This contrasts the original claim that D-term domination avoids the supergravity eta problem [1], [3] with the argument that FI terms cannot appear in consistent quantum gravity because of global-symmetry requirements [4].

questions.question: What model-building ingredients can decouple the inflationary scale from an observationally excluded cosmic-string tension while preserving monopole avoidance and baryogenesis in SUSY GUT hybrid inflation?
questions.rationale: The issue follows from the claim that cosmic-string formation is unavoidable in acceptable SUSY GUT hybrid-inflation breaking chains and that string mass is proportional to the inflationary scale [2].

questions.question: Do novel FI embeddings without gauged R-symmetry or constrained-multiplet uplifts provide a consistent replacement for anomalous-U(1) D-term inflation in string-derived supergravity?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the supergravity-Maxwell FI construction without gauged R-symmetry and its similarity to anti-D3 uplift constructions [5], in tension with older anomalous-D-term models [3].

node_b27e58d5475a.summary: These works examine string-motivated large-field inflation from axions, moduli, and non-Abelian gauge fields, including axion monodromy, F-theory natural inflation, and reheating.

questions.question: Can string axion inflation produce radiatively stable large-field dynamics without relying on super-Planckian fundamental axion decay constants or controlled de Sitter vacua?
questions.rationale: This question combines N-flation's many-axion radiative stability in [1], sub-Planckian two-axion completion of natural inflation in [3], and the de Sitter-vacua challenge in [5].

questions.question: How do dilaton and moduli masses of order the gravitino mass constrain reheating, thermal inflation, and the viability of string-motivated axion inflation models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the generic dilaton and moduli cosmology in [2] and the use of thermal inflation to address the Polonyi/moduli problem in [4].

questions.question: What observable prediction would discriminate many-field N-flation from aligned two-axion natural inflation when both are embedded in string vacua with gravitational-strength moduli interactions?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the many-axion mechanism in [1], the two-axion effective large-scale mechanism in [3], and the model-independent moduli-sector implications in [2].

node_9592350a1940.summary: Studies string-theoretic moduli in early-universe cosmology, emphasizing inflation, post-inflationary evolution, moduli stabilization, decay, and mechanisms for resolving the cosmological moduli problem.

questions.question: Which moduli-mass, coupling, and decay regimes allow a post-inflationary matter-dominated era to remain compatible with BBN while producing observable consequences for baryogenesis, dark matter, CMB observables, or structure growth?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the generic gravitational-strength moduli of [1] and the post-inflationary matter-dominated histories reviewed in [4].

questions.question: Can thermal inflation or large Hubble-induced moduli masses solve the cosmological moduli problem without erasing the density perturbations and inflationary predictions of the primary inflationary epoch?
questions.rationale: This follows from the thermal-inflation solution proposed in [2] and the C-dependent relaxation mechanism analyzed in [5].

node_b27e58d5475a_1.summary: Explores large-field inflation driven by axions, axion monodromy, and non-Abelian gauge fields in string-inspired models, including reheating and observational constraints.

questions.question: Can axion-alignment or many-axion constructions deliver an effective super-Planckian field range while remaining compatible with the quantum-gravity and effective-field-theory concerns that motivate sub-Planckian fundamental axion scales?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the many-axion radiative-stability proposal of [1] and the two-axion alignment mechanism of [2].

questions.question: In axion inflation with a phi F Ftilde coupling, what parameter region simultaneously provides enough gauge-field dissipation to support inflation on steep potentials and avoids excessive scalar perturbations or non-Gaussianity?
questions.rationale: The tension is stated directly by the dissipative natural-inflation mechanism in [4] and the sourced-fluctuation non-Gaussianity analysis in [5].

questions.question: How can models with gauge fields active during inflation distinguish background anisotropy effects from perturbative gauge-field production in CMB observables?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review of gauge fields as either background fields or perturbative sources during inflation in [3], together with the axion-sourced perturbation effects in [5].

node_8576bcd69b7e.summary: Examines type IIB and F-theory moduli stabilization, loop corrections, de Sitter vacuum constructions, and related string-inflation scenarios.

questions.question: What ten-dimensional criterion decisively distinguishes KKLT-like de Sitter uplifts that fail through volume-modulus backreaction from racetrack or related stabilizations that can evade the obstruction?
questions.rationale: Ref. [4] finds that the simplest single-Kahler-modulus KKLT uplift remains AdS because of stronger backreaction, while racetrack stabilization can avoid this issue.

questions.question: Can the perfect-square ten-dimensional treatment of gaugino condensation be turned into a calculational framework that reproduces four-dimensional supergravity while resolving integrated Einstein-equation objections?
questions.rationale: Ref. [5] argues that a finite perfect-square form for gaugino condensation yields a 10D-derived effective potential consistent with 4D supergravity.

questions.question: Which observation or internal consistency test would most sharply discriminate between the claim that string theory has no de Sitter vacua and nilpotent-multiplet KKLT de Sitter constructions?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1] and [2] frame the central dispute between de Sitter swampland skepticism and advanced KKLT or pure d=4 de Sitter supergravity constructions.

node_ec72cde4259e.summary: Covers nonlinear supersymmetry breaking, nilpotent goldstino superfields, supergravity couplings, and collider phenomenology of sgoldstino and goldstini states.

questions.question: When is replacing a linear goldstino multiplet by a nilpotent constrained superfield a controlled low-energy operation rather than an assumption about the ultraviolet supersymmetry-breaking sector?
questions.rationale: [1] constructs low-energy constrained-superfield Lagrangians by identifying the goldstino superfield X with the short-distance spurion and using constraints to remove heavy degrees of freedom.

questions.question: Can nilpotent-superfield inflation and pure de Sitter supergravity be derived from explicit string compactifications with all moduli stabilized and no hidden sgoldstino dynamics affecting cosmological evolution?
questions.rationale: [2] uses nilpotent goldstino multiplets to remove sgoldstino stabilization from supergravity inflation, [4] constructs scalar-free de Sitter supergravity, and [5] derives a nilpotent multiplet from an anti-D3-brane in KKLT vacua.

questions.question: What collider signatures remain generic for low-scale supersymmetry breaking once a putative sgoldstino resonance is constrained by diphoton, dijet, diboson, Higgs-coupling, and exotic-Higgs-decay searches?
questions.rationale: [3] ties sgoldstino diphoton production and decay rates to gaugino masses over the supersymmetry-breaking scale, while [S1] surveys generic goldstino and sgoldstino collider channels.

node_b07e380e9b8d.summary: Surveys Hubble and structure-growth tensions, early and dynamical dark energy proposals, and observational challenges to the standard LambdaCDM cosmological model.

questions.question: What observation would most decisively tell us whether the H0 tension is new physics, unexpected large-scale structure, or multiple unrelated systematic errors?
questions.rationale: The Hubble-tension review stresses that high-precision early- and late-time data leave a constrained solution space spanning new physics, large-scale structure, and systematics [1].

questions.question: Can any dark-energy or modified-gravity extension relieve H0 and S8 simultaneously without worsening CMB, lensing-amplitude, nucleosynthesis, or late-universe consistency tests?
questions.rationale: The intertwined-cosmology and LambdaCDM-challenges reviews frame H0, sigma8-S8, A_L, and other anomalies as a linked set of tests rather than isolated discrepancies [3,5].

questions.question: Do f(T) teleparallel cosmologies provide a genuinely predictive explanation of late-time acceleration and cosmological tensions once both background expansion and perturbation-level observables are fitted together?
questions.rationale: The f(T) review presents torsional gravity as a framework for late-time acceleration and studies its cosmological solutions at both background and perturbation levels [2].

node_d7e508cdd544.summary: Analyzes Planck, DESI BAO, and supernova constraints on evolving dark energy equations of state, including quintessence-like and phantom-crossing behavior.

questions.question: What combination of DESI BAO, supernovae, CMB, and growth data can cleanly distinguish thawing quintessence from tracking-freezing models that remain nearly degenerate with LambdaCDM?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], where tracking-freezing quintessence is found hard to distinguish from LambdaCDM while thawing models have constrained present-day equation of state.

questions.question: If current data prefer an evolving dark-energy equation of state, which consistency test can decide whether the signal is dark energy or modified gravity rather than a parametrization artifact?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dark-energy versus modified-gravity classification and observable signatures in [4] and the consistency-test emphasis in [5].

questions.question: Can dynamical dark-energy fits address any theoretical part of the cosmological-constant problem, or do they only shift the coincidence problem into scalar-field initial conditions?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the cosmological-constant and cosmic-coincidence problems reviewed in [2] and the broader beyond-LambdaCDM assessment in [3].

node_7eb43aa8c16f.summary: Develops scalar-field models of dark energy and unified dark-sector scenarios, focusing on potentials, equation-of-state evolution, and theoretical fine-tuning issues.

questions.question: What observation would most decisively distinguish thawing quintessence from tracking-freezing models that are nearly degenerate with LambdaCDM in current expansion-history data?
questions.rationale: This derives from the analytic w evolution and the finding that tracking-freezing models are hard to distinguish from LambdaCDM while thawing models are constrained in [1].

questions.question: Can consistency tests combining expansion history and growth of structure separate canonical scalar-field dark energy from modified gravity under the equivalence-principle distinction?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dark-energy versus modified-gravity classification in [4] and the observables and consistency-test program reviewed in [5].

questions.question: Do scalar quintessence potentials meaningfully reduce the cosmological-constant fine-tuning and cosmic-coincidence problems, or do they merely reparametrize them in w(a)?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question is motivated by the cosmological-constant and coincidence problems in [2] and the broader beyond-LambdaCDM assessment in [3].

node_9313c9326cac.summary: Reviews alternatives to a pure cosmological constant, including time-varying Lambda models, modified gravity, scale-invariant couplings, and broader beyond-LambdaCDM frameworks.

questions.question: What consistency test using expansion history and growth of structure can cleanly distinguish dark-energy stress energy from modified gravity defined by violations of the weak or strong equivalence principle?
questions.rationale: The dark-energy-versus-modified-gravity review explicitly proposes an equivalence-principle-based distinction and links it to cosmological observables [3].

questions.question: Can single-scalar dark-energy models with equation-of-state crossing w = -1 be made stable, predictive, and distinguishable from flexible parametric w(z) descriptions?
questions.rationale: The single-scalar model was proposed to realize crossing of w = -1, while the observables review emphasizes parametric descriptions and consistency tests [5].

questions.question: Which problem should count as the strongest reason to move beyond LambdaCDM: cosmological-constant naturalness, CMB or small-scale anomalies, inflation testability, dark-matter microphysics, or large-scale gravity?
questions.rationale: The beyond-LambdaCDM review lists these theoretical and observational motivations while noting that LambdaCDM remains observationally successful [2].

node_5e58ff40feff.summary: Studies quintessence models coupled to dark matter, Higgs, gauge, or hidden-sector fields as mechanisms for dark energy and unified dark-sector dynamics.

questions.question: Can interacting quintessence models be distinguished from LCDM if tracking freezing solutions remain observationally nearly degenerate with a cosmological constant?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the review finding that tracking freezing quintessence is hard to distinguish from LCDM using supernovae, CMB, and BAO data [1].

questions.question: What coupling structures to dark-sector or supersymmetry-breaking fields can reduce the fine tuning of the quintessence potential without spoiling the required range -1 < w < 0?
questions.rationale: This combines the fine-tuning problem for V(phi) with models where dynamical supersymmetry breaking supplies a scalar component with quintessence-like equation of state [2],[3].

node_d7e508cdd544_1.summary: Focuses on recent DESI BAO, CMB, and supernova evidence for dynamical dark energy, testing the robustness of late-time transitions beyond LambdaCDM.

questions.question: Is the DESI BAO plus CMB plus supernova preference for dynamical dark energy stable under controlled replacements of the CPL ansatz by late-time transition parameterizations with comparable statistical power?
questions.rationale: The DESI robustness paper directly tests whether the CPL parameterization drives the reported preference for quintessence-like present behavior and past phantom crossing [5].

questions.question: Can a phenomenological emergent dark-energy model with no effective early-time dark energy resolve the H0 tension while remaining consistent with DESI BAO, Planck CMB, and supernova constraints?
questions.rationale: The emergent dark-energy model was proposed to address H0 tensions through late-time emergence with zero extra degrees of freedom relative to LambdaCDM [1].

questions.question: How do curvature, Neff, modified-gravity parameters, and time-varying dark energy covary in combined DESI-like distance measurements, weak lensing, and CMB analyses when spatial flatness is not imposed a priori?
questions.rationale: DES Y1 explored curvature, Neff, w0-wa, and modified gravity extensions, while BAO plus CMB data strongly constrain curvature through geometric degeneracy breaking [2,3].

node_151739d71f6e.summary: Investigates early dark energy and other early-universe modifications as possible explanations for the Hubble tension and related cosmological parameter discrepancies.

questions.question: What joint data set would decisively distinguish an early-dark-energy reduction of the sound horizon from late-time or systematic explanations while keeping H0, S8, A_L, and lower-significance anomalies mutually consistent?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the reviews' framing of H0, S8, A_L, and other tensions as simultaneous constraints on any new-physics solution [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: In scalar-field early dark energy, how tightly must the activation redshift near z>=3000, the EDE fraction, and the perturbation evolution be constrained for Planck-inferred H0 to rise without degrading the CMB fit?
questions.rationale: This derives from the EDE model in which the component behaves like a cosmological constant at early times, dilutes rapidly later, and requires a detailed perturbation calculation [5].

questions.question: What falsifiable criterion can decide whether the early-late universe discrepancies reflect one coherent extension of LambdaCDM or several unrelated observational systematics?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reviews' emphasis that persistent early-late discrepancies may demand new physics but remain challenged by high-precision data and possible systematics [1], [2], [3].

node_0fa7c6bf05b3.summary: Uses non-CMB probes such as BAO, supernovae, quasars, Hubble-parameter data, gamma-ray bursts, and starburst galaxies to constrain cosmological parameters.

questions.question: Which combination of low-redshift luminosity-distance, BAO, Hubble-parameter, and quasar-anisotropy data can distinguish true departures from FLRW assumptions from hidden systematics in the Planck curvature and lensing anomalies?
questions.rationale: Planck closed-universe evidence [1], luminosity-distance discordance [4], and quasar dipole anomalies [2] all challenge standard low-redshift consistency tests.

questions.question: Can deviations from the cosmological principle explain H0-related discordances without violating the observed pattern of large-scale isotropy and homogeneity across independent tracers?
questions.rationale: The cosmological-principle review frames H0 tension as potentially extending beyond LambdaCDM to the CP itself [3].

questions.question: How large can second-order inhomogeneity corrections and super-Hubble variance be before low-redshift expansion-rate constraints become biased at the level relevant to current tensions?
questions.rationale: The inhomogeneous-expansion calculation finds small mean corrections but variance sensitive to unknown super-Hubble perturbations [5].

node_4f9ee1dbdbe5.summary: These papers review the discrepancy between early- and late-universe Hubble constant measurements, its relation to other cosmological tensions, and possible new-physics explanations beyond ΛCDM.

questions.question: What observational result would decisively show whether the H0 tension is a single new-physics signal rather than an unresolved systematic or several unrelated data-set discrepancies?
questions.rationale: This broad framing follows from the review emphasis in [1] and [5] on persistent early-late H0 disagreement despite multiple independent measurements.

questions.question: Can any proposed extension of LambdaCDM relieve H0 while simultaneously remaining consistent with S8, lensing-amplitude, and other lower-significance anomalies?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the intertwined-tensions perspective of [2] and the unified update on LambdaCDM challenges in [4].

questions.question: How should early- and late-universe probes be combined so that parameter shifts forced by one epoch do not simply move the tension into another epoch's observables?
questions.rationale: This follows from the workshop framing of early-versus-late cosmological tensions in [3] and the solution-space constraints reviewed in [1].

node_556c25ea401f.summary: This cluster studies how future gravitational-wave standard sirens from ground- and space-based detectors can constrain H0, dark energy, and other cosmological parameters independently of traditional probes.

questions.question: How many well-localized third-generation standard sirens are needed for H0 constraints to become competitive with ACT-plus-BAO and Planck-era measurements without importing their cosmological assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the ACT lensing and BAO H0 precision in [1] and the Einstein Telescope event-count forecasts in [2].

questions.question: Can standard sirens from Cosmic Explorer or the Einstein Telescope independently distinguish LambdaCDM, wCDM, CPL dark energy, and scalar-tensor modified propagation through luminosity-distance measurements?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the scalar-tensor standard-siren bounds in [4] and the CE forecasts for LambdaCDM, wCDM, and CPL models in [5].

node_f8522fce2fa4.summary: These works examine early dark energy models that reduce the sound horizon to ease the Hubble tension, together with CMB, lensing, and large-scale-structure constraints on their viability.

questions.question: Is there any early-dark-energy scalar dynamics that raises the CMB-inferred H0 while remaining consistent with ACT DR6, Planck polarization, CMB lensing, DESI BAO, and supernova constraints?
questions.rationale: EDE reduces the sound horizon to raise H0, but ACT DR6 extended-model analyses combine primary CMB, lensing, BAO, and supernova data to constrain such extensions [1][3].

questions.question: Which perturbation signatures can distinguish oscillating scalar EDE with z_c near 10^3.5 and roughly 10 percent fractional energy density from degeneracies in standard cosmological parameters?
questions.rationale: Oscillating scalar-field EDE fits prefer a frozen field that activates near log10(z_c) around 3.5, contributes about 10 percent, and is constrained by Planck polarization perturbation dynamics [5].

node_4b9e1bd8db13.summary: This cluster develops and tests models in which vacuum energy or gravitational coupling evolves with cosmic expansion, connecting quantum-field-theory vacuum effects to H0 and σ8 tensions.

questions.question: Can running-vacuum models resolve H0 and sigma8 tensions without relying on data combinations whose BAO, LSS, and CMB correlations drive the apparent preference?
questions.rationale: RVM analyses claim evidence from combined SNIa, BAO, H(z), LSS, BBN, and CMB fits and identify BAO, LSS, and CMB as the main sources of dynamical-vacuum signals [2],[5].

questions.question: What quantum-field-theoretic calculation in an expanding universe would fix the allowed H-dependent powers in rho_Lambda(H) rather than treating them phenomenologically?
questions.rationale: The running-vacuum framework writes rho_Lambda(H) as a constant plus powers of H and motivates this structure as potentially linked to QFT in the expanding universe [2].
kg_prereqs: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

questions.question: Can Higgs electroweak vacuum energy and the cosmological constant problem be connected quantitatively to mild late-time vacuum running?
questions.rationale: The cosmological-constant review emphasizes the tension between vacuum-energy expectations, including electroweak Higgs vacuum energy, and the observed cosmological constant [1].

node_4e591fe3d8a8.summary: These papers address why quantum vacuum energy appears enormously larger than the observed cosmological constant, exploring renormalization, sequestering, string vacua, and thermodynamic perspectives.

questions.question: Can any radiatively stable sequestering mechanism fully remove Standard Model vacuum energy, including electroweak phase-transition contributions, while retaining a local diffeomorphism-invariant formulation of gravity?
questions.rationale: This question directly connects the Standard Model vacuum-energy crisis emphasized in [1] with the global and local sequestering proposals of [2] and [4].

questions.question: Is the observed cosmological constant more plausibly fixed by a measured finite residual curvature term, by trans-Planckian frozen tail modes, or by a revision of how vacuum divergences are regulated?
questions.rationale: The alternatives are motivated respectively by the residual finite curvature in [4], the trans-Planckian tail modes of [3], and the Lorentz-invariant regularization argument in [5].

questions.question: What observation or consistency condition could distinguish a true gravitational decoupling of matter-sector vacuum energy from a cancellation that merely shifts the cosmological constant problem into boundary conditions or UV-sensitive finite parts?
questions.rationale: This follows from [2] and [4], where vacuum energy is sequestered but a finite curvature contribution remains to be fixed by measurement.

node_617f46179e68.summary: This cluster explores dark matter as a gravitational-sector phenomenon involving massive spin-2 fields, bigravity, multimetric theories, Kaluza-Klein gravitons, and related cosmological signatures.

questions.question: What cosmological stability and perturbation criteria define the viable mass, coupling, and abundance window in which a massive spin-2 field behaves as all of dark matter without introducing bimetric instabilities?
questions.rationale: This follows from the heavy spin-2 dark matter proposal in [2] and [4] together with the linear-stability criteria for bimetric cosmology in [3].

questions.question: Can coherent oscillating spin-2 dark matter produce detectable signals in atomic clocks, spectroscopy, resonant-mass detectors, or axion-like-particle searches without violating gravitational-strength coupling assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is based on [5], which identifies oscillating electric-charge and resonant-detector signatures as tests of spin-2 dark matter from bimetric theory.

questions.question: How strongly do CMB tensor-mode limits constrain Planckian interacting massive-particle or spin-2 dark matter production mechanisms when the dark sector couples only through Planck-suppressed operators?
questions.rationale: This derives from [1], where Planck-scale interacting dark matter masses above a threshold are tied to the absence of tensor modes in the CMB.

node_5e44f9206764.summary: These works focus on observational evidence and phenomenological consequences of dynamical vacuum energy models, especially their ability to challenge ΛCDM and mitigate H0 and σ8 tensions.

questions.question: Which combination of SNIa, BAO, H(z), LSS, BBN, and CMB observables can decisively distinguish a running vacuum rho_Lambda(H) from flexible XCDM or CPL dynamical-dark-energy parametrizations?
questions.rationale: The reported evidence for vacuum dynamics arises from combined fits in which BAO, LSS, and CMB provide much of the discriminating power, but similar signals appear in XCDM and CPL fits [1],[3],[5].

questions.question: Can a single Lambda(H) running-vacuum framework simultaneously improve the H0 and sigma8 tensions without relying on matter non-conservation or varying G assumptions that conflict with BBN and CMB constraints?
questions.rationale: Running-vacuum models allow dynamical rho_Lambda, possible G variation, and possible matter non-conservation, and have been applied specifically to the H0 controversy and global data fits [1],[2].

node_4876a02822f2.summary: This cluster links dark energy to neutrino physics through mixing-induced vacuum condensates, mass-varying neutrino scenarios, and neutrino condensate mechanisms.

questions.question: Is the neutrino-dark-energy link best tested as a running cosmological constant tied to neutrino number density, or do existing mass-varying-neutrino scenarios reduce observationally to standard dark energy?
questions.rationale: Ref. [1] argues that the dark sector behaves like a cosmological constant that runs as neutrino mass changes with temperature and becomes important when neutrinos become nonrelativistic.

questions.question: Can late-time neutrino condensate models simultaneously evade cosmological neutrino mass bounds and predict observable flavor-rate deviations in extraterrestrial neutrino fluxes?
questions.rationale: Ref. [2] predicts neutrinos massless until a late meV-scale phase transition and enhanced neutrino decays testable in future IceCube data.

questions.question: What field-theoretic calculation would settle whether particle-mixing vacuum condensates can produce a dark-energy-sized contribution with adiabatic index close to -1 without conflicting with known neutrino and quark phenomenology?
questions.rationale: Ref. [5] attributes a dynamically evolving dark-energy contribution to particle-mixing vacuum condensates for neutrinos and quarks.

node_9597eedf5504.summary: These papers review and constrain scalar-tensor, Horndeski, teleparallel, and effective-field-theory dark energy models in light of gravitational-wave speed bounds and cosmological tests.

questions.question: Which scalar-tensor dark-energy operators remain technically natural after imposing c_g = c not only on the observed cosmological background but also on nearby matter-density histories?
questions.rationale: This follows from the post-GW170817 requirement that gravitational-wave speed constraints hold without tuning for nearby cosmological solutions in EFT and covariant Horndeski-like languages [2],[3].

questions.question: Can f(T) teleparallel cosmology reproduce late-time acceleration and perturbation-level tests while satisfying the same multimessenger gravitational-wave speed bounds that rule out large classes of scalar-tensor models?
questions.rationale: This links the review of f(T) background and perturbation cosmology to the GW170817 constraints on modified-gravity dark-energy candidates [1],[2].

questions.question: How can cosmological tests distinguish surviving modified-gravity explanations of acceleration from LambdaCDM once GW170817 has fixed three effective dark-energy parameters on astrophysical scales?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in reviews of cosmological modified-gravity tests and the implication that GW170817 severely constrains several EFT parameters of scalar-tensor gravity [4],[5].

node_da6bc495fb1b.summary: This cluster surveys modified gravity alternatives such as f(T), f(R), Galileon, and Horndeski models, emphasizing cosmological acceleration, structure growth, and possible relief of Hubble tension.

questions.question: Which perturbation-level observables can cleanly distinguish teleparallel or non-metricity models that reproduce a LambdaCDM-like background evolution, especially the power-law f(Q)=Q+alpha Q^n case with |n|<1?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finding that power-law f(Q) can match LambdaCDM at the background level while still being analyzed through matter perturbations and the growth index [4].

questions.question: Can a unified set of cosmological tests discriminate late-time acceleration from geometric torsion or non-metricity terms versus dark energy without violating Solar-System and astrophysical gravity constraints?
questions.rationale: The question combines the f(T) review's emphasis on late-time acceleration from torsion with the broader modified-gravity testing program across local and cosmological scales [1],[2].

questions.question: Do ISW-galaxy cross-spectra and CMB lensing provide a decisive test of self-accelerating Galileon-like modified-gravity models relative to f(T) or f(Q) alternatives?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Galileon analysis using CMB, BAO, H0, CMB lensing, and the sign of C_l^{Tg} from the evolution of the lensing potential [5].

node_a581a868c946.summary: These works develop effective-field-theory and generalized Horndeski frameworks for dark energy and modified gravity, incorporating constraints from GW170817 and cosmological perturbations.

questions.question: What scalar-tensor dark-energy operators remain technically natural after imposing c_g equals c not only on the observed background but also on nearby cosmological solutions?
questions.rationale: This follows from [2], which argues that avoiding tuning requires the gravitational-wave speed constraint to hold under small changes in matter abundance.
kg_prereqs: effective field theory of dark energy

questions.question: Can the post-GW170817 surviving Horndeski, beyond-Horndeski, and DHOST subclasses produce observable cosmological perturbation signatures without reintroducing forbidden gravitational-wave-speed deviations?
