questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1,3,5], which show that GW170817 eliminates or severely restricts large regions of scalar-tensor dark-energy theory.

questions.question: Can attractor mechanisms toward general relativity in ultra-light scalar-tensor quintessence be embedded consistently in the restricted post-GW170817 theory space?
questions.rationale: This derives from [4], which uses simultaneous tracker and general-relativity attractors to accommodate ultra-light scalar fields.

node_a581a868c946_1.summary: This cluster centers on effective-field-theory descriptions of Horndeski and beyond-Horndeski cosmology, especially how gravitational-wave speed measurements restrict viable dark energy models.

questions.question: What technically natural scalar-tensor dark-energy theories remain after imposing c_g equal to c not only on the observed cosmological background but also on nearby matter-density histories?
questions.rationale: The GW170817 EFT analysis argued that avoiding tuning requires the gravitational-wave speed to remain luminal on nearby cosmological solutions, imposing precise operator relations [2].

questions.question: Can DHOST degeneracy conditions preserve a viable single scalar degree of freedom while satisfying the GW170817 constraints on the EFT parameters relevant to astrophysical scales?
questions.rationale: The neutron-star merger implications paper constrained three of the five effective dark-energy parameters, while DHOST theories rely on degeneracy to avoid an Ostrodradsky mode [3], [5].

questions.question: Are the surviving scalar-tensor routes after GW170817 observationally distinguishable from quintessence through equivalence-principle tests or time variation of couplings?
questions.rationale: The post-GW170817 analysis left only restricted scalar-tensor alternatives, and scalar-tensor quintessence highlights ultra-light scalar risks for equivalence-principle violations and varying couplings [1], [4].

node_de6f3d5c065c.summary: These papers study how perturbations, scalar-field effective fluids, and viscous stresses modify averaged cosmological expansion and dark-energy-like dynamics.

questions.question: Can the effective energy-momentum tensor of long-wavelength perturbation backreaction be defined in a gauge-robust way that yields an observationally meaningful dark-energy-like component?
questions.rationale: Backreaction from long-wavelength modes was argued to mimic a cosmological-constant contribution through an effective energy-momentum tensor [1].

questions.question: Which effective-fluid descriptions of modified expansion, such as f(R), Cardassian interaction terms, hyperfluids, or viscous inflation, can be observationally distinguished using perturbations rather than background expansion alone?
questions.rationale: The representative papers emphasize that models with similar backgrounds can have distinct dark-energy perturbations, torsion or non-metricity, interaction pressure, or viscous inflationary observables [2], [3], [4], [5].

node_1c304cfdd617.summary: This cluster tests dark matter, dark energy, and dark radiation interaction models against CMB, BAO, supernova, lensing, and structure-growth data to address cosmological tensions.

questions.question: Can interacting dark energy models with coupling proportional to the dark-energy density reduce both the H0 and cosmic-shear tensions without becoming inconsistent with BAO, SNeIa, CMB lensing, and galaxy-clustering data as the datasets improve?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the finding that such interacting dark energy models can reduce the H0 tension and interact nontrivially with DES cosmic-shear constraints [1].

questions.question: What is the most general stable parameter space for coupled dark matter-dark energy models once the dark-energy equation of state w and early-time superhorizon stability conditions are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows from the observation that interactions and w are formally independent but practically correlated by the need to avoid early-time instabilities [2].

questions.question: Can a unified principal-component or detectability-factor framework compare decaying dark matter, interacting dark energy, and dark radiation models using the same CMB and matter-power-spectrum response functions?
questions.rationale: This extends the single-number CMB detectability approach for dark matter decay [3] and the Boltzmann-hierarchy treatment of decays into invisible radiation [4].

node_7088ecf5d14f.summary: These works use horizon thermodynamics, entropy production, holographic equipartition, and running or decaying vacuum terms to model cosmic expansion.

questions.question: Can horizon-entropy or running-vacuum cosmologies provide a viable alternative early expansion history that preserves BBN while producing testable consequences for dark matter, baryogenesis, gravitational waves, or primordial black holes?
questions.rationale: This broad framing question follows from [1], which reviews the weak empirical constraints on pre-BBN radiation domination and its consequences for several relics.

questions.question: Which entropy form on the Hubble horizon yields mutually consistent continuity equations from thermodynamics and Friedmann dynamics without failing background expansion or matter-perturbation constraints?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [3] and [4], which show viability problems for entropic-force dark energy and analyze consistency for entropy proportional to powers of the Hubble horizon.

questions.question: Can particle and entropy production in the running-vacuum model be distinguished observationally from LambdaCDM while retaining a nonsingular early state, graceful exit, and final de Sitter behavior?
questions.rationale: This derives from [5], which presents the running-vacuum universe as a global cosmic history with entropy production and observational performance competitive with LambdaCDM.

node_2e01e23dc428.summary: This broad cluster connects primordial non-Gaussianity, inflationary perturbations, CMB constraints, and effective field theory descriptions of large-scale structure.

questions.question: What level of primordial B-mode sensitivity and foreground control would be enough to decide whether the simplest slow-roll single-field models remain the default inflationary paradigm?
questions.rationale: CMB-S4 is designed to cross critical thresholds in the search for primordial gravitational-wave B modes, while the inflationary landscape review argues for testing simple slow-roll single-field models first in the absence of non-minimal signals [1,5,S2].

questions.question: Can the effective field theory of inflation and the cosmological bootstrap be joined into a predictive framework that constrains g^{00}, extrinsic-curvature operators, sound speed effects, and primordial correlator singularities from unitarity, locality, and symmetry?
questions.rationale: The EFT of inflation organizes single-field fluctuations through unitary-gauge operators such as g^{00} and K_mu nu, while the cosmological bootstrap constrains primordial correlators using singularities, unitarity, locality, and symmetry [4,S1].

questions.question: Which correlated pattern of curvature perturbations, residual isocurvature, and non-Gaussianity would distinguish curvaton generation from inflaton-generated perturbations in CMB-S4 and large-scale-structure data?
questions.rationale: The curvaton mechanism converts an initially isocurvature perturbation into curvature perturbations and predicts any residual isocurvature to be fully correlated with the curvature perturbation [3].

node_681b4271e0db.summary: These papers examine inflationary gravitational-wave claims and constraints alongside effective field theory and quantum-loop corrections to primordial perturbations.

questions.question: What foreground-cleaned B-mode measurement threshold would robustly distinguish primordial tensor power from lensed LambdaCDM plus dust, given the BICEP2 and Planck cross-correlation lesson?
questions.rationale: CMB-S4 is designed to cross critical B-mode thresholds, while the BICEP2 excess was reinterpreted through joint BICEP2/Keck and Planck dust correlations [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: Which EFT-of-inflation operators built from g00 and K_mu_nu remain experimentally unconstrained, and how would their allowed sizes separate slow-roll, small-sound-speed, and Ghost Inflation regimes?
questions.rationale: The EFT of inflation organizes single-field fluctuations using operators such as g00 and extrinsic curvature and maps them onto broad single-field scenarios [3].

questions.question: Can efficient exploration of the slow-roll single-field landscape convert CMB-S4 tensor limits into decisive exclusions of whole classes of minimal inflationary models?
questions.rationale: The Encyclopaedia Inflationaris identifies the large slow-roll landscape as a central challenge, and CMB-S4 targets critical tensor sensitivity [1], [4], [S1].

node_681b4271e0db_1.summary: This cluster focuses on the Planck, WMAP, BICEP2, and Keck implications for tensor modes, dust contamination, and viable single-field inflation models.

questions.question: What level of multifrequency foreground control is required for a degree-scale B-mode excess at ell around 80 to be interpreted as primordial tensors rather than Galactic dust?
questions.rationale: BICEP2 reported an excess at degree scales, but the joint BICEP2/Keck and Planck analysis detected significant 150x353 GHz B-mode dust correlation in the same sky region [1],[3].

questions.question: After Planck and BICEP/Keck, which slow-roll single-field inflation models remain favored once tensor limits, Bayesian evidence, and model complexity are evaluated together?
questions.rationale: The inflationary model surveys used Planck data, Bayesian evidence, ASPIC, and MULTINEST to rank large classes of slow-roll single-field scenarios and rule out many models [2],[5].

questions.question: Can lensing B modes and Galactic foregrounds be separated well enough to make a future primordial-tensor detection a model-discriminating test rather than only an upper limit?
questions.rationale: The B-mode review explains how inflationary gravitational waves, lensing, and Galactic foregrounds each generate B modes and how they must be distinguished observationally [4].

node_8c8a8aa3b440.summary: These works compare and classify inflationary scenarios using WMAP, Planck, BICEP2, and Bayesian evidence to identify observationally favored models.

questions.question: What observation of primordial tensors, non-Gaussianity, isocurvature, or features would most efficiently break the Bayesian degeneracy among the currently favored slow-roll single-field inflation models?
questions.rationale: This follows from the systematic Bayesian ranking of single-field models and the white-paper emphasis on tensors, non-Gaussianity, and features as key observational targets [2][4].

questions.question: Can model-selection pipelines incorporate initial-condition and multiverse-unpredictability costs without double-counting the Occam penalties already used in Bayesian evidence?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in Bayesian model comparison after Planck and the critique that plateau-like favored models worsen initial-condition and predictability problems [2][3].

questions.question: What limited reconstruction of the inflaton potential is actually achievable from realistic scalar and tensor spectra, given that full functional reconstruction is not foreseeable?
questions.rationale: This derives from the reconstruction formalism and its conclusion that full potential reconstruction is impractical with foreseeable observations [5].

node_4bfc58c60840.summary: This cluster centers on interpreting BICEP2 B-mode polarization through joint Planck analyses, foreground dust modeling, and tensor-spectrum constraints.

questions.question: What combination of multi-frequency B-mode cross-spectra would constitute a decisive test that degree-scale BICEP2-like excess power is primordial rather than polarized Galactic dust plus lensing?
questions.rationale: This follows from the original BICEP2 excess at ell about 80 in [1], the high-significance 150 x 353 GHz dust cross-correlation in [2], and the foreground degeneracy emphasized in [4].

questions.question: How much does uncertainty in the dust B-mode power-spectrum shape and polarization fraction limit future constraints on the tensor-to-scalar ratio r in low-foreground sky regions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the Planck dust-polarization uncertainty and assumed C_l^BB proportional to l^-2.42 in the joint analysis of [5].

questions.question: Can lensing B modes, Galactic foregrounds, and inflationary tensors be separated with enough robustness that the remaining systematics are subdominant to sample variance at degree angular scales?
questions.rationale: The separation problem is laid out in the review of inflationary, lensing, and foreground B modes in [3] and tested empirically by the joint BICEP2/Keck and Planck analysis in [2].

node_6ac89531e827.summary: These papers analyze quantum and one-loop corrections to curvature perturbations, especially in ultra-slow-roll or effective field theory inflation settings.

questions.question: In the EFT of inflation with g00 and extrinsic-curvature operators, which one-loop corrections to the curvature perturbation remain radiatively stable once slow-roll, small sound speed, and ghost-inflation limits are treated in one common power-counting scheme?
questions.rationale: This follows from the EFT-of-inflation construction and from power-counting analyses aimed at identifying the validity limits of classical inflationary treatments [1], [3].

questions.question: Can heavy fields near the cutoff leave observable power-spectrum or squeezed-limit bispectrum features through rapid turns without invalidating the single-clock or quasi-single-field EFT expansion?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by studies showing that fast turns can imprint heavy physics in the CMB power spectrum and by the EFT treatment of quasi-single-field inflation with Hubble-scale massive scalars [4], [5].

questions.question: What observable tensor signatures can uniquely identify curvature-squared or parity-violating loop corrections rather than scalar-sector higher-derivative interactions?
questions.rationale: The question derives from EFT analyses finding that leading tensor corrections arise from curvature-squared terms, including parity-violating helicity-dependent propagation [2].

node_b1beb7342b74.summary: This cluster contains pedagogical reviews of standard cosmology, inflation, perturbations, dark matter, dark energy, and CMB spectral-distortion probes.

questions.question: What combination of CMB-S4 observables would most decisively distinguish inflationary tensor signals from late-time or astrophysical contaminants while also constraining neutrino masses and light relics?
questions.rationale: This follows from CMB-S4's stated goal of crossing thresholds in B-mode searches, neutrino-sector measurements, light relics, dark energy, and large-scale gravity tests [1].

questions.question: Can the perturbation-theory framework used to explain structure formation be extended into a quantitatively predictive account of reheating and back-reaction without introducing model-dependent assumptions that erase inflation's explanatory power?
questions.rationale: The question combines the perturbation lectures' role in explaining the origin of structure with the identified problems of reheating and perturbative back-reaction [2,5].

questions.question: Is minimal empirical completion of the Standard Model, with only the degrees of freedom needed for dark energy, dark matter, neutrino masses, baryogenesis, and inflation, a meaningful benchmark against which more aesthetic BSM constructions should be judged?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the New Minimal Standard Model's claim that six new degrees of freedom can accommodate the empirical failures of the Minimal Standard Model [3].

node_0dded6ebe4bf.summary: These papers explore bouncing-universe alternatives to inflation, including Galileon and positive-curvature scenarios, their perturbations, and observational signatures.

questions.question: Can any nonsingular bounce produce a red, quasi scale-invariant, purely adiabatic scalar spectrum while simultaneously avoiding NEC violation instabilities and shear growth?
questions.rationale: This is the central viability tension identified in the critical review of classical bouncing cosmologies against Planck constraints [2].

questions.question: Which bounce mechanisms preserve or convert curvature perturbations through a smooth bounce in a way that evades the strongly scale-dependent ekpyrotic spectrum found when gravitational back-reaction is included?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the finding that including gravitational back-reaction makes the ekpyrotic curvature spectrum strongly scale-dependent and continuous across a smooth bounce [3].

questions.question: Can future surveys distinguish bouncing scenarios from slow-roll inflation through robust tensor signatures such as the blue tensor tilt predicted in string-gas Hagedorn models?
questions.rationale: The Hagedorn string-gas calculation predicts nearly scale-invariant tensors with a small blue tilt, unlike slow-roll inflation [5].

node_fc4ba3100751.summary: This cluster uses CMB and galaxy-clustering bispectra, especially within the effective field theory of large-scale structure, to constrain primordial non-Gaussianity.

questions.question: Can EFTofLSS galaxy power-spectrum and bispectrum analyses reach primordial non-Gaussianity constraints competitive with Planck while marginalizing over bias, redshift-space distortions, bulk flows, and short-scale counterterms?
questions.rationale: This question connects Planck bispectrum limits [1], the perturbative bias framework [2], and BOSS EFTofLSS power-spectrum analyses [4] and [5].

questions.question: Which squeezed-to-equilateral bispectrum shapes from quasi-single-field inflation remain distinguishable in large-scale structure after nonlinear evolution and bias expansion are included?
questions.rationale: The intermediate bispectrum shapes of quasi-single-field inflation [3] motivate asking how robustly they survive the galaxy-bias and perturbative modeling framework reviewed in [2].

node_82b679bf61b1.summary: These papers develop and apply CMB and large-scale-structure bispectrum methods to constrain primordial non-Gaussianity, including local, equilateral, orthogonal, parity-violating, and foreground-biased signals.

questions.question: Can large-scale-structure bispectrum analyses with one-loop EFT systematics reach the Delta f_NL^local,equil ~ 1 target without degeneracies with bias, foregrounds, and late-time nonlinearities?
questions.rationale: The target sensitivity is argued in [4], while [5] shows current BOSS EFT power-spectrum and bispectrum limits remain much weaker.

questions.question: Which non-Gaussian feature templates can break the degeneracy among distinct inflationary mechanisms that otherwise project onto nearly Gaussian, adiabatic, scale-invariant observables?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in [2], which emphasizes features in primordial correlation functions as discriminants among parent theories.

questions.question: How can CMB temperature-polarization bispectrum estimators and LSS bispectrum estimators be cross-calibrated so that a future f_NL detection is robust to estimator choices and foreground-biased signals?
questions.rationale: Planck's separable, binned, and modal estimator consistency tests in [1] and the LSS promise discussed in [3] motivate this cross-calibration problem.

node_04c7f56a6154.summary: This cluster centers on the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure, using loop calculations, bias expansions, IR resummation, redshift-space modeling, and simulations to predict galaxy clustering observables.

questions.question: Can the EFTofLSS bias expansion remain finite-parameter and predictive for next-generation galaxy clustering when nonlocal-in-time bias, redshift-space distortions, short-scale counterterms, and IR-resummed BAO effects are all varied in the likelihood?
questions.rationale: This combines the bias review, full BOSS power-spectrum modeling, IR resummation, and nonlocal-in-time bias formulation [1,2,4,5].

questions.question: Which combination of one-loop power-spectrum multipoles and bias parameters most robustly breaks degeneracies among A_s, Omega_m, H0, neutrino mass assumptions, and fixed primordial-spectrum inputs in BOSS-like analyses?
questions.rationale: This follows from the BOSS EFTofLSS analyses that scan cosmologies and measure A_s, Omega_m, and H0 under specified priors and fixed inputs [2,3].

questions.question: Can Lagrangian IR resummation remove the residual BAO-scale disagreement with simulations at the percent level without importing significant simulation calibration into the EFTofLSS prediction?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the IR-resummed EFTofLSS result identifying BAO-related residuals and the BOSS analysis emphasizing validation with limited simulation input [3,4].

node_a3dd8093304d.summary: These works study squeezed-limit bispectra and consistency relations in single-field, non-attractor, ultra-slow-roll, and quasi-single-field inflation, clarifying when large local non-Gaussianity can arise.

questions.question: Which squeezed-limit observables can cleanly separate single-field consistency-relation effects from quasi-single-field massive-isocurvature exchange and multifield transfer of non-Gaussianity?
questions.rationale: Quasi-single-field and multifield models generate large bispectra through massive isocurvature modes or transfer from isocurvature to adiabatic fluctuations [1][2].

questions.question: How should late-time coordinate effects in CMB bispectra and scale-dependent halo bias be incorporated before interpreting a squeezed-limit signal as a violation of Maldacena's single-field relation?
questions.rationale: The observed-squeezed-limit framework uses Fermi and conformal Fermi coordinates to relate primordial bispectra to late-time observables and recover the single-field squeezed result [4].

node_efa3adaa7f55.summary: This cluster explores alternatives to purely inflaton-generated curvature perturbations, especially curvaton, mixed inflaton-curvaton, isocurvature, and spectator-field mechanisms for producing primordial fluctuations.

questions.question: What pattern of correlated isocurvature perturbations and primordial non-Gaussianity would uniquely identify a curvaton or modulus-sourced curvature perturbation rather than an inflaton-generated one?
questions.rationale: This follows from the curvaton conversion mechanism and correlated isocurvature in [1], the modulus effects on the CMB in [2] and [4], and the second-order non-Gaussianity calculation in [3].

questions.question: Can a spectator vector field generate the observed curvature perturbation without producing unacceptable statistical anisotropy, given the required tachyonic mass during inflation and positive oscillatory mass afterward?
questions.rationale: The mass-sign change, pressureless oscillation, and anisotropy concerns are the central conditions of the vector-curvaton proposal in [5].

node_57ccb03801b9.summary: These papers focus on curvaton model building in supersymmetric and Peccei-Quinn settings, including curvaton dynamics, decay, isocurvature constraints, and predicted non-Gaussianity.

questions.question: In supersymmetric curvaton or moduli models, what decay and thermalization conditions guarantee complete erasure of residual isocurvature while preserving the observed curvature perturbation?
questions.rationale: The curvaton mechanism in [1] removes isocurvature only if the curvaton fully decays into thermalized radiation, while [2] and [4] emphasize correlated adiabatic-isocurvature mixtures from moduli decay.

questions.question: Can second-order non-Gaussianity distinguish a curvaton that dominates before decay from one that only partially contributes to the curvature perturbation?
questions.rationale: The exact second-order non-Gaussianity expression in [3] is especially relevant when the curvaton dominates the energy density before decay.

questions.question: How far can the curvaton hypothesis relax slow-roll and inflation-scale constraints before CMB isocurvature and high-multipole signatures exclude the resulting supersymmetric model space?
questions.rationale: The curvaton hypothesis relaxes slow-roll model building in [5], while [2] shows that moduli-induced correlated perturbations alter CMB constraints and high-multipole power.

node_b0585b2cdaa2.summary: This cluster studies vector and two-form fields during or after inflation as sources of curvature perturbations, statistical anisotropy, anisotropic non-Gaussianity, and vector-curvaton phenomenology.

questions.question: Can vector-curvaton models generate an acceptably isotropic power spectrum while preserving the distinctive anisotropic bispectrum predicted when the vector remains light after inflation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the vector-curvaton curvature-perturbation mechanism in [1] and the anisotropic spectrum and bispectrum predictions in [5].

questions.question: What observational combination of scalar anisotropy, tensor modes, and non-Gaussianity can distinguish vector-impurity anisotropic inflation from spectator-field tensor enhancement?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by vector-induced anisotropic expansion and tensor production in [2] and the spectator-field tensor enhancement mechanism in [3].

questions.question: Are prolonged anisotropic inflationary solutions in vector-field and solid-inflation models governed by a common failure mode of cosmic no-hair assumptions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the vector-impurity violation of isotropic expansion in [2] and the scalar-field solid-inflation example evading cosmic no-hair conditions in [4].

node_87bdb230fcfe.summary: These works develop analytic, bootstrap, Schwinger-Keldysh, Mellin-space, and de Sitter QFT tools for computing inflationary correlation functions and their massive-particle signatures.

questions.question: Can cosmological bootstrap constraints from symmetry, singularities, locality, and unitarity determine quasi-de Sitter correlators beyond tree-level exchange diagrams computed in the in-in formalism?
questions.rationale: The question links loop-level in-in correlations in [1] with the bootstrap program for contact and exchange correlators in [3] and [S1].

questions.question: How model-independent are squeezed-limit mass, spin, angular, and phase signatures of Hubble-scale particles when inflationary interactions break approximate conformal symmetry?
questions.rationale: This follows from the cosmological-collider signatures in [2], the soft-limit theorems in [4], and the EFT templates for spinning particles in [5].

node_254dca50c996.summary: This cluster focuses on deriving inflationary wavefunctions and correlators from analyticity, symmetries, factorization, singularities, Mellin representations, and loop-level in-in formalisms.

questions.question: Can loop-level in-in inflationary correlators be bootstrapped from analyticity, locality, unitarity, and singularity structure with the same predictive control now available for tree-level exchange?
questions.rationale: This follows from the extension of in-in calculations to loop graphs and the Snowmass emphasis on singularities and unitarity as future bootstrap directions [1,S1].

questions.question: What is the minimal set of scalar seed correlators and weight-shifting operators needed to generate all slow-roll correlators with massless external spin-1 and spin-2 fields and massive spinning exchange?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the reduction of correlators to scalar exchange seeds and the use of spin-raising and weight-raising operators for spinning and massless external fields [4,5].

questions.question: How far can soft-limit theorems constrain the spectrum of additional light fields during inflation once quasi-single-field dynamics and nonperturbative bootstrap formulations are included?
questions.rationale: The question derives from universal soft-limit theorems as probes of additional light fields and the Snowmass discussion of nonperturbative bootstrap formulations [3,S1].

node_47c9526d78d4.summary: These papers address infrared divergences, secular growth, stochastic inflation, large-N resummation, Schwinger-Dyson equations, and renormalization group methods for quantum fields in de Sitter space.

questions.question: Can open-EFT corrections to stochastic inflation be organized into a controlled late-time expansion that remains infrared finite beyond the simplest lambda phi^4 examples?
questions.rationale: This derives from the open-EFT derivation of corrected noise and drift in [5] and the earlier resolution of de Sitter infrared divergences for light scalar theories in [3].

questions.question: What is the precise overlap between dynamical-RG secular resummation, large-N resummation, and stochastic-inflation predictions for dynamically generated masses in de Sitter space?
questions.rationale: The comparison is motivated by the DRG resummation and large-N discussion in [2] and the nonperturbative stochastic correlation functions in [1].

questions.question: Where is the boundary between reliable semiclassical inflationary predictions and full stochastic or nonperturbative treatment for very flat or super-Planckian scalar potentials?
questions.rationale: This follows from the classicality criterion and power-spectrum suppression found in [1] and the loop-expansion breakdown diagnosed by infrared power counting in [4].

node_df22297c287e.summary: This cluster studies how massive particles present during inflation leave distinctive oscillatory or power-law imprints in primordial non-Gaussianity, potentially observable in CMB and galaxy surveys.

questions.question: How accurately can squeezed-limit power-law and oscillatory bispectrum templates disentangle the mass, spin, and quantum phase of Hubble-scale particles in realistic CMB and galaxy-survey analyses?
questions.rationale: Cosmological collider physics identifies squeezed-limit scaling, oscillations, angular dependence, and relative phase as the carriers of mass, spin, and quantum information [1].

questions.question: What is the minimal Standard Model background template set needed before claims of new cosmological-collider particles can be made robust?
questions.rationale: The Standard Model background paper argues that known particle-physics signals during inflation are a prerequisite for using non-Gaussianity to discover new physics [3].

questions.question: Can gauge-Higgs heavy-lifting scenarios yield distinguishable non-Gaussian signatures that separate standard Higgsing from curvature-induced Higgs scales during inflation?
questions.rationale: The heavy-lifting study contrasts constant Higgs scales with curvature-induced Higgs scales and their observability through primordial non-Gaussianity [5].

node_85382d752b7d.summary: These works examine the post-inflationary transfer of energy into particles through perturbative reheating, preheating, parametric resonance, non-equilibrium dynamics, and warm-inflation dissipation.

questions.question: What model-independent criterion can decide whether post-inflationary energy transfer is controlled by perturbative decay, stochastic broad parametric resonance, tachyonic instability, or later thermalization?
questions.rationale: The representative reheating papers show that the transition to a hot universe is strongly model-dependent and can proceed through multiple nonperturbative stages [1][2][5].

questions.question: What observable or theoretical result would most sharply determine the pre-nucleosynthesis maximum radiation temperature, given that low reheating temperatures can radically alter WIMP relic abundances?
questions.rationale: The low-reheat-temperature study shows that temperatures as low as the MeV scale change dark-matter production and model constraints relative to the standard freeze-out picture [4].

questions.question: Can nonlinear preheating simulations be connected quantitatively to baryogenesis, dark-matter production, and supersymmetric model constraints without relying on Born-approximation estimates of particle production?
questions.rationale: The reheating literature stresses that parametric resonance can make first-order perturbative estimates unreliable and that preheating has applications to baryogenesis, dark matter, and supersymmetry [3][5].

node_2fe08400d2a0.summary: This cluster concentrates on reheating and preheating mechanisms after inflation, including parametric resonance, tachyonic instabilities, lattice dynamics, and Higgs-inflation reheating.

questions.question: Which inflationary potentials and couplings produce preheating through broad stochastic parametric resonance or tachyonic instability while yielding a thermalization history consistent with baryogenesis, dark matter, and nucleosynthesis constraints?
questions.rationale: This derives from the broad resonance preheating dynamics in [1]-[3], the low-reheat-temperature cosmological implications in [4], and the applications reviewed in [5].

questions.question: How can lattice simulations of nonlinear inflaton decay quantify the transition from explosive particle production to a radiation era when perturbative reheating estimates fail?
questions.rationale: This follows from the failure of first-order perturbative estimates emphasized in [2] and [3] and the nonperturbative preheating stage reviewed in [5].

node_befe8f466dd7.summary: These papers study how coherent inflaton oscillations transfer energy into particles and perturbations through parametric resonance after inflation.

questions.question: What model-independent criterion determines when expanding-universe inflaton oscillations enter broad stochastic parametric resonance rather than perturbative reheating?
questions.rationale: The foundational reheating analysis found that large-amplitude inflaton oscillations in an expanding universe can produce unusually broad, stochastic resonance beyond perturbation theory [1].

questions.question: How do the resonance bands and backreaction history in lambda phi^4 plus g^2 phi^2 chi^2 theories change across arbitrary g^2/lambda once expansion, rescattering, and production of both chi and phi quanta are included?
questions.rationale: The Lamé-equation study showed a nontrivial dependence of the stability chart on g^2/lambda and provided analytic limits that invite extension beyond the idealized resonance analysis [3].

questions.question: Under what conditions do tachyonic preheating fluctuations generate lasting nonthermal phase transitions, topological defects, or secondary inflation rather than rapidly completing symmetry breaking in one oscillation?
questions.rationale: Tachyonic-preheating simulations found symmetry breaking can complete within a single oscillation, while nonthermal fluctuations from preheating may trigger new phase transitions, defects, and secondary inflation [2],[5].

node_befe8f466dd7_1.summary: This cluster focuses on preheating as a nonlinear, nonequilibrium process involving resonance structure, backreaction, curved spacetime effects, and numerical simulations.

questions.question: Can a unified analytic criterion predict when broad stochastic resonance, Lamé-band resonance, tachyonic resonance, and fermion preheating each dominate before backreaction shuts off reheating in expanding-universe simulations?
questions.rationale: This follows from the different resonance mechanisms identified in massive, quartic, trilinear, and fermionic preheating models [1][2][4][5].

questions.question: What features in the primordial power spectrum would robustly distinguish resonant particle production during inflation from nonlinear preheating after inflation?
questions.rationale: The question derives from resonant production during inflation leaving sharp power-spectrum features, contrasted with the post-inflation resonance dynamics studied in preheating [3][1].

node_bdbf7103aad1.summary: These works analyze rapid particle production from spinodal or tachyonic instabilities during symmetry breaking after hybrid, new, or related inflationary models.

questions.question: For which classes of hybrid, F-term, and D-term inflation potentials does tachyonic preheating truly complete symmetry breaking within one field oscillation once full nonlinear lattice dynamics are included?
questions.rationale: This directly extends the single-oscillation tachyonic preheating result and its application to SUSY-motivated hybrid inflation models in [1].

questions.question: How do nonthermal fluctuations generated during tachyonic or parametric preheating determine the abundance and spectrum of topological defects in subsequent phase transitions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the nonthermal phase-transition mechanism and defect production discussed in [3] and the rapid conversion of potential energy into classical waves in [2].

questions.question: Can improved lattice simulations predict a universal relation between tachyonic preheating efficiency, the early equation of state, and the onset of radiation domination before thermal equilibrium?
questions.rationale: This combines the simulation framework of LATTICEEASY in [4] with the rapid approach to radiation domination before thermalization found in [5].

node_be138a57746a.summary: This cluster develops the general theory of post-inflationary reheating, including perturbative decay, nonperturbative preheating, dissipation, and eventual thermalization.

questions.question: What model-independent criterion determines whether reheating after inflation is dominated by perturbative inflaton decay, parametric resonance, tachyonic instability, or delayed thermalization?
questions.rationale: This follows from the foundational result that reheating is strongly model-dependent and proceeds through multiple stages, with explosive decay often occurring during inflaton oscillations [1], [4].

questions.question: How can nonlinear lattice simulations of preheating be connected quantitatively to a final reheat temperature and thermal distribution before BBN?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in reviews emphasizing nonperturbative nonlinear preheating dynamics and the incomplete understanding of how the universe reaches a thermal state before nucleosynthesis [4], [5].

questions.question: How robust are dark-matter and baryogenesis predictions when the maximum radiation-era temperature is far below the conventional freeze-out temperature?
questions.rationale: This derives from the low-reheat-temperature study showing that WIMP abundances can differ drastically from standard freeze-out expectations even when the reheat temperature is below the freeze-out scale [3].

node_85aebd98e265.summary: These papers investigate dark matter created purely through gravitational effects during inflation, reheating, or thermal gravitational annihilation.

questions.question: How robust are gravitationally produced superheavy relic abundances against realistic reheating histories and inflationary transitions beyond idealized matter- or radiation-dominated post-inflationary phases?
questions.rationale: This follows from the abundance estimates for superheavy particles produced by expansion at the end of inflation in [1] and the model-dependent numerical WIMPZILLA study in [5].

questions.question: Can the inflationary-fluctuation mechanism for massive vector dark matter be distinguished from Stueckelberg-vector misalignment using the predicted power-spectrum shape, isocurvature suppression, mass-Hubble relation, and kinetic-mixing signatures?
questions.rationale: The question combines the peaked vector power spectrum and abundance relation in [2] with the Stueckelberg light-vector condensate and kinetic-mixing phenomenology in [3].

questions.question: Can models that tie inflation to neutrino masses and baryogenesis coexist with purely gravitational dark-matter production without spoiling the claimed independence from non-gravitational production details?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the common-source nuMSM inflation and sterile-neutrino dark-matter construction in [4] and the non-gravitational-independence claim for superheavy production in [1].

node_85aebd98e265_1.summary: This cluster studies minimal dark matter scenarios where relic abundance arises from gravity alone, including scalar, fermion, vector, and superheavy candidates.

questions.question: How model-independent is the predicted abundance of superheavy gravitationally produced dark matter once the inflation-to-reheating transition is varied beyond idealized matter- or radiation-dominated histories?
questions.rationale: This is based on the claim that particles with masses near the inflaton scale can be produced in cosmologically relevant abundance largely independently of nongravitational details [1], and on numerical studies across inflation models [4].

questions.question: Can the distinctive intermediate-wavelength power spectrum of inflationary vector dark matter be used to separate purely gravitational vector production from misalignment or dark-Higgs parametric resonance histories?
questions.rationale: This follows from the peaked vector spectrum and suppressed long-wavelength isocurvature found for inflationary vector production [2], contrasted with dark-Higgs resonance production requiring separate transverse and longitudinal dynamics [5].

questions.question: What observational signatures remain for ultralight vector dark matter if its relic density is fixed only by inflationary fluctuations or Stueckelberg misalignment and kinetic mixing is strongly bounded?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the light-vector condensate scenario and its kinetic-mixing bounds and signatures [3].

node_04050aaa2ef5.summary: These works examine how evolving spacetime, metric perturbations, and oscillating backgrounds produce dark-sector particles during and after inflation.

questions.question: What features of the inflation-to-oscillation transition determine whether purely gravitational dark matter heavier than the Hubble scale but lighter than the inflaton is abundantly produced?
questions.rationale: Purely gravitational dark-matter studies emphasized efficient production for masses above the inflationary Hubble scale but below the inflaton mass during the transition and oscillation epochs [2].

questions.question: How do spin, longitudinal vector modes, and reheating history change the predicted abundance and momentum spectrum of purely gravitational fermion and vector dark matter?
questions.rationale: A systematic analysis of fermionic and vectorial gravitational dark matter and a dark-photon calculation both track production and evolution through reheating [1].

questions.question: Can oscillations of the Hubble parameter or scale factor in extended gravity models generate observable dark radiation, moduli, or gravitational-wave relics without direct non-gravitational couplings?
questions.rationale: Oscillating backgrounds in Einstein and extended gravity were shown to produce particles with implications for dark matter, radiation, moduli, and other cosmological relics [3].

node_3030f0264871.summary: This cluster emphasizes superheavy and vector dark matter generated by inflationary fluctuations, tachyonic enhancement, nonminimal gravity couplings, or inflaton interactions.

questions.question: For massive vector dark matter produced by inflationary fluctuations, how robust is the predicted abundance relation between m and H_I once reheating dynamics and the transition from inflation to radiation or matter domination are varied across inflation models?
questions.rationale: The precise mass-Hubble abundance prediction in [2] must be reconciled with the inflation-model dependence of gravitational superheavy production studied in [1] and [4].

questions.question: Can the transverse and longitudinal spectra from dark-Higgs parametric resonance be matched onto late-time pressureless vector dark matter without generating excluded isocurvature or anisotropic stress?
questions.rationale: The distinct transverse and longitudinal mode equations in [5] make this a technical extension of the isocurvature suppression result for inflationary vector production in [2].

questions.question: What observable signatures distinguish a Stueckelberg vector condensate produced by misalignment from an inflationary-fluctuation vector whose spectrum is peaked at intermediate wavelengths?
questions.rationale: The Stueckelberg misalignment scenario and kinetic-mixing signatures in [3] are conceptually distinct from the peaked inflationary spectrum of [2].

node_d8ce5693cc1d.summary: These papers propose models in which the inflaton also accounts for dark matter, often linking inflation to neutrino masses, reheating, or Standard Model extensions.

questions.question: Can light-inflaton models that mix with the Higgs simultaneously satisfy CMB constraints, reheating requirements, and rare kaon or B-meson decay limits?
questions.rationale: This follows from light-inflaton models where the Higgs portal controls both reheating and collider production, with searches in kaon and B decays [2], [5].

questions.question: How does the inflaton potential power Phi^k determine whether dark matter production is controlled by the maximum post-inflation temperature or by the reheating temperature?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the systematic reheating analysis showing that dark matter production depends strongly on the inflaton potential and on Tmax for k greater than 2 [3].

questions.question: Can a single low-scale extension such as the nuMSM plus inflaton explain inflation, sterile-neutrino dark matter, baryogenesis, and neutrino oscillation data without introducing additional high scales?
questions.rationale: This derives from the enlarged nuMSM construction that links inflation, electroweak symmetry breaking, right-handed neutrino masses, dark matter, and baryon asymmetry [1].

node_cf235426dbc4.summary: This cluster explores warm inflation, where dissipative particle production sustains a radiation bath during inflation and alters perturbation predictions.

questions.question: What microphysical criteria determine whether a warm-inflation model remains in a controlled near-thermal, adiabatic nonequilibrium regime throughout the observable e-folds?
questions.rationale: [1] reviews finite-temperature real-time derivations of dissipation and stochastic fluctuations, while [2] stresses that warm inflation is well defined only when departures from equilibrium and macroscopic motion are sufficiently adiabatic.

questions.question: Can strong dissipative warm inflation be realized with a natural particle spectrum that avoids the very large field multiplicities required in early multi-field constructions?
questions.rationale: [2] gives an existence proof but requires more than 10^4 fields, motivating the model-building problem addressed in [1] and [5].

questions.question: How generic is the warm-little-inflaton mechanism for protecting the inflaton potential from both quadratic divergences and leading thermal corrections while retaining nonlocal dissipation and Planck-compatible perturbations?
questions.rationale: [4] realizes warm inflation with a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone inflaton protected from leading thermal corrections and obtains Planck-compatible predictions from dissipative dynamics.

node_7664a171756a.summary: These works use CMB observables and reheating parameters such as duration, temperature, and equation of state to constrain inflationary models.

questions.question: What combination of spectral tilt, tensor amplitude, and model evidence would make reheating constraints decisive rather than primarily a prior choice over N_k, w_re, and T_re?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the use of reheating duration, temperature, and equation of state to constrain single-field models and from the model-evidence analysis over many inflationary potentials [4].

questions.question: Can CMB-derived limits on w_re and T_re robustly distinguish canonical w_re = 0 reheating from the negative-w_re reheating required by some monomial or axion-monodromy potentials?
questions.rationale: The question comes from the result that alpha = 1 and alpha = 2/3 potentials require more exotic reheating unless n_s shifts, while natural inflation constraints depend on reasonable w_re ranges [1].

questions.question: In Palatini R^2 and nonminimally coupled Higgs-like inflation, how much of model viability is controlled by the scalar power spectrum rather than by unspecified reheating microphysics?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the Palatini R^2 analysis, which emphasizes severe scalar-power-spectrum constraints while not specifying a reheating mechanism [5].

node_3888821e803e.summary: This cluster centers on Higgs inflation and related nonminimally coupled models, including vacuum stability, unitarity, and observational predictions.

questions.question: What UV-completion assumptions are minimally sufficient to make Higgs inflation predictive above the cutoff scale associated with a large nonminimal coupling?
questions.rationale: This targets the central tension between the effective-field-theory consistency argument in [4] and the naturalness and cutoff critique in [5].

questions.question: Can observations of n_s and r distinguish Standard Model Higgs inflation from conformal or alpha-attractor models whose predictions converge through geometric flattening of the scalar potential?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Higgs-inflation prediction framework of [1], the alpha-attractor relation for n_s and r in [2], and the universality mechanism in conformal inflation in [3].

questions.question: During reheating and the post-inflationary evolution, does the background-dependent cutoff remain above all relevant dynamical scales once loop corrections are included consistently?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the background-dependent validity domain and loop-correction scheme discussed for Higgs inflation in [4].

node_effaee558cb2.summary: These papers develop and scrutinize Standard Model Higgs inflation with large nonminimal gravity coupling, including radiative corrections, mass constraints, naturalness, and unitarity completion.

questions.question: What UV-completion assumptions are required to connect the Standard Model Higgs potential above M_P/xi to inflationary field values without spoiling background-dependent EFT consistency?
questions.rationale: This follows from the EFT consistency argument in [2] and the naturalness and cutoff objection in [3].

questions.question: How stable are Higgs-inflation predictions for n_s, r, and allowed Higgs/top mass windows under two-loop effective-potential corrections, running Planck-mass effects, and Einstein- versus Jordan-frame renormalization prescriptions?
questions.rationale: This combines the two-loop Higgs-mass and frame-dependence analysis in [4] with the running-coupling and running-Planck-mass treatment in [5].

questions.question: Can reheating in nonminimally coupled Higgs inflation be computed within the same cutoff hierarchy that keeps the inflationary epoch under EFT control?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the claim in [2] that the cutoff remains above relevant dynamical scales throughout inflation and reheating.

node_33f2694561de.summary: This cluster centers on Higgs-driven inflation and how loop corrections, Higgs-top masses, criticality, and cutoff assumptions determine its viability and CMB predictions.

questions.question: What ultraviolet-completion-independent observables, if any, can make Higgs inflation predictive when the inflationary field range lies above the cutoff scale m_p/xi?
questions.rationale: The naturalness critique argues that extrapolating the Standard Model Higgs potential above Lambda = m_p/xi is unwarranted without microscopic input [2].

questions.question: Can a renormalization prescription be formulated in which the Einstein-frame and Jordan-frame treatments give demonstrably scheme-stable predictions for n_s and r once two-loop running is included?
questions.rationale: The two-loop analysis found that Higgs-inflation predictions depend on the renormalization procedure associated with the Einstein and Jordan frames [3].

questions.question: How do the measured Higgs and top masses place the Standard Model near or away from the critical region where radiative running sharply changes Higgs-inflation predictions?
questions.rationale: Running-inflation analyses found a sharply varying relation among n_s, the Higgs mass, and the top mass near m_h around 120-135 GeV [4].

node_03ae5c5f7145.summary: These works analyze perturbative unitarity problems in Higgs inflation and propose or test UV completions, Palatini variants, and derivative-coupling models that raise the cutoff.

questions.question: Which scattering amplitudes in Higgs inflation provide the frame-independent diagnostic of the background-dependent cutoff across vacuum, inflation, and reheating?
questions.rationale: The consistency analysis argues that the cutoff depends on the background Higgs field and remains above relevant dynamical scales, while the rebuttal finds unitarity problems in both Einstein and Jordan frames [1,2].

questions.question: What assumptions on the UV completion are actually necessary to connect low-energy Standard Model parameters to inflationary observables in metric Higgs inflation?
questions.rationale: The EFT treatment of loop corrections explicitly states that additional UV-completion assumptions are needed to connect electroweak physics to inflationary predictions [1].

questions.question: Can Palatini Higgs inflation and sigma-field unitarization be experimentally or theoretically distinguished if both raise the cutoff above the Hubble scale during inflation?
questions.rationale: One extension unitarizes Higgs inflation with a real scalar sigma up to the Planck scale, while the Palatini formulation claims a parametrically higher cutoff than the Hubble rate [3,4].

node_7eb72b6f8aad.summary: This cluster studies inflationary models with scalar-curvature couplings in metric versus Palatini gravity, often adding R-squared terms or scale-invariant dynamics to alter predictions.

questions.question: What is the precise strong-coupling cutoff of Palatini nonminimal inflation once scalar self-interactions, derivative couplings, and possible R^2 terms are treated in the same frame-independent EFT?
questions.rationale: Breakdown near M_Pl/xi from scalar self-interactions is argued in [2], while metric-Palatini predictions differ because of their distinct xi dependence in [4].

questions.question: Can future measurements of r, n_s, and running distinguish metric, Palatini, and F(R) reconstructions when all are tuned to current Planck-compatible regions?
questions.rationale: Metric and Palatini formulations give different inflationary parameters in [4], and F(R) reconstruction is compared with Planck and BICEP2 data in [5].

questions.question: Are large Palatini nonminimal couplings radiatively stable in Higgs-like inflation once the conditions for avoiding dangerous quantum corrections are extended beyond the pure kinetic and gravity sectors?
questions.rationale: Radiative stability is claimed for a special derivative Higgs-gravity coupling in [1], while quantum consistency concerns for nonminimal scalar inflation are analyzed in [2].

node_205621431bcc.summary: These papers focus on Palatini formulations with R-squared or modified-gravity terms, exploring how independent connections, scalar couplings, and induced Planck scales reshape inflation and quintessence.

questions.question: In Palatini inflation with an R2 term and nonminimally coupled scalars, which combinations of scalar potential, nonminimal coupling, and R2 coefficient remain distinguishable once ns, r, and running are matched to current CMB data?
questions.rationale: This follows from the different metric versus Palatini dependence on the nonminimal coupling and from Palatini R2 models coupled to quadratic, induced-gravity, Higgs-like, and Coleman-Weinberg scalars [2], [4].

questions.question: Can the absence of a propagating scalaron in Palatini R2 gravity be turned into a robust diagnostic that separates Palatini inflation from metric Starobinsky-like models in reheating or perturbation observables?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the statement that the Palatini Starobinsky model alone does not inflate because its R2 term lacks a propagating scalar degree of freedom [4].

questions.question: How strongly must higher polynomial f(R) terms be suppressed in Palatini nonminimal inflation once loop-motivated Rn corrections and physical scalar couplings are included simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This extends the finding that polynomial f(R) inflation requires exponentially suppressed Rn coefficients when confronted with Planck-era constraints [5].

node_c232f7bd6830.summary: This cluster examines broad single-field inflation models with scalar-curvature or derivative nonminimal couplings, showing how such couplings flatten potentials and improve agreement with observations.

questions.question: What nonminimal coupling functions K(phi) and potentials V(phi) satisfy the asymptotic flattening condition V(phi)/K(phi)^2 while remaining under perturbative control during the full inflationary trajectory?
questions.rationale: General nonminimal-coupling inflation found that a flat potential is obtainable only when V(phi)/K(phi)^2 is asymptotically constant, while quantum consistency can fail near M_pl/xi in some models [2][4].

questions.question: Can derivative coupling to the Einstein tensor provide gravitational friction for Higgs or natural inflation without introducing hidden degrees of freedom or dangerous radiative corrections?
questions.rationale: Derivative-coupling models were proposed as unique interactions that preserve the degree-of-freedom count, improve slow roll, and avoid dangerous quantum corrections [1][3].

questions.question: How do trace-anomaly effects determine the graceful exit and parameter viability of de Sitter or quasi-de Sitter inflation in modified-gravity realizations such as f(T), R^2 gravity, and bigravity?
questions.rationale: The trace-anomaly study found that anomaly-induced instabilities can end de Sitter inflation in f(T) gravity and affect the viable parameter regions of higher-derivative gravity and bigravity [5].

node_fd7d7d9c36c7.summary: These papers develop alpha-attractor inflation in supergravity and related frameworks, emphasizing universal predictions controlled by hyperbolic field-space geometry and robust against potential details.

questions.question: What observation or theoretical consistency condition would most directly falsify the claim that a second-order pole in the Einstein-frame kinetic term is the common origin of alpha-, conformal-, xi-, and universal attractor predictions?
questions.rationale: The unity-of-attractors paper identifies a second-order kinetic pole as the shared source of attractor behavior across these inflationary model classes [4].

questions.question: How far can alpha-attractor universality survive corrections to the hyperbolic Kahler geometry, reheating uncertainties, and strong deformations of the scalar potential while maintaining predictions for ns and r?
questions.rationale: Alpha-attractor and conformal-inflation papers attribute stable predictions to Kahler curvature, exponential moduli-space stretching, and robustness under potential deformations [1][2].

questions.question: Can the initial-condition problem for Planck-favored attractor models be resolved without relying on eternal-inflation arguments or transmuting generic potentials into hilltop regimes?
questions.rationale: The Planck-era review highlights initial conditions for favored attractor theories, while hilltop inflation argues for generic observable inflation near a potential maximum [3][5].

node_a2f04dc2fda5.summary: This cluster investigates how electroweak vacuum metastability, Higgs and top masses, curvature effects, reheating, and high-scale inflation constrain the survival of our vacuum.

questions.question: What precise combination of Higgs mass, top Yukawa coupling, reheating temperature, and Higgs-curvature or Higgs-inflaton coupling determines whether inflationary fluctuations seed lethal anti-de Sitter patches?
questions.rationale: The cosmological vacuum-instability analysis derived inflationary Hubble bounds that depend on reheating and Higgs couplings to curvature or the inflaton [2].

questions.question: Can RG-generated curvature corrections during high-scale inflation robustly stabilize the Higgs potential, or does the answer depend too sensitively on the electroweak-scale value of the nonminimal coupling xi?
questions.rationale: One-loop curvature corrections can either stabilize or destabilize the Higgs during high-scale inflation depending on the RG-running value of xi [4].

questions.question: Is metastable Higgs inflation viable after gravitational corrections and matching near M_P/xi are included, or do cosmological perturbation constraints rule out the required fine-tuned potentials?
questions.rationale: Metastable Higgs inflation can survive through matching effects near M_P/xi, while gravitationally corrected Standard Model inflation was found inconsistent with observed perturbations [3] and [5].

node_8d6b4ca7de9d.summary: These works explore cosmological evolution in extra-dimensional brane models, including Randall-Sundrum scenarios, radion stabilization, modified Friedmann equations, and brane-driven inflation.

questions.question: Can radion-stabilization mechanisms generically recover ordinary four-dimensional FRW cosmology while preserving the hierarchy-solving features of Randall-Sundrum compactification?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Goldberger-Wise stabilization mechanism and the claim that stabilized compact brane models reproduce ordinary FRW evolution without brane-density constraints [1,3].

questions.question: What early-universe observables could distinguish the faster-than-standard high-energy brane expansion from conventional cosmology while remaining compatible with nucleosynthesis?
questions.rationale: The question follows from modified brane Friedmann equations that can allow normal nucleosynthesis-era expansion but faster very-early expansion [4].

questions.question: Under what conditions can brane separation drive enough inflation in low-scale quantum-gravity models without creating the cosmological pathologies found in some localized-gravity scenarios?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in brane inflation from displaced branes and the viability problems identified for certain five-dimensional localized-gravity cosmologies [2,5].

node_f25d3f0140aa.summary: This cluster focuses on five-dimensional braneworld cosmologies and the conditions under which brane expansion, bulk stress-energy, compactification, and thick-brane effects reproduce standard cosmology.

questions.question: What minimal set of brane and bulk stress-energy ingredients is sufficient to recover standard H proportional to sqrt(rho) cosmology through nucleosynthesis while allowing genuinely five-dimensional expansion at earlier times?
questions.rationale: This question is based on the H proportional to rho problem and its remedy using brane and bulk cosmological constants in [1], and the radiation-era expansion analysis in [5].

questions.question: Can the non-compact localized-gravity scenario be made cosmologically viable without inheriting the contracting-universe pathology found in the compact hierarchy-motivated setup?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from [2], which finds the non-compact fifth dimension potentially viable but the hierarchy-solving scenario cosmologically problematic.

questions.question: Where does the low-energy three-brane effective field theory break down in cosmological settings where the brane thickness, chiral fermion localization, or internal brane structure becomes dynamically relevant?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [4], which gives a finite-domain EFT for fluctuating 3-branes and notes that it fails when the internal structure of the brane is resolved, and from the shell-universe thickness scale in [3].

node_0c10a1023014.summary: These papers study stabilization of the Randall-Sundrum modulus or radion, its cosmological dynamics, effective couplings, phase transitions, and phenomenological signatures.

questions.question: What class of radion stabilization potentials yields ordinary four-dimensional FRW cosmology without fine tuning when both branes carry time-dependent matter densities?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Goldberger-Wise bulk-scalar stabilization mechanism in [1] and the recovery of conventional FRW expansion once the radius is stabilized in [2].

questions.question: In which stabilized-modulus regimes is the radion generically lighter than the lowest Kaluza-Klein modes, and how would its TeV-scale couplings modify early-universe phenomenology?
questions.rationale: This question is based on [3], which finds that a small bulk scalar mass can make the radion the first direct signature with couplings fixed by four-dimensional covariance.

questions.question: Can inflation with a static or initially small extra dimension be consistently matched onto radion stabilization while preserving the hierarchy solution and COBE-normalized perturbations?
questions.rationale: This connects the static extra-dimensional inflationary solutions in [4], rapid asymmetric inflation with small extra dimensions in [5], and stabilization of the compactification scale in [1].

node_f6dca36dc4d3.summary: This cluster examines brane-world and Gauss-Bonnet-assisted inflation models, including low-scale gravity, chaotic or natural potentials, Higgs variants, and compatibility with CMB data.

questions.question: Which CMB observable would most decisively distinguish brane-assisted slow roll from ordinary four-dimensional chaotic inflation when the high-energy Friedmann equation modifies damping and perturbation tilt?
questions.rationale: Modified brane Friedmann dynamics assist slow roll and drive perturbations toward scale invariance in [2].

questions.question: Can tachyon-assisted inflation on stacks of unstable branes produce viable reheating and scalar perturbations without relying on fine-tuned noninteracting tachyon sectors?
questions.rationale: Assisted tachyon condensation and multi-tachyon inflation are proposed to overcome the steep single-tachyon potential in [3] and [4].

questions.question: Are Gauss-Bonnet bounce reconstructions dynamically stable enough to unify an early bounce with late-time acceleration while remaining compatible with inflationary constraints?
questions.rationale: Modified F(G) gravity is reconstructed to realize stable bouncing, ekpyrotic, and late-acceleration solutions in [5].

node_88634f90d8be.summary: This cluster surveys possible time or space variation of fundamental couplings, linking observational bounds on constants to scalar-field and screened modified-gravity models.

questions.question: What observational combination would turn current bounds on varying constants into a model-discriminating test of scalar-field dynamics rather than a collection of separately parametrized limits?
questions.rationale: The need follows from the review of fine-structure, mass-ratio, and interaction-coupling constraints with their underlying hypotheses [1].

questions.question: Can chameleon or symmetron screening constraints from laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological probes be recast into a common parameterization without losing the environmental physics of screening?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the review's observation that screening searches are often presented in different parametrizations, complicating comparison across probes [2].

questions.question: Which future experiment can most directly test strongly matter-coupled light scalars that evade inverse-square-law, equivalence-principle, Casimir, BBN, and CMB constraints?
questions.rationale: The question follows from chameleon scalar models that can couple more strongly than gravity while remaining light and experimentally viable [4], together with inverse-square-law constraints on scalar and vector exchange forces [3].

node_88634f90d8be_1.summary: These papers examine theoretical motivations and observational constraints on changing fundamental constants such as alpha, particle masses, and QCD scales.

questions.question: Are reported variations of alpha better interpreted as true cosmological time evolution, environmental density dependence, or correlated changes among several dimensionless constants?
questions.rationale: This question follows from the observational-status review emphasizing underlying hypotheses in [1] and the density-dependent scalar models in [3].

questions.question: Can Oklo, atomic spectroscopy, and astrophysical measurements be combined without hidden nuclear-structure assumptions into a common likelihood for Delta alpha and Delta(m_p/m_e)?
questions.rationale: This derives from the reanalysis of Oklo resonance constraints and their nuclear and temperature uncertainties in [2], together with the comparison problem highlighted in [1].

questions.question: What pattern of slow drift plus oscillatory modulation in fundamental constants would uniquely identify quadratic couplings of scalar or pseudoscalar dark matter to photons, electrons, and light quarks?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dark-matter-induced slow and oscillating variations constrained by BBN and dysprosium spectroscopy in [4].

node_139c759784d2.summary: This cluster focuses on how unified gauge theories relate variation of the fine-structure constant to other couplings and how clocks, CMB, Oklo, and astrophysical data constrain it.

questions.question: Which correlated pattern of variations in alpha, Lambda_QCD, weak couplings, Yukawa couplings, and the electroweak scale would most sharply discriminate gauge-unified varying-constant models from single-parameter alpha variation?
questions.rationale: This follows from the gauge-unification claim that alpha variation should be accompanied by significant and calculable variations of Lambda_QCD and possibly other couplings [3,5].

questions.question: Can the Oklo resonance-energy constraint be reformulated to separate electromagnetic and strong-coupling variations without relying on overly rigid nuclear-model assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the revised Oklo analyses emphasizing reactor-temperature uncertainty, rare-earth isotope data, isotope shifts, and nuclear-interaction assumptions [2,4].

questions.question: What single observational cross-check between atomic clocks, CMB or astrophysical spectra, and nuclear bounds would most directly test the hidden hypotheses behind claimed variations of fundamental constants?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review's emphasis that different measurements constrain constants only through specific metrological and theoretical assumptions that must be compared consistently [1].

node_efe7e501f211.summary: These works study scalar-field, quintessence, dark-matter, and extra-dimensional mechanisms for fine-structure constant evolution and confront them with cosmological and laboratory limits.

questions.question: How can laboratory equivalence-principle tests, atomic-clock or dysprosium spectroscopy, BBN, and astrophysical spectra be combined to distinguish time evolution of alpha from environmental density dependence of scalar-mediated couplings?
questions.rationale: Density-dependent couplings are proposed in [1], dark-matter-driven oscillating and slow variations are constrained in [2], and joint laboratory-astrophysical searches are reviewed in [5].

questions.question: Can a scalar field that drives apparent alpha variation also act as quintessence without violating fifth-force bounds once couplings to baryons, dark matter, and the cosmological constant are all included?
questions.rationale: The link between varying alpha, ultralight scalars, fifth forces, and quintessence is made in [3], while dark-matter and cosmological-constant couplings are added in [4].

node_7b1f840b242c.summary: This cluster studies chameleon, symmetron, and Vainshtein screening mechanisms that hide fifth forces while remaining testable in laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological settings.

questions.question: What common parametrization can compare laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological constraints on chameleon and symmetron screening without hiding model-dependent assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review's observation that screened-gravity searches are often presented in different parametrizations that are difficult to compare [1].

questions.question: Can atom interferometry in ultra-high vacuum close the strongest remaining window for light dark-energy scalars that evade bulk fifth-force tests through environmental screening?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the cesium atom-interferometry constraint strategy that reduces screening by using individual atoms near a source mass [4].

questions.question: How strongly can scalar fields couple to matter while remaining consistent with inverse-square-law, Casimir, compact-object, BBN, and CMB bounds once nonlinear self-interactions are included?
questions.rationale: This derives from the result that strongly matter-coupled chameleon fields can evade multiple terrestrial, astrophysical, and cosmological constraints [3].

node_76b6902a0a35.summary: These papers use global and fluctuating 21 cm signals, especially the EDGES anomaly, to constrain dark matter scattering, annihilation, decay, and dark-sector interactions.

questions.question: Can global and fluctuating 21 cm measurements break degeneracies between dark-matter annihilation, decay, and baryon-scattering explanations of altered thermal histories during cosmic dawn?
questions.rationale: This combines the Planck annihilation framework in [1], electromagnetic energy-injection constraints in [4], and baryon-cooling minicharged dark matter scenario in [3].

questions.question: What SKA measurement of cosmic dawn or reionization would most sharply improve on CMB limits on exotic electromagnetic energy injection from dark matter?
questions.rationale: The question follows from SKA's projected role in fundamental physics through cosmic dawn and reionization [2] and the CMB energy-injection bounds in [1] and [4].

questions.question: How should 21 cm constraints on dark-sector cooling be combined with Lyman-alpha limits on small-scale structure in ultralight or subcomponent dark-matter scenarios?
questions.rationale: This links the early-universe baryon-cooling sensitivity of 21 cm observations in [3] with Lyman-alpha constraints on scalar dark matter and its allowed fraction in [5].

node_c771f271185f.summary: This broad cluster covers theoretical calculations of heavy meson and baryon weak decays, including form factors, branching ratios, CKM extractions, and CP violation.

questions.question: Which combination of Belle II heavy-flavor observables would most cleanly separate CKM-fit inconsistencies from hadronic-theory uncertainties in branching ratios, CP asymmetries, and rare decays?
questions.rationale: The CKM-fit and Belle II papers emphasize that global unitarity-triangle constraints, B decay asymmetries, and high-statistics intensity-frontier data must be interpreted together with nontrivial hadronic inputs [2],[5],[S1].

questions.question: Can effective-Hamiltonian calculations beyond leading logarithms and heavy-quark effective theory reduce theoretical uncertainties enough for rare B and K decays to become unambiguous new-physics tests?
questions.rationale: The NLO weak-decay review identifies renormalization-scale ambiguities as a central uncertainty, while the heavy-quark-symmetry review focuses on symmetry-breaking corrections and form-factor calculations [1],[3].

questions.question: How can correlations among rare kaon branching ratios, q2 distributions, epsilon_K, epsilon'/epsilon, Delta M_K, and |V_cb| be used to discriminate flavor models rather than only constrain them?
questions.rationale: The rare-kaon Snowmass paper stresses that correlated observables, especially their sensitivity to |V_cb|, can help disentangle the nature of possible new physics [S3].

node_93a8cdfe22d2.summary: These works compute semileptonic heavy-meson decay form factors using lattice QCD, light-cone sum rules, and quark models to support CKM determinations.

questions.question: How can lattice-QCD, light-cone-sum-rule, and heavy-quark-effective-theory inputs be combined to reduce the dominant hadronic uncertainty in semileptonic B-meson form factors across the full q2 range?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark symmetry gives model-independent structure, while LCSR calculations identify hadronic input parameters as limiting 10 percent level form-factor uncertainties [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: Which power-suppressed soft-collinear effects in heavy-to-light currents must be parameterized before form-factor calculations can become systematically improvable beyond leading power?
questions.rationale: The SCET formulation beyond leading power was presented as a first step toward treating power corrections in hard processes without an OPE [3].

questions.question: Can quark-model form-factor parametrizations constrained by heavy-quark symmetry remain useful once LCSR and lattice inputs determine the high-recoil and low-recoil regions with comparable precision?
questions.rationale: ISGW2 improved quark-model predictions using heavy-quark-symmetry constraints and more realistic high-recoil behavior, but modern sum-rule work aims for systematically updateable inputs [2], [4].

node_94eeca1c9e88.summary: This cluster emphasizes unquenched lattice QCD calculations of B, Bs, and Lambda_b semileptonic form factors used to extract Vub and Vcb.

questions.question: Can a joint lattice-experimental fit using dispersive bounds, conformal expansions, and HQET subleading Isgur-Wise functions remove the dominant form-factor-shape uncertainty in exclusive |V_cb| from B->D and B->D* decays?
questions.rationale: This follows from the dispersive treatment of all B(*)->D(*) form factors, nonzero-recoil lattice extractions, and the combined HQET fit including O(Lambda_QCD/m_Q) uncertainties [1], [3], and [5].

questions.question: What lattice systematics in f_+(q^2) and f_0(q^2), including heavy-quark discretization, chiral-continuum extrapolation, and correlations, must be reduced before z-expansion truncation becomes negligible in |V_ub| and |V_cb| determinations?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the conformal-parametrization analysis of B->pi and the unquenched nonzero-recoil B->D lattice calculations over the full q^2 range [2], [3], and [4].
