node_94eeca1c9e88_1.summary: These papers calculate lattice-QCD form factors for B, Bs, and Lambda_b semileptonic decays across heavy-to-heavy and heavy-to-light channels.

questions.question: Can lattice calculations of B -> D(*) and B -> pi form factors be combined with dispersive z-expansion bounds to reduce the dominant |V_cb| and |V_ub| shape uncertainties across the full q^2 range?
questions.rationale: Dispersive constraints for B -> D(*) are derived in [1], and the model-independent z expansion for B -> pi is used to determine |V_ub| in [2].

questions.question: How do lattice heavy-quark actions and chiral-continuum extrapolations affect the nonzero-recoil B -> D form factors f_+(q^2) and f_0(q^2) used to extract |V_cb| and R(D)?
questions.rationale: The nonzero-recoil lattice calculations in [3] and [4] use different heavy-quark formulations and extrapolation strategies to obtain B -> D form factors.

questions.question: Can combined B -> D and B -> D* analyses include all O(Lambda_QCD/m_{c,b}) Isgur-Wise uncertainties and non-Standard-Model currents without biasing R(D(*)) predictions?
questions.rationale: The combined analysis in [5] emphasizes neglected subleading Isgur-Wise uncertainties and computes corrections for all possible b -> c currents.

node_dc03d6ac18fb.summary: This cluster focuses on lattice-QCD determinations of heavy-to-light semileptonic decay form factors such as B to pi, Bs to K, and D to K or pi.

questions.question: Can lattice-QCD heavy-to-light form-factor calculations be combined with dispersive z-expansion bounds so that truncation errors, higher resonances, and lepton-mass-suppressed form factors are propagated consistently into |V_ub| and rare-decay observables?
questions.rationale: This extends the precision dispersive corrections of [1] and the model-independent heavy-to-light bounds of [2] to the lattice form-factor program represented by [4] and [5].

questions.question: What lattice strategy can control the full q^2 dependence of B -> K* l+l- and Bs -> phi l+l- form factors, including resonance and finite-width effects, at the precision needed for Standard Model rare-decay tests?
questions.rationale: The need for accurate hadronic form factors in these rare decays is the central motivation of the lattice calculation in [5].

questions.question: How far can heavy-quark symmetry relations near zero recoil constrain heavy-to-light and baryonic lattice form factors before second-order power corrections become numerically limiting?
questions.rationale: This draws on the HQET 1/m_Q^2 formalism and zero-recoil normalization conditions in [3], together with relativistic-heavy-quark lattice form factors for Lambda_b decays in [4].

node_44b7faf2c489.summary: These works compute lattice-QCD form factors for rare and semileptonic B, Bs, and Lambda_b decays relevant to flavor-changing neutral currents and CKM physics.

questions.question: How can lattice-QCD rare-decay form factors for B → K*ℓ+ℓ− and Bs → φℓ+ℓ− be combined with dispersive bounds to control truncation errors across the full physical q2 range?
questions.rationale: Dispersive methods tighten form-factor parameterizations and truncation errors [1], while lattice calculations provide rare B and Bs form factors needed for Standard Model tests [5].

questions.question: What level of heavy-quark power corrections and current-renormalization uncertainty must be reached for baryonic Λb form factors to sharpen |Vub| and |Vcb| extractions?
questions.rationale: HQET organizes second-order 1/mQ corrections and zero-recoil constraints [3], while Λb lattice form factors are used to determine |Vub| and |Vcb| [4].

node_6b3cc0fa1240.summary: This cluster studies lattice-QCD form factors for semileptonic B and D decays into light pseudoscalar or vector mesons, with emphasis on controlling heavy-quark, chiral, and continuum systematics.

questions.question: How can lattice calculations of B -> pi l nu form factors extend precision from high q^2 toward the full kinematic range while keeping heavy-quark, chiral, and continuum extrapolation errors subdominant in |V_ub| extractions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the high-q^2 unquenched B -> pi calculation in [1] and the earlier emphasis on heavy-quark matching, lattice-spacing dependence, and kinematic cuts in [3].

questions.question: Can lattice heavy-to-light form factors and nonfactorizable low-q^2 treatments be combined consistently enough to sharpen new-physics interpretations of B -> K^* l^+ l^- angular observables?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the need to go beyond form-factor uncertainties to helicity-suppressed nonfactorizable terms in [2].

questions.question: What lattice strategy can reduce uncertainties in vector final-state form factors such as A_2 and V/A_1 enough to test heavy-quark scaling from D decays to B decays?
questions.rationale: This derives from the large uncertainties in vector-meson form factors and heavy-quark extrapolation tests reported in [5], together with the O(a)-improved calculations in [4].

node_896bad02135f.summary: This cluster uses unquenched lattice-QCD calculations of B to D, D*, and pi semileptonic form factors to extract CKM elements such as |Vcb| and |Vub| and related observables.

questions.question: Can a joint lattice-plus-dispersive analysis of B -> D and B -> D* form factors resolve whether exclusive |V_cb| is limited by zero-recoil normalization, nonzero-recoil shape, or subleading Isgur-Wise uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This combines dispersive shape bounds, nonzero-recoil lattice form factors, and the warning that subleading heavy-quark uncertainties affect combined B -> D(*) fits [1],[3],[5].

questions.question: How many z-expansion coefficients are actually required for B -> pi l nu once modern lattice correlations and unitarity constraints are treated conservatively across the full q^2 range?
questions.rationale: This derives from the model-independent conformal parametrization of f_+(q^2) and its use of unitarity to estimate truncation systematics in |V_ub| extraction [2].

questions.question: Can lattice calculations of all relevant B -> D(*) currents reduce the theory uncertainty in R(D) and R(D*) enough to distinguish Standard Model form-factor effects from new physics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by lattice determinations of B -> D form factors and combined analyses including all possible b -> c currents and subleading corrections [3],[5].

node_c897096fdbff.summary: This cluster combines lattice determinations of K and D semileptonic form factors with experimental decay data to determine |Vus|, |Vcs|, and |Vcd|.

questions.question: What lattice and experimental improvements are needed for kaon leptonic and semileptonic decays to make first-row CKM unitarity tests limited by electroweak and isospin corrections rather than by f_K/f_pi or form-factor uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This follows from the global kaon analysis in [1] and the high-precision f_K/f_pi determination and unitarity test in [3].

questions.question: Can lattice calculations of D to pi and D to K form factors at q^2=0 reduce charm-sector CKM uncertainties enough to provide a competitive, lattice-only cross-check of |V_cd| and |V_cs|?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in [2] and [5], which combine lattice D-meson form factors with experimental branching ratios to extract charm CKM elements.

questions.question: How should correlated lattice systematics from chiral extrapolation, scale setting, and physical light-quark masses be propagated in combined kaon-and-charm CKM fits?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the reduction of chiral-extrapolation errors in [2] and [5] and the physical-quark scale-setting strategy in [3].

node_3b0d4a58ecf1.summary: This cluster focuses on lattice-QCD calculations of the K to pi semileptonic vector form factor f+(0) for precision determinations of |Vus|.

questions.question: What reduction in lattice uncertainty on f_+^{K pi}(0), including controlled SU(3)-breaking and unquenching effects, is needed for K_l3 decays to dominate first-row CKM unitarity tests?
questions.rationale: The need for percent-level control of 1-f_+(0) originates in [5], while global kaon analyses use this input for stringent Standard Model tests in [1] and [4].

questions.question: Can a single lattice-QCD analysis consistently combine f_+^{K pi}(0) and f_K/f_pi with electromagnetic and isospin corrections to resolve any residual tension between leptonic and semileptonic determinations of |V_us|?
questions.rationale: The leptonic extraction in [2] and [3] and the semileptonic global analyses in [1] and [4] rely on different hadronic inputs and correction budgets.

questions.question: How should correlations among experimental kaon branching fractions, semileptonic form-factor shapes, and lattice hadronic matrix elements be propagated in future global |V_us| fits?
questions.rationale: The combined world-data analyses in [1] and [4] stress correlated experimental and theoretical constraints as central to precision |V_us| extraction.

node_6d6d33d7efe2.summary: This cluster studies lattice-QCD form factors for D to K and D to pi semileptonic decays, enabling determinations of |Vcs| and |Vcd|.

questions.question: Can lattice calculations of D to pi and D to K form factors reach sub-percent control of chiral, continuum, and current-normalization systematics needed for competitive |Vcd| and |Vcs| determinations?
questions.rationale: Early three-flavor and 2+1-flavor calculations reduced chiral extrapolation errors and combined f_+(0) with branching ratios to extract |Vcd| and |Vcs| [1], [2].

questions.question: How should z-expansion chiral-continuum fits be generalized across the full q^2 range while preserving the advantage of scalar-current determinations that avoid operator matching?
questions.rationale: The HISQ D to K study used scalar-current matrix elements requiring no operator matching and introduced a z-variable method for chiral and continuum extrapolation over all q^2 [3].

questions.question: What lattice strategy can quantify and remove hypercubic artifacts in moving-frame D to pi and D to K matrix elements without sacrificing kinematic coverage?
questions.rationale: The N_f=2+1+1 twisted-fermion calculation observed clear Lorentz-symmetry breaking from hypercubic effects in many moving and rest-frame kinematic conditions [5].

node_cf3753a0ff39.summary: This cluster develops QCD light-cone sum-rule calculations of B-meson transitions to light pseudoscalar, vector, and multipion final states for semileptonic, penguin, and radiative decays.

questions.question: Which hadronic inputs to pion, kaon, eta, and vector-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes dominate the remaining 10 percent uncertainty in B-to-light form factors, and can lattice updates reduce them coherently across channels?
questions.rationale: The LCSR calculations identify twist-2 distribution-amplitude parameters and other hadronic inputs as leading uncertainty sources for pseudoscalar and vector form factors [1][3].

questions.question: Can power-suppressed SCET currents and LCSR equation-of-motion constraints produce a systematically improvable prediction of tensor-to-vector form-factor ratios and helicity-amplitude zeros in B to K* l+l-?
questions.rationale: SCET beyond leading power addresses long-distance power corrections [2], while the B to V l+l- LCSR analysis uses equation-of-motion constraints to improve tensor-to-vector ratios and helicity-amplitude zero predictions [4].

node_cf3753a0ff39_1.summary: This cluster revisits and improves light-cone sum-rule predictions for B to pi, K, eta, rho, K*, and related form factors, including radiative and higher-twist corrections.

questions.question: How much can B-to-light pseudoscalar and vector form-factor uncertainties be reduced by combining updated twist-2 distribution-amplitude inputs with full error-correlated LCSR-lattice fits over the whole q^2 range?
questions.rationale: This combines the hadronic-input uncertainty budget and lattice-update strategy in [1] and [3] with the correlated LCSR-lattice fitting program described in [4].

questions.question: Can equations-of-motion constraints on higher-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes be turned into quantitatively stable predictions for tensor-to-vector form-factor ratios and helicity-amplitude zeroes in B -> K* l+ l-?
questions.rationale: The question follows from [4], which argues that twist-4 and twist-5 amplitudes constrained by equations of motion improve tensor-to-vector ratios and the prediction of helicity-amplitude zeroes.

questions.question: Can SCET beyond leading power provide a unified parameterization of the same symmetry-breaking and long-distance power corrections that appear in LCSR predictions for large-recoil heavy-to-light form factors?
questions.rationale: This connects the second-order SCET current and Lagrangian expansion in [2] with the perturbative symmetry-breaking corrections to large-recoil form-factor relations computed in [5].

node_cf3753a0ff39_2.summary: This cluster emphasizes light-cone sum rules using B-meson distribution amplitudes and perturbative QCD corrections to compute heavy-to-light B transition form factors.

questions.question: Can B-meson light-cone sum rules reduce heavy-to-light form-factor uncertainties below the current 10% level by combining updated distribution-amplitude inputs with lattice constraints across q^2?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the stated dominant hadronic-input uncertainties and the need to incorporate future lattice updates in pseudoscalar and vector form-factor LCSRs [1,2].

questions.question: How robust are tensor-to-vector form-factor ratios and helicity-amplitude zero predictions in B to K* l+l- once equation-of-motion constraints and full error correlations are propagated?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the claim that twist-4 and twist-5 inputs constrained by equations of motion improve tensor-to-vector ratios and helicity-zero predictions [3].

questions.question: Which heavy-quark and large-energy symmetry relations among B-to-light form factors survive radiative corrections, higher-twist terms, and SU(3)-breaking effects at phenomenological precision?
questions.rationale: This connects the LEET symmetry reduction of heavy-to-light form factors [5] with LCSR calculations including radiative, higher-twist, and SU(3)-breaking corrections [4].

node_d706b63b401c.summary: This cluster applies light-cone sum rules to D, Ds, Bc, and related charm transitions, including semileptonic decays into pseudoscalar, scalar, axial-vector, and vector mesons.

questions.question: Can LCSR determinations of D -> pi and D -> K vector and scalar form factors reduce the theory error on V_cd and V_cs enough to compete with lattice-QCD extractions across the full usable q^2 range?
questions.rationale: This follows from the updated MS charm-mass LCSR form factors and CKM extractions in [2], together with the earlier lattice and data comparison in [1].

questions.question: How sensitive are B_c semileptonic decay predictions to the modeled leading-twist charmonium and heavy-meson distribution amplitudes when chiral currents are used to suppress twist-3 contributions?
questions.rationale: The dependence on final-meson distribution amplitudes and the use of chiral currents are central to the B_c LCSR analysis in [3].

questions.question: Can NLO HQET sum-rule results for the universal tau_1/2(y) function be reconciled with LCSR heavy-quark scaling laws for scalar and vector heavy-to-light form factors?
questions.rationale: This connects the NLO QCD sum-rule calculation of tau_1/2(y) in [4] with the heavy-quark-mass and scalar-form-factor analysis in [5].

node_b1bf96d1b7ea.summary: This cluster analyzes heavy-to-light form-factor factorization at large recoil using soft-collinear effective theory, including soft overlap, endpoint behavior, symmetry relations, and power corrections.

questions.question: Can a complete subleading-power SCET factorization theorem for heavy-to-light form factors be formulated that consistently parameterizes soft-overlap long-distance effects where no local OPE exists?
questions.rationale: The unresolved problem of power-suppressed long-distance effects without an OPE motivates the second-order SCET current and Lagrangian construction in [1].

questions.question: Which symmetry-breaking alpha_s and Lambda_QCD/m_b corrections dominate the uncertainty in large-recoil B -> V l+l- observables such as the forward-backward asymmetry zero?
questions.rationale: Perturbative symmetry-breaking corrections to heavy-to-light form factors were computed and applied to the B -> V l+l- asymmetry zero and C_9 sensitivity in [2].

questions.question: How can hard-collinear matching and endpoint behavior be constrained so that universal soft form factors and hard spectator-scattering terms remain separately meaningful beyond leading power?
questions.rationale: The SCET factorization analysis separates soft, hard-collinear, and collinear modes and derives hard spectator-scattering contributions after integrating out the hard-collinear scale [5].

node_8041d9c35c94.summary: This cluster uses QCD and light-cone sum rules to compute form factors, decay widths, and branching ratios for heavy meson and baryon semileptonic or rare transitions.

questions.question: Can light-cone QCD sum rules for B to vector gamma and B to K(*) l+l- form factors be systematically matched to modern z-expansion fits so that rare-decay angular observables carry transparent hadronic uncertainties?
questions.rationale: This links the radiative B to V gamma form-factor analysis in [1], rare B to K(*) l+l- sum rules in [2], and the z-series use of light-cone sum-rule inputs in [4].

questions.question: How large are Coulomb-like alpha_s/v corrections and spin-symmetry constraints in B_c sum-rule predictions for semileptonic, nonleptonic, and lifetime-dominating exclusive modes?
questions.rationale: This follows from the B_c three-point QCD sum-rule calculation with Coulomb-like corrections and HQET/NRQCD spin relations in [3] and the broader B_c sum-rule discussion in [5].

node_1683c9b6e6b0.summary: This cluster focuses on QCD sum-rule calculations of Bc and related heavy-meson semileptonic and radiative decay form factors and branching fractions.

questions.question: How large are Coulomb-like alpha_s/v corrections in three-point QCD sum rules for Bc to Bs and Bs* semileptonic form factors away from zero recoil?
questions.rationale: Bc sum-rule calculations included Coulomb-like alpha_s/v corrections and derived HQET/NRQCD spin-symmetry relations near zero recoil [3].

questions.question: Can QCD sum-rule and potential-model inputs for Bc decay constants, radiative transitions, and exclusive decay widths be combined into a lifetime prediction with controlled duality and factorization uncertainties?
questions.rationale: Bc lifetime estimates sum dominant exclusive modes using QCD and NRQCD sum rules, while broader Bc studies combine potential models and QCD sum rules for spectroscopy and decays [4].

questions.question: Do form-factor relations known from rare and semileptonic B decays have a reliable analogue for Bc transitions with two heavy constituents and different recoil kinematics?
questions.rationale: Rare B-decay sum-rule analyses study relations among semileptonic and rare B to K(*) form factors, while Bc decays rely on heavy-quark spin-symmetry relations in a distinct heavy-heavy system [2].

node_af85b0191f2e.summary: These papers use QCD and light-cone sum rules to compute form factors and decay rates for semileptonic heavy-baryon transitions such as Lambda_b, Xi_b, and Xi_c decays.

questions.question: How can light-cone sum rules for Lambda_b to p transitions be made insensitive to negative-parity heavy-baryon contamination and interpolating-current choices?
questions.rationale: Heavy-baryon light-cone sum rules combine different kinematical structures to eliminate negative-parity contributions and reduce sensitivity to interpolating currents [2].

questions.question: Which Lambda baryon distribution amplitudes most strongly affect heavy-quark-spin-symmetry-breaking form factors in Lambda_b to Lambda gamma and Lambda_b to Lambda l+ l- decays?
questions.rationale: Higher-twist Lambda distribution amplitudes have little effect on spin-symmetry-preserving form factors but can significantly impact spin-symmetry-breaking ones [4].

questions.question: Can all twelve Lambda_b to Lambda l+ l- form factors from light-cone QCD sum rules be constrained well enough for LHCb angular and branching-ratio tests of the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: A light-cone sum-rule analysis constructed all twelve form factors for Lambda_b to Lambda l+ l- and found the branching ratio likely detectable at LHCb [5].

node_93a18e520eb1.summary: This cluster studies semileptonic, nonleptonic, and rare weak decays of heavy mesons and baryons using relativistic constituent or quasipotential quark models.

questions.question: Can relativistic quark models and HQET be matched into a common uncertainty framework for Bc semileptonic and nonleptonic form factors across the full kinematic range?
questions.rationale: Bc decay studies compute form factors from relativistic wave-function overlaps and branching ratios, while heavy-baryon and excited-meson analyses emphasize HQET symmetry structures and 1/mQ corrections [2][3][4][5].

questions.question: Which exclusive angular distributions in Bc to J/psi plus light-hadron cascades provide the cleanest experimental tests of factorization and relativistic wave-function dynamics?
questions.rationale: The Bc decay analysis gives full angular distributions for cascade modes such as Bc to J/psi rho as guidance for experimental exploration under the factorization approximation [3].

node_2d25f3272e47.summary: These works calculate form factors, branching fractions, and decay distributions for rare and weak B, B_s, and B_c meson transitions in relativistic quark models.

questions.question: Which B_c semileptonic and nonleptonic observables can most cleanly discriminate relativistic and nonrelativistic quark-model form factors across the full accessible kinematic range?
questions.rationale: This follows from relativistic and nonrelativistic B_c decay studies that compute form factors, widths, asymmetry parameters, and compare sensitivities to model assumptions [2], [4], [5].

questions.question: Can angular distributions in cascade decays such as B_c -> J/psi rho provide enough information to test factorization approximations in exclusive nonleptonic B_c decays?
questions.rationale: This derives from the explicit full angular-distribution formulas provided for B_c cascade decays within the factorizing approximation [2].

questions.question: How large are finite-mass corrections to heavy-quark spin-symmetry predictions in exclusive B and B_c transitions, and which helicity channels expose them most directly?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the HQET analysis of semileptonic B decays to excited charmed mesons and the finding of large corrections to the infinite-mass limit in some B_c form factors [3], [5].

node_59c22e027df9.summary: This cluster focuses on quark-model predictions of weak B and B_c decay form factors across kinematic regions, including rare channels and transitions to excited charmed mesons.

questions.question: How can order Lambda_QCD/m_Q and alpha_s corrections to B to excited-D helicity amplitudes be constrained away from zero recoil without letting quark-model assumptions dominate the branching-ratio predictions?
questions.rationale: The HQET analysis gives model-independent zero-recoil relations but introduces model dependence away from zero recoil [1].

questions.question: Which B_c semileptonic and nonleptonic observables most sharply discriminate relativistic overlap-integral form factors from nonrelativistic constituent-potential predictions over the full q^2 range?
questions.rationale: The relativistic and nonrelativistic quark-model studies both compute B_c form factors and decay observables, with sensitivity to wave functions and interquark potentials [3].

questions.question: Can lattice-constrained dispersion quark models reduce long-distance uncertainties in B to K(*) l+l- spectra and forward-backward asymmetries enough for rare-decay Standard Model tests?
questions.rationale: The rare-decay study uses lattice-constrained dispersion form factors and analyzes the sensitivity of spectra and asymmetries to long-distance effects [5].

node_01a2a79fd510.summary: These papers analyze semileptonic, radiative, and nonleptonic B_c decays to charmonium, charm, and bottom-strange final states using quark models and NRQCD.

questions.question: Which measured B_c -> charmonium semileptonic angular distributions would most sharply discriminate among relativistic quark-model form-factor predictions?
questions.rationale: Relativistic constituent quark models provide explicit form factors and full cascade angular distributions for B_c decays to J/psi and other charmonium states [2][4].

questions.question: Can LHCb yields in exclusive B_c modes determine whether factorization is adequate for nonleptonic B_c -> charmonium transitions?
questions.rationale: The main nonleptonic branching-ratio predictions use the factorizing approximation, while LHCb studies estimate yields, efficiencies, and backgrounds for several B_c modes [2][3][5].

questions.question: How consistently can one set of heavy-quark potential parameters describe the c bbar spectrum, electromagnetic cascades, and B_c transition form factors?
questions.rationale: The spectroscopy study derives c bbar spectra and cascade rates from heavy-quark interactions, while decay studies tune quark-model parameters to masses, lifetimes, and leptonic or radiative inputs [1][2][4].

node_14cf0b6a2696.summary: This cluster applies relativistic, light-front, and three-quark models to weak decays of singly and doubly heavy baryons, emphasizing transition form factors and decay asymmetries.

questions.question: Which semileptonic decay asymmetries of singly and doubly heavy baryons provide the cleanest test of heavy-quark spin symmetry beyond model-dependent form-factor normalizations?
questions.rationale: This follows from HQET descriptions of heavy-baryon transitions and relativistic three-quark calculations of Isgur-Wise functions, decay rates, and asymmetry parameters [1], [2].

questions.question: How large are the model uncertainties in doubly heavy baryon form factors when scalar and axial-vector diquark pictures, light-front dynamics, and nonrelativistic three-body wave functions are compared against the same decay channels?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in light-front predictions for doubly heavy baryon weak decays and nonrelativistic quark-model calculations using several interquark potentials [4], [5].

questions.question: Can LHCb measurements of Xi_cc and future bc or bb baryons overconstrain quark-model predictions for masses, magnetic moments, and weak transition form factors?
questions.rationale: This derives from the Xi_cc observation motivating systematic predictions for doubly heavy baryon decays and static properties [4], [5].

node_8a8627f9c1ee.summary: These studies use covariant confined and light-front quark models to compute form factors, branching fractions, and polarization observables for B, B_c, B_s, D, and D_s decays.

questions.question: Can covariant light-front and covariant confined quark models be cross-calibrated to produce form-factor shapes over the full q2 range without relying on model-dependent extrapolations from the spacelike region?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] evaluates Bc transition form factors at q2<0 and extrapolates them with a three-parameter fit, while [5] reviews precision charm semileptonic data testing such form factors.

questions.question: Which polarization and forward-backward asymmetry measurements in tauonic and rare Lambda_b decays most directly test the scalar and helicity-flip contributions predicted by covariant quark models?
questions.rationale: Papers [2] and [3] compute lepton-side and hadron-side asymmetries and baryon polarizations for Lambda_b semileptonic and rare decays.

questions.question: Can future D and Ds semileptonic branching-fraction data distinguish the internal structure of scalar and axial-vector final-state mesons within covariant quark-model form factors?
questions.rationale: Paper [4] argues that charm-factory measurements of D and Ds decays to scalar and axial-vector mesons can clarify hadronic transition form factors and even-parity meson structure.

node_708e797db507.summary: This cluster develops lattice, light-front, dispersion, and chiral approaches to heavy-meson weak decay form factors, including Isgur-Wise functions and heavy-quark symmetry limits.

questions.question: Can heavy-quark symmetry breaking corrections to semileptonic B and D form factors be constrained tightly enough to make universal Isgur-Wise functions predictive across heavy-to-heavy and heavy-to-light channels?
questions.rationale: This derives from the HQET review's treatment of universal form factors and symmetry-breaking corrections in weak decays of single-heavy-quark hadrons [1].

questions.question: How can dispersion-based constituent quark calculations reduce dependence on effective quark masses and meson wave functions while preserving correct analytic properties over the full physical q2 region?
questions.rationale: This follows from the relativistic dispersion approach using double spectral representations and fitted quark-model inputs to compute B, Bs, D, and Ds form factors [4].

questions.question: Which measurements of B to D** transitions and D**s decay constants most stringently test covariant light-front predictions for s-wave and p-wave heavy mesons?
questions.rationale: This is based on the covariant light-front study's comparison of heavy-to-light and B to D** form factors with data from B to D** pi and B to D D**s decays [5].

node_c1a94c89849b.summary: These papers model heavy-to-heavy and heavy-to-light meson transitions with light-front, constituent, and chiral frameworks to predict decay constants and semileptonic form factors.

questions.question: How accurately do covariant light-front form factors reproduce heavy-quark-symmetry relations and their symmetry-breaking corrections for heavy-to-heavy and heavy-to-light meson transitions?
questions.rationale: Heavy-quark symmetry provides model-independent constraints and symmetry-breaking corrections, while the covariant light-front approach computes decay constants and form factors and examines their heavy-quark-limit behavior [1],[5].

questions.question: Can quark-model wave functions and effective quark masses be constrained well enough to make full-q^2 predictions for B_s, B, D_s, and D semileptonic form factors systematically reliable?
questions.rationale: The relativistic dispersion approach reduces model ambiguities by fitting quark masses and wave functions while enforcing analytic properties and heavy-quark-limit requirements across the full physical q^2 region [4].

questions.question: Which measurements of B to D** pi and B to D D_s** most directly test p-wave decay constants and B to D** transition form factors in light-front or chiral effective descriptions?
questions.rationale: The covariant light-front study uses experimental B to D** pi and B to D D_s** decays to test D_s** decay constants and B to D** transition form factors [5].

node_aa1e32daf440.summary: This cluster centers on light-front and dispersion calculations of pseudoscalar-to-pseudoscalar and pseudoscalar-to-vector weak transition form factors for B and D mesons.

questions.question: Can light-front and relativistic-dispersion form-factor calculations be reconciled by a common treatment of meson wave functions, analytic constraints, and heavy-quark-symmetry limits across the full physical q2 region?
questions.rationale: This follows from dispersion calculations using double spectral representations and covariant light-front calculations of heavy-to-light and heavy-to-heavy form factors [2][3].

questions.question: Which large-recoil observables in pseudoscalar-to-vector and pseudoscalar-to-pseudoscalar decays can isolate leading- versus subleading-twist wave-function contributions to heavy-meson form factors?
questions.rationale: The question is based on the asymptotic analysis showing that large-recoil form factors are controlled by leading- and subleading-twist meson wave functions [4].

questions.question: How much of the uncertainty in quark-model form factors is reducible by fitting effective quark masses and wave functions to leptonic decays, and how much remains as model dependence?
questions.rationale: This derives from the ISGW2 and dispersion-model efforts to reduce quark-model uncertainties while enforcing heavy-quark-symmetry and analytic constraints [1][2].

node_96b7b5c89906.summary: These works build heavy-quark and chiral effective Lagrangians for heavy-light mesons to describe semileptonic decays, resonances, and strong decays of excited states.

questions.question: Which symmetry-breaking terms in heavy-meson chiral Lagrangians most limit model-independent extraction of semileptonic B and D form factors?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] reviews HQET symmetry-breaking corrections, while [4] builds weak-current form factors from a heavy-light effective Lagrangian including nearest-pole contributions.

questions.question: Can the couplings governing strong decays of positive-parity and p-wave heavy mesons be fixed well enough from one- and two-pion decay widths to make predictive tests of heavy-quark symmetry?
questions.rationale: Paper [3] constructs a chiral Lagrangian for excited heavy mesons and computes D2 and D1 one- and two-pion decay rates governed by soft pion and kaon interactions.

questions.question: How consistently can SU(3)V-breaking chiral corrections describe f_Ds/f_D and B_s to anti-B_s versus B0 to anti-B0 mixing matrix-element ratios in a framework with both meson and anti-meson fields?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] calculates leading SU(3)V-violating contributions to decay-constant and mixing-amplitude ratios and discusses the needed heavy-quark effective-theory formalism.

node_5860538c607d.summary: This cluster investigates the Isgur-Wise function and its slope for heavy meson and baryon semileptonic decays using lattice QCD, sum rules, and relativistic bound-state models.

questions.question: Can heavy-quark sum-rule bounds on the Isgur-Wise slope, especially rho^2 > 3/4, be sharpened or falsified by modern Lambda_b -> Lambda_c differential-rate measurements?
questions.rationale: The exact heavy-quark sum-rule paper derives the lower bound on the Isgur-Wise slope, and LHCb directly measures the Lambda_b -> Lambda_c Isgur-Wise shape [2,5].

questions.question: How universal is the approximate proportionality xi_3(w) proportional to xi(w) once radiative and 1/m_Q corrections are tested against B -> D* form-factor ratios?
questions.rationale: The QCD sum-rule calculation finds large alpha_s corrections but predicts xi_3/xi approximately constant and testable through A_2/A_1 in B -> D* l nu [3].

questions.question: What duality prescription in the small-velocity limit gives a stable Isgur-Wise shape while preserving angular isotropy for S-wave states?
questions.rationale: The small-velocity sum-rule study shows that the Isgur-Wise function is sensitive to the continuum-duality prescription and imposes isotropy constraints [4].

node_f7ac8b86337c.summary: Reviews and global fits of CP violation in K and B systems use CKM unitarity-triangle observables and decay asymmetries to test the Standard Model and constrain beyond-Standard-Model phases.

questions.question: What combination of Belle II measurements of gamma, sin2alpha, rare K -> pi nu nubar decays, and CP asymmetries in pi pi, K pi, rho pi, and rho rho modes would most decisively reveal a non-CKM CP-violating phase rather than residual hadronic uncertainty?
questions.rationale: This follows from the global CKM-fit program and its emphasis on combining B-factory asymmetries, isospin analyses, QCD-factorization inputs, and rare kaon constraints [1].

questions.question: Can multibody and non-CP-eigenstate D decays in B+- -> D K+- make gamma precise enough that it becomes a limiting test of CKM unitarity, rather than a supporting input to global fits?
questions.rationale: The question combines the enhanced-interference strategy using common D0 and anti-D0 final states with the multibody-D method that avoids hadronic resonance-model uncertainty [3,4].

questions.question: Where will Belle II's high-statistics, low-background data most strongly stress the CKM paradigm: overconstrained B-sector triangle angles, rare flavor-changing neutral-current decays, or correlated charm and tau measurements?
questions.rationale: Belle II is framed as a broad intensity-frontier program capable of measuring many Standard Model parameters and probing new particles far above direct collider scales [2,S1].

node_fd297ff4e82f.summary: Model-independent analyses and flavor observables search for deviations from Standard Model CP violation through B mixing, B to pi K and pi pi anomalies, electroweak penguins, and rare leptonic decays.

questions.question: Can time-dependent measurements of B_s -> mu+ mu- observables A_DeltaGamma and S_mumu separate scalar new-physics contributions and CP-violating phases even when the branching fraction remains compatible with the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the observation that the measured B_s -> mu+ mu- branching fraction constrains but does not exhaust new-physics possibilities in [1] and [5], and from the CP-observable proposal in [3].

questions.question: What correlated pattern among Delta m_s, Delta Gamma_s, a_fs^s, and mode-dependent B decay CP asymmetries would unambiguously indicate new decay amplitudes rather than a universal new contribution to B mixing?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the reduced theoretical uncertainties in B_s mixing from the operator-basis update in [2] and the distinction between mixing and decay-amplitude new physics in [4].

questions.question: If rare B anomalies are due to heavy new physics, can mu+ mu- -> b s rates and b-jet forward-backward asymmetries at a 10 TeV muon collider determine the chirality structure consistently with low-energy B data?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the Snowmass proposal that mu+ mu- -> b s can probe new-physics explanations of rare B anomalies and diagnose chirality with forward-backward asymmetry [S1].

node_85b0ad6b6905.summary: These papers study how beyond-Standard-Model contributions to neutral B and D meson mixing could appear through CP asymmetries, semileptonic observables, and B_s mixing parameters.

questions.question: Which combination of Delta m_s, Delta Gamma_s, and flavor-specific CP asymmetries gives the cleanest separation between new physics in B_s mixing and residual hadronic uncertainty in Gamma_12^s?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], which introduces an improved operator basis for Gamma_12^s and reduces hadronic uncertainty in Delta Gamma_s/Delta m_s.

questions.question: Can mode-by-mode deviations among neutral-B CP asymmetries distinguish new decay amplitudes from universal new contributions to the mixing amplitude?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [2], which contrasts universal mixing effects with decay-mode-dependent new physics in neutral B decay amplitudes.

questions.question: What updated global Delta F=2 fit would determine whether current B_d, B_s, and K mixing data still allow non-minimal flavor violation beyond MFV scenarios?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [3], which parametrizes generic new physics in neutral-meson mixing and compares uncorrelated and MFV scenarios.

node_ce7ab07755d6.summary: The cluster focuses on model-independent constraints and possible signals of new CP-violating physics in B_d and B_s mixing, including dimuon asymmetries and b to s transitions.

questions.question: Can the new operator basis and all-order charm-mass logarithm treatment for Gamma_12^s be pushed to a precision where Delta Gamma_s/Delta m_s and a_fs^s become limited by lattice matrix elements rather than by 1/m_b or alpha_s corrections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reduction of large 1/m_b and alpha_s corrections and hadronic uncertainty in the Bs mixing update [1].

questions.question: Which pattern of mode-dependent CP asymmetry shifts would cleanly separate new physics in B decay amplitudes from a universal new phase in Bd or Bs mixing?
questions.rationale: The systematic analysis in [2] emphasizes that mixing effects are universal across decay modes whereas new decay amplitudes vary by channel.

questions.question: Do current and future constraints on Delta_d, Delta_s, and kaon mixing parameters leave any non-MFV explanation of b to s anomalies that is distinguishable from hadronic or CKM-fit uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The anatomy study [3] parameterizes generic new physics in Bq mixing by complex Delta_q and contrasts unconstrained sectors with MFV scenarios.

node_d72e312e9595.summary: These works quantify small Standard Model corrections and null tests in time-dependent CP asymmetries such as B to psi K_S, penguin-dominated B decays, radiative modes, and rare K decays.

questions.question: What is the irreducible Standard Model theory uncertainty on extracting sin(2 beta) from B0 to J/psi K0 once long-distance penguin contractions and penguin operators are constrained by all available flavor data?
questions.rationale: A fit to long-distance penguin effects in B0 to J/psi K0 found Delta S consistent with zero but with a finite 95 percent interval [4].

questions.question: Which pattern of deviations among S_eta-prime K_S, S_phi K_S, and S_K+K-K_S would unambiguously exceed SU(3)-bounded Standard Model pollution and point to new b to s flavor-changing phases?
questions.rationale: SU(3) analyses bound mode-dependent deviations from S_psi K_S, while phi K_S was proposed as a clean new-physics test if b to u ubar s enhancement is excluded [3], [5].

node_b857d7cb779f.summary: The papers use rare B_s,d to lepton-pair decays, especially B_s to mu+ mu-, as precision tests of the Standard Model and sensitive probes of new physics.

questions.question: Can simultaneous measurements of BR(B_s to mu+mu-), the effective lifetime, A_DeltaGamma^mumu, and S_mumu disentangle scalar amplitudes and CP-violating phases even if the branching fraction remains Standard-Model-like?
questions.rationale: This follows from the role of A_DeltaGamma^mumu and S_mumu in exposing hidden new physics [2] and the effective lifetime as a clean observable enabled by nonzero DeltaGamma_s [4].

questions.question: What residual theory uncertainty remains in the Standard Model prediction for BR(B_s,d to mu+mu-) after higher-order electroweak corrections and the mapping between experimental time-integrated and theoretical rates are standardized?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the reappraisal of the SM prediction, including electroweak scheme dependence and the distinction between experimentally measured and theoretically defined rates [5].

questions.question: How would mu+mu- to b s production at a 10 TeV muon collider, including forward-backward asymmetry and beam polarization, break degeneracies among new-physics explanations constrained by rare B decays?
questions.rationale: This is based on the Snowmass proposal that mu+mu- to b s can probe heavy new physics behind rare B anomalies, with chirality diagnostics from the b-jet forward-backward asymmetry and improved sensitivity from polarization [S1].

node_f5568ca79fe1.summary: This cluster examines puzzling B to pi pi and B to pi K branching ratios and CP asymmetries, often interpreting them through electroweak penguin effects and possible new physics.

questions.question: What single pattern of B -> pi K branching ratios and direct CP asymmetries would distinguish enhanced electroweak penguins with a new CP phase from Standard-Model nonfactorizable interference?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Standard-Model accommodation of B -> pi pi features and electroweak-penguin new-physics interpretation of B -> pi K in [2] and [4].

questions.question: Can NLO perturbative-QCD corrections to vertex, quark-loop, and magnetic-penguin amplitudes resolve the B -> pi K CP-asymmetry pattern without worsening the remaining B -> pi0 pi0 branching-ratio puzzle?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the pQCD NLO resolution of the B -> pi K direct-CP difference and the unresolved pi0 pi0 rate noted in [5].

questions.question: How should rare radiative and electroweak b -> d,s penguin modes be folded into B -> pi K fits to test new flavor-changing neutral-current interactions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the NLO predictions for radiative and electroweak penguin observables in [1] and the new electroweak-penguin phase scenario in [4].

node_f4fa337cff8e.summary: These papers develop methods to extract CKM phases alpha and gamma from charged and neutral B decays using interference, flavor symmetries, and control of penguin contributions.

questions.question: How can gamma extractions from B+- -> DK+- with multibody D decays be made robust against residual charm-decay modeling, detector binning, and strong-phase uncertainties while preserving the no-hadronic-uncertainty advantage?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the multibody D-decay method using only Cabibbo-allowed modes and resonance-induced strong phases in [2].

questions.question: Which pattern of discrepancies among GLW/ADS-style charged-B determinations of gamma, B-factory unitarity-triangle fits, and B_s time-dependent observables would indicate new physics rather than underestimated penguin or strong-phase effects?
questions.rationale: This combines the enhanced CP-violation methods in [1] and [4], the B-factory CKM-angle synthesis in [3], and the B_s mixing-phase probes in [5].

node_f4fa337cff8e_1.summary: The cluster centers on determining the CKM angle gamma from B to DK, Dpi, pi K, pi pi, and related B_s modes while reducing hadronic and electroweak-penguin uncertainties.

questions.question: What combination of GLW, ADS, and multibody Dalitz strategies can extract gamma with minimal hadronic uncertainty while controlling charm strong phases and D-mixing effects?
questions.rationale: ADS and related methods enhance CP violation using common non-CP D final states, while multibody D decays can extract gamma without assuming a resonance model [1],[2],[3].

questions.question: How precisely must U-spin-breaking corrections be quantified for Bd to pi+pi- and Bs to K+K- to remain competitive with theoretically clean B to DK determinations of gamma?
questions.rationale: The U-spin strategy relates Bd to pi pi and Bs to K K so that gamma can be extracted with theoretical accuracy limited mainly by U-spin breaking [5].

questions.question: Can Bs decay observables disentangle a new CP-violating mixing phase from the Standard Model gamma extraction program using only tagged and untagged lifetime and branching-ratio information?
questions.rationale: The Bs analysis proposed tagged and untagged methods, including lifetime and branching-ratio measurements, to detect a sizeable CP-violating Bs mixing phase beyond the Standard Model [4].

node_d2af7ebe1884.summary: These works propose theoretically clean gamma determinations from B decays involving D mesons, scalar or tensor mesons, and U-spin-related B_s and B_d channels.

questions.question: How can ADS and GLW B+- to K+-D analyses optimally combine CP eigenstates, doubly Cabibbo-suppressed D decays, and multibody D final states to extract gamma with minimal theory input?
questions.rationale: The ADS and improved GLW strategies use common D0 and Dbar0 final states, including non-CP eigenstates and three-body D decays, to enhance direct CP violation and extract gamma [2].

questions.question: What level of U-spin breaking in Bd to pi+pi- and Bs to K+K- can be tolerated before the gamma extraction loses its claimed immunity to penguin and final-state-interaction effects?
questions.rationale: The U-spin strategy is theoretically clean except for U-spin-breaking corrections, after relating the two decay modes by d-s interchange [4].

questions.question: Can gamma bounds from B+- to pi K branching ratios remain complementary and clean once electroweak penguins and strong rescattering are included in a model-independent way?
questions.rationale: The pi K bound was designed to improve on earlier analyses by treating electroweak penguin and rescattering effects in a model-independent SU(3)-based framework [5].

node_b2153914b4d0.summary: The papers exploit interfering B decay amplitudes into D, K, pi, scalar, tensor, and B_c final states to measure the CKM angle gamma with enhanced CP asymmetries.

questions.question: Can combined ADS and GLW analyses of B+- to K+-D with multibody D final-state distributions determine gamma with controlled strong-phase inputs and without prior knowledge of Br(B- to K- anti-D0)?
questions.rationale: The enhanced-interference methods use common non-CP D final states and multibody D information to extract gamma while avoiding difficult branching-ratio inputs [1][2].

questions.question: How can B to pi K bounds on gamma be made robust against SU(3)-breaking, electroweak penguins, and rescattering while remaining complementary to global unitarity-triangle fits?
questions.rationale: The pi K strategies derive clean or generalized gamma constraints but emphasize sensitivity to electroweak penguins, rescattering, and SU(3)-breaking effects [3][4][5].

questions.question: Which minimal set of D-interference modes and pi K branching-ratio combinations can overconstrain gamma enough to isolate a hadronic-penguin inconsistency within the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: The representative papers combine interference-based gamma extraction with pi K consistency bounds on current-current and penguin amplitudes [2][4][5].

node_c0d1015d75aa.summary: This cluster uses U-spin-related neutral B_d and B_s decays to extract gamma, control penguin topologies, and probe new CP-violating phases in B_s mixing.

questions.question: How precisely must U-spin breaking in Bd→π+π− and Bs→K+K− be controlled before gamma extraction becomes limited by experiment rather than theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the U-spin strategy whose theoretical accuracy is limited by U-spin-breaking corrections while avoiding penguin and final-state-interaction ambiguities [2].

questions.question: Can combined tagged and untagged Bs→DsK and related modes provide an unambiguous extraction of phi_s+gamma once DeltaGamma_s and the (-1)^L angular-momentum factor are included?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the phase-convention-independent treatment of Bs→DsK observables and the importance of untagged rates when DeltaGamma_s is sizeable [5].

questions.question: Which lifetime, branching-ratio, and angular-moment observables in Bs decays provide the cleanest signal of a new CP-violating Bs mixing phase without relying on two-exponential fits?
questions.rationale: This combines the proposed untagged lifetime-and-branching-ratio method with angular-moment analyses of Bs→J/psi phi for extracting mixing parameters [1],[3].

node_0a5e0d016fa9.summary: These papers develop symmetry- and amplitude-based methods to extract the weak phase gamma from charged and neutral B decays such as B to pi K, pi pi, DK, and Bs to KK.

questions.question: How can multibody B± -> DK± analyses preserve the no-hadronic-uncertainty advantage while exploiting large strong phases across D -> K_S pi pi, K_S K K, and K_S pi pi pi0 phase space?
questions.rationale: The method in [1] relies on Cabibbo-allowed multibody D decays, large resonance-induced strong phases, and no assumed resonance model.

questions.question: Which combinations of B -> pi K and B -> pi pi branching ratios and direct CP asymmetries make electroweak penguins and SU(3)-breaking corrections the limiting uncertainty in gamma bounds?
questions.rationale: The SU(3)-based charged-B method with electroweak penguins and factorized SU(3) breaking in [3] is generalized by the model-independent uncertainty analysis in [4].

questions.question: Can rate inequalities in B±,0 -> D X_s±,0 multibody modes become competitive with exclusive B± -> DK± strategies for bounding sin^2 gamma?
questions.rationale: The model-independent inequalities for sin^2 gamma using partial-rate ratios and CP asymmetries in D X_s final states are proven in [5].

node_a58a02b23eb5.summary: This cluster focuses on determining CKM angle alpha from B to pi pi, rho rho, and related modes while controlling QCD and electroweak penguin pollution using isospin, SU(3), and time-dependent CP asymmetries.

questions.question: Which combination of B to pi pi, rho rho, pi K, and K K observables can determine alpha while directly bounding the QCD and electroweak penguin pollution rather than assuming SU(3)-controlled corrections?
questions.rationale: This follows from the B-factory alpha program in [1] and the warnings that electroweak penguins can invalidate SU(3)-based phase extractions in [2,3].

questions.question: Can the model-independent Q9 and Q10 electroweak-penguin relations be combined with measured tree-amplitude ratios to make gamma and alpha extractions internally consistent across B to pi pi and B to K pi?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the SU(3) electroweak-penguin relations and weak-phase strategies developed in [4,5].

node_2bddc00dafbc.summary: These works analyze how QCD and electroweak penguin amplitudes affect CP-violation measurements in nonleptonic B decays, including corrections to alpha, gamma, and benchmark modes like J/psi KS.

questions.question: How precisely can electroweak-penguin amplitudes be measured from SU(3)-related B to pi pi, pi K, and K K modes so that gamma extractions remain valid without uncontrolled hadronic assumptions?
questions.rationale: SU(3)-based strategies show that electroweak penguins can invalidate simple phase extractions but can also be constrained experimentally through amplitude relations [1], [3], [4].

questions.question: What is the smallest set of branching-ratio and CP-asymmetry measurements needed to bound QCD and electroweak penguin corrections to alpha from B to pi pi when B to pi0 pi0 data are limited?
questions.rationale: The alpha isospin analysis is largely protected from electroweak penguins, and penguin-induced errors can be bounded using charged and neutral pion branching information [1], [5].

questions.question: Can relations involving the dominant Q9 and Q10 electroweak-penguin operators be extended beyond two-pseudoscalar modes while preserving model-independent cancellation of EWP uncertainties?
questions.rationale: Model-independent EWP-tree relations were derived for charmless two-pseudoscalar decays by retaining the dominant Q9 and Q10 operators [4].

node_b7bb6d2633ff.summary: This cluster studies extractions of the CKM angle alpha from charmless B decays such as pi pi, rho rho, rho pi, and KK, with emphasis on bounding penguin-induced theoretical uncertainties.

questions.question: Can a unified amplitude analysis of B to pi pi, rho rho, and rho pi reduce the penguin-induced shift between alpha and alpha_eff without adding model assumptions beyond the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the exact analytic treatment of the penguin-to-tree unknown in B0 to pi+ pi- in [2] and the Dalitz-plot strategy for B to rho pi in [5].

questions.question: Which measured branching ratios and time-dependent CP asymmetries are sufficient to remove the remaining discrete ambiguities in alpha extractions from charmless B modes?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the discrete ambiguity in clean CKM phase extraction in [1] and the hadronic information needed to resolve sin 2phi ambiguities in [4].

questions.question: Can time-dependent angular analyses of CP-admixed final states provide independent hadronic constraints that cross-check penguin corrections inferred from two-body charmless B decays?
questions.rationale: This derives from the formalism for extracting CKM phases and hadronic parameters from angular distributions with penguin contributions in [3].

node_1113c0b61a45.summary: These papers propose Dalitz-plot and model-independent strategies using B to DK and related multibody decays to measure the unitarity-triangle angle gamma with reduced hadronic uncertainty.

questions.question: How should model-independent B to DK Dalitz analyses optimize binning and CP-tagged D statistics to make gamma extraction limited by data rather than hadronic amplitude modeling?
questions.rationale: The feasibility study relates phi_3 precision to B and CP-tagged D statistics in B to DK with D to K_S pi+ pi- [2].

questions.question: Can time-dependent Dalitz analyses of penguin-free resonant three-body B decays resolve discrete ambiguities in beta and measure 2 beta plus gamma with competitive precision?
questions.rationale: Time-dependent B to DPP Dalitz modes were proposed to measure cos(2 beta), resolve beta ambiguities, and access 2 beta plus gamma, with penguin-free Cabibbo-dominant channels identified [5].

node_3fdce3b2eecb.summary: This broad review cluster surveys CP violation, CKM-matrix phenomenology, unitarity-triangle constraints, rare decays, and implications for Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model flavor physics.

questions.question: What combination of Belle II measurements of B, charm, tau, rare decays, and kaon K+->pi+ nu nubar or KL->pi0 nu nubar would expose non-SM flavor structure rather than merely tighten the CKM unitarity triangle?
questions.rationale: This derives from the use of rare kaon and B observables in CKM fits and Belle II's projected broad intensity-frontier program [1], [2], [S1].

questions.question: Can global CKM fits treat theoretical uncertainties in penguin-contaminated B->pipi, Kpi, rhopi, rhorho modes and epsilon'/epsilon robustly enough that a claimed tension is not an artifact of Rfit versus Bayesian assumptions?
questions.rationale: This follows from the explicit comparison of B decay theory treatments and the statistical-framework emphasis in global CKM analyses [1], [3].

node_a4c6d3fc2500.summary: These papers review the Standard Model description of CP violation in kaon and B-meson systems, including CKM tests, rare K decays, B-factory measurements, and new-physics sensitivity.

questions.question: How precise must K+ -> pi+ nu nubar and KL -> pi0 nu nubar become to overconstrain the CKM unitarity triangle against B-factory determinations of alpha, beta, and gamma?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed CKM global-fit role of rare K decays and B CP asymmetries in [1] and the clean determination of Im(Vts*Vtd) and J_CP from KL -> pi0 nu nubar in [4].

questions.question: Can penguin contamination in B -> pi pi, K pi, rho pi, and rho rho be controlled well enough that CKM-fit tensions are not dominated by hadronic theory assumptions?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the detailed treatment of these B decay modes, isospin separation, and QCD factorization comparisons in [1].

questions.question: Which combination of epsilon_K, epsilon'/epsilon, B_d,s mixing, V_cb, V_ub, and NLO short-distance corrections gives the sharpest Standard Model test of CP violation after the top-quark mass input is fixed?
questions.rationale: This derives from the review of how top mass, CKM inputs, NLO QCD corrections, mixing, epsilon_K, epsilon'/epsilon, and rare K and B decays constrain CP violation [3].

node_bdd8a5794c08.summary: This cluster collects reviews of CKM-based CP violation, quark mixing, rare K and B decays, and how experimental constraints test the Standard Model against possible new physics.

questions.question: Which combination of rare K decay branching ratios and B-meson CP asymmetry phases would overconstrain the CKM unitarity triangle with the smallest theoretical ambiguity?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], [2], and [3], which emphasize global CKM fits, rare K -> pi nu nubar modes, and B-decay CP asymmetries as clean Standard Model tests.

questions.question: Can a small Standard-Model CP phase in B decays be measured precisely enough to reveal new physics using phase information alone?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by [5], which argues that new physics can be detected from CP-violating phase measurements if a small Standard-Model phase is included, while CKM nonunitarity is hard to establish from phases alone.

questions.question: How should penguin contamination in B -> pi pi, K pi, rho pi, and rho rho modes be controlled so that sin2alpha, beta, and gamma remain clean inputs to CKM fits?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which discusses isospin treatment of penguin contributions and QCD-factorization analyses of these B decay channels.

node_70c6a3996a91.summary: These works review the theory and experimental program of B physics at B factories, the Tevatron, and the LHC, emphasizing CP violation, mixing, rare decays, and future precision tests.

questions.question: Which combined program of CP violation, mixing and lifetimes, rare decays, semileptonic decays, and spectroscopy most overconstrains the CKM picture at hadron colliders?
questions.rationale: This follows from the Tevatron B-physics working-group structure and physics prospects laid out in [1].

questions.question: What theoretical or experimental advance would resolve the inclusive-versus-exclusive V_cb and V_ub determinations well enough for B decays to diagnose new particles found elsewhere?
questions.rationale: The inclusive-exclusive CKM issue and the role of B decays in interpreting new physics are emphasized in [5].

questions.question: Can b -> s g* fragmentation channels such as B -> eta' X_s and X_g = K+K- reveal nonstandard CP phases even when their contributions to total rates are only at the ten-percent level?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the proposed direct-CP strategy using off-shell-gluon fragmentation states in [4].

node_cf4280a41cf9.summary: This cluster surveys quark-flavor physics as a probe of new physics, covering CKM precision constraints, B and D decays, Belle II prospects, and flavor-changing neutral-current observables.

questions.question: What pattern of Belle II, LHCb, ATLAS, and CMS flavor measurements would most clearly reveal a non-Standard-Model flavor structure rather than only tightening CKM and FCNC constraints?
questions.rationale: This broad question follows from the lack of established new physics but strong flavor constraints in [2] and the complementary Belle II and LHCb programs in [1], [3], and [5].

questions.question: How should global flavor analyses combine low-background Belle II observables with hadron-collider measurements to separate TeV-scale flavor dynamics from direct high-pT new-particle searches?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by Belle II's unique intensity-frontier reach [S1] and the HL/HE-LHC flavor complementarity with top, Higgs, and direct searches in [5].

questions.question: Which persistent B-decay or muon-g-2 anomaly explanations remain compatible with the full set of quark-flavor, charm, tau, and FCNC constraints expected over the next decade?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the anomaly and flavor-model-building discussion in [S2] and the broad Belle II physics program in [1].

node_4dd17d119d70.summary: These papers focus on determining CKM matrix parameters through global fits that combine CP asymmetries, rare decays, mixing observables, unitarity constraints, and statistical treatments of theoretical uncertainties.

questions.question: Which future measurement would most reduce the ambiguity between CKM unitarity tests as Standard Model consistency checks and CKM global fits as parameter determinations?
questions.rationale: The Rfit framework explicitly distinguishes model testing from metrological CKM parameter extraction while treating theoretical uncertainties carefully [1].

questions.question: Can rare K_L to pi0 nu nubar measurements and neutral-B CP asymmetries determine all CKM elements with genuinely negligible hadronic uncertainty in realistic future scenarios?
questions.rationale: A proposed strategy uses B-decay CP asymmetries plus Br(K_L to pi0 nu nubar) and V_us to determine CKM elements essentially free of hadronic uncertainties [4].

questions.question: How precisely must lattice-QCD decay constants and bag parameters be known for Delta m_s,d and B_s,d to mu mu correlations to remain competitive probes of new flavor physics?
questions.rationale: Older CKM constraints emphasized f_B and Delta m_s [3], while MFV relations reduce decay-constant dependence in Br(B_q to mu mu)/Delta M_q using better-controlled bag parameters [4].

node_b255e1bd927d.summary: This cluster studies direct CP violation across baryon, B, Bc, two-body, and three-body hadronic decays, often using factorization, penguin amplitudes, meson mixing, and Dalitz-plot dynamics.

questions.question: Which direct CP asymmetry measurements in B -> X_s gamma and low-q^2 B -> K* l+l- angular observables would most cleanly reveal non-CKM CP violation while keeping hadronic uncertainties controlled?
questions.rationale: The Standard-Model smallness of A_CP in B -> X_s gamma [1] and the potentially O(1) T-odd CP asymmetries in B -> K* l+l- [2] make these channels sharp new-physics tests.

questions.question: Can NLO factorization calculations and angular/Dalitz analyses determine the strong phases needed to interpret CP asymmetries across PP, PV, VV, Kpi e+e-, and pipi e+e- final states?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the angular CP observables of [3], the NLO low-q^2 framework in [2], and the factorization-based charmless two-body analysis in [5].

node_ac7eb7d15d57.summary: This cluster studies direct CP asymmetries in baryonic and mesonic B decays, emphasizing penguin effects, factorization choices, and resonance mixing such as rho-omega enhancement.

questions.question: Which direct CP asymmetry observable in b to s transitions remains clean enough that an O(1%) Standard Model expectation makes a larger signal unambiguous evidence for new CP phases?
questions.rationale: This follows from [1], where a sizable A_CP in inclusive B to X_s gamma is argued to be a clean new-physics signature because the Standard Model value is below 1%.

questions.question: Can T-odd angular CP asymmetries in B to K* l+l- and untagged B_s to phi l+l- isolate non-standard CP violation with reduced sensitivity to strong phases and flavor tagging?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [2], which finds T-odd CP asymmetries can be O(1), and [5], which identifies low-recoil CP observables with reduced hadronic uncertainties and untagged accessibility.

questions.question: How stable are factorization-based predictions of direct CP asymmetries in charmless B to PP, PV, and VV decays once soft final-state interactions are included?
questions.rationale: This follows from [4], which estimates these asymmetries using generalized factorization and NLO perturbative strong phases while omitting soft final-state interactions.

node_9579021271b6.summary: This cluster focuses on CP violation in three-body B decays, where Dalitz-plot interference, resonances, final-state interactions, and CPT constraints shape large localized asymmetries.

questions.question: How can Dalitz-plot analyses of B0 to K+K-KS(L) separate tree pollution from genuine penguin-sector deviations in the mixing-induced CP asymmetry relative to B to J/psi KS?
questions.rationale: The three-body KKK analysis finds that color-allowed tree amplitudes can make Delta sin2beta in this penguin-dominated mode sizeable [2].

questions.question: Which angular CP observables in Bbar to K pi e+e- and pi pi e+e- are least contaminated by resonance modeling of K*, rho, and long-distance vacuum-polarization effects?
questions.rationale: The rare-decay study constructs meson-angle, lepton-angle, and plane-correlation observables using the b to s(d)e+e- Hamiltonian, while related CP asymmetries depend on rho, omega, and J/psi resonance phases [1,5].

questions.question: Can approximate CP-rate-difference relations in B to K pi be generalized to local regions of three-body phase space without violating CPT constraints from coupled final-state interactions?
questions.rationale: The K pi papers use leading-order relations among CP-violating rate differences to combine modes, while the node's three-body context centers on localized asymmetries shaped by resonances and final-state interactions [3,4].

node_41207ec3c103.summary: This cluster concerns global determinations of the CKM matrix and unitarity triangle using kaon, charm, and B-physics constraints, including sensitivity to new physics.

questions.question: Which future combination of Delta M_d/Delta M_s, sin(2 beta), K -> pi nu nubar, and rare B decays would most cleanly falsify the universal unitarity triangle framework for minimal-flavor-violation models?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposal that a universal unitarity triangle can be determined from these observables in models with only CKM flavor violation and no new operators [1].

questions.question: How should global CKM fits consistently combine frequentist theoretical-uncertainty treatments with lattice inputs when constraining generic Delta F=2 new physics?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by CKMfitter's use of Rfit theoretical uncertainties and its constraints on generic Delta F=2 new physics [5].

questions.question: What observable currently carries the weakest consensus in unitarity-triangle fits: |Vub/Vcb|, epsilon_K, B-mixing inputs, or direct alpha and gamma determinations?
questions.rationale: This derives from UTfit and earlier CKM analyses emphasizing the impact of experimental constraints and theoretical uncertainties on the triangle parameters [4].

node_4ffd9305b09a.summary: This cluster covers QCD and perturbative-QCD factorization calculations for exclusive nonleptonic B decays, predicting branching ratios and CP asymmetries across PP, PV, and VV final states.

questions.question: Which experimentally accessible pattern of branching ratios and direct CP asymmetries in B -> pi pi, pi K, PP, and PV modes would most sharply test whether heavy-quark-limit QCD factorization is the right organizing principle?
questions.rationale: This broad test follows from the factorization predictions for B -> pi pi strong phases and CP violation [2], the pi K and pi pi extraction of Wolfenstein parameters [4], and the comprehensive PP/PV phenomenology [5].

questions.question: Can chirally enhanced terms and weak-annihilation contributions be promoted from phenomenological estimates to controlled power corrections without spoiling the factorized leading-power description?
questions.rationale: The issue is explicitly raised by the estimated chirally enhanced and annihilation power corrections included in B -> pi K, pi pi [4] and PP/PV analyses [5].

questions.question: How can SCET matching and Sudakov evolution for heavy-to-light currents be integrated with nonleptonic QCD factorization to reduce uncertainties in strong phases?
questions.rationale: SCET gives one-loop matching and RG evolution for heavy-to-light currents [1], while QCD factorization computes nonfactorizable order-alpha_s corrections and strong phases in nonleptonic B decays [2].

node_6e4e9c026a06.summary: This cluster analyzes charmless B and Bs two-body decays with pQCD and QCD factorization methods, including tree, penguin, annihilation, and nonfactorizable contributions.

questions.question: Can QCDF and pQCD predictions for B->pi K, pi pi, PP, and PV decays be reconciled by a first-principles treatment of chirally enhanced power corrections and weak-annihilation amplitudes?
questions.rationale: This is drawn from the QCDF calculations including chirally enhanced and annihilation estimates and the pQCD claims that annihilation and penguin enhancement are numerically important [1], [2], and [3].

questions.question: Which B->K pi branching-ratio ratios and CP asymmetries can isolate dynamically enhanced penguin matrix elements and large annihilation strong phases from CKM-angle effects?
questions.rationale: This follows from the pQCD analyses of penguin enhancement, annihilation strong phases, and the limited constraining power of then-current K pi data on phi_3 [3] and [4].

node_a10d85819dee.summary: This cluster applies perturbative QCD to specific B and Bs decay channels to compute branching fractions and CP asymmetries, often highlighting annihilation and NLO penguin effects.

questions.question: Can perturbative-QCD factorization give a single consistent description of branching ratios and direct CP asymmetries in B -> pi pi, pi rho, and pi omega once annihilation amplitudes and strong phases are constrained by data?
questions.rationale: This follows from pQCD predictions that nonfactorizable and annihilation contributions generate large strong phases and sizable direct CP asymmetries in B -> pi pi and pi rho/pi omega channels [1,3].

questions.question: How can one separate hard-spectator, vertex, and annihilation corrections in radiative B -> K* gamma and B -> rho gamma decays strongly enough to resolve the form-factor tension with data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the NLO large-energy effective-theory calculation finding large hard-spectator corrections and requiring lower form factors to reconcile B -> K* gamma rates [2].

questions.question: Do pure-annihilation channels such as B_s -> pi+ pi- provide a clean test of penguin-dominated pQCD predictions for small direct CP violation but potentially sizable mixing-induced asymmetry?
questions.rationale: This derives from the pQCD calculation of B_s -> pi+ pi- where penguin annihilation dominates, direct CP asymmetry is below a few percent, and mixing-induced CP asymmetry may reach the ten-percent level [5].

node_92e3c6353fc7.summary: This cluster examines strong, charming, and higher-order penguin contributions in charmless B decays, especially their impact on K pi and pi pi branching ratios and CP observables.

questions.question: Which combination of B to pi K and pi pi branching ratios and CP asymmetries can decisively distinguish QCD-factorization power corrections from perturbative-QCD penguin enhancement and annihilation-generated strong phases?
questions.rationale: QCD factorization treats chirally enhanced and annihilation power corrections as estimates [1,2], while perturbative QCD finds enhanced penguins and large annihilation strong phases [3,4].

questions.question: Can charmless PP, PV, and VV data constrain the endpoint-sensitive annihilation and spectator-scattering terms tightly enough to make extractions of alpha, gamma, and Wolfenstein parameters theory-limited rather than model-limited?
questions.rationale: This derives from the use of B to pi K and pi pi amplitudes for CKM constraints in [1] and the broad PP/PV phenomenology with estimated power corrections in [2].

node_5dfaae84bf44.summary: This cluster develops phenomenological QCD-factorization descriptions of charmless two-body B decays, including power corrections, weak annihilation, electroweak penguins, and CKM parameter extraction.

questions.question: Can power corrections from chirally enhanced terms, weak annihilation, and long-distance charming penguins be constrained from data well enough to make QCD factorization predictive for CP asymmetries in charmless B decays?
questions.rationale: QCD-factorization analyses estimate chirally enhanced and annihilation corrections, while SCET arguments allow leading long-distance c cbar penguin effects [1], [2], [5].

questions.question: Which pattern of B to PP, PV, and VV branching ratios would most decisively separate QCD factorization from perturbative-QCD claims of enhanced penguins and large annihilation strong phases?
questions.rationale: QCDF provides predictions for broad PP and PV decay sets, whereas perturbative QCD finds dynamically enhanced penguin operators and non-negligible annihilation phases in B to K pi [2], [3].

questions.question: How reliably can Wolfenstein parameters alpha and gamma be extracted from B to pi K and pi pi once electroweak penguins, SU(3)-breaking distribution amplitudes, and factorization-breaking effects are propagated coherently?
questions.rationale: The original QCDF phenomenology used B to pi K and pi pi amplitudes with electroweak penguins, SU(3) violation, and estimated power corrections to constrain the unitarity triangle [1].

node_2e7fda1d20df.summary: This cluster centers on long-distance charm-loop penguin amplitudes in B decays and their consequences for branching ratios, strong phases, and CP-violation measurements.

questions.question: Can long-distance charming-penguin amplitudes in charmless B decays be constrained enough by branching ratios and CP asymmetries to separate them from dynamically enhanced short-distance penguins and annihilation-induced strong phases?
questions.rationale: The question combines the perturbative-QCD enhancement and large annihilation phases in B to K pi with the long-distance charm-loop effects invoked to enhance B to pi0 pi0 and vector final states [1], [2], [4].

questions.question: How stable are SCET or SU(3)-based extractions of weak phases once long-distance charming penguins and electroweak corrections to penguin isospin structure are included in the same amplitude analysis?
questions.rationale: SCET fits to two-body B decays and NLO electroweak corrections both show that nonperturbative and isospin-breaking penguin effects can change weak-phase interpretations [3], [5].

node_c4ae000a2cd4.summary: This cluster combines pQCD studies of Bc decay modes with analyses of vector, axial-vector, and charmonium final states, including branching ratios, CP asymmetries, and polarization fractions.

questions.question: Which polarization observables in B_s to VV and B to VV decays can isolate penguin-annihilation transverse amplitudes from electroweak-penguin or right-handed-current effects?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the transverse-polarization enhancement in penguin-dominated B_s decays in [1] and the proposed polarization tests for right-handed currents and electroweak penguins in [2,3].

questions.question: Can NLO pQCD form-factor calculations for semileptonic B, B_s, and B_c transitions be made precise enough to calibrate the hadronic inputs used in nonleptonic polarization and CP-asymmetry predictions?
questions.rationale: This connects the pQCD B_c to eta_c and J/psi form-factor program in [4] with NLO pQCD form factors for B and B_s semileptonic decays in [5].

node_c28adde6180a.summary: This cluster focuses on pQCD calculations of Bc semileptonic and exclusive decay form factors and branching ratios, especially transitions to charmonium, B mesons, and tensor states.

questions.question: Can NLO pQCD corrections be computed for the Bc -> eta_c and Bc -> J/psi form factors F0, F+, V, and A0,1,2, and do they preserve the branching-ratio pattern between light-lepton and tau modes?
