questions.question: What nontrivial structure of the CKM-MNS correlation matrix F_nu is forced by data in grand-unified seesaw models, especially its nonzero (1,3) element?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3], which finds that bimaximal F_nu is disfavored and that the (1,3) element cannot be zero or too small.

questions.question: Which Clebsch-Gordan factor patterns in SU(5) or Pati-Salam models can generate the observed leptonic theta13 while preserving viable first- and second-family quark-lepton mass ratios?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [4], which shows that non-symmetric mass matrices with novel Clebsch-Gordan factors can yield larger theta13 predictions than symmetric zero-(1,1) textures.

node_29301ac02b0d.summary: This cluster develops Wolfenstein-like, Kobayashi-Maskawa, and quark-lepton complementarity parametrizations for describing CKM and lepton mixing angles.

questions.question: Which Wolfenstein-like parametrization of the PMNS matrix best separates Cabibbo-sized quark-lepton unification effects from genuinely leptonic sources of large mixing and CP violation?
questions.rationale: Cabibbo haze motivates leptonic Cabibbo shifts, while correlated-hierarchy parametrizations separate grand-unified quark-lepton relations from charged-lepton and seesaw sources of large angles [2], [3].

questions.question: Can relations such as theta_sol plus theta_C equals pi/4 survive current precision data once realistic flavor-symmetry breaking, fermion masses, and theta_13 corrections are imposed?
questions.rationale: Grand-unified quark-lepton complementarity predicts specific angle sums and theta_13 scaling, while later unified parametrizations require small corrections to zeroth-order angle choices [1], [4].

node_fda6a8d638a2.summary: These papers connect quark mass hierarchies, flavor symmetries, CKM parametrizations, and rephasing invariants to CP violation driven largely by phases in the light-quark sector.

questions.question: What observable relation among quark mass ratios, the Cabibbo angle, and the CKM unitarity triangle would establish that the dominant CP phase originates in the light-quark sector rather than being only a useful parametrization?
questions.rationale: This follows from the light-quark-sector phase description in [3] and the mass-ratio unitarity-triangle construction in [5].

questions.question: Can basis-invariant CP-violating quantities in scalar-fermion theories identify physical phases in quark texture models more robustly than CKM parametrization-dependent statements?
questions.rationale: This derives from the systematic construction of scalar-fermion CP invariants in [2].

questions.question: How stable are maximal-CP-violation texture predictions such as alpha near 90 degrees when quark singlets or GUT-motivated vector-like matter are allowed to alter mixings and B-decay asymmetries?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the maximal-CP texture predictions in [5] and the singlet-quark effects on mixings and B-decay CP asymmetries in [4].

node_d5776c073d5c.summary: This cluster systematically classifies Hermitian or symmetric quark mass matrices with texture zeros and tests which patterns reproduce CKM mixing, quark masses, and CP violation.

questions.question: Which texture-zero patterns retain physical content after arbitrary weak-basis transformations, and can they be characterized by basis-invariant criteria rather than by matrix zeros themselves?
questions.rationale: This question derives from the demonstration in [5] that some commonly used texture zeros can be produced by weak-basis transformations and therefore have no direct physical content.

questions.question: Can improved measurements of CKM elements, quark mass ratios, |Vub/Vcb|, and sin 2 beta decisively separate the surviving symmetric or Hermitian five-, six-, and four-zero quark mass textures?
questions.rationale: The need for sharper CKM and CP tests follows from the surviving texture classifications in [1] and the phenomenological tests in [2] and [4].

node_f3abccd067c0.summary: These works analyze one-zero, two-zero, hybrid, and minor-constrained neutrino mass textures against oscillation data to predict mass orderings, CP phases, and neutrinoless double beta decay.

questions.question: Which currently viable two-zero Majorana mass textures would be falsified first by a joint improvement in theta_23, delta, absolute neutrino mass, and neutrinoless double beta decay sensitivity?
questions.rationale: This follows from the seven viable two-zero textures and their predictions for masses and CP phases in [1], [2], and [4].

questions.question: Can Abelian symmetry realizations of texture zeros remain predictive once charged-lepton, quark-sector, and possible grand-unified constraints are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: The question is based on the symmetry-enforcement program for arbitrary fermion mass-matrix zeros in [5].

questions.question: In two-right-handed-neutrino seesaw models, which texture-zero structures can simultaneously accommodate oscillation data, leptogenesis, and lepton-flavor-violation bounds without losing testable predictions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the combined analysis of two-right-handed-neutrino phenomenology, leptogenesis, lepton flavor violation, and texture zeros in [3].

node_9be95f674dc1.summary: This cluster studies bimaximal and tribimaximal lepton mixing patterns and their charged-lepton or symmetry-breaking corrections needed to generate nonzero theta13, CP violation, and realistic angles.

questions.question: What residual symmetry or symmetry-breaking pattern can produce the observed nonzero theta13 and leptonic CP violation while retaining the predictive structure that made tri-bimaximal mixing successful?
questions.rationale: This high-generality question follows from the original tri-bimaximal ansatz [1], its independent symmetries and CP-violating generalizations [2], and nearly tri-bimaximal CP-violating modifications [3].

questions.question: Can charged-lepton or neutrino-sector corrections to bimaximal and tri-bimaximal mass matrices be distinguished through correlated predictions for solar, atmospheric, reactor, and long-baseline oscillation observables?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the bimaximal framework's predictions for non-maximal mixing in future long-baseline experiments [4] and the tri-bimaximal deviation analyses of solar, atmospheric, and reactor oscillations [3].

questions.question: Which constraints from neutrinoless double beta decay, cosmological neutrino mass, and oscillation data are most damaging to mass-matrix constructions derived from maximal symmetric mixing limits?
questions.rationale: This derives from the bimaximal mass-matrix construction that imposed no neutrinoless double beta decay and a hot-dark-matter component to obtain a viable three-neutrino mass matrix [5].

node_b4972ccbd39c.summary: These papers refine tribimaximal-inspired neutrino mixing with Cabibbo-sized, charged-lepton, and CP-phase corrections to match reactor-angle measurements and modern oscillation constraints.

questions.question: Which residual symmetries of tri-bimaximal mixing can be broken minimally to generate the measured reactor angle while preserving the successful solar and atmospheric structure?
questions.rationale: Tri-bimaximal mixing is tied to simple mass matrices and independent residual symmetries, but realistic data require controlled departures from the exact ansatz [1,2].

questions.question: Can nearly tri-bimaximal ansaetze predict leptonic CP violation sharply enough to distinguish intrinsic neutrino-sector phases from charged-lepton or permutation-symmetry corrections?
questions.rationale: Nearly tri-bimaximal scenarios incorporate CP violation and compare alternatives with and without intrinsic neutrino-oscillation CP violation [3].

questions.question: What observable deviations from bimaximal or tri-bimaximal limits would rule out the old maximal-mixing paradigm rather than merely require small corrective rotations?
questions.rationale: Bimaximal constructions predicted CP-conserving maximal structures and future-observable nonmaximal oscillation channels when solar and atmospheric mixing depart from maximality [4,5].

node_c6457bc613c8.summary: This cluster develops phenomenological parametrizations of the PMNS matrix, CP violation, geometric phases, and deviations from bimaximal or tribimaximal lepton mixing.

questions.question: Which algebraic perturbations of the Babu-Ma-Valle nonstandard-CP mass-matrix relation preserve maximal theta23 and maximal leptonic CP violation while accommodating arbitrary theta13 and an unrestricted solar angle?
questions.rationale: This follows from the nonstandard CP transformation that enforces maximal atmospheric mixing and maximal CP violation while allowing arbitrary theta13 in [1].

questions.question: How can PMNS parametrizations in matter separate the Dirac phase measured in long-baseline oscillations from Majorana phases relevant to neutrinoless double beta decay and from possible sterile-neutrino mixing?
questions.rationale: This derives from the model-independent discussion of Dirac and Majorana phases, matter effects, and sterile mixing in [3] and the PMNS paradigm summary in [4].

questions.question: Can flavor-democracy or nearly bimaximal lepton-mixing schemes still produce percent-level rephasing-invariant CP or T violation in nu_mu -> nu_e channels under precision constraints on all three PMNS angles?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the long-baseline nu_mu <-> nu_e prediction in [2] and the percent-level CP or T violation model in [5].

node_5e07f8072e6e.summary: These papers derive and apply renormalization group equations for neutrino masses, mixing angles, and CP phases in seesaw, supersymmetric, Dirac, and inverse-seesaw frameworks.

questions.question: Can threshold-matched seesaw RG evolution be made precise enough that high-scale flavor models can be falsified by next-generation measurements of theta_13, theta_23, and leptonic CP phases?
questions.rationale: Successive integration of heavy singlets and analytic estimates of running effects are developed in [2], with future experimental precision expected to resolve such corrections.

questions.question: Which combinations of Dirac and Majorana phases maximize radiative magnification or suppression of neutrino mixing angles between the lepton-number-violation scale and the weak scale?
questions.rationale: Running can convert small high-scale mixing into large weak-scale mixing in [1], and compact phase-dependent analytic formulae are derived in [3].

questions.question: How robust are phenomenological conclusions about neutrino running to scheme choices and beta-function tensor structures, given known revisions of the dimension-five operator RGE?
questions.rationale: The RGE for the neutrino mass operator was rederived with modifications to mixing-angle and CP-phase evolution in [5].

node_19d456a25cf4.summary: This cluster examines mu-tau reflection and related flavor symmetries, their predictions for maximal atmospheric mixing and CP violation, and how radiative or explicit breaking modifies them.

questions.question: What pattern of deviations from theta23 equals 45 degrees and deltaCP equals plus or minus 90 degrees would falsify exact mu-tau reflection while preserving approximate mu-tau flavor symmetry?
questions.rationale: Exact mu-tau reflection predicts equal mu and tau moduli and observable oscillation consequences in [1], while approximate and softly broken symmetry are reviewed in [2].

questions.question: Can the measured size of theta13 distinguish whether mu-tau symmetry breaking scales as sqrt(Delta m_sol^2/Delta m_A^2) or Delta m_sol^2/Delta m_A^2 in normal hierarchy models?
questions.rationale: The theoretical significance of precision theta13 measurements for different mu-tau breaking patterns is emphasized in [4].

questions.question: Which neutrino mass-matrix textures allow large Dirac CP violation from mu-tau breaking while avoiding Majorana CP violation and respecting current oscillation data?
questions.rationale: Correlations between mu-tau breaking, theta13, theta12, and the Dirac phase are studied in [3], and textures with maximal CP but no Majorana CP violation are proposed in [5].

node_ca2fa9576b45.summary: These works build and review grand-unified and discrete-flavor models that explain quark and lepton masses, neutrino mixing patterns, and flavor phenomenology through symmetries such as SO(10), A4, S4, and A5.

questions.question: What minimal set of correlated measurements in PMNS deviations from tri-bimaximal, bimaximal, or golden-ratio mixing, lepton-flavor violation, leptogenesis, and quark-sector flavor would make discrete unified flavor symmetries distinguishable from flexible phenomenological fits?
questions.rationale: This follows from the reviews' emphasis on A4, S4 and related finite groups as explanations of neutrino mixing patterns and their linked implications for lepton-flavor violation, leptogenesis, and quark extensions [2].

questions.question: Can vacuum-alignment mechanisms in A4 or related finite-group models naturally accommodate the measured nonzero reactor angle while preserving predictive solar or atmospheric mixing sum rules?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the A4 extra-dimensional construction of exact HPS mixing and its higher-dimensional corrections, together with later reviews stressing deviations required after Daya Bay and RENO [5].

questions.question: How can model-independent SUSY flavor mass-insertion bounds on FCNC and CP violation be consistently embedded into unified flavor-symmetry models without losing their claimed predictivity?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the full mass-insertion analysis of gluino- and photino-mediated FCNC and CP constraints and its applications to SUSY-GUTs and flavor-nonuniversal supergravity [1].

node_6b9b3274751d.summary: This cluster uses horizontal, Froggatt-Nielsen, U(1), U(2), and related gauge symmetries to generate Standard Model fermion mass hierarchies while addressing supersymmetric flavor constraints.

questions.question: Is quark-squark alignment from Abelian horizontal symmetries a viable alternative to squark degeneracy once the full FCNC and CP-violating mass-insertion constraints are imposed?
questions.rationale: The alignment proposal is motivated as an alternative to degeneracy, while the mass-insertion analysis provides the relevant FCNC and CP bounds [1], [2].

questions.question: What is the minimal anomaly-consistent horizontal gauge extension that generates the observed fermion mass and mixing hierarchies without excluding TeV-scale flavor dynamics?
questions.rationale: Horizontal U(1) gauge factors constrained by anomaly cancellation and the possibility of accessible flavor dynamics are central claims of the mass-matrix models [3], [5].

questions.question: Which exact relations among mass ratios, mixing angles, the mu term, and neutrino masses survive realistic horizontal-symmetry breaking and remain experimentally falsifiable?
questions.rationale: The sequel paper highlights exact mass-mixing relations, the mu problem, and neutrino-mass mechanisms as possible consequences of broken horizontal symmetries [4].

node_a8bcd6f93603.summary: These papers explore supersymmetric and radiative mechanisms for fermion mass hierarchies, including sfermion effects, decoupling, flavor symmetries, and loop-generated Yukawa structures.

questions.question: Can Abelian horizontal-symmetry alignment suppress gluino and photino mass-insertion contributions to K, B, and D mixing and epsilon-prime over epsilon without requiring near-degenerate squarks?
questions.rationale: This follows from the model-independent FCNC and CP mass-insertion analysis and the proposed quark-squark alignment alternative to squark degeneracy [2].

questions.question: Which exact mass-ratio and mixing-angle relations from broken horizontal symmetries survive the combined constraints from charged-fermion hierarchies, neutrino oscillations, and CP violation?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in horizontal-symmetry mass-matrix models and the broader flavor-structure review including massive neutrinos and CP-violating effects [5].

questions.question: How low can flavor dynamics or supersymmetric flavor nonuniversality lie while still satisfying FCNC, CP, Landau-pole, and mu-problem constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the TeV-scale flavor-dynamics possibility in mass-matrix models and the explicit FCNC and CP constraints on nonuniversal SUSY extensions [1].

node_c562213db6e6.summary: This cluster focuses on models where gauge or discrete flavor symmetries and loop effects generate the observed hierarchical quark and lepton masses across families.

questions.question: What experimental pattern in K, B, and D mixing would distinguish horizontal-symmetry quark-squark alignment from approximate squark degeneracy as the mechanism suppressing supersymmetric FCNCs?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1] and [5] propose alignment or gauged horizontal symmetries as alternatives to strong squark degeneracy and predict possible effects in B, D, and CP observables.

questions.question: Can a single broken horizontal symmetry account for quark mass ratios, CKM angles, the mu problem, and viable lepton-sector flavor structures without forcing the flavor scale beyond TeV reach?
questions.rationale: Refs. [2] and [3] argue that broken horizontal symmetries can generate mass hierarchies, exact mass-mixing relations, the mu problem solution, and accessible flavor dynamics.

questions.question: How should radiative or symmetry-generated charged-fermion hierarchies be extended to massive neutrinos while preserving predictive CP-violating correlations across quarks and leptons?
questions.rationale: Ref. [4] reviews the flavor puzzles of charged fermions and neutrinos, including mass spectra, mixing patterns, CP violation, and underlying flavor structures.

node_30d711a1b5ed.summary: These papers develop high-energy flavor, GUT, clockwork, RG, and F-theory mechanisms that generate Standard Model Yukawa hierarchies and quark-lepton mass patterns.

questions.question: Can infrared renormalization-group suppression of anarchic Yukawa matrices reproduce quark and lepton hierarchies as predictively as horizontal or U(1)A flavor symmetries?
questions.rationale: RG flow without flavor symmetry can generate hierarchical Yukawas [2], while U(1)A models generate charged-fermion textures through higher-dimension operators [4].

questions.question: What experimental flavor-violating signatures would distinguish low-scale gauged flavor protection by inverted fermion hierarchies from SUSY-GUT horizontal-symmetry suppression of soft terms?
questions.rationale: Low-scale flavor gauge symmetries suppress flavor violation through an inverted hierarchy [3], while SU(5) × U(3)H relates fermion masses to soft SUSY-breaking terms [5].

node_6e5f10661be6.summary: This cluster centers on horizontal or family symmetries, radiative effects, multiple Higgs structures, and supersymmetric alignment as explanations for fermion mass matrices and flavor-changing constraints.

questions.question: Can Abelian horizontal symmetries predict quark-squark alignment accurately enough to replace squark degeneracy once K, B, and D mixing constraints are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: The alignment mechanism was proposed to suppress gluino-squark box contributions without degeneracy [1], while gauged horizontal symmetries give only barely sufficient degeneracy for neutral K phenomenology [4].

questions.question: Which exact mass-ratio and mixing-angle relations from broken horizontal symmetries remain viable if the flavor scale is as low as the TeV scale?
questions.rationale: Horizontal mass-matrix models relate small quark parameters to powers of a symmetry-breaking parameter and allow potentially accessible flavor dynamics [2],[3].

node_97acca0c705c.summary: These works analyze how supersymmetric soft terms, sfermion spectra, radiative Yukawa generation, and minimal flavor violation control FCNC and CP-violating observables.

questions.question: Which gluino- and photino-mediated mass insertions remain viable after simultaneously imposing Delta F = 1, Delta F = 2, epsilon-prime/epsilon, and leptonic-sector CP constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the comprehensive mass-insertion FCNC and CP analyses in [1] and the generalized non-universal soft-term constraints in [5].

questions.question: Can decoupling first- and second-generation sfermions solve the SUSY flavor problem without two-loop RG evolution driving third-generation scalar masses tachyonic?
questions.rationale: The decoupling proposal and its two-loop stop-mass obstruction are analyzed quantitatively in [3].

questions.question: Could radiatively generated light-fermion Yukawas from chiral flavor violation in soft terms be tested through momentum-dependent Higgs-fermion form factors or apparent hard Higgsino-coupling violations?
questions.rationale: The radiative soft-Yukawa mechanism, vacuum-stability limits, enhanced form factors, and Higgsino-coupling effects are described in [4].

node_6488c6d0eb50.summary: The papers use anomalous Abelian horizontal symmetries, often in supersymmetric or string-inspired settings, to produce Yukawa textures, neutrino masses, supersymmetry breaking, and flavor alignment.

questions.question: How uniquely do anomaly-cancellation or Green-Schwarz conditions determine viable anomalous U(1) charge assignments once quark, charged-lepton, and neutrino textures are fit simultaneously?
questions.rationale: Horizontal U(1) models derive mass textures from anomaly-constrained gauge symmetries [1], and anomalous U(1) textures can require Green-Schwarz cancellation [5].

questions.question: Can a single U(1) family symmetry reproduce large solar and atmospheric neutrino mixing through single right-handed-neutrino dominance without losing predictivity in the quark sector?
questions.rationale: SRHND plus a U(1) family symmetry gives analytic conditions for large LMA and atmospheric mixing [4].

questions.question: What flavor-violating or CP-violating observables most sharply distinguish anomalous U(1) textures from U(2)-based supersymmetric flavor alignment?
questions.rationale: U(2) symmetries address the supersymmetric flavor problem and predict Yukawa textures [2,3], while anomalous U(1) models generate different texture structures [5].

node_83f1ef5a0110.summary: This cluster compares anomalous and nonanomalous U(1) horizontal gauge symmetries as frameworks for fermion mass hierarchies, Yukawa textures, and supersymmetric flavor control.

questions.question: Can anomalous horizontal U(1) charge assignments simultaneously reproduce present quark, charged-lepton, and neutrino textures while satisfying Green-Schwarz anomaly relations and current bounds on proton decay and R-parity violation?
questions.rationale: This extends the anomaly-constrained U(1) texture program and its neutrino/R-parity generalizations in [3], [4], and [5].

questions.question: What observable low-energy flavor or CP-violating pattern would sharply distinguish anomalous Abelian horizontal symmetries from non-Abelian 2+1-family constructions used to solve the supersymmetric flavor problem?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the contrast between anomaly-driven Abelian texture models in [1], [3] and the U(2)-based supersymmetric flavor scenarios in [2].

questions.question: Is the string-scale prediction of the electroweak mixing angle in anomalous U(1) texture models robust once realistic neutrino masses, singlet sectors, and higher-dimensional operators are included?
questions.rationale: Both [3] and [5] tie acceptable Yukawa textures to Green-Schwarz cancellation and sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 at the string scale, while [4] adds neutrino and proton-decay implications.

node_b0980d94f691.summary: These papers develop U(2) and related non-Abelian flavor models that organize quark, lepton, and neutrino masses while addressing supersymmetric flavor-changing problems.

questions.question: Do present Delta F = 2 data still select the minimal U(2)^3 breaking directions that correlate K0, Bd, and Bs mixing, or are additional spurions now required?
questions.rationale: The correlation among Delta F = 2 amplitudes and the minimal U(2)^3 breaking hypothesis are the core results of [3] and [5].

questions.question: Can unified U(2) flavor models retain their precise fermion mass and CKM unitarity-triangle relations once the neutrino sector is required to accommodate large solar and atmospheric mixing?
questions.rationale: This connects the U(2) mass-matrix relations and CKM tests in [4] with the large-mixing neutrino conditions from right-handed-neutrino dominance in [2].

questions.question: What flavor observable would most decisively distinguish approximate U(2)^3 from full U(3)^3 minimal flavor violation in supersymmetric or composite-Higgs realizations?
questions.rationale: The contrast between U(2)^3 and conventional U(3)^3 MFV is developed in [3], and the broader EFT and composite-Higgs consequences are analyzed in [5].

node_5c8041edf6ff.summary: This cluster studies nonperturbative and strong-interaction mechanisms, including lattice and Schwinger-Dyson approaches, that dynamically generate elementary fermion masses.

questions.question: Is the idea of a distinct high scale of Dirac fermion mass generation physically meaningful once multi-longitudinal-vector-boson final states remove the Appelquist-Chanowitz bound beyond the electroweak symmetry breaking scale?
questions.rationale: This broad field-level question follows directly from the challenge to the fermion mass-generation scale bound in [1].

questions.question: What observable precision-electroweak pattern would uniquely indicate momentum-dependent dynamical fermion masses with m_f(p) proportional to Lambda_j^2 over p^2 rather than conventional Higgs Yukawa masses?
questions.rationale: Power-law running masses and their allowed precision-electroweak corrections are proposed in [2].

node_b0e4da08c736.summary: These works review and construct non-Abelian discrete flavor symmetry models, such as A4, S4, A5, and S3, to explain neutrino mixing patterns and lepton flavor phenomenology.

questions.question: After the nonzero reactor angle, which residual breaking patterns of A4, S4, A5, or related finite groups yield falsifiable PMNS sum rules for solar, atmospheric, and CP phases?
questions.rationale: The reviews emphasize tri-bimaximal, bimaximal, and golden-ratio patterns and the deviations required after Daya Bay and RENO [1], [3], [5].

questions.question: Can the vacuum-alignment problem in non-Abelian discrete flavor models be solved naturally without ad hoc parameter relations, as in extra-dimensional A4 constructions of HPS mixing?
questions.rationale: The A4 extra-dimensional model identifies VEV alignment as the crucial issue and proposes a natural mechanism for exact HPS mixing at leading order [4].

questions.question: What group-theoretic criteria identify finite non-Abelian groups that can simultaneously address lepton mixing, lepton flavor violation, leptogenesis, and quark-sector extensions?
questions.rationale: The discrete-symmetry reviews catalog finite groups and their tensor products while linking models to lepton flavor violation, leptogenesis, and quark extensions [1], [2], [3].

node_b0e4da08c736_1.summary: This cluster focuses on finite discrete groups and their residual symmetry breaking patterns as predictive sources of lepton and quark mixing matrices.

questions.question: Which finite non-Abelian discrete groups and residual breaking patterns still yield predictive lepton-mixing sum rules once the measured nonzero reactor angle is imposed?
questions.rationale: This follows from [3] and [5], which review bimaximal, tri-bimaximal, golden-ratio, and residual trimaximal patterns after Daya Bay and RENO established a nonzero reactor angle.

questions.question: Can vacuum-alignment mechanisms such as extra-dimensional A4 constructions be generalized to larger finite groups without introducing ad hoc parameter relations or uncontrolled higher-dimensional-operator corrections?
questions.rationale: The question derives from [4], where exact HPS mixing is obtained from A4 with an extra-dimensional solution to VEV alignment and an analysis of higher-dimensional-operator corrections.

questions.question: What finite-group data, such as tensor products and subgroup decompositions, are the limiting bottleneck for building unified quark-lepton flavor models rather than only lepton-sector mixing patterns?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in [1], which discusses quark extensions and phenomenology, and [2], which emphasizes representations, tensor products, breaking patterns, and decompositions for many concrete finite groups.

node_a291eacd8890.summary: The papers emphasize tri-bimaximal neutrino mixing and its realization through non-Abelian discrete family symmetries, seesaw structure, and vacuum alignment.

questions.question: After the measured nonzero reactor angle, which residual discrete-symmetry breaking patterns preserve the predictive content of tri-bimaximal models through solar or atmospheric mixing sum rules?
questions.rationale: This follows from the need for deviations from tri-bimaximal mixing after Daya Bay and RENO and the resulting charged-lepton or trimaximal sum rules [3].

questions.question: Can A4, S4, or larger finite-group models solve vacuum alignment without ad hoc parameter relations while remaining compatible with lepton flavor violation and leptogenesis constraints?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the A4 extra-dimensional construction of HPS mixing and its vacuum-alignment problem [4], together with the phenomenological scope of discrete flavor models [1].

questions.question: Which finite non-Abelian group structures best connect lepton mixing to quark flavor without losing the calculability of tensor products, breaking patterns, and multiplet decompositions?
questions.rationale: This derives from the group-theoretical survey of finite groups used in particle model building and their breaking patterns [2].

node_41fbf883283c.summary: This cluster surveys phenomenological models of lepton and quark masses based on discrete flavor symmetries, including predictions for mixing angles, CP violation, and rare processes.

questions.question: After the measured nonzero reactor angle, which residual discrete flavor symmetries still make falsifiable predictions for theta_23, delta_CP, mass ordering, and neutrino mass sums?
questions.rationale: This follows from the shift from tri-bimaximal mixing to deviations, sum rules, and current global-fit targets discussed in [2], [3], and [5].

questions.question: Can a finite group model simultaneously explain lepton mixing and realistic quark masses without relying on unstable vacuum-alignment assumptions?
questions.rationale: The question is grounded in the T' model's use of doublet representations for quarks and its leading and higher-order vacuum-alignment problem in [4].

questions.question: Which rare processes, leptogenesis observables, or quark-sector correlations can distinguish A4, S4, T', bimaximal, and golden-ratio flavor constructions that otherwise fit present oscillation data?
questions.rationale: This derives from the phenomenological implications and alternative mixing patterns reviewed in [1] and [2].

node_dde867e47e55.summary: These papers investigate specific non-Abelian finite family groups and discrete subgroups of SU(3) or SO(3) that can produce tri-bimaximal mixing and fermion mass hierarchies.

questions.question: Can vacuum-alignment mechanisms based on extra dimensions, SO(3) constrained sequential dominance, or Delta(27) be classified by the residual symmetries they preserve and by their predictions for charged-lepton and quark corrections to tri-bimaximal mixing?
questions.rationale: The A4, SO(3), and Delta(27) models generate tri-bimaximal mixing through different alignment structures and different charged-lepton or quark-lepton corrections [2][3][4].

questions.question: What experimental pattern of neutrino mass ordering, CP phase, and charged-lepton mixing corrections would decisively distinguish A4, SO(3), Delta(27), and related finite non-Abelian family groups?
questions.rationale: The group-theory review catalogs candidate groups, while the SO(3) and maximal-atmospheric models make concrete predictions for phases, CKM-related corrections, and mass ordering [1][3][5].

questions.question: Can higher-dimensional operators allowed by the same family symmetries that enforce HPS mixing generate realistic deviations without destroying the parameter economy of the original non-Abelian model?
questions.rationale: The A4 extra-dimensional construction obtains HPS mixing at leading order and explicitly identifies higher-dimensional corrections as the crucial next test [2].

node_34172fea5e35.summary: These papers classify how finite discrete flavor groups and generalized CP symmetries constrain lepton and quark mixing angles and phases through residual symmetries.

questions.question: Can finite modular groups beyond the known relevant Gamma_N cases produce genuinely new viable lepton-mixing sum rules once residual charged-lepton and Majorana-neutrino symmetries are imposed?
questions.rationale: This is based on the finite modular group scan finding only Gamma_N with N=3,4,5,7,8,16 relevant under specified residual symmetries [1].

questions.question: How can generalized CP plus a finite flavor group be systematically extended to include quark mixing without losing the one-parameter correlations among lepton angles and CP phases?
questions.rationale: This derives from the one-parameter lepton-mixing correlations in finite flavor plus CP models and the stated prospect of extending modular ideas to quarks [1],[2].

questions.question: Which future measurements of theta_23 and the Dirac phase would most sharply distinguish residual-symmetry predictions such as S4, A4, A5, and von Dyck mixing constraints?
questions.rationale: This follows from the residual-symmetry equations that predict nonzero theta_13, deviations from maximal theta_23, and restricted delta ranges [3],[5].

node_865ae0b9b94d.summary: This cluster develops S3 and related family-symmetry models that generate fermion mass hierarchies, large neutrino mixing, and realistic quark-lepton mixing patterns.

questions.question: Can S3-based mass matrices be reformulated so that the observed nonzero reactor angle and CP phase arise as controlled symmetry-breaking effects rather than ad hoc departures from tri-bimaximal mixing?
questions.rationale: Exact S3 and 2-3 symmetry constructions naturally yield tri-bimaximal or maximal atmospheric mixing with Ue3 = 0, while modern data require deviations [1,2].

questions.question: What renormalization-group trajectories from a high-scale 2-3 symmetric neutrino mass matrix can reproduce present oscillation data without spoiling the assumed neutrino mass hierarchy?
questions.rationale: High-scale 2-3 symmetry predicts maximal atmospheric mixing and vanishing Ue3, with MSSM renormalization effects proposed to generate experimental-scale deviations for normal hierarchy [2].

questions.question: Can S3 or SU(3) family-symmetry models simultaneously fit quark-lepton masses, large neutrino mixing, and suppressed supersymmetric flavor violation with fewer auxiliary discrete assumptions?
questions.rationale: SU(3) family-symmetry models connect fermion masses, nearly maximal lepton mixing, and squark-slepton degeneracy, while minimal S3 extensions attempt unified quark and lepton parameter fits [3,5].

node_bc3ab733c65d.summary: These works use S4 and nearby non-Abelian discrete symmetries to build lepton and quark flavor models with tribimaximal or corrected neutrino mixing.

questions.question: Can S4 flavor models still provide a compelling organizing principle once tribimaximal or bimaximal leading-order mixing must be corrected by Cabibbo-sized charged-lepton effects?
questions.rationale: The bimaximal S4 model explicitly relies on Cabibbo-order charged-lepton corrections and needs tuning to reproduce the small mass-squared-difference ratio [1].

questions.question: Which residual symmetry breaking pattern in S4 with generalized CP gives the most falsifiable joint prediction for theta_13, atmospheric mixing, and Dirac and Majorana phases?
questions.rationale: The S4 plus CP models predict trimaximal mixing and specific CP patterns, including maximal or preserved CP and phases controlled by one parameter [4,5].

questions.question: Can an S4 flavor symmetry be embedded in SO(10) or a continuous flavor group while fitting both quark and lepton masses without relying on accidental rank-one deviations?
questions.rationale: The S4 GUT-oriented construction seeks simultaneous SO(10) and continuous-flavor embeddability and realizes viable examples as small deviations from rank-one matrices [2].

node_bc3ab733c65d_1.summary: This cluster focuses on S4-based constructions for lepton masses and neutrino mixing, often embedding CP, supersymmetry, or 3-3-1 gauge structure.

questions.question: Can S4 models that start from bimaximal or tri-bimaximal mixing naturally accommodate the measured reactor angle and charged-lepton hierarchy without fine-tuning the ratio of neutrino mass-squared splittings?
questions.rationale: This follows from S4 constructions where bimaximal mixing receives Cabibbo-sized charged-lepton corrections and the small ratio r remains the main tuning [1].

questions.question: How predictive are S4 x CP vacuum-alignment models once the preserved neutrino-sector Z2 x CP subgroup is varied by real flavon-potential parameters?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by models where S4 combined with generalized CP breaks to Z2 x CP in the neutrino sector, yielding trimaximal mixing and restricted CP phases [4,5].

questions.question: Can an S4 flavor symmetry simultaneously organize quark and lepton masses in a way compatible with SO(10) embeddability and continuous flavor groups, while remaining phenomenologically distinct from other tri-bimaximal flavor models?
questions.rationale: This derives from bottom-up S4 models designed for SO(10) and continuous flavor embeddability and from supersymmetric S4 models that claim phenomenological inequivalence to other flavor groups [2,3].

node_62a1d4fd612c.summary: These papers apply Delta(27), T7, and related flavor symmetries in Standard Model or 3-3-1 extensions to explain fermion masses, CP violation, and seesaw-generated neutrino mixing.

questions.question: Can Delta(27) models that yield near-tribimaximal mixing be updated to accommodate current oscillation data while preserving sharp predictions for neutrinoless double beta decay?
questions.rationale: Delta(27) was used to obtain near-tribimaximal mixing and a definite prediction for m_ee in neutrinoless double beta decay [2].

questions.question: What scalar-sector signatures at the LHC would distinguish geometrical CP violation from generic spontaneous CP violation in Delta(27) or Delta(54) flavor models?
questions.rationale: A Delta(27) model connects geometrical CP phases to realistic quark masses and mixings with exotic scalar properties testable at the LHC, while Delta(54) realizes related calculable phases [4], [5].

node_b47baa129863.summary: This large cluster studies supersymmetric SO(10) grand unified models that relate quark, charged-lepton, and neutrino mass matrices through Higgs representations and seesaw mechanisms.

questions.question: Can minimal SO(10) models with one complex 10 and one 126 Higgs representation still predict neutrino spectra once updated running quark and lepton masses and seesaw thresholds are propagated to the GUT scale?
questions.rationale: This derives from the predictive minimal SO(10) 10+126 construction and the updated running masses at electroweak, TeV, seesaw, and GUT scales [1] and [3].

questions.question: Which low- or high-energy signatures would distinguish canonical from type-II or noncanonical seesaw realizations tied to b-tau unification and large atmospheric mixing?
questions.rationale: This follows from the type-II link between b-tau unification and atmospheric mixing and the broken-D-parity SO(10) seesaw with light B-L, quasi-Dirac heavy leptons, and LFV signals [2] and [5].

node_c0dab5e42023.summary: These works examine SU(5), SO(10), and related grand unified settings where flavor symmetries and seesaw physics produce observed fermion masses and neutrino mixing.

questions.question: Can SU(5)-based flavor-symmetry GUTs accommodate updated running quark and charged-lepton masses at the GUT and seesaw scales while retaining predictive neutrino mixing and charged-fermion mass relations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the use of scale-dependent fermion masses for GUT-scale model building in [1] and the SU(5) flavor constructions with Georgi-Jarlskog relations and neutrino mixing in [3] and [4].

questions.question: What minimal deformation of tri-bimaximal SU(5) flavor models based on discrete symmetries can reproduce realistic CKM and lepton mixing without reintroducing low-dimension proton-decay operators?
questions.rationale: This follows from the SU(5) x dT model in which discrete symmetries restrict Yukawa operators and suppress proton decay while producing near tri-bimaximal lepton mixing and CKM structure [3].

questions.question: Can TeV-scale flavor-sector states that address lepton-flavor non-universality in B decays be embedded consistently in SU(5) or Pati-Salam-like flavor unification without spoiling high-scale fermion-mass fits?
questions.rationale: The question connects the three-site Pati-Salam explanation of flavor hierarchies and B-decay anomalies [2] with the high-scale fermion-mass constraints emphasized in [1].

node_78922e160c8e.summary: This cluster addresses neutrino mass and mixing textures in supersymmetric GUT, string-inspired, and supersymmetry-breaking frameworks motivated by oscillation data.

questions.question: How stable are supersymmetric SU(5) or GUT neutrino mass textures under updated running quark and lepton masses at M_Z, TeV, seesaw, and GUT scales?
questions.rationale: This follows from the use of running fermion masses for high-scale model building and SU(5) texture explanations of quark and lepton mass patterns [1],[2],[5].

questions.question: Can asymmetric SU(5)-related down-quark and charged-lepton mass matrices still naturally explain large atmospheric mixing once modern neutrino oscillation data and high-scale mass running are imposed?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the semiquantitative SUSY SU(5) model where large atmospheric mixing follows from asymmetric mass matrices [2].

questions.question: What observable consequences follow from the supersymmetric theorem linking neutrino Majorana masses and B-L-violating sneutrino mass terms in realistic texture models?
questions.rationale: This derives from the low-energy theorem relating nonzero neutrino Majorana mass to nonzero sneutrino B-L-violating mass terms [4].

node_00b49ca99c92.summary: These papers build SU(5) grand unified flavor models with discrete symmetries such as S4, A4, and Delta(96) to fit quark-lepton masses and lepton mixing angles.

questions.question: After the measured departure from exact tri-bimaximal mixing, which SU(5) discrete-flavor constructions retain predictive relations among CKM angles, charged-lepton corrections, and neutrino mixing without adding many unconstrained operators?
questions.rationale: Papers [2] and [3] build SU(5) models based on discrete groups that produce near tri-bimaximal lepton mixing and realistic quark masses.

questions.question: Can the same flavor-gauge structure that explains quark and lepton mass hierarchies also accommodate lepton-flavor non-universality in B decays while satisfying proton-decay and high-pT bounds?
questions.rationale: Paper [1] links flavor hierarchies and B-decay non-universality in a three-site Pati-Salam model, while [2] stresses symmetry suppression of proton-decay operators.

questions.question: Is the SU(5) explanation of complementary quark and lepton mixing patterns more robust in asymmetric Fritzsch-like textures or in unparallel family structures from coset-space unification?
questions.rationale: Paper [5] uses asymmetric Fritzsch-like SU(5) textures, while [4] obtains large lepton mixing from an E7/SU(5) x U(1)^3 family structure.

node_c816b499892d.summary: This cluster analyzes minimal and non-minimal SO(10) Yukawa sectors, especially 10, 120, and 126 Higgs representations, through detailed fits to fermion masses and mixings.

questions.question: Do current fermion masses, PMNS parameters, and neutrino ordering data still leave a predictive minimal renormalizable SO(10) model with only 10 and 126 Higgs Yukawa couplings, or is an additional 120 or higher-dimensional operator sector unavoidable?
questions.rationale: This extends the minimal 10 plus 126 SO(10) program in which charged-fermion observables tightly determine the Majorana neutrino mass matrix and neutrino spectrum [1].

questions.question: Can the type-II seesaw link between b-tau unification and large atmospheric and solar mixing survive realistic SUSY-threshold corrections and updated limits on Ue3?
questions.rationale: This is motivated by the claim that type-II seesaw dominance plus b-tau unification naturally produces large theta23, large theta12, and a small but testable Ue3 in minimal SUSY SO(10) [3][5].

questions.question: What low-energy lepton-flavor or CP-violating signatures would decisively test SO(10) scenarios with TeV-scale B-L breaking and quasi-Dirac heavy leptons?
questions.rationale: This follows from the broken-D-parity SO(10) seesaw proposal in which TeV-scale neutral gauge bosons and quasi-Dirac heavy leptons can mediate appreciable lepton flavor and CP violation [2].

node_847b4a8c6148.summary: These works focus on supersymmetric SO(10) texture models and numerical fits that connect Higgs-sector choices, family symmetries, and seesaw neutrino predictions.

questions.question: Can minimal renormalizable SUSY SO(10) fits with 10H and 126H Higgs sectors satisfy fermion mass sum rules, CKM CP violation, neutrino mixing, and proton-decay bounds simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows from detailed type-I/type-II seesaw fits and the very limited proton-decay-compatible region in minimal renormalizable SUSY SO(10) [3][5].

questions.question: Which GUT-scale Yukawa texture assumptions remain predictive after including tan beta-enhanced threshold corrections and updated quark-lepton mass uncertainties?
questions.rationale: The question derives from systematic SO(10) operator analysis and updated MSSM GUT-scale mass fits where threshold corrections rescue some classic mass relations [1][4].

questions.question: Can an SO(10) x A4 construction predict absolute neutrino masses without losing the successful charged-fermion fits required at the unification scale?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the SO(10) x A4 model that fits charged fermion masses and predicts absolute neutrino masses through seesaw dynamics [2].

node_4b6544354284.summary: This cluster presents predictive SUSY SO(10) models with U(2), D3, or minimal Higgs structures that fit fermion data while predicting neutrino mixing and CP violation.

questions.question: Can minimal supersymmetric SO(10) models with only 10 and 126 Higgs representations still fit the charged-fermion sector, all neutrino mixings, and leptonic CP violation once arbitrary complex phases are included?
questions.rationale: This extends the predictive 10 plus 126 construction in [1] using the CP-phase generalization in [5].

questions.question: What low-energy or collider signatures of a TeV-scale B-L sector, light neutral gauge boson, and quasi-Dirac heavy leptons would distinguish the broken-D-parity SO(10) seesaw from high-scale minimal type-II seesaw models?
questions.rationale: This question is grounded in the novel supersymmetric SO(10) seesaw mechanism and its TeV-scale phenomenology in [2].

questions.question: Is b-tau unification necessary and sufficient for large atmospheric and solar neutrino mixing in realistic minimal SUSY SO(10), or does that link weaken once CP phases and fit uncertainties are included?
questions.rationale: The b-tau and type-II-seesaw connection is established in [3] and [4], while phase freedom is added in [5].

node_d4f248e28718.summary: This cluster covers how CP violation, flavor effects, sterile-neutrino oscillations, and seesaw dynamics generate the cosmic baryon asymmetry through leptogenesis.

questions.question: What combination of finite-temperature corrections, spectator processes, and charged-lepton flavor effects is required to make thermal leptogenesis predictions quantitatively robust rather than model-dependent?
questions.rationale: This follows from the review's emphasis that recent progress in leptogenesis hinges on finite-temperature effects, spectator processes, and especially flavor physics [1].

questions.question: Can the lower bound on the lightest right-handed-neutrino mass and reheating temperature be relaxed without abandoning the seesaw origin of neutrino masses or the observed oscillation scale?
questions.rationale: The question is motivated by the model-independent CP-asymmetry bound and resulting requirement M_N and T_reh above about 10^8 GeV in hierarchical thermal leptogenesis [4].

questions.question: How precisely must nearly degenerate heavy Majorana neutrino masses and widths be treated in kinetic equations before TeV-scale resonant leptogenesis becomes a predictive framework?
questions.rationale: This derives from resonant leptogenesis, where mass splittings comparable to decay widths, real-intermediate-state subtraction, resummation, and gauge-mediated collisions determine the baryon asymmetry [3].

node_a4e973370a12.summary: This cluster emphasizes standard and resonant thermal leptogenesis from heavy Majorana neutrino decays, including washout, flavor, and nonthermal extensions.

questions.question: Can a single finite-temperature kinetic framework consistently include flavor, spectator processes, gauge scatterings, RGE corrections, and real-intermediate-state subtraction for both hierarchical and resonant leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the leptogenesis review of finite-temperature and flavor effects, the resonant-leptogenesis treatment of unstable mixing and RIS subtraction, and the complete thermal-leptogenesis study [1], [3], and [5].

questions.question: How robust are lower bounds on M_1 and T_RH once arbitrary initial heavy-neutrino abundance, washout by decays and inverse decays, and reheating dynamics are varied within oscillation-compatible neutrino masses?
questions.rationale: This follows from the analytical dependence on M_1, tilde m_1, and light-neutrino scale, and from the model-independent lower-bound and reheating analyses [2], [4], and [5].

node_0d04d096b0a9.summary: This cluster focuses on early seesaw leptogenesis models where heavy Majorana neutrino decays create lepton asymmetry later converted to baryon asymmetry by sphalerons.

questions.question: What observable or calculable combination of finite-temperature effects, spectator processes, and flavor dynamics would most sharply test classic thermal seesaw leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: The review in [1] identifies finite-temperature corrections, spectator processes, and flavor physics as key developments beyond the basic heavy-neutrino decay mechanism.

questions.question: How robust is the analytic dependence of the baryon asymmetry on M1, tilde m1, and the absolute light-neutrino mass scale once scattering processes and flavor evolution are treated beyond the decay-dominated regime?
questions.rationale: The analytic treatment in [2] finds decay and inverse decay dominance in the oscillation-preferred tilde m1 range and quantifies scattering effects as subleading.

questions.question: Can baryogenesis via sterile-neutrino oscillations be continuously connected to classic heavy-neutrino decay leptogenesis in a unified flavor-density evolution framework?
questions.rationale: Heavy-neutrino decay leptogenesis is developed in [4] and [5], while [3] generates lepton asymmetries through CP-violating sterile-neutrino oscillations.

node_12d37f59ab2a.summary: This cluster links baryogenesis to heavy-neutrino decay, lepton mixing, and supersymmetric or nonsupersymmetric SO(10) unification frameworks.

questions.question: Can SO(10)-motivated neutrino mass matrices satisfy the thermal leptogenesis bounds on M_1, tilde m_1, bar m, and epsilon_1 while matching current light-neutrino data?
questions.rationale: The model-independent thermal-leptogenesis parameter constraints in [2] and the SO(10)-subgroup treatment with three right-handed neutrinos in [4] directly motivate this question.

questions.question: When does CP asymmetry from heavy-Majorana-neutrino mixing dominate over direct decay asymmetry in realistic SO(10) spectra?
questions.rationale: The mixing mechanism in [3] can exceed direct-decay asymmetry by orders of magnitude, while [1] and [4] connect heavy Majorana decay to baryogenesis.

questions.question: How do lepton-number-violating washout processes constrain pre-existing baryon asymmetries and quasi-degenerate light-neutrino spectra in SO(10) leptogenesis models?
questions.rationale: The neutrino mass-window analysis in [5] finds efficient washout for tilde m_1 larger than m_* and an upper light-neutrino mass bound, consistent with the quasi-degenerate exclusion in [2].

node_99ad187b46f2.summary: This cluster collects review-oriented and alternative leptogenesis scenarios, including sterile-neutrino oscillations, Dirac neutrinos, and mechanisms without high-scale B-L violation.

questions.question: Which finite-temperature corrections, spectator processes, and lepton-flavor effects dominate the deviation from the simple analytic thermal-leptogenesis picture in the m_sol <= m_tilde_1 <= m_atm regime?
questions.rationale: The importance of these effects is reviewed in [1], while the transparent analytic dependence on M_1, m_tilde_1, and the light-neutrino mass scale is developed in [2].

questions.question: Can sterile-neutrino oscillation leptogenesis be formulated with sufficiently precise quantum-coherence and damping treatments to map the successful nuMSM mass and coupling region unambiguously?
questions.rationale: The oscillation mechanism of [3] and the nuMSM coherence, damping-rate, and parameter-space analysis in [5] motivate this question.

questions.question: How do Abelian U(1) and non-Abelian U(2) flavor structures in neutrino-mass models alter the evolution equations and viability conditions for baryogenesis by heavy-neutrino decay?
questions.rationale: The flavor-structured evolution equations and comparison of U(1) and U(2) family-symmetry models are developed in [4].

node_092dc542a197.summary: This cluster studies how lepton flavor, near-degenerate heavy neutrinos, TeV-scale models, and quantum kinetic effects modify or enhance leptogenesis predictions.

questions.question: What quantum-kinetic treatment best replaces Boltzmann equations when heavy Majorana mass splittings are comparable to decay widths in resonant leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: Resonant leptogenesis depends on unstable-particle mixing, real-intermediate-state subtraction, and nearly degenerate heavy neutrinos with mass differences of order their widths [1,2].

questions.question: How do flavor-dependent washout and CP violation in scattering change the viable lower bound on reheating temperature in realistic thermal leptogenesis models?
questions.rationale: Flavor studies found order-of-magnitude changes in the baryon asymmetry and a relaxation of the reheating-temperature bound when flavor dynamics are included [3,4,5].

questions.question: Can successful leptogenesis with zero total CP asymmetry epsilon_1 be made predictive once individual lepton-flavor asymmetries and efficiencies are constrained by neutrino data?
questions.rationale: Flavor effects allow successful leptogenesis even when the total CP asymmetry vanishes and require flavor-dependent efficiency factors [3,5].

node_962d2b861dc7.summary: This cluster centers on low-scale resonant leptogenesis where flavor-dependent washout and nearly degenerate right-handed neutrinos can yield observable baryogenesis signatures.

questions.question: What density-matrix or Boltzmann framework consistently treats unstable-neutrino mixing, real-intermediate-state subtraction, gauge scatterings, and flavor-dependent washout in TeV-scale resonant leptogenesis?
questions.rationale: Resonant leptogenesis relies on nearly degenerate Majorana neutrinos with mass splittings comparable to widths and requires careful treatment of scatterings and unstable-particle mixing [1].

questions.question: Can an individual lepton-flavor asymmetry, such as tau number, dominate baryogenesis near the electroweak phase transition in a way that is insensitive to initial heavy-neutrino abundances?
questions.rationale: Electroweak-scale resonant leptogenesis found that single-flavor effects can create the observed baryon asymmetry with weak dependence on initial conditions [5].

questions.question: How far do flavor effects relax the apparent lower bounds on reheating temperature and light-neutrino mass constraints in low-scale resonant scenarios?
questions.rationale: Flavor treatments show that asymmetries can change sign, arise even with zero total CP asymmetry, and weaken conventional model-independent bounds [2], [3], [4].

node_8dd9d6f686b2.summary: This cluster develops nonequilibrium quantum field theory treatments of leptogenesis using Kadanoff-Baym, Schwinger-Keldysh, and closed-time-path kinetic equations.

questions.question: How should quantum kinetic equations consistently combine resonant heavy-neutrino mixing, coherent flavor oscillations, and charged-lepton decoherence when mass splittings are comparable to the Majorana widths?
questions.rationale: The issue is central to the flavor-covariant resonant-leptogenesis equations [3] and the Kadanoff-Baym treatment of the maximally resonant regime [5].

questions.question: What finite-temperature and scattering corrections are needed for CP asymmetries in Majorana decays and two-body lepton-number-violating scatterings to match a first-principles CTP or Kadanoff-Baym description?
questions.rationale: This extends the relation between decay and scattering CP asymmetries [2] together with the finite-temperature issues noted in resonant Majorana-neutrino baryogenesis [1].

node_7430dabd658e.summary: This cluster examines leptogenesis in supersymmetric, inflationary, and SO(10) settings, including inflaton decay, sneutrino dynamics, thermal corrections, and right-handed neutrino mass bounds.

questions.question: What class of supersymmetric leptogenesis models can satisfy the lower reheating-temperature requirement for thermal right-handed-neutrino production while evading the gravitino bound?
questions.rationale: Thermal leptogenesis requires high right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating temperatures, creating a conflict with the cosmological gravitino bound in supersymmetric theories [1,2].

questions.question: Can nonthermal right-handed-neutrino production from inflaton decay or preheating replace the thermal lower-bound logic without losing predictivity in the CP asymmetry and washout calculation?
questions.rationale: Inflaton decay and preheating scenarios produce heavy Majorana neutrinos nonthermally and can lower the reheating temperature compared with standard thermal leptogenesis [4,5].

questions.question: Which neutrino-mass and seesaw parameters most directly determine whether sphaleron conversion of a primordial B-L asymmetry remains viable in supersymmetric inflationary settings?
questions.rationale: Leptogenesis reviews tie baryon asymmetry generation to neutrino spectra, the seesaw mechanism, and sphaleron conversion of lepton or B-L asymmetry [3].

node_d5d8693078c1.summary: This cluster investigates whether observable PMNS Dirac or Majorana CP phases in minimal and radiative seesaw models can be directly responsible for successful leptogenesis.

questions.question: Under what precise CP-invariance conditions on the seesaw Yukawa matrix and the orthogonal R matrix can the baryon asymmetry be generated exclusively by the observable PMNS Dirac or Majorana phases?
questions.rationale: This is based on the low-energy CP leptogenesis conditions derived using flavored leptogenesis and the orthogonal parametrization in [5].

questions.question: Can future neutrino oscillation and neutrinoless double beta decay measurements determine not only the presence but the cosmological sign of leptonic CP violation in the class of models where it fixes the baryon-number sign?
questions.rationale: This follows from the proposed relation between the sign of the universe's baryon number and neutrino-oscillation CP violation in [3], and from the review of observable leptonic CP effects in [4].

questions.question: How do wave-function mixing, vertex corrections, and lepton-flavor effects compare in singlet-neutrino versus heavy-Higgs-triplet leptogenesis when the only CP phases are low-energy phases?
questions.rationale: This connects the loop-level CP asymmetry calculation for heavy singlet neutrino decays in [1] with the economical heavy Higgs triplet route to neutrino masses and leptogenesis in [2].

node_86a330d3bd97.summary: This cluster compares minimal, type-I, type-II, triplet, left-right, and TeV-scale seesaw constructions that connect neutrino mass generation with leptogenesis.

questions.question: In mixed type-I plus scalar-triplet seesaw models, can the proportionality between each sector's neutrino-mass contribution and its lepton-asymmetry contribution be turned into a data-driven reconstruction of the dominant leptogenesis source?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the result that right-handed-neutrino and triplet contributions to the lepton asymmetry track their respective contributions to the neutrino mass matrix [2].

questions.question: What minimal deformation of hierarchical type-I seesaw spectra can raise the baryon-to-photon ratio from the too-small generic prediction while preserving the low-energy neutrino data used to infer the heavy-neutrino sector?
questions.rationale: This follows from the finding that hierarchical Dirac masses generically imply M_i proportional to m_Di squared and an asymmetry far below observation [3].

questions.question: Can GeV-scale two-singlet seesaw baryogenesis become overconstrained by combining SHiP-accessible heavy-neutral-lepton parameters, neutrinoless double beta decay, and PMNS CP phases?
questions.rationale: This derives from the claim that, for inverted ordering, future SHiP and neutrinoless-double-beta data could in principle predict the cosmic matter-antimatter asymmetry [5].

node_0311c2eabcc8.summary: This cluster focuses on theoretical links between low-energy leptonic CP violation, lepton-flavor violation, neutrinoless double beta decay, and the CP asymmetries required for leptogenesis.

questions.question: Under what minimal flavor assumptions can the sign of the cosmological baryon asymmetry be robustly inferred from the Dirac CP phase measured in neutrino oscillations?
questions.rationale: This derives from the proposal that, in a class of models, the baryon-number sign can be related to low-energy neutrino CP violation [2].

questions.question: Can leptogenesis driven exclusively by PMNS Dirac and Majorana phases survive once flavor effects, neutrinoless double beta decay limits, and lepton-flavor-violation constraints are treated in one fit?
questions.rationale: This combines the low-energy CP leptogenesis conditions in flavored scenarios with the observables emphasized in oscillations and neutrinoless double beta decay [3,4,5].

questions.question: Which CP-invariance conditions on the seesaw Yukawa matrix and the orthogonal R matrix remain experimentally distinguishable through low-energy CP observables?
questions.rationale: The question follows from the derivation of CP-invariance conditions for the neutrino Yukawa couplings and the complex orthogonal R parametrization [4].

node_740cff01f5cf.summary: Studies charged lepton flavor violation in supersymmetric seesaw frameworks, connecting neutrino Yukawa couplings, slepton mixing, muon g-2, rare muon and tau decays, mu-e conversion, and collider signals.

questions.question: Which rare charged-lepton-flavor-violation channel provides the cleanest test of supersymmetric seesaw Yukawa structures: mu -> e gamma, tau -> mu gamma, mu-e conversion, or tau-sector modes?
questions.rationale: Supersymmetric seesaw studies predict large mu -> e gamma and tau -> mu gamma rates from right-handed-neutrino Yukawa couplings, while Snowmass highlights the discovery potential of tau-sector CLFV searches [2,4,S1].

questions.question: Can minimal-flavor-violation logic be generalized to the lepton sector in a way that preserves predictive links among neutrino data, slepton mixing, and rare muon or tau decays?
questions.rationale: MFV builds flavor breaking from Yukawa spurions, whereas supersymmetric seesaw analyses connect observed neutrino mixing to FCNC and LFV amplitudes through right-handed-neutrino Yukawa couplings [1,2].

questions.question: Does making the first two sparticle families heavy suppress lepton flavor violation enough to reconcile supersymmetric seesaw models with naturalness and future high-intensity muon constraints?
questions.rationale: Effective Supersymmetry suppresses flavor violation with 5-20 TeV first- and second-family sparticles, while muon-decay reviews stress rare muon processes as sensitive probes of supersymmetric new physics [3,5].

node_e7c138032b03.summary: Examines charged lepton flavor violation induced by heavy neutrinos and supersymmetric or low-scale seesaws across radiative decays, three-body muon and tau decays, and mu-e conversion.

questions.question: What pattern across mu->e gamma, mu-e conversion, tau->mu gamma, and tau-sector LFV would most clearly distinguish supersymmetric seesaw flavor violation from an MFV-like effective theory?
questions.rationale: This follows from the MFV EFT framing and the seesaw/SUSY predictions for radiative LFV decays and conversion observables [1], [2], [3], [5], and [S1].

questions.question: Can bottom-up LFV predictions remain robust once the heavy-neutrino spectrum, tan beta, Yukawa hierarchy, and soft SUSY-breaking boundary conditions are varied over the ranges consistent with neutrino oscillation data?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the bottom-up mu->e gamma analysis and the right-handed-neutrino Yukawa studies showing strong tan beta and mixing-angle dependence [2] and [3].

node_accf719b50a0.summary: Focuses on supersymmetric and non-supersymmetric low-scale seesaw mechanisms that generate observable charged lepton flavor violation in rare decays, conversion experiments, and LHC slepton channels.

questions.question: Which pattern among mu -> e gamma, mu-to-e conversion, tau -> 3l, and tau-sector CLFV would distinguish inverse seesaw non-unitarity from supersymmetric slepton-mediated flavor violation?
questions.rationale: The supersymmetric inverse seesaw can enhance LFV through both heavy-lepton exchange and supersymmetric diagrams [5], while tau-sector discovery channels are emphasized in [S1].

questions.question: Can lepton-sector minimal flavor violation reconstruct the full low-scale seesaw flavor structure from neutrino masses, mixing angles, and CP phases once CLFV limits improve?
questions.rationale: Minimal flavor seesaw models can reconstruct flavor structure from light-neutrino parameters, including CP phases, and predict rare processes such as mu -> e gamma [4].

questions.question: Under what low-scale seesaw conditions does non-decoupling of heavy neutral leptons make charged-lepton decay rates observable without violating cosmological and low-energy constraints?
questions.rationale: Heavy Dirac or Majorana neutral leptons can violate decoupling in flavor-dependent graphs and generate observable charged-lepton decays in [1].

node_188b515a3b25.summary: Covers lepton flavor violation in supersymmetric and other seesaw extensions beyond the MSSM, emphasizing model origins, rare decay patterns, mu-e conversion, and collider tests.

questions.question: Which pattern among mu to e gamma, mu-to-e conversion, tau LFV decays, and EDMs would distinguish lepton-sector MFV from inverse-seesaw non-unitarity or supersymmetric slepton-mediated flavor violation?
questions.rationale: Refs. [1]-[4] compare charged-lepton flavor observables, MFV expectations, inverse-seesaw non-unitarity, and supersymmetric diagram contributions.

questions.question: Can low-energy LFV data reconstruct or sharply constrain seesaw Yukawa couplings and heavy-neutrino masses using parametrizations based only on light-neutrino observables plus an auxiliary Hermitian matrix?
questions.rationale: Ref. [5] introduces a seesaw parametrization relating Yukawa couplings and Majorana masses to light-neutrino observables and a Hermitian matrix H that can be constrained by LFV and CP observables.

questions.question: In type-II and inverse seesaw realizations, how large can the separation between total lepton-number violation and lepton-flavor violation scales be while keeping rare charged-lepton processes experimentally reachable?
questions.rationale: Refs. [2] and [3] show that measurable LFV rates arise when lepton-number and lepton-flavor violating scales separate, especially in type-II and inverse seesaw MFV realizations.

node_516e478fb6db.summary: Connects charged lepton flavor violation predictions to neutrino masses and mixing in low-scale seesaw, supersymmetric, beyond-MSSM, and minimal-flavor-violation approaches.

questions.question: Can low-energy charged-lepton-flavor-violation data reconstruct the heavy-neutrino Yukawa and Majorana structure in supersymmetric seesaw models without assuming a unique high-scale completion?
questions.rationale: The Hermitian-matrix parametrization relates low-energy LFV and CP observables to Yν and MN scans, and observed LFV would directly constrain those quantities [5].

questions.question: Which measurements best separate MFV lepton-sector predictions from inverse-seesaw enhancements driven by non-unitary charged-current mixing or slepton flavor violation?
questions.rationale: Leptonic MFV expresses charged LFV in terms of neutrino masses and mixings [2],[3], whereas supersymmetric inverse seesaw models can enhance LFV through heavy-lepton and supersymmetric diagrams [4].

node_469c47d914c7.summary: Investigates lepton flavor violating decays of Z and Higgs bosons in seesaw, inverse seesaw, Zee, flavon, and supersymmetric models as probes of heavy neutrinos and flavor dynamics.

questions.question: Which pattern among H -> l_k l_m, Z -> l_i l_j, mu-e conversion, and mu -> 3e would cleanly identify nondecoupling heavy-neutrino mixing rather than a decoupling seesaw origin of lepton flavor violation?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the nondecoupling behavior of heavy-neutrino loop amplitudes in [1] and the Z and Higgs LFV studies in [2] and [3].

questions.question: Can inverse-seesaw Higgs LFV rates remain observable once neutrino data, perturbative Yukawa bounds, and charged-lepton flavor constraints are imposed simultaneously?
questions.rationale: This follows directly from the generic three-pair inverse-seesaw analysis with neutrino-data and perturbativity constraints in [4].

questions.question: How can Higgs-mediated B_{s,d} and tau LFV decays be combined with tau -> mu gamma and B_{s,d}->mumu bounds to reconstruct or exclude supersymmetric-seesaw Yukawa flavor structures?
questions.rationale: The question derives from the correlated constraints on Higgs-mediated B and tau LFV decays in supersymmetric seesaw models in [5].

node_b336d4677bf1.summary: Studies lepton flavor violating tau and muon decay modes in seesaw, supersymmetric, Higgs-mediated, triplet, and effective-operator models to distinguish possible new physics sources.

questions.question: Which pattern of tau LFV channels would distinguish dipole-dominated, Higgs-mediated, and non-dipole MSSM sources of mu-tau flavor violation?
questions.rationale: The MSSM operator analysis showed that tau to mu gamma, tau to three leptons, semileptonic tau modes, Z to mu tau, and Higgs to mu tau have different correlations depending on dipole and non-dipole operators [2].

questions.question: Can future tau-factory limits on tau to three charged leptons decisively test the nondecoupling heavy-neutral-lepton effects predicted in general seesaw scenarios?
questions.rationale: General seesaw calculations emphasized flavor-dependent nondecoupling graphs and found tau to eee or e mu mu branching ratios as large as about 10^-6 [1].

questions.question: How should tau-sector searches be prioritized across Belle II, Super Tau Charm Factory, LHC, EIC, and FCC-ee if the goal is to identify the underlying source of charged lepton flavor violation rather than only discover it?
questions.rationale: The Snowmass tau CLFV white paper frames tau lepton flavor violation as an unambiguous new-physics signature and compares discovery prospects across present and future facilities [S1].

node_9841b7bd02ab.summary: Explores correlations between neutrino-induced supersymmetric flavor violation, muon anomalous magnetic moment anomalies, grand unified models, and rare processes such as mu to e gamma.

questions.question: If the muon g-2 anomaly persists while mu -> e gamma remains unobserved, what charged-lepton flavor hierarchy is required in supersymmetric seesaw models?
questions.rationale: The review in [4] explicitly frames the joint interpretation of g-2 and mu -> e gamma as a probe of charged-lepton flavor hierarchy.

questions.question: How do large-angle neutrino mixing and an O(1) third-generation neutrino Yukawa coupling reshape the correlation among mu -> e gamma, tau -> mu gamma, and mu -> e conversion?
questions.rationale: Large rates from right-handed neutrino Yukawa couplings are found in [2], while [1] identifies large-angle solar mixing and large Yukawa couplings as especially constraining for mu -> e gamma.

questions.question: Can LFV and CP-violating observables distinguish SU(5) from SO(10) supersymmetric unification more cleanly than proton decay or neutrino-mass observables?
questions.rationale: The unified-theory analyses in [3] and [5] argue that mu -> e gamma, mu -> e conversion, tau -> mu gamma, and the electron EDM provide significant tests of supersymmetric unification.

node_ae3bdd60d0e1.summary: Develops and tests minimal and next-to-minimal flavor violation frameworks through effective field theory, MSSM flavor structure, meson mixing, B decays, and neutrino-mass operators.

questions.question: What single set of flavor observables would most sharply falsify the MFV assumption that Standard Model Yukawa matrices are the only low-energy flavor-breaking spurions?
questions.rationale: The EFT formulation of MFV ties all flavor violation to Yukawa spurions and relates FCNC predictions between B and K physics [1].

questions.question: Can next-to-minimal flavor violation evade the very strong Delta F=2 bounds on non-standard operators without losing predictive correlations among meson-mixing observables?
questions.rationale: Non-standard Delta F=2 operators are far more constrained than the Standard Model operator because of RG and matrix-element enhancements [2].

questions.question: Which low-energy dimension-six lepton-number-conserving operators can experimentally distinguish singlet, fermion-triplet, and scalar-triplet seesaw origins of the same dimension-five Majorana mass operator?
questions.rationale: Different seesaw completions induce distinct dimension-six operators even though they share the same low-energy dimension-five neutrino-mass operator [3].

node_c425994b588c.summary: Analyzes mu-e conversion in nuclei and related charged lepton flavor violation channels using effective Lagrangians, inverse seesaw models, nuclear calculations, and comparisons with mu to e gamma.

questions.question: Which target nucleus or set of nuclei best separates dipole, scalar, vector, and other LFV operators through the atomic-number dependence of coherent mu-e conversion?
questions.rationale: The detailed nuclear calculation shows the conversion rate varies with Z, peaks for intermediate nuclei, and can help distinguish theoretical LFV models [2].

questions.question: Can ratios among mu-e conversion, mu -> e gamma, and mu -> eee identify the seesaw mass scale in quasi-degenerate right-handed-neutrino scenarios?
questions.rationale: The type-I seesaw study finds that in quasi-degenerate right-handed-neutrino spectra, these process ratios depend only on the seesaw mass scale [4].

questions.question: How should future high-intensity muon programs prioritize normal muon-decay precision versus rare LFV channels to maximize sensitivity to supersymmetric flavor physics?
questions.rationale: Muon-decay and CLFV reviews emphasize both precision normal decay and rare muon processes as probes of supersymmetric and other beyond-Standard-Model flavor structures [1],[3],[5].

node_7e483d51c694.summary: Reviews and extends charged lepton flavor violation searches in muon decays, muonic atoms, future lepton and electron-proton colliders, and models tied to muon g-2.

questions.question: Which pattern of results or null limits across mu -> e gamma, mu -> 3e, coherent mu -> e conversion, and tau channels would most cleanly identify whether CLFV is dipole-dominated, contact-dominated, or conversion-dominated?
questions.rationale: This follows from the multi-channel experimental program reviewed in [2] and [3].

questions.question: How should future high-intensity muon-source programs balance precision normal-muon-decay measurements against rare CLFV searches to maximize sensitivity to new physics beyond the Standard Model?
questions.rationale: This is grounded in the joint emphasis on precision muon decay and rare lepton-flavor-violating processes in [1].

questions.question: Can a common dimension-six EFT with leading QED and QCD running provide model-independent high-scale exclusions when operator mixing makes mu -> e gamma, mu -> 3e, and mu -> e conversion mutually entangled?
questions.rationale: This derives from the renormalization-group improved EFT treatment of the three muonic processes in [4] and the one-loop dimension-six analysis of mu -> e gamma in [5].

node_5b486ba35448.summary: Focuses on theoretical calculations and model discrimination for muon-to-electron conversion in nuclei, including effective operators, nuclear structure, strange quark effects, seesaw scenarios, and lepton-number-violating variants.

questions.question: Which pair or set of nuclear targets can most robustly separate dipole, scalar, and vector LFV operators once realistic proton/neutron density uncertainties and lattice-QCD hadronic inputs are propagated?
